sessions.t: 100 Million Bugs Later: A Field Report From the Agentic Era (sponsored by CodeRabbit)
sessions.a: CodeRabbit reviews code generated by major coding agents: 30M+ pull requests and 200K+ independent code reviews each day across open source and enterprises. As agentic development accelerated, PR volume grew 4x while review rounds per PR fell 20%. AI-co-authored PRs carry about 1.7x more issues and up to 2.74x more security issues than human-written code. David Loker, CodeRabbit VP of Applied AI, shares 12 months of review telemetry behind 100M caught bugs—and the enterprise pattern it reveals: heterogeneous coding-agent stacks are the end state. He introduces Agentic Change Management: an independent, agent-agnostic quality gate that assesses every change, surfaces what needs human attention, and explains what it approves. Leave with a vendor-neutral framework for scaling an agentic SDLC without sacrificing quality, security, or control. This presentation is brought to you by CodeRabbit, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: 10 tips for querying Apache Iceberg data with Amazon Redshift
sessions.a: Learn practical strategies for working with Apache Iceberg on Amazon Redshift - from schema design and file sizing to partition pruning, compaction, sort order optimization, predicate pushdown, materialized views, and metadata management. Walk away with an actionable checklist to improve your Iceberg workloads.

sessions.t: 10 tips for querying Apache Iceberg data with Amazon Redshift [REPEAT]
sessions.a: Learn practical strategies for working with Apache Iceberg on Amazon Redshift — from schema design and file sizing to partition pruning, compaction, sort order optimization, predicate pushdown, materialized views, and metadata management. Walk away with an actionable checklist to improve your Iceberg workloads.

sessions.t: 10x Faster Vector Indexes: GPU Acceleration in Amazon OpenSearch with NVIDIA cuVS (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.a: At billion-vector scale, vector index construction can become a performance and cost bottleneck for retrieval, RAG, and AI workloads. Amazon OpenSearch Service Vector Acceleration uses NVIDIA cuVS to accelerate index construction, delivering up to 10x faster builds at a quarter of the indexing cost while preserving the OpenSearch experience. This 300-level session goes under the hood of the architecture: how eligible builds are offloaded to managed GPU workers, how cuVS and CAGRA accelerate graph construction through the Faiss backend, and how the graph is converted into an HNSW index for CPU-based search. We will examine how segment size, quantization, and ingestion patterns affect GPU utilization, build speed, and efficiency. Attendees will leave with guidance for identifying good-fit workloads, optimizing ingestion, and modeling performance and cost benefits for their own deployments. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: 10x or bust: How Amazon's Frontier teams ship with Kiro
sessions.a: Amazon teams using Kiro and AI-native workflows are shipping features in hours that used to take weeks. But the gains didn't come from better prompts. They came from better practices, from rethinking how developers and teams work instead of just adding shiny tools on top of existing SDLC processes. This session dissects three real experiments: a pathfinder initiative, a structured sprint, and in-situ pilots across 50+ teams. You'll learn the five practices that compound into 4.5x–10x gains, the mistakes that kill momentum, and how to run your own pilot starting Monday.

sessions.t: 15 Minutes Is Too Late: Stop AWS Intrusions with CrowdStrike’s Cloud SOC Agent (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
sessions.a: In seconds, adversaries can move from a stolen credential to the AWS control plane, workloads, and Kubernetes before the SOC even begins triage. In this session, see how CrowdStrike Falcon Cloud Security turns a complex AWS attack into one high-confidence incident. Follow an end-to-end intrusion as adversary-informed correlated detections connect identity, control-plane and workload activity; AI-based anomaly detection exposes behavior static rules miss; and Real-Time CDR analyzes AWS activity as it streams in. Then watch CrowdStrike’s Cloud SOC Agent investigate, enrich and prioritize the intrusion, staging rapid response actions for human analyst approval before it becomes a breach. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: 1 Customer, 1 Context, From all the Channels: (sponsored by Redis)
sessions.a: Join Toshish Jawale, Head of AI Engineering at Invoca, to learn how his team is putting context at the center of the business’ customer journeys. Hear how Invoca and Redis are delivering real-time, mutli-source context for Invoca’s agents, how they’re helping customers interact with their brand in exciting ways, and how they’re delivering complete pictures of user brand experiences. This presentation is brought to you by Redis, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: 3 a.m. and Already Fixed: How PagerDuty’s SRE Agent Is Rewriting Incident Response (sponsored by PagerDuty)
sessions.a: Every SRE knows the pattern: an alert fires, and the next 20 minutes disappear into triage before you've even confirmed what's broken. Context is scattered across dashboards, runbooks, and tribal knowledge, and much of incident response is just reconstructing what already happened. This session explores how autonomous operations changes that story. PagerDuty’s SRE Agent investigates before a human is even involved and proposes fixes you simply approve. See it firsthand through PD Labs, a hands-on site for trying autonomous workflows, and SRE Workbench, launching in early access, where humans, agents, and automation meet in order to investigate, diagnose, and remediate issues. This presentation is brought to you by PagerDuty, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: 3rd Party Risk Management Tabletop Experience
sessions.a: Embark on "Third Party Risk Management," an engaging tabletop designed to challenge and refine your approach to managing external partnerships and vendor relationships. In this immersive experience, leaders are thrust into a high-stakes environment where they must navigate complex scenarios involving third-party risks. This tabletop not only enhances your ability to manage third-party risks effectively but also equips you with practical insights and strategies to safeguard your organization’s interests and strengthen its external partnerships. Join us to elevate your risk management acumen and drive resilient, forward-thinking approaches in an interconnected business landscape.

sessions.t: 4 foundations every enterprise needs to scale agents (sponsored by IBM)
sessions.a: AI agents are moving fast, but isolated agents will not change how the enterprise runs. To create value at scale, agents need trusted real-time data, secure access, workflow context and modern applications they can act on. Join IBM and industry leaders to explore how organizations are moving from isolated agents to governed agentic systems on AWS. You’ll leave with a practical blueprint for scaling enterprise AI—connecting data, workflows, applications and access controls so agents can move from one-off tasks to enterprise-wide execution. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: 4 primitives to evaluate your on-call agent's autonomy (sponsored by Resolve AI)
sessions.a: AI that handles on-call autonomously requires agents to take on alert triage, investigations, acting on production, and learning from what happened. Autonomy progresses unevenly as investigations are bottlenecked on quality while actions are limited by trust. In this session we will walk through how we build each primitive of our autonomous agents at Resolve AI, and how we help engineering teams handle on-call and incident resolutions. This presentation is brought to you by Resolve AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: 50k daily iOS builds with virtualization on Amazon EC2 Mac
sessions.a: A leading automotive manufacturer migrated its CI/CD infrastructure from on-premises to AWS to support over 130,000 daily builds (50k + iOS) across 1,300+ microservices. To accelerate iOS mobile app development, the team adopted Amazon EC2 Mac instances with virtualization using OpenAI Tart virtualization toolset, enabling ephemeral macOS VMs that boot in seconds with pre-configured toolchains. This approach reduced average build times from 90 to 35 minutes, a 61% improvement, while eliminating hardware management overhead. The platform now scales to 50,000+ daily iOS builds, serving 3,000+ developers with cost-optimized, reliable, and secure pipelines across hundreds of AWS accounts worldwide.

sessions.t: 5 Amazon ECS features that prevent common production incidents
sessions.a: Five configuration mistakes cause the majority of Amazon ECS production incidents. All five are fixable in under a minute. AZ spread off means one zone failure takes your service down. Short health check grace periods kill containers that are still starting. Disabled circuit breakers let bad deploys roll forward across every task. Default dependency timeouts turn one slow call into a cascading outage. Placement constraints pack tasks onto too few hosts. In this lightning talk, see the incident each feature prevents, the specific attribute to verify, and the fix. Leave with a production-readiness checklist your team can use before every release.

sessions.t: 5 Questions Terraform, OpenTofu, and CloudFormation Can't Answer (sponsored by Spacelift, Inc.)
sessions.a: Every infrastructure change is one run: code, an engine, a plan, an apply. That run is still a wall of unstructured log text, and the questions about your estate go unanswered. Five to ask of your IaC: Did Terraform, OpenTofu, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, or Ansible run it, and does it matter? Where does the time go, and can OpenTelemetry tracing show you? What happens outside the engine: providers, state, policy-as-code, drift, queue time? What about unmanaged resources, the half of your AWS account no run ever touched? Who gets self-service, and can an AI agent be trusted with an apply? This presentation is brought to you by Spacelift, Inc., an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: 5 steps to faster data center exits with AWS Transform
sessions.a: 70% of applications still sit on-premises, and the longer they stay, the more tech debt compounds. AWS Transform uses agentic AI to compress the entire data center exit journey from assessment through execution. Start with AI-powered discovery that right-sizes thousands of servers, compares cost scenarios, and builds a business case that gets executive buy-in in days. Move into automated wave planning and landing zone deployment. Then see how network architectures convert into production-ready VPCs and workloads rehost to Amazon EC2 at scale. We follow one customer's real timeline from plan to exit and unpack what made it work.

sessions.t: Accelerate AI workloads with GPUs on Amazon ECS Managed Instances
sessions.a: Running GPU workloads in containers means choosing the right accelerator, right-sizing instances, and scaling without over-provisioning. Amazon ECS Managed Instances handles infrastructure lifecycle while giving you access to the latest GPUs and accelerators. In this session, explore how to launch GPU capacity with managed provisioning, scale based on real GPU metrics rather than CPU proxies, and automatically recover from hardware failures. Hear how a customer built and scaled their production AI infrastructure on Amazon ECS Managed Instances to serve GPU-backed workloads while optimizing cost and operational agility.

sessions.t: Accelerate analytics and AI with an open lakehouse architecture on Apache Iceberg
sessions.a: Stop choosing between your data lake and data warehouse. Join this session to explore how to build a unified, open, and secure data lakehouse architecture, on Apache Iceberg. Learn how the lakehouse breaks down data silos and opens your data estate offering flexibility to use your preferred query engines and tools that accelerate time to insights. Learn about recent launches that improve data interoperability and performance, and enable large language models (LLMs) and AI agents to interact with your data. Discover robust security features, including consistent fine-grained access controls, attribute-based access control, and tag-based access control that help democratize data without compromises.

sessions.t: Accelerate application development with Amazon ECS Express Mode
sessions.a: What if deploying a containerized application on Amazon ECS required just your code and a few configuration choices? Amazon ECS Express Mode makes that possible by handling observability, networking, and security out of the box. In this session, learn how Express Mode accelerates development for individual developers and platform teams without sacrificing control. Discover practical techniques to optimize your workflows, enhance reliability, and reduce operational overhead. Leave with actionable strategies to increase development velocity using the latest Amazon ECS innovations.

sessions.t: Accelerate database protection and testing with EBS Snapshots and clones
sessions.a: Teams that rely on backups alone risk slow dev cycles, compliance gaps, and prolonged recovery times. Learn how Amazon EBS Snapshots and Volume Clones solve these challenges together. See how Snapshots deliver incremental, cross-region data protection with automated lifecycle policies for compliance, while Volume Clones create instant local copies for development and testing. We'll compare cost, performance, and architectural tradeoffs. You'll leave with a decision framework for when to snapshot, when to clone, and how to combine both in production architectures.

sessions.t: Accelerate database protection, recovery, and testing with Amazon EBS
sessions.a: Protecting your data and troubleshooting issues are essential for running production self-managed databases on AWS. This builders’ session tackles both. Get hands-on with EBS Snapshot Lock for immutable backups, Recycle Bin for accidental deletion recovery, and Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager for automated, application-consistent snapshots. Learn Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization for predictable restore throughput and use EBS Volume Clones to create virtually instant point-in-time copies without impacting production. You will leave with a practical playbook to improve your database resilience. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Accelerate data migrations with AWS DataSync at any scale
sessions.a: Long migration windows, limited visibility, and complex source environments can slow your data migrations to AWS, whether you are transferring data from on-premises file servers, Hadoop clusters, or multicloud object storage. In this chalk talk, AWS storage experts show you how AWS DataSync Enhanced mode's parallel pipeline simultaneously lists, prepares, transfers, and verifies your data to dramatically reduce those timelines. You will learn how to configure for maximum throughput, design endpoint connectivity for secure and efficient data movement, and use richer metrics and monitoring to gain full visibility into your transfer pipeline.

sessions.t: Accelerate intelligent document processing with Amazon Textract
sessions.a: Building custom extraction pipelines on foundation models is powerful but expensive to maintain. Textract Intelligence gives you the same GenAI flexibility as a managed service: custom-field extraction, document classification, splitting, and summarization, all backed by purpose-built OCR instead of a vision model guessing at pixels. In this session we compare approaches head-to-head on accuracy, latency, and cost, then show how 40-language support and trustworthy confidence scores close the gaps that push teams to DIY solutions.

Join this hands-on session to experience how Apache Iceberg Materialized Views on AWS simplify medallion architectures, lakehouse migrations, accelerate BI query transactions and complex joins.

sessions.a: Legacy applications on outdated frameworks and deprecated runtimes represent a growing modernization challenge. In this workshop, use AWS Transform custom to build and execute transformations that accelerate Java modernization at scale. You'll define transformation rules using natural language and code examples, execute multi-step upgrades (Java 8 to 21, Spring Boot 2 to 3, Jakarta EE), refine quality through the agentic AI feedback loop, validate with built-in testing, and run campaigns across multiple repositories. You'll leave with reusable transformation definitions you can apply to your own Java codebases. Laptop required.

AWS and NVIDIA have partnered to simplify the entire Physical AI development lifecycle: from synthetic data generation and model training through sim-to-real validation and hardware-in-loop testing. In this session, discover how the Physical AI Toolchain from AWS provides access to AWS managed infrastructure and NVIDIA’s foundation models and training applications to accelerate every stage of development, reduce time-to-market, and optimize resource utilization across your pipeline.

sessions.t: Accelerate platform engineering on Amazon EKS
sessions.a: Platform teams struggle to balance developer velocity with operational efficiency. Self-service platforms promise faster delivery, but require orchestrating multiple tools, managing infrastructure complexity, and maintaining governance. In this workshop, you'll build an Internal Developer Platform using Amazon EKS Capabilities, which provides fully managed Argo CD for continuous deployment, ACK for AWS resource management, and kro for Kubernetes resource orchestration. You'll deploy polyglot applications, implement progressive delivery strategies, and automate infrastructure management while leveraging AI to boost productivity. Leave with practical experience in platform engineering patterns to ship faster without sacrificing control. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.a: Service onboarding workflows consume hours across security, risk, and governance teams through manual approvals, evidence gathering, and threat modeling. These tasks are auditable, repetitive, and ripe for agentic decomposition. In this chalk talk, we walk through a composable AI plugin pattern that decomposes service onboarding into lightweight modules any agentic client can consume. We discuss how each plugin integrates with any agentic client to execute governance checks end-to-end. We share architecture patterns, working code examples, and show you how to reduce security review time. You’ll leave with a decomposition pattern and an open-source repo to get started.

sessions.a: As organizations optimize AI workflows to keep GPUs highly utilized, Amazon EBS plays a distinct role in the AI pipeline where key business data is close to compute. In this session, learn how EBS minimizes pre-staging time for model weights with low latency, accelerates data preparation and checkpoints on high-performance EBS volumes, and reduces response times by serving vector embeddings at sub-millisecond latencies during inferencing, all while delivering elasticity and configurability in storage and performance. Leave with architecture patterns, volume configurations, and a framework for extending your storage architecture with EBS for AI/ML workloads.

sessions.t: Accelerating AI-powered business transformation and SAP Modernization
sessions.a: The legacy ERP systems that once drove competitive advantage now creates technical debt and blocks innovation and yet modernizing it remains complex, costly, and risky. In this panel, discover how AWS AI services are changing the economics of SAP modernization, making it possible to transform business processes by through AI-powered automations, while delivering breakthrough performance, cost savings and innovation.

sessions.t: Accelerating Apache Spark 4.0 workloads with AWS Analytics
sessions.a: Apache Spark 4.0 is the latest engine upgrade, and AWS is the best place to run it. Learn best practices for building high-performing Spark 4.0 applications using Amazon EMR. Explore what's new, from the ANSI-compliant type system and Variant data type to Spark Connect and Python-first APIs, and how the AWS performance-optimized runtime amplifies these improvements at scale. See how the Spark Troubleshooting and Upgrade agent accelerates migration by automatically identifying deprecated APIs and recommending code fixes, and how AWS Glue and Apache Iceberg integrations simplify pipelines with open table formats.

sessions.t: Accelerating Auto Manufacturing with NVIDIA Omniverse: VW's GS7 Battery Digital Twin (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.a: Deloitte helped Volkswagen Group Components design and deploy a cloud-native, AI-ready digital twin on AWS, powered by NVIDIA Omniverse and the OpenUSD standard, for the GS7 battery production environment. By consolidating fragmented factory data — CAD models, robot programs, camera configurations, and defect imagery — into a photorealistic, simulation-ready scene on AWS, the team enabled virtual commissioning, synthetic inspection data generation, and earlier production validation. The result is a reusable, scalable platform built on AWS infrastructure and NVIDIA's industrial metaverse stack that reduces physical trial effort, accelerates line ramp-up, and creates a foundation for AI-driven quality inspection at scale. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Accelerating AWS Graviton migrations at scale with AI
sessions.a: In this session, we explore how agents accelerate AWS Graviton migrations, improving price/performance for workloads across every phase from migration planning, compatibility validation, to performance testing and optimization. We’ll examine various agentic tools where attendees will learn how to choose the right solution and practical steps to implement the tools in their environments. Participants will leave with actionable strategies to reduce manual overhead and harness AI to unlock Graviton’s benefits at scale.

Join this session to learn how you can accelerate your optimization outcomes while maintaining flexibility in how savings are distributed across your organization. See how you can also measure, share and continuously improve your results.

sessions.t: Accelerating data analytics on Apache Iceberg with Amazon S3 Tables
sessions.a: Every analytics query starts with how your data is stored. In this session, learn how Amazon S3 Tables deliver purpose-built Iceberg table storage that accelerates query performance, reduces storage costs, and eliminates table maintenance overhead. See how to pair S3 Tables with Athena, Redshift, and EMR to get faster results at lower cost, automate compaction and snapshot management, and simplify your lakehouse without changing your query engine or workflow.

sessions.t: Accelerating Data Processing: GPU Accelerated Amazon EMR at the Scale of Netflix (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.a: As demand for more responsive analytics grows, so does the cost of delivering it at scale. This session explores how GPU acceleration integrated with Amazon EMR can improve performance and efficiency, with the NVIDIA cuDF Router that enables seamless migration and simplifies adoption across a large enterprise setting. Applying operational metrics to AI-driven optimization, the smart router continuously directs workloads for better performance and cost efficiency. See how Netflix operates this architecture at scale and hear the practical lessons learned along the way. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Accelerating Fusion Innovation with AMD EPYC on AWS HPC, Analytics, and Agentic AI (sponsored by AMD)
sessions.a: Learn how Pacific Fusion is leveraging AMD EPYC-powered AWS infrastructure to build a scalable platform for high-performance computing, advanced analytics, and agentic AI. By unifying simulation, data processing, and AI-driven research workflows, Pacific Fusion can accelerate scientific discovery while optimizing cost and resource utilization. Discover how AWS elasticity and AMD EPYC performance enable researchers to rapidly scale from compute-intensive simulations to data-rich analytics and intelligent automation, helping transform scientific data into actionable insights and accelerating the path toward commercially viable fusion energy. This presentation is brought to you by AMD, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Accelerating semiconductor design, simulation and verification on AWS
sessions.a: EDA workflows demand different compute across frontend, backend, and production phases. This session covers how AWS EC2 instances map to each design phase. Learn how to select instances for throughput-heavy frontend simulation versus memory-intensive backend verification, and hear how ISVs are qualifying tools on AWS Graviton and other CPU processors to unlock better price-performance for chip design workload.

sessions.t: A closer look at AWS Lambda durable functions
sessions.a: Lambda durable functions let you write reliable, long-running workflows as sequential code. We start with how durable execution works: checkpointing, replay-based recovery, and the programming model. Next, we explore production patterns including sagas, fan-out/fan-in, and human-in-the-loop waits. Finally, we cover observability, a decision framework to help you choose when to use durable functions versus AWS Step Functions, and operational considerations like concurrency, cost, and versioning.

sessions.a: Across AWS, on-prem, and other clouds, workloads need verifiable identity without long-lived secrets. Meet SPIFFE. In this chalk talk, we show you how to issue SPIFFE SVIDs and how they flow into AWS. Follow this SVID through SPIRE attestation, cross-cloud federation, exchange for STS credentials via IAM Roles Anywhere or AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, and presentation to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity for AI agent tool access. Leave with a decision framework for adopting SPIFFE workload identity on AWS.

sessions.t: A Day Without Handoffs: Telecom Operations With Amazon Quick
sessions.a: See how telecom employees use Amazon Quick to handle billing disputes, automatically address network issues, and manage service requests from a single workspace. Pulled from real-world use cases at telecom companies around the world, these demos pull context from OSS/BSS, run complex workflows, and close the loop without handing off to another team!

sessions.t: Adding agentic AI to your legacy app without a rewrite
sessions.a: Full legacy application rewrites take years. Agentic AI lets you deliver value now. In this code talk, we build an AI agent that wraps an existing legacy application without changing the core system. You'll see how the agent understands user intent, calls existing application functions, and helps users complete business tasks through a modern conversational experience. Ask questions as we go from legacy to AI-assisted workflow in real time. You'll leave ready to put agentic AI in front of your legacy application today.

sessions.t: A deep dive on IAM policy evaluation
sessions.a: Every API call in AWS passes through IAM policy evaluation, but few truly understand what happens in that moment between request and access decision. In this chalk talk, we go deep into the weeds of how IAM actually evaluates your policies: how the request context is assembled, how each policy type interacts in the evaluation chain, where implicit and explicit denials come from, and why some evaluation scenarios behave in ways that may be surprising. We will work through real scenarios, common gotchas, and edge cases live.

sessions.t: A DevOps Approach to Recover at Scale from Disaster or Ransomware
sessions.a: Recovering your cloud workload completely after a regional event or ransomware attack is not a checklist; it demands a culture of resilience that turns individual craft into reliable recovery. That culture is built through DevOps. Clear communication, team empowerment, and frequent experimentation and measurement are what separate teams that recover from teams that hope. This session covers the technical requirements for recovering cloud workloads at scale, and the DevOps practices that make those requirements actually work under pressure. You'll leave with practical knowledge to drive full recovery in the face of the worst disasters.

sessions.t: Adopt evolving Amazon DynamoDB resiliency design patterns
sessions.a: In this session, discover recently developed resilience mechanisms for DynamoDB workloads and how existing, advanced resilience patterns have been evolving. Learn how to use the global tables architecture with specific metrics and thresholds that drive effective failover decisions, as well as DR patterns that achieve low RTO and RPO without global tables overhead. Through whiteboard discussion, explore a variety of resilient DynamoDB workload solutions for specific use cases, including incremental export for undoing bad writes, which is faster and less disruptive than a full PITR table restore, approaches to protect against ransomware and data destruction, and cross-account table migration strategies.

sessions.t: Advanced AWS Network Security: Defending Against Emerging Threats
sessions.a: In this hands-on workshop, master AWS network security techniques using AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall. Gain practical experience configuring URL category filtering to detect unauthorized AI service usage, and explore recent feature improvements for container workload protection and advanced DNS-layer defenses. Through real-world scenarios, you'll implement IDS/IPS filtering, east-west traffic controls, and domain-based policies using fully managed AWS services. Leave equipped to build resilient network defenses that address both traditional and emerging threats.

sessions.t: Advanced data modeling for Amazon ElastiCache
sessions.a: This session delves into the intricacies of Amazon ElastiCache data modeling using the purpose-built Valkey data types to optimize application performance and scalability. Explore the use of strings, sets, sorted sets, hashes, bitmaps, and geospatial indexes to model complex relationships and solve use cases such as caching, session store, feature store, real-time analytics, geospatial applications, and rate limiters.

sessions.t: Advanced data modeling with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.a: Amazon DynamoDB is a popular choice for modern applications because it’s a serverless database that provides single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. Optimizing your usage of DynamoDB requires a different approach to data modeling than traditional relational databases. In this session, explore advanced techniques to help you get the most out of DynamoDB. Learn how to “think in DynamoDB” by learning the DynamoDB foundations and principles for data modeling. Further, learn practical strategies and DynamoDB features to handle difficult use cases in your application.

sessions.t: Advanced Optimization & Cost-Saving Strategies for Amazon Athena
sessions.a: Dive deep into Amazon Athena's most powerful capabilities in this interactive chalk talk for experienced practitioners. We'll explore cost-saving techniques—CTAS for materializing expensive query results, partition projection to eliminate metadata lookups, and EXPLAIN-based tuning to minimize bytes scanned. Discuss workgroup budgets, provisioned capacity for predictable pricing, and query result reuse to avoid redundant scans. We'll cover Athena's latest innovations including Amazon S3 Tables integration for fully managed Iceberg tables and enhanced Spark notebooks.

sessions.t: Advanced S3 performance engineering: From multipart to resilience
sessions.a: Master advanced Amazon S3 performance optimization techniques across storage classes, including S3 Standard for general purpose storage and S3 Express One Zone for the highest performance needs. This expert-level workshop focuses on implementing sophisticated data transfer patterns using multipart uploads and Transfer Manager. Design and deploy resilient applications with advanced retry strategies and robust error handling mechanisms. Through technical exercises, build high-performance solutions for large-scale data transfers across different S3 storage classes. Learn to optimize your applications for specific performance requirements, from cost-effective general storage to ultra-low latency implementations. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

sessions.t: Advanced security patterns on Amazon S3
sessions.a: Amazon S3 security settings and access controls suit virtually any workload, but as data estates grow to millions of buckets across organizational boundaries, standard policy approaches hit limits. In this chalk talk, equip yourself with proven patterns for managing access at scale: optimizing policy evaluation with access points and access grants, scaling beyond IAM policy limits with cross-account structures, implementing attribute-based controls that adapt as teams and datasets grow, and securing your data lake perimeter with resource control policies. Join the S3 security team for a structured discussion of the patterns that solve the hardest multi-account access problems at scale.

sessions.t: Advanced vaulting: Ransomware resilience with AWS Backup
sessions.a: Bad actors increasingly target backups alongside production data, and organizations need a vaulting strategy that puts them out of reach. Isolation, immutability, and encryption form the pillars of that strategy, and this session dives deep into how to implement all three with AWS Backup. We'll cover logically air-gapped vault architecture, including how backups are stored in isolated, immutable infrastructure by default, encryption with AWS-owned and customer-managed keys, and durable recovery pathways with Multi-party approval. We'll also cover how these vaulting patterns feed into recovery workflows so that what's protected stays recoverable.

sessions.a: Amazon VPC is a foundational service on AWS, giving you control over your virtual networking environment. Every year, AWS makes updates to Amazon VPC to help improve functionality, security, and usability. In this session, learn about the latest updates to Amazon VPC and how you can use them to enhance your current architectures.

sessions.t: Aflac’s Modernization journey to a resilient and innovative future (sponsored by Kyndryl)
sessions.a: Modernizing critical systems is never just about technology. In this executive panel, leaders from Aflac, Kyndryl, and AWS share the real-world experience behind Aflac’s transformation journey, from overcoming operational challenges and reducing downtime risk to enabling future innovation & continuous modernization. Learn how a strong customer-partner relationship helped balance transformation with business continuity, security, and regulatory requirements. Gain insights into managing large-scale transformation, avoiding common pitfalls, and building a roadmap that delivers measurable business value while preparing for the next generation of cloud and AI-driven innovation. This presentation is brought to you by Kyndryl, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Agentic AI Control Plane on AWS: govern agents at enterprise scale (sponsored by Tata Consultancy Services)
sessions.a: Enterprises are moving from a handful of agents to hundreds. Without a shared layer for identity, policy, orchestration, and observability, that growth stalls. In this 20-minute launch session, we introduce the Agentic AI Control Plane on AWS: a governed foundation for building, deploying, and running agents across business and IT workflows. See how it handles agent onboarding, guardrails, cost and performance visibility, and human oversight, with a live look at the platform. Built for CIOs, data and AI leaders, and platform and risk teams who need agent fleets to scale safely, with the controls their auditors expect. This presentation is brought to you by Tata Consultancy Services, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Agentic AI for manufacturing: Build a cross-domain digital thread
sessions.a: Manufacturing data lives in silos — from engineering systems through production lines. In this workshop, build an agentic digital thread: a knowledge-graph-powered AI system that unifies OT and IT data across the product lifecycle and answers cross-domain questions in real time. Using Amazon Neptune, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and AWS IoT SiteWise, deploy agents that autonomously traverse connections from product design through production operations — linking engineering changes to equipment assets to quality events — without point-to-point integrations. Leave with a deployable reference architecture adaptable to any manufacturing environment.

sessions.t: Agentic AI for Security: How AWS CIRT reduced triage time to minutes
sessions.a: When a security event hits a customer account, every minute counts. Learn how AWS CIRT built an agentic AI system using Amazon Kiro that performs investigation workflows autonomously: ingesting case data, baselining environments, analyzing indicators, and producing triage assessments. We cover architecture decisions for AI agents with live AWS API access, evaluation frameworks measuring accuracy against expert answer keys, and guardrails keeping humans in the loop. Leave with patterns for applying agentic AI to operational workflows where accuracy is non-negotiable.

sessions.t: Agentic AI for software-defined vehicles: Compress the V-Cycle with Kiro
sessions.a: Automotive embedded software teams face complex V-Cycle workflows, safety standards, and competitive pressure to ship faster. In this workshop, experience how agentic AI transforms the embedded software V-Cycle — compressing timelines from weeks to hours without sacrificing quality or traceability. Attendees build a remote start/stop feature for an autonomous mower platform, using Kiro to orchestrate agents across requirements engineering, code generation, virtual-target testing, and test automation.

sessions.a: As agentic AI expands into regulated industries, autonomous decisions must meet compliance before production. This session gives partners a governance framework spanning technical and non-technical requirements — not just architecture. We demo a working multi-agent system and share the code.

sessions.t: Agentic AI Governance Tabletop Experience
sessions.a: Navigate AI-driven security threats as they escalate in real time. In this immersive executive tabletop, participants allocate a constrained governance budget, then respond to live crisis events scored across six dimensions. Practice navigating high-stakes scenarios including autonomous AI deployment failures, third-party security incidents, and emerging regulatory obligations. Confront real attack techniques, compliance frameworks, and enterprise liability exposure while aligning cross-functional teams under pressure. This experience sharpens governance instincts and crisis fluency—equipping leaders to govern Agentic AI risks, enforce accountability, and make decisive resource allocation calls before a real crisis demands it.

sessions.t: Agentic AI in Production: Natera Saves Lives, Cuts Costs, Grows Revenue
sessions.a: Natera, a global leader in cell-free DNA testing for oncology, women's health, and organ health, built reusable agentic infrastructure on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore to power multiple internal platforms from a single framework. Natera's VP of Engineering shares the technical decisions behind this infrastructure and provides a blueprint for building once and scaling across your organization. See a live demo of one platform built on this foundation for revenue cycle management, cutting prior-authorization denial rates 6x, reducing touchpoints by 5x, and enabling new use cases to go live in under a week.

sessions.t: Agentic AI Jam - brought to you by Nvidia
sessions.a: Come with your team of four or join a team and meet new friends in the session. Are you ready to build and deploy agentic AI solutions on AWS? We provide hands-on environments where you can architect intelligent and production-ready agents. How do you orchestrate multi-step agent reasoning with tool use? How can you design agents that plan, act, and self-correct autonomously? Whether you are new to AWS or a seasoned Cloud Ninja, this Jam is your chance to demonstrate your skills and learn new ones. Structured for all experience levels, our sessions include guided exercises, helpful clues, and support from AWS experts to accelerate your agentic AI expertise. Team up, compete with others, climb the leaderboard, and win prizes based on speed and accuracy. With expert guidance every step of the way, all you need is a computer, a desire to learn, and a competitive spirit.

sessions.t: Agentic AI Meets ‘Human-Guided-Autonomy’ (sponsored by Terra)
sessions.a: AI is accelerating how fast code ships and how fast attackers find exploitable weaknesses, and annual pentests cannot keep pace. This session looks at what it takes to make security validation genuinely continuous rather than just more frequent, tracking what changed instead of retesting everything from scratch. Self-driving cars, robotic surgery, and other sensitive actions all became viable the same way: not by removing the human, but by defining exactly which actions the machine takes on its own and which ones need a hand on the controls. This talk will cover the delegate balance between autonomy, safety and control in Offensive Security.

sessions.t: Agentic AI Meets the Line-of-Business Buyer
sessions.a: Budget authority is migrating from CIOs to line-of-business leaders - CFOs, Chief Medical Officers, Heads of Manufacturing - who buy outcomes, not infrastructure. At the same time, agentic AI is making it possible to automate entire business processes end-to-end, not just assist them. The partners who win are the ones who can connect these two shifts: framing autonomous agents as measurable business outcomes (revenue acceleration, cost compression, speed-to-market) in the language LOB leaders understand.

sessions.t: Agentic AI Needs Agentic Infrastructure: Autonomy on Amazon EKS (sponsored by ScaleOps)
sessions.a: Enterprises now ship software that reasons and acts on its own. The infrastructure underneath still waits for a human to edit YAML. This session makes the case that autonomous workloads demand autonomous infrastructure, and shows what it looks like on Amazon EKS today: agents held to fractional GPU allocations that track real consumption, pod requests that stay honest as behavior drifts, and Karpenter consolidating nodes fed by accurate signals. You'll hear how enterprises run this in production with ScaleOps, and where autonomous resource management goes next. Leave with a blueprint for infrastructure that manages itself. This presentation is brought to you by ScaleOps, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Agentic commerce in production: multi-agent orchestration on AgentCore
sessions.a: A single agent that both advises and sells gets fragile fast. This session shows a production multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents, running for real Shopify merchants, where an orchestrator coordinates two specialists: a wellness advisor in a regulated domain and a commerce agent that owns decision and checkout. We walk the decisions that matter: orchestration topology, intent routing and handoffs, shared versus isolated memory across agents, where the action boundary and per-agent guardrails live, and the latency and token cost that coordination multiplies. A demo follows one conversation from advice to checkout. You leave with an orchestration pattern, and the code to implement it directly in your online store.

sessions.t: Agentic commerce: shopping assistants to agent-ready infrastructure
sessions.a: AI agents are reshaping how consumers discover and purchase products, and retail and CPG brands have a massive opportunity to meet them where they are. This chalk talk covers both sides of the agentic commerce stack. First, we walk through how retailers can launch conversational shopping customized to their catalog and brand voice in weeks with the Agentic Shopping Assistant on AWS, powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and inspired by Amazon's own AI shopping experience. Then we explore how to make your platform discoverable by external AI agents through structured product feeds, headless APIs, and payment orchestration for machine-initiated transactions.

sessions.t: Agentic commerce: Use AI agents with AWS Marketplace
sessions.a: Managing software procurement across dozens of tools, teams, and accounts is slow and error-prone. In this lightning talk, we use AI agents to automate the buyer journey on AWS Marketplace to discover and evaluate products, accept discounted offers instantly, enforce governance, achieve operational excellence, request refunds and cancellations, and gain unified visibility into spend and cost management. Compress procurement from weeks to minutes while maintaining governance and financial controls.

sessions.t: Agentic developer experience with Amazon EKS
sessions.a: Transform your Kubernetes development workflow using generative AI. In this workshop, use your choice of agentic AI CLI, Kiro CLI, Claude Code, or Codex, with the EKS MCP Server to automate complex operations, troubleshoot applications through natural language, and deploy microservices on Amazon EKS. Work through hands-on labs: explore clusters using natural language, fix connectivity and ingress issues by orchestrating the EKS MCP Server with Terraform, and deploy new application components using AI-guided analysis. Leave with practical skills to integrate AI-powered automation into your existing Kubernetes workflows and dramatically improve developer productivity.

sessions.t: Agentic development with AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
sessions.a: AI coding agents can write application logic, but can they provision your infrastructure too? In this chalk talk, explore AWS Cloud Development Kit's (AWS CDK) latest capabilities—Mixins, the CDK Toolkit Library, and programmatic synth/deploy APIs—make CDK a first-class target for agentic workflows. See how agents reason about constructs, compose infrastructure from natural-language intent, and validate results before deployment. We'll discuss patterns that work, guardrails that keep agents safe, and where human judgment still matters. Bring your questions—this is an interactive session for anyone curious about the intersection of AI agents and infrastructure as code.

sessions.t: Agentic fairness: Practical methods to detect bias in AI-driven decisions
sessions.a: AI agents are increasingly making real-world decisions — approving loans, issuing refunds, offering discounts — yet most fairness testing still focuses on whether chatbots use offensive language. This gap creates real business and regulatory risk. Join this session to explore how to assess whether your agentic AI systems apply equitable treatment across chosen demographic attributes using defined fairness criteria. Through hands-on examples spanning financial services, customer support, and commerce, discover how to move from language-level toxicity checks to decision-level fairness audits. Learn to identify disparate treatment, choose appropriate fairness metrics for your use case, and implement testing frameworks that catch bias where it matters most: in the outcomes that affect people's lives.

sessions.t: Agentic Integration: How AI Agents Replace Static CRM Connectors
sessions.a: Every enterprise has dozens of integrations connecting their CRM, ticketing, and backend systems to their customer experience platform, and every one of them is static, brittle, and expensive to maintain. In this chalk talk, we explore how Amazon Connect Customer, powered by Model Context Protocol (MCP), shifts integration from point-to-point connectors to intelligent, agentic orchestration. The AI agent reasons across multiple systems in real time, assembling unified customer context that no single system holds alone. We whiteboard the architecture: how MCP connections work, how each new system compounds the intelligence available to every interaction, and how to evaluate which integrations to migrate first. Bring your integration pain (Salesforce, ServiceNow, homegrown systems) and we'll design the agentic alternative on the whiteboard.

sessions.t: Agentic Memory: Build AI Agents That Learn from Every Interaction
sessions.a: Today's AI agents forget everything after each conversation ends. A customer calls back about the same issue for the third time, and the agent starts from zero. In this chalk talk, we explore how to architect persistent memory systems for Amazon Connect Customer AI agents, enabling them to remember customer preferences, recall prior issue context, and adapt resolution strategies over time. We walk through three memory patterns: episodic (past interactions), semantic (customer knowledge graphs), and procedural (learned resolution paths). We whiteboard real architectures using Customer Profiles, Bedrock knowledge bases, and DynamoDB to build agents that reduce repeat contacts and deliver personalized experiences, without retraining models. Bring your memory challenge and we'll design the persistence layer on the whiteboard.

sessions.a: AWS Transform orchestrates AI agents that analyze, refactor, and convert legacy applications without manual line-by-line rewrites. In this bootcamp, set modernization objectives, let AI agents decompose and transform .NET Framework code to cross-platform .NET on Linux, then migrate a SQL Server database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Practice agentic assessment, wave planning, code transformation, and schema conversion end to end.

sessions.t: Agentic Powered AWS Frontier Agents
sessions.a: Application failures and security vulnerabilities demand fast answers to reduce downtime. In this bootcamp, learn how to setup AWS DevOps Agent and automate investigation failures through logs, metrics, and code changes, then generate remediation plans. Learn how to use AWS Security Agent to configure domain-scoped penetration tests, monitor real-time execution, and interpret severity-rated findings. Gain hands-on experience with two agents that compress hours of investigation into minutes.

sessions.t: Agentic Process Transformation at Enterprise Scale
sessions.a: Your customers don't need another automation tool, they need the leap forward they're actually looking for with AI. Agentic Process Transformation (APT) is the framework partners use to help customers move past isolated task automation and into enterprise-wide process reinvention: redesigning entire processes from the ground up to grow revenue and improve the bottom line at a scale automation alone can't reach. We'll share how to spot these transformation opportunities and the architectural patterns that turn them into production solutions. Leave with a concrete strategy for helping your customers make that leap today.

sessions.t: Agentic Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) with the UK Home Office (sponsored by Capgemini)
sessions.a: The UK Home Office is tasked with keeping the UK Safe and Prosperous. Capgemini is working with the Home Office to increase effectiveness and efficiency of its digital and cloud services. Key areas include case management, legacy modernization and SDLC efficiency. This is being delivered in collaboration with AWS and Anthropic. Using Claude agents via AWS Bedrock, this capability is forecast to deliver >30% cashable savings compared to existing processes and improve quality by >20% through better informed decisions. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Agents at the Edge: Global AI on Cloudflare + Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by Cloudflare)
sessions.a: Most AI apps put the model and the user on opposite sides of the planet. This talk shows a better pattern: run inference on Amazon Bedrock, and run the agent itself on Cloudflare's edge, within ~50ms of 95% of the world's users. We'll walk through building a working agent with Workers (0ms cold starts), the Agents SDK, and Durable Objects for memory, with AI Gateway in front of Bedrock for caching, rate limiting, cost control, and observability. You'll leave with a reference architecture for shipping fast, cheap, and observable AI to a global audience. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudflare, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Agents need names too: Open standards for agent discovery
sessions.a: As AI agents proliferate, the internet needs a decentralized way to name, discover, and trust them. This session explores how AWS contributes to open source projects like DNS-AID (IETF/Linux Foundation) and AI-Catalog (Linux Foundation) to define the agent discovery layer atop existing DNS infrastructure. We'll walk through the specs — SVCB records, W3C DIDs, Verifiable Credentials, HTTP Message Signatures — and show how anyone can resolve and verify an agent with off-the-shelf libraries and a single DNS query. No vendor lock-in. Standards in, standards out.

sessions.t: Agents on call: Autonomous DB ops on Amazon Aurora with Expedia Group
sessions.a: Expedia Group manages thousands of database instances across hundreds of AWS accounts. When incidents strike at this scale, every second counts. In this session, learn how a customer-driven vision for agentic AI evolved into a joint design partnership for autonomous database operations on Amazon Aurora. Discover how agents diagnose incidents across fleet-scale telemetry and deliver actionable recommendations to engineers. This joint initiative demonstrates how AI agents reduce incident response time and serves as a blueprint for teams seeking to automate database operations at scale. Learn how AWS is building the underlying capabilities to make autonomous operations real.

sessions.t: Agents run at the edge. The blast radius lives in the cloud (sponsored by Sysdig)
sessions.a: Every agent your company runs, on a developer laptop, in a CI runner, or in an Amazon EKS pod, ends its work the same way, with an API call against your AWS account using a credential nobody reviewed. Endpoint tools stop at the laptop. The credentials that matter live in the cluster. This year's worst agent incidents involved no attacker. An agent did what it was permitted to do, and nobody rendered a decision at the moment a permitted step became an incident. In fifteen minutes, Sysdig follows one person's agents from their laptop into EKS, shows what each action would reach in your account, and stops the one whose reach includes admin-equivalent permissions before it executes. Bring your own agents. Ask us what they can reach. This presentation is brought to you by Sysdig, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Agents that train themselves: autonomous reinforcement learning on AWS
sessions.a: What if an agent could design reward functions, launch reinforcement learning, evaluate policies in simulated environments, and iterate autonomously until convergence? This session demonstrates a Strands agent orchestrating the full RL loop on SageMaker: generating rewards from a natural language objective, evaluating against quantitative success criteria, diagnosing failure modes, adjusting hyperparameters, and repeating without human intervention. We cover tool interfaces for each pipeline stage, how the agent decides when to iterate vs. stop, evaluation design for automated pass/fail, and how this pattern extends to any domain requiring iterative experimentation from robots to game playing and control systems.

sessions.t: Agents under oath: HIPAA-compliant agentic AI on AWS
sessions.a: AI agents in government healthcare don't just query databases. They reason, remember, and act. Each of those capabilities opens a new surface where protected health information (PHI) can leak model responses, persistent memory, tool calls, RAG retrieval, and agent traces. Traditional RBAC and encryption were not built for this. In this chalk talk, we will walk through a real prior authorization determination scenario together, map where PHI bleeds through an ungoverned agent and then redesign the architecture as a group — four trust zones, sixteen controls, all mapped to HIPAA Security Rule safeguards. Come ready to draw and debate.

sessions.t: Agents Under Oath: HIPAA-compliant agentic AI on AWS
sessions.a: Agents expose PHI across five surfaces RBAC can't see: model responses, persistent memory, tool calls, RAG retrieval, and agent traces. This chalk talk walks a HIPAA-compliant reference architecture on AWS: four trust zones, sixteen controls mapped to Security Rule safeguards. Bring questions.

sessions.t: AI-accelerated migration from self-managed Kubernetes to EKS Auto Mode
sessions.a: Teams managing their Kubernetes fleet carry the full weight of the cluster: control plane, node lifecycle, add-on upgrades, and the operational toil. This session shows how to move that undifferentiated work to Amazon EKS Auto Mode, and how AI accelerates the migration itself. See how agentic tooling analyzes your existing clusters, translates manifests and add-on configurations, and flags what needs to change before you cut over. Learn the patterns for migrating workloads with minimal disruption, from node pools to networking to storage. Discover how teams reach a managed, self-scaling cluster in a fraction of the time manual migration takes.

sessions.t: AI agents are crawling your website? Identify, optimize, rate-limit, & monetize them
sessions.a: AI agents are the new web visitors - but how do you protect your content while unlocking new revenue? In this code talk, we deploy a Single Page Application on CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, and Bedrock, then progressively secure and monetize AI agent traffic. We integrate AWS WAF Bot Control to identify agents via the WBA protocol, implement intelligent routing in CloudFront Functions to serve optimized content per visitor type, and enforce rate limits by bot identity and actual resource consumption. Finally, we enable AI Traffic Monetization in WAF and demonstrate end-to-end paid content access using the x402 payment protocol with a Bedrock AgentCore.

sessions.t: AI agents for HPC operations
sessions.a: Managing HPC infrastructure shouldn’t slow down science and engineering. Learn how AI-powered agents with AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS) automate workload placement, detect and recover from failures, and simplify day-to-day cluster operations. Through practical examples, we’ll show how intelligent automation reduces operational overhead, improves resource utilization, and enables platform teams to spend less time managing infrastructure and more time supporting research and innovation.

Through practical examples, we’ll show how intelligent automation reduces operational overhead, improves resource utilization, and enables platform teams to spend less time managing infrastructure and more time supporting research and innovation.

sessions.t: AI agents for PostgreSQL replication and partitioning
sessions.a: Recent PostgreSQL releases introduced transformative capabilities for logical replication and partitioning, including filtering, parallel apply, sequence replication, and improved planning for partition-heavy workloads. These features are powerful, but tuning them for a specific environment remains complex. In this session, learn to build agents for these core PostgreSQL concepts on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: one that analyzes workloads to recommend optimal logical replication configuration, and a partitioning agent that evaluates query patterns and table bloat to guide table partitioning strategy.

sessions.t: AI Agent Teams at Scale
sessions.a: When one event impacts hundreds, or even thousands, of customers simultaneously (a cancelled flight, a power outage, a system failure), contact centers cannot scale human agents fast enough. In this hands-on workshop, you orchestrate parallel AI agent teams using Amazon Connect Customer. You configure AI agents that fan out across dozens of affected customers at once: rebooking flights, issuing credits, and scheduling callbacks, all while a single human orchestrator monitors progress, approves exceptions, and intervenes only where needed. Walk away with a working parallel orchestration pattern and the configuration to deploy 1-to-many AI response at scale. This is not 1-to-1 AI coaching. This is 1-to-many crisis orchestration.

sessions.t: AI Assistant for Public Sector: Governance Without Compromise with Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Public sector organizations serve diverse populations with strict boundaries: students and administrators, citizens and case workers, patients and providers. They need AI that works across these groups without compromising data isolation, compliance, or governance. Multi-tenant environments demand security frameworks most AI assistants were not built to meet. Hear from a higher education customer who faced these constraints and displaced their incumbent tool in favor of Amazon Quick's governance-first architecture: tenant-level data isolation, role-based access controls across distinct user populations, and compliance frameworks built for regulated environments. Learn why existing solutions fell short, how Quick's native governance model met their requirements without custom engineering, and what the transition looked like from decision to deployment.

sessions.t: AI-assisted data modeling for Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.a: In this session, learn practical Amazon DynamoDB data modeling through an AI-assisted approach. Architect complex data models using sophisticated techniques right inside an AI-powered IDE, then go from modeling to production, building a full-stack, serverless application powered by DynamoDB and other AWS services via a coding agent of choice. Optimize access patterns, leverage secondary indexes, and express application requirements in natural language to generate and refine a complete solution built on DynamoDB. Discover how AI-assisted database design accelerates complex NoSQL decisions at every stage of development. Bring your laptop to participate.

Architect complex data models using sophisticated techniques right inside an AI-powered IDE, then go from modeling to production, building a full-stack, serverless application powered by DynamoDB and other AWS services via a coding agent of choice. sessions.t: AI-Assisted Incident Response: Preparing for AI-Assisted Offensive
sessions.a: The tools to raise the bar on incident response are here. AI can handle the volume so your team can focus on the nuance. But making that shift in practice, earning trust, building feedback loops, securing the tools themselves, is where we have seen teams get stuck. In this chalk talk, AWS Customer Incident Response Team (CIRT) leaders share exactly how we made that transition and what we learned along the way. We'll diagram the pipeline live, simulate an investigation, and spend real time working through your scenarios at the whiteboard.

sessions.t: AI at Lennar: Driving 80,000 Home Deliveries with Bedrock & Coralogix (sponsored by Coralogix)
sessions.a: Lennar is bringing AI into the everyday work behind more than 80,000 home deliveries a year, from land research and acquisition to construction, customer engagement, and sales. Join Ralph Gootee, CTO of Lennar, and Ariel Assaraf, CEO of Coralogix, for a practical look at moving AI from experimentation into production. They’ll share how Lennar is building and scaling AI agents on Amazon Bedrock, using AWS inference services and open-source models, and how Coralogix helps teams understand adoption, performance, cost, and business impact. This presentation is brought to you by Coralogix, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AI Didn't Wait for Security: Now What?
sessions.a: AI didn't wait for your security review. Developers already ship code with agentic AI, coding assistants, and MCP servers without governance; blocking them lowers efficiency and leaves you falling behind. This builder-focused session dissects the architecture of a governed AI platform. You'll learn how to build a centralized MCP broker with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and Runtime, and how agent requests gain identity and permissions. You'll build and distribute a curated agentic skills catalog and reusable agentic blueprints. Finally, you'll see how AI SDLC frameworks bring consistency and higher-quality artifacts, with DevOps and security agents woven into key stages.

sessions.t: AI discipline: UCLA's data foundation and framework for saying no
sessions.a: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) invested in their data foundation first. Their large-scale data modernization—Bruin Cloud and the campus Data Hub—created a unified, governed data environment across a sprawling research university, but it wasn't enough. As AI demand surged, Deputy CIO Veronica Garcia and her team built a disciplined product management approach to evaluate, prioritize, and scale AI use cases against UCLA's mission. Learn how UCLA’s technical architecture accelerated data modernization, the framework used to determine AI priorities, and the governance model that keeps it all aligned that launched high-impact use cases from increasing fundraising, advancing research, and supporting student safety and success.

sessions.t: AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC)
sessions.a: The AI Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) reimagines how teams plan, build, and ship software with AI as a first-class participant. In this bootcamp, learn the three phases (Inception, Construction, Operation) , apply the Intent-Unit-Bolt framework to decompose requirements into AI-executable work items, then use Kiro IDE's Spec-Driven Development to generate domain models, application code, tests, and infrastructure. You leave with a working application built entirely through the AI-DLC methodology.

sessions.t: AI-driven optimizations for HPC configurations on AWS
sessions.a: Choosing the right HPC configuration often requires extensive benchmarking across instance types, MPI implementations, core counts, and application-specific settings. Learn how AWS uses AI to predict optimal HPC configurations from historical workload data, helping engineers make informed decisions before launching large-scale jobs. We’ll cover the models behind these recommendations and demonstrate how AI reduces trial and error while improving performance, cost efficiency, and time to solution.

sessions.t: AI-driven serverless development with Kiro
sessions.a: What if an AI assistant could apply serverless patterns and best practices to help you build production-ready code faster? In this workshop, use Kiro to create a serverless application with authentication, tests, observability, and an optional CI/CD pipeline. Along the way, your AI assistant reviews and explains code, looks up configuration settings, and generates tests—accelerating your development workflow while teaching you serverless fundamentals. Whether you're new to serverless or looking to boost productivity, you'll walk away with a working application and practical AI-assisted development techniques. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: AI-Enabled SRE: Empowering Incident Commanders at Riot Games
sessions.a: Learn how Riot Games built an AI-powered post-incident review workflow within its LiveOps Process & Analytics (P&A) team using AWS AgentCore. Integrated with Datadog, Slack, Jira, and version-control sources, the platform orchestrates modular AI agents that gather evidence, validate incident impact, and generate structured reviews and RCA drafts. With humans in the loop to review and approve outputs, it accelerates analysis, reduces toil, and improves consistency—helping teams identify root causes and prevent recurrence. Beyond post-incident response, this work establishes a reusable foundation for standardizing and scaling AI-assisted operational workflows across LiveOps, enabling teams to adopt intelligent automation while maintaining human oversight.

sessions.t: AI-First SecOps: The Future of Cloud Security on AWS​ (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
sessions.a: Security operations are entering a new era where analysts give intent, agents do the heavy lifting, and humans stay in control. Join Splunk for a look at the latest in AI-first security and agentic SecOps for AWS-centered teams. We’ll explore how cloud-native telemetry, federated investigation, streaming detections, AI-guided triage, and human-approved response can help SOC teams move from finding to action faster. See what’s next for integrated security operations on AWS, with a preview of emerging capabilities designed to reduce friction, accelerate detection, and strengthen resilience.​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AI flight plan: How British Airways’ parent builds and measures AI ROI (sponsored by NTT DATA)
sessions.a: British Airways’ parent, International Airlines Group (IAG), has moved rapidly from AI experimentation to production deployments delivering measurable results. This session explores how IAG and its partner NTT DATA assess AI opportunities by giving business units ownership of value realization, build momentum by prioritizing high-impact use cases, and operationalize AI through scalable technology, operating models, governance and change management. Attendees will learn how to connect AI strategy to top- and bottom-line impact through real-world examples, including procurement optimization, contract leakage detection and citizen-developed agents that accelerate safe, responsible AI adoption across the enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by NTT DATA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AI for Impact: Elevating human potential through inclusive innovation
sessions.a: Learn how California's Department of Developmental Services (DDS) is leveraging AWS to modernize legacy systems and unify data for half a million individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities across 21 regional centers and acute care hospitals. See how this aligns with HR.1 (the One Big Beautiful Bill Act) requirements for government modernization within CA Health and Human Services. Explore responsible AI agents with fairness scoring and bias detection that improve equitable service delivery. Discover how multi-agent architectures on Amazon Bedrock enable transparent, auditable decisions for vulnerable populations — a replicable blueprint for ethical AI at scale.

sessions.t: AI governance: from foundations to agentic speed
sessions.a: As organizations move from experimental AI to production agentic workloads, governance has to keep up without slowing teams down. In this session, learn how to build a governance foundation for AI using AWS Control Tower, AWS Config, AWS Organizations, and automatic evidence collection, then extend it to govern autonomous agents operating at machine speed. See how to implement preventive and detective controls for Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker, automate compliance evidence collection, and map controls to frameworks like ISO 42001. Leave with a practical approach to govern AI workloads from first model invocation to fully autonomous agents.

sessions.t: AI Governance: The Framework, The Pitfalls, The Playbook (sponsored by Vanta)
sessions.a: The AI revolution is upending organizations’ security and GRC programs. Shadow AI is exploding as employees adopt new agent harnesses, workflows, platforms, and plugins. Even sanctioned AI poses new challenges that don’t yet have standardized solutions. Meanwhile, developers are moving AI applications from experimentation to production, introducing new risks. This session will break down what AI Governance is all about, cover common concerns that it’s meant to resolve, and provide attendees with practical tips for solving some of their most pressing AI Governance challenges. What you’ll learn. What AI Governance entails, from practical policy to active protections. How to solve AI Governance concerns across different layers of the AI stack. This presentation is brought to you by Vanta, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AI is Breaking Data Security… And Fixing It (sponsored by Concentric AI)
sessions.a: AI is rapidly becoming one of the biggest drivers of productivity and innovation in the enterprise — and one of the fastest-growing sources of data security risk. As copilots, assistants, and public AI tools become integrated into daily work, sensitive data is flowing into systems that most security teams can’t fully see, understand, or control. The problem is that traditional data security controls were never built for this. In fact, many organizations were already struggling to operationalize data security before AI accelerated the challenge. The good news? AI isn’t just creating the problem — it’s also enabling a smarter, more effective way to solve it. Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how AI is reshaping data security — and how they can use that same technology to gain control, minimize exposure, and support safer AI adoption across the business. This presentation is brought to you by Concentric AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AI Is Getting Smarter. AI-Generated Code Isn’t Getting Safer. (sponsored by Veracode, Inc.)
sessions.a: AI-generated code is scaling fast, but its security performance is not keeping up. Across more than 100 models tested since 2023, the average security pass rate remains stuck at 56%, even as syntax performance approaches perfection. For security leaders, this is no longer a developer tooling discussion. It is a verification, release-control, and accountability issue. In this session, Veracode leaders unpack the findings from the 2026 GenAI Code Security Report and turn them into practical actions for secure software delivery at scale. Whether you’re a developer, security lead, or business decision-maker, this session will help you navigate the real-world security implications of GenAI in your development workflow. This presentation is brought to you by Veracode, Inc., an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AI Meets Production: The New Reliability Playbook for Financial Services (sponsored by Traversal)
sessions.a: Financial services depend on software that needs to be available around the clock. When that software fails, the consequences can affect millions of customers and create regulatory, financial, and reputational risk. This panel brings together technology leaders from some of the world’s largest financial institutions across banking, payments, and investment management for a conversation moderated by Anish Agrawal, CEO & Cofounder of Traversal, the AI SRE helping diagnose, fix, and prevent incidents across complex enterprise environments. Together, they’ll discuss how AI is changing production reliability across financial services, where it’s already being used, the emerging role of AI SREs, what teams look for when evaluating new approaches, and what it takes to deploy AI safely in highly regulated environments. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AIOPs for cloud data infrastructure (sponsored by NetApp)
sessions.a: Cloud data infrastructure rarely stays optimal — workloads change, configurations drift, and data infrastructure expertise is scarce. AIOps applies AI-powered, agentic automation to cloud data storage operations: continuously assessing the environment, analyzing it against workload-specific best practices, recommending fixes, and applying them at the level of autonomy you choose. In this lightning talk, we’ll explore how NetApp Workload Factory does all this while providing customers with right-sized cost, on-target performance, stronger resilience and protection — without the need for deep data infrastructure expertise, and while always staying in control. This presentation is brought to you by NetApp, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AIOps for SAP on AWS: Proactive Log Intelligence with Amazon Bedrock Agents
sessions.a: SAP operations teams spend hours sifting through thousands of log lines to diagnose outages, often only after business impact has occurred. In this workshop, learn how to implement AI-powered operations for SAP workloads on AWS, whether customer-managed or RISE with SAP. Ingest SAP system logs into Amazon CloudWatch using the CloudWatch Agent and SAP ECS LogServ, then apply Amazon Bedrock–powered agents for proactive analysis and reactive root-cause investigation. See how AWS DevOps Agent extends this with autonomous remediation. Leave with a deployable architecture, real customer examples, and guidance to get started in days.

sessions.t: AIOps strategy: foundations before firefighting
sessions.a: Most teams turn on AI-driven operations before deciding what they actually want it to handle, investment is racing ahead of maturity. This chalk talk works through an AIOps strategy at the whiteboard, using real support-case patterns showing that most critical failures are catchable before they reach production. We map the two halves that teams miss: using AI to run operations and the operational foundations that let AI scale safely, such as cost, security, and organizational readiness. We discuss what to automate, what stays human, and where agents earn autonomy. Leave with a foundational framework and a maturity checklist for your team.

sessions.a: Amazon Quick brings AI-powered analytics, automation, and research into a single workspace. sessions.a: Embed FinOps as an operational discipline using AI-powered cost optimization. This hands-on workshop demonstrates how to shift left on cloud financial management by integrating cost discipline throughout development. Explore AWS services for automated optimizations, rightsizing, and savings plans. Gain experience with AI/ML and container workload cost allocation, multi-cloud reporting, and AI-powered spend analysis. Implement automated strategies using real workload data. Laptop required
