sessions.t: AI-Powered Profitability: How Partners Are Winning with AWS
sessions.a: AI is reshaping partner economics. Hear from AWS VP Julia Chen about how to build a profitable AI-first business. This session covers the evolution of AWS Partner Programs, from transactional resell to outcome-driven partnerships, and reveals which programs, incentives, enablement, and tools deliver the highest ROI. Discover how AI-powered differentiation lowers your cost of sales, attracts high-value customers, deepens relationships, and enables innovation at scale. You'll leave with insights about where to invest and pathways for growth.

sessions.t: AI Spreadsheets and the Modern Data Stack: An AWS Story (sponsored by Row Zero)
sessions.a: AWS relies on spreadsheets for planning, forecasting, business intelligence, and self service analytics. To improve self-serve data analysis, AWS rolled out Row Zero, a cloud-based AI spreadsheet that can open billion row datasets, connect directly to data warehouses, and provide enterprise grade security controls. This session covers how AWS solved their legacy spreadsheet problems that are constrained by the compute and memory resources of employee laptops and a 1 million row limit. By adopting Row Zero, business users can derive insights and have secure access to governed data in Amazon S3, Redshift, or Athena at massive scale. This presentation is brought to you by Row Zero, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AI Systems Performance Engineering on AWS: A practitioner's deep dive
sessions.a: Extracting useful throughput from GPU clusters is a discipline: profile kernels, tune collectives, feed the GPUs, and survive the failures that compound with scale. In this workshop, you walk the full stack on Slurm-managed NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances — compute, network, and storage; the ML software stack from drivers to distributed frameworks — and stand up the observability that ties them together, from GPU, EFA, and Lustre counters to training throughput and MFU. At each layer: measure, attribute, fix with the tool that sees inside. Leave with dashboards you built yourself and a goodput methodology for your training clusters.

sessions.t: AI Systems Performance Engineering on AWS: A practitioner's deep dive
sessions.a: Extracting useful throughput from GPU clusters is a discipline: profile kernels, tune collectives, feed the GPUs, and survive the failures that compound with scale. In this workshop, you walk the full stack on Slurm-managed NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances — compute, network, and storage; the ML software stack from drivers to distributed frameworks — and stand up the observability that ties them together, from GPU, EFA, and Lustre counters to training throughput and MFU. At each layer: measure, attribute, fix with the tool that sees inside. Leave with dashboards you built yourself and a goodput methodology for your training clusters.

sessions.t: AI That Answers: Customer Experiences Reimagined with Amazon Connect (sponsored by PwC)
sessions.a: Join PwC and four leading clients across industries to hear real examples of how Amazon Connect is transforming customer experience and delivering business outcomes. This session showcases cutting-edge omnichannel solutions across voice, chat, and messaging, along with agentic AI capabilities driving automation in areas like order management and real-time updates. Hear how organizations are deploying next-generation, AI-powered voice solutions in production, with new innovations continuing to emerge. Discover how these advancements deliver measurable business value, backed by PwC's outcome-based approach that ties technology investment directly to efficiency gains and improved customer and business performance. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AI Threat Readiness: Securing AWS Workloads at Machine Speed (sponsored by Wiz)
sessions.a: As AI accelerates development in the cloud, it’s also increasingly expanding the cloud attack surface. With autonomous agents accelerating both software deployment and vulnerability exploitation, traditional security workflows can no longer keep pace. Organizations need a new operating model for AI Threat Readiness inside high-velocity AWS environments that builds agentic trust without slowing innovation. This session explores how combining full AWS visibility with agentic workflows, including Wiz Red, Green, and Blue Agents, transforms reactive cloud security into proactive, machine-speed defense across Amazon Bedrock, containers, and serverless architectures. This presentation is brought to you by Wiz, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AI Transformation: Redesigning How Work Gets Done (sponsored by Lucid Software)
sessions.a: Every major technology shift starts the same way. We use new technology to do the old thing. Early factories replaced steam engines with electric motors, but real transformation came when they redesigned the factory around what electricity made possible. We’re doing the same thing with AI. AI transformation isn’t about adding agents to existing workflows. It’s about redesigning how work gets done. That starts with context. In this session, we’ll show how teams can make work visible, give humans and AI a shared understanding of it, redesign workflows around agents, and turn that understanding into action. This presentation is brought to you by Lucid Software, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: AI workloads from cloud to edge: Choosing the right hybrid deployment
sessions.a: Organizations are running AI workloads, including training, inference, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, across an expanding set of environments, from AWS Regions to AWS Local Zones, AWS Outposts, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS AI Factories. The right deployment option depends on latency, data sovereignty, compute density, and scale. Explore how customers deploy GPU-accelerated AI across the full hybrid spectrum: G7e instances for edge inference, NVIDIA GPU-based and AWS Trainium-powered instances on Local Zones, purpose-built AWS AI Factories for large-scale training and model serving, and edge deployments for real-time applications like robotics. Hear how customers navigate these decisions and learn architectural patterns for placing AI workloads where your data lives, without compromising performance or compliance.

sessions.t: AI Writes the Code. Who Reviews the Reviewer?
sessions.a: AI coding assistants now write, refactor, and even review code at scale but who's actually accountable when something breaks in production? This session explores how AI has reshaped the code review process: faster first-pass reviews, AI-generated suggestions, and agentic tools running directly in CI/CD pipelines. We'll examine where AI genuinely improves review quality, where it creates false confidence, and why human judgment remains the deciding factor. You'll leave with a practical framework for combining AI speed with human accountability in your own review process.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to advanced team models in an agentic world
sessions.a: You built multi-skilled teams for cloud. That shape does not absorb agents. Cheaper execution does not remove work, it relocates it into judgment, verification, and spotting confidently wrong answers. The question we want answered is not about reporting lines, it is "does this new world include me?" The twenty-year senior, the junior who cannot get in, the manager of a smaller team: each needs a different answer. Four operating models return, from today's anti-pattern to the hourglass, with a first-person account of what works inside Amazon and what doesn't. The answer is yes, but the entry requirement has changed.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to escaping proof-of-concept purgatory
sessions.a: Drawing on 1,000+ customer conversations about building competitive advantage with data and AI, Rahul Pathak, VP of AWS Data & AI GTM, shares what separates organizations getting real value from agentic AI from those stuck in pilots. When everyone has the same models, your data is the only differentiator. Rahul covers how to set goals worth deploying against, why working backwards from outcomes matters, why cross-functional teams outperform centralized AI functions, what governance must exist before agents reach production, not after, and how to create urgency without a mandate. Field notes from 1,000+ rooms, and a playbook for Monday morning.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to how AI is changing Amazon’s ways of working
sessions.a: AI is changing how Amazon hires, builds, manages, and deploys teams across every function to innovate and deliver on behalf of customers. This session shares Amazon's emerging framework: the mental models fueling transformation, a state model for understanding where teams are on the AI journey, and real case studies of teams that have crossed from AI-enhanced to AI-native and beyond. We'll walk through the implications, share the questions we're still wrestling with, and offer practical recommendations for leaders navigating the same transition. First-person data from an organization at scale, shared with candor.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to how Amazon built its data foundation for agents
sessions.a: Organizations racing to put AI agents on top of their data keep hitting the same walls: security, privacy, scale, and data they can't trust. In this session, Anas Fattahi (VP, Amazon Business Data Technologies) and G2 Krishnamoorthy (VP, AWS Databases) share how years of foundational investment positioned Amazon to move quickly when the agentic AI moment arrived, and where the hard problems still live. You'll hear which bets paid off, what's working now, what they're still building, and how to inspect your own setup against what they've learned.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to modernizing systems for AI, with AI
sessions.a: Every enterprise faces the same sequencing problem: "Before we can deploy AI, we need to fix our legacy systems." This is technology's most expensive false binary. Organizations that made real progress rejected that sequence. They use AI to understand undocumented code, decompose monoliths, and rebuild the very systems blocking deployment. One airline uses AI to comprehend reservation logic only three people understand. Another enterprise uses agents to reverse-engineer decades of business rules into microservices. The recursive unlock: the technology you want to deploy removes what blocks it. This session covers the funding, sequencing, and organizational decisions that make it work.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to reimagining complex business processes with agents
sessions.a: Most enterprises use AI as an assistant, automating individual tasks for incremental 20% gains. The leaders unlocking profound productivity gains are doing something different: reimagining entire business processes from the outcome backward, so every step hands forward context, confidence, and decision authority, not just data. This session shows what it takes to transform your most strategic operations with agentic AI and scale them, then Thomson Reuters walks through the lessons of rebuilding its M&A process end-to-end. You leave knowing which processes to reimagine and how to move them into production, where value compounds.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to scaling AI adoption without losing control
sessions.a: I gave the organization AI tools — why did adoption stall? Most enterprises equip teams with AI and expect transformation to follow. It doesn't. Amazon scaled agentic AI to thousands of production deployments not by mandate, but by investing in what surrounds the model: governance that guards what truly matters — customer trust, privacy, security, and cost — while loosening its grip everywhere else, a culture where experimentation and oversight coexist, and upskilling that turns casual prompters into confident builders. This session names the structural bets that move adoption, the debts you're quietly acquiring, and why losing control isn't the failure — over-constraining is.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to security at the speed of AI, powered by Mythos
sessions.a: As AI capabilities advance, so do the capabilities of those who attack software. The pace of modern development has outgrown point-in-time security reviews, leaving vulnerabilities exploitable longer than any leader should accept. Periodic snapshots cannot keep up when code changes constantly, so security has to become continuous, evaluating posture as the code itself evolves. Amazon used frontier-model capabilities, through Mythos, to make security continuous at its own scale, finding issues and guiding builders to fix them as they work. This session explores that shift. Senior leaders will learn how to secure their organizations at AI speed.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to the AI speed trap
sessions.a: Your developers are faster with AI. Your organization isn't. AI tools accelerate individual teams, but organizational outcomes depend on what happens between teams: coordination, dependencies, and end-to-end value streams that extend far beyond code. Most productivity metrics miss this entirely because they stop at the team boundary. In this session, we present real patterns from startups, scaleups, digital natives, and large organizations, introduce measurement frameworks that capture what matters at the organizational level, and share practical approaches for turning team-level acceleration into outcomes your customers will notice.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to the AI you haven't seen yet
sessions.a: Most AI strategy is built for the AI leaders can see. The models in production today are the constrained ones, gated by capacity and cost, and that gate is lifting. When it lifts, a dozen breakthrough applications becomes a million, and AI systems get as cheap and as common as a website. Progress has stopped being predictable too: capability arrives in step changes that can obsolete a year of work in a quarter. This session asks what you would build if AI were free and never made a mistake, and how to tell a durable bet from a disposable one.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to the hardest investment decision in AI
sessions.a: Fund the platform or fund the use case? Demand proof before investing or invest to generate the proof? Scale the winner or explore the next opportunity? These decisions determine whether AI compounds or stalls, and they require the CIO and CFO to act together. Two former operators share how the best CIO-CFO pairs align on what to fund, what to kill, and what "good enough evidence" looks like when certainty isn't available. You leave with the approach that replaces "requestor and approver" with co-ownership, and the questions every pair should answer before their next AI investment.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to what separates AI leaders from the rest
sessions.a: In early 2026, the Reimagine research program interviewed senior technology leaders under conditions of candor: off-the-record, non-attributable, no marketing follow-up. What they said contradicts the prevailing conference narrative. Nobody is running agents autonomously, not one. The most advanced organizations are carrying the most technical debt. The AI generating real value looks nothing like the demos. This session synthesizes the patterns that emerged when executives stopped performing confidence and started sharing reality.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to what your board must know about AI (and shouldn't)
sessions.a: Your board is asking about AI — and that's a good thing. Their curiosity is the opening you need. But that attention can create more heat than light: dashboards and benchmarks that generate activity without moving the organization forward. The real opportunity is to channel that interest — show AI's true potential and turn your board into a genuine partner for a transformation that needs their conviction to succeed. In this session, assess where your board sits, understand the personas at play, and learn proven tactics to move them from curiosity to conviction.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to why agentic AI just made your data problem urgent
sessions.a: The data problem you tolerated for years just became an emergency. Agents do not politely work around missing metadata. They guess confidently, and you find out three weeks later. Enterprises assumed they could solve AI first and data second. They can't. You get the framework that separates compounding value from programs that never finish. AWS Marketing built an agentic system over thousands of warehouse tables. It worked. Its first output: an inventory of every undocumented decision in the warehouse. That exposure was worth more than the answers. You leave knowing what to fix first, and why analytical demand climbs.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to why your AI economics are wrong
sessions.a: Most AI business cases use ROI frameworks built for deterministic systems, measuring cost avoidance while missing the metrics that predict success. The gap between pilot and production economics is 10-50x, and most finance teams still model AI as capital expense rather than variable. This session names the three assumptions that guarantee your AI business case is wrong, and the costs that blindside CFOs in production. It presents the financial model Amazon uses internally to forecast AI operating expenditure. You leave knowing which line items to remove from your next business case, and which to add that nobody tracks yet.

sessions.t: A leader's guide to why your AI governance can't keep up
sessions.a: Your governance model is built of deterministic applications, platforms, and infrastructure. The AI of your organization is reasoning, problem solving, and acting with agency. The governance model you need requires your traditional technology controls but also needs the controls, auditability, and observability for the things you are worried about when your AI acts more like humans than the prescriptive hard coded software we are used to. Monitoring not just the applications but the decisions it takes and how your workforce is interacting with it.

sessions.t: Align cost with value through outcome-based pricing in AWS Marketplace
sessions.a: Customers increasingly expect software to be priced in terms of value delivered, paying only for results like resolved tickets or documents processed not API calls or compute hours or seats. In this Code Talk, learn how to implement outcome-based pricing and see live examples of metering and billing in AWS Marketplace. Follow along as we go from prototype to published listing, billing per resolved ticket, processed document, or any measurable result you choose.

sessions.t: Allianz: Scaling product reach with agentic commerce across channels
sessions.a: Customers increasingly start product discovery inside the AI assistants they use daily, and companies that aren't present miss them entirely. Learn how Allianz built a unified agentic-commerce backend on Amazon Bedrock, grounded in open standards. The same backend powers its own conversational AI across web and mobile and extends the same experience into third-party AI platforms through one AI gateway. We cover the agentic architecture and how shared MCP servers for corporate identity, GDPR compliance, consent, and authentication free business teams to focus on their core services. Customers discover products, get non-binding quotes, and connect to agencies across every channel.

sessions.t: Ally Financial’s Journey: Modernizing Data Processing on AWS (sponsored by Impetus Technologies Inc)
sessions.a: Discover how Ally Financial modernized FICO data processing with a scalable Snowflake-based platform on AWS. Built on Amazon S3, AWS Glue, AWS Lambda, and other AWS services, the solution supports real-time and batch ingestion at scale—enabling 10x faster processing and near-real-time data availability for mission-critical analytics use cases. The platform also enabled unified observability, helping Ally Financial’s teams detect and resolve issues faster while strengthening platform reliability and operational stability significantly. This presentation is brought to you by Impetus Technologies Inc, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Amazon API Gateway: Migration strategies and agent-ready APIs
sessions.a: Unlock the full potential of Amazon API Gateway for modern workloads. In this chalk talk, we discuss migration strategies from legacy API platforms using OpenAPI extensions, schema validation, and Infrastructure as Code. Then we tackle the agentic era: how do you design APIs that AI agents can discover, authenticate against, and call reliably? We explore custom authorizers, mutual TLS, and exposing your endpoints as MCP-compatible tool definitions. Bring your questions—we'll work through them on the whiteboard.

sessions.t: Amazon Aurora architecture patterns for open table format analytics
sessions.a: Modern analytics architectures increasingly rely on open table formats like Apache Iceberg but combining operational and analytical data remains complex. This session explores emerging patterns for bridging Amazon Aurora with open table format analytics. Learn architectural patterns for bidirectional data flow between databases and data lakes. Topics include design patterns for analytical workloads, performance optimization and reverse ETL, and deep dives into maintaining transactional consistency when streaming database changes to Amazon S3 Tables, delivery guarantees, and type mapping.

sessions.t: Amazon Aurora DSQL: A developer's perspective
sessions.a: In this live coding session, we'll show you how to work with Amazon Aurora DSQL from a developer's perspective. We'll develop a sample application to highlight some of the ways developing for Aurora DSQL is different than PostgreSQL. We'll cover authentication and connection management, optimistic concurrency transaction patterns, primary key selection, analyzing query performance, and best practices.

sessions.t: Amazon Aurora HA and DR design patterns for global resilience
sessions.a: Amazon Aurora is a serverless relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and DSQL. Aurora provides managed high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) capabilities in and across AWS Regions. In this session, explore the Aurora HA and DR capabilities and discover design patterns that enable the development of resilient applications. Learn how to establish in-Region and cross-Region HA and DR using Aurora features including Multi-AZ deployments and Aurora Global Database, and how Aurora DSQL multi-Region clusters provides the highest level of availability and application resilience.

sessions.t: Amazon DocumentDB for expert practitioners
sessions.a: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fully managed database service for native document data model enterprise workloads. It removes the undifferentiated heavy lifting of operating a database so that teams can focus time on delivering value for customers. In this session, dive deep into the implementation details and trade-offs of features to improve compression and performance while lowering cost for various workloads.

sessions.t: Amazon DocumentDB for expert practitioners
sessions.a: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fully managed database service for native document data model enterprise workloads. It removes the undifferentiated heavy lifting of operating a database so that teams can focus time on delivering value for customers. In this session, dive deep into the implementation details and trade-offs of features to improve compression and performance while lowering cost for various workloads.

sessions.t: Amazon DynamoDB: How to build a foundational service
sessions.a: Whether to take a dependency or reimplement something are important decisions in any system architecture, affecting performance, durability, and availability. Amazon DynamoDB serves millions of customers while also underpinning many AWS services, a dual role that forces rigorous decisions about dependencies, failure isolation, and multi-Region architecture. In this session, the DynamoDB engineering team walks through how those constraints shape architectural choices, including when DynamoDB uses DynamoDB to implement itself. The session presents a structured framework for dependency analysis, covering multi-zone and multi-Region tradeoffs, applicable to any system you build and operate, to help identify design risks before they become failures.

sessions.t: Amazon EC2: New silicon, new instances, new possibilities
sessions.a: Amazon EC2 continues to push the boundaries of cloud compute. Join this session to explore the latest innovations — from new AWS Graviton processors to the newest Intel, AMD, and Mac instances built for demanding workloads. Hear how customers are using EC2 to accelerate application development, high-performance computing, and AI inference on the CPU. Learn how the AWS Nitro System delivers strong isolation and performance, and leave with practical guidance to match the right EC2 instance to your workload.

sessions.t: Amazon EKS incident response and remediation with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.a: When an incident hits, engineers lose time pivoting between kubectl, metrics, logs, and traces to find root cause. In this builder session, you'll drive the AWS DevOps Agent through a production-realistic incident end to end: detect the anomaly from observability signals, correlate metrics, logs, and traces to a root cause, and execute automated remediation with a human-in-the-loop gate. You'll wire the observability inputs the agent consumes, review its diagnosis journal, and validate recovery. Leave with a repeatable detect-diagnose-remediate-verify pattern and a permission-scoped remediation playbook you can adapt to your own clusters.

sessions.t: Amazon EKS incident response and remediation with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.a: When an incident hits, engineers lose time pivoting between kubectl, metrics, logs, and traces to find root cause. In this builder session, you'll drive the AWS DevOps Agent through a production-realistic incident end to end: detect the anomaly from observability signals, correlate metrics, logs, and traces to a root cause, and execute automated remediation with a human-in-the-loop gate. You'll wire the observability inputs the agent consumes, review its diagnosis journal, and validate recovery. Leave with a repeatable detect-diagnose-remediate-verify pattern and a permission-scoped remediation playbook you can adapt to your own clusters.

sessions.t: Amazon EKS: Infrastructure as code, GitOps, or CI/CD
sessions.a: Explore diverse architectures for deploying workloads including agents on Amazon EKS. Learn about secure software supply chain automation options including CI/CD pipelines, IaC (using Terraform & CDK), and GitOps patterns with Argo CD. Discover how Amazon EKS Capabilities, a suite of fully-managed platform features for deployments and resource orchestration eliminate operational overhead for building on Kubernetes. You will understand how these approaches complement each other from developer, architect, and operator perspectives. Get insights on selecting the right deployment strategy based on team structure and skill sets, and learn how to effectively combine DevOps and GitOps patterns to match your needs.

sessions.t: Amazon EKS: Infrastructure as code, GitOps, or CI/CD
sessions.a: Explore diverse architectures for deploying workloads including agents on Amazon EKS. Learn about secure software supply chain automation options including CI/CD pipelines, IaC (using Terraform & CDK), and GitOps patterns with Argo CD. Discover how Amazon EKS Capabilities, a suite of fully-managed platform features for deployments and resource orchestration eliminate operational overhead for building on Kubernetes. You will understand how these approaches complement each other from developer, architect, and operator perspectives. Get insights on selecting the right deployment strategy based on team structure and skill sets, and learn how to effectively combine DevOps and GitOps patterns to match your needs.

sessions.t: Amazon EVS: How to deploy & operate your VMware stack in the cloud
sessions.a: What if you could rapidly migrate your VMware-based workloads to the cloud without giving up control over how you build, configure, and operate your environment? Amazon EVS lets you run the latest VMware Cloud Foundation software within your Amazon VPC using EC2 bare-metal instances. Use the tools and processes your team already knows, now backed by AWS scale and flexibility. Retain control of your virtualization stack, from networking and storage to disaster recovery. We'll walk through deployment workflows and integration patterns with AWS Partners and native AWS services. Hear lessons from a customer who fast-tracked their migration with EVS.

sessions.t: Amazon Leo: Connectivity Beyond the Reach of Existing Networks (sponsored by Amazon Leo)
sessions.a: Amazon Leo is building a constellation of over 3,200 low Earth orbit satellites to deliver fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities worldwide. In this session, learn how Leo's advanced satellite technology, purpose-built customer antennas, and deep integration with AWS will extend reliable connectivity to enterprises, governments, and individuals — wherever they are. Walk away with a clear understanding of Leo's architecture, use cases, and how it complements existing network infrastructure to close the global digital divide. This presentation is brought to you by Amazon Leo, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Amazon Linux: Securing and scaling your workloads on AWS
sessions.a: Amazon Linux powers the majority of workloads on AWS, from containers and AI/ML to enterprise applications and managed services. In this session, we introduce Amazon Linux 2027 (AL2027), cover its security enhancements, optimizations, and key features. Learn how AL2027 addresses the needs of modern AI/ML and container workloads, and what the roadmap means for your infrastructure planning. Whether you are planning a migration or evaluating your OS strategy, this session is for you.

sessions.t: Amazon S3 cost optimization: when to tier, and when not to
sessions.a: Moving data to a colder storage class is the obvious way to cut Amazon S3 costs, but sometimes it makes your bill go up. Learn about the full cost model behind storage-class decisions: transition requests, minimum billable object sizes, per-object overhead, minimum durations, and retrieval. See why small objects, high-churn datasets, and request-heavy workloads are frequently cheaper left where they are, and how to spot them. Using S3 Storage Lens, S3 Inventory, and S3 Metadata, diagnose where you're spending and leave with clear guidance on when to tier, when to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and when to do nothing.

sessions.t: Amazon S3 performance: Architecture, design, and optimization
sessions.a: Go behind the scenes of Amazon S3 performance architecture while learning practical optimization strategies for today's most demanding workloads. Explore how internal systems for S3 manage massive throughput, handle concurrent requests, and balance loads across its distributed infrastructure. From request routing and partitioning strategies to multipart transfers and byte-range fetches, understand the technical foundations that power real-time analytics, AI/ML training, and high-frequency data pipelines. Then see how S3 Express One Zone extends these capabilities with consistent single-digit millisecond latency through directory buckets and compute co-location. Walk away with patterns to maximize performance at every tier.

sessions.t: Amazon S3 security and access control best practices
sessions.a: As organizations consolidate critical data in Amazon S3 across accounts, teams, and workloads, security and access control decisions multiply. Which identity model scales without becoming brittle? Where do you enforce encryption policy? How do you detect misconfigurations? This session walks you through a layered security framework for S3: perimeter controls that prevent unintended public exposure, identity and attribute-based access that scales across organizational boundaries, encryption options that satisfy compliance without adding operational friction, and monitoring that continuously validates your posture. You will learn how these layers compose into a cohesive strategy and which controls matter most as your environment grows.

sessions.t: Amazon S3 security: Implementing access controls, policies & audits
sessions.a: Amazon S3 provides security settings and granular access controls to suit virtually any workload. In this workshop, learn how to manage access and define scalable user and resource-based policies using Amazon S3 access management tools. Learn techniques for monitoring and auditing data to find out who is accessing what data, from where, and when. Through practical scenarios, learn how to apply various S3 security tools and capabilities to meet diverse security requirements. Gain expertise in implementing robust security measures, from basic access controls to advanced audit systems, suitable for any workload complexity. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

sessions.t: Amazon S3 security: Implementing access controls, policies & audits
sessions.a: Amazon S3 provides security settings and granular access controls to suit virtually any workload. In this workshop, learn how to manage access and define scalable user and resource-based policies using Amazon S3 access management tools. Learn techniques for monitoring and auditing data to find out who is accessing what data, from where, and when. Through practical scenarios, learn how to apply various S3 security tools and capabilities to meet diverse security requirements. Gain expertise in implementing robust security measures, from basic access controls to advanced audit systems, suitable for any workload complexity. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

sessions.t: Ambient accessibility: Architecting real-time ASL on a Wearable
sessions.a: What if a DHH person could wear a device and get sign language translation of every conversation around them in under a second? We architect a pipeline that ingests Amazon Bee's ambient audio, transcribes it, transforms English to ASL grammar, generates avatar animations, and streams signed video back. That one-second constraint drives every architectural tradeoff, from whether translation stages run on-device for speed or in the cloud for accuracy, to whether we sign full sentences or start mid-utterance with partial context. We explore the edge-cloud splits and pipeline staging that make sub-second delivery feasible.

sessions.t: Analyze your portfolio, prioritize what to fix, and transform it
sessions.a: You know your portfolio needs modernization, but which apps go first, and based on what criteria? In this workshop, you'll run the full analyze-prioritize-transform cycle end to end. Using AWS Transform's Agentic Readiness Analysis and Modernization Analysis, you'll evaluate applications from two angles: whether agents can safely reach your logic (API exposure, identity, state, guardrails, observability) and how cloud-native mature your architecture is (compute, data, security, operations). You'll interpret scores, scale across a portfolio with the orchestrator, then close the loop by triggering a containerization transformation on the app that needs it most. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Analyze your portfolio, prioritize what to fix, and transform it
sessions.a: You know your portfolio needs modernization, but which apps go first, and based on what criteria? In this workshop, you'll run the full analyze-prioritize-transform cycle end to end. Using AWS Transform's Agentic Readiness Analysis and Modernization Analysis, you'll evaluate applications from two angles: whether agents can safely reach your logic (API exposure, identity, state, guardrails, observability) and how cloud-native mature your architecture is (compute, data, security, operations). You'll interpret scores, scale across a portfolio with the orchestrator, then close the loop by triggering a containerization transformation on the app that needs it most. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Analyze your telemetry data with natural-language queries
sessions.a: During high-severity incidents, dependency on a single engineer who knows the query language creates critical bottlenecks. This code talk explores the architecture and design trade-offs behind a natural-language query workflow that translates plain-language questions into executable queries across metrics, logs, and traces. Live coding demonstrates how to integrate AI-powered query capabilities, correlate telemetry signals from a unified interface, and surface root-cause insights without writing query syntax. You'll see the underlying prompt construction, query translation patterns, and signal correlation strategies that drive reliable observability workflows in production environments.

sessions.t: An Epic Tale: Hyperscale Storage & Compute for the Fortnite Ecosystem
sessions.a: The metaverse will not be built by one studio. It will be built by thousands of teams shipping petabytes of content, running millions of build and render jobs across regions every day. The engineers behind Lore, Epic's distributed version control system for massive binary repositories, and Overmind, a multi-region ephemeral compute orchestrator, reveal the AWS architecture that makes it possible: self-managed scheduling on EC2, S3/DynamoDB/Keyspaces/Aurora for the data plane, EKS-hosted control planes running durable workflows, and MSK for replayable event streams. Leave with a concrete reference architecture and lessons on tenant isolation, regional sovereignty, and global platform scale.

sessions.t: An insider’s look into architecture choices for Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.a: To overcome the performance and scale limitations of relational databases, AWS built Amazon DynamoDB to deliver consistent single-digit millisecond performance at any scale for the most demanding applications on the planet. In this session, learn about the architecture choices for Amazon DynamoDB. Gain a better understanding of when to use DynamoDB and why DynamoDB is used by over one million AWS customers, and powers hundreds of applications that exceed half a million requests per second. Leave with a new perspective on how to design your own applications.

sessions.t: Aon: Turning raw exposure data into faster underwriting
sessions.a: Insurers and brokers process thousands of Statements of Values annually, complex unstructured documents that require manual extraction and validation and delay quoting and bind decisions. In this lightning talk, learn how Aon built an AI-powered exposure data ingestion platform on Amazon Bedrock using Anthropic Claude, AWS Lambda, and Amazon S3. See how the platform transforms unstructured data into standardized, risk-ready information with improved address quality, geocoding precision, and hazard identification, reducing document processing from days to minutes and feeding higher-quality inputs to catastrophe models.

sessions.t: Apache Iceberg V3 on AWS: Lower Costs, Better Lakehouse Performance
sessions.a: Apache Iceberg V3 is now production-ready, and adopting deletion vectors, row lineage, and new data types across your lakehouse requires careful planning. In this session, explore implementation patterns using Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, Amazon Athena, and Amazon S3 Tables. Learn when deletion vectors outperform copy-on-write, how row lineage enables compliance without extra pipelines, and how V3 incremental processing cuts batch costs. Leave with a practical migration strategy for your Iceberg upgrade.

sessions.t: Apache Iceberg V4: Fast commits, smart metadata, and portable tables
sessions.a: Apache Iceberg V4 is the biggest architectural evolution of the format, shifting from batch-first to real-time ready. Explore how single-file commits eliminate metadata bottlenecks for streaming ingestion, how Parquet-based metadata and redesigned content statistics accelerate query planning, and how relative paths make tables portable across regions and clouds without costly rewrites. We'll walk through what's changing under the hood and what it means for the way you design and operate lakehouses. Discover how V4 delivers the speed and flexibility modern lakehouses demand.

sessions.t: Aperf: An all-in-one tool for performance data collection and analysis
sessions.a: Aperf is an open-source project created by AWS to accelerate the performance debugging process by enabling experienced users to deep dive into extensive data and less experienced users to identify issues without specialized knowledge. During this session, we'll present its key features and run a demo showing the analysis workflow, from installation, data collection, and then analysis. Finally, we'll open the conversation to collect feedback and feature requests from the audience.

During this session, we'll present its key features and run a demo showing the analysis workflow, from installation, data collection, and then analysis. sessions.t: API Gateway unleashed
sessions.a: Gain essential hands-on skills to create, deploy, and manage APIs efficiently with Amazon API Gateway. Learn message transformation, request validation, and security best practices. Master deploying APIs using Infrastructure as Code and integrating with AWS serverless services. Dive into monitoring and debugging to ensure your APIs perform optimally, and explore building and testing WebSocket backends. Whether you're creating REST APIs or real-time communication layers, this workshop equips you with the knowledge to streamline application development and enhance API management. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Application Archeology: Digging up lost knowledge with Kiro
sessions.a: Every organization bleeds knowledge when people leave. For mission-driven teams, a single departure can erase years of context from codebases, runbooks, and integrations. In this builder session, use Kiro — AWS's AI-powered development environment — to reverse that loss. Configure steering files that encode your team's conventions, connect MCP servers to pull context from docs and APIs, and deploy subagents that generate living architecture diagrams and knowledge bases as your code evolves. Walk away with a Kiro workspace that turns any new hire into a productive contributor from day one — no more tribal knowledge walking out the door.

sessions.t: Apply Amazon's frontier team playbook to your organization
sessions.a: AI coding agents sped up code generation, but not how fast it reaches customers. Teams seeing 4.5x to 10x gains aren't just adopting tools. They've redesigned how they work. In this chalk talk, learn what these "frontier teams" do differently: investing in agent context and steering files, making intent explicit before code is written, feeding agents well-scoped work instead of babysitting them, shifting testing left so agents self-correct before they reach the pipeline. We'll unpack real examples from teams across Amazon and talk through how to run your own pilot. Bring your questions about making AI work in your organization.

sessions.t: Applying the Well-Architected Framework to AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
sessions.a: AWS Outposts and Local Zones bring cloud closer to your users and data but introduce architectural decisions that do not exist in a purely cloud-native model. How do you design for resilience when infrastructure sits in your facility? What does security and cost optimization look like across hybrid topologies? In this chalk talk, we walk through the Well-Architected Framework pillar by pillar, exploring how each applies and where it bends at the edge. Bring your toughest design questions. We will draw out real-world patterns, discuss trade-offs, and build a practical mental model for well-architected hybrid solutions.

sessions.t: A practical guide to Amazon S3 data protection
sessions.a: Learn step-by-step methods to protect your critical Amazon S3 data against accidental deletion, ransomware, and corruption, even at billion-object and petabyte scale. This chalk talk provides hands-on guidance for implementing essential safeguards through S3 Versioning, Replication, Object Lock, and Resource Control Policy guardrails, plus techniques for recovering from unwanted changes across large datasets. We also cover how GuardDuty Malware Protection for AWS Backup lets you verify data is malware-free before restoring. Whether you’re meeting compliance requirements or ensuring business continuity, leave with actionable steps from basic backup policies to advanced immutability and malware-scanning controls.

sessions.t: A practical guide to Apache Iceberg migration on AWS
sessions.a: Many organizations want to adopt Apache Iceberg but face a practical challenge: how do you migrate existing data lake tables — Hive-style, Apache Hudi, or Delta Lake — without disrupting production workloads? In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn and implement the full spectrum of migration techniques on AWS, from zero-copy in-place approaches to full data rewrites targeting both self-managed Iceberg tables in S3 and Amazon S3 Tables. Beyond the mechanics, you'll implement real-world migration strategies and learn how to choose among them based on downtime tolerance, writer constraints, and data volume. You'll leave with a repeatable playbook for migrating your data lake to Iceberg with minimal risk and zero data loss.

sessions.t: A practitioner’s guide to data for agentic AI
sessions.a: In this session, gain the skills needed to deploy end-to-end agentic AI applications using your most valuable data. This session focuses on data management using processes like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and provides concepts that apply to other methods of customizing agentic AI applications. Discover best practice architectures using AWS database services like Amazon Aurora, DynamoDB, and Neptune, along with analytical, data processing and streaming experiences found in SageMaker. Learn data lake, governance, and data quality concepts and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Bedrock Knowledge Bases, and other features tie solution components together.

sessions.t: A practitioner’s guide to migrating from 3rd-party CDN and WAF to AWS
sessions.a: Considering migrating from a third-party CDN/WAF provider to AWS services? In this chalk talk, we’ll walk through the migration phases together: defining success criteria, running low-risk proof of concepts, designing your target architecture with Amazon Route 53, Amazon CloudFront, AWS WAF, and edge compute, executing the DNS cutover, and managing post-migration operations. Most of this session is open discussion: you bring your questions and stories, and we’ll share what we’ve learned running these migrations in production.

sessions.t: Architect AI-powered analytics with Amazon Quick and Snowflake
sessions.a: As organizations adopt AI-powered analytics, they need architectures that connect BI and conversational AI experiences across their data platforms. Explore how Amazon Quick and Snowflake work together to solve this challenge. We'll diagram architectural patterns for connecting Snowflake as a data source, enabling BI dashboards, embedded analytics, and text-to-SQL through dataset Q&A so business users can query and visualize data using natural language. We'll also explore connecting Quick to Snowflake Cortex Agents via MCP for live, agentic workflows. Together we'll tackle real-world integration challenges including authentication, performance optimization, and governance. This session is ideal for architects and technical leaders looking to build AI-powered analytics across their data platforms.

sessions.t: Architect and optimize your VMware environment on Amazon EVS
sessions.a: Dive deep into the architectural decisions that shape a resilient, high-performing VMware environment on Amazon EVS. Explore VCF 9 support, Windows Server license-included entitlements, networking designs, storage configurations tuned for performance and cost, and operational patterns for backup, patching, and disaster recovery. Hear from a customer running production workloads on EVS and leave with actionable architectures tailored to your VMware workloads.

sessions.t: Architect for production AI: A decision framework that scales
sessions.a: Organizations deploying AI face a critical decision at every step. Which service handles which job, and will those decisions hold up as you scale? This chalk talk delivers an opinionated decision framework for choosing between Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and when to combine both for unified security, governance, and models that move between services without rearchitecting. We cover model access patterns (API, custom model import, marketplace), deployment trade-offs between self-managed and fully managed inference, and cost-performance optimization at production scale.

sessions.t: Architect for production AI: A decision framework that scales
sessions.a: Organizations deploying AI face a critical decision at every step. Which service handles which job, and will those decisions hold up as you scale? This chalk talk delivers an opinionated decision framework for choosing between Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and when to combine both for unified security, governance, and models that move between services without rearchitecting. We cover model access patterns (API, custom model import, marketplace), deployment trade-offs between self-managed and fully managed inference, and cost-performance optimization at production scale.

sessions.t: Architecting anti-piracy defenses for video streaming with Amazon CloudFront
sessions.a: Modern streaming demands instant revocation, concurrent stream limits, device-bound sessions, and per-user policy decisions at the edge. In this chalk talk, whiteboard the full decision space with us. We'll map the trade-offs between signed URLs, signed cookies, and emerging token approaches like Content Access Tokens (CAT) built on CBOR Web Tokens, then diagram the architecture patterns behind them: embedding custom claims and evaluating them in CloudFront Functions, using CloudFront KeyValueStore for real-time revocation without key rotation, and chaining tokens across HLS/DASH segments. Bring your hardest content protection scenarios - credential sharing, restreaming, geo abuse - and we'll work through them together at the board, leaving you with a framework for matching protection mechanisms to your security and business requirements.

sessions.t: Architecting Firewalls on AWS: A Layered Defense Strategy
sessions.a: Automated traffic now exceeds half the web. L7 attacks are getting smarter. A single firewall isn't enough. This chalk talk explores how AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall work together for layered protection. We cover deployment patterns for internet-facing apps, outbound controls, and workload segmentation, including TGW-attached firewall patterns. We dig into trade-offs: centralized vs. distributed inspection, cost vs. latency, and when each service carries the load alone vs. when you need both. Bring your architecture diagrams. We'll whiteboard protection that scales with your environment.

sessions.t: Architecting for digital sovereignty: Choosing your AWS hybrid cloud infrastructure
sessions.a: Digital sovereignty requirements vary widely across government, defense, healthcare, and financial services. In this session, we use real-world case studies to compare architectural differences across AWS Dedicated Local Zones, AWS Outposts within the AWS European Sovereign Cloud, and AWS Regions. We examine how data residency boundaries, network separation, operational controls, and cryptographic key management differ across these options. We then demonstrate how to configure account access, data residency controls, and network ingress/egress policies for strict versus moderate requirements, including how to detect and prevent non-permitted data flows between hybrid infrastructure, the parent Region, and on-premises environments.

sessions.t: Architecting for non-deterministic components
sessions.a: Our systems used to behave the same way every time. Now we give them judgment and agency, so they decide and act on their own, and the same inputs can produce different outcomes. Designing reliable architectures around that non-determinism comes down to three questions: where to enforce determinism around the model, when to verify behavior through automated evaluation and reasoning versus human judgment, and how to adapt the patterns (event flows, orchestration, automation) for components that don’t behave predictably. This session presents the design patterns for building systems that decide and act, while preserving the reliability your architecture depends on.

sessions.t: Architecting for resilience and data residency
sessions.a: Your data can't leave the jurisdiction, but your workload still has to survive a Region degradation. This chalk talk explores architecture patterns that address both resilience and data residency together. We break the challenge into practical layers: where data lives, how workloads recover, what isolation looks like, and how to maintain business continuity across geographic boundaries. We map each layer to AWS capabilities including Dedicated Local Zones, Outposts, and policy controls, then work through real scenarios together. Bring your architecture challenges and we will whiteboard design patterns and tradeoffs with you.

sessions.t: Architecting for six nines with multi-region hedging (sponsored by Capital One)
sessions.a: Traditional disaster recovery assumes you can afford a recovery window. At six nines, your entire annual downtime budget is 31 seconds, a single failover event can consume it all. In this session, learn how to eliminate recovery windows entirely and make regional impairments invisible to customers without operational intervention. Explore a decision framework for selecting multi-region topologies based on simultaneous failure tolerance, data consistency, and cost tradeoffs. See how cell-based architecture limits blast radius and continuous fault injection proves resilience before incidents occur. Walk away with a pattern selection model you can apply to your own mission-critical workloads to move beyond failover toward true continuous availability. This presentation is brought to you by Capital One, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Architecting vector-driven AI applications with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.a: Vector search is the engine behind intelligent AI, transforming data into meaning-driven insights that power smarter search, recommendations, and generative experiences. In this session, discover how to combine cost-optimized, fully elastic vector storage delivered by Amazon S3 Vectors with multimodal embedding models in Amazon Bedrock to extract and index text and image semantics at scale. Learn how to leverage S3 Vectors with popular AWS AI services to power AI-driven applications that can efficiently search through large vector datasets. Whether you’re building media search applications or search-enabled AI, you’ll learn how to optimize your use of S3 Vectors.

sessions.t: Architecting vector-driven AI applications with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.a: Vector search is the engine behind intelligent AI, transforming data into meaning-driven insights that power smarter search, recommendations, and generative experiences. In this session, discover how to combine cost-optimized, fully elastic vector storage delivered by Amazon S3 Vectors with multimodal embedding models in Amazon Bedrock to extract and index text and image semantics at scale. Learn how to leverage S3 Vectors with popular AWS AI services to power AI-driven applications that can efficiently search through large vector datasets. Whether you’re building media search applications or search-enabled AI, you’ll learn how to optimize your use of S3 Vectors.

sessions.t: Architecting video search at trillion scale with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.a: Storing and querying 1.5 trillion vectors demands rethinking traditional vector database architecture. Join this talk to learn how Bright Data built its video search retrieval layer on Amazon S3 Vectors, covering index partitioning across massive collections, embedding storage layout for sub-second nearest-neighbor queries, and cost/latency trade-offs versus dedicated vector databases at this scale. Bright Data walks through its approach to sharding, metadata filtering, and query routing, with benchmarks comparing throughput and cost per million queries. You'll leave with concrete architectural patterns for evaluating S3 Vectors in large-scale search, RAG, or embedding retrieval systems.

sessions.t: Architect, launch, and optimize solutions with AWS Marketplace
sessions.a: Discover how new AWS Marketplace capabilities can help turn your solutions into scalable commercial offerings including AI-powered and multi-product offerings. In this interactive workshop, explore key decisions across architecture, packaging, deployment, pricing, and launch readiness. Connect directly with AWS Marketplace subject-matter experts to evaluate approaches for your business, validate your listing strategy, and identify opportunities to simplify the customer experience. Leave with practical guidance and an actionable plan to accelerate launch, drive recurring revenue, and improve customer retention.

sessions.t: Architect Oracle Database@AWS for resiliency and scale
sessions.a: Dedicated Exadata infrastructure inside AWS data centers gives Oracle workloads full feature compatibility alongside cloud native flexibility, but architecting for resiliency at scale demands deliberate design choices. In this session, explore architecture patterns for primary and disaster recovery deployments on Oracle Database@AWS, including strategies for multi-terabyte migration and managing petabyte-scale Oracle estates. Join a live whiteboarding discussion where AWS experts cover ODB@AWS deployment options, DR configurations, and operational design choices. Leave with actionable best practices drawn from real customer deployments at scale.

sessions.t: Architect production MCP servers on Amazon ECS
sessions.a: Your MCP server works perfectly on a single Amazon ECS task. Then agents multiply, sessions collide, and scaling breaks everything. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the infrastructure patterns that make MCP servers production-ready on Amazon ECS. We'll cover horizontal scaling with externalized session state, request routing, fine-grained authentication, and autoscaling based on agent request patterns. We'll discuss multi-service topologies where different tool categories run as independent ECS services behind a shared ingress layer. Bring your current MCP architecture, and we'll design the production upgrade together.

sessions.t: Architect resilient agentic systems: Patterns beyond the happy path
sessions.a: Every agentic system works on the happy path. The real test is what happens when your AI agent times out mid-reasoning, returns a malformed action, or cascades a single failure across an entire chain. In this session, you implement four resilience patterns built for non-deterministic agents: circuit breakers that trip on semantic failure, fallback hierarchies from AI to rules to human, bulkhead isolation between agents, and timeout budgets for chain-of-thought latency. Leave with a decision framework mapping failure modes to pattern combinations you can implement immediately. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Architect resilient, multi-region workforce access on AWS
sessions.a: Truly resilient workforce access stays available even when an entire Region or identity provider goes down. In this session, explore how to architect layered workforce access resilience across four tiers: IAM Identity Center multi-region replication for external IdP customers, ADFS direct IAM federation as an emergency path for Active Directory environments, regional STS endpoints to remove hidden dependencies, and break-glass IAM users as a last resort. Learn which layers an environment needs, how to sequence failover across them, and how to validate resilience without disrupting production.

sessions.t: Architectural patterns for predictable multi-agent costs at scale
sessions.a: Agents consume several times more tokens than chat interactions, and multi-agent coordination pushes that higher. Monitoring alone isn't enough to manage costs, token economics must be considered when building agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architectural patterns that improve token economics for multi-agent applications, covering orchestration design decisions (orchestrator-subagent, generator-verifier, shared state) and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's temporal policies and cost optimization features improve cost-determinism. We'll illustrate these patterns with practical examples, then open the whiteboard for attendees to share their challenges and solutions.

sessions.t: Architectures for ultra-low latency with accelerated networking on AWS Outposts
sessions.a: This session covers networking on AWS Outposts Gen2, from scalable multi-site topologies to ultra-low latency bare metal deployments for financial trading. We explore the Gen2 dedicated Network rack, LGW routing domains for segmentation, and Intra-VPC and Inter-VPC communication. We then expand to multi-site interconnections spanning Outposts and Local Zones, extended VPC designs, and resilient architectures grounded in Well-Architected principles. Finally, we dive into bare metal instances with high-throughput accelerated networking, kernel bypass, NIC selection, and rack topology for co-located workloads where every microsecond matters. This is an interactive session driven by attendee questions and real-world challenges.

sessions.t: Architect your metadata hub with AWS Glue Data Catalog
sessions.a: Your metadata is scattered across warehouses, lakes, ML pipelines, and BI tools. In this session, learn how AWS Glue Data Catalog serves as a single metadata hub that connects all your data assets, enforces consistent governance, and makes every table, model, and feature discoverable across engines and teams. See how to register, enrich, and share metadata at scale, enable cross-account discovery, and give AI agents the context they need to query your data accurately.

sessions.t: A responsible AI challenge: Audit your agentic AI before the regulator does
sessions.a: Accuracy is necessary, but it isn't enough for agentic systems. Your agents can handle most requests correctly and still fail when someone asks how a decision was made, who approved it, or how to override it. In this hands-on workshop, you inherit a multi-agent claims system seeded with responsible AI gaps. Using the Well-Architected Responsible AI governance skill in your IDE, you audit the code against responsible AI dimensions like fairness, transparency, and accountability, investigate what you find, fix it, and generate an evidence-backed report. Walk away with a repeatable audit workflow you can run on your own agentic systems.

sessions.t: Armis from ServiceNow:  See Everything, Know What Matters: Powered by AWS (sponsored by ServiceNow)
sessions.a: Cyber threats are evolving faster than traditional security tools can respond. In this session, discover how Armis - now part of ServiceNow - delivers complete asset visibility and real-time threat detection across IT, OT, and IoT environments. Hear directly from a customer who faced these challenges head-on and learn how Armis, powered by AWS, helped them identify risk, respond faster, and build a stronger security posture across their entire enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by ServiceNow, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Ask the News: Making Decades of Publisher Content Instantly Searchable (sponsored by MongoDB)
sessions.a: TPublishers sit on enormous archives: decades of articles, millions of photos, entire histories of coverage. Most of it is invisible the moment someone needs more than a keyword match. ArcXP built Ask the News to close that gap: a standalone, API-first product giving publishers natural-language access to their own content, powered by MongoDB Atlas Vector Search. The system combines lexical and vector search so results reflect what was meant, not what was said. One of the hardest parts was visual: a pipeline that generated descriptions and embeddings for roughly five million historical images, making decades of archives searchable by meaning for the first time. You'll leave understanding a working pattern for combining lexical and vector search, and a model for exposing natural-language search as an API-first product, not a bolt-on feature. Featuring ArcXP, presented by MongoDB. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Assess your workloads with SELinux compatibility on Amazon Linux 2027
sessions.a: AL2027 preview enforces SELinux by default. In this session, deploy an application that hits SELinux denials, learn to read audit logs, diagnose the root cause, and write a custom policy that resolves it. You will leave with the practical skills to adopt AL2027's security defaults.

sessions.t: Assume Breach, Prove Recovery: A ransomware resilience workshop
sessions.a: Most organizations have backups. Few can prove clean recovery after ransomware, and regulators now demand exactly that proof. In this hands-on workshop, you configure a resilient backup architecture on AWS using vaults and immutable storage. You then experience a simulated ransomware event, validate that your recovery infrastructure held, restore to an isolated clean room environment, and scan recovered resources for attacker persistence using GuardDuty Malware Protection. You leave with a recovery validation approach and an understanding of why least privilege, vault lock, and validation are non-negotiable.

sessions.t: AtoZ AI Co-Scientist: Multi-Agent Systems That Do Research With You
sessions.a: Can an AI system move beyond answering questions to actually conducting research alongside you? We built one. AtoZ AI Co-Scientist is a multi-agent orchestration platform where specialized agents collaborate through a unified interface to discover literature, synthesize knowledge via graph-routed retrieval, generate hypotheses, implement baselines from papers, and run experiments autonomously. In this chalk talk, we dissect the compositional architecture, the graph-routed retrieval system achieving <200ms with structural signals flat search cannot capture, and Co-Scientist Bench—our agent-agnostic evaluation framework. Bring hard questions about reliability, memory, and human oversight.

sessions.t: At Petabyte Scale: Building an AI Telemetry Lake with Coralogix (sponsored by Coralogix)
sessions.a: The Access Group is turning petabytes of telemetry from hundreds of teams into an engine for business performance. Its telemetry lake gives teams a clearer view of product health, helping them spot risks sooner, solve problems faster, and understand how technology shapes the customer experience. Join The Access Group CTO Thad Széll and Coralogix CEO Ariel Assaraf to learn how unified telemetry is moving the business from reactive troubleshooting to continuous product improvement. Hear how it is sharpening decisions, focusing teams on what matters most, and creating the trusted data foundation needed to advance The Access Group’s AI ambitions. This presentation is brought to you by Coralogix, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Attesting to Secrets in Zero Knowledge
sessions.a: It is possible to prove factual statements about systems to observers without revealing any details about those systems beyond the stated claims. This is surprising, but not as surprising as the fact that it is borderline practical using Zero Knowledge Proofs. This talk will give an overview of the mathematical foundations of Zero Knowledge Proofs and introduce both interactive and non-interactive proof schemes. It will then dive into the details of some of the current general purpose Zero Knowledge proof systems (e.g., zk-SNARK and zk-STARK) and show how to use Zero Knowledge libraries to attest to (or prove) properties of software systems without sharing the implementations of those systems.

sessions.t: A Unified AWS Data and AI Strategy for SAP Customers
sessions.a: Explore how AWS and SAP customers can unlock value through converging data and AI strategies. From zero-copy integration with SAP Business Data Cloud and Amazon S3, to enterprise AI agents via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, learn practical approaches to automate SAP processes and accelerate innovation at scale.

sessions.t: Authentication, authorization, and audit for agentic AI on AWS
sessions.a: In this session you will learn how to secure identities and permissions for AI agents across your agentic workflows. Using Strands SDK, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, Cognito, and Verified Permissions, you implement user and machine authentication, fine-grained authorization, consent management, and permission delegation for agents, tools, and LLMs. The session follows a "choose your own adventure" format so you focus on the scenarios most relevant to you, whether that is agent-to-agent delegation, human-in-the-loop consent, or least-privilege tool access. You leave ready to apply these patterns to your own agentic AI systems.

sessions.t: Automate AI governance and risk management
sessions.a: Governance frameworks designed for static deployments struggle to keep pace with AI systems that learn, adapt, and act autonomously. In this session, walk through AWS Responsible AI best practices for governing AI across the full development lifecycle. Then see how AI Risk Intelligence (AIRI) puts these principles into practice, automating risk management with static checks that verify controls at the code and documentation level and dynamic checks that analyze APIs and traces in real time, giving you continuous visibility into AI risk posture as systems evolve. Learn what it takes to move from periodic manual assessments to continuous, automated governance.

sessions.t: Automate and secure EC2 Image Builder with AI agents
sessions.a: EC2 Image Builder pipelines sprawl fast, and frontier agents that run for hours unattended need guardrails. In this builders' session, decompose Image Builder operations into reusable agent skills run via Kiro, Claude Code. Author AWSTOE components and orchestrate workflows, then harden images and scan for CVEs. Mid-build, a WaitForAction step pauses the pipeline and hands the image to AWS Security Agent to pentest; what it finds decides whether the build ships, bounded by severity, iteration caps, and human approval. Leave with a reusable skill library and governance pattern.

sessions.t: Automated Compliance Evidence from Day One
sessions.a: Your compliance team spends weeks collecting evidence manually before every audit. Automated evidence collection eliminates that burden from day one. In this builders' session, you'll learn how to leverage AWS GRC services, including AWS Config, AWS Organizations, AWS CloudTrail, and Control Catalog, to configure automated evidence collection, map controls to your target framework, use the AI compliance agent to validate both technical controls and procedural policies, and build continuous drift detection that alerts you before your next audit finds the gap.

sessions.t: Automate disaster recovery with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.a: Financial institutions face stringent regulatory requirements for operational resilience, demanding reliable disaster recovery with tight RTO/RPO targets across complex application portfolios. Yet failover procedures often remain manual and prone to error under pressure. In this chalk talk, we explore how to design a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that orchestrates end-to-end disaster recovery automation for regulated workloads. We’ll walk through how a coordination agent delegates to specialized sub-agents for readiness verification, infrastructure operations, Terraform code generation, Git operations, and deployment validation—each with human-in-the-loop approval gates.

sessions.t: Automate dispute resolution with Amazon Connect and Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Dispute resolution calls require agents to navigate multiple systems simultaneously, frustrating customers and driving up costs. In this session, integrate Amazon Connect with Amazon Bedrock to build an AI-assisted dispute workflow. Amazon Connect flows retrieve transaction context from Amazon DynamoDB while an Amazon Bedrock agent drafts resolution options ranked by policy compliance. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway manages tool calling with Cedar-based access policies and centralized observability across each interaction. Real-time transcription surfaces relevant account history and post-call summarization auto-populates the CRM. Implement PII redaction in call recordings, configure retention policies, and test escalation paths when AI cannot resolve a dispute.

sessions.t: Automated memory forensics at scale with generative AI
sessions.a: In a live demo, we deploy malware built from APT41 tradecraft onto a Kubernetes cluster and watch an AI agent autonomously investigate the forensic evidence — acquiring volatile memory, identifying injected code, and tracing the attack chain without human intervention.

sessions.t: Automate Investigations to Resolve Application Failures with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.a: Every minute of downtime is a minute your customers notice. What if an agent could correlate your logs, metrics, and change history the moment an application fails? In this hands-on lab, use AWS DevOps Agent to autonomously investigate operational issues across your AWS environment. Trigger investigations from simulated application failures, observe the agent correlate logs, metrics, and change history in real time, and review root cause analyses with actionable mitigation plans.

sessions.t: Automate patching and compliance with AI-powered visibility
sessions.a: Tracking patch compliance across hundreds of accounts is manual, slow, and hard to prove to auditors. In this hands-on builder's session, you automate patching and continuous compliance across Linux and Windows, then let AI do the heavy lifting: generate a multi-account compliance dashboard with spec-driven development and answer compliance questions with natural language instead of hand-building reports. You define patch baselines, maintenance windows, and exception rules, then reason through the trade-offs, rather than running pre-made scripts.

sessions.t: Automate Penetration Tests with AWS Security Agent
sessions.a: Security testing shouldn't require weeks of manual effort anymore. In this hands-on lab, configure and execute automated penetration tests using AWS Security Agent. Set up an Agent Space with VPC networking, verify target domains, scope tests by risk type, and monitor execution in real time. Analyze findings with CVSS scores and reproduction steps, then generate actionable reports for your development teams.

sessions.t: Automate savings with AWS Billing and Cost Management services
sessions.a: Managing Savings Plans well is a continuous job. In this chalk talk, we discuss approaches to making commitment purchases more intelligent and less manual. We will cover how you can build a purchasing cadence that incorporates your organization's demand patterns through automation and the right level of human oversight. We'll also cover Automation, a feature within AWS Compute Optimizer that enables you to apply optimization recommendations to your AWS resources, which can help you reduce costs and improve performance. Bring your questions and challenges.

sessions.t: Automate threat detection and response across your logs
sessions.a: Security teams cannot manually hunt through every log for the one event that matters, and threats move faster than analysts can query. In this hands-on builders session, you will build automated detection and response on your security telemetry: metric filters and anomaly detectors that flag suspicious activity, findings routed to alarms that page the right people, and automated remediation that acts before an analyst logs in. After tuning detections to cut false positives, walk away with a pipeline that watches your logs so your team does not have to.
