sessions.a: Transform your organization's data landscape and eliminate silos in this hands-on workshop with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Unify data management and design data interoperability across data lakes, data warehouses, and federated data sources. Through practical exercises, discover how to create a single source of truth while maintaining security and governance across your entire data estate. You'll implement real-time analytics, optimize query performance, and design scalable architectures. Perfect for data engineers, ML practitioners, and solution architects looking to modernize their data infrastructure for building agentic AI applications.

sessions.a: Enterprise AI falls short when agents lack live business context. See how SAP's Business AI Platform and AWS solve this: Joule Studio enables developers and business users to build and deploy custom AI agents grounded in SAP's process knowledge, while bidirectional, zero-copy integration between SAP Business Data Cloud and Amazon Athena gives AWS services secure access to trusted SAP data. Watch a live demo of building agents that reason with business context, collaborate across SAP and AWS, and act across enterprise processes with governance.​ This presentation is brought to you by SAP, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build agentic automations for business processes with Amazon Quick Automate
sessions.a: In this session, learn how to build an enterprise-grade automation using Amazon Quick Automate. Through a financial services example, explore how specialized AI agents work together to handle complex interactions across web pages and business applications. You'll create a production-ready automation featuring custom agents that leverage knowledge and tools to transform a merchant onboarding process. Using Quick Automate's chat based authoring and visual studio, you'll configure a workflow with multiple agents, integrate with multiple tools, test and debug the workflow, and then deploy it using robust enterprise controls. Walk away knowing how to develop agentic automations for real-world use cases.

sessions.t: Build agentic fraud detection with a transaction foundation model
sessions.a: Organized fraud rings exploit the gaps between siloed detection systems, making them invisible to traditional rules-based approaches. In this workshop, you’ll construct a fraud detection optimization system that tackles them at scale. Load 24M transactions into Apache Iceberg, build a knowledge graph with Amazon Neptune to reveal hidden fraud networks, and train an ensemble combining transaction foundation model embeddings with graph embeddings for measurable score improvement. Then deploy a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that autonomously investigates patterns, expands fraud rings, and creates validated detection rules. Leave with an end-to-end working system you can replicate in your own environment.

sessions.t: Build agentic GraphRAG apps with Amazon Neptune
sessions.a: GraphRAG combines knowledge graphs with RAG to produce explainable responses grounded in semantic relationships between concepts, entities, and underlying content. Agentic GraphRAG takes this further, allowing agents to autonomously decide which GraphRAG tools to use to achieve information goals. In this session, build an agentic GraphRAG application using the open source AWS GraphRAG Toolkit. You will transform unstructured and semi-structured data into a catalog of domain-specific GraphRAG tools to enable agents to answer multi-faceted questions that require context from multiple distinct knowledge sources to provide a contextually complete answer. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
sessions.a: As applications evolve from RAG to agentic workflows, retrieval must support more than top-k semantic matches. In this session, use Aurora PostgreSQL as the core search and context engine for agentic hybrid retrieval. Implement PostgreSQL full-text search for lexical retrieval, pgvector semantic similarity, SQL and metadata filters, fuzzy matching, reciprocal rank fusion, model-based reranking, source attribution, and retrieval diagnostics. Then wire these capabilities into agent tools that decompose complex questions, gather targeted evidence, compare sources, explain ranking signals, and synthesize cited answers. Leave with working code, schema patterns, ranking templates, and techniques for trustworthy retrieval-heavy AI applications.

sessions.a: In this workshop, discover how to create an AI agent that takes a single user prompt, finds anomalies using observability and monitoring tools, and takes proper actions on your behalf. Using solutions available in AWS Marketplace, you can incorporate leading generative AI models into your agentic AI workflows while maintaining privacy leveraging stands agents. Deploy third-party products in your AWS account, ensuring that prompts, data, and model responses stay within the boundaries of your account and are not shared with model providers. This is important for business use cases where competitive or confidential information may be used with models. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build agentic payment investigators on Aurora PostgreSQL & AgentCore
sessions.a: Payment dispute resolution and ledger reconciliation require agents that reason over transactional history, retrieve precedent with precision, and write through idempotent workflows. In this session, learn how to build two production-grade payment agents on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: a dispute investigator that classifies cardholder disputes and drafts representment narratives, and a reconciliation agent that resolves breaks between internal ledgers and bank statements. Both share one investigator pattern: an agent reasoning over structured records, retrieving precedent with pgvector, and writing through an idempotent ledger. Go deep on SERIALIZABLE state machines, hybrid retrieval that knows when a trigram index beats an embedding, confidence-scored human-in-the-loop routing, and trace-to-row observability with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

sessions.t: Build Agentic Video Streaming Observability Using Kiro and Bedrock
sessions.a: Media operations teams struggle to correlate issues across complex live streaming pipelines, In this hands-on session, build an agentic video observability and analytics application using Kiro and Amazon Bedrock that monitors the entire live streaming chain AWS Elemental MediaConnect, MediaLive, MediaPackage, MediaTailor and Amazon CloudFront. Deploy AI agents using Strands Agents SDK and MCP servers to ingest, visualize, and investigate end-to-end QoE/QoS analytics across three layers: origin health, CDN performance, and client-side CMCD telemetry. Leave with a unified dashboard and natural language interface for streaming quality investigation across every pipeline stage.

sessions.t: Build agents on OSS models with blazing fast inference on SageMaker AI
sessions.a: Stop paying frontier-model prices for agentic workloads. In this hands-on session, build production-ready AI agents powered by open-source models like Qwen3 and Gemma4 running entirely on Amazon SageMaker AI. You'll deploy models with optimized serving, connect them to multi-turn tool-use workflows through OpenAI-compatible APIs, and enable real-time bi-directional streaming for responsive agent interactions. Leave with a working cost-optimized agent stack you fully control — fast inference, zero vendor lock-in, and patterns for scaling agentic workloads on your own terms.

sessions.t: Build a governed enterprise AI/ML platform on SageMaker AI
sessions.a: Enterprises struggle with fragmented ML tooling, inconsistent governance, and limited model health visibility. This session demonstrates a unified platform on Amazon SageMaker AI addressing these challenges across regulated industries. We cover multi-account architecture with environment-isolated domains, SageMaker AI Studio and MLflow/Model Registry as the central governance checkpoint with approval workflows, and CI/CD-driven model promotion with validation gates. We extend this to LLM fine-tuning — adapter versioning, evaluation benchmarks, and human-in-the-loop sign-off within the same registry-driven pipeline. Finally, we close the loop with model monitoring for drift, inference logging, and automated alerting. Leave with a reference architecture and decision frameworks.

sessions.t: Build a governed semantic layer with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and MCP
sessions.a: Financial services organizations struggle with inconsistent metric definitions, AI hallucination risks, and analyst bottlenecks. In this session, you’ll build a governed semantic layer with three key pillars (accuracy, consistency, and explainability) essential for agents to operate securely at scale. You’ll then connect to AI agents powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that query, interpret, and act on financial data via MCP, enabling natural language access to complex financial metrics. Your agents reason rather than guess, with full auditability for financial regulators. Leave with a production-ready architecture pattern that goes beyond "chat with your data" demos.

sessions.t: Build a grounded AI support assistant on Amazon OpenSearch Service
sessions.a: You want to build an AI assistant: where do you even start? A model alone is not the answer. The hard part is grounding it in your own data so it gives real answers, remembers the conversation, and holds up as that data grows, and grounding is a search problem. In this hands-on workshop, you build a customer support assistant grounded in Amazon OpenSearch Service. Starting from a pre-deployed base, you create an OpenSearch Serverless collection, add hybrid search for relevance, and add agentic memory so your assistant retains context across the conversation. You connect your tools and data with the OpenSearch MCP server, the AWS Knowledge MCP, and the AWS MCP. You leave with working code, an architecture that scales itself, and a clear path from a blank page to an assistant that answers from real data.

sessions.t: Build AI agents on Amazon S3 Files
sessions.a: S3 Files is the first cloud object store with fully-featured, high-performance file system access to your data. In this hands-on session, you'll create an S3 file system, attach it to an Amazon EKS cluster, and build an AI agent that loads model weights and processes data directly from S3 via standard file I/O. No SDK rewrites, no data duplication, just native POSIX access. You'll fine-tune synchronization behavior between S3 and the file system, controlling how data flows between object and file interfaces. Finally, you'll configure cross-Region replication to establish a disaster recovery strategy for your production workloads.

sessions.t: Build AI agents that serve customers like your best reps on AgentCore
sessions.a: Chatbots answer questions. Your best reps remember context, pull up the right data, take action, and resolve the issue in one conversation. This session shows how to build conversational agents on AgentCore that work the same way: low-latency streaming on Runtime, multi-turn and cross-session context with Memory, Gateway-connected tools so the agent checks orders, modifies accounts, and triggers workflows mid-conversation, guardrails that keep every interaction on-policy, and human handoff when needed.

sessions.t: Build AI agents to operate desktop and mainframe apps on WorkSpaces
sessions.a: You rely on desktop and mainframe applications for critical workflows, but these interfaces remain inaccessible to AI agents. Your Robotic Process Automation efforts have struggled to keep pace as applications and configurations constantly change. Amazon WorkSpaces lets AI agents securely operate the same desktop and mainframe applications your employees use, without any application modernization. WorkSpaces supports Model Context Protocol (MCP), so it works with any agent framework. In this workshop, connect to a pre-provisioned WorkSpace, build a custom agent, run agents that complete desktop workflows, and monitor agent sessions with CloudWatch and CloudTrail. Bring laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build AI photo discovery with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.a: Learn how S3 Vectors turns millions of untagged images into a semantically searchable collection without standing up a separate vector database. In this builders' session, you will generate multi-modal embeddings from photo assets, store and index them in S3 Vectors with metadata predicates for filtered search, and wire an AI agent that discovers images using natural language queries. You will explore index configuration, batch ingestion throughput, and cost patterns at scale. You will leave with a working prototype and production patterns for building vector-native search directly on S3.

sessions.t: Build AI-Powered Analytics with Conversational BI on Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Construct a complete AI-powered analytics pipeline from data ingestion through conversational consumption. Using Amazon Quick's Direct Lake on S3 Tables, query live data without moving it into SPICE, enrich datasets with calculated fields and imported metadata, then build natural-language Q&A experiences. Through guided exercises on financial reporting, configure AI agents that automate root-cause analysis, report creation, and action triggers via MCP servers. Leave with a working prototype covering dashboards, variance analysis, and NL-driven self-service analytics.

sessions.t: Build AI-Powered Contact Center Agents with Amazon Connect
sessions.a: Customer-facing AI Agents can resolve issues end-to-end. In this bootcamp, build two complementary AI agents on Amazon Connect AI Customer. First, create an agent-assistance copilot that watches live chats and surfaces real-time knowledge base answers and customer data lookups to human agents. Then build a self-service AI agent that handles routine customer requests autonomously, using MCP tools for Cases and Customer Profiles, and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context when a human is needed.

sessions.t: Build a KMS key lifecycle dashboard with usage and cost insights
sessions.a: Determining which KMS keys are actively in use and which can be safely retired has historically required manual CloudTrail log analysis, and meanwhile, unused keys accumulate as operational clutter. In this hands-on builders session, you'll use the GetKeyLastUsage API to identify which keys are protecting production workloads and which are candidates for retirement. You'll configure policy conditions that prevent accidental deletion of active keys, and build a Amazon Quick dashboard that surfaces usage and cost optimization opportunities across accounts. You leave with a working multi-account key lifecycle solution you can recreate in your organization.

sessions.t: Build a knowledge graph-based agent guardrail with Amazon Neptune
sessions.a: AI agents assert relationships such as compatible products, cleared counterparties, or approved suppliers, derived from LLM reasoning rather than verified data. When these assertions are wrong, downstream business decisions fail. In this session, explore how to implement Amazon Neptune as a post-generation verification layer. Before the agent responds, a graph traversal confirms or contradicts the assertion against a live knowledge graph. Learn how to build the verification tool, the override pattern when Neptune contradicts the model, and the graph data model for storing authoritative relationship data that constrains agent behavior. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build a Live App in Under 20 Minutes, Then See How It Actually Worked (sponsored by MongoDB)
sessions.a: Most teams know what they want to build long before they have something they can show someone. This workshop gets you there fast, then shows you what's behind that build. First, you'll build a real app. Using MongoDB Build Lab from your laptop, turn an idea (a search tool, an AI assistant, a dashboard, anything) into a working, deployed app backed by MongoDB Atlas. No repo setup, no infrastructure work. You'll touch the full stack, generation, database, and deployment, and walk away with a functional prototype. Then we open up the system behind it: planning, safety checks, a durable job queue, containerized workers on Amazon EC2, automated testing, targeted repairs, and deployment. We'll unpack what makes it repeatable, like isolating generated code, keeping credentials at trusted boundaries, and preserving state across restarts with Atlas. A MongoDB Build Lab workshop, with AWS. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build a multi-agent system for hyper-personalized customer journeys
sessions.a: Delivering personalized experiences across complex customer journeys requires agents that understand intent, maintain context, and coordinate across systems. In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI personal banker using a home buying scenario as the example. Your agents extract intent from natural conversation, build dynamic customer profiles, and orchestrate workflows across internal banking systems and external ecosystem APIs. Implement multi-agent patterns for shared memory, readiness signals, and coordinated decisioning using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents Framework, and MCP. Walk away with reusable orchestration patterns you can apply to any personalized customer experience.

sessions.a: In this session, get hands-on experience with Amazon Aurora DSQL, a serverless distributed SQL database that delivers active-active high availability. Learn how to build a retail rewards points application with active-active resiliency across multiple Availability Zones and two Regions. Explore how ACID transactions and active-active replication work in Aurora DSQL. Discover best practices for data model and application design and more. Bring a laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build an Agentic AI Marketing Engine Powered by Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: In this hands-on builder session, construct a multi-agent AI system that automates the full marketing lifecycle—plan, launch, and optimize. Build specialized agents on Amazon Bedrock (planner, media buyer, analyst, and creative) that turn campaign parameters into data-driven recommendations: audience targeting, budget allocation, performance forecasts, and localized creative assets grounded in your brand guidelines and historical data. Activate campaigns through Amazon Ads DSP, then deploy an optimizer agent with human-in-the-loop approvals to reallocate budget across channels as performance shifts. Leave with a working blueprint for agentic marketing workflows using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Marketplace solutions—and become the marketeer of the future.

sessions.t: Build an agentic AI system on Amazon EKS with CPU-only inference
sessions.a: In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI system on Amazon EKS with EKS Auto Mode that serves every model on CPU instances. Deploy four inference components: a fine-tuned intent router and a fine-tuned embedding model for vector search (both ONNX, trained on CPU), a cross-encoder re-ranker for retrieval quality, and a quantized generative analyst served with llama.cpp and grounded by RAG context from OpenSearch. Amazon Bedrock generates the synthetic training data, judges every answer through a faithfulness gate, and answers the edge cases the small models cannot. You'll finish by running the control test that puts a frontier LLM in the same seat, so you know whether the small model is good enough on your workload. By the end, you'll have a working multi-agent system on standard compute, using open-source tooling you can adapt.

sessions.a: Most knowledge graphs answer questions but never close the loop with operational systems. In this session, explore how to build an ontology-driven context layer that transforms a knowledge graph into an active control plane for AI agents. The session covers RDF ontology design, SHACL constraint validation, synchronization patterns, agent integration, and write-back mechanisms that propagate decisions to systems of record. Hear how Lockheed Martin applied these patterns in production, enabling agents to reason across supply chain, manufacturing, and engineering domains. Leave with a concrete architectural blueprint and lessons learned from building context layers that act while increasing your trust.

sessions.t: Build an Agentic Enterprise to Enable Autonomous Action (sponsored by Snowflake)
sessions.a: Building an agentic enterprise empowers organizations to automate complex work and drive measurable business outcomes. True transformation happens when autonomous AI operates across systems using trusted data, flexible models, connected applications, and a unified, agentic control plane. By bringing knowledge workers and technical builders into a shared agentic environment, teams move faster without sacrificing governance. Learn how the Snowflake AI Data Cloud unifies enterprise context, model choice, and app connections into a single architecture. Discover how to turn enterprise data into reliable, autonomous action and long-term competitive advantage in your AWS cloud environment. This presentation is brought to you by Snowflake, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build an AI navigator that makes every frontline worker an expert
sessions.a: A member is on the line, a regulation changed last week, and the answer isn't in any manual yet. Frontline staff don't need a search box — they need a guide that surfaces the next right action in the moment. In this builder session, build a self-improving frontline navigator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness: ground it in your policies with a Managed Knowledge Base, keep it current with live rule changes via AgentCore Web Search, and close the loop with AgentCore Optimization so it measurably improves from every real interaction. Unlike a static knowledge base, this agent recommends actions, adapts as policies shift, and learns on the job. Whether you serve members, patients, or beneficiaries, leave with a deployed self-improving navigator and the architecture behind it.

In this builders' session, you'll construct a multi-agent system that analyzes your AWS Backup environment across four dimensions: coverage gaps, ransomware resilience scoring, vault security, and cost optimization. You'll build an MCP server exposing backup APIs as agent tools, wire specialist subagents into an orchestration graph, and deploy a remediation agent with human-in-the-loop approval to AgentCore Gateway. Leave with a scalable pattern you can run in your own environment.

sessions.t: Build an AI-Powered student services contact center
sessions.a: Education contact centers are overwhelmed. Repetitive inquiries surge during enrollment and financial aid deadlines while staff burn out and students get inconsistent answers. In this chalk talk, we will architect an agentic AI powered contact center on Amazon Connect that transforms campus support. We will cover configuring a knowledge base with university content, delivering real-time AI-generated recommendations to human agents during live calls, and deploying agentic self-service that autonomously resolves common student inquiries over voice and chat. Key topics include deterministic intent handling vs. agentic reasoning and FERPA guardrails. Leave with a reference architecture you can adapt for your campus.

sessions.t: Build an AI Student Advisor: Agents for Education
sessions.a: Universities lose 15 percent of students due to inadequate academic advising. Advisors are overwhelmed, and students face long wait times for responses. In this chalk talk, we explore the end-to-end architecture of an AI student advising agent: building the agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands, connecting it to student record systems via MCP, adding guardrails for sensitive student welfare queries, and surfacing it to students through Amazon Quick embedded in their existing LMS. We'll whiteboard designs for real-world advising scenarios (course selection, wellbeing, careers) and discuss the trade-offs between automation and human escalation.

sessions.t: Build an AI testing safety net before you modernize
sessions.a: Modernizing applications is risky without comprehensive test coverage, and most apps that need modernization don't have it. In this workshop, you'll build an AI-powered testing safety net before touching a line of production code. Starting with a deployed insurance application, you'll use Kiro to generate spec-driven tests from source code and Nova Act to discover UI tests through autonomous exploration. Then you'll apply AWS Transform to modernize the codebase and re-run your AI-generated test suite to prove functional equivalence. You'll leave knowing how to de-risk modernization by letting GenAI build your safety net first. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Build an AI Travel Assistant with AgentCore Gateway
sessions.a: Your agent handles conversations well, but to search for flights or check weather it needs access to external tools and APIs. In this SimuLearn session, you create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and register Lambda functions as MCP-compatible tool targets. You then deploy a travel planning agent using the Strands Agents SDK that connects to the Gateway, sequentially invokes flight search and weather tools, and synthesizes results into a trip recommendation through one secure MCP endpoint.

sessions.t: Build an automated evaluation pipeline for AI agents
sessions.a: Stand up a continuous evaluation pipeline for your generative AI applications. In this hands-on workshop, you'll build an end-to-end evals infrastructure using Amazon Bedrock and open-source tooling. We cover designing evaluation datasets, implementing automated scoring (LLM-as-judge and programmatic metrics), tracking model performance over time, and triggering alerts on quality regressions. Leave with a working pipeline you can adapt for your organization's models and prompts.

sessions.a: Stand up a continuous evaluation pipeline for your generative AI applications. Leave with a working pipeline you can adapt for your organization's models and prompts.

sessions.t: Build and deploy agents to Lambda and EKS with Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Bring an agent idea and leave with it deployed. In this workshop you use the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock to build an agent from scratch, give it tools and memory, and add guardrails, permissions, and observability. There are multiple ways to deploy agents in production including Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Lambda MicroVMs, and Amazon EKS. In this lab you deploy to Lambda and EKS. Leave with a reference architecture for agents you can actually ship. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Build and deploy a voice agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic
sessions.a: Build and deploy a voice agent with Amazon Nova 2 SonicLearn how to build and deploy a voice agent using Nova 2 Sonic, Strands BidiAgent, AgentCore, and customized Skills. The session covers both bidirectional streaming architecture (Nova Sonic) and cascading architectures using Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Polly. Attendees will learn reference architectures, implementation patterns, deployment steps, and best practices for building scalable, production-ready voice agents using AI coding tools.

sessions.t: Build and optimize data transfers with AWS DataSync Enhanced mode
sessions.a: When you're moving petabytes from on-premises file servers and multicloud object stores into AWS, transfer speed and operational visibility are equally critical. In this builders session, you'll configure AWS DataSync Enhanced mode to move data from diverse source environments into AWS using its parallel pipeline for high-throughput transfers. Enhanced mode generates detailed task reports and transfer logs as it works. You'll then use Amazon Bedrock to analyze that data, surfacing performance bottlenecks and generating optimization recommendations. Walk away with reusable patterns for fast data movement and AI-powered transfer visibility.

sessions.t: Build and Ship an AI-Powered App with Amazon Quick
sessions.a: In this hands-on builder session, you'll use Amazon Quick to design, iterate on, and publish a fully functional application through natural-language conversation. You'll connect to a live data source (pre-provisioned via MCP), shape your app interactively with generative AI, persist state across users, and publish something your team or customers can use immediately. Whether you're accelerating decision-making, automating operational workflows, or putting insights directly in the hands of end users, this session shows how Quick Apps collapses the gap between having an idea and shipping a solution. Bring your laptop and be ready to build.

sessions.t: Build and test HA/DR architectures for Microsoft workloads on AWS
sessions.a: Can your Windows Server applications and SQL Server databases survive a system outage? In this builders' session, you'll find out by building and testing HA/DR architectures against simulated failures. Get hands-on experience with Elastic Disaster Recovery and Systems Manager to construct resilient infrastructure and recovery automation. Measure RTO and RPO in real time as you purposely break production workloads. Explore additional topics like RDS, S3, Elastic Beanstalk, and AWS Managed AD. You'll leave with a validated resiliency blueprint and the confidence to protect your most critical Microsoft workloads.

sessions.t: Build an intelligent contact center with Zendesk and AWS (sponsored by Zendesk)
sessions.a: Contact center teams need to resolve issues consistently across channels while giving agents the information and tools to act. In this session, discover how Zendesk and AWS work together to create a native contact center experience within Zendesk that connects customer interactions, workflows, and systems in one connected environment. Learn how AI can enhance voice support by handling routine needs, guiding conversations, and helping customers reach resolution faster. See how human handoffs preserve the customer’s history, needs, and progress, giving agents the context they need to step in seamlessly, personalize the experience, and move each interaction toward resolution. This presentation is brought to you by Zendesk, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build a payment-enabled agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments
sessions.a: AI agents that can autonomously transact open new possibilities in financial services—from purchasing market data to paying for risk scores in real time. In this builders' session, you'll configure an AI agent using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments with the open source x402 protocol. You'll set up payment managers, connect to data providers, define budget controls with IAM policies, and monitor transactions with Amazon CloudWatch. Leave with a working agent that autonomously transacts, reasons about costs, and delivers results end to end.

sessions.t: Build a payment-enabled agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments

sessions.t: Build a per-tenant observability stack for Agentic SaaS
sessions.a: Multi-tenant ISVs need per-tenant observability that traditional dashboards can't deliver — aggregated metrics hide the tenant causing the problem, and shared traces don't tell you whose agent misbehaved. In this session, build a per-tenant observability stack for agents. You'll instrument agent invocations with tenant-aware traces and session replay, build tenant-scoped dashboards that surface noisy neighbors and latency outliers, and configure alerting that fires on per-tenant thresholds rather than aggregate signals. By the end, you'll have an observability setup that scales with your tenant count without a separate data pipeline — and patterns to extend it as your agent architecture grows.

sessions.t: Build a Physical AI Model Factory on SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.a: Physical AI teams in robotics and autonomous vehicles can't collect enough real data for the rare edge cases that dominate risk. The answer is a continuous data flywheel: generate synthetic scenarios, post-train policies, evaluate, repeat. Running that at scale is GPU-hungry and orchestration-heavy. This chalk talk shows how to run the full Physical AI model factory on SageMaker HyperPod with EKS: provision heterogeneous GPU pools, schedule multi-stage jobs, and leverage auto-healing infrastructure.

sessions.t: Build a production multi-Agent Systems with Strands
sessions.a: Build, deploy, and scale agents with re-usable multi-agent patterns in Strands Agents. You will create an agentic system that is capable of decomposing complex tasks and delegating sub-tasks to specialized worker agents. These agents will manage shared state and memory across boundaries, gracefully handle failures, and enforce quality guardrails. Subsequently, these agents will be deployed to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for production scaling and observability, featuring harness capabilities for checkpointing and long-running multi-agent workflow capabilities. Upon completion, you will be equipped with reusable design patterns and industry best practices to construct production-grade multi-agent systems utilizing the Strands Agent SDK.

sessions.t: Build a production multi-Agent Systems with Strands
sessions.a: Build, deploy, and scale agents with re-usable multi-agent patterns in Strands Agents. sessions.t: Build a production multi-tier application on Amazon ECS
sessions.a: Real applications have frontends, APIs, workers, and databases that all need to communicate reliably. In this workshop, build a complete multi-tier containerized architecture on Amazon ECS from scratch. Configure service-to-service networking with Service Connect, implement per-tier autoscaling policies, deploy updates with automated rollback, and observe your application using CloudWatch Container Insights. Walk away with a working architecture you can use as a reference for your own workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build a production multi-tier application on Amazon ECS
sessions.a: Real applications have frontends, APIs, workers, and databases that all need to communicate reliably. sessions.t: Build a real-time data lakehouse with CDC streams on S3 Tables
sessions.a: Learn how to build a real-time transactional data lakehouse using Amazon S3 Tables with Apache Iceberg. In this hands-on session, you will ingest CDC streams from Amazon MSK into a medallion architecture, transform batch and streaming data into business-ready gold layer tables with Amazon SageMaker, and query the results through Amazon Quick. You'll configure S3 Tables maintenance policies per layer and compare binpack, sort, and z-order compaction strategies to optimize query performance. You will leave with production patterns for continuous ingestion, incremental processing, and low-latency analytics at scale.

sessions.t: Build a Research Co-Scientist Using Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Learn how to build your own co-scientist with Amazon Quick. In this builder session, you'll gain hands-on experience with loading life sciences domain skills directly into Amazon Quick, and work through your own scientific questions with guidance from AWS's life sciences experts. You'll leave with firsthand experience on bringing expert-level reasoning to everyday research workflows.

sessions.t: Build a SaaS control plane with Kiro specs and Strands multi-tenant constructs
sessions.a: A SaaS control plane - tenant onboarding, billing, configuration management, agent provisioning is the most repeatable software every software vendor builds from scratch. In this builder's session, use Kiro specs to define the control plane requirements and let Kiro implement the scaffolding, then wire multi-tenant agent capabilities using Strands' open-source constructs. You'll build a working onboarding flow, a tenant configuration store, and a simple agent provisioning endpoint - all from a spec, not from scratch. Leave with a reusable starting point for your own control plane and a pattern for using Kiro and Strands together to accelerate platform development.

sessions.t: Build a SaaS control plane with Kiro specs and Strands multi-tenant constructs
sessions.a: A SaaS control plane - tenant onboarding, billing, configuration management, agent provisioning is the most repeatable software every software vendor builds from scratch. In this builder's session, use Kiro specs to define the control plane requirements and let Kiro implement the scaffolding, then wire multi-tenant agent capabilities using Strands' open-source constructs. Leave with a reusable starting point for your own control plane and a pattern for using Kiro and Strands together to accelerate platform development.

sessions.t: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall
sessions.a: AI agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore accept untrusted input and make outbound API calls, creating both ingress and egress attack surfaces. In this session, learn how to defend both paths using AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall. See how WAF authenticates callers, enforces rate limits, and blocks prompt-injection payloads before they reach your agent, while Network Firewall applies managed threat-intelligence categories to drop egress traffic to malicious destinations without maintaining custom deny lists. Walk away with a deployable defense-in-depth boundary pattern for your agentic AI workloads.

sessions.t: Build at scale real-time ingestion pipelines for Apache Iceberg tables
sessions.a: Landing streaming data into Apache Iceberg at scale is a complex undertaking. In this chalk talk, we dissect practical reference architectures for real-time ingestion into Iceberg tables, covering Kafka to Flink, Kinesis to Firehose, and managed pipelines through Amazon S3 Tables. Learn which architecture fits your latency and cost requirements, how to keep Iceberg tables query-ready under continuous writes, and how these pipelines feed downstream analytics and AI workloads.

sessions.t: Build a unified student insight platform on Amazon Quick
sessions.a: From advisors triaging at-risk students to deans auditing course difficulty to executives tracking retention trends, every role in a university needs student-success insights, but today they use disconnected tools. In this session, learn how Amazon Quick connects to your institutional data and delivers explainable, persona-aware insights through one unified architecture. Chat Agents explain early-warning signals with cited data, automated Flows trigger interventions, and Stories generate executive-ready narratives. Explore the architecture and take away patterns for explainable, natural-language analytics on AWS.

sessions.t: Build a Video Semantic Layer for Media Agent and Agent Harness on AWS
sessions.a: This workshop tackles a question most media organizations have yet to ask: your video pipeline extracts rich metadata for human search and discovery, but is it actually optimized for agents? In this hands-on session, you will build the semantic infrastructure that bridges that gap: multimodal embeddings tuned for machine recall, hybrid search that combines vector similarity with keyword precision, and an entity graph that maps content relationships into structures agents can reason over. By the end of this workshop, you will have a media agent harness that queries, enriches, and continuously improves their video understanding, making video content not just searchable by people but optimized at scale for agents.

sessions.t: Build a well-governed natural language-to-SQL agentic pipeline for Amazon Redshift
sessions.a: The Amazon Redshift MCP Server enables AI agents to generate and execute SQL using natural language—but going from demo to production means answering critical security questions on preventing query hallucination, prompt injection, unbounded scans, and inadvertent PII exposure by the LLM. In this session, you will build a well-governed text-to-SQL agentic pipeline for Amazon Redshift with security gates that validate every AI-generated query before execution including schema allow-listing to constraining LLM context, authorized tables, columns and rows, SQL AST validation and enforced read-only access.

sessions.t: Build better agent retrieval with OpenSearch Service
sessions.a: Your AI agents and assistants are only as good as the answers they retrieve. Out-of-the-box frameworks get you started, but production-ready AI applications demand more from their search layer including higher relevance on complex queries, persistent memory across sessions, and tools the model can invoke reliably. Amazon OpenSearch Service delivers these capabilities natively. In this chalk talk, we dig into how to make OpenSearch Service the backbone of your AI agents and assistants, covering hybrid retrieval for better accuracy, MCP-based access to your data, and built-in conversation and long-term memory so your applications maintain context across interactions. Bring your architecture questions. Whether you're optimizing retrieval accuracy, adding persistent context, or connecting your agent to search via MCP, we work through it together and leave you with patterns you can apply.

sessions.t: Build Bidstream Agents and Simulate Auction with AgentCore
sessions.a: In this hands-on workshop, learn to build Agentic Real-Time Framework (ARTF)-compliant agents that operate inside the bidstream and simulate auction scenarios using the Agents for Advertising framework on Amazon Bedrock. Construct an agent container that accepts bid requests and returns pricing decisions following the ARTF specification. Orchestrate multi-agent pipelines to simulate adversarial auction environments, test bidding strategies, and evaluate outcomes that feed back into model improvement. Run interactive simulations that generate learning signals, and gain hands-on experience applying your own bidding models—plus a practical understanding of how bidstream agents and agentic workflows connect end to end.

sessions.t: Build conversational AI agents for query federation with Amazon Athena
sessions.a: Stop copying data just to query it. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use MCP server integration with Amazon Athena for faster conversational analytics where agents translate natural language to federated SQL queries across custom databases and multi-cloud data stores – without moving or copying data. You’ll learn how federated queries eliminate complex ETL pipelines, enable cross-source joins in a single SQL statement, and integrate with your lakehouse on AWS for unified governance.

sessions.t: Build Custom Transformation Agents with the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit
sessions.a: Partners spent years building their modernization tooling. AWS Transform now meets them where they are, ATX agents exposed via MCP, callable from any partner-native orchestrator. We'll cover the integration pattern, agent-card model, and field-tested wins from GSI and ISV partners already in production.

sessions.t: Build Custom Transformation Agents with the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit
sessions.a: Every organisation's modernization journey is unique — we whiteboard how to build, deploy, and share custom transformation agents using the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit — from orchestrator architectures and MCP patterns to one-command Bedrock AgentCore deployment. Bring your challenges.

sessions.t: Build deeper into AWS with a traffic layer you own (sponsored by HAProxy Technologies)
sessions.a: Most teams on AWS accumulate separate systems for load balancing, WAF, bot management, rate limiting, and Kubernetes routing. Each brings its own config model and failure domain, another hop in the request path, and a configuration that does not travel. This session makes the case for one layer, on Graviton, benchmarked at over 2 million HTTPS requests per second, with no traffic leaving your VPC for inspection, managed and observed from one control plane. Because that layer runs unchanged in every environment you add, it becomes the one part of your architecture that never has to move. This presentation is brought to you by HAProxy Technologies, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build durable AI agents with AgentCore and Temporal (sponsored by Temporal)
sessions.a: An AI agent completes five steps, waits for approval, and then its runtime is replaced. How does it recover without repeating costly tool calls or losing the business process? In this session, learn how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, and Temporal combine AWS-native agent infrastructure with durable execution. We’ll build a production agent that preserves progress across failures, coordinates tools, agents, and people, and safely evolves while work is still running. You'll see how Temporal natively supports serverless compute infrastructure, complementing AgentCore Runtime with durable execution, preserving workflow progress across failures, approvals, runtime changes, and scale to zero, without pushing recovery and coordination logic into application code. This presentation is brought to you by Temporal, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build End-to-End AI Pipelines on SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.a: Modern AI pipelines demand unified frameworks for petabyte-scale data prep, large-model training, and low-latency serving. In this hands-on workshop, build a complete data processing → distributed training → model serving pipeline on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, fine-tuning and serving an LLM end-to-end. Experience HyperPod's native distributed computing integration with managed orchestration, embedded observability, tiered checkpointing, hung-job detection, and managed KV cache for inference. Simulate a node failure and watch training auto-resume in seconds. Leave with a working serving endpoint, production patterns, and a resilient platform that eliminates the infrastructure toil of running distributed AI workloads at scale.

sessions.t: Build End-to-End Testing & Self-Healing Framework for Agentic AI
sessions.a: Organizations are accelerating their deployment of AI agents, yet the critical gap remains: proving they work reliably and responding when they don't. This workshop delivers a hands-on framework for the complete testing and operational lifecycle of agentic AI on Amazon Connect Customer. First, build a layered testing strategy using native Testing & Simulation — functional, integration, and regression tests for flows and bots, wired to dashboard-driven observability. Then, implement automated operational responses such as threshold-based alerting triggers pre-approved remediations. You will leave with a reusable testing playbook and an implementable pattern for closed-loop operational automation — reducing manual validation effort and moving toward self-managing AI agents at scale.

sessions.t: Build End-to-End Testing & Self-Healing Framework for Agentic AI

sessions.t: Build eval-driven skills for Aurora PostgreSQL operations
sessions.a: Frontier agents like Amazon DevOps Agent are strong at broad investigation, correlation, and orchestration, but production database operations require domain-specific execution depth. In this workshop, turn Aurora PostgreSQL runbooks into eval-driven agent skills that DevOps Agent can invoke. Define evals across deterministic scenarios such as lock contention, replica lag diagnosis, long-running transactions blocking vacuum cleanup, connection saturation, and query plan regression. Run evals to surface gaps, then author a skill with pre-flight checks, execution sequence, validation, and rollback. Iterate with eval results, wire the skill into DevOps Agent, and leave with a working skill, harness, and reusable productionization methodology.

sessions.t: Build event-driven applications with AWS Streaming and Messaging
sessions.a: Dive deep into AWS messaging services in this hands-on workshop where you'll build a real-world, event-driven application. Learn to architect sophisticated event-driven systems using Amazon SQS, SNS, MSK, and Amazon MQ. Through guided exercises, implement critical features including fan-out architectures, FIFO queues, and hybrid patterns while optimizing for security, cost, and performance. Gain practical insights into how architectural decisions impact scalability, latency, and operational complexity in production systems.

sessions.t: Build explainable AI agent observability with DynamoDB and Neptune
sessions.a: Unintended agent actions and incorrect outputs are difficult to investigate without a structured provenance layer. In this session, learn how to design an agent observability system using Amazon DynamoDB to capture the operational audit log and Amazon Neptune to model causal dependencies between retrieved facts and agent decisions. Explore the data model, instrumentation patterns, and graph query techniques that answer what data an agent retrieved, what it concluded, and how those conclusions shaped the final output, making every agent decision traceable and explainable. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build GenAI-Powered Workflows with AWS Serverless and AWS AI Services
sessions.a: In this builders' session, design and deploy a workflow that chains AI service calls—document analysis, content generation, and decision routing—using AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions for checkpoint and recovery. Working in small groups, you'll implement error handling, human approval gates, and cost controls for AI-powered pipelines. Walk away with reusable patterns for production-ready GenAI workflows. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build governed agentic AI search with Aurora, RDS, & Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.a: Production agentic AI applications demand strong governance, precise retrieval, and consistent policy enforcement across every agent interaction. In this session, explore a retail shopping scenario where a Strands SDK dispatcher routes shoppers to specialist agents. Aurora powers hybrid search with PostgreSQL full-text search, pgvector for semantic retrieval, and Cohere Rerank for relevance ranking, while managing inventory, orders, customer records, and a queryable JSONB audit ledger. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, Memory, Gateway, and Policy orchestrate agents, preserve context, expose tools, and apply Cedar authorization to sensitive actions. Build your own governed agentic AI search application and leave with reusable patterns. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build governed agentic AI search with Aurora, RDS, & Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.a: Production agentic AI applications demand strong governance, precise retrieval, and consistent policy enforcement across every agent interaction. sessions.t: Build governed remediation workflows for Aurora database operations
sessions.a: AI-powered database intelligence can surface recommendations for slow queries, vacuum issues, index changes, and parameter tuning, but acting on those recommendations safely in production requires governance. In this session, build a governed recommendation-to-remediation workflow for Aurora PostgreSQL. Starting with a performance troubleshooting recommendation, learn to classify operational risk, validate the proposed change, apply policy-based approval gates, execute with scoped permissions, and capture an auditable trail from insight to action. Explore custom security controls, blast-radius reduction, human-in-the-loop governance, rollback planning, post-change verification across development, staging, and production environments, and integration with signals from your own agents. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build, Guard, Route: Trustworthy, Cost-Aware AI Agents with the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.a: Bring a laptop and build a governed multi-agent system on AWS, end to end. In this hands-on workshop you'll wire Strands SDK agents to inference on Amazon Bedrock and NVIDIA NIM-on-AWS, sandbox tool execution with OpenShell (Landlock, seccomp, eBPF, cgroups), and install signed skills, connectors, and runbooks from an open, versioned registry that federates with AWS AgentCore. You'll watch a five-layer enforcement spine crystallize in a run-DAG where every prompt, model call, tool call, and delegation becomes a visible, proven step. Then you'll graduate the same governance from laptop to AWS unchanged, with SPIFFE/SPIRE attesting which instance ran each step. You'll leave with a working reference deployment in your own AWS account and reusable patterns you can adapt to real agents. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build hybrid data planes for government GenAI pipelines
sessions.a: The California Community Colleges—the largest higher education system in the U.S., serving 1 in 4 community college students nationally—lost $30M+ to financial aid fraud since 2024. Ghost students consumed class seats and financial aid meant for real learners. As the first layer of defense, machine learning on Amazon SageMaker screens applicants centrally, driving a 64% decrease in attempted fraud year over year. Campus-level detection tools add additional layers, catching 2x more scammers than human staff alone. This session covers the end-to-end fraud defense—ML architecture, campus integration, intelligence sharing—and how it directly improved the student experience.

sessions.t: Build hybrid data planes for government GenAI pipelines
sessions.a: Strict national security mandates block government agencies from adopting cloud GenAI. To resolve this, architects deploy a decoupled edge-to-cloud tokenization pattern. In this workshop, use AWS CDK to build a three-phase data plane that isolates sensitive citizen data in a simulated edge environment. You will deploy local data tokenization, route masked payloads to Amazon Bedrock for stateless inference, and reconcile state on-premises. Leave with an infrastructure-as-code blueprint to unlock frontier AI and satisfy federal localization mandates.

sessions.t: Build hybrid quantum-classical solutions for science and engineering on Amazon Braket
sessions.a: Take the next step into hybrid quantum computing. This expert-level workshop combines Amazon Braket and AWS Parallel Computing Service to build hybrid quantum-classical resources that enable scientific and engineering research in fields like physics. You learn how to structure hybrid programs, manage classical resources, and interpret results from real quantum devices. Expect hands-on exercises, detailed guidance, and examples you can use as a foundation for you own projects

sessions.t: Building 10x Organizations - Using Modern Productivity Metrics (sponsored by Atlassian)
sessions.a: 10x developers may be a myth, but 10x organizations are very real, as proven by the influential study performed in the 1980s, ‘The Coding War Games.’ In this keynote-style session, teams will take a detailed, granular look at the barriers to productivity developers face today and modern approaches for removing them. You’ll learn about the history of productivity theory, and how previous practices have influenced our current understanding. DevOps and Platform Engineering philosophy is clearly converging on developer experience. But which of these approaches works? DORA? SPACE? DevEx? What should we invest in and create urgency behind today so we don’t have the same discussion again in a decade? This presentation is brought to you by Atlassian, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building a Cost Governance framework for AI that scales
sessions.a: AI spend starts with model tokens but often misses costs from agent runtimes, memory, data, and supporting services. In this chalk talk, we'll map an AI workload from architecture to bill, then apply a practical framework to measure, attribute, optimize, and govern its cost and value. Using AWS FinOps Agent as an example, we'll examine how its architecture creates costs across Amazon Bedrock and supporting services, and how to govern those costs. Bring your AI cost challenge and leave with a model that helps FinOps and engineering teams assign ownership, find waste, and set effective controls.

sessions.t: Building Advanced Agentic AI Systems on AWS
sessions.a: Multi-agent systems unlock powerful workflows, but production demands more than chaining agents together. This bootcamp covers advanced patterns using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Implement agent-as-tool communication, share memory across agents, optimize context windows for cost and performance, and secure deployments with policy-based access control and VPC integration. Configure distributed tracing, build evaluation frameworks, and design deployment strategies that take your agentic systems from prototype to production-ready state.

sessions.t: Building a flexible and scalable AWS account access strategy with IAM Identity Center
sessions.a: AWS Identity services are evolving to meet the demands of modern, multi-account environments. Learn how to use IAM Account Access Manager together with IAM Identity Center multi-Region replication and your existing IAM primitives to enable rule-based role assignment at scale across your organization; without recreating your roles or provisioning model. We'll then walk through how a customer migrated to this architecture, building a resilient identity solution across multiple AWS Regions and account structures without compromising security.

sessions.t: Building Agentic AI architectures with AWS Serverless
sessions.a: Build production-ready AI agent architectures using AWS serverless services. In this builders' session, design and deploy an agentic system that uses AWS Lambda for tool execution, Amazon Bedrock for reasoning, and Amazon EventBridge for inter-agent communication. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll implement tool-calling patterns, configure agent memory, and wire up event-driven coordination between specialized agents. Walk away with a working multi-agent architecture you can extend for your own use cases. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Building Agentic AI architectures with AWS Serverless
sessions.a: Build production-ready AI agent architectures using AWS serverless services. In this builders' session, design and deploy an agentic system that uses AWS Lambda for tool execution, Amazon Bedrock for reasoning, and Amazon EventBridge for inter-agent communication. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll implement tool-calling patterns, configure agent memory, and wire up event-driven coordination between specialized agents. Walk away with a working multi-agent architecture you can extend for your own use cases. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Building agentic apps with serverless: Lambda as your agent's toolbox
sessions.a: Agents need tools—functions they can call to retrieve data, take actions, and interact with external systems. Lambda is well-suited for this, but designing functions as agent tools requires different thinking than traditional API backends. In this chalk talk, discuss design principles for agentic Serverless: single-responsibility tools with clear input/output schemas, MCP-compatible interfaces for universal agent consumption, and multi-tenant isolation that keeps workloads secure. We'll whiteboard the trade-offs that matter—provisioned concurrency versus on-demand cold starts, cost per invocation at agent scale, and where Serverless fits versus where you need different compute.

sessions.t: Building a governed AI ready data foundation on AWS (sponsored by Fivetran)
sessions.a: Most data stacks were built for dashboards, not AI. Duplicated pipelines, competing definitions, and slow reporting make it difficult to deliver the fresh, trusted, governed data AI demands. Learn how a fast growing organization replaced engineering heavy operations with a self serve model built on AWS, Fivetran, and dbt. Understand how to standardize ingestion, apply governed transformations and semantic definitions, and cut pipeline development from months to days. You'll walk away with a practical approach to freeing engineering time, providing business teams with trusted access to data, and building a governed foundation that scales AI from experiments to production. This presentation is brought to you by Fivetran, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building AI Agents with Vercel and AWS (sponsored by Vercel)
sessions.a: This session explores how Vercel and AWS work together to support the development and deployment of AI agents. You’ll learn about first party connectivity to AWS databases and services through the Vercel Marketplace, along with the backend capabilities agents need, including APIs, durable workflows, queues, cron jobs, and MCP servers. You’ll see how these building blocks, together with the EVE framework, can simplify agent development, followed by a live demo showing how to build an agent using Vercel and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building AI-powered, app-centric unified observability
sessions.a: Your apps run everywhere, but you're still switching tabs to understand what's happening. In this session, we'll show how CloudWatch delivers AI-powered, app-centric infrastructure monitoring where you already work. We'll walk through how unified observability connects application health to underlying infrastructure across hybrid and multi-cloud environments, and how AI surfaces the insights that matter before you go looking. You'll see how CloudWatch shifts from reactive dashboards to proactive, intelligent monitoring that meets you where you are.

sessions.t: Building a Knowledge & Context Engineering Foundation for AI Agents
sessions.a: Every enterprise building agentic AI hits the same wall: AI agents can't deliver trusted guidance without governed knowledge behind them. In this session, learn how AWS solved this internally with an agentic specialist teammate for Amazon Connect powered by a structured knowledge governance framework. We'll show how specialist reasoning is captured, validated, and scaled across 92 domains to 30K+ field members, and demonstrate the live workflow from governed knowledge delivery to human escalation. Walk away with a repeatable reference architecture for making your own AI agents production-ready and trustworthy.

Walk away with a repeatable reference architecture for making your own AI agents production-ready and trustworthy.

sessions.t: Building and scaling inference workloads on Amazon EKS
sessions.a: Kubernetes has become the platform of choice for production gen AI inference at scale. This builders' session covers deploying and scaling large language models on Amazon EKS with NVIDIA GPUs - from cluster setup optimized for GPU workloads to efficient model serving with vLLM, distributed inference with Ray, and observability using Prometheus and Grafana. Real-world patterns address cost optimization and enterprise-grade reliability for teams moving beyond experimentation. Attendees leave with hands-on experience and best practices for running production-grade gen AI infrastructure on Kubernetes. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Building and scaling low latency web apps with AWS Serverless
sessions.a: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this code talk, build a full-stack web application entirely on AWS serverless services, live in code: API endpoints, business logic, data persistence, and authentication. We walk through architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and show how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with patterns you can apply to your own projects.

sessions.t: Building and securing AI agents on Amazon EKS
sessions.a: AI agents now generate and run their own code at runtime, turning secure agent execution into a platform engineering problem. Containers alone were not built to run untrusted, autonomous code safely at scale. In this hands-on workshop, you will build an agent on Amazon EKS using the Strands Agent SDK, MCP, and Amazon Bedrock, then progressively harden and operate it: run it with stronger workload isolation, apply controls over what it can access, establish scoped identity for secure communication, and manage its lifecycle in production. You will leave able to architect, deploy, secure, and operate production-ready agentic workloads on Kubernetes.

sessions.t: Building an Open and Real-time Fraud and Decisioning Engine with Mastercard and Redis (sponsored by Redis)
sessions.a: Ever get a text that your Mastercard was used in a transaction you didn't make? That's because every card swipe has to be evaluated before it's cleared to keep fraud from slipping through. Join Sivakumar Palanasami, Mastercard's EVP of Data Platforms, to learn how his team's real-time fraud decisioning model built with Redis on AWS and for a sneak peek of what they're doing next. This presentation is brought to you by Redis, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building Apache Iceberg data lakes with Amazon S3 Tables
sessions.a: Amazon S3 Tables are setting a new standard for Apache Iceberg data lakes: fully managed, open, and AI-ready. In this session, learn everything you need to know about S3 Tables, from how we continuously optimize Iceberg tables as your data scales, to support for ingestion, migration, data protection, cost-efficiency, and performance. We’ll explore how S3 Tables make it easy for AI agents to build on Iceberg tables and dive into the latest re:Invent announcements. Hear real-world customer stories and walk away equipped to bring S3 Tables to your organization.

sessions.t: Building a partner business on Amazon Lightsail
sessions.a: Amazon Lightsail is a simple, low-cost cloud platform designed for small and medium business workloads. In this chalk talk, we start with an overview of what Lightsail offers and common use cases partners are delivering today. We then introduce the Lightsail Partner Program and the benefits available to partners who build their practice on Lightsail. Bring your scenarios. We'll work through partner economics, discuss real use cases, and how Lightsail helps partners tackle onboarding and scaling challenges. You'll leave with a clearer understanding of how to leverage Lightsail to build your partner business.

sessions.t: Building a private service fabric across AWS accounts and orgs
sessions.a: Deploying workloads across AWS accounts - whether across an organization, between business units, or alongside acquired entities - creates connectivity complexity that traditional networking options don't cleanly solve. You face IP coordination headaches, overly broad network surface exposure, and heavy per-resource infrastructure just to share a service privately. Bidirectional sharing doubles the problem. In this session, build a private service fabric—a federated architecture where multiple organizations share services privately and bidirectionally with independent governance. Combine Amazon VPC Lattice, resource gateways, AWS PrivateLink, and AWS Resource Access Manager into a cross-organization platform covering bidirectional topologies and federated governance.

sessions.t: Building a semantic layer with AWS Glue Data Catalog and AWS Context
sessions.a: In this chalk talk, we dive into how AWS Context assembles semantic data from multiple semantic stores to create a semantic layer, which is then turned into a unified context layer through a knowledge graph. This enables AI agents and analytics engines to understand business meaning, relationships, and intent — not just schema and location. We'll work through architecture patterns for defining semantic data annotations, propagating semantics across lakehouse tables, and exposing discoverable, agent-ready metadata at query time.

sessions.t: Building a Zero Trust for Agentic AI Practice: A Partner Framework
sessions.a: AI agents create identity, authorization, governance, and tenant-isolation challenges that map directly to partner revenue streams. In this builders' session, you'll work hands-on with the Zero Trust Agent Maturity (ZAM) Framework and configure Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity and Gateway to enforce verifiable agent identities, auditable interaction chains, and centralized policy authorization that scopes every agent action to its tenant boundary. You'll run a live ZAM assessment on a sample multi-tenant deployment, revealing security gaps that become partner opportunities: red-teaming engagements, MCP security proxies, multi-tenant isolation reviews, and compliance automation. Leave with a repeatable assessment methodology to secure multi-tenant agent deployments.

sessions.t: Building better quantum computers with digital twins
sessions.a: Quantum computers could revolutionize fields like pharmacy and logistics, but today's hardware is too error-prone for practical use. To design better error-correction strategies, simulating how real quantum hardware operates is essential, yet computationally intractable. In this talk, we demonstrate quantum processor digital twins developed by Quantum Elements and powered by AWS HPC infrastructure - that faithfully mimic real hardware at experimental scale. Attendees will leave understanding why error correction matters and how classical compute accelerates the path to useful quantum computing.

sessions.t: Building Beyond the Hardware: Transforming IBM i/AIX Workloads with AWS (sponsored by Lightedge)
sessions.a: IBM Power organizations support mission-critical workloads across industries. Now, there are more infrastructure options than ever before, providing hybrid transformation opportunities and challenges. This session explores how to develop a hybrid strategy that balances performance, resiliency, security, and business objectives. Hear how enterprises are exploring a phased modernization strategy that rehosts IBM workloads in a hybrid cloud environment, connects to AWS, and evolves their infrastructure. Learn how they establish secure, low-latency AWS connectivity and integrate IBM business logic with cloud-native services. This session provides proven frameworks, architectural insights, and modernization strategies to reduce risk, accelerate transformation, and maximize infrastructure value. This presentation is brought to you by Lightedge, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building conversational AI with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic
sessions.a: We'll explore how bidirectional audio streaming enables natural, low-latency dialogue, with expressive voices across multiple languages. See how new capabilities like cross-modal voice-and-text switching, asynchronous tool calling for multi-step tasks, and a large context window let you build voice agents, customer service automation, and conversational apps.

sessions.t: Building Cross-Enterprise AI Agents with MCP and A2A on AWS
sessions.a: Enterprises run hundreds of applications from ERP, CRM, supply chain, and beyond and yet orchestrating intelligent actions across these systems remains a challenge. In this chalk talk, learn how to architect and manage cross-enterprise agentic orchestration using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We explore how Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication enable AI agents to seamlessly interact across application boundaries through a single, unified chat interface. Walk away with practical architecture patterns for connecting SAP and adjacent enterprise systems like SalesForce, ServicesNow etc into a cohesive, AI-powered automation layer

sessions.t: Building enterprise agent platform on AgentCore
sessions.a: As agents multiply across teams, platform owners need control without becoming a bottleneck. In this session, learn best practices for building a governance foundation for your agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Use gateway as a central control point for all agent-to-tool traffic, enforce authorization with policies at the infrastructure layer that agents cannot bypass, and propagate identity end to end for a complete audit trail. Use the Agent Registry to catalog, discover, and approve agents and tools across the organization, and end-to-end tracing for fleet-wide visibility. Includes a demo. Leave with a governance blueprint teams can adopt.

sessions.t: Building enterprise-scale event buses with Amazon EventBridge
sessions.a: Discover how Amazon EventBridge simplifies enterprise-scale event routing across accounts and teams. In this hands-on builders' session, configure an event bus with routing policies, schema discovery, and access controls that let platform teams govern event flows while application teams ship independently. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll implement multi-account event routing patterns and test event delivery at scale. Bring your laptop and come ready to build!

sessions.t: Building enterprise-scale event buses with Amazon EventBridge  [REPEAT]
sessions.a: Discover how Amazon EventBridge simplifies enterprise-scale event routing across accounts and teams. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll implement multi-account event routing patterns and test event delivery at scale. Bring your laptop and come ready to build!

sessions.t: Building eval-driven observability for AI agents
sessions.a: Multi-agent systems fail in ways your dashboards cannot show: one agent hands off bad context, another retries, and the API still returns 200. In this live coding session, start with a multi-agent app on LangGraph, Strands, and CrewAI, and instrument it with OpenTelemetry and OpenInference. Trace it from the first prototype run, evaluate agents on demand with LLM-as-judge evaluators, A/B test prompt and model variants before promoting to production, pull production traces into a versioned dataset, reproduce the failure locally, and ship the fix. All from your IDE, without switching tools.

sessions.t: Building event-driven architectures
sessions.a: Event-driven architectures help development teams operate more independently, release features faster, and build more scalable applications. In this workshop, learn the fundamentals of event-driven design using Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, and more. Through hands-on exercises, discover how to choose the right AWS messaging and eventing service for your use case, design loosely coupled systems that scale independently, and optimize for both cost and performance. Whether you're starting your event-driven journey or refining existing patterns, you'll leave with practical skills you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Building event-driven architectures in the age of AI agents
sessions.a: Event-driven architectures have powered serverless applications for a decade. Now AI agents bring non-deterministic producers, multi-step reasoning chains, and agent-to-agent coordination via events. Learn how the patterns you already know, such as queues, events, and retries, evolve when your consumers are autonomous agents rather than just microservices.
