Whether you're starting your event-driven journey or refining existing patterns, you'll leave with practical skills you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Building event-driven, multi-agent architectures on serverless
sessions.a: Multi-agent AI systems need communication patterns that are decoupled, observable, and scalable. In this chalk talk, we map out agent coordination patterns using Amazon EventBridge: peer-to-peer messaging, supervisor-worker hierarchies, and broadcast coordination. We discuss how to choose an orchestration approach, handle multi-agent failure modes like cascading hallucinations and circular delegation, and design real-time coordination protocols that prevent conflicting actions.

sessions.t: Building fast with automated reasoning at Amazon S3 scale
sessions.a: S3 has a long history of using automated reasoning, but a core challenge has been applying these techniques to large systems while maintaining development velocity. Over time, we've learned to balance cutting-edge science with engineering velocity to accelerate development. We'll share diverse techniques for validating critical storage components, from black-box model-based validation using formal API specifications, to white-box verification with specialized concurrency checkers for ensuring transaction serializability and crash consistency. You'll learn how S3 engineers and scientists are advancing systems verification with new tools and ideas that you can apply to your own systems.

sessions.t: Building for Always-On: Resilient Trading to Agentic AI on Modern Data Foundation (sponsored by Cognizant)
sessions.a: Learn how LPL Financial built an always-on trading platform on AWS that supports 32,000+ financial advisors with resilient, multi-region architecture for mission-critical, latency-sensitive workloads. Discover how a unified data foundation across trading, brokerage, and custodial systems creates a trusted layer for innovation, and learn the realities of deploying agentic AI in a regulated broker-dealer environment. Gain practical insights into architecture patterns, governance, real-time data access, key tradeoffs, and lessons learned that can help accelerate your own modernization and AI initiatives. This presentation is brought to you by Cognizant, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building globally distributed applications with DynamoDB global tables
sessions.a: Failures happen. Regions degrade, Availability Zones go offline, and networks partition. In this session, learn how to architect Amazon DynamoDB applications that maintain availability and data integrity across a spectrum of failure modes, from single-AZ impairments to full-Region disruptions. Explore the DynamoDB primitives that underpin resilience, including global tables, multi-Region strong consistency, backup and restore, snapshots, and streaming, and how to compose them into patterns that meet strict RTO and RPO objectives. Using scenarios drawn from recent large-scale events, examine trade-offs between consistency, latency, and availability, and discover operational best practices for detecting, responding to, and recovering from failures.

sessions.t: Building high-quality data products for AI agents
sessions.a: AI agents are only as effective as the data they rely on. This chalk talk focuses on how to build and manage high-quality data products and contextual information for use by AI agents. You'll learn how to deliver accurate, up-to-date, and well-governed data for AI systems, including context engineering, RAG strategies, fine-tuning dataset curation, and automated quality checks. We'll cover how to manage AI context, handle data drift, and perform classical data management activities in the Agentic AI world.

sessions.t: Building interactive web applications on AWS Serverless
sessions.a: Web applications need fast responses, server-side rendering, and real-time updates, but managing origin servers, CDN configurations, and scaling infrastructure pulls you away from building features. In this builders' session, deploy a full-stack web application entirely on AWS Serverless. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll configure routing and static asset delivery, implement server-side rendering with consistent low latency, and add real-time interactivity. Walk away with a working application and deployment patterns for production web workloads. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Building lightning-fast web apps
sessions.a: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this lightning talk, hear how a customer built a full-stack web application entirely on AWS Serverless services, from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. They cover architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical takeaways for production-ready serverless web development.

sessions.t: Building Managed Security Practices with AWS Security Hub Extended and Partners
sessions.a: Your customers don't want more tools—they want outcomes. In this session, learn how AWS Security Hub Extended, AWS Artifact, and other tools combine to create a powerful foundation for partners delivering managed security and compliance services at scale. Security Hub Extended gives MSSPs a single pane of glass and OCSF-normalized findings that eliminate integration headaches. Pair this with our extended security portfolio to create the foundation for audit-ready compliance frameworks across financial services, healthcare, and public sector, and you have a differentiated "detect, respond, and prove compliance" offering your customers can't get elsewhere. Whether you're an MSSP building SOC-as-a-Service, an ISV integrating into the Security Hub ecosystem, or a consulting partner delivering compliance transformations, this session shows you the better together story of working with AWS.

sessions.t: Building migration readiness when the timeline is tight
sessions.a: Most organizations don't get years to plan a large-scale migration. Licensing changes, compliance requirements, or rising hardware costs can compress your timeline fast. This session covers how to build readiness quickly so your team can move hundreds of workloads with confidence. Learn how to assess your environment, build team capability, and match the right migration pathway to each workload. Hear from a customer who moved hundreds of applications under real pressure with zero critical outages. Walk away with a practical framework for getting your organization ready to move at any speed.

sessions.t: Building modern web applications on AWS Serverless
sessions.a: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this session, discover how to build full-stack web applications entirely on AWS serverless services—from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. Learn architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers. Explore how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical blueprints for production-ready serverless web development.

sessions.t: Building multi-tenant RAG: Isolation, cost, and scale
sessions.a: Customers building multi-tenant RAG platforms must balance tenant data isolation, cost, and operational scale. This chalk talk examines a production architecture serving thousands of tenants on Amazon Bedrock and compares multiple approaches. We whiteboard isolation patterns, tenant routing, per-knowledge-base scaling and limits, managed embedding models, and multimodal document parsing. We will discuss the tradeoffs that determine when to build your own retrieval stack and when to use a fully managed knowledge base.

sessions.t: Building ontologies with Amazon Neptune
sessions.a: Large language models pattern-match on tokens, not business meaning, which causes subtle failures when applied to enterprise data. Ontologies address this by giving AI systems a formal structure for knowledge: a graph defining what exists, how entities relate, and what questions are meaningful. In this workshop, build an ontology-driven semantic layer using Amazon Neptune to power accurate, trustworthy agentic workloads across diverse data sources. Bring a laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Building ontologies with Amazon Neptune
sessions.a: Large language models pattern-match on tokens, not business meaning, which causes subtle failures when applied to enterprise data. Ontologies address this by giving AI systems a formal structure for knowledge: a graph defining what exists, how entities relate, and what questions are meaningful. In this workshop, build an ontology-driven semantic layer using Amazon Neptune to power accurate, trustworthy agentic workloads across diverse data sources. Bring a laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Building optimized enterprise HPC systems for CAE and CFD
sessions.a: High-fidelity Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations require significant compute infrastructure. We’ll discuss how organizations are migrating CAE and CFD workloads from on premises to AWS, combining scalable HPC infrastructure with cloud-native engineering applications to accelerate product development. Learn how to architect your enterprise HPC system to optimize cost, queue wait times, and throughput with Amazon EC2 HPC-optimized instances, Savings Plans, and Amazon FSx.

sessions.t: Building Production Graph Pipelines with Nodestream and Amazon Neptune
sessions.a: Nodestream is an open source declarative framework for building, maintaining, and analyzing graph data, built collaboratively by engineers at Intuit and AWS. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Nodestream connects data sources like Apache Kafka, APIs, and files to graph databases with automatic schema migrations and zero database-specific code. We'll dive into the Amazon Neptune plugin, discuss how declarative pipelines eliminate brittle ETL, and share lessons learned from real world customer scenarios. Bring your graph data challenges and we'll solve them live.

sessions.t: Building Production-Ready Agents Securely: Lessons from AWS at Scale
sessions.a: Most AI agent demos work on stage but break in production. Real enterprise agents need multi-layer guardrails, tenant identity isolation, graceful degradation, and continuous evaluation. In this code talk, we share patterns from shipping two production security agent systems on AWS: one that investigates incidents across customer accounts, and one that helps security practitioners author threat detections. We cover practices that any team can adopt such as prompt injection defense, tenant-scoped sessions, circuit breakers, observability, and eval-driven improvement.

sessions.t: Building Proprietary Multi-Agentic AI Workflows for Low Latency and High Reliability (sponsored by Capital One)
sessions.a: Enterprise AI requires scalable, multi-agentic workflows capable of handling complex reasoning without sacrificing real-time speed. This session explores how Capital One designs proprietary multi-agent systems on AWS, optimized for governance, performance, and reliability. You’ll hear how state-of-the-art serving frameworks like vLLM, efficient distributed serving platforms like llm-d, and advanced agentic inference optimization techniques can enhance latency and boost throughput. We’ll showcase these principles through real-world applications, including complex real employee- and customer-facing banking use cases while meeting rigorous business standards around accuracy, reliability, and risk management. This presentation is brought to you by Capital One, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building real-time applications with event-driven architectures
sessions.a: Build real-time features using AWS AppSync Events in this hands-on builders' session. Working in small groups with guidance from AWS experts, you'll implement in-app notifications and live updates, configure WebSocket connections, and design data persistence strategies. Using provided code samples, you'll gain practical experience creating responsive, event-driven applications that push updates to connected clients instantly. By the end of this 60-minute session, you'll have working real-time patterns you can apply directly to your own applications. Bring your laptop and come ready to code!

sessions.t: Building resilience against ransomware using AWS Backup
sessions.a: To counter evolving cyber threats, organizations must fortify their backup infrastructure for recovery resilience. This session applies threat modeling to design a multi-account AWS Backup architecture across three pillars: immutability with isolation, integrity validation, and guaranteed accessibility. Walk through a phased reference architecture using logically air-gapped vaults for tamper-proof backups, restore testing and GuardDuty malware scanning for integrity assurance, and multi-party approval for secure recovery during account compromise. Learn how to define your minimum viable company to sequence recovery priorities, distinguish cyber RPO from operational RPO, and align your strategy to NIST CSF 2.0 for recovery resilience and business continuity.

sessions.t: Building resilient Amazon ECS applications: a multi-layer approach
sessions.a: In this interactive chalk talk, we explore how to build resilient Amazon ECS architectures by examining failure modes across multiple layers of the stack. We walk through specific scenarios such as deployment failures, Availability Zone impairments, and dependency cascades that cycle tasks faster than you can debug them. We discuss architectural patterns, ECS capabilities for resilience, and common mistakes to avoid that turn minor issues into incidents. You'll leave with a concrete mental model for hardening your ECS services and a checklist you can apply to your own workloads.

sessions.t: Building resilient authentication with Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication
sessions.a: Authentication is the front door to your app, and if that's unavailable, everything is unreachable. Amazon Cognito is the managed CIAM service that handles sign-up, sign-in, federation, and threat protection at scale. In this chalk talk, learn how Cognito's new multi-Region replication (MRR) unlocks resilient authentication across Regions. We'll whiteboard reference architectures for B2C, B2B, and M2M workloads, cover implementation considerations like customer managed keys and in-Region dependencies, and walk through failover strategies. Leave ready to architect authentication that keeps customers connected.

sessions.t: Building resilient deployment pipelines with Amazon ECS
sessions.a: Every application has a different risk profile when you ship a new version. A payments API needs different safeguards than a marketing page. In this workshop, learn how to match Amazon ECS deployment strategies to your workload requirements. Configure blue/green deployments for services requiring instant failback, canary deployments for APIs where you validate with real traffic before full cutover, and linear deployments for gradual migrations that build confidence at each step. Integrate pause hooks for manual approvals and external validation, and set alarm-based triggers that automatically revert bad releases before customers notice. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Building searchable live sports with AWS Elemental and Amazon CloudFront
sessions.a: Live sports fans no longer watch one feed and wait for the recap - they expect every angle live and every key play instantly findable. In this session, see how you turn live sports into searchable fan moments on AWS. Using AWS Elemental inference, the platform generates highlight clips in real time and pairs them with conversational AI powered by Amazon Bedrock, so fans can ask for "the catch in the third quarter" and get it in seconds instead of hours. Then go deeper into the delivery workflow: composing multi-view experiences so viewers follow simultaneous matches and camera angles, enriching clips with AI-generated titles and captions, and delivering live feeds and clips globally through a single Amazon CloudFront architecture.

sessions.t: Building Serverless AI agents
sessions.a: AI agents need more than an LLM and a prompt. Production agents require tool execution with least-privilege isolation, orchestration that recovers from partial failures, and observability that tracks token spend alongside function duration. In this chalk talk, we discuss architectural patterns for Serverless AI agents: model routing across providers and cost tiers, fault-tolerant orchestration with Step Functions and Lambda durable functions, isolated code execution using MicroVMs, and state management for long-running multi-step workflows. We whiteboard the decisions that matter for your workload shape and where each pattern introduces complexity you may not need.

sessions.t: Building serverless applications with Terraform
sessions.a: Master the integration of serverless technology with Infrastructure as Code using Terraform on AWS. In this hands-on workshop, learn to efficiently define, deploy, and maintain serverless architectures—from Lambda functions and API Gateway endpoints to DynamoDB tables and EventBridge rules. Whether you're new to Terraform or looking to apply it to serverless workloads, you'll gain practical experience writing reusable modules, managing state, and automating deployments across environments. Walk away with patterns you can immediately apply to your own serverless projects. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Building Serverless applications at AI speed
sessions.a: Manually wiring up Lambda functions, API Gateway routes, and IaC templates for every new service is repetitive work that AI handles well. In this builders' session, use Kiro to go from natural language specifications to a deployed serverless application. You'll configure MCP tool servers to give the AI agent access to AWS APIs, author steering documents that produce consistent output, and iterate on generated infrastructure until it passes validation. Walk away with techniques for getting reliable, production-ready code from AI-assisted workflows. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Building Serverless distributed data processing workloads
sessions.a: Processing large-scale data shouldn't require provisioning clusters or managing batch infrastructure. In this builders' session, design and deploy a distributed data processing pipeline using AWS Step Functions Distributed Map, AWS Lambda, and Amazon S3. Working in small groups, you'll implement fan-out patterns that process thousands of objects in parallel, handle partial failures gracefully, and optimize for cost and throughput. Learn when Distributed Map is the right choice versus other parallelization strategies, and walk away with a reusable pipeline template. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Building stateful AI workflows with Serverless orchestration
sessions.a: AI workflows need state such as conversation history, intermediate results, and human approvals, but managing it shouldn't require a database and custom recovery logic. In this builders' session, build a stateful AI workflow that checkpoints progress, recovers from failures automatically, and pauses for external callbacks. Working hands-on with AWS experts, you'll implement multi-step reasoning chains with retry semantics, compare orchestration approaches for different workflow shapes, and deploy a working agent pipeline. Walk away with patterns for choosing the right orchestration tool for your workload. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Building stateful AI workflows with Serverless orchestration

sessions.t: Building the Construction Cloud: How Procore AI &Amazon Bedrock Power the Built World (sponsored by Procore)
sessions.a: Construction generates massive volumes of structured and unstructured data, such as drawings, RFIs, and safety reports, that most AI infrastructure isn't built to handle. In this session, we'll break down how Amazon Bedrock's model access, guardrails, and enterprise controls power Procore AI, and why that combination is what makes construction-specific AI viable at enterprise scale. You'll leave with a clear picture of the architecture, and why we think this is the first real blueprint for AI in the built environment. This presentation is brought to you by Procore, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building the data architecture that survives agentic analytics (sponsored by Edelbyte)
sessions.a: Human queries are bounded, repeatable, and predictable, so techniques like caching, sampling, and precomputation keep them fast and affordable. AI agents are none of those. One prompt becomes dozens of novel, complex queries at machine speed, so caching an agent's curiosity is nearly impossible. At a leading automotive R&D group, 1,400 engineers and their agents query 200 petabytes of vehicle telemetry, with 600 terabytes ingested daily, to engineer higher-quality, more reliable vehicles and reach production faster. This session shows the AWS architecture behind it and how it delivers real-time analytics with full retention at the scale agents have made standard. This presentation is brought to you by Edelbyte, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building the Intelligent Health System, CXO blueprint for the agentic era (sponsored by PwC)
sessions.a: The health systems that will lead the next decade are not simply digitizing existing processes. They are reimagining what a health system looks like with AI native to every layer. On AWS that means a unified data foundation across electornic health records, claims, images, devices, and genomics; real-time AI at the point of decision; agentic workflows that absorb entire categories of administrative burden; and governance that holds up to audit at scale. Chief Information, Digital, and AI Officers building this now share what worked and what they would do differently. Attendees leave with a practical sequence, from data foundation to agentic deployment. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building the Intelligent Utility: PG&E’s AI and Cloud Transformation on AWS (sponsored by PwC)
sessions.a: PG&E and PwC will share how they are harnessing AWS to modernize utility operations through AI, automation, and cloud-native engineering. Learn how a unified data and observability foundation delivers real-time operational intelligence, improves system resilience, and enables faster, more informed decision-making. Hear practical lessons on scaling AI responsibly, operationalizing automation, and creating measurable business outcomes across complex enterprise environments. Attendees will leave with a blueprint for transforming traditional operations into intelligent, data-driven services while building a foundation that can support the next wave of generative AI and autonomous operations capabilities. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building the semantic intelligence layer for enterprise AI agents
sessions.a: Every AI agent in the enterprise reasons better when it shares a common semantic understanding of the business. In this chalk talk, we show you how to build an Agentic Intelligence Layer that resolves meaning across every system and makes it innately consumable by any agent. We break down how to combine semantic embeddings, knowledge graph relationships, and natural-language memories into a single, governed layer that every agent reads from and writes back to. We take product and customer intelligence as the first domains and show how the same architecture extends to supply chain, operations, finance, and workforce. The result is a semantic intelligence layer that compounds learning across the business and transforms everything from demand forecasting to conversational commerce to enterprise decision-making.

sessions.t: Building Trust into Agentic AI on AWS in the Age of Autonomous Agents (sponsored by Check Point)
sessions.a: AI agents are evolving from assistants into autonomous systems that call APIs and take actions on behalf of users. Traditional perimeter controls aren't enough; threats now emerge from prompt injection, excessive permissions, and unmonitored tool use. In this session, we'll show how Check Point's AI security intelligence integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to enforce real-time guardrails at the agent runtime layer inspecting intent, validating actions, and preventing policy violations before they execute. Walk away with a practical framework for securing agentic AI on AWS with Check Point. This presentation is brought to you by Check Point, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Building Your AI Practice: From Business Model to Partner Revenue
sessions.a: Enterprises expect agentic outcomes. That changes how solutions are built and deployed. Traditional delivery practices are evolving to agentic delivery, outcome-based models, and scalable IP transacted through AWS Marketplace. Partners moving first are delivering measurable business outcomes faster and building new revenue alongside their customers. In this session, learn the three-stage practice-building path. See how Forward Deployed Engineering gives partners a new engagement architecture and faster delivery: pod-based, and time-boxed. See where AWS co-investment programs and AI-specific enrollment paths de-risk each stage of practice growth. Walk away with example GTM models and a concrete action plan.

sessions.t: Building your first event-driven application
sessions.a: A customer places an order. Inventory updates. Payment processes. Notifications fire. In a monolith, one failure cascades through everything. In this builders' session, build a retail order system where each step runs independently using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. Through guided exercises, you'll publish and subscribe to events, handle failures in one service without breaking others, and trace event flows across your system. No prior event-driven experience required—you'll leave with a working application and the core patterns for decomposing synchronous workflows into resilient, asynchronous systems. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Building zero-trust personal AI with EC2 confidential computing
sessions.a: Learn how Bee built a personal AI assistant where privacy is cryptographically guaranteed - not policy-promised. Bee processes user data exclusively within hardware-isolated EC2 Confidential VMs powered by AWS Nitro, where no one - including Amazon - can access unencrypted data. We'll dive into NitroTPM attestation that lets devices verify server integrity before sharing keys, Sigstore transparency logs for auditability, mutual TLS with embedded attestation proofs, and key lifecycle management within encrypted VM memory. A practical blueprint for building zero-trust AI on Amazon EC2.

sessions.t: Build interactive web apps with AWS Lambda
sessions.a: Web applications need persistent connections, session state, and native HTTP handling - capabilities that don't map obviously to Lambda's request-response model. In this session, see how to run web frameworks like Express, Hono, and Next.js directly on Lambda using runtime adapters that preserve the framework's native patterns. If you're running containerized web apps today, we walk through practical migration paths that move your existing framework code to Lambda with minimal changes.

sessions.t: Build It, Govern It, Ship It: A Hands-On Multi-Agent System with NVIDIA Agent Toolkit (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.a: Building an AI agent is easy. Building one you can trust, safe, affordable, and contained, is the hard part. In this session we build a working agent end to end on AWS using the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit: Nemotron reasoning models served as NIM microservices on AWS GPUs, NeMo Guardrails screening every prompt and response at the inference boundary, NeMo Switchyard routing easy requests to smaller models and hard ones to larger models to cut inference cost, and OpenShell sandboxing tool execution at the kernel with Landlock, seccomp, and eBPF. You will see each layer added live, then watch a side-by-side cost and latency comparison of routed versus un-routed traffic. Everything runs on open foundations, on Amazon Bedrock and NIM-on-AWS. Leave knowing how to assemble safe, cost-aware agents from open components you can adopt one piece at a time. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build It or Bring It: Getting AI Agents into CX Faster
sessions.a: Getting agentic AI from prototype to production in your customer experience application is slow, and the gap is widening. In this chalk talk we give you two levers to close it on Amazon Connect Customer. Build new AI agents on the agentic CX designer canvas, describing what you want in natural language and applying enterprise guardrails to reach production-grade quickly. Or bring the agents your business has already built, anywhere, and orchestrate them through Connect Customer using the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol. We demonstrate both, then whiteboard how they fit together architecturally. Come ready to challenge the design and share where you would use each.

sessions.t: Build layered defenses for agentic AI from prompt to tool execution
sessions.a: Attendees build a defense-in-depth security architecture for an AI agent. You start with a pre-deployed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with Lambda tools, then run adversarial test scenarios to observe how gateway and tools respond without controls. You layer defenses from Bedrock Guardrails for prompt-attack detection, through AgentCore Policy Engine with Cedar policies-based tool authorization, including Dogwood temporal policies, and finally native rate limits paired with CloudWatch anomaly detection. By progressing through each scenario again, you verify how each protection aligns with a layered security pattern you can apply to your agentic workload.

sessions.t: Build long-running agents that persist for days on AgentCore
sessions.a: Most agents handle a single request and forget everything. Production workloads are different — an incident investigation spans hours, a document review takes days, a customer onboarding stretches across weeks. These agents need to persist state, survive restarts, and pick up exactly where they left off. This session covers how to build long-running agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Runtime for durable execution and Memory for cross-session context. Learn checkpointing patterns, human-in-the-loop pause and resume, and cost strategies that keep idle agents from burning through your budget.

sessions.t: Build low latency real-time bidding workloads with AWS RTB Fabric
sessions.a: With the growth of digital media, including streaming video and retail media, customers that operate advertising platforms need to buy, sell, deliver, and measure millions of ad transactions per second while meeting stringent latency requirements. In this chalk talk, you will learn how to run real-time bidding workloads with your AdTech partners on a dedicated network in the cloud using AWS RTB Fabric. You will learn how to setup, onboard, and integrate AWS RTB Fabric with your supply and demand-side-platforms. Additionally, you will learn about key features including the core network, modules, and pricing model of the service.

Automate testing and docs with hooks, enforce AI behavior with steering rules, and extend capabilities through powers. Ideal for federal devs and architects.

sessions.t: Build multi-agent warranty and repair intelligence for automotive
sessions.a: Warranty and repair workflows span claim history, technical service bulletins, supplier quality records, and regulatory thresholds — a high-cost, fragmented data challenge for automotive OEMs. In this builders session, construct a multi-agent warranty and repair intelligence system using Strands SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Build a triage agent that classifies incoming cases, a research agent that queries Bedrock Knowledge Bases across TSBs and repair records, and a resolution agent that synthesizes findings into a structured decision with cited evidence routed for technician approval via human-in-the-loop controls.

sessions.t: Build Multi-Agent Workflows with Amazon Quick, MCP & AgentCore
sessions.a: Design and build a multi-agent system inside Amazon Quick where specialized agents collaborate to automate complex business processes. Connect to enterprise systems through MCP servers on Bedrock AgentCore, implement inter-agent communication, configure OAuth 2.0 authentication, and deploy autonomous workflows using Quick Flows. Modeled after production deployments running 12+ coordinated agents across ERP, finance, and procurement, you'll leave with a working multi-agent solution you can replicate in your own environment.

sessions.t: Build multi-agent workflows with Strands Agents SDK on AWS
sessions.a: In this hands-on workshop, build a multi-agent system using the Strands Agents open source SDK. You will create specialized agents with distinct roles, connect them via MCP for tool access, implement agent-to-agent delegation patterns, and add memory for stateful conversations. Deploy and test your multi-agent workflow end-to-end. Walk away with working code and reusable patterns for orchestrating collaborative AI agents using open source tooling.

sessions.t: Build nanochat models with PyTorch and Trainium-Easier than you think
sessions.a: Can you train an LLM on AWS Trainium, our purpose built AI chip for better price performance, using PyTorch with minimal code changes? We'll show you with nanochat, a 560M-parameter GPT you can train in about two hours on a single Trainium instance using familiar PyTorch workflows. We cover end-to-end training from data preparation through distributed configuration to model test practices with interactive chat — showing what works out of the box and what few changes are required. Walk away ready to train your own LLM on Trainium with PyTorch.

sessions.t: Build Once, Deploy Anywhere: Agentic AI from Data Center to Edge with Qualcomm & AWS (sponsored by Qualcomm)
sessions.a: AI is moving beyond the cloud, requiring developers to deploy intelligent workloads across data centers, edge infrastructure, vehicles, industrial systems, PCs, and mobile devices. The challenge is scaling AI efficiently across diverse hardware environments. In this session, learn how Qualcomm and AWS enable developers to build agentic AI applications across the compute continuum, from cloud training to real-time edge and on-device inference. Discover how open frameworks, portable AI runtimes, and streamlined workflows accelerate development and deployment. Through examples spanning automotive, IoT, industrial edge, mobile, datacenter, and cloud use cases, explore how a unified developer experience reduces complexity, increases flexibility, and helps deliver scalable AI applications anywhere. This presentation is brought to you by Qualcomm, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build on top of large codebases without breaking your code
sessions.a: Your AI agent writes code fast, but when you unleash it on a large codebase, context can fill up quickly and the agent can make questionable implementation choices. Learn how Kiro uses neurosymbolic techniques to understand what you want to build, removing ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. Then, learn simple practices you can use to keep your agent implementation surgical, and detect drift before it spreads all over your codebase.

sessions.t: Build optimized, resilient inference endpoints on Amazon SageMaker AI
sessions.a: Deploy, optimize, and monitor an LLM inference endpoint end-to-end on Amazon SageMaker AI. In this hands-on workshop, use Inference Recommender to discover optimal configurations — reducing search time from weeks to days, learn how to train EAGLE speculative decoding heads on your own data for up to 2.5× throughput gains, and benchmark results with NVIDIA AIPerf. Then, configure capacity-aware instance pools with priority-based GPU fallback and weighted autoscaling for production resilience. Throughout, interact with endpoints via OpenAI-compatible APIs. Leave with working notebooks and production-ready deployment patterns you can apply immediately.

sessions.t: Build orchestration agents for AWS Glue ETL
sessions.a: What happens when you give an AI agent the keys to your ETL infrastructure? In this builder session, you'll build an agentic workflow using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that accepts natural language instructions and autonomously orchestrates ETL jobs on AWS Glue. Using MCP servers, your agent will reason job configurations, construct parameters, execute transformations, interact with the Glue Data Catalog, handle retries on failure, and surface results—all from a single conversational prompt.

sessions.t: Build production AI assistant with Hugging Face Libraries and models
sessions.a: Every product team wants an embedded AI assistant—but closed APIs erode margins and limit customization. In this Chalk Talk, we architect a production-ready solution using open building blocks: retrieval, reranking, and generation models working together in real time. We diagram how to fine-tune for your domain, orchestrate multi-model pipelines, and serve thousands of concurrent users cost-efficiently. Walk away understanding how Native Hugging Face models and libraries on AWS Trainium let you own your AI stack and scale.

sessions.t: Build Production Grade Agents with OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by OpenAI)
sessions.a: Learn how to ship agents for your applications with Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents, powered by OpenAI, and accelerate development with Codex agents. Explore architecture patterns for reliable, governable workflows across enterprise systems, covering tool use, evaluations, observability, identity, and permissions. See how to keep agent behavior measurable, access secure, and actions aligned with organizational policies.

sessions.t: Build provable AI agents with Automated Reasoning checks
sessions.a: Neurosymbolic AI pairs the language understanding of LLMs with the mathematical rigor of automated reasoning, enabling agent decisions that are provably correct, not just statistically likely. In this hands-on workshop, you'll take real-world business rules (e.g. insurance eligibility or financial compliance) and formalize them into Automated Reasoning policies that agents invoke at decision time. Starting from natural-language documents, you'll translate requirements into verifiable logic, then integrate your policies with agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, validating outputs at inference time. Leave able to build Automated Reasoning policies that guarantee correctness, where every decision is logically grounded, traceable, and auditable.

sessions.t: Build ransomware recovery with AWS Backup air-gapped vaults
sessions.a: When ransomware compromises your account, your backups are the last line of defense. The question is whether they're isolated, verified, and accessible when you need them most. In this workshop, you'll build ransomware recovery capabilities using AWS Backup logically air-gapped vaults, restore testing, and Backup Audit Manager. Working through a simulated account compromise scenario, you'll implement protection across three pillars: immutability with isolation, integrity validation, and predictable availability. Configure vault isolation policies, validate backup integrity, orchestrate recovery when primary credentials are compromised, and walk away with a tested recovery playbook. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

sessions.t: Build real-time applications with AWS Amplify
sessions.a: Learn how to create applications that use real-time data to keep users engaged. In this workshop, build a multiplayer application with live updates and group chat functionality using AWS Amplify Gen 2. Define your backend—data model, auth rules, and real-time subscriptions—in TypeScript and deploy to a cloud sandbox in seconds. Connect your frontend to a serverless backend powered by AWS AppSync WebSockets. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build Reliable AI Agents on AWS with Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: When your data changes frequently, RAG helps your agent access the latest information at query time. Fine-tuning an LLM with domain data brings precision in how the agent responds and executes. In this hands-on lab, build reliable AI agents by fine-tuning an LLM on Amazon SageMaker AI for valid tool-call output and consistent persona, and connect it to Amazon Bedrock RAG to ground responses in your latest policies and customer data.

sessions.t: Build Resilient AI Platforms with Oracle AI Database@AWS (sponsored by Oracle)
sessions.a: AI applications demand continuous access to trusted, business-critical data. In this lightning session, learn how Oracle Maximum Availability Architecture helps protect AI workloads running on Oracle AI Database@AWS. Explore proven patterns for high availability, disaster recovery, data protection, and automated failover across AWS Availability Zones and Regions. See how capabilities such as Oracle Active Data Guard and integrated backup and recovery services help minimize downtime, reduce data loss, and keep AI applications operating through planned maintenance and unexpected disruptions. This presentation is brought to you by Oracle, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build resilient apps on AWS: AI-driven resilience at any scale
sessions.a: Most teams discover resilience gaps during outages, not before. In this interactive chalk talk, you'll use the next generation of AWS Resilience Hub to map user journeys, define recovery objectives, discover dependencies, and run AI-powered failure mode assessments. You'll implement high availability improvements, deploy multi-region disaster recovery, and run the right automated disaster recovery tests that fit your architecture and use case. Walk away with a repeatable framework you can plug into your own environment next week.

sessions.t: Build, run, and improve: inside a production AI inference platform (sponsored by Baseten)
sessions.a: Getting a model to work is the easy part. Keeping it fast, cheap, and reliable in production is the hard part. Sai Maddali, Product Manager at Baseten, walks through the platform behind some of the highest-volume inference workloads running today: how GPU capacity is sourced and managed across clouds, how runtimes are tuned per workload, and how dedicated inference, model APIs, and training sit on one pool of compute. He shows why the teams pulling ahead treat build, run, and improve as a single loop, and what that changes about latency, cost, and model quality. This presentation is brought to you by Baseten, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build scalable streaming and messaging applications with Amazon Kinesis and AmazonMSK
sessions.a: Messaging and streaming should be simple, elastic, and cost-efficient, no matter how your workloads change. In this session, discover how Amazon MSK and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is making it easier and more affordable to build messaging and streaming applications at any scale. Learn how you can stop worrying about capacity planning and reduce costs automatically as your traffic scales up and down. See how you can land your streaming data directly into Amazon S3 and S3 Tables without building or managing separate pipelines so you can focus on deriving insights instead of maintaining infrastructure. Join us to see how these innovations come together to help you move faster, spend less, and eliminate operational overhead at any scale.

sessions.t: Build secure APIs faster with Amazon API Gateway and Kiro CLI
sessions.a: Secure your APIs with confidence and build them faster. In this builders' session, dive into Amazon API Gateway authorization strategies including Amazon Cognito user pools, Amazon Verified Permissions, Lambda custom authorizers, IAM authorizers, and machine-to-machine scenarios. Through hands-on exercises, implement each strategy and understand their trade-offs. Once secured, ship faster—use Kiro CLI, OpenAPI, and MCP servers to go from spec to deployed API in minutes. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Build self-healing agents from diagnosis to disaster recovery
sessions.a: Most AI agents stop at the root cause report, leaving engineers to act under pressure. In this workshop, build three cooperating agents on a pre-provisioned workload using Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon Application Recovery Controller. A live app throws 4XX errors and a troubleshooting agent runs root cause analysis. Then build a remediation agent to apply the fix. When 5XX errors signal an Availability Zone impairment, you'll extend the remediation agent to consult a resilience agent before acting. Leave with a working reference implementation you can adapt to your financial services or enterprise environment.

sessions.t: Build self-healing Serverless applications with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.a: Production incidents at 2 a.m. don't wait for your team to wake up. In this builders' session, work with a deployed serverless application and use AWS DevOps Agent to resolve real-world failures autonomously. You'll inject common production issues—such as Lambda throttling, timeout cascades, DynamoDB throughput exceeded, and SQS dead-letter queue buildup—then configure the agent to perform root cause analysis, propose remediation, and apply fixes. You'll tune detection sensitivity, set approval gates for automated actions, and evaluate where autonomous remediation is safe versus where human oversight is required. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Build Self-Service AI Experiences with Amazon Connect Customer AI Agents
sessions.a: Customers expect instant answers about their orders, accounts, and open cases. In this hands-on lab, build a self-service AI agent in Amazon Connect that autonomously resolves customer requests by looking up profiles, searching and creating cases through MCP tools, and retrieving FAQ answers from a knowledge base. Configure AI Guardrails for content safety and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context for human agents.

sessions.t: Build, simulate, and validate physical AI-driven robotic systems
sessions.a: Commissioning industrial robots typically takes weeks of physical testing. Digital twins with real-time physics simulation and multi-agent AI optimization can compress that timeline from weeks to hours. In this builders session, construct a digital twin of a multi-robot manufacturing cell using virtual PLCs and controllers, real fieldbus connectivity, real-time physics simulation in NVIDIA Omniverse, and Amazon EC2 as the compute backbone. Leave with an AI-optimized robotic program validated against real-world conditions before ever touching real hardware. Generated in 60 minutes using open standards and open toolchains, the result is a reusable blueprint that scales across cells, lines, and sites.

sessions.t: Build stablecoin infrastructure from key management to agentic payments
sessions.a: Stablecoins are redefining payments and settlement infrastructure in financial services. In this session, build a production-ready stablecoin infrastructure on AWS spanning secure key management with AWS Key Management Service and and AWS Nitro Enclaves, multi-signature governance workflows, token minting/burning/swapping operations, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments for autonomous agent-to-agent transactions. Get hands-on experience building wallet infrastructure and executing USDC stablecoin operations end-to-end. Walk away with a working architecture that bridges traditional key management with the emerging agentic commerce paradigm.

sessions.t: Build stateful agentic AI workflows with Aurora, MCP, and AgentCore
sessions.a: Most agentic AI architectures stitch together separate stores for vectors and workflow state, adding cost and operational overhead. In this session, explore how Aurora PostgreSQL consolidates these roles into a single database, using pgvector for semantic retrieval, PostgreSQL full-text search for keyword queries, and native state persistence for multi-agent checkpointing. Learn to connect agents directly to Aurora using Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, govern every interaction with row-level security and audit trails, and orchestrate resilient, stateful workflows with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, and LangGraph without additional infrastructure. Leave with reusable patterns for governed, real-time agentic systems.

sessions.t: Build the Agentic Workplace: What's New on the Slack Developer Platform (sponsored by Salesforce)
sessions.a: Slack is becoming a multiplayer work operating system, where humans and AI agents build together, not just chat. This session shows AWS developers how to ship on the modern Slack Platform: Code Channels, a new space where agents like Claude Code, Devin, and Cursor collaborate with teams in real time; the Slack Agent Kit for building first-class agents; deep bidirectional MCP support, including the Slackbot MCP Client; Real-Time Search (RTS) for grounding agents in live workspace context; and Block Kit for rich, interactive UI. Leave with a clear path to build your first agentic app on Slack. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build the full agent optimization loop on AgentCore
sessions.a: How do you know your agent is still performing? Stop guessing. This workshop walks you through the full optimization loop on AgentCore: instrument with OpenTelemetry traces, score with built-in and custom evaluators, generate data-backed recommendations that rewrite your system prompt or tool descriptions, validate offline with batch evaluation, then split live traffic with A/B testing through AgentCore Gateway until you have statistical confidence to promote. You will run every step hands-on, ship a measurably better agent configuration, and leave with a repeatable process that replaces guess-and-check prompt iteration with evidence.

sessions.t: Build the Patient Record Your Healthcare AI Agents Actually Need
sessions.a: The average US patient has records scattered across 40+ systems. Medication lists conflict, allergies are duplicated, and clinical notes contradict structured data. Every AI agent you connect downstream inherits that mess. In this builder session, you use AWS HealthLake to resolve patient identities across fragmented sources, normalize clinical concepts to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm, and produce a unified, queryable FHIR record. Then you use a unified SDK to wire Amazon Connect Health agents to your clean data layer, simulate a patient encounter, and generate a structured clinical note that writes back to HealthLake. You leave with a deployable data foundation that accelerates Connect Health agent integration today and supports any custom agent you choose to connect tomorrow.

sessions.t: Build the right inference strategy on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Generative AI workloads place very different demands on inference. Customer support chatbots and coding assistants may prioritize responsiveness, while large-scale document processing can favor greater cost efficiency. Some workloads can tolerate flexible processing times, while others need predictable capacity and performance. Healthcare applications may also need inference processing to remain within a specific geography. Learn how to match Amazon Bedrock inference offerings to different workload needs, balancing performance and cost while meeting data residency requirements.

sessions.t: Build the Right Next Thing: A Forward Deployed Approach to AI ROI (sponsored by Slalom)
sessions.a: Two years ago, standing up generative AI technology was the hard part. Today, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore make the path to production more straightforward—but technology alone does not create value. AI initiatives often stall because ROI is undefined and business, user, and technical priorities are disconnected. Learn how Slalom’s Forward Deployed Expertise (FDX) model places a cross-functional team spanning product, business, industry, UX, and technology alongside customers. Using real data, these teams compare opportunities, prioritize the highest-value use cases, and co-build the right next thing through production, adoption, and measurable outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Slalom, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build Trust in AI with Agent Observability​ (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
sessions.a: AI agents behave (and fail) in unpredictable and nuanced ways that erode customer trust before engineering teams know anything is wrong. Teams want to deploy agents into critical business workflows, but it's hard to know if agents are behaving as intended or returning wrong answers.​ ​ In this talk, you’ll learn how to observe the entire AI stack, optimize tokenomics, and see a demo on how to evaluate and control agent behavior with guardrails to stop harmful or inaccurate outputs. All of this can be done in near real- time and at low cost.​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build Voice AI experiences with Amazon Polly and Transcribe
sessions.a: Give your applications a voice and ears. This session shows how Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text and Amazon Polly turns text into lifelike speech. See how to build real-time voice agents, and multilingual experiences, with practical patterns for latency, accuracy, and scale.

sessions.t: Build voice-enabled applications with Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe
sessions.a: We'll use Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe to add natural speech and accurate transcription to your applications. With Polly, you'll build expressive, emotionally engaged voices using its generative and long-form engines, covering streaming audio, speech marks for word-level timing, and newscaster styles. With Transcribe, you'll turn speech into text for captions, search, and analytics, handling real-time streaming and batch workloads. We'll show how these services work together to power voice agents, accessibility features, and conversational experiences, giving your applications the ability to both speak and listen naturally across a wide range of use cases and customer scenarios.

sessions.t: Build Wealth Advisor Agents with Full-Stack Agent Architecture
sessions.a: In this SimuLearn session, you leverage the entire Amazon Bedrock AgentCore platform ito build production-grade wealth management advisor. You create Memory resources for client personalization, configure a Gateway with MCP tool targets for account and market data, deploy specialist agents and a supervisor to Runtime, and authenticate users through Cognito. The result is a multi-agent advisor that recognizes each client, remembers their goals, and produces auditable financial guidance through governed tools.

sessions.t: Build What’s Next with an AI-Ready Programmable Network (sponsored by Lumen)
sessions.a: As AI, cloud, and data-intensive applications reshape business, infrastructure must become as dynamic as the workloads it supports. In this session, Lumen explores how programmable networking helps organizations simplify connectivity, improve performance, and securely scale across cloud, edge, and enterprise environments. Learn how real-time network orchestration gives teams greater agility and control while accelerating AI and modernization initiatives. Through examples, including Lumen’s collaboration with AWS to streamline enterprise connectivity, discover how a programmable network creates the resilient digital foundation needed to build what’s next. This presentation is brought to you by Lumen, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Build Your Agentic Transformation Roadmap with AWS Transform
sessions.a: You want to adopt agentic AI, but with hundreds of applications at different maturity levels, knowing where to start is the real challenge. In this chalk talk, we'll work through a practical framework for turning AWS Transform's automated agentic readiness and modernization analyses into a phased transformation plan. You'll see how to interpret portfolio-level scores, prioritize applications by business value and technical debt, sequence work into actionable phases, and connect readiness gaps to concrete next steps. Bring your portfolio challenges — you'll leave with a prioritization approach you can apply immediately

sessions.t: Build your AI data pipeline to Amazon S3 and Bedrock
sessions.a: Agentic AI applications are only as good as the data supporting them, and that data often lives across on-premises systems, other clouds, and distributed AWS storage. In this workshop, you'll build an end-to-end pipeline that moves data from these sources into Amazon S3 and connects it to Amazon Bedrock to build agentic applications. You'll configure data movement services including Storage Gateway, DataSync, and Transfer Family, establish secure transfer patterns, and integrate your migrated data into a gen AI workflow. Leave with a working architecture pattern for scalable data lakes that feed AI applications, grounded in real-world migration and processing scenarios.

sessions.t: Build your controls strategy org-wide to accelerate innovation
sessions.a: AWS Organizations policies drive governance through native service integrations. In this session, explore service control policies and resource control policies for data perimeters. Use declarative policies to enforce resource configurations, such as Amazon S3 public access restrictions, and centralize AWS Security Hub settings org-wide. Deploy AWS Config organizational rules and conformance packs for continuous compliance, leverage multi-party approval, enforce best practices via the AWS Control Tower controls catalog, and explore automated compliance assessments. Leave with a governance architecture driven by policy integrations.

sessions.t: Build Your Defense Factory for Continuous Defense with OpenAI (sponsored by OpenAI)
sessions.a: Put agents to work discovering vulnerabilities and driving fixes autonomously with OpenAI and AWS. Learn how to implement continuous defense with OpenAI tooling, Daybreak cyber models, and AWS infrastructure including Amazon Bedrock, drawing on lessons from OpenAI's internal Defense Factory. Explore routing findings to the right owners, reducing duplicate findings, and using development environments to validate vulnerabilities and test fixes. As broadly available cyber models help threat actors find decade-old vulnerabilities, this session focuses on how defenders can put continuous defense into practice.

sessions.t: Build your iOS CI/CD pipeline with AI agents on EC2 Mac
sessions.a: Build iOS CI/CD pipelines on Amazon EC2 Mac using AI-powered workflows with Kiro CLI and AWS MCP Server. Define infrastructure as declarative specs while AI agents guide deployment, explain concepts, and validate configurations. This hands-on workshop covers EC2 Mac architecture, dedicated hosts, Xcode automation, GitLab setup, and CloudWatch monitoring through interactive AI modules. Learn to collaborate with agents and balance automation with understanding. Gain practical experience in both EC2 Mac operations and modern spec-driven, AI-assisted development workflows for Apple platforms.

sessions.t: Build your own crew: hands-on with Kiro Crew
sessions.a: Kiro Crew is an open-source, multi-agent workspace you can bend to your own workflows. In this hands-on workshop, you'll put it to work. Hand your crew a real task and watching it plan, spawn parallel subagents, and gate each action for your approval. Then personalize: wire in the tools you already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold. Finally, assemble a purpose-built App to run a workflow end-to-end, from intake through review. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Built by Agents: Rethinking Reliability for AI-Native Companies (sponsored by Traversal)
sessions.a: AI is changing how quickly software can be built, shipped, and scaled. For AI-native companies, that can mean more services and complexity earlier in their growth. Many traditional reliability practices were designed for a different pace, when teams had more time to document, instrument, and build operational knowledge as they scaled. This conversation brings together leaders from a fast-growing legal AI company and one of the world’s largest digital banks, alongside leaders from Traversal, the AI SRE that diagnoses, fixes, and prevents incidents across enterprise environments. They’ll discuss how AI is changing development and operations, new failure modes in AI-native systems, how lean teams approach reliability as they scale, and the role of AI SREs in a broader shift toward AI understanding, managing, and improving production systems. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Canva's migration to AWS Graviton: from 2% to 54% in 10 months
sessions.a: Canva shifted its massive compute fleet from 2% to 23% Graviton adoption in just two months, then scaled to 54% over the following eight months, delivering meaningful cost savings and performance improvements along the way. This session covers the technical blockers the team encountered and overcame and the strategies that made rapid migration possible at enterprise scale. Walk away with practical, battle-tested patterns for planning and executing large-scale Arm migrations, whether you're just getting started or looking to accelerate an existing effort.

sessions.t: Can You Stop ALTERED SPIDER? A Live AWS Cloud Breach Challenge (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
sessions.a: The breach is underway. Watch CrowdStrike Experts put cloud detection and response into action during a live, audience-driven investigation of a simulated AWS intrusion. They will uncover evidence, determine the next move, and capture flags hidden across identities, workloads, and cloud activity. Get briefed on cloud-focused adversary ALTERED SPIDER, then connect the clues, contain the threat, and stop the attack. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Capital One's WorkSpaces Journey: 320 to 20,000 Desktops in 72hrs
sessions.a: Learn how to achieve enterprise-scale cloud desktop deployment from Capital One, who went from 320 manual provisions per day to 20,000 compliant desktops in 72 hours. Gain production-tested architectural patterns for meeting compliance requirements without slowing delivery. You'll also get a first look at the latest WorkSpaces innovations and our vision for the future of cloud desktops, including how we're expanding what's possible for IT teams managing modern workloads at scale. This session is for those migrating from VDI, scaling an existing fleet, or planning for what's next.

sessions.t: Catch it before production: Instrument your AI agents
sessions.a: You need visibility into your AI workloads before they reaches production, not after they fails, yet most teams have no telemetry on their agents at all. In this workshop, you instrument a live AI agent end to end, capturing token cost, latency, tool calls, and reasoning traces. You make the instrumentation decisions, build the dashboards and anomaly alerts. Leave with a working setup you can apply to your own agentic workloads.

sessions.t: Cell-based architecture: Designing blast-radius boundaries
sessions.a: Cell-based architecture limits the blast radius of failures by partitioning systems into independent, isolated units. But deciding cell boundaries — by customer, geography, or workload — involves trade-offs between operational complexity and fault isolation. This session reveals the decision framework for cell sizing, routing, and cross-cell coordination. You'll learn when cells outperform active-active patterns, how to implement cell-aware deployments, and the true operational cost of cell management. Walk away with a reusable pattern for systems, where failures stay contained, impact reduced, and availability increased.

sessions.t: Cell-based architecture: Designing blast-radius boundaries [REPEAT]
sessions.a: Cell-based architecture limits the blast radius of failures by partitioning systems into independent, isolated units. But deciding cell boundaries — by customer, geography, or workload — involves trade-offs between operational complexity and fault isolation. This session reveals the decision framework for cell sizing, routing, and cross-cell coordination. You'll learn when cells outperform active-active patterns, how to implement cell-aware deployments, and the true operational cost of cell management. Walk away with a reusable pattern for systems, where failures stay contained, impact reduced, and availability increased.

sessions.t: Centralize AWS PrivateLink endpoints at scale with Amazon VPC Lattice
sessions.a: Organizations scaling across multiple AWS accounts need AWS PrivateLink endpoints in every VPC, driving up costs and fragmenting access controls. In this session, construct a centralized endpoint architecture in a shared services VPC and expose endpoints to consumers through Amazon VPC Lattice. Configure resource gateways to front endpoints and custom domain names to simplify DNS management—eliminating Amazon Route 53 Profiles or manual records. Learn how to layer in fine-grained access controls that scale with your environment. Walk away with a deployable pattern for endpoint consolidation at scale.

sessions.t: Centralize AWS PrivateLink endpoints at scale with Amazon VPC Lattice

Configure resource gateways to front endpoints and custom domain names to simplify DNS management—eliminating Amazon Route 53 Profiles or manual records. Learn how to layer in fine-grained access controls that scale with your environment. Walk away with a deployable pattern for endpoint consolidation at scale.

sessions.t: Centralized governance for multicloud environments
sessions.a: When AI agents and automated pipelines ship changes across AWS, Azure, and other providers in minutes, governance that runs on separate toolchains can't keep pace. You end up with disparate security findings along with mis-aligned operational metrics, and a team that spends its time reconciling dashboards instead of actually reducing risk. In this session, see how to collapse multicloud governance into a single operating model across AWS and Azure, leveraging Amazon CloudWatch unified telemetry for centralized observability and AWS Security Hub for aggregated findings into a single surface.You'll walk through a deployable architecture that gives one analyst a unified view across clouds, so your governance moves at the same speed your engineering teams already do.

sessions.t: Champagne AI on a beer budget: Cost-optimized AI architectures live
sessions.a: A surprise cloud bill can wipe out a nonprofit's budget, but running frontier-quality generative AI doesn't have to cost frontier prices. In this code talk, we build an architecture that gets premium model output on a fraction of the spend. Starting with a naïve workload where every request hits the same large model, we layer in routing to send requests to the lowest-cost model meeting the quality bar, caching to reduce token counts, and token budgets with kill switches that gracefully degrade. You'll leave with working code your engineers can implement, and your finance team won't panic over.

sessions.t: Change. Wait. Debug. Let AI drive the infrastructure loop. (sponsored by HashiCorp)
sessions.a: Make a change. Deploy it. Wait. Dig through the logs. Try again. For years, that loop has cost infrastructure engineers countless hours—time that could be spent shipping what comes next. In this session, discover how to take engineers out of the routine operational loop without giving up oversight. Define the outcome, let AI work through the iterations, and step back in only when a real decision needs you. See the pattern in action with Terraform, Vault, Kubernetes, Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and more. This presentation is brought to you by HashiCorp, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Chaos engineering: Network fault injection with Gateway Load Balancer
sessions.a: Your application works perfectly in the lab—but what happens with 45ms latency and 0.1% packet loss? In this session, deploy a transparent network fault simulator using AWS Gateway Load Balancer and Linux Traffic Control (TC) on Amazon EC2. Inject delay, jitter, packet loss, and bandwidth constraints into live traffic, then observe how a tightly coupled application degrades in real time. Use the results to set SLA thresholds, validate AWS Direct Connect failover behavior, and justify architectural decisions. Leave with a reusable, parameterized emulator pattern deployable via AWS Systems Manager.

sessions.t: Chaos engineering: Network fault injection with Gateway Load Balancer
sessions.a: Your application works perfectly in the lab—but what happens with 45ms latency and 0.1% packet loss? In this session, deploy a transparent network fault simulator using AWS Gateway Load Balancer and Linux Traffic Control (TC) on Amazon EC2. Leave with a reusable, parameterized emulator pattern deployable via AWS Systems Manager.

sessions.t: Charting the AI Search Frontier: From Retrieval to Reasoning
sessions.a: Large language models have shifted expectations about search: from retrieving documents to answering questions directly; from single-type data to multi-modal data; from one-shot lookup to multi-step reasoning. This is the new frontier of search empowered by AI. What should you know about the AI Search frontier? How can you make AI search provide the highest accuracy on your data, while keeping latency and costs in check? Join us to chart the course — and leave with a practical map.

sessions.t: Choosing a game server instance without guessing
sessions.a: Most game studios pick server instances based on vibes. This session replaces that with numbers. We cover tick-rate budgets by genre (128-tick shooters need max frequency; 30-tick survival and 10-tick MMOs don’t), how to instrument Unreal, Unity, and Godot game loops, and how to build bot-driven load tests that tell you exactly how many players fit on an instance. Then we demonstrate it: same open-source game, deployed on M8azn and Graviton, player count ramped until it falls over. You’ll see where high clock speed matters and where you’re paying for headroom you don’t need.

sessions.t: Choosing the right AWS storage for low-latency workloads
sessions.a: Not all latency-sensitive workloads have the same storage requirements. From AI/ML training checkpoints to real-time analytics and high-frequency data pipelines, choosing between Amazon S3 Express One Zone, Amazon FSx for Lustre, and instance storage depends on access patterns, throughput needs, and cost constraints. In this chalk talk, we break down the decision framework for selecting low-latency storage across common workload types. Bring your architecture questions as we compare directory buckets, parallel file systems, and caching strategies side by side. Leave with a clear mental model for matching your performance requirements to the right AWS storage tier.

sessions.t: Choosing the right AWS storage service
sessions.a: AWS storage spans block, file, and object services alongside purpose-built storage for vectors, tables, and migration, each optimized for distinct access patterns, latency requirements, and cost profiles. Choosing the most efficient option can help you reduce complexity, over-provisioning, or rearchitecting later. In this chalk talk, AWS storage experts walk you through a decision framework based on workload characteristics, not product names. Bring your architecture questions and work through real scenarios interactively. You will leave with a clear mental model for matching workloads to storage services and the confidence to make the right decision as your requirements evolve.

sessions.t: Choosing the right AWS storage service
sessions.a: AWS storage spans block, file, and object services alongside purpose-built storage for vectors, tables, and migration, each optimized for distinct access patterns, latency requirements, and cost profiles. sessions.t: Claude It Your Way: Anthropic on AWS
sessions.a: Your teams want Claude for coding, agents, and knowledge work, and there are more ways than ever to reach it. This session maps every path to Anthropic on AWS. Start with the models, served two ways: Amazon Bedrock, with Haiku for speed, Sonnet for balance, and Opus for long-running agentic work, or Claude Platform on AWS for Anthropic's first-party API. Add the applications on top: Claude Code for agentic development, Claude Desktop for broader knowledge work. Govern both with the Claude apps gateway, one control plane across them. Leave knowing how the layers fit your teams.

sessions.t: Claude Keeps Building: How Coding Agents Change Software Development (sponsored by Anthropic)
sessions.a: Coding agents make sustained, autonomous progress on real software. The question is what happens to the rest of the software development lifecycle. Claude Code runs for hours unattended, works beyond the terminal, and takes on more of the work around the code. We'll show where it stands and how engineering changes when the whole lifecycle becomes automatable: what engineers do, how review and testing evolve, where quality comes from when code is cheap. Live demos on AWS and numbers from our engineering, where Claude writes most of our code. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Cleared for Takeoff Hybrid Observability at the Busiest Airport (sponsored by SolarWinds)
sessions.a: Managing over a thousand network nodes across terminals, baggage systems, and cloud infrastructure requires more than reactive troubleshooting. Join Cedric Reed, Network Administrator at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, and SolarWinds to discover how the world’s busiest airport replaced manual oversight with proactive observability. Learn how unified visibility across on-premises hardware and AWS Cloud eliminates noise, reduces downtime, and keeps critical systems online for millions of daily travelers. Discover how hop-by-hop visualization and real-time telemetry seamlessly monitor a vast network of surveillance systems covering the entire 7-mile campus to optimize operational resilience and passenger safety. This presentation is brought to you by SolarWinds, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: CLI Agent Orchestrator: Open source multi-agent AI for developer CLIs
sessions.a: Complex projects outgrow a single AI agent's context and capability. CLI Agent Orchestrator (CAO), an awslabs open source project, coordinates 8 CLIs including Amazon Kiro CLI, Claude Code, and Codex into a multi-agent powerhouse via the Model Context Protocol and tmux. It provides a centralised harness with shared skills, memory, and integration with OpenClaw and Hermes Agent. In this builders' session you'll install CAO, launch a supervisor and specialist agents, and put the team to work on a real change in a sample repo. You'll walk away with a multi-agent workflow to drop into your projects.

sessions.t: CLI Agent Orchestrator: Open source multi-agent AI for developer CLIs
