sessions.t: Clinical Trials, Reimagined at the Speed of AI (sponsored by PwC)
sessions.a: Bringing a new drug to market takes over a decade, and much of that time is lost to paperwork rather than science. This session tells how pharma leaders are transforming clinical development with agentic AI on AWS. Attendees will hear how PwC’s Digital Trial Core turns clinical protocols into structured, machine-readable data, powering AI agents that draw on historical insights and reusable, modular content to streamline study startup activities such as vendor selection, budgeting, negotiations, and trial documentation. Industry leaders will share how these solutions move from proof of concept into live studies, bringing treatments to patients sooner. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Close the loop: From guardrail blocks into layered defense
sessions.a: Guardrails block malicious prompts. Every blocked attempt is a signal: proof of what your defenses caught and a clue toward what will be attempted next. Capture that signal instead of discarding it. In this session, you design and deploy a layered enforcement architecture that closes the loop. A stateful detection tier identifies repeated probing across sessions and propagates block decisions to the network edge. You evaluate signals from guardrail violations and apply policies to classify and block the threat. You leave with a deployed pattern applicable to any AI agent workload. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Closing the compliance loop when agents change your infrastructure
sessions.a: AI agents and automated pipelines now change your infrastructure faster than any review can keep up, and not every change comes through CloudFormation. In this workshop, you'll close the compliance loop end to end: author a CloudFormation Hook that enforces encryption and tagging before deployment, then extend the same logic into an AWS Config custom rule with CloudFormation Guard so out-of-band changes get caught continuously. You'll build auto-remediation with SSM Automation, package it into a Conformance Pack for org-wide reach, and use Resource Timeline to trace drift. You leave able to keep compliance closed however fast change arrives.

sessions.t: Closing the Loop: How Cognition’s AI Continuously Improves Itself (sponsored by Datadog)
sessions.a: As AI accelerates software development, production systems are changing faster than teams can understand manually. Cognition is closing that gap by giving Devin, its software engineering AI agent running on AWS, access to its own production telemetry through Datadog. Devin uses that context to reason about its production behavior and take action when needed. That feedback loop turns production insights into improvements to Devin’s reliability and future task performance. In this session, we’ll show how Devin investigates alerts, correlates metrics and logs, distinguishes real issues from noise, and uses those insights to improve its harness and workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Closing the Loop: Using Frontier Agents for Continuous Governance
sessions.a: Build a Well-Architected workload with three AI agents working design-to-runtime for always-on AI governance. In this builders' session, combine Security Agent (now part of Continuum) for pre-deployment checks, DevOps Agent for triage and root-cause analysis, and Bedrock AgentCore for orchestration via MCP tools. You'll scan for OWASP Top 10 issues, run pen tests, and use ready-to-merge fix PRs. You'll author a skill encoding your runbooks, catch a privilege escalation bug that manual review missed, witness DevOps Agent diagnose an incident, and ship a complete loop: design, code review, adversarial tests, CI/CD gates, monitoring, AI-driven RCA, mapped to a Well-Architected pillar.

sessions.t: Cloud agent work needs infrastructure. We built it. (sponsored by Asana)
sessions.a: Organizations need an operating layer where humans and agents can run critical workflows together. That’s Asana. As software development shifts toward work performed by agents in the cloud, engineering teams need the same connected approach at enterprise scale. Command brings Asana’s operating layer to engineering, giving developers one surface for project management and coding work—connecting planning, assignment, and execution across the organization. Command works with coding agents teams already use, including Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. See the challenges Command solves for product and engineering teams and how it works against real engineering workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Asana, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Cloud Migration Journey Tabletop Experience
sessions.a: Experience a dynamic simulation of leading a digital transformation initiative. Navigate cloud migration, security automation, and operational excellence challenges. Architect secure cloud environments while balancing stakeholder needs and compliance. Compete to optimize speed, security, and innovation amid real-world obstacles. Gain actionable insights into cloud security governance and risk-aligned architecture.

sessions.t: Cloud-native Java on Amazon EKS
sessions.a: Learn how to build cloud-native Java applications based on best practices, and discover ways you can optimize application performance for fast startup and efficient resource usage in containerized environments. In this builders’ session, gain hands-on experience as you learn how to reduce memory overhead, lower cold start latency, and achieve sub-second startup times when building Java applications on Amazon EKS. You will also learn how to use Amazon Bedrock to analyze profiling and thread dump data to uncover performance patterns and generate optimization insights.

sessions.t: Cocktails to Code Building AI Bartenders with Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Plain-language AI orders fail if models hallucinate items that are out of stock. I built a reliable AI bartender grounded strictly in live inventory data. This session covers how an AI agent on Amazon Bedrock uses Strands Agents, AgentCore, and MCP tools to fetch real-time menus. We will dive into the serverless architecture, see what breaks during live text streaming, and evaluate the cost versus performance tradeoffs of production grounding. You will leave with a reusable pattern and the repository to build reliable, data-driven agents.

sessions.t: Code real-time multi-agent AI systems with Amazon ElastiCache
sessions.a: Modern algorithmic trading platforms deploy fleets of specialized AI agents, including market analysts, risk assessors, order executors, and compliance monitors, that must coordinate in real time without conflict. In this session, follow along as a trading platform's multi-agent workflows are coded live using Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey. Valkey Streams organize agent task queues, pub/sub channels broadcast market signals to agent swarms with low latency, and vector similarity search gives agents memory of prior market scenarios. Discover how atomic Lua scripts prevent duplicate orders and enable exactly-once workflow transitions.

sessions.t: Coding an AI agent from scratch with AWS Lambda durable functions
sessions.a: AI agents need multi-step reasoning, tool execution, human approvals, and long-running waits, all while keeping resilient state across failures. In this code talk, we build an AI agent from scratch using Lambda Durable Functions. You'll see how to implement a tool-use loop, add retries with exponential backoff, pause for human approval without paying for idle time, and recover cleanly from a mid-execution failure. We'll experiment with agent suspend and resume live, and watch it resume from a checkpoint deterministically. Leave with production-ready patterns for building stateful AI agents using familiar programming constructs.

sessions.t: Coding event-driven retry patterns that prevent outages
sessions.a: In this code talk, you'll instrument an event-driven integration layer with the patterns that contain failure: exponential backoff with jitter, circuit breakers, poison-pill isolation, and replay-from-archive - all live, in code. See how jittered retries prevent thundering herds, how circuit breakers protect healthy services from impaired ones, and how idempotency makes every replay safe. By the end, you'll have hands-on patterns for EventBridge and Step Functions that shrink your blast radius from total outage to graceful degradation.

sessions.t: Coding high-throughput data pipelines with AWS Lambda durable functions
sessions.a: Processing large datasets usually means hand-wiring queues, coordinators, and state tracking. In this code talk, we live-build a high-throughput data pipeline with Lambda durable functions instead. You'll see the fan-out/fan-in pattern in code: split a large dataset across parallel durable executions, isolate and retry the branches that fail without reprocessing the ones that succeeded, and offload checkpoints to S3 so a job too big for a single invocation survives restarts. We'll tune concurrency to protect a downstream database from overload, then compare the durable-functions approach with other design patterns on both developer velocity and cost. Leave with patterns you can apply to your own data workloads immediately.

sessions.t: Coding the tool layer for AI agents on Serverless
sessions.a: Agents don't need new infrastructure - they need access to what you've already built. In this code talk, you'll retrofit a Serverless API into a production-ready agent tool, live in code. Implement an MCP server with versioned tools, wire it to AgentCore Gateway for discovery and invocation, then expose an entire Step Functions workflow, human-in-the-loop gates and all, as a single callable tool. Add scoped agent identity, watch an unauthorized call get blocked, then an authorized one go through. Walk away with a repeatable playbook for turning existing APIs into agent-ready tools.

sessions.t: Coding the tool layer for AI agents on Serverless
sessions.a: Agents don't need new infrastructure - they need access to what you've already built. In this code talk, you'll retrofit a Serverless API into a production-ready agent tool, live in code. sessions.t: Compete to build an AI agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.a: Organizations are ready to move beyond rule-based workflows to agents that reason, adapt, and act. In this gamified workshop, you'll use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to assemble a realistic conversational banking agent end-to-end: orchestration with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness; secure tool integration with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway; and guardrails with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy. Prebuilt modules accelerate development so you can focus on agent logic. Compete in real time as your agent's accuracy and efficiency are scored on a live leaderboard. Leave with a working agent pattern you can adapt to your own use cases and bragging rights on the leaderboard.

sessions.t: Compete to build an AI agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.a: Organizations are ready to move beyond rule-based workflows to agents that reason, adapt, and act. In this gamified workshop, you'll use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to assemble a realistic conversational banking agent end-to-end: orchestration with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness; secure tool integration with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway; and guardrails with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy. Prebuilt modules accelerate development so you can focus on agent logic. Compete in real time as your agent's accuracy and efficiency are scored on a live leaderboard. Leave with a working agent pattern you can adapt to your own use cases and bragging rights on the leaderboard.

sessions.t: Composing the right orchestration for serverless workflows
sessions.a: Both AWS Lambda durable functions and AWS Step Functions handle retries, long-running execution, and failure recovery - so how do you choose? In this session, we cut through the confusion with a clear decision framework across three scenarios: human-in-the-loop approvals, long-running AI agent workflows, and multi-service sagas. We'll also show a hybrid pattern where Durable Functions handle inner business logic while Step Functions orchestrate at the macro level - code-level flexibility inside, visual observability outside. Leave with a practical framework and a real production example to guide your next serverless workflow decision.

sessions.t: Compute innovation with the AWS Nitro System
sessions.a: The AWS Nitro System has fundamentally changed how we build and deliver EC2 instances, accelerating our pace of compute innovation while improving security and performance for customers. This session explores the Nitro architecture and the latest innovations it enables: multi-host for smaller metal sizes, reduced blast radius, higher performance, how Nitro has helped us in accelerating the pace of innovation, and delivering Flex instances. We'll dive deep into how the Nitro System continues to push the boundaries of what's possible in cloud compute.

sessions.t: Computing‑Power‑Cooling Synergy: Building the Future of Global Data Infrastructure (sponsored by Kehua Tech)
sessions.a: The rapid growth of AI workloads is driving new demands for large-scale data center infrastructure, with challenges in power supply, high-density cooling, and system integration. In this session, we will share real-world deployment practices and introduce end-to-end infrastructure solutions, including highly reliable UPS power systems, liquid cooling technologies, and turnkey integrated solutions. We will explore how computing, power, and cooling synergy can optimize data center efficiency, improve deployment agility, and accelerate the development of AI-ready infrastructure. This presentation is brought to you by Kehua Tech, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Configure Security & Governance Controls for Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Implement comprehensive security and administrative controls for Amazon Quick. Practice configuring identity integration, access policies, and data governance frameworks. Learn to establish monitoring, auditing, and compliance controls that meet enterprise requirements. Work through scenarios covering user management, content governance, and security best practices for Quick Suite environments in production.

sessions.t: Connect agents across frameworks live using the A2A open protocol
sessions.a: Agents built on different frameworks need to talk to each other. In this session we will build two agents on Strands and LangGraph, then wire them together using the A2A protocol hosted at the Linux Foundation. You will see the full handshake: AgentCard publication for discovery, task negotiation, streaming artifact exchange, and multi-turn collaboration between agents that share nothing except the protocol. We will deploy both sides on AgentCore Runtime and demonstrate cross-framework interoperability working live. You will leave with the patterns to make any framework's agents collaborate over a standard wire.

sessions.t: Connect and secure service-to-service networking on Amazon ECS
sessions.a: When your containerized services grow beyond a single cluster, networking becomes the bottleneck. Security groups block health checks, cross-VPC traffic needs custom solutions, and encrypting traffic feels like a full-time job. In this builder's session, configure secure service-to-service communication on Amazon ECS using Service Connect for discovery and encryption, VPC Lattice for cross-account connectivity, and load balancer patterns for external traffic. Implement end-to-end TLS, test failover between services, and observe traffic flows in real time. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.t: Connect everything, everywhere: AWS global connectivity
sessions.a: Point solutions don't scale globally—and stitching together and managing dozens of them creates blind spots. In this session, discover what's new in AWS Cloud WAN and AWS Direct Connect: simplified hybrid connectivity, smarter segmentation, and real-time visibility across global traffic. See how AWS Cloud WAN's policy engine and AWS Direct Connect's latest capabilities combine to deliver seamless connectivity from anywhere to anywhere. Walk away with patterns to build a borderless, resilient global network.

sessions.t: Connecting Amazon Quick to enterprise databases with MCP & AgentCore
sessions.a: Amazon Quick is a powerful AI assistant, but its real value unlocks when connected to your enterprise data. In this session, we demonstrate how to expose time series databases and other enterprise data stores to Amazon Quick using MCP servers and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. Starting from a production implementation querying 20M market trade records via natural language, we show how the same pattern extends to different databases. We cover building custom MCP tool servers, securing access with Cognito and AgentCore Gateway, and enabling business users to query complex data conversationally through Amazon Quick.

sessions.t: Connecting to Enterprise Data to Amazon Quick and Surfacing It Everywhere
sessions.a: Your AI agents are only as smart as the data they can reach. In most enterprises, that data is scattered across dozens of systems, siloed, ungoverned, and invisible to the agents that need it most. In this chalk talk, we architect a context layer from the ground up: connecting enterprise knowledge into a unified index, then enriching that foundation with a knowledge graph that maps organizational relationships, business rules, and domain context, giving agents permission-scoped, relationship-aware intelligence at runtime. Then we take that intelligence to where users work: browser, desktop, mobile, collaboration tools, and productivity suites. Each surface independently governed yet sharing one agent identity, one memory, and one set of guardrails. Bring your architecture. We'll whiteboard the end-to-end path together.

sessions.t: Connectivity strategies across AWS Partitions
sessions.a: Organizations increasingly operate across AWS commercial, GovCloud, European Sovereign Cloud, and China Regions to satisfy regulatory, data residency, and national security requirements—but connecting them introduces networking challenges that go well beyond standard multi-Region design. In this session, learn cross-partition connectivity patterns using AWS Site-to-Site VPN, AWS Direct Connect, and application-layer proxies alongside DNS resolution strategies, compliance boundary enforcement, and operational trade-offs. We walk through architectural blueprints for securely linking partitions while preserving the isolation guarantees they exist to enforce, and share lessons learned from customers navigating ITAR, GDPR, and national sovereignty mandates at scale.

sessions.t: Connect NetApp FSx for ONTAP File Data to AI Apps with S3
sessions.a: Your AI workloads need enterprise data including documents, datasets, and unstructured content already sitting in ONTAP. The usual answer is to copy it to S3, build a sync pipeline, and hope nothing drifts. There's a better option. This session shows how to use FSx for ONTAP file shares directly via the S3 API so Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker can read them in place with no migration, no pipeline. Your existing access controls and data management policies stay intact. We'll cover the architecture, configuration steps, and how to pair ONTAP's data management capabilities with S3-based AI/ML services.

sessions.t: Connect your Amazon ECS services without the complexity
sessions.a: Service-to-service communication in containerized environments introduces routing, discovery, and encryption challenges. This chalk talk explores when to use Service Connect, VPC Lattice, load balancers, or direct service discovery on Amazon ECS and how to combine them as your architecture grows. Understand the trade-offs across latency, cost, and operational overhead so you can match the right pattern to each workload. Bring your architecture questions for an open technical discussion.

sessions.t: Connect your Amazon ECS services without the complexity
sessions.a: Service-to-service communication in containerized environments introduces routing, discovery, and encryption challenges. This chalk talk explores when to use Service Connect, VPC Lattice, load balancers, or direct service discovery on Amazon ECS and how to combine them as your architecture grows. Understand the trade-offs across latency, cost, and operational overhead so you can match the right pattern to each workload. Bring your architecture questions for an open technical discussion.

sessions.t: Content at the Speed of Live: AI-Powered Media Ops at Live Nation
sessions.a: Live Nation's subsidiaries generate petabytes of live event content across siloed storage. When an artist creates a viral moment, teams need it in fans' hands in minutes not days. In this session, learn how Live Nation built the AI Media Center on AWS, a platform that unifies fragmented media silos so teams can search, create, and publish at the speed of live. Built using the guidance for a Media Lake on AWS, along with Amazon Bedrock, the platform uses AI-driven moment detection to surface key content automatically. We cover architecture, lessons from festival-scale deployment, and impact on fan experience.

sessions.t: Context-Aware Agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory
sessions.a: Customers expect personalized service and context retention without repeating themselves every session. In this lab, you build a customer service agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that remembers each client across conversations. You create a Memory resource with Semantic, Summary, and User Preference strategies, deploy a Lambda-based agent backed by Amazon Nova Lite, and seed multi-turn conversations. The agent retrieves preferences and facts from long-term memory to personalize responses and recommend products from a DynamoDB catalog.

sessions.t: Context engineering for agents: memory, SQL, knowledge graphs & skills
sessions.a: An agent's context window is a finite attention budget, and database-backed agents must keep that context current, selective, and traceable. In this session, architect solutions to trace a task as it builds context using Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, Amazon Neptune, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Examine how agents cache hot state, retrieve operational rows, apply SQL filters, maintain vector and full-text indexes, refresh stale records, traverse knowledge-graph relationships, load skills, and discover MCP tools. Explore freshness policies, invalidation, provenance ledgers, access boundaries, and compaction patterns for production-grade agentic applications. Leave with practical patterns for production-grade agents.

sessions.t: Context engineering for production agents on AgentCore
sessions.a: An agent is only as good as what fills its context window. System prompts, skills, tool definitions, conversation history, retrieved documents, long-term memory, they all compete for limited space. Get the mix wrong and you waste tokens, degrade reasoning, or lose critical instructions mid-conversation. This chalk talk breaks down every layer of context that shapes agent behavior on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We cover how to structure system prompts, define skills effectively, manage tool context through gateway, retain the right conversation history, and use Memory strategies to persist what matters across sessions. Bring your agents, we optimize them live.

sessions.t: Context Over Code: Making AI-Native Development Work at Scale
sessions.a: AI coding assistants generate code quickly, but that's not the problem most teams need solved. After rolling out an AI coding companion to 150+ engineers, we learned the real unlock was rethinking how we work, not how fast we type. This session covers our path from AI code companion to AI-Driven Development Lifecycle: building a Context Store with Bedrock Knowledge Bases and MCP to surface decades of institutional knowledge, implementing steering and verification patterns, and managing the organizational change that makes AI-native development stick. You'll leave with a framework for scaling AI beyond individual productivity.

sessions.t: Context to Action: Turning Agent Memory into a Customer Retention Lever (sponsored by MongoDB)
sessions.a: When a customer calls, a support rep has seconds to understand what they need, what device they're on, and how to solve it fast. Get it right, and you earn trust. Get it wrong, and churn becomes a real risk. T-Mobile closes that gap with agent memory: session context pre-populated before the call starts, enriched turn by turn as it unfolds, with real-time graph traversal connecting customer, device, and issue so the rep sees the full picture. MongoDB Atlas runs it all, from vector search over T-Mobile's knowledge corpus to in-call graph traversal to the live session-memory documents. Afterward, AWS Neptune turns that history into a graph shaping future routing and retention. Walk away with an architecture pattern for building agent memory in real time, and a way to decide what belongs in short-term memory versus what should persist. Featuring T-Mobile, presented by MongoDB. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Continuous Attack Chains Across Every Surface (sponsored by Terra)
sessions.a: Most security tools score vulnerabilities in isolation, but attackers do not think in isolation. This session shows how Terra continuously chains signals into real attack paths across web applications, APIs, AI systems, and network infrastructure using agentic AI, the same way a human adversary would pivot from one weak point to the next. Every proposed chain is validated by an expert human pentester before it becomes a finding, turning a pile of low severity noise into a small number of confirmed, exploitable risks. Learn how continuous, cross surface attack chaining changes what a security team should actually prioritize first. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) on AWS
sessions.a: Whether you're shipping a monolith or hundreds of microservices, every change needs to reach production safely and quickly. AWS gives you a unified set of tools to plan, build, test, and deploy code—with safety woven into every stage. In this session, learn how to assemble end-to-end CI/CD pipelines using infrastructure as code, then layer in safe-deployment strategies—canary and linear traffic shifting, automated CloudWatch alarm gates, and one-click stage rollbacks—so you can release with confidence and recover in seconds when something goes wrong.

sessions.t: Controlling the AI Software Factory (sponsored by LaunchDarkly)
sessions.a: AI isn't just making software faster; it's changing how software is produced. Engineering teams now run agents that write code, review PRs, validate releases, and deploy around the clock. The promise is real, but so is a new problem: how do you stay in control of systems that never stop evolving? Edith Harbaugh, CEO of LaunchDarkly, argues the defining challenge of the AI era isn't generating code, it's controlling autonomous systems in production, where agents drift and the old detect-fix-redeploy playbook breaks down. She'll share what LaunchDarkly learned building its own AI software factory, and how engineers stay in charge. This presentation is brought to you by LaunchDarkly, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Control What Goes Out: Egress Security for AI Workloads
sessions.a: Most AWS workloads rely on two fundamental outbound mechanisms—DNS queries and network connections—both of which can be abused for data exfiltration. Learn how to lock down both. We'll cover DNS Firewall enhancements to secure the DNS path, Network Firewall improvements for outbound connection control, and how integrating DNSFW with NFW delivers advanced, unified DNS security. We'll also explore URL and domain categories, managed threat intelligence, and extending egress protections to containerized and AI workloads—helping you achieve compliance and simplified operations at scale.

sessions.t: Conversational AI to accelerate Apache Spark operations on Amazon EMR
sessions.a: Customers manage dozens of Apache Spark applications on Amazon EMR — and every major upgrade, unexpected failure, or performance regression pulls engineers away into reactive firefighting. In this workshop, experience a fundamentally different approach with AI-powered agents that handle the undifferentiated heavy lifting of Spark modernization and incident resolution. You'll work hands-on with conversational agents such as the Apache Spark Upgrade Agent and the Apache Spark Troubleshooting Agent across real-world scenarios on EMR Serverless and EMR on EC2 to simplify the operational burden through natural language, automated code transformation, workload analysis and data quality validation.

sessions.t: Core banking agent-ready: From composable to agentic financial services on AWS
sessions.a: The shift from composable to agentic banking is a re-architecture. Discover the reference architecture for turning a core banking platform into an intelligent core with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for orchestration, Amazon ECS for the control plane, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases for domain context, and Amazon EventBridge for event-driven ingestion. We explore two consumption patterns ISVs can offer bank customers: exposing core banking APIs to customer-owned agents, and shipping a managed agentic layer for conversational AI and autonomous lending, deposit, and payment operations, eliminating up to 70% of repetitive manual work. Learn the hard-won lessons on infrastructure, governance, and product differentiation.

sessions.t: Correlate app signals to infra root cause in hybrid environments
sessions.a: Your app is slow, but is it the code, the container, or the underlying host? When your stack spans clouds, hybrid, and on-prem, correlating application performance to infrastructure health means jumping between tools and guessing at root cause. Join this session as we walk through how to map application signals such as traces, errors, and latency directly to the infrastructure, regardless of where it runs. You'll see how to pinpoint whether the problem is your app or the compute it sits on, without stitching dashboards together manually.

sessions.t: Correlate database query latency to user impact
sessions.a: Diagnosing performance degradation across distributed applications requires more than isolated database or application metrics. It demands correlated, end-to-end telemetry. This code talk demonstrates a scenario that unifies database performance signals with application-layer telemetry using OpenTelemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Learn how to implement trace-to-query correlation, design log aggregation patterns for accelerated root cause analysis, and build metric relationships that surface bottlenecks across the full stack. You'll be able to connect a slow database query to its downstream user impact.

sessions.t: Cost-effective serverless data integrations and workflows for AI-ready data
sessions.a: AI is only as good as the data beneath it and building high-quality, well-integrated data products shouldn't break your budget. In this session, learn how to build cost-effective AI-ready datasets using AWS Glue, Amazon MWAA and Apache Iceberg. We'll show how Glue Data Quality and Glue serverless ETL, now with generative AI-assisted development, lets you ingest, transform, and prepare high-quality data at scale. We’ll demonstrate how Amazon MWAA serverless empowers a single DAG to coordinate workloads across AWS Glue, and other engines - all of this while paying only for what you use. Pairing this setup with Apache Iceberg further enhances your AI workloads with query-ready production data pipelines that move the needle without breaking the bank.

sessions.t: Cost optimization for Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.a: Developers love building on powerful, serverless Amazon DynamoDB, and as their production tables grow in size and traffic, they want to discover what mechanisms and optimizations can be applied to reduce costs. Cost optimization can be done both in the design phase and during operations. In this session, learn how to model and measure costs, explore Database Savings Plans to reduce spend on predictable workloads, and discover cost optimization tools that can help you along the way.

sessions.t: Cost optimization for Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.a: Developers love building on powerful, serverless Amazon DynamoDB, and as their production tables grow in size and traffic, they want to discover what mechanisms and optimizations can be applied to reduce costs. Cost optimization can be done both in the design phase and during operations. In this session, learn how to model and measure costs, explore Database Savings Plans to reduce spend on predictable workloads, and discover cost optimization tools that can help you along the way.

sessions.t: Craft, Don’t Vibe, Your MVP
sessions.a: Many people today use LLMs only for code generation. The best teams embrace AI across all stages of the SDLC. The decisions made before building the first version of your product directly affect its viability and success. Rather than relying on vibe coding to make these decisions implicitly, agents can be used to evaluate architectural options, compare trade-offs and challenge assumptions before a single line of code is created. This session explores how high-performing teams are investing time capturing standards, patterns and expertise, making them available for agents to apply consistently. Learn from practical real world examples how AI is being used to accelerate the delivery of production-ready systems, rather than those that carry technical debt from day one.

sessions.t: Creating resilient multi-channel customer experiences for NAB with Amazon Connect (sponsored by Deloitte)
sessions.a: National Australia Bank (NAB) modernized its digital customer service capability by migrating priority banker groups from legacy messaging platforms to Amazon Connect Chat. The transformation delivered a scalable, integrated, and future-ready messaging environment while improving banker productivity, operational control, and reporting capabilities, and enabling a pathway to enhanced self-service and assisted-service experiences. Deloitte led the end-to-end migration through a structured release approach, encompassing experience design, backlog and epic management, governance, business readiness, training, cutover planning, and operational risk management using AWS services. This session explores the strategy, execution, and lessons learned from delivering a successful enterprise messaging transformation. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Crossing the kill chain: IR when attackers pivot between clouds.
sessions.a: When a threat actor compromises credentials in one cloud and pivots into another, the kill chain crosses boundaries that no single-cloud tool can follow. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the detection and response patterns for cross-cloud lateral movement using Security Hub, Inspector, and multicloud telemetry sources.

sessions.t: Cross-modal search with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings
sessions.a: Build search and RAG that understand more than text. In this hands-on workshop, you'll use Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings that embeds text, documents, images, video, and audio into one semantic space for cross-modal retrieval. You'll generate embeddings across modalities, load them into a vector store, and build a working app that searches with text, an image, or an audio clip and retrieves relevant results from any modality. We'll cover indexing strategies, query routing, and accuracy tuning for production agentic RAG. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Crypto Escape Room: Race to migrate to quantum resistance
sessions.a: The migration to post-quantum cryptography is on and here's a chance to test your skills. In this gamified builders' session, each team races a visible countdown clock through different cryptographic migration challenges: TLS endpoint migration, data-at-rest re-encryption, code signing rotation, certificate lifecycle automation, or secrets key rotation. Teams unlock "quantum resistance badges" as they complete steps using AWS Key Management Service (KMS), AWS Certificate Manager, and AWS Secrets Manager. A live leaderboard tracks progress across teams. Leave with new skills and the confidence you can execute under pressure.

sessions.t: Cryptographic computing on AWS: homomorphic encryption in practice
sessions.a: What if your customers' data needs to stay invisible even to you? Cryptographic computing makes computation on encrypted data without decrypting it possible. Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) has become practical for ML inference. In this session, learn what FHE is, why it now works at scale on AWS, and how to get started. We will walk through two examples: encrypted ML inference on medical images and financial transactions, and encrypted ETL that aggregates records without exposing individual values. Leave with a deployment blueprint built for regulated industries.

sessions.t: Customer paths to production grade domain-specific AI with Forge
sessions.a: Domain-specific AI delivers accuracy that is difficult for general models to match. In this session, see how real customers use Amazon Nova Forge to accelerate the path from idea to production..

sessions.t: Customize and serve models at scale on Amazon EKS
sessions.a: Serving and customizing models in production often involves running expensive GPUs at high utilization, maintaining low latency as traffic spikes, and scaling to demand without over-provisioning. Increasingly teams are doing it on Amazon EKS. This session covers how to efficiently run GPU workloads, select the right accelerator for each workload, and apply optimization techniques that increase utilization and lower costs. Explore model customization through fine-tuning and RAG, and serving and autoscaling patterns that keep inference fast and efficient. See how hybrid workloads span cloud and on-premises GPUs with EKS Hybrid Nodes and where AWS is investing next.

sessions.t: Customize open models for accuracy, cost, and latency on SageMaker AI
sessions.a: An off-the-shelf model may not meet the accuracy, cost, or latency requirements of your specialized business task. Across businesses from retail to financial services, organizations are customizing open-weight models to unlock higher value. In this session, learn how to customize open-weight models with Amazon SageMaker AI, including for domain-specific workflows and agents. Intuit shares how it is using SageMaker AI with features such as serverless model customization and reinforcement learning, on its proprietary data to unlock business value and cut costs.

sessions.t: Customize workspaces and build guided workflows using AI in Connect Customer
sessions.a: In this workshop, you build the complete agent and business user experience in Amazon Connect Customer. First, you create persona-specific workspaces using the no-code UI builder, customizing page layouts, applications, and views so frontline agents, back-office workers, and supervisors each see only the information, tools, and guidance they need. Then, you create AI-powered guided workflows using natural language: describe the experience you want, and AI generates the step-by-step workflow automatically. You test and validate end-to-end in the Agent Workspace, seeing how custom layouts and AI-built guides work together to accelerate resolution. Walk away with persona-tailored workspaces and working guided workflows built in minutes instead of days.

sessions.t: Custom SRE agents: From prompt to proactive ops with DevOps agent
sessions.a: In this builder session, learn how to create custom SRE agents that turn a simple prompt into automated, environment-specific operational workflows. Using pre-configured tools and integrations, you'll define agents tailored to your priorities, whether that's anomaly detection, performance optimization, cost analysis, or resiliency recommendations. See how agents combine real-time observability data with structured reasoning to surface actionable improvements without manual investigation. Walk away with hands-on experience designing an agent that monitors your operational patterns and proactively recommends next steps, so your team spends less time diagnosing and more time shipping.

See how agents combine real-time observability data with structured reasoning to surface actionable improvements without manual investigation. Walk away with hands-on experience designing an agent that monitors your operational patterns and proactively recommends next steps, so your team spends less time diagnosing and more time shipping.

sessions.t: Cut cost migrating agentic AI workloads to Graviton5 on EKS AutoMode
sessions.a: Learn how to cut agentic AI infrastructure costs by migrating to AWS Graviton5 on Amazon EKS Auto Mode — with no compromise on latency or reliability. This hands-on workshop covers the full playbook: building multi-architecture container images, designing ARM64 NodePools, configuring IAM Roles for Service Accounts for secure agent-to-AWS communication, and tuning Graviton-optimized inference runtimes for predictable tail latency. Run live cost benchmarks against x86 equivalents to see exactly where Graviton5 pays back, and instrument with CloudWatch Container Insights to confirm performance parity. Walk away with a reusable pattern, a reproducible benchmark methodology, and a clear migration path you can apply to your own workloads the same week.

sessions.t: Cut cost migrating agentic AI workloads to Graviton5 on EKS AutoMode
sessions.a: Learn how to cut agentic AI infrastructure costs by migrating to AWS Graviton5 on Amazon EKS Auto Mode — with no compromise on latency or reliability. This hands-on workshop covers the full playbook: building multi-architecture container images, designing ARM64 NodePools, configuring IAM Roles for Service Accounts for secure agent-to-AWS communication, and tuning Graviton-optimized inference runtimes for predictable tail latency. Walk away with a reusable pattern, a reproducible benchmark methodology, and a clear migration path you can apply to your own workloads the same week.

sessions.t: Cut through Kubernetes signal overload with unified observability
sessions.a: Kubernetes at scale buries teams in high-cardinality signals that traditional pipelines truncate or split across separate backends, so the answer you need is never in one place. In this hands-on builders session, you send OpenTelemetry metrics and logs from an EKS cluster into Amazon CloudWatch, deploy Container Insights, and decide which signals actually matter. You use automatic resource enrichment to build your own dashboards and alerts, deciding what to alert on and why rather than running pre-made scripts. You leave knowing how to cut through high-cardinality noise and set up alerts that drive action.

sessions.t: Cut through the noise: risk-based prioritization for your security findings
sessions.a: Security Hub prioritizes critical security risks and helps you respond at scale. By correlating threats, vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations across AWS and multicloud environments, it surfaces attack paths and prioritizes what needs attention first. In this chalk talk, we deep dive into how exposures work, how risk prioritization scores are calculated, and how to operationalize the findings in your environment.

sessions.t: Cut through the noise: risk-based prioritization for your security findings
sessions.a: Security Hub prioritizes critical security risks and helps you respond at scale. By correlating threats, vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations across AWS and multicloud environments, it surfaces attack paths and prioritizes what needs attention first. In this chalk talk, we deep dive into how exposures work, how risk prioritization scores are calculated, and how to operationalize the findings in your environment.

sessions.t: Cut through the options: Choosing the right AWS connectivity solution
sessions.a: AWS offers a growing range of connectivity services—AWS Direct Connect, AWS Interconnect (multicloud and last mile), AWS Transit Gateway, and AWS Cloud WAN—but when should you use one over another? In this chalk talk, evaluate your connectivity options and avoid over-engineering your network design. Walk through real-world scenarios and a structured decision framework to understand which service aligns with your requirements. Leave with clear guidance and practical decision tools for selecting the right service for your scenario. Come prepared with your questions.

sessions.t: Cut through the options: Choosing the right AWS connectivity solution
sessions.a: AWS offers a growing range of connectivity services—AWS Direct Connect, AWS Interconnect (multicloud and last mile), AWS Transit Gateway, and AWS Cloud WAN—but when should you use one over another? In this chalk talk, evaluate your connectivity options and avoid over-engineering your network design. Leave with clear guidance and practical decision tools for selecting the right service for your scenario. Come prepared with your questions.

sessions.t: Cut token costs by 50%: Building context efficient agents with Strands
sessions.a: AI agents degrade as conversations exceed context windows. You need retrieval strategies, compression policies, and adaptive storage backends. This code talk covers the three-tier context cache hierarchy of AWS's open source Strands Agents SDK. We'll discuss context management as composable primitives with extension points for custom backends, compression, and retrieval. We'll explore trade-offs between framework and agent-controlled context, how plugins compose without coupling, and where abstractions break under extreme workloads. For developers building or extending agent frameworks.

sessions.t: Cut your data lake and lakehouse bills: Cost and performance tuning best practices
sessions.a: Open data lakehouses and data lakes can quietly accumulate cost through uncompacted small files, over-partitioned tables, and inefficient scan patterns. In this session, learn advanced cost savings and tuning techniques on AWS that cut storage and compute costs while improving performance. We cover partitioning strategies, predicate pushdown optimizations, compaction tradeoffs, graviton efficiencies, intelligent-tiering storage and how to eliminate common anti-patterns that inflate your bill. Learn from practical examples of real-world workloads on Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, Amazon EMR and leave with a comprehensive playbook to lower you analytics costs.

sessions.t: Danske Bank's AI City: Scaling AI agents across an enterprise
sessions.a: Getting AI agents into production across a regulated enterprise means solving governance and security first. Danske Bank started with a handful of generative AI experiments and now runs more than 40 use cases in production. In this session, learn how Danske Bank built "AI City"—a governed, reusable platform that cut time-to-production from months to days. See how they structured the platform so new teams can ship agents without rebuilding authorization, logging, or model access controls from scratch, with production examples from personal banking, compliance, and capital markets, and explore the Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore architecture underneath it all.

sessions.t: Dark Factory or Human in Every Loop: Building the Agentic SDLC in Between (sponsored by Port IO)
sessions.a: Your developers ship faster than ever. Your organization doesn't. The bottleneck moved from writing the code to everything that happens after it. Agents can help, but only with a trustworthy picture of your org and real permission to act in it. That's an agentic SDLC. Nobody ships you one, because yours is shaped like your organization. So we'll build one live for a company that doesn't exist: a t-shirt printer whose three factories disagree on what a medium is. Then we take the humans out and see how dark the factory gets. An agent built it in two hours. This presentation is brought to you by Port IO, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Data & AI Security, Resilience and Recovery in AWS  (sponsored by Veeam)
sessions.a: As AI adoption accelerates on AWS, cloud and platform teams need to know exactly what Veeam can do to keep their data secure and their environments resilient. This session takes you on a tour of Veeam's capabilities built for the AWS developer and cloud practitioner: discovering sensitive data, monitoring AI agent activity, and closing visibility gaps before they become incidents. You'll see how security posture and backup protection work together in practice, giving teams confidence in what's protected. And when something does go wrong, precise, granular recovery means restoring exactly what changed, nothing more. This presentation is brought to you by Veeam, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Datacenter to Cloud: Safety, Security, & Trust for AI Agents & Models (sponsored by Red Hat)
sessions.a: Deploying enterprise AI requires a unified framework across four governance pillars: Safety, Security, Risk, and Trust. Demystify multi-layer vulnerabilities spanning base models, agentic harnesses, and tool usage, addressing threats like Mythos model risks. Learn defense-in-depth strategies for agents—including sandboxing, privilege control, reasoning tracing, and dynamic red-teaming—to mitigate prompt injection, data leakage, and excessive agency. We’ll map these practices to global frameworks like NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act to ensure continuous production readiness. This presentation is brought to you by Red Hat, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Data governance for trustworthy AI: from raw data to trusted products
sessions.a: In this hands-on workshop, transform fictional retailer RetailMax's raw, ungoverned data into trusted, governed data products using Amazon SageMaker platform . Learn to build a business glossary and metadata forms, create an analysis-ready dataset with an ETL job, and trace end-to-end data lineage. Gain hands-on experience enforcing data quality rules, enriching and publishing a governed data product, and sharing it through a publish-and-subscribe model with approval workflows and least-privilege access. Discover how to deliver trustworthy, explainable answers with the Gen-AI data agent. Leave equipped to build the governance and metadata foundation that makes data — and the AI that runs on it — trustworthy across your organization. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Data mesh at scale: The automation layer, proven at Experian
sessions.a: Federated data ownership is easy to draw and hard to enforce. Is governance enforced in process, or in the platform? Enforce it in the platform, and the hard part becomes the seam between central policy and self-serve provisioning most teams never build. On Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio we architect that seam: one project per data-domain for blast-radius isolation, contracts that block non-compliant publication, policy that cascades but only tightens, and a reconciler turning Git-committed JSON into infrastructure. Experian runs it across dozens of data domains in regulated financial services, cutting domain onboarding from months to self-serve.

sessions.t: Data mesh to agentic AI: Building an AI-ready enterprise on AWS
sessions.a: How do you make a trillion-dollar investment engine faster, smarter, and AI-ready without compromising governance? CPP Investments answered that question. Facing the reality that fragmented data was constraining investment decisions, their CTO led a deliberate shift: a governed, AI-ready enterprise data platform on AWS using data mesh, decentralized ownership, and low-code platform engineering to deliver scale with guardrails. The result? Trusted, near real-time data at the fingertips of every investment team, and a foundation accelerating Agentic AI and conversational data experiences at institutional scale. This is the playbook for turning data infrastructure into competitive advantage.

sessions.t: Data Prep to Deployment: How Tencent Games Scaled to 1,000 GPUs on SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.a: Join us to see how Amazon SageMaker HyperPod lets teams build complete training pipelines, from data prep and transformations through distributed training to seamless model deployment, all on one resilient, self-healing platform with no re-platforming required. Then, hear how Tencent Games, a game AI team (not an infra team), went from first cluster to thousand-GPU training in weeks for their VISVISE engine powering 90+ titles including PUBG Mobile. Walk away with lessons learned from real production workloads and best practices for EFA networking, FSx storage, and GPU fault tolerance.

sessions.t: Data protection and resilience with AWS storage
sessions.a: Data unavailability is costly, and the threats driving it are only growing in frequency and severity. Recovering well means recovering deliberately, not reactively, with a strategy built for the unpredictability of what can go wrong. In this session, you'll learn how the 3-2-1-1-0 defense-in-depth framework provides that structure, guiding you from failure scenario analysis through recovery objective planning to layered protection across local, cross-region, and immutable isolated copies. You'll see how AWS storage services bring each layer to life, from native replication and disaster recovery for availability to centralized backup with immutable isolated vaults for cyber recovery.

sessions.t: Death, taxes, and runtime deprecations: automate your way out
sessions.a: Your inbox fills with runtime deprecation notices—hundreds of Lambda functions on Node.js 20, Python 3.10, and whatever's next. Handling them one by one drains capacity you'd rather spend on features. This hands-on workshop flips the script: instead of chasing individual apps, you'll modernize a fleet. Using AWS Transform custom, you'll run AWS-provided transformations to upgrade Lambda runtimes at scale, then stand up continuous modernization to scan repositories against a baseline, prioritize what's drifting, and open pull requests automatically. Turn a wall of end-of-support alerts into a queue of ready-to-merge PRs. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.a: Your inbox fills with runtime deprecation notices—hundreds of Lambda functions on Node.js 20, Python 3.10, and whatever's next. Handling them one by one drains capacity you'd rather spend on features. This hands-on workshop flips the script: instead of chasing individual apps, you'll modernize a fleet. Using AWS Transform custom, you'll run AWS-provided transformations to upgrade Lambda runtimes at scale, then stand up continuous modernization to scan repositories against a baseline, prioritize what's drifting, and open pull requests automatically. Turn a wall of end-of-support alerts into a queue of ready-to-merge PRs. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Decision Frameworks, Evaluation, and Cost Management with Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Moving from one agent to enterprise-wide automation means choosing the right path — Flows, Automate, Custom Agents, persistent agents — and the right trigger model. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a decision framework that bakes in evaluation and cost management from the start, not as afterthoughts. We'll connect orchestration across 25+ connectors, skills, and workstreams to measurable outcomes and dollars. Bring your automation backlog — you'll leave with a decision matrix, eval harness, and ROI story.

sessions.t: Decision patterns for AI Agents with Amazon Connect Customer
sessions.a: Contact center AI agents require critical architecture decisions around tool integration, voice prompt engineering, and quality evaluation. In this chalk talk, we'll explore when to use first-party tools, when AWS Lambda gives you more flexibility, and when MCP integrations make sense—with latency, operational complexity, and compliance requirements as the deciding factors. We’ll discuss patterns for voice prompt engineering with Amazon Connect Customer AI agents and automated evaluation pipelines using Contact Lens and generative AI to score 100% of interactions. You'll leave with a decision model you can apply to your own contact center, including guidance for financial services and regulated industries.

sessions.t: Decompose a monolith database into microservices with agentic AI
sessions.a: Enterprise architects face a critical challenge: breaking monolithic database-centric applications into microservices while managing risk and cost. Where do you draw domain boundaries? How do you extract 20 years of business logic from stored procedures into the application layer? This chalk talk reveals the two-layer decomposition strategy—combining database structure and runtime execution patterns—to identify service boundaries. Leveraging AWS Transform and Kiro, collapse months of manual analysis, design and development into hours of executable code. Through live whiteboarding, learn the data-driven framework enabling business logic extraction, independent deployment, licensing cost reduction, and faster modernization.

sessions.t: Decouple and scale Amazon ECS workloads with event-driven patterns
sessions.a: Not every container workload needs to run all the time. Some should wake up when an event arrives, process it, and stop. Amazon ECS makes this straightforward, but choosing the right trigger pattern matters. In this chalk talk, discuss how to connect events to containers using Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SQS, and AWS Step Functions. Walk through four common patterns: single-event task launch, queue-based consumer scaling, fan-out processing, and multi-step workflow orchestration. Explore how to handle failures gracefully with dead-letter queues and retry policies, and how Amazon ECS provides serverless compute for event-triggered deployments.

sessions.t: Deep dive into Amazon Aurora and its innovations
sessions.a: With an innovative architecture that decouples compute from storage and advanced features like Aurora Global Database and low-latency read replicas, Aurora reimagines what it means to be a relational database. Aurora is a built-for-the-cloud, serverless relational database that delivers unparalleled performance and availability at global scale for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and DSQL. In this session, dive deep into the newest Aurora features. Explore how Aurora supports agentic AI through vector search and MCP servers for agent access. Also, learn about Aurora DSQL, the fastest serverless distributed SQL database.

sessions.t: Deep dive into Amazon Aurora DSQL and its architecture
sessions.a: Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database that uses decades of Amazon innovation and operational excellence. In this session, dive into the design and key innovative technologies that make Aurora DSQL the ideal choice for new applications and applications that require the highest level of resilience. Learn how active-active architecture in Aurora DSQL delivers single- and multi-Region resiliency and virtually unlimited scale

sessions.t: Deep dive into Amazon DocumentDB and its innovations
sessions.a: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a serverless, fully managed, MongoDB API-compatible document database service. In this session, take a deep dive into the most exciting features Amazon DocumentDB offers including serverless, enhanced compression, performance upgrades, and the latest query APIs. Learn how the implementation of these features in your organization can improve resilience, performance, and the effectiveness of your applications.

sessions.t: Deep dive into Elastic Load Balancing for modern workloads
sessions.a: Architect high-performance, resilient network infrastructure using Network Load Balancer and Gateway Load Balancer. This deep dive covers advanced load balancing, multi-protocol support, and security appliance integration at scale. In this session, we explore NLB source IP preservation, GWLB transparent inspection architecture, and deployment patterns. Topics include performance optimization, troubleshooting methodologies, QUIC support, and resilience capabilities including Zonal Shift and Zonal Autoshift. Walk away with practical blueprints for designing architectures that deliver high availability and predictable performance while maintaining inline security inspection and compliance—whether you're running financial trading platforms, gaming backends, or large-scale SaaS.

sessions.t: Deep dive into networking architectures for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes
sessions.a: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore hybrid networking design patterns for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes. We’ll cover different IPAM and routing strategies for hybrid pod networks, including Cilium BGP control-plane integration with your on-premises infrastructures. We’ll also explore various load balancing and Kubernetes services networking options for your hybrid nodes. Additionally, we’ll deep dive into the new Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway, demonstrating how it simplifies pod-to-pod communication, webhook connectivity, and AWS service integration across cloud and on-premises environments - without requiring changes to your existing network infrastructure.

sessions.t: Deep dive into networking architectures for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes

sessions.t: Deep dive on S3 Files with use case architectures and best practices
sessions.a: What if every application, AI agent, and team in your organization could access S3 data as a shared file system? With S3 Files, connect thousands of compute resources to your data in S3 through a high-performance file interface that scales to multiple terabytes per second. Stop duplicating data between object and file storage. Stop building staging workflows just to read a file. In this session, you'll see how S3 Files turns S3 into the shared file system your workloads already expect, and how customers are replacing copy-heavy pipelines with direct file access today.

sessions.t: Deepfakes, Deception, and the New Rules of Reality (sponsored by KnowBe4)
sessions.a: Deepfakes are transforming the rules of trust. As AI-generated voice, video, and imagery become easier to create, attackers use synthetic media to make deception feel familiar, urgent, and credible. In this session, KnowBe4 shows how deepfakes fit into broader social engineering campaigns built around narrative, timing, and cross-channel reinforcement. The fake clip is rarely the whole attack; it is one piece of a larger story designed to short-circuit judgment when it matters most. Attendees will learn what separates an interesting tech demo from a nation-state-level attack. They will see how these attacks work and why convincing stories and cognitive biases override technical skepticism even in well-trained people. Perry Carpenter will also cover how organizations can prepare for high-stakes moments when trust is under pressure—before the call comes in, not after This presentation is brought to you by KnowBe4, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Defeat Player Evasion: AI Moderation at Scale on Amazon Bedrock.
sessions.a: Players evade moderation with leetspeak, homoglyphs, emoji sequences, and fast-evolving slang. Brute-force AI classification catches evasion but is cost-prohibitive at scale. In this workshop, build a tiered moderation pipeline on Amazon Bedrock that routes 80–90% of traffic through deterministic normalization and pre-filters before invoking a model. Ambiguous content gets classified by Amazon Nova at sub-500ms latency. Only the hardest cases escalate to multi-agent analysis on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for context-dependent decisions. Configure per-category thresholds, instrument cost-per-decision tracking, and stress-test against real gaming evasion patterns. Walk away with a deployable, cost-optimized pipeline. Laptop required

sessions.t: Defending the Three Lanes: Preventing Toxic Agentic Combinations with Cyera and AWS (sponsored by Cyera)
sessions.a: Agentic AI is entering production faster than enterprise authorization models can keep up, and most access decisions are made without regard to the sensitivity of the data agents can reach, turning over-permissioned agents into high-value targets. This session introduces the three lanes: the data agents touch, the identity they act as, and the actions they take, as the framework for defending agentic AI on AWS. See how Cyera's Agent Guardian extends Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity with data-aware authorization to enforce least privilege, monitor agent-to-data activity, and prove it to auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Defense in depth for Strands AI agents with Cedar, AgentCore, and Rex
sessions.a: AI agents that generate and execute code on remote systems need more than a single permission check - they need policy enforcement at every trust boundary. In this builders' session, you’ll configure Cedar policies at two distinct enforcement points for a Strands pre-built operations agent : AgentCore Policy on AgentCore Gateway and Trusted Remote Execution (REX) on the target remote host. You’ll see why both are necessary, how they compose, and how the agent gracefully adapts when it hits either boundary.

sessions.t: Delivering Measurable Customer Business Outcomes
sessions.a: Proving business impact at the C-suite level is what separates a deployment partner from a strategic advisor. That's where the Value Realization Plan (VRP) comes in, the structured approach at the heart of the AWS Business Value Realization motion. We'll cover building a compelling case for change, defining KPIs that resonate with executives, and driving adoption through change management. Learn the pitfalls that stall outcome conversations, how to accelerate buy-in, and how to frame impact in terms executives act on. Leave with a repeatable approach for your next engagement and a foundation for a customer success practice that scales.

sessions.t: Delivering next-generation devices on Amazon Braket
sessions.a: In this session, we discuss bringing next-generation quantum hardware to Amazon Braket and dive deep on how our combined hardware and software capabilities unlock the best performance of these fault-tolerant devices. We share early results and outline how organizations can begin preparing today for the fault-tolerant era.

sessions.t: Democratizing precision time on EC2: make clocks work for you
sessions.a: Distributed systems builders have avoided relying on wall clock time for anything critical. Times are changing. Amazon Time Sync now delivers microsecond accuracy on EC2, making clock precision a feature, not a bug, in your system design. We whiteboard how customers in databases, AI, financial services, and media approach design in new ways, and share our open source ClockBound work on the clock error bound as a standard interface for your applications.

sessions.t: Demystifying Aurora DSQL transactions and concurrency control
sessions.a: Join this session to learn about Amazon Aurora DSQL's optimistic concurrency control (OCC). Explore building an application to understand the impact of OCC on your relational workloads, how it differs from traditional databases, and how to achieve the desired semantics in DSQL's OCC model.

sessions.t: Demystifying Aurora DSQL transactions and concurrency control
sessions.a: Join this session to learn about Amazon Aurora DSQL's optimistic concurrency control (OCC). Explore building an application to understand the impact of OCC on your relational workloads, how it differs from traditional databases, and how to achieve the desired semantics in DSQL's OCC model.

sessions.t: Demystifying AWS KMS authorization: building key policies that scale
sessions.a: Authorization to your key involves a mix of key policies, IAM policies, grants, SCPs, and VPC endpoint policies — each playing a distinct role in access decisions. This talk demystifies how these policies are evaluated in the context of AWS KMS, then applies that understanding to create a scalable policy design. You'll learn about ABAC, using grants for dynamic delegation, and AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) which offers a simpler yet scalable way to share keys in your organization. You'll leave with the mental model to predict outcomes and reusable patterns that grow with your organization.

sessions.t: Demystifying the shared security model on Amazon ECS
sessions.a: Running containers in production demands security controls at every layer. This chalk talk covers the Amazon ECS shared responsibility model, including IAM policies for task isolation, VPC networking with awsvpc mode, and runtime protections. Explore how Amazon ECS Managed Instances and AWS Fargate automates security patching and enforces instance refresh cycles while maintaining workload availability. Discuss practical patterns for secrets injection, image scanning, and network segmentation. Bring questions about securing your specific container architectures for an open technical discussion.

sessions.t: Deploy accelerated workloads with Amazon ECS Managed Instances
sessions.a: Amazon ECS Managed Instances let you run workloads on specialized EC2 hardware without managing the infrastructure underneath. In this workshop, deploy accelerated workloads across Graviton and ML accelerators on fully managed compute. Configure capacity providers, select instance types, and optimize costs through multi-task placement and Spot instances. Observe performance using CloudWatch Container Insights. Walk away with a working configuration you can adapt for your own accelerated workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Deploy Agentic AI on AWS AI Infrastructure for Production Agents
sessions.a: Autonomous agents demand multi-step reasoning, tool calling, and long-running sessions. In this chalk talk, we'll show how you can deploy self-managed agentic AI infrastructure on Amazon EC2 to solve its core scaling problem: agent turns are bursty — GPU-bound while reasoning, CPU-bound while orchestrating. We'll discuss when to use disaggregated inference to optimize for prefill and decode, KV cache management for multi-turn sessions, autoscaling for bursty traffic, and CPU-based compute for orchestration. We'll close with guardrails, cost controls, and reference architectures for multi-model agentic RAG and policy-based routing to managed endpoints.

sessions.t: Deploy agents you can trust
sessions.a: You're ready to put AI agents into production, but you can't prove they will stay within bounds. When agents act autonomously, governance, safety, and security become one question: can you trust what they do next? In this session, explore what it takes to build a unified governance approach across identity, policy, observability, and compliance. Then see how automated reasoning delivers mathematical proof that agent policies hold under all conditions, including the ones you'd never think to test. Leave knowing how to govern what your agents do and verify they do only what you intend.

sessions.t: Deploy a HIPAA-Compliant AI Agent with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
sessions.a: Your clinical team wants an AI agent that summarizes patient notes—but one leaked SSN means a $1.5M HIPAA penalty. In this session, we build a working Amazon Bedrock Agent with HIPAA controls baked in. Guardrails automatically redact low-risk identifiers and block critical PHI, routing flagged content through Amazon EventBridge to an SQS review queue. AWS CloudTrail captures the full audit trail, and IAM restricts the agent to BAA-covered services only. You leave with a deployable CDK stack ready for production.

sessions.t: Deploy AI agent sandboxes on EC2
sessions.a: AI agents write, execute, and iterate on code autonomously. Every session needs an isolated sandbox to run untrusted code safely. This session explores how customers deploy agent sandboxes on EC2 across distinct patterns, each offering different trade-offs between isolation, latency, and performance across our instance families. We cover isolation trade-offs, cost per sandbox-second, and capacity planning at scale. Attendees leave with a decision model for selecting the right pattern based on their scale, security posture, and operational maturity.

sessions.t: Deploy AI agents on containers with Amazon S3 Files and S3 Vectors
sessions.a: Build a multi-agent architecture on Amazon EKS using S3 Files as the shared workspace and S3 Vectors as persistent semantic memory. Mount an S3 file system across agent containers using standard POSIX file I/O. Agents read, write, and hand off artifacts without custom SDKs or message brokers. A background process generates embeddings stored in S3 Vectors, giving agents long-term memory they query semantically. Deploy a self-managed orchestrator that spawns agents, routes tasks via file system events, and retrieves vector history. Fine-tune synchronization, monitor with CloudWatch, and establish DR with cross-Region replication. Walk away with a production-ready, self-managed multi-agent system.

sessions.a: Build a multi-agent architecture on Amazon EKS using S3 Files as the shared workspace and S3 Vectors as persistent semantic memory. sessions.t: Deploy AI planning teammates without changing how your team works
sessions.a: Most planning tools force your team to change how they work. See the opposite approach. Watch AI teammates plug into the workflows your planners already follow, connect to the systems you already run, and improve as they learn your business. You will see a live product walkthrough, learn where AI takes work off your team's plate, and leave with a clear picture of how to add planning capacity without retraining people or rebuilding your stack.

sessions.t: Deploy and manage blockchain nodes on AWS
sessions.a: Self-managing blockchain nodes at scale requires expertise in infrastructure sizing, storage optimization, chain synchronization, snapshot management, and patching, amid rapidly evolving protocols. In this session, explore a reference architecture for deploying self-managed nodes on AWS using Amazon EC2 and AWS Blockchain Node Runners, an open source initiative. The session includes a whiteboard walkthrough of a sample solution, diving deep into each component, addressing key challenges, and exploring AI-driven node deployment with Kiro and how to leverage AWS DevOps Agent for management. Leave equipped to deploy, manage, optimize for data transfer, and scale blockchain workloads on AWS.

sessions.t: Deploy and optimize world models with agentic AI workflows
sessions.a: World models generate real-time video by learning environment dynamics—powering interactive simulation for gaming, robotics, and autonomous driving—but deploying these latency-sensitive pipelines is complex. In this builders session, we deploy and optimize a real-time video world model on AWS Trainium using AWS Neuron Agentic Development skills that automate compilation, profiling, and kernel optimization through natural-language interaction. See the agent identify bottlenecks, then select optimized kernels from Hugging Face or write custom kernels from scratch. Walk away with practical patterns for using agentic tools to achieve optimized, real-time inference on purpose-built AI silicon.

sessions.t: Deploy infrastructure with speed and safety using AWS CloudFormation
sessions.a: In this workshop, build and test AWS CloudFormation templates hands-on. Create stacks to deploy and manage resources, then use the CloudFormation Language Server to author with real-time validation in your IDE. Explore testing tools—cfn-lint, CloudFormation Guard, and early change-set validation—to catch errors before deployment. Learn language features like Stack Refactoring and drift-aware change sets that help you evolve templates safely over time. You must bring your laptop to participate.
