sessions.t: Deploying Frontier Voice Agents Privately on AWS (sponsored by ElevenLabs)
sessions.a: Frontier voice agents are already handling live customer calls inside health systems, banks and insurers, without audio ever leaving the customer's AWS account. This session covers the architecture that makes that possible, from in-VPC deployment and zero data retention to integration with their existing stack. Working from a production deployment taking real calls, we walk through the latency budget that keeps conversational voice feeling human, the trade-offs private deployment brings, and how to size it for your own environment. Leave with an understanding of where ElevenAgents fits in your current environment, a reference architecture and a deployment checklist. This presentation is brought to you by ElevenLabs, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Deploying Governed AI Agents in Clinical AI
sessions.a: Millions of patients wait too long for imaging each year as demand outpaces capacity, and the shortage is projected to worsen significantly by 2030. Radiology Partners is tackling this with MosaicOS, a full imaging lifecycle system powered by agentic AI that spans order placement through billing. In this lightning talk, learn how MosaicOS uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to orchestrate multiple AI models across the radiology workflow while maintaining governance and observability required in regulated clinical environments. See how agentic orchestration moves radiology from tool-level automation to coordinated, clinician-directed intelligence at scale.

sessions.t: Deploying mission-critical applications with Amazon EBS
sessions.a: Millions of customers run their performance-intensive enterprise applications and databases on AWS. In this workshop, explore deploying a high-performance application on Amazon EC2 and Amazon EBS for optimized availability, resiliency, and cost performance. Discover and choose the ideal Amazon EC2 instance types and Amazon EBS volume types for various workloads. Learn about on-demand storage flexibility and performance using Elastic Volumes. Monitor and optimize Amazon EBS using Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and observe how AWS DevOps Agent autonomously investigates and helps remediate storage performance issues. Build resilience and fault tolerance using AWS Fault Injection Service. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Deploying the foundation for successful enterprise AI (sponsored by Glean)
sessions.a: Successful enterprise AI depends on more than just the latest models. It requires context that connects knowledge across systems, intelligence that turns information into useful action, and protection that preserves permissions, security, and trust. This session presents a practical foundation for deploying AI across the enterprise—using AWS and Bedrock to move from isolated pilots to governed workflows. Learn how leaders are designing for adoption, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement from the start. This presentation is brought to you by Glean, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Deployment strategies for highly available edge applications
sessions.a: Organizations need to be able to deploy critical applications that are highly available and fault-tolerant at the edge. These workloads are often some of the most demanding in terms of durability and availability requirements. Deploying workloads on AWS hybrid cloud and edge computing services like AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts requires planning for networking, compute, storage, and other failure modes. In this chalk talk, dive deep into each of these services, review use cases, and examine reference architectures. Learn design considerations, deployment patterns, and best practices for high availability and disaster recovery.

sessions.t: Deploy without drama: Safe, automated releases on AWS
sessions.a: Releasing software shouldn't mean holding your breath. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS CodePipeline, CodeBuild, and AppConfig help you automate safe, hands-off deployments to Amazon EC2, ECS, and Lambda across accounts and Regions. Learn to apply canary and linear traffic-shifting strategies, wire CloudWatch alarms for automatic rollback, and use stage-level conditions to gate promotions on integration tests. Whether you're deploying a single service or orchestrating hundreds, leave with patterns for zero-downtime releases you can trust.

sessions.t: Deploy your applications with AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
sessions.a: In this workshop, build and deploy applications using infrastructure as code with the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). Create resources using familiar programming languages, apply CDK Mixins to compose reusable behaviors across constructs, and safely reorganize stacks with CDK Refactor. Learn maintenance and operations tips including cross-account output references and programmatic deployments with the CDK Toolkit Library. Get an introduction to building your own constructs. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Describe It, Deploy It: Building AI Agents in Natural Language [REPEAT]
sessions.a: What if you could describe the customer experience you want in natural language and have an AI agent built for you, complete with tools, guardrails, and conversation flows? Amazon Connect Customer lets you build agentic experiences by describing what you want in natural language with no code. In this chalk talk we show how a plain-language description becomes a working, governed AI agent ready for production. We demo a guided walkthrough, then whiteboard what sits under the hood: how natural-language authoring generates the production infrastructure - AI agents, tools, knowledge bases, routing, and escalation - and how deterministic and agentic reasoning coexist on a single governed application. We close with best practices for testing before deployment and keeping agents improving from real conversations, plus an open architecture discussion.

sessions.t: Design a governed ontology in Neptune that any agent can query
sessions.a: Your agents can answer questions. Can they explain why, and would two agents give the same answer? Most enterprise AI stalls in pilot because business meaning lives in scattered prompts, pipelines, and code. In this session, learn how to use Amazon Neptune to turn entities, relationships, policies, and rules into a governed ontology and knowledge graph that any agent framework can query. See how AI-assisted authoring cuts modeling from months to hours, where one rule update propagates across every agent and each answer carries an inspectable reasoning trace. The graph stays in your account.

sessions.t: Designing  AI Agents with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and Voice AI
sessions.a: Multimodal AI agents need to understand more than text and interact through more than a screen. In this interactive chalk talk, we’ll explore how Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings connects knowledge across text, documents, images, video, and audio, including semantic search over spoken content and sound, while voice AI enables natural conversational interaction. We’ll examine cross-modal retrieval, audio and video segmentation, multimodal context, conversational orchestration, latency, and grounding tradeoffs for building responsive agents that can listen, understand, retrieve, and converse across modalities.

sessions.t: Designing cost-efficient Iceberg data lakes on Amazon S3 Tables
sessions.a: Apache Iceberg data lakes that aren't thoughtfully planned can accumulate small files, excessive metadata, and redundant snapshots, ultimately degrading query performance and inflating costs. In this session, we dive into the design and maintenance choices that determine whether your Iceberg lake stays fast and cost-efficient or slowly deteriorates, including compaction strategies, snapshot expiration, and partition design. For each, we'll walk through the trade-offs, what happens when you get it wrong vs. right, and how Amazon S3 Tables can automate the heavy lifting for you. Leave with actionable strategies to balance performance and cost at scale.

sessions.t: Designing Portable Multicloud Architectures with Open Specifications
sessions.a: Enterprises pursuing multicloud strategies often equate portability with containerization — but true architectural portability requires deliberate decisions across the full stack. In this chalk talk, we start from the foundational layers of compute, storage, and networking and build outward through data, security, observability, and AI. At each layer, we explore how open specifications enable portability — and in what parts of your architecture does portability matter most. Along the way, we challenge common myths: that managed services equal lock-in, that Kubernetes equals portable, and that open source alone guarantees freedom. Through interactive whiteboarding, we'll design portable architecture patterns together — examining real trade-offs, open specifications like Apache Iceberg, OpenTelemetry, OPA, and MCP, and how to make deliberate portability decisions across your stack.

sessions.t: Designing security governance for your AWS multi-account foundation
sessions.a: AWS gives you flexibility to design your multi-account environment, but customer needs guidance choosing the right security services to deploy, where, and how to validate the deployment against AWS best practices. This session shows how the AWS Security Reference Architecture provides a prescriptive security blueprint you layer on top of your account governance foundation. Using whiteboarding, you cover OU design, service prioritization, centralized vs. distributed placement, design considerations, validation with SRA Verify, and deployment acceleration. You leave with a tailored governance model ready for implementation.

sessions.t: Designing the AWS Secure Research Environment: Architecture deep dive
sessions.a: Discover how the AWS Secure Research Environment (SRE) helps universities stand up NIST 800-171 and CMMC Level 2 eligible infrastructure in hours to weeks. Explore the architecture behind the solution, from Landing Zone Accelerator customization, multi-account strategy with Service Catalog vended accounts, preventive SCPs versus detective controls, Network Firewall egress patterns for GovCloud, and automated evidence collection feeding Security Hub. Learn from real design decisions, including what we got wrong and how we iterated, and access the open-source templates available on GitHub. Attendees deploy the SRE and experience the architecture firsthand.

sessions.t: Designing your AWS network for scale: From one VPC to many
sessions.a: You started with a single Amazon VPC - and it worked. But as your organization grows, so does your network complexity. In this chalk talk, we'll work through the decision points of scaling from one VPC to many. When should you split workloads? How do you connect VPCs - peering, hub-and-spoke, or mesh? How do you segment traffic, centralize inspection and egress, plan IP addressing at scale, and integrate hybrid connectivity? Bring your architecture challenges - we'll draw through solutions together on the whiteboard.

sessions.t: Design your AWS Transform pipeline for parallel modernization at scale
sessions.a: How do you modernize thousands of applications concurrently to meet aggressive migration timelines? In this chalk talk, we'll work through architectural patterns for scaling AWS Transform with CI/CD integration: parallel processing with serverless compute, programmatic orchestration via APIs, container strategies, observability at scale, and campaign coordination across teams. Bring your use case and whiteboard it with us. Whether you need pipeline integration, secure private repo processing, or a self-service modernization platform, we'll design your architecture together.

sessions.t: Design your cedar authorization model with AI coding agents
sessions.a: Your identity provider handles authentication, but how do you design the authorization model that follows? In this chalk talk, learn how to use OIDC token claims from providers, including Amazon Cognito, with a Cedar-based authorization model. We'll walk through implementing RBAC, ReBAC, and ABAC patterns locally or in Amazon Verified Permissions, and show how to use AI coding agents (Kiro, Claude) to generate your schema and policies. Bring your use case for this interactive session. You'll leave with a repeatable approach to designing fine-grained authorization from scratch.

sessions.t: Deterministic control for probabilistic agents: proving safety holds
sessions.a: AI agents are probabilistic: vulnerable to prompt injection, hallucination, and unexpected tool composition. The controls around them must be deterministic. This session explores how to define provable safety envelopes for autonomous agents, drawing from the authorization and formal verification research behind AgentCore policy. We examine how automated reasoning guarantees policy correctness, how neuro-symbolic approaches combine LLM flexibility with mathematical verification for policy authoring, and how agents' action spaces can be reduced before execution. Attendees will also get a first look at new research extending these guarantees to emerging agentic authorization challenges.

sessions.t: Deterministic meets probabilistic: Patterns for reliable AI integration
sessions.a: Production systems demand determinism. AI outputs are probabilistic. The boundary between these two worlds is where this must be resolved. This chalk talk will whiteboard the contracts and integration patterns that hold that boundary: typed interfaces treating model output as untrusted input, propose/commit separation so AI never performs its own side effects, asymmetric verification, bounded generate-verify-repair loops, and compensating actions in place of rollback. We'll work through typical anti-patterns that quietly reach production, where to place the contract in your architecture to avoid these, and the reliability arithmetic that these patterns enable.

sessions.t: Develop with natural language and agentic AI in Amazon SageMaker
sessions.a: Dive into modern approaches to data engineering and machine learning using natural language and agentic AI assistance. We'll walk through practical examples that show how conversational AI and agents can streamline the development of data and ML workflows within Amazon SageMaker. You'll leave with the technical know-how you need to automate data engineering tasks and streamline ML development without writing code.

sessions.t: DevOps and Modernization Jam
sessions.a: Come with your team of four or join a team and meet new friends in the session. Compete head-to-head, race to the top of the leaderboard, and win prizes based on speed and accuracy. What if AI agents could autonomously manage your entire deployment pipeline? In this Jam, we provide hands-on environments where you can refactor applications using Kiro and automate operations with the Amazon DevOps Agent. Use spec-driven development to transform legacy monoliths into modern architecture. Configure AI agents that optimize your CI/CD pipelines for production. Structured for all experience levels, our sessions include guided exercises, helpful clues, and support from AWS experts to boost your modernization and DevOps expertise. All you need is a computer, a desire to learn, and a competitive spirit.

sessions.t: Digital sovereignty: Verifiable controls, greater choice, & innovation
sessions.a: Evolving regulations and geopolitical shifts are prompting organizations to rethink how they protect data, limit access, and maintain control in the cloud, without slowing innovation and AI adoption. This session explores how AWS helps customers meet their digital sovereignty requirements without compromising on capability through a range of offerings, including the AWS European Sovereign Cloud, backed by verifiable, auditable, and enforceable controls. Learn what AI sovereignty means in practice, get answers to the most common questions, and hear how AWS and partners are helping organizations cut through complexity in a fast-changing landscape.

sessions.t: Disaggregated inference at scale: when to split prefill from decode
sessions.a: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto independent GPU pools, eliminating the interference that lets one long prompt stall every active generation — and letting each phase scale on its own terms. It isn't free: KV cache must cross the network, and a well-cached unified deployment can still win. The difference is your traffic. In this hands-on builders session, you run both architectures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances, move KV cache between pools over Elastic Fabric Adapter, and benchmark them against realistic agentic traffic. Learn the decision framework — input length, prefix reuse, latency SLO — and leave with runnable configurations.

sessions.t: Distributed transactions with Step Functions and durable functions
sessions.a: Distributed transactions across microservices break in ways monoliths never did: partial failures, inconsistent state, rollbacks that don't roll back. In this builders' session, build a payment processing using saga pattern that orchestrates multiple serverless microservices using AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions. You'll implement compensation mechanisms that handle partial failures, compare orchestration approaches for short-lived versus long-running transactions, and monitor transaction flows across distributed services. Walk away with working saga patterns and the observability setup to troubleshoot them in production. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Dive deep into Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.a: This session provides a deep dive into Amazon DynamoDB and shares insights into how DynamoDB is architected and how it’s able to deliver the scalability and response times that customers have come to expect. DynamoDB is used by over one million AWS customers, and powers hundreds of applications that exceed half a million requests per second. In this talk we explore the architecture of DynamoDB, and of several specific features. You will understand how we architected DynamoDB to deliver predictable low latency at any scale, and how best to develop your own applications to delight your customers.

sessions.t: Dive deep into Amazon DynamoDB using design puzzles
sessions.a: In this session, dive deep into how Amazon DynamoDB works at scale by collaboratively solving a few design puzzles that may seem simple but are actually complex. Learn how to look beyond the obvious solution to find a more effective and scalable one with an understanding of how DynamoDB operates.

sessions.t: Don't ban it, broker it: Govern AI coding agents with Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: AI coding agents are becoming embedded in development workflows. In regulated environments (e.g.,financial services), that raises concerns around data residency, code exfiltration, auditability, and runaway costs. But banning the tools creates shadow AI. In this session, we'll whiteboard a better path by pointing AI coding agents at Amazon Bedrock through a gateway in your VPC. One control point for identity, data residency, prompt inspection, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, cost controls, and immutable audit. We'll walk through the request lifecycle, debate trade-offs around latency, budgets, and MCP tool calls, and show how the same broker pattern governs any agent touching sensitive data.

sessions.t: Don’t blame the model, it’s a context problem (sponsored by Confluent)
sessions.a: Your agents can't act on yesterday's data. In this session, learn how Confluent and IBM connect streaming events, governed data, and agent orchestration into one production-ready AI pattern on AWS. Confluent Intelligence brings streaming decisions into the flow of business, Granite TS predicts what comes next, and watsonx Orchestrate routes actions through the right agent—all grounded in fresh, governed business context. You'll leave with practical patterns for moving from brittle data pipelines to streaming-native AI, built for speed, trust, and scale. This presentation is brought to you by Confluent, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Don't build agents, build environments instead (sponsored by Modal)
sessions.a: The hard part of background agents is the background, not the agent. We'll talk about the common design that software factories have converged to and why building environments for agents is still hard. This presentation is brought to you by Modal, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Don't rewrite your APIs: Make them agent-ready for agentic AI
sessions.a: Organizations want agentic AI, but valuable capabilities sit behind legacy APIs, AWS Lambda functions, and internal services. In this chalk talk, we explore practical, low-lift patterns for making existing endpoints agent-ready without replacing systems of record. Using a financial services scenario, we walk through how OpenAPI specs, AWS Lambda facades, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway expose existing endpoints as composable agent tools. We show how existing RBAC and OAuth scopes map into Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Cedar policies so you reuse your governance posture. Walk away with a 5-level maturity model you can apply to your own API estate.

sessions.t: Don’t trust the model: automated reasoning as agent guardrails
sessions.a: Your agent is only as safe as the constraints it can’t bypass. This chalk talk covers how to enforce hard invariants on LLM-driven agents using formal policy languages — Cedar for stateless authorization, Dogwood for temporal reasoning over action history, and human-in-the-loop for the decisions machines shouldn’t make alone. We’ll dig into the Strands Agents intervention system, the neurosymbolic architecture that lets probabilistic and deterministic reasoning coexist, and where the open problems are.

sessions.t: Drive AI at full speed: The enterprise blueprint (sponsored by HashiCorp)
sessions.a: AI gave teams a faster car. It did not fix the roads. As teams create more applications, infrastructure and complexity, the challenge shifts from moving faster to operating smarter. Enterprises need context to understand what is happening, agency to act across the tools they already use, and control to keep speed from becoming chaos. In this session, see how Terraform and Vault together with Kubernetes, Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore and IBM Concert to standardize delivery, secure access and connect application context to action across hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by HashiCorp, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Drive multi-server migrations from discovery to cutover with AWS Transform
sessions.a: Migrating VMware or other on-premises environments to AWS involves dozens of coordinated steps, and most teams spend more time planning handoffs than actually moving workloads. In this workshop, you'll experience how AWS Transform's agentic AI orchestrates the full migration lifecycle: intelligent discovery, AI-driven wave planning, automated network translation, and server rehost execution. Specialized AI agents coordinate across each stage, making autonomous decisions while keeping you in control. You'll leave with hands-on experience using agentic AI to execute a real end-to-end multi-server migration. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Drug discovery and materials use cases with Amazon Braket and Q-CTRL
sessions.a: Classically hard problems such as simulating strongly correlated electrons and 1D NMR spectra, critical to material and drug discovery, can be sped up on quantum computers but until now had not been demonstrated. Q-CTRL shows how Fire Opal on Amazon Braket enables simulating 1D NMR spectra for spin systems up to 34 qubits and achieved a 3,000x speedup on the Fermi-Hubbard model at 120 qubits, demonstrating practical quantum advantage. This chalk talk unpacks how AWS hybrid workflows enabled these outcomes and what enterprises should do now to capture ROI with quantum.

sessions.t: DTCC: Rethinking mainframe modernization with spec-driven development
sessions.a: Services like Kiro, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Continuum, and AWS DevOps Agent have enabled DTCC to rethink its software delivery lifecycle. Now, the company is harnessing agents to modernize its legacy mainframe infrastructure. DTCC has adopted a spec-driven approach to COBOL refactoring, front-loading the process with a focus on principles, target architecture, and anti-pattern avoidance. In this session, you’ll see how a small team of engineers produced a fully functional microservice-based trade data ingestion platform in a few weeks, cutting the development timeline by 60% while laying the foundation to scale to peaks of 300+ million trades per day and beyond.

sessions.t: Duke Energy: Human-Led, Agent-Driven Enterprise App Innovation on AWS
sessions.a: Duke Energy is pioneering a new frontier in software creation by combining human leadership with agent-driven execution using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and AppGen, its enterprise AI platform. Specialized agents enable both developers and business users to rapidly build production-ready, full-stack applications with speed and precision, driving millions in cost savings while accelerating innovation. This strategic, multi-year collaboration is transforming manual workflows into intelligent, automated processes across business units. The approach supports scalable adoption of agentic AI while ensuring strong governance, reliability, and operational excellence—empowering teams to innovate faster, reduce complexity, and modernize systems consistently across the enterprise.

sessions.t: DynamoDB: the database designed for trillion-scale vector search
sessions.a: As vector search becomes a standard component of AI applications, scaling to billions or even trillions of vectors while maintaining single-digit millisecond latency and high recall remains a significant challenge. In this session, deep dive into the decisions made when building vector indexes for DynamoDB, including how vector indexes shard alongside table data, the scatter-gather query mechanism that keeps latencies tight, and the filtering that avoids recall degradation at scale. Learn how the partition key in DynamoDB maps naturally to multi-tenant workloads, enabling per-tenant index isolation without operational overhead. Discover the trade-offs between recall, latency, and cost in production for real-time vector search.

sessions.t: Earned autonomy: handing production over to agents (sponsored by incident.io)
sessions.a: Nobody hands an agent the keys to production on day one. Trust is earned the way it is with a new engineer: start read only, prove judgement on real incidents, widen the blast radius one scoped permission at a time. Drawing on building Investigations, an agent that does root cause analysis on live production incidents, this talk covers what agents are genuinely good at mid incident, where they fail badly, and the guardrails that make incremental autonomy safe: evidence backed reasoning, adversarial self checking, and a human on every action. This presentation is brought to you by incident.io, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Easy Self-Service AI: Design Agents with the Agentic CX Designer
sessions.a: Creating AI-powered self-service shouldn't require prompt engineering expertise - and in this hands-on workshop, you'll prove it. Go from a blank canvas to a deployed, production-ready AI agent in under two hours using Amazon Connect Customer’s agentic CX designer. Design conversational flows on the visual canvas, blending generative AI responses with deterministic business logic for scenarios like payment processing and identity verification. Connect your agent to external data sources, pass context seamlessly across conversation turns, then test and evaluate your agent's performance using built-in analytics and simulation tools. You'll leave with a working multi-channel AI agent, a repeatable design pattern you can apply to your own use cases, and confidence that your team can build and validate self-service experiences without specialized AI skills - no coding required.

sessions.t: EC2 Flex and T instances: Get modern performance at lower cost
sessions.a: Many workloads do not fully use all of the compute resources of a given instance, and we offer Flex and T instances to help cost-optimize for such workloads while getting the latest generation performance. In this session, we will dive deep into both Flex and T instances, which workloads are most suitable for these instances, high-level design, and ways customers can monitor the performance experience with these instances.

sessions.t: EC2 instances from launch to fleet orchestration
sessions.a: Amazon EC2 now offers over 1,000 instance types, five purchasing models, and a growing set of fleet and capacity tools. How do you bring it all together? This session is your comprehensive guide to AWS compute today. We cover the full EC2 portfolio from Graviton5 to accelerated instances, walk through On-Demand, Spot, Savings Plans, and Capacity Reservations, and show how EC2 Fleet, Auto Scaling, and Capacity Manager help you run the right instances at the right price. Whether you're new to EC2 or a seasoned practitioner, leave with a clear map of modern compute on AWS.

sessions.t: EC2 Spot: Capacity patterns and strategies from the team that runs it
sessions.a: In this chalk talk, two engineers from the EC2 Spot team share what they see from the inside: how capacity behaves across regions, instance families, and time of day, including why Graviton-based Spot is consistently available and how seasonal patterns create predictable opportunities. Bring your Spot architecture questions. We'll whiteboard real diversification strategies, walk through anonymized examples from our most successful customers, and discuss what separates workloads that scale effortlessly on Spot from those that struggle.

sessions.t: Edge-to-Action: Streaming On-Prem Data to Power Agentic AI (sponsored by Cloudera)
sessions.a: To build production-ready autonomous agents, AI requires continuous, real-time context. Deploying Cloudera’s services directly on-premises unlocks critical edge streaming telemetry, ingesting high-frequency data into Apache Iceberg tables on Cloudera’s Open Data Lakehouse on AWS. Learn how grounding generative AI models with streaming telemetry and dynamic operational context enables real-time anomaly detection. Discover how autonomous multi-agent workflows leverage streaming RAG and Model Context Protocol tools to execute closed-loop business actions from alerting operational teams to dispatching automated remediations without creating processing bottlenecks on primary databases. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Elastic Fabric Adapter powering the largest AI workloads on AWS
sessions.a: AWS built Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to bring high-performance networking to the cloud - powered by the Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) protocol designed for elastic, reliable, cloud-scale performance. This session explores EFA's origins in high-performance computing (HPC) and its evolution into the backbone of today's largest AI training and inference architectures. Discover how early architecture decisions now unlock novel use cases across pretraining, reinforcement learning, and disaggregated inference with hundreds of thousands of accelerators. We dive into recent innovations including library integrations, protocol optimizations, and performance gains.

sessions.t: Elasticsearch - the Search database for Context Engineering and AI
sessions.a: Your agentic applications have an accuracy and cost problem, and it's not your model choice. Sound familiar? If you're a developer trying to get LLMs to work effectively with your business context, this session is for you. Come learn how we rearchitected Elasticsearch as the database of choice for the different data types your enterprise knowledge is buried in — docs, logs, metrics, tickets, sales call transcripts, and more. From foundational innovations like Columnar and VectorDB mode with no ETL, to best-in-class retrieval that combines vector search, Jina embedding models, and native inference, Elastic is the context database for your production needs. Join this session to learn the best practices, from optimizing data preparation to retrieval patterns, to make your agents a production reality.

sessions.t: Elevate your observability with OpenTelemetry on AWS
sessions.a: Getting full visibility across your stack shouldn't mean stitching together disconnected tools and proprietary formats. When you standardize on OpenTelemetry with AWS, you get rich, unified telemetry from metrics, logs, and traces across your containers, Kubernetes clusters, AI workloads, and everything in between. Collect deep telemetry using OTLP ingestion, PromQL querying, and automatic enrichment with Amazon CloudWatch's native OpenTelemetry. No fragmented data. No vendor lock-in. Just one telemetry foundation that gives you the context you need to understand what's happening across your entire environment. Learn how to achieve richer data, unified observability, and a production-ready architecture that scales with you.

sessions.t: Embed Amazon Quick Chat Agents in Enterprise Applications
sessions.a: Deploy a fully serverless, production-ready solution that embeds Amazon Quick agents and dashboards into your enterprise web applications. Using AWS CDK, configure Amazon Cognito OAuth 2.0 authentication, Lambda, API Gateway, CloudFront, and WAF to create a secure embedding architecture. Implement the Quick Embedding SDK, configure domain security and token validation, and deploy a working chat agent accessible from any enterprise application — turning Quick into the conversational AI layer that meets users where they already work.

sessions.t: Embed FinOps into your CI/CD pipelines
sessions.a: Cost overruns from infrastructure changes often go undetected until after deployment, making shift-left cost governance a critical capability for platform and DevOps engineers. This builders' session guides attendees through constructing a working cost estimation gate integrated directly into a CI/CD pipeline. Using AWS CodePipeline, the AWS Pricing Calculator, and CloudFormation change sets, attendees build a pipeline stage that evaluates infrastructure cost impact at pull request time and enforces configurable spend thresholds before deployment proceeds. Bring a laptop to complete hands-on exercises with expert guidance in a small-group setting.

sessions.a: Multi-agent systems are rapidly evolving beyond static orchestration patterns. In this chalk talk, we explore the newest collaboration paradigms gaining momentum, including ephemeral agent patterns and self-improving agents, alongside established approaches like hierarchical, sequential, and peer-to-peer coordination. Walk through how to apply these patterns to claims adjudication, underwriting, and financial portfolio advisory using Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness engineering best practices. We'll discuss when to select each pattern, how to combine them for complex workflows, and how AgentCore harness capabilities enable scalable, governed multi-agent architectures. Gain practical guidance for designing the next generation of agentic applications.

sessions.t: Empowering 155,000 people without compromising trust: Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Allianz needed to empower 155,000 employees with AI without sacrificing trust. With operations across dozens of regulated markets, the security, privacy, and works council requirements were non-negotiable. Every stakeholder asked the same question: how do you move fast and still earn the trust of those guarding your company's security? Hear how Allianz partnered with AWS to deploy the capabilities that make Amazon Quick enterprise-ready: protection of confidential information, structured approval workflows for agentic actions, custom branding per business unit, and multi-language support. Learn how Allianz navigated the full approval process and moved from "not yet" to "go" in six weeks.

sessions.t: Enabling agentic development loops with a local cloud validation layer (sponsored by LocalStack)
sessions.a: Agentic coding loops let AI develop, test, and iterate on code autonomously. But agents often lack the permissions required to validate how code behaves in the cloud, stalling the cycle and holding back velocity. This session will show how simulating your AWS application environments locally can enable AI agents to identify and fix bugs faster, more securely, and more effectively than human engineers can when building in live cloud development environments. This presentation is brought to you by LocalStack, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Encoding Authorization in Logic from Puzzles to Production
sessions.a: Automated theorem provers can reason symbolically about a system's behavior and prove properties like "no user can ever escalate their own privileges" across all possible inputs. Of course, this requires modeling your problem in first-order logic, which demands careful thinking to precisely capture all behaviors of your system. In this session, learn how to encode your problem in first-order logic: starting with a logic puzzle to build intuition, then a toy authorization language, and finally what it takes for a full production system like Cedar, a fine-grained authorization language built with high assurance. We discuss challenges including ensuring correctness and completeness of the encoding.

sessions.t: End-to-end agentic modernization with United Airlines & Bank Hapoalim
sessions.a: Legacy applications across mainframe, midrange, and distributed platforms have long resisted modernization efforts. A new approach that combines deterministic methods with agentic AI is changing that by delivering speed and accuracy. Learn how United Airlines modernized crew operations while maintaining FAR compliance, and how Bank Hapoalim analyzed a 3.2-million-line mortgage application and delivered an insurance module to production under a board-mandated deadline while reducing operational risk. Follow the end-to-end journey, from automated discovery and business rule extraction with AWS Transform through microservices engineering with Kiro to production deployment. Leave with a playbook for modernizing the applications everyone said were untouchable.

sessions.t: End-to-end foundation model pipelines on SageMaker HyperPod with EKS
sessions.a: Train, deploy, and serve a foundation model end-to-end on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod with on Kubernetes. In this hands-on workshop, prepare training data at scale leveraging high speed storage, launch distributed fine-tuning across multi-node GPU clusters with auto-healing and checkpointless recovery that maximizes goodput, and transition seamlessly to production inference on the same cluster— eliminating re-platforming. Throughout, monitor cluster health and inference latency. Leave with working notebooks and production-ready patterns you can deploy immediately.

sessions.t: End-to-End ModelOps on SageMaker AI: Experiment to Production
sessions.a: Hands-on workshop where practitioners experiment with SageMaker AI end-to-end ModelOps capabilities: onboard, build, govern, deploy, monitor. Attendees track experiments with managed MLflow, orchestrate repeatable training workflows with SageMaker Pipelines and built-in lineage tracking, register and version models in Model Registry with model cards and approval gates, deploy through CI/CD promotion pipelines, and monitor for drift and quality with Model Monitor. Governance such as access control, validation, approvals, and Responsible AI guardrails is embedded into every step. Attendees leave with a repeatable, governed path from experiment to production they can stand up within a week

sessions.t: End-to-End ModelOps on SageMaker AI: Experiment to Production
sessions.a: Hands-on workshop where practitioners experiment with SageMaker AI end-to-end ModelOps capabilities: onboard, build, govern, deploy, monitor. Attendees track experiments with managed MLflow, orchestrate repeatable training workflows with SageMaker Pipelines and built-in lineage tracking, register and version models in Model Registry with model cards and approval gates, deploy through CI/CD promotion pipelines, and monitor for drift and quality with Model Monitor. Governance such as access control, validation, approvals, and Responsible AI guardrails is embedded into every step. Attendees leave with a repeatable, governed path from experiment to production they can stand up within a week

sessions.t: End-to-End Voice Agents with AWS and Deepgram (sponsored by Deepgram)
sessions.a: Voice agents are growing in popularity, but most fall apart the first time a caller interrupts or asks a hard question. In this session, Deepgram builds one live on AWS: the Deepgram Voice Agent API streams speech in and out within minutes, with Amazon Bedrock as the reasoning layer. You'll see natural, expressive voices, sub-second responses, and barge-in handling that actually works. Compliance requirements? The same models deploy via Amazon SageMaker inside your own VPC, so audio never leaves your AWS perimeter. Leave with running code and an architecture your security team can approve. This presentation is brought to you by Deepgram, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Enforce AI guardrails across your organization without the friction
sessions.a: When a cloud-native energy company needed to build security operations from scratch, they faced a choice: hire a SOC team or find a smarter way to triage threats. In this talk, the AWS Customer Incident Response Team walks through how customers go from manual CloudTrail analysis to AI-assisted triage, and why that matters now that adversaries are using AI to accelerate their own attacks.

sessions.t: Enforce AI guardrails across your organization without the friction
sessions.a: When a cloud-native energy company needed to build security operations from scratch, they faced a choice: hire a SOC team or find a smarter way to triage threats. In this talk, the AWS Customer Incident Response Team walks through how customers go from manual CloudTrail analysis to AI-assisted triage, and why that matters now that adversaries are using AI to accelerate their own attacks.

sessions.t: Enforce encryption in transit using Amazon VPC Encryption Controls
sessions.a: Regulated workloads demand encryption in transit, but verifying coverage across VPCs, instances, and endpoints is manual and error-prone. In this session, audit and enforce encryption in transit for Amazon VPC traffic using VPC Encryption Controls. Learn how to enable Monitor Mode to assess current encryption posture, migrate to Nitro instances, activate AWS Transit Gateway encryption for cross-VPC traffic, and switch to Enforce Mode. Analyze encryption status across Amazon EC2, NLB, AWS Transit Gateway, and Amazon S3 endpoint flows with Amazon VPC Flow Logs. Leave with hands-on experience enforcing encryption for HIPAA, PCI DSS, and FedRAMP compliance.

sessions.t: Enforce encryption in transit using Amazon VPC Encryption Controls
sessions.a: Regulated workloads demand encryption in transit, but verifying coverage across VPCs, instances, and endpoints is manual and error-prone. In this session, audit and enforce encryption in transit for Amazon VPC traffic using VPC Encryption Controls. Learn how to enable Monitor Mode to assess current encryption posture, migrate to Nitro instances, activate AWS Transit Gateway encryption for cross-VPC traffic, and switch to Enforce Mode. Analyze encryption status across Amazon EC2, NLB, AWS Transit Gateway, and Amazon S3 endpoint flows with Amazon VPC Flow Logs. Leave with hands-on experience enforcing encryption for HIPAA, PCI DSS, and FedRAMP compliance.

sessions.t: Engineering AI Agents You Can Trust in Production (sponsored by Workato)
sessions.a: Your agent nails the demo, then breaks in production. More often than not, the model isn't what failed, it's everything around it. We'll walk through a methodology for making agent actions reliable, recoverable, and observable in production. You'll leave with patterns you can build yourself, drawn from lessons learned over 100+ enterprise MCP deployments. This presentation is brought to you by Workato, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Engineering the Context that Makes Enterprise AI Work (sponsored by Impetus Technologies Inc)
sessions.a: Every enterprise has access to the same AI models. The real differentiator is context. Discover Impetus’ Context Engineering Delivery Lifecycle, a proven methodology than ensures no AI agent reaches production without a signed-off context bundle, evaluation record, and explainability trace. Learn how to engineer enterprise data, domain knowledge, industry ontologies, business rules, and governance into a robust context layer agents need to deliver accurate, trusted outcomes. Get practical insights on building AI systems on AWS that are grounded, explainable, reliable, and ready to scale. This presentation is brought to you by Impetus Technologies Inc, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Enhance Production Applications with AI-Assisted Development in Kiro
sessions.a: Enhancing production apps requires balancing delivery velocity with code safety. Kiro gives you both. In this hands-on lab, add features to enhance a live application using AI-assisted development on Kiro. Define coding standards with steering files and specs, generate UI components from natural language prompts, automate quality checks with agent hooks, install powers for domain expertise, and delegate backend analysis to custom subagents. Deploy your changes confidently to production environments.

sessions.t: Enterprise AI is missing a key ingredient: The knowledge layer (sponsored by Neo4j)
sessions.a: You don't need another post-mortem to know why enterprise AI projects fail. Organizations that have moved AI from pilot to production know it runs on context. A knowledge layer shows AI how facts relate, what's changed, and what's already been decided. Trained on siloed data, a model sees disconnected records, not relationships, and can't reason well without that context. The knowledge layer connects GenAI and agentic systems to data that's organized and accessible. In this session, we'll cover why the knowledge layer is the missing piece your enterprise AI needs, and what your organization gains from implementing one: Trust every AI answer, back to your source data. Prove every AI decision with a complete audit trail. Synthesize intelligence across disparate systems and teams. Use your existing data investments instead of replacing them. This presentation is brought to you by Neo4j, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Enterprise-Grade Outcomes. Within Reach for Growing Businesses. (sponsored by Accenture)
sessions.a: Discover how Accenture Edge for AWS helps growing organizations (under $3B in annual revenue) achieve the same transformative outcomes as larger enterprises through pre-built, outcome-driven solutions designed for speed, simplicity, and value. We are taking enterprise-grade talent and tools and making them accessible and approachable. Translation: Big outcomes at lower costs thanks to pre-configured solutions. Hear real examples of customers that accelerated cloud adoption, reduced costs, strengthened security, and modernized faster with Accenture and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Enterprise-Ready: How NetEase Governs AI at Scale
sessions.a: Learn how NetEase, one of the world's largest gaming companies, is building enterprise AI governance as AI adoption scales across the organization. Discover how Amazon Bedrock enables multi-model routing, cost controls, and team-level budget management to optimize AI usage. See how NetEase enforces governance with company-wide AI policies, Bedrock Guardrails for content safety, and Bedrock AgentCore for orchestrating agentic AI workflows with centralized governance and observability. Learn why a platform-first approach to cost, access, and safety is critical for enabling AI innovation at enterprise scale.

sessions.t: Escaping IIoT Pilot Purgatory: Why Your Database Breaks at Scale (sponsored by Tiger Data)
sessions.a: Seventy-four percent of industrial IoT projects stall somewhere between pilot and production. The hard part is that the pilot worked. That is exactly what makes the failure so difficult to diagnose. Pilots succeed because a few hundred sensors over a few weeks fits comfortably in almost any database. Production does not. Storage costs compound faster than the budget that approved them, ingest hits a cliff with no warning, and the real-time dashboard that sold the project turns into a loading screen. See where industrial systems and typical AWS pipelines reach their limits and how to scale beyond them. We’ll explore a proven architecture using AWS IoT Core, Amazon Kinesis, AWS Lambda, and a single Postgres database to support more than one million connected devices reporting every second. This presentation is brought to you by Tiger Data, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Essentials for migrating from Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
sessions.a: Migrating from Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition can be a transformative journey, offering significant cost savings and performance benefits. However, this transition requires careful planning and execution. In this session, discover the essential things you need to know to ensure a smooth and successful migration from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL and the optimal architectures to enable such a migration. Learn best practices and pitfalls to avoid from seasoned experts who have helped many customers walk this path.

sessions.t: EU Operational Autonomy in Action: AWS European Sovereign Cloud
sessions.a: The AWS European Sovereign Cloud is built on fully isolated infrastructure within the EU, operated exclusively by EU-resident staff, with no access from outside Europe. In this lightning talk, learn from the AWS European Sovereign Cloud Managed Operations team what independent operations means in practice and how it works day to day.

sessions.t: Eval-Driven LLM Routing: Cut Costs Without Losing Accuracy
sessions.a: This session shows how to build an eval-driven LLM routing system: harvest a production eval dataset, define accuracy KPIs using LLM-as-judge, set a non-negotiable accuracy floor as the practitioner's decision, benchmark candidate models, and generate a routing policy optimized for cost within that floor. Result: approximately 80% cost reduction at maintained accuracy. A reference architecture you can start implementing immediately.

sessions.t: Evaluate, Disclose, Safeguard: A Production-Readiness Framework for AI Agents
sessions.a: Every organization is building AI agents, but few have made it to production. You can't prove it works, you can't prove it's responsible, and compliance won't sign off. In this chalk talk, we walk through a production-readiness framework for AI agents on Amazon Connect. First, evaluation: measuring resolution with the Connect Simulation API to score AI agents on the same bar as human agents. Second, responsible AI: disclosure patterns that build trust, escalation triggers for sensitive journeys, and harm avoidance for regulated industries. Third, safeguards: defense-in-depth governance for agents that process refunds and access sensitive data, including asymmetric PII, MCP tool authorization for human confirmation, and automated escalation when confidence drops. Leave with a checklist: what to measure, what to disclose, what to block, and when to ship.

sessions.t: Evaluate Enterprise AI Agents with an Eval-First Approach
sessions.a: A successful agent demo does not guarantee production readiness because agents can behave inconsistently across question types and multi-turn sessions. In this spotlight lab, you build two custom evaluators for an agent: THELMA, which scores single-turn RAG quality across seven dimensions including hallucination detection via groundedness scoring, and Mind the Goal, which computes Goal Success Rate across entire conversations and attributes failures to root causes. You register both as native AgentCore evaluators, run batch evaluations, and use diagnostic outputs to pinpoint exactly what to optimize first.

sessions.t: Evaluate, select, optimize and find your best model
sessions.a: Most teams pick a model on instinct. In this hands-on workshop, you'll build a structured evaluation pipeline for your own use case, run it against multiple model candidates (frontier and open-weight), and learn exactly when customization is worth the investment vs. when prompt engineering or RAG is enough. You'll leave with a working evaluation harness, a decision framework for technique selection (SFT vs. RFT vs. CPT), and a trained model you can take home.

sessions.t: Evaluating AI agents for production in financial services
sessions.a: Financial institutions building AI agents face a core challenge: how do you prove an agent is reliable enough for production when regulators demand explainability and consistency? How do you reliably detect when a production agent's behavior drifts? In this chalk talk, we explore patterns for rigorous agent evaluation in regulated environments. We discuss defining ground truth, measuring agent quality with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, and automating re-evaluation as prompts, tools, and parameters evolve. Leave with practical blueprints for constructing datasets, choosing metrics, and building continuous agent evaluation workflows for production.

sessions.t: Evaluating AI agents for production in financial services

sessions.t: Evaluating AI Agents for your Nonprofit: From Vibes to Metrics on AWS
sessions.a: You shipped an agent. How do you know it works? For organizations where AI decisions affect people's lives, rigorous evaluation isn't optional — it's ethical. This chalk talk introduces a structured evaluation framework combining Amazon Bedrock model evaluation, AgentCore observability, and CloudWatch metrics. We cover building eval datasets, measuring tool-use accuracy, detecting hallucination in agentic chains, benchmarking latency and cost, and setting up automated regression testing. Leave with a repeatable eval pipeline you can plug into CI/CD — turning agent quality from subjective to measurable.

sessions.t: Event-driven agents at scale: building agentic AI on Amazon MSK
sessions.a: Production agents need to dispatch long-running actions, wait on external systems, fan results out to analytics, and re-enter the conversation when work finishes — not sit in a synchronous loop. In this session, we present reusable patterns for building multi-tenant, event-driven agentic systems on Amazon MSK: dispatch-and-resume for long-running tool calls, topic and partition design keyed to tenant and conversation, decoupling the agent loop from channels and analytics, and durability and replay so in-flight work survives deploys and retries. Learn a practical approach for designing agentic SaaS that stays reliable as load, tools, and channels grow.

sessions.t: Event-driven AI agents for security triage with AWS Continuum
sessions.a: Security teams need to detect, correlate, and respond to threats faster than manual processes allow. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS Continuum orchestrates event-driven AI agents that triage, investigate, and escalate security incidents in real time. We walk through how alerts from Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub flow through Amazon EventBridge, triggering AWS Lambda functions that invoke agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, with human-in-the-loop controls for high-severity events. Discover best practices for reducing alert fatigue, accelerating MTTR, and scaling security operations for financial services and other regulated industries where every response must be explainable and audit ready.

sessions.t: Event storming: Find your service boundaries before production does
sessions.a: Split a system in the wrong place and you get a distributed monolith: coupled services with network hops instead of function calls. This session tackles the problem most teams get wrong, where to draw the boundary, using Event Storming. Together we map a real domain, trace information flow between actors, and identify natural division points, deciding ownership, data locality, transaction scope, and deployment independence at each boundary. Every decision is evidence based, grounded in observed event flow rather than intuition. Then you go hands on, taking one boundary and deploying it as an independent service on AWS. Leave with a repeatable method for boundary definition plus working code you built yourself. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Every Flight Has a Story. Here’s What It Takes to Power It. (sponsored by ZS)
sessions.a: United and ZS go behind the scenes of the data, AI and technology powering personalized flight stories for travelers at scale. This presentation is brought to you by ZS, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Everyone is a Coder. Govern what they build. (sponsored by Coder)
sessions.a: Suddenly, everyone is a coder. People who never wrote code now build apps, dashboards, and prototypes with AI, faster than most teams can govern them. The result is shadow AI, ungoverned data, and IP risk. See how a leading global private investment firm gave citizen developers a governed place to build on its existing AWS infrastructure, replacing scattered, unmanaged tools. Learn how approved models, scoped templates, centralized container management, and a complete audit trail let hundreds of builders move fast inside guardrails. Attendees leave with a practical model for governing AI adoption on their own AWS environment. This presentation is brought to you by Coder, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Everyone Says They Have an Ontology. Almost Nobody Does (sponsored by TextQL)
sessions.a: Ontology has become one of the defining ideas in enterprise AI. Every cloud and data platform now claims to have one. They rarely converge on the same structure, conventions, or architecture. Those differences determine whether an ontology can support agentic AI. That test comes down to three things: how it's structured, how it's generated from the systems and context already in place, and how it stays current as the business changes. This talk lays out the practical requirements for an ontology built for agentic AI, drawing on the architecture TextQL runs across the messiest data estates at Fortune 50 companies. This presentation is brought to you by TextQL, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Everything you've wanted to know about performance on EC2 instances
sessions.a: Getting the best compute performance is an art, and knowing low-level details helps a lot. This talk covers everything you've wanted to know: memory topology, accessing hardware counters, hyperthreading side-effects, and how to properly run performance tests and optimize your latency for production.

sessions.t: Evolve Amazon DynamoDB data models with no application impact
sessions.a: Master advanced techniques for evolving Amazon DynamoDB data models without application interruption. Learn versioning strategies, backward compatibility patterns, and migration approaches for production applications. In this session, architect a solution that covers attribute addition and removal, data type changes, and index modifications while maintaining 24/7 availability. Explore real-world migration scenarios, rollback strategies, and handling distributed application dependencies. The best practices covered in this session are essential for teams managing large-scale DynamoDB applications requiring continuous evolution while serving millions of requests.

sessions.t: Expand your GPU playbook: Amazon EC2 G7e/G7 for inference and training
sessions.a: Not every ML workload needs the same GPU. Amazon EC2 G7e and G7 instances, powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with GDDR7 and native FP4 support, deliver compelling price-performance for inference and select training use cases. This session breaks down where G7e/G7 fits: inference prefill (competitive FLOPS/$) and decode (FP4 and higher concurrency close the HBM gap), and training via pipeline parallelism. We'll cover the toolchain (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, TransformerEngine, CUTLASS FP4 kernels), walk through a TCO comparison, and close with a decision framework for when G7e/G7 is the right call vs. P-family instances.

sessions.t: Expedite model loading times on Kubernetes using kro and ACK - from storage to GPU
sessions.a: LLM inference on Kubernetes is bottlenecked by loading multi-gigabyte model weights through the storage → network → CPU → PCIe → GPU path. In this chalk talk we benchmark four approaches to accelerating model delivery to GPU memory: SOCI for lazy-loading container image layers, s5cmd parallel downloads, Mountpoint for Amazon S3 CSI streaming, and Run.ai Model Streamer for direct S3-to-GPU pipelining. We walk through when each technique shines, how they compose together, and the tradeoffs platform teams face when optimizing inference cold starts on Amazon EKS. Learn how kro and ACK enable declarative provisioning of optimized storage pipelines, allowing platform teams to compose reusable stacks.

sessions.t: Expedite model loading times on Kubernetes using kro and ACK - from storage to GPU

sessions.t: Experience catalog federation on AWS: build a multi-cloud open data lakehouse
sessions.a: Enterprise data teams have distributed data catalogs across multiple cloud providers, each with partial visibility and no shared query surface. This hands-on workshop demonstrates how catalog federation unifies cross-cloud data silos into an open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Using Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation with Apache Iceberg as the open, engine-neutral table format for seamless interoperability and zero data duplication across AWS, Snowflake, and Databricks, you'll federate remote catalogs to build a unified lakehouse on AWS to run AI-assisted business analytics.

sessions.t: Exploit a software vulnerability, then stop it - From code to containment
sessions.a: Step into the role of a DevSecOps engineer tasked with hardening your organization's web applications after a security audit. In this hands-on workshop, a simulated lab walks you through real threat scenarios, and you respond using layered AWS security services. Start with Amazon Inspector Code Security to catch vulnerabilities pre-deployment, then use Kiro's agentic capabilities to auto-remediate issues without leaving your IDE. Scan EC2 instances and SBOMs for supply-chain risk, apply virtual patches via AWS WAF, and fully remediate with AWS Systems Manager. Finally, contain an active GuardDuty-detected incident by blocking C2 communication with Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall and AWS Network Firewall — proving that layered defenses hold even against unpatched vulnerabilities.

sessions.t: Explore agentic data engineering in Amazon SageMaker
sessions.a: Data engineering teams lose time to siloed data, manual ETL, and tribal knowledge. This session shows how agents change that in Amazon SageMaker. Use SageMaker Data Agent to trace errors, refactor code, and deploy pipelines in natural language, then bring your own agents through MCP servers to work with third-party clients and models directly on your data. See how the same agentic approach extends across SageMaker, so teams can consolidate fragmented pipelines, standardize environments, and put agents to work on more of the data engineering lifecycle.

sessions.t: Extend Amazon EKS clusters for on-premises and edge use cases
sessions.a: Dive deep into strategies for modernizing distributed applications with Amazon EKS across AWS Regions, AWS Local Zones, and AWS Outposts. This chalk talk demonstrates how EKS delivers a consistent experience across these deployment options, minimizing latency and enabling data residency. Through a real-world scenario, we'll deploy an application to an EKS cluster, showcasing seamless integration across distributed environments while maintaining a unified control plane. By exploring practical use cases and best practices, you'll gain actionable insights into architecting resilient and scalable applications. This session follows AWS Well-Architected Framework principles, helping you optimize your AWS deployments for consistency and security.

sessions.t: Extend AWS WAF to the APIs your AI agents call (sponsored by Wallarm)
sessions.a: Network and edge controls stop the traffic patterns they were built to recognize. AI agents introduce a different pattern: authenticated requests, at machine speed, against business logic rather than known vulnerabilities. Teams running AWS WAF often find these requests pass inspection because nothing about them is malformed. In this session, examine how agent-driven traffic reaches APIs, which risks fall outside signature and rate-based inspection, and what an additive API security layer contributes. Learn how teams instrument existing AWS WAF deployments for API-level visibility, apply real-time redaction to sensitive data in responses, and enforce without adding latency. This presentation is brought to you by Wallarm, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Extending your cloud network with Amazon Leo satellite connectivity
sessions.a: Your cloud network doesn't have to end where fiber does. In this interactive whiteboard session, you'll design hybrid network architectures that combine Amazon Leo's low-earth orbit satellite connectivity with AWS networking services including VPN, Transit Gateway, and Cloud WAN. We'll start with Leo's real-world performance characteristics: latency, throughput, and availability. Then, we'll work through three architecture patterns: first-day connectivity for new sites, primary connectivity for remote locations, and satellite-based redundancy for existing terrestrial links. You'll leave with reference architectures you can adapt to your environment and a clear understanding of how the constellation fits in your network design.

sessions.t: Fanatics path to AWS: 5 data centers, 1,800 servers, 48% savings
sessions.a: If your migration is stuck because no one can agree on what moves first while licensing costs compound and dependencies stay undocumented, the problem isn’t willingness. It’s sequencing. Fanatics Commerce had 1800 servers across five data centers and projected 48% infrastructure savings on AWS. Their team shares the structured path: OLA for licensing clarity, DAP for dependency mapping, EBA for organizational alignment, MAP for execution. Walk away with: (1) a concrete OLA-to-MAP sequence, (2) an AI-assisted dependency mapping approach that surfaced connections no one had documented (3) a phased AWS Transform modernization strategy that earns engineering trust before scaling.

sessions.t: FanDuel: What we learned running containers on hundreds of AWS Outposts
sessions.a: Running containerized workloads across dozens of AWS Local Zones and hundreds of AWS Outposts demands operational patterns that hold up at fleet scale. In this session, learn how FanDuel operates Amazon EKS across a massive hybrid edge fleet with a focus on high availability, patching, observability, service-disruption handling, and autoscaling. We dive into how workloads respond gracefully to service-link and hardware disruptions, and how autoscaling behaves when capacity is constrained to physical racks. Discover the operational model that keeps a large edge fleet healthy without growing the platform team at the same rate.

sessions.t: Fast and easy bulk operations with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.a: In this session, learn patterns for executing fast, safe, cost-aware bulk operations in Amazon DynamoDB using AWS Glue, Spark SQL, and open source tooling that hides the complexity. Discover how to find, filter, diff, load, and update billions of items in parallel. Explore how lightweight AI can make bulk work more powerful and user-friendly. Attendees leave with reusable patterns, real-world workload insights, and tools that simplify DynamoDB bulk processing.

sessions.t: Fast and easy bulk operations with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.a: In this session, learn patterns for executing fast, safe, cost-aware bulk operations in Amazon DynamoDB using AWS Glue, Spark SQL, and open source tooling that hides the complexity. Discover how to find, filter, diff, load, and update billions of items in parallel. Explore how lightweight AI can make bulk work more powerful and user-friendly. Attendees leave with reusable patterns, real-world workload insights, and tools that simplify DynamoDB bulk processing.

sessions.t: Faster root cause analysis for IAM access denied errors
sessions.a: When an IAM request is denied, teams can spend valuable time finding the root cause. Now, access denied error messages go beyond surfacing the policy type or ARN that blocked a request—they tell you the exact reason access was denied. In this session, we'll walk through how the feature works, how to put it to use, and considerations for larger AWS environments where different policy types are owned by different teams.

sessions.t: Fault-tolerant AI agents: Choosing the right recovery pattern
sessions.a: When an AI agent crashes at step 20 of 30, you can't just start over. Once state accumulates, a blind retry becomes dangerous. Most teams default to the wrong recovery strategy because they apply stateless retry thinking to stateful workflows. In this session, we compare three approaches: replay-based recovery with idempotent tool execution, checkpoint-and-resume with human-in-the-loop pause/resume, and event-driven compensation across trust boundaries. We'll whiteboard each pattern, map it to real failure scenarios, and build a decision framework based on your agent's state model and fault domain.
