sessions.t: Financial data modeling with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.a: Designing business applications for low latency, high throughput, high consistency, and high availability presents unique challenges at scale. In this session, learn how to model business entities including accounts, journals, and ledgers using Amazon DynamoDB to support workflows that process millions of requests per second. Explore distributed computing patterns that leverage multi-Region replication features in DynamoDB. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Financial data modeling with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.a: Designing business applications for low latency, high throughput, high consistency, and high availability presents unique challenges at scale. In this session, learn how to model business entities including accounts, journals, and ledgers using Amazon DynamoDB to support workflows that process millions of requests per second. Explore distributed computing patterns that leverage multi-Region replication features in DynamoDB. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Find and fix storage bottlenecks for self-managed OLTP on EC2 with EBS
sessions.a: ​​When you run a self-managed OLTP database on Amazon EC2, the storage bottleneck is rarely where you assume. This hands-on session teaches a repeatable method for finding and fixing it. Use Flexible IO tester and a PostgreSQL/pgbench workload to connect storage metrics to database symptoms. Measure latency, IOPS, throughput, and queue depth; determine whether the limit is the volume, instance bandwidth, or I/O pattern; then tune the right EBS volume configuration. Validate every change with EBS detailed performance statistics and CloudWatch. Leave with a proven sizing-and-tuning method for database workloads on EC2.

sessions.t: Find failure modes faster: AI-powered resilience assessments
sessions.a: Manual resilience reviews are slow, inconsistent, and routinely miss failure modes that don't surface until an incident occurs. In this workshop, you'll use the generative AI-driven assessment engine in AWS Resilience Hub to automatically discover dependencies across AWS services, internal endpoints, and third-party systems. You'll evaluate workloads against the Well-Architected Framework and your own defined resilience policies including availability SLOs, RTO, and RPO targets, then receive prioritized, actionable recommendations tied to business impact. Working with a reference architecture, you'll build a complete end-to-end assessment and leave with a repeatable framework you can run against any workload as your architecture evolves. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Fine-grained access control across engines with AWS Glue Data Catalog
sessions.a: Your data lives in a catalog but is queried from many engines. How do you enforce consistent access policies without duplicating rules everywhere? In this chalk talk, we explore how AWS Glue Data Catalog centralizes fine-grained access control so that permissions defined once are enforced uniformly whether users query from Redshift, Athena, EMR, or Spark. We'll work through patterns for column and row-level security, tag-based policies, cross-account sharing with least-privilege grants, and how to audit who accessed what. Bring your multi-engine governance challenges.

sessions.t: Fine-Tune Agents That Reason: Multi-Turn RL on SageMaker AI
sessions.a: AI agents doing real work, like financial advising, coding, customer operations, reason across turns, call tools, and recover when steps fail mid-conversation. Prompting won't get you there; building multi-turn RL from scratch takes weeks. We'll whiteboard how SageMaker AI's managed MTRL connects your Strands, LangChain, or CrewAI agent under 10 lines of code - handling rollouts, trajectories, and checkpointing, auto-cataloged in SageMaker catalog. We'll cover reward design, rollouts in managed gym environments, decoupled training compute keeping GPUs from idling, and smaller specialized models outperforming larger ones at lower inference cost. Bring your agent use case for mapping the path.

sessions.t: Fine-tune and evaluate NVIDIA Nemotron 3 with Amazon SageMaker Serverless Fine-tuning (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.a: Learn how to customize NVIDIA Nemotron 3 using Amazon SageMaker Serverless Fine-tuning without managing training infrastructure. This session walks through preparing a dataset, fine-tuning the model, and evaluating the customized model against the base model to measure improvements in quality. Attendees will leave with a practical workflow for adapting Nemotron to domain-specific use cases on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: FinOps for AI: Cost allocation strategies for Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how spend maps to business outcomes. In this builders' session, you'll get hands on with the latest cost management capabilities for Amazon Bedrock. You'll tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control Gen AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. You'll then query new product metadata in CUR2 and visualize cost-per-million-token trends in CUDOS. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

sessions.t: FinOps for AI: Cost allocation strategies for Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how spend maps to business outcomes. In this builders' session, you'll get hands on with the latest cost management capabilities for Amazon Bedrock. You'll tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control Gen AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. You'll then query new product metadata in CUR2 and visualize cost-per-million-token trends in CUDOS. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

sessions.t: FinOps for AI: Open the black box on AI spend (sponsored by Apptio)
sessions.a: AI spend often arrives as a black box: a rising bill with little clarity into which teams, models or features drove it. In this breakout, learn how Cloudability helps teams apply FinOps discipline to AI on AWS by categorizing costs, connecting spend to business goals and identifying waste. Discover how we turn that visibility into action for AI workloads running on Amazon EKS, improving GPU efficiency, Kubernetes workload right-sizing and application performance. Then apply the same cost discipline to Amazon Bedrock, including smarter provisioned throughput decisions, so teams can explain, defend and optimize AI spend. This presentation is brought to you by Apptio, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: FinOps for AI: Scale Investments That Work. Stop Ones That Don't. (sponsored by Kion)
sessions.a: Most organizations can tell you what they spend on AI. Fewer can tell you what they're getting for it. FinOps for AI closes that gap, but it takes three things: visibility into spend by use case; controls that act on what the data tells you instead of just surfacing it; and value tracking that connects spend to outcomes your stakeholders can evaluate. This session includes real examples of token attribution, guardrail patterns that respond to data, and a model for turning ROI signals into corrective action. This presentation is brought to you by Kion, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: First principles at LLM scale: Architecting Forge
sessions.a: When we set out to build Forge, Amazon's foundation model customization platform, we assumed the hardest problems would be ML problems. They weren't. They were classical problems Amazon's been solving for years, at a new scale. Same Well-Architected principles, evolved techniques. We will deep-dive into three workloads from the team behind Forge. First, serverless training of large language models on AWS. Second, enterprise-grade inference serving. Third, observability and evaluation tools optimizing toward smaller, performant models. Leave with lessons for your own AI platform.

sessions.t: Fix Data Gaps Fast: Agentic Onboarding with Amazon Connect Decisions
sessions.a: 81% of enterprises report AI initiatives delayed or abandoned due to data and governance gaps — and 80–90% of new enterprise data is unstructured. The bottleneck isn't the model; it's the data. In this session, see how Amazon Connect Decisions uses agentic AI teammates to eliminate that gap. Watch a supply chain planner go from zero to a running demand forecast — connecting raw CSVs with no pre-cleaning, letting AI intelligently map and type-convert data, catching and fixing quality issues conversationally, and encoding tribal knowledge from a Word doc into live decision rules. No ETL code, no JIRA tickets, no months-long implementation. Onboarding in weeks, not months.

sessions.t: Fleet-wide AIOps for Amazon EKS with the AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.a: Operating one EKS cluster is manageable. Operating a fleet of them is where the hard problems live: failures that surface far from their cause, VPC CNI IP exhaustion, Karpenter churn, and upgrades that stall across clusters. This chalk talk shows how AIOps and the AWS DevOps Agent bring order to operations at fleet scale. See how the DevOps Agent correlates signals across clusters to find root cause instead of chasing symptoms. Learn how it turns noisy telemetry into a diagnosis and a recommended fix. Discover the guardrails that let agents act on your fleet safely, with the blast radius bounded.

sessions.t: Follow that log from pipeline to intelligence
sessions.a: You've got logs flowing from everywhere, but when an issue spans multiple accounts or regions, you're stuck jumping between consoles trying to piece together what happened. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard the end-to-end path a log takes from ingestion pipeline to a unified data layer to log analytics. We'll break down where visibility gaps form and why. Learn how you can connect these layers to trace a problem across your entire environment without losing context.

sessions.t: Foundational architecture excellence: the operability trade-off
sessions.a: Elegant architectures that ignore operational reality become expensive liabilities. From hundreds of enterprise engagements, we expose the architectural decisions that silently create operational debt — decomposition without observability boundaries, blast-radius assumptions that fail under correlated load, and abstraction layers hiding the signals operators need. We unpack where good architecture and operable architecture diverge, which trade-offs are worth making early, and what questions your team should be asking before committing to a design. The best architecture is one you can actually run in production.

sessions.t: Foundational Model Ops with Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Build a fine-tuning pipeline that proves its own results. In this workshop, run the full loop, baseline eval, fine-tune, RL, re-eval, against the same bar every time. Start with a benchmark baseline on a Hugging Face model. Then fine-tune with QLoRA on Amazon SageMaker AI Training Jobs, with full control over your training script and compute. Add an RL pass with RLAIF or RLVR to optimize against a reward signal the benchmark alone can't score, and re-evaluate against that same baseline to see whether the gain is real or just a lower loss number. Put the whole sequence into a SageMaker Pipeline so it reruns on new data without manual rework. Bedrock Guardrails sit at the deployment gate.

sessions.t: Four agents, one answer: multi-agent synthesis on AWS
sessions.a: We live-build a multi-agent system where specialized agents — a document searcher, a data analyst, a claims verifier, and a synthesizer — collaborate to produce evidence-backed summaries from unstructured sources. Using Bedrock's multi-model routing, each agent selects the optimal foundation model for its task. Along the way we solve hard coordination problems: message routing, shared state, deadlock avoidance, and cost control. One presenter codes; the other narrates architecture decisions. Whether you synthesize research literature, member feedback, grant requirements, or compliance updates — leave with replicable patterns for your domain.

sessions.t: Four agents, one answer: multi-agent synthesis on AWS
sessions.a: We live-build a multi-agent system where specialized agents — a document searcher, a data analyst, a claims verifier, and a synthesizer — collaborate to produce evidence-backed summaries from unstructured sources. Using Bedrock's multi-model routing, each agent selects the optimal foundation model for its task. sessions.t: Four labs to shrink your Windows and SQL Server licensing bill
sessions.a: Lift-and-shift gets you to the cloud, but it doesn't solve the licensing costs that follow. In this builders' session, you'll work through four labs to reduce your Windows and SQL Server spend on Amazon EC2: (1) enable Compute Optimizer for continuous fleet right-sizing; (2) use Optimize CPU to align cores with compute requirements; (3) classify SQL Server HA clusters to remove passive-node licensing fees; and (4) downgrade SQL Server Enterprise to Standard edition. Leave with a production-ready cost optimization blueprint.

sessions.t: Free your .NET app from Windows licensing with AI-powered portability
sessions.a: This workshop walks you through modernizing a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to cross-platform .NET 10. You will learn how to transform a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to .NET 10 Blazor using AWS Transform Interactive Mode. Throughout the session, you will interact with the AI agent in real-time asking questions, reviewing assessment and transformation plans, and examining transformation results, including code diffs and build verification. Finally, use Kiro to identify and fix post-transformation runtime issues, such as layout problems, and containerize and deploy the transformed application to Amazon ECS Fargate using the Kiro IDE.

sessions.t: Fresh Threats, Stale Defenses: The Race for Real‑Time Security (sponsored by Booz Allen)
sessions.a: Cyber conflict has entered a new phase, accelerated by AI that increases the volume, velocity, and sophistication of attacks. The shift is not that attackers are unstoppable — it is that they operate on a faster clock than the systems meant to contain them. Their advantage is freshness: exploiting what changed before defenders reconcile it, exploiting uncertainty before it becomes understanding, and exploiting stale proof before records drift from reality. AI compresses discovery and action, scaling tasks that once required teams. In this session, learn how defense can be rebuilt around real‑time truth, continuous visibility, and inspectable, defensible action. This presentation is brought to you by Booz Allen, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From 1 to 20,000: Scale reliably on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS
sessions.a: As AI workloads scale, infrastructure failures become inevitable, causing stalled jobs, degraded throughput, and wasted accelerator capacity. In this chalk talk, we’ll show how to build resilient AI workloads on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS. We’ll whiteboard the full resiliency stack: Neuron DRA Driver for topology-aware scheduling; UltraServer Operator for provisioning UltraServer workloads; Neuron Observer for sub-second fault detection; and Device Taint for automated recovery. We’ll walk through how these patterns support fault-tolerant distributed training and large-scale inference workloads from a single accelerator to 20,000. You’ll leave with reusable operational patterns for running AI workloads reliably at any scale.

sessions.t: From 1 to 20,000: Scale reliably on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS
sessions.a: As AI workloads scale, infrastructure failures become inevitable, causing stalled jobs, degraded throughput, and wasted accelerator capacity. In this chalk talk, we’ll show how to build resilient AI workloads on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS. We’ll whiteboard the full resiliency stack: Neuron DRA Driver for topology-aware scheduling; UltraServer Operator for provisioning UltraServer workloads; Neuron Observer for sub-second fault detection; and Device Taint for automated recovery. We’ll walk through how these patterns support fault-tolerant distributed training and large-scale inference workloads from a single accelerator to 20,000. You’ll leave with reusable operational patterns for running AI workloads reliably at any scale.

sessions.t: From AI-Assisted Engineering to Autonomous Operations (sponsored by Dynatrace)
sessions.a: As enterprise AI matures, the opportunity extends far beyond software development. Join United Airlines, AWS, and Dynatrace to discover how insights powered by AI, full stack cloud observability, and runtime intelligence are helping engineering and operations teams improve reliability, accelerate delivery, and reduce operational complexity. Learn how leading organizations are using real-time data to automate investigations, predict issues before customer impact, and move toward autonomous operations. The session will cover real-world adoption lessons, AI governance considerations, and practical steps to balance automation with accountability while unlocking greater value from AI across the software lifecycle at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Dynatrace, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From AI proof of concepts to enterprise-grade production systems on Ubuntu (sponsored by Canonical)
sessions.a: AI stacks are complex, interdependent, and high-stakes. Spinning an AI prototype is easy while making it enterprise-ready is much more challenging. Most organizations can’t keep track of their dependencies within their AI projects, leading to solutions that fail security checks and break easily. How do you move to a robust, secure AI solution that is built to last? Learn how to architect, secure, and maintain a resilient enterprise-grade AI infrastructure on Ubuntu, without sacrificing speed. This presentation is brought to you by Canonical, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From AI Skeptic to Enterprise AI Champion with Amazon Quick
sessions.a: You deployed an AI assistant. Your team tried it for a week and stopped. The tool could not access the systems where real work happens, gave generic answers because it was disconnected from your enterprise context, and security would not approve broader rollout because the governance story was unclear. That is where most AI deployments stall. Hear from a customer who lived that exact cycle: low adoption, frustrated leadership, and a growing sense that the investment was wasted. They evaluated multiple alternatives and made the switch to Amazon Quick, an AI assistant with governed access to enterprise data, native connectors to the systems their teams already use, and agentic workflows that span business units. Learn what broke in their first deployment, what they looked for in a replacement, and how governed data access turned single-digit adoption into organization-wide usage.

sessions.t: From AI Tasks to Autonomous Multi-Agent Workflows with Amazon Quick
sessions.a: The workflows that matter most in financial services span multiple systems, require multiple types of expertise, and today rely on people as the coordination layer. One person pulls data, another reviews it for compliance, a third routes it for approval. That coordination tax is where your team's time disappears. Amazon Quick changes that equation. Instead of one AI assistant doing one task, specialized agents each handle their piece and hand off to the next automatically. The human stays in the loop for judgment calls, not for data gathering and routing. Hear from a customer who moved from standalone AI use cases to compound, multi-agent workflows with Amazon Quick. Learn how they identified which workflows to orchestrate first, how they designed agent handoffs that satisfy compliance, and what it means now that the coordination layer runs autonomously.

sessions.t: From AI to Action: Powering Agentic Enterprises with AWS and Infosys (sponsored by Infosys)
sessions.a: As AI evolves from generating insights to driving action, leading organizations are adopting intelligent agents to transform how work gets done. Hear from enterprise leaders as they share their journeys to building agentic businesses with AWS and Infosys, accelerating decision making, improving productivity, and unlocking measurable business value at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Infosys, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From carbon data to action: Optimize AI workloads on AWS
sessions.a: Not all workloads are equal in carbon impact, but how do you know which choices matter most? In this chalk talk, we pull back the curtain on how AWS measures and allocates cloud emissions, balancing scientific rigor with practical usability. Through real-world examples, you'll see how this data reveals meaningful differences across diverse AI workloads. You'll leave with an understanding of the methodology behind your carbon data and how to apply those insights to build AI workloads with a lower environmental footprint, and, often, lower cost.

sessions.t: From chatbot to proactive agent: Connect AI to your nonprofit systems
sessions.a: Agents stall at the demo stage because core enterprise systems — ERPs, legacy databases, and internal APIs — were never built for AI. In this session, we whiteboard two patterns to bridge the gap: request-driven integration via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with access-control interceptors, and event-driven routing via Amazon EventBridge with confidence-based human-in-the-loop fallback. We trace both approaches using a legacy system with no modern API surface — wrapping its interfaces as MCP tools without modifying the original code. The patterns apply whether your blocker is a SOAP endpoint, a stored-procedure layer, or a REST API with no auth story for agents. Leave with a maturity rubric and two practical reference architectures.

sessions.a: Agents stall at the demo stage because core enterprise systems — ERPs, legacy databases, and internal APIs — were never built for AI. Leave with a maturity rubric and two practical reference architectures.

sessions.t: From chips to applications: How Trainium powers the next AI frontier
sessions.a: Every AI breakthrough demands innovation across the full stack — chips, servers, software, and the models built on top — each layer making the next faster, cheaper, and more capable. In this session, discover how AWS and frontier AI builders drive full-stack innovation on AWS Trainium to scale post-training and reinforcement learning, serve at high throughput, and bend the cost-per-token curve. Examine real architectural decisions from silicon to application, then look ahead to what's next in Trainium and AWS infrastructure. Leave with understanding of how each layer of innovation compounds and where to place your bets on AI infrastructure.

sessions.t: From Commit to Secure: Catch Vulnerabilities at Machine Speed with AWS Security Agent
sessions.a: Organizations struggle to detect vulnerabilities before code reaches production. This session demonstrates how to integrate AWS Continuum for code scanning and AWS Continuum for penetration testing (capabilities are delivered through AWS Security Agent) directly into your CI/CD pipeline. Learn how to shift security left, catch vulnerabilities at commit and build stages, surface actionable remediation guidance that prevents vulnerable code from reaching production, and accelerate secure software delivery without slowing developer velocity.

sessions.t: From Confirmed Exploit to AWS WAF Rule in Minutes (sponsored by Terra)
sessions.a: A confirmed pentest finding still needs a code fix reviewed and shipped, and that takes days or weeks while the exploit path stays open. This talk covers Terra Security's Prevention capability. When Terra confirms an exploitable finding, it generates a rule scoped to that exact attack path, stages it inside the customer's existing AWS WAF web ACL, and lets the team validate it against the real exploit before activation. Attendees will leave with the mechanics of the integration and a model for closing the gap between proof and fix in AWS environments. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From Cost Center to Revenue Driver: AI-Powered, Proactive CX
sessions.a: You've cut handle time. You've increased deflection. You've optimized every metric designed to make customer interactions cheaper. And your customers still leave. The metrics you optimized for were built for a world where every interaction was a cost. This session flips the script - stop measuring what you avoided, start measuring what you created, and turn service into a growth lever and not a cost center.

sessions.t: From Cost to Compliance: Scaling Scalable GenAI with Amazon Nova
sessions.a: Enterprises putting generative AI into production face three converging pressures: controlling inference cost at scale, meeting compliance and data-residency requirements, and migrating off incumbent models without losing accuracy or quality. Amazon Nova is purpose-built for this reality. In this session, learn how organizations across regulated and cost-sensitive industries are standardizing on Amazon Nova to run high-volume GenAI workloads at a fraction of the cost while meeting strict compliance requirements.

sessions.t: From CSV to Iceberg: Understanding open data formats on Amazon S3
sessions.a: Building a data lake on Amazon S3 and need to decide between Parquet, Hive, and Iceberg – or understand how your team already did? In this session we develop the mental model for storing structured data on Amazon S3 and trace how it evolved. Understand formats from CSV to Parquet that accelerate analytic queries, walk through the evolution of table and partition schemas that organize data at scale, and learn how open table formats like Apache Iceberg bring database-like capabilities to your data lake. Leave with a clear picture of each and how Amazon S3 Tables bring it all together as a fully managed experience.

sessions.t: From Dashboards to Agents: Building an Agentic NOC (sponsored by Selector AI)
sessions.a: For decades, NOCs have been built around dashboards, alerts, and humans manually stitching together signals from dozens of disconnected tools. That model is breaking under the complexity of modern hybrid networks and sprawling multi-cloud estates. Simply bolting AI onto existing monitoring tools isn't enough to fix it. This talk reimagines the NOC around purpose-built agents built for cloud-scale operations, each progressing through a five-stage maturity model (Observe, Monitor, Triage, Optimize, and Act), that governs how much autonomy each agent earns over time. Attendees will leave with a concrete mental model for evolving their own cloud operations stack from tools that observe to agents that act. This presentation is brought to you by Selector AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From Databases to Agentic AI: Powering Innovation with AMD EPYC on AWS (sponsored by AMD)
sessions.a: Today's organizations need infrastructure that can efficiently support everything from mission-critical databases to next-generation AI applications. Join AMD and AWS to explore how customers are leveraging Amazon EC2 instances powered by AMD EPYC processors across Amazon RDS, analytics, Agentic AI, HPC, and cloud-native applications. Learn how AMD-powered AWS infrastructure delivers compelling price-performance, scalability, and operational efficiency while helping organizations accelerate innovation, optimize costs, and meet growing compute demands. This presentation is brought to you by AMD, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From dataset to a deployed fine-tuned LLM in hours on SageMaker AI
sessions.a: Go from dataset to a custom foundation model in just a few hours, without the need to set up any infrastructure. In this hands-on workshop, you will fine-tune LLMs using Amazon SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization, requiring no infrastructure setup or GPU management. You will walk through the entire workflow — preparing datasets, launching training jobs, registering assets in the SageMaker AI Registry, evaluating using the "LLM-as-a-Judge" technique, and deploying to a real-time endpoint — leveraging Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with LoRA as a memory-efficient optimization method. By the end of the workshop, you will be ready to customize models at scale immediately.

sessions.t: From Demo to Production: The Craft Behind AI Agents at Scale
sessions.a: Your agent reasons, calls tools, and demos beautifully. Then production happens. This session is about the craft that lives after the demo: the unglamorous engineering that separates agents that ship from agents that stay in notebooks. Using real AWS accounts and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, I'll walk through deterministic guardrails that make destructive actions impossible (not just discouraged), spend limits an agent can't prompt-inject its way past, evaluation you can trust, and the IAM that silently breaks first. You'll leave with a production-readiness framework for agentic systems—and honest stories about everything that failed on the way there.

sessions.t: From Design to Deployment: Embedding Security into Every Phase of the SDLC
sessions.a: AWS Continuum embeds security expertise at every stage of the software development lifecycle: AWS Continuum for threat modeling for architecture documents, AWS Continuum for code scanning for pull requests and full repositories, and AWS Continuum for penetration testing for deployed applications. In this chalk talk, we dive deep into how AWS Continuum coordinates multiple analysis passes with built-in safety guardrails and multi-step validation to deliver high-confidence findings. Bring your questions about integrating security into CI/CD pipelines and scaling AppSec across multiple teams.

sessions.t: From dial tone to AI agent: Build a community portal in 60 min
sessions.a: City governments face rising citizen expectations with shrinking staff. In this builders' session, learn how to deploy a fully functional AI-powered community engagement portal using Amazon Connect agentic voice in under one hour. See how to build a voice agent that answers common citizen inquiries about permits, utilities, parks, and city services, routes callers to the right department, and seamlessly escalates to live agents with full conversation context when needed. Walk away with a production-ready reference architecture that operations team can configure, deploy, and manage independently.

sessions.t: From discoverable to buyable: Commerce stacks for agent-driven shoppers (sponsored by Stripe)
sessions.a: Join Stripe on how AI is changing how shoppers find and buy products—and what it means for your commerce stack. With 20% of holiday ecommerce traffic projected from AI agents, this session is designed for retail leaders moving from "exploring" to "ready." Converting this traffic requires a different approach to catalog readiness, checkout, fraud, and fulfillment. Attendees will leave with clear priorities to act on today and carry into 2027. This presentation is brought to you by Stripe, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From DNA to discovery: Build a genomics HPC pipeline on AWS
sessions.a: Build and run a real genomics variant-calling Slurm pipeline on AWS PCS using a mixed Graviton + GPU fleet. Cover PCS queue design, Slurm partition strategy, FSx for Lustre, EFA networking, and result aggregation to S3. Walk away with a reproducible, production-grade HPC workflow for life-sciences workloads.

sessions.t: From Event Streams to Enterprise AI with Cloudera Anywhere Cloud (sponsored by Cloudera)
sessions.a: Distributed edge assets, remote sensors, and transactional systems often leave operational data isolated from enterprise AI platforms. This session demonstrates how global organizations break down these operational boundaries using Cloudera Anywhere Cloud. Discover an event-driven architectural blueprint that standardizes real-time streaming, unifies hybrid pipelines, and routes live activity directly into downstream analytics and AI agents. Learn how a single operational standard across hybrid environments simplifies data sovereignty and enables real-time enterprise automation. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From First Prompt to Production: Running AWS's AI-DLC at Trillion-Token Scale (sponsored by Anaconda)
sessions.a: Bring AWS's AI-DLC methodology together with open source agents, Amazon Bedrock inference, and a governed Python foundation. Watch a full bolt run live — business intent to deployed AWS workload — with model choice, dependency provenance, and cost attribution intact. AI-native development the enterprise can actually put into production. This presentation is brought to you by Anaconda, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From First Workload to the Autonomous Enterprise: Transform and Scale with SAP on AWS (sponsored by SAP)
sessions.a: Agentic AI is making ERP modernization more urgent than ever. To coordinate decisions across the organization enterprise, AI must be grounded in a modern cloud ERP foundation—one that connects data, processes, business rules, and controls. ERP is no longer just where work is recorded. It has become the operational foundation that enables enterprise agentic AI and ultimately the Autonomous Enterprise.​ SAP and AWS are partnering to help clients accelerate their AI vision Autonomous Enterprise where people set direction, AI executes operational tasks, and organizations respond faster to change leveraging a single intelligent system with full business context. Join us to explore how SAP on AWS helps moves organizations of all sizes to move beyond isolated AI pilots to enterprise-wide outcomes delivered with reliability and confidence.​ This presentation is brought to you by SAP, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From Fragmented Infra to Golden Path: An Internal Developer Platform on EKS
sessions.a: Every team wanted to ship faster, but each was reinventing the same wheels: clusters, pipelines, infrastructure, access. So we built an internal developer platform on Amazon EKS — one golden path that lets product teams go from idea to running service without becoming Kubernetes experts. This is the honest story of that journey. We'll show how we used EKS as the foundation, Crossplane to provision cloud infrastructure through Kubernetes APIs, and Argo CD to drive everything through GitOps. We'll walk through the challenges that nearly derailed us and share what actually moved the needle. You'll leave with a realistic map of the terrain: what worked, what hurt, and what we'd do differently.

sessions.t: From Gen AI to Agentic AI: Transforming Finance Operations on AWS with Barclays (sponsored by Capgemini)
sessions.a: Barclays is transforming finance operations through an AWS-powered AI platform that combines Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector knowledge bases, and Agentic AI. The platform unifies structured and unstructured finance data to automate SOX controls, enhance management reporting, enable finance data enrichment, and support intelligent decision-making across strategic finance initiatives. Built with enterprise-grade governance, explainability, and auditability, the solution helps strengthen control effectiveness, improve regulatory compliance, and accelerate reporting outcomes. Learn how AI-powered agents, explainable workflows, and governed human-in-the-loop processes are driving operational efficiency, enhancing regulatory confidence, improving audit readiness, and laying the foundation for autonomous finance operations. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From hardware to application: new EC2 monitoring capabilities
sessions.a: This chalk talk covers EC2 health monitoring across hardware, instance, and application layers, including new functionality like EC2 Application Status Checks. Application Status Checks enable you to detect application health impairments by monitoring your applications via configurable paths and ports for HTTP/S. You will learn how to use EC2 health signals to build operational automation for your workloads and integrate these signals with Auto Scaling Groups and Kubernetes.

sessions.t: From hardware to application: new EC2 monitoring capabilities
sessions.a: This chalk talk covers EC2 health monitoring across hardware, instance, and application layers, including new functionality like EC2 Application Status Checks. Application Status Checks enable you to detect application health impairments by monitoring your applications via configurable paths and ports for HTTP/S. You will learn how to use EC2 health signals to build operational automation for your workloads and integrate these signals with Auto Scaling Groups and Kubernetes.

sessions.t: From Hours to Minutes: Fast Android Builds and Virtual Testing on AWS
sessions.a: Automotive software teams lose hours to a slow development cycle: Android builds run for hours, and testing means waiting on scarce physical target hardware. This chalk talk shows how to compress that cycle on AWS. SourceFS cuts Android build times from ~3 hours to under 5 minutes, and the Virtual Engineering Workbench (VEW) lets engineers test against virtual targets in the cloud instead of queuing for physical boards. We'll build up the reference architecture live, show where each piece fits, and walk through the adoption path customers are on today.

sessions.t: From Hours to Minutes: Fast Android Builds and Virtual Testing on AWS
sessions.a: Automotive software teams lose hours to a slow development cycle: Android builds run for hours, and testing means waiting on scarce physical target hardware. This chalk talk shows how to compress that cycle on AWS. SourceFS cuts Android build times from ~3 hours to under 5 minutes, and the Virtual Engineering Workbench (VEW) lets engineers test against virtual targets in the cloud instead of queuing for physical boards. We'll build up the reference architecture live, show where each piece fits, and walk through the adoption path customers are on today.

sessions.t: From Humans to Agents: Rethinking Identity for Your Next Wave of Growth (sponsored by Okta)
sessions.a: Software is replacing humans as the primary application interface, turning identity into the core control plane for the emerging agent economy. Existing systems, built for human users, fail to support autonomous agents acting at scale. This session outlines a modern identity model that unifies humans, machines, APIs, and AI agents into a single, extensible layer. Learn how to turn identity from an operational requirement into a secure competitive advantage, scaling your business safely from your first user to full agent fleets. This presentation is brought to you by Okta, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From Intention to Production: Loop Engineering with the FDE Kit
sessions.a: The AWS FDE Delivery Kit replaces linear agent pipelines with delivery loops: each program's output enriches shared state and feeds the next. Live-coding: from plain-English intention to production CDK infrastructure, Bedrock agents with guardrails, and AgentCore via re-resolve cycles.

sessions.t: From Intention to Production: Loop Engineering with the FDE Kit
sessions.a: The AWS FDE Delivery Kit replaces linear agent pipelines with delivery loops: each program's output enriches shared state and feeds the next. Live-coding: from plain-English intention to production CDK infrastructure, Bedrock agents with guardrails, and AgentCore via re-resolve cycles.

sessions.t: From Intent to Interconnection: Building Multicloud Networks in Minutes (sponsored by Equinix)
sessions.a: Modern enterprises span clouds, AI providers, private infrastructure, partners, and sovereign environments, yet networking is still built one connection at a time. Equinix Fabric One introduces a new approach: declare the business outcome you need and let the platform automatically compose the secure, resilient, any-to-any network required to deliver it. In this live demo, see how Fabric One transforms multicloud networking into an intent-driven experience. Watch a simple declaration trigger automated routing, cloud peering, encryption, resiliency, and failover across multiple providers and destinations. See how Equinix enables organizations to move from “choose, design, configure, operate” to “declare, compose, deliver.” This presentation is brought to you by Equinix, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From Legacy to Agentic: Modernization Beyond the Code (sponsored by SoftServe)
sessions.a: What if modernization started beyond the code? SoftServe is reimagining application modernization by working backwards from business needs and desired outcomes to determine what should change and why. In this session, see how SoftServe Agentic Application Modernization combines this outcome-driven approach with CAST Software, AWS Transform, Kiro, AI-DLC and specialized AI agents to accelerate discovery, assessment, transformation, and validation. Learn how SoftServe provides the AI foundation to orchestrate and govern these agents, turning modernization into an intelligent, repeatable journey that enables AI for organizations, connects business intent with technology decisions and execution on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by SoftServe, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From Manual to Autonomous: AI-Driven AWS Partner Ops with Quick & MCP
sessions.a: 38% of partners cite SA access as their #1 GenAI need; 42% cite technical complexity as the implementation barrier. Expertise locked in SMEs doesn't scale, the answer is architectural. This session shows how Amazon Quick, the Partner Central MCP Server, and Marketplace AI Listing Experience automate end-to-end partner operations — co-sell, technical validation, MP listings optimized via SEO/GEO, Express Private Offers, and demand generation. We cover MCP protocol integration, agent orchestration across Partner Central and Marketplace, cross-system auth, and extensibility patterns. Leave ready to build your own MCP-based workflows automating specialist-knowledge access and pipeline at scale.

sessions.t: From MCP poisoning to defense: securing the agent tool supply chain
sessions.a: MCP is becoming the standard for connecting AI agents to tools, but MCP servers are packages that present supply chain risk. In this builders session, you will observe a live MCP tool poisoning attack, then build three defense layers hands-on: gateway validation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy to restrict tool actions, a pre-deployment integrity scanner that detects silent tool definition changes, and runtime monitoring that flags anomalous tool behavior. Leave with a working understanding of how MCP supply chain attacks work and how to defend against them.

sessions.t: From migration to continuous modernization: reduce tech debt at scale
sessions.a: Learn how agentic AI is transforming enterprise modernization from one-off projects into an always-on practice. In this session, we explore how organizations are accelerating cloud migration, modernizing mainframe, Windows, and custom applications, and continuously reducing tech debt across their entire portfolio, evolving their pipelines from CI/CD to CI/CD/CM (continuous modernization). See how teams are compressing modernization timelines from years to months while keeping codebases current and AI-ready. Hear from product leader Neha Goswami on the latest innovations and what's ahead.

sessions.t: From Millions of Gamers to AI at Scale: Roblox's Hybrid AWS Architecture Unleashed
sessions.a: "Auto-scaling was only the beginning. At Roblox, scaling means continuously adapting to changing capacity, hardware availability, GPU constraints, and unpredictable global demand. Join Roblox to learn how they combine AWS with on-premises infrastructure to dynamically place workloads across regions, architectures, and AI providers. Using EC2 Capacity Health Visualizer, hybrid scheduling, multi-region load balancing, self-hosted AI inference alongside Amazon Bedrock, and heterogeneous compute (x86, Graviton, Inferentia, Trainium, GPUs), you will learn how Roblox keeps gaming and AI services responsive under record-breaking load."

sessions.t: From On-Premises to Agentic AI: Bayer's Amazon Connect Transformation Journey (sponsored by Capgemini)
sessions.a: Capgemini transformed 414 contact center hotlines across more than 68 countries by replacing Cisco UCCE with Amazon Connect and introducing AgentX, an AWS-native agentic AI platform deployed across the Bayer enterprise. Built on Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Connect, Amazon Lex, AWS Lambda, and other AWS services, AgentX delivers real-time agent assistance, automated call summarization, governance controls, predictive analytics, and autonomous workflow execution. Learn how Bayer established a "build once, deploy globally" operating model that enables consistent AI innovation across business units while reducing operational complexity, improving agent productivity, and delivering significant cost savings. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From our Agents to yours: Build, Optimize and Certify
sessions.a: AWS builds its certification exams, from foundational cloud to agentic AI, using production AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. In this session, we show how we built our reasoning agents with AWS Well-Architected practices to solve real operational challenges: climbing latency, spiraling token costs, and non-deterministic failures. You’ll leave with concrete patterns to apply on AWS, plus a clear path to validate those skills through AWS Certification

sessions.t: From Pilot to Enterprise Scale with Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Your AI pilot proved value with a small team. Now you need to deploy across the organization without a dedicated rollout team and without losing what made it work. Hear from a customer who scaled Amazon Quick from an initial deployment to thousands of users across their enterprise. Learn the phased strategy they used to expand Quick's capabilities: connecting teams to enterprise data, automating repetitive workflows, and rolling out agentic features that kept usage growing after the initial adoption wave. Discover what metrics justified continued investment and the operational model they built so scaling Quick did not create a support burden for IT. Walk away with a repeatable framework for taking Amazon Quick from proof-of-concept to production deployment across your organization.

sessions.t: From Pilot to Production in weeks with the Agentic CX Designer
sessions.a: Most conversational AI initiatives never reach production, stuck in months of custom integration work and developer hand offs. Amazon Connect Customer's agentic CX designer changes that. Learn how a no-code visual canvas lets CX business teams blend deterministic steps like identity verification, payments, and compliance disclosures with agentic AI that reasons and acts, all in one governed flow. Go from concept to live in weeks, not months, with built-in governance at no additional cost. Walk away with a practical approach to closing the production gap.

sessions.t: From pod to multi-region: Resilient workloads on Amazon EKS
sessions.a: Building resilient workloads on Amazon EKS requires thinking in layers, from pod-level reliability to multi-region failover. In this chalk talk, explore each layer: Pod Disruption Budgets and Topology Spread Constraints, Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode for fast node recovery, EFS vs EBS for stateful workloads, AWS Backup for cross-region protection, and Route 53 with ARC for region switching. Debate active-active vs active-passive tradeoffs and validate RTO/RPO targets with Resilience Hub.

sessions.t: From pod to multi-region: Resilient workloads on Amazon EKS
sessions.a: Building resilient workloads on Amazon EKS requires thinking in layers, from pod-level reliability to multi-region failover. In this chalk talk, explore each layer: Pod Disruption Budgets and Topology Spread Constraints, Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode for fast node recovery, EFS vs EBS for stateful workloads, AWS Backup for cross-region protection, and Route 53 with ARC for region switching. Debate active-active vs active-passive tradeoffs and validate RTO/RPO targets with Resilience Hub.

sessions.t: From prompts to loops: inference best practices for agents
sessions.a: Every layer of an agent, from context and harness to planning loops, places additional demand on the inference engine. Each model turn created by planning, tool use, retrieval, reflection, or retry shapes cost, latency, and reliability. This chalk talk traces that evolution on Amazon Bedrock and shows the inference impact of each layer, with best practices to get them right: versioning prompts, grounding context, engineering a reliable harness, setting verifiable goal conditions, and designing loops that know when to stop. Leave knowing how each layer shapes cost, latency, and reliability.

sessions.t: From prompts to loops: inference best practices for agents

sessions.t: From prompt to pipeline: Agentic data engineering
sessions.a: Data engineers spend weeks building pipelines describable in a single sentence. AI agents change this by autonomously discovering data, building transformations, and orchestrating workflows via natural language. Explore how the Model Context Protocol (MCP) gives agents standardized access to AWS analytics services. See a live demo of an agent composing across AWS Glue, Amazon Redshift, and MWAA Serverless to build a pipeline from a single prompt. Leave with patterns and tools to start building.

sessions.t: From Proofs to Production: Neurosymbolic AI and Provable Security
sessions.a: AWS has spent a decade proving the correctness of critical infrastructure, from IAM policy evaluation to cryptographic implementations and network isolation. This session traces the evolution from early automated reasoning tools to today's neurosymbolic AI, where formal verification and large language models converge. We examine how mathematical proof engines like Lean, combined with reinforcement learning and agentic workflows, enable provable security guarantees at scale. Attendees will learn how specification-driven development, whole-service data flow analysis, and Bedrock Guardrails' automated reasoning checks are moving the industry beyond "test and hope" toward mathematically verified trust.

sessions.t: From raw data to custom model: Dataset prep with Amazon SageMaker AI
sessions.a: Great models start with great data. In this hands-on workshop, use SageMaker AI Agent skills to profile, curate, and validate datasets for the full model customization lifecycle — no infrastructure to manage. Assess data completeness and distribution, apply auto-labeling at scale, run human-in-the-loop review for edge cases, and fix quality issues like deduplication and toxicity filtering. Generate synthetic data to fill coverage gaps, then prepare datasets for Supervised Fine-Tuning, Direct Preference Optimization, Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, and RLAIF. Launch training, evaluate with LLM-as-a-Judge, and deploy. Walk away ready to go from raw data to custom model in hours.

sessions.t: From raw data to custom model: Dataset prep with Amazon SageMaker AI
sessions.a: Great models start with great data. In this hands-on workshop, use SageMaker AI Agent skills to profile, curate, and validate datasets for the full model customization lifecycle — no infrastructure to manage. Assess data completeness and distribution, apply auto-labeling at scale, run human-in-the-loop review for edge cases, and fix quality issues like deduplication and toxicity filtering. Launch training, evaluate with LLM-as-a-Judge, and deploy. Walk away ready to go from raw data to custom model in hours.

sessions.t: From Reactive to Proactive: Omnichannel AI Outreach with Connect Customer
sessions.a: Every organization is building AI agents for inbound, but who's automating outreach? In this workshop, you become a carrier responding to a device safety recall. Instead of posting a notice and waiting for calls, you build a system that identifies affected customers, prioritizes them by risk and value, and deploys an AI agent to reach them by voice before they ever pick up the phone. Walk away with a working proactive outreach engine and the architecture to deploy anticipatory engagement at scale.

sessions.t: From Reactive to Proactive: Omnichannel AI Outreach with Connect Customer
sessions.a: Every organization is building AI agents for inbound, but who's automating outreach? In this workshop, you become a carrier responding to a device safety recall. Instead of posting a notice and waiting for calls, you build a system that identifies affected customers, prioritizes them by risk and value, and deploys an AI agent to reach them by voice before they ever pick up the phone. Walk away with a working proactive outreach engine and the architecture to deploy anticipatory engagement at scale.

sessions.t: From repeated remediation to permanent prevention at scale
sessions.a: You remediate a finding today and detect the same class of finding next week. This chalk talk explains how to break that cycle. You take a real AWS Security Hub finding category and explore all four control layers. An SCP that prevents the misconfiguration, a Guard rule that catches it before deployment, an AWS Config rule that detects existing violations, and AI-generated auto-remediation that corrects drift. You leave with a repeatable framework that turns every remediation into permanent prevention at scale

sessions.t: From rules to reasoning: Build an intelligent tagging compliance agent with AgentCore
sessions.a: AWS Config rules detect missing tags, but what about resources where the correct tag value isn't obvious? In this builder session, you'll create an AI agent using AgentCore that goes beyond detection to intelligent remediation. Your agent analyzes resource context, account ownership, VPC placement, creator identity, naming patterns to infer correct tag values, and handles ambiguous cases by requesting human input. Start where Config rules end: not just "is it tagged?" but "what should the tag be?"

sessions.t: From SAP to Agentic AI: Building a unified data strategy on AWS
sessions.a: This chalk talk presents a unified architecture spanning SAP Business Data Cloud, Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS-native services. Learn how AWS enables progressive modernization from zero-copy federation via BDC Connect, to Iceberg-based lakehouse architectures, to AI-powered analytics with Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, and QuickSight. We introduce the AWS for SAP MCP Server, accessing OData services as AI-ready tools via Model Context Protocol. Live demos showcase AI agents resolving supply chain exceptions, generating Customer 360 insights, and accelerating BW modernization.

sessions.t: From self-managed to AWS managed: agentic AI for Kafka and MQ migrations
sessions.a: Migrating self-managed Apache Kafka and RabbitMQ to Amazon MSK and Amazon MQ is hard. Topic mapping, offset translation, ACL migration, and the notoriously long cutover phase slow teams down for weeks. In this chalk talk, we walk through these challenges and show how agentic AI paired with AWS replication tooling compresses the longest migration phase from days to minutes. Watch a complete live migration executed end-to-end in under 60 minutes and leave with a repeatable playbook for your own migration.

sessions.t: From shopping agents to shoppers: Amazon CloudFront patterns for peak retail
sessions.a: Peak retail traffic is no longer just more shoppers - AI shopping agents, scrapers, and personalized experiences now collide on the same edge. In this session, learn advanced Amazon CloudFront patterns to handle all three. See how to classify and verify agentic traffic using CloudFront Functions, Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore, and AWS WAF Bot Control, then serve tiered responses without touching origin. Hear how you can serve AI-powered personalization on every page in about a millisecond by encoding decision-tree models in KeyValueStore, fed by an Amazon Bedrock pipeline. Leave with battle-tested patterns for your next cyber week.

sessions.t: From Signals to Action for Sempra: AI-Powered Cybersecurity on AWS (sponsored by Accenture)
sessions.a: AI is reshaping cybersecurity, but security teams must act faster without adding complexity. Sempra Energy, AWS, and Accenture deployed Accenture Cyber.AI on AWS to create a unified view of cyber risk and identify the highest-priority actions across the enterprise. Learn how the team integrated existing security investments, addressed governance and architecture requirements, and operationalized AI-driven risk management. Speakers will share key design decisions, implementation lessons, and practical guidance for using AI to improve cyber resilience, strengthen security operations, and maintain control of data and infrastructure in cloud environments. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From static to dynamic - modernizing bidirectional federation
sessions.a: Static credentials remain the most common source of identity-related security incidents, yet many workloads still rely on them across trust boundaries. AWS now eliminates them in both directions. Humans and workloads outside AWS can use OIDC, SAML, or X.509 certificates to federate in and obtain temporary AWS credentials. Conversely, IAM outbound identity federation lets AWS workloads exchange IAM identities for short-lived JWTs when calling external clouds like Azure and Google Cloud, AI providers like OpenAI or Anthropic, SaaS platforms like Databricks and Snowflake, and your own applications. This session covers how to configure trust, scope credentials, and enforce authorization controls.

sessions.t: From static to self-improving agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.a: AI agents that learn from every production cycle deliver better outcomes without retraining or manual prompt tuning. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations scores live agent behavior across multiple quality dimensions and how the optimization capability discovers better system prompts and tool configurations from production traces. Learn how the agent improves continuously from production results, expert corrections, and revised context your team contributes. We'll demonstrate the full observe-evaluate-improve cycle with an underwriting agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents Framework, then discuss how the pattern applies to claims, fraud, and customer service agents.

sessions.t: From static to self-improving agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.a: AI agents that learn from every production cycle deliver better outcomes without retraining or manual prompt tuning. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations scores live agent behavior across multiple quality dimensions and how the optimization capability discovers better system prompts and tool configurations from production traces. Learn how the agent improves continuously from production results, expert corrections, and revised context your team contributes. sessions.t: From system thinking to outcome thinking: The AI-native architect
sessions.a: The architect role is changing faster than at any point since the cloud itself emerged. AI is reshaping not just what architects build, but how they think, where they spend their time, and what organizations expect. We share observations from leading a global transformation of thousands of AWS Solutions Architects into AI-native practitioners: what shifted in daily practice, what surprised us, and what broke. We explore how outcome-oriented thinking replaces system-oriented thinking, and why the line between building and advising is dissolving. You leave with a practical mental model for how the architecture role delivers value in an AI-native world.

sessions.t: From Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering At Scale
sessions.a: Most developers use AI coding assistants as interactive tools and see modest gains. A small cohort works differently: they treat agents as autonomous workers they direct and validate, and the results are a step function in productivity improvements, not an increment. In this session, we break down what these power users do differently, share success stories, where experts still find friction, and the bottlenecks coming next. We'll share demos so you leave with concrete, repeatable practices for getting orders-of-magnitude more out of Kiro agents.

sessions.t: From vulnerability to exploit to fix: detect and respond in real time
sessions.a: In this builder session, you start with a deployed web application containing known OWASP vulnerabilities and race to find and fix them before attackers do. Using AWS Security Agent, you review application designs, reproduce vulnerabilities, and push fixes through a CI/CD pipeline. Simultaneously, Amazon GuardDuty detects active exploitation attempts targeting those same weaknesses — and you respond in real time by isolating compromised resources and hardening configurations. Experience the full closed-loop workflow: Inspector identifies the vulnerability, GuardDuty catches the exploit, and Security Agent generates the remediation.

sessions.t: From Workloads to Agents: Rethinking Cloud Resilience (sponsored by Cohesity)
sessions.a: Under the shared responsibility model, you own the security and recoverability of your entire cloud estate - and that estate now includes AI agents. These agents are becoming core infrastructure, executing actions across interconnected systems at machine speed. Yet most organizations can't recover agent memory, credentials, or configurations any better than they could recover a corrupted server a decade ago. Join us to see how Cohesity's resilience platform extends AWS-native protections to agents and infrastructure alike, so risk doesn't outrun your ability to recover. This presentation is brought to you by Cohesity, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: From your first Amazon EKS cluster to a self-serve developer platform
sessions.a: The best Kubernetes platforms are invisible to the people who use them. Developers provision, deploy, and scale through self-service interfaces without needing Kubernetes expertise, while platform teams reclaim the cycles once spent on cluster operations and lifecycle management. That is the standard now that Amazon EKS is engineered to deliver. Come hear how EKS sees developer experience evolving: Auto Mode removing undifferentiated operational load through managed compute, scaling, and add-ons; EKS Capabilities exposing AWS services as governed, self-serve building blocks; and AI agents taking on operational workflows (upgrades, diagnostics, remediation) that platform teams have owned for years.

sessions.t: From Zero to 20,000 Desktops: Getting Started with Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Your team is drowning in context-switching: toggling between email, documents, data tools, and chat just to complete a single task. Productivity tools promise to help, but most add complexity instead of removing it. In this fireside chat, hear from customers who faced that exact challenge and deployed an AI work companion across 20,000+ users in under 90 days. Learn what convinced their leadership to invest, how they integrated AI into daily workflows without disrupting existing tools, and what the first 90 days of adoption actually looked like. Walk away with a practical roadmap for bringing Amazon Quick AI assistant to your workforce at scale.

sessions.t: From zero to HPC: Build production clusters with AWS PCS
sessions.a: Master AWS Parallel Computing Service at re:Invent. Build fully managed compute environments with zero setup. This hands-on session covers job submission, resource optimization, and intuitive interfaces to accelerate workflows for researchers and engineers. Scale faster without the complexity.

sessions.t: Fuel Intelligent AI Agents with Trusted Enterprise Context (sponsored by Salesforce)
sessions.a: To unlock transformative business outcomes, AI agents require a foundation of trusted data with rich enterprise context. Delivering success means bridging the knowledge, trust, and action gaps across a highly complex data landscape. In this session, learn how Informatica Intelligent Data Management Cloud (IDMC) provides the comprehensive context envelope needed to power reliable AI workflows. Explore how headless IDMC architecture via integrations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Agent Registry and Amazon Quick fuels agents with trusted enterprise context and end-to-end governance, driving impactful results and long-term project success This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Full-stack data agents using Box MCP and AWS
sessions.a: Organizations struggle to assess contract compliance as terms live in unstructured documents while structured financial and risk data sit in operational databases across the enterprise. In this session, build an AI agent that performs real-time contract compliance analysis, bridging unstructured content stored in Box with operational structured data on AWS. Using Box MCP in AWS Marketplace, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon Aurora, you implement a multi-MCP architecture, routing to Box for contract extraction and to AWS databases for operational data, producing auditable compliance determinations citing both unstructured content and structured data. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Full stack development on AWS: bring your questions
sessions.a: Building modern web and mobile front ends means juggling a lot of moving parts, and everyone's stack looks a little different. This chalk talk is an open Q&A, so bring your real questions and challenges. We'll talk through how AWS Amplify helps you define backends in code and ship full-stack apps fast, how AWS AppSync powers real-time and offline data with managed GraphQL and WebSocket APIs, and how AWS Device Farm lets you test across real browsers and mobile devices before your users do. Whether you're starting a greenfield app or scaling an existing one, come ready to steer the conversation.

sessions.t: Fundamentals to scale Kubernetes across your organization
sessions.a: Ready to get hands-on with Amazon EKS? This modular workshop begins with Kubernetes fundamentals and lets you choose topics that match your interests including generative AI, observability, networking, security, and more. You can learn how to optimize scaling with Karpenter, automate day-to-day operations with EKS Auto Mode, troubleshoot real-world issues, and extend clusters on-premises with EKS Hybrid Nodes. Get hands-on building resilient, production-grade clusters on Amazon EKS following industry best practices and explore the latest Amazon EKS features, choosing only the modules that matter most to you.

sessions.t: Fundamentals to scale Kubernetes across your organization
sessions.a: Ready to get hands-on with Amazon EKS? This modular workshop begins with Kubernetes fundamentals and lets you choose topics that match your interests including generative AI, observability, networking, security, and more. You can learn how to optimize scaling with Karpenter, automate day-to-day operations with EKS Auto Mode, troubleshoot real-world issues, and extend clusters on-premises with EKS Hybrid Nodes. Get hands-on building resilient, production-grade clusters on Amazon EKS following industry best practices and explore the latest Amazon EKS features, choosing only the modules that matter most to you.

sessions.t: Future-Proof Your Customer Service with Salesforce, Slack and AWS (sponsored by Salesforce)
sessions.a: Modern service demands always-on, personalized experiences. See how Agentforce Service and Slack partner with Amazon Connect Customer, so you can cut handle times, costs & boost CSAT. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Gaining insights with S3 Metadata and annotations
sessions.a: Learn how S3 annotations let you attach rich, structured context (JSON, XML, YAML, or plain text) directly to your objects without re-uploading them. In this session, you will configure annotations on a live dataset, build an enrichment pipeline that attaches AI-generated summaries on ingest, query annotation payloads at scale through S3 Metadata's Apache Iceberg table in Athena, and wire an AI agent that discovers and retrieves objects using annotation-based search. You leave with patterns for zero-read agentic discovery and metadata architectures that scale to billions of objects.

sessions.t: Gatekeepers & guardrails: Secure AI agents across your nonprofit stack
sessions.a: AI agents that reach across your tools via MCP are a force multiplier — but letting an agent call OAuth-protected APIs means handling credentials, identity, and blast radius. Get it wrong and you expose sensitive data. In this code talk, deploy an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and walk through three-legged OAuth live: secure token storage via AgentCore Identity, identity propagation across agent chains, confused-deputy prevention, and guardrails on tool results. Whether you're a 5-person nonprofit team or a 5,000-person enterprise, leave with deployable IaC for your own environment.

sessions.t: Gemini gets closer to traders with AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
sessions.a: Gemini, a NASDAQ-listed crypto exchange, serves trading clients with diverse latency needs. For the most latency-sensitive workloads, AWS Outposts at Gemini's NY5 facility runs matching-engine-adjacent with sub-millisecond connectivity via cross-connects. For cloud-native traders, AWS Local Zones in NYC deliver sub-2ms latency through VPC Peering: bringing compute into the New York area cut round-trip latency roughly 80%, with provisioning in minutes rather than months. For customers prioritizing simplicity, the Region offers a fully managed API, including agentic trading systems connecting via MCP. Hear how Gemini's tiered model turns compute placement into a competitive lever you can apply to your own location-sensitive workloads.

sessions.t: Gemini gets closer to traders with AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
sessions.a: Gemini, a NASDAQ-listed crypto exchange, serves trading clients with diverse latency and infrastructure needs. Using AWS Outposts at its NY5 colocation facility, Gemini provides sub-millisecond connectivity via cross-connects. With AWS Local Zones in NYC, cloud-native traders achieve sub-2ms latency through VPC Peering—an 80% improvement—with provisioning in minutes instead of months. The AWS Region offers a fully managed API for customers prioritizing simplicity, including agentic trading systems connecting via MCP. Hear how Gemini architected a tiered connectivity model that meets customers where they are, from HFT firms to AI-driven agents to university traders onboarded in days.

sessions.t: GenAI chip selection: From training to inference
sessions.a: Every GenAI workload hits the same question: GPU, Trainium, Graviton, or Inferentia—and when do you use each? In this chalk talk, we walk through a practical decision tree covering model training, real-time inference, and agentic AI workloads. We then go deep on inference cost optimization: right-sizing GPU instances, offloading pre/post-processing to Graviton, using Spot for batch inference, prompt caching, and moving production inference to Inferentia2. Expect opinionated guidance, real customer math from teams that cut inference costs without sacrificing latency, and a whiteboard framework you can take back to your team on Monday.

sessions.t: Get started on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: New to Bedrock, or considering it for your next workload? In this hands-on workshop you go from your first API call to a working application in a single sitting. You choose a model, ground it with Managed Knowledge Bases and websearch, apply Guardrails, pick a service tier, then deploy and monitor what you built. Along the way you learn the core building blocks and how they fit together. You leave with an application you built yourself and a repeatable path your team can follow to build the next one.

sessions.t: Getting Started with AgentCore: ship an agent to production in 3 hours
sessions.a: You can build an agent in an afternoon. Getting it to production takes months. Not because the AI is hard, but because the infrastructure around it is: memory, tool access, identity, policy, observability, evaluation. This workshop closes that gap in three hours. Build a customer support agent from scratch and progressively add each production capability using the AgentCore CLI: runtime, memory, gateway, identity, policy, observability, and evaluation. AgentCore is framework and model agnostic, so everything applies whether you use LangGraph, CrewAI, Strands, or your own stack. Leave ready to ship.

sessions.t: Getting Started with Amazon Quick: How a Customer Went from Curious to Deployed
sessions.a: Your team spends hours on work that should take minutes: summarizing meetings, drafting documents, finding answers buried across systems, pulling data from multiple platforms. You know AI should help, but you need to see it work in a real environment before you commit. In this session, see how a customer put Amazon Quick into daily workflows across their organization and watch live as it composes documents, analyzes data, summarizes conversations, and connects to enterprise systems. Hear what problems they were solving, what changed for their teams after deployment, and what surprised them about adoption. Leave with a clear picture of the problems Quick solves and how to evaluate whether it fits your organization.

sessions.t: Getting Started with Apache Iceberg: The AI-Ready open lakehouse advantage
sessions.a: In the agentic AI era, the same modern lakehouse is also your AI-ready foundation: the quality, openness, and organization of your data is what separates successful AI outcomes. Apache Iceberg on Amazon S3 Tables gives you that true portability and engine interoperability to build your AI-ready data foundation. Welcome to this hands-on workshop, where you will build an open lakehouse on AWS to serve analysts and agents both, while tackling real-world data challenges including a medallion architecture, table maintenance, change data capture and GDPR compliance.

sessions.t: Getting the capacity you need: EC2 Launch APIs and Intelligent Auto Scaling deep dive
sessions.a: Getting the right compute at the right time is a two-part challenge: launching instances effectively and scaling them intelligently. This deep dive covers both. First, we explore RunInstances—EC2's oldest and most important API—sharing launch best practices, how flexibility helps you get the capacity you need, and how EC2 Fleet incorporates advanced strategies into your calls. Then we go under the hood of EC2 Auto Scaling, and the intelligence that also scales DynamoDB, WorkSpaces, EMR, SageMaker AI, and Aurora. Learn how to use target tracking, predictive scaling, and auto-tuning to automatically and intelligently scale your workloads.

sessions.t: Ghost agents: Governing ephemeral AI & machine access in real-time (sponsored by SailPoint)
sessions.a: Ephemeral AI agents and cloud workloads spin up, access resources, and vanish in minutes, never landing in traditional identity registries. How do you govern what you can’t track? The answer lies in securing the non-human identities (NHIs) they leave behind. Join SailPoint for a live demo on governing ephemeral agent behavior. We’ll show you how to untangle NHI ownership, expose over-privileged access, and establish real-time governance over transient machine identities before they expose your cloud. Walk away with a blueprint to manage non-human access risk at cloud scale. This is clarity you can act on. This presentation is brought to you by SailPoint, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Give AI Agents Business Context with Genie One and Genie Ontology (sponsored by Databricks)
sessions.a: Connecting an AI agent to enterprise data is easy. Getting it to understand which tables, metrics, definitions and sources to trust is much harder. In this session, learn how Genie Ontology on Databricks combines governed semantics with context automatically learned from queries, dashboards, notebooks and connected systems, then ranks that knowledge by relevance and authority while enforcing user permissions. See how Genie One uses this shared context to reason over live structured and unstructured data, call tools through MCP, take action and deliver more accurate results with less costly agentic exploration on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Databricks, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Give your AI agent an expert-level playbook with the Agent Toolkit for AWS
sessions.a: What if your AI agent could explore schemas, generate correct SQL, load data, and run migrations — all through the Agent Toolkit for AWS with expert-level context? In this chalk talk, we explore how the AWS MCP Server paired with packaged AWS Analytics skills give agents like Claude Code, Kiro, and Cursor deep AWS service expertise — from SQL syntax and metadata discovery to migration planning and performance tuning. Bring your toughest questions — we'll cover setup, agent workflows, and best practices for your environments.

sessions.t: Give your AI agents business context with AWS Glue Data Catalog
sessions.a: An AI agent pointed at a data catalog that has schema but no meaning will guess — and in a regulated environment, guessing is a compliance liability. In this builders' session, learn how to turn the AWS Glue Data Catalog into a trust layer for AI agents. Enrich the catalog with business context — Skill Assets, golden queries, business glossary terms, ownership, and access restrictions — then connect an MCP-compatible AI agent and watch its answers shift from hallucination to governed, data-literate reasoning. Use semantic search to discover data by business meaning, add queryable metadata forms at scale, and leave with architecture patterns to roll this out across your existing catalog. You must bring your laptop to participate.
