sessions.t: Give Your Best Engineers Back to the Roadmap, Not the Pager (sponsored by NeuBird AI)
sessions.a: Forty percent of engineering time goes to firefighting instead of the roadmap you funded. The problem isn’t a lack of dashboards or headcount, it’s that these engineers are forced to act as the glue across these fragmented tools. Between incidents, an autonomous Production Ops Agent keeps working. It deepens its model of your environment, right sizes observability spend, and turns every incident into a captured fix nobody has to relearn. This session shows how NeuBird AI has helped teams recover 200 plus engineering hours a month and cut incident costs 60 percent or more, not by hiring more people or buying more dashboards, but by giving one agent the job of running production so your senior engineers can go back to building it. This presentation is brought to you by NeuBird AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Giving Your AI Agent a Wallet: The Architecture of Spend Control
sessions.a: AI agents can now hold a wallet and pay for APIs, data, and even other agents. The demo takes a few hours; making it safe to ship takes much longer. At the whiteboard, using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments, x402 micropayments, and Cedar policy, we design an agent that spends under a hard budget, then break it together. We work through where guardrails belong, why session limits aren't enough, custodial versus non-custodial tradeoffs, and human-in-the-loop without human-in-the-way. Bring your edge cases. You leave with a reference architecture and a checklist for bounded agent autonomy.

sessions.t: Global transactions in Amazon Aurora DSQL
sessions.a: Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database built for global scale. In this session, Marc Brooker, AWS VP and Distinguished Engineer, dives into the exact algorithms Aurora DSQL uses to achieve faster-than-light consistent reads, strong isolation, durability, and atomicity across regions. The session covers the specific tradeoffs each algorithm makes and what those tradeoffs mean in practice.

sessions.t: Go from Code to Deployed Agent with AgentCore CLI
sessions.a: Go from zero to a deployed, observable AI agent in under an hour. Use the AgentCore CLI to scaffold a Strands agent with a custom tool, test it locally against the Runtime contract, then deploy to AgentCore Runtime via CDK. Invoke the agent to demonstrate session isolation, inspect automatic CloudWatch logs and X-Ray traces, and confirm the framework-agnostic contract by replacing the agent with a plain Python function.

sessions.t: Go Hack Yourself. With AI. (sponsored by Horizon3.ai)
sessions.a: Defenders often drown in noise while attackers move at machine speed. To truly secure your environment, you must adopt an attacker’s perspective. Horizon3 CEO Snehal Antani shares insights from 250,000+ autonomous pentests across 6,000+ environments, demonstrating how AI hackers find exploitable paths that scanners miss, such as credential theft and domain compromise without CVEs. You’ll learn why vulnerable doesn’t mean exploitable, how to validate controls through a Hack-Fix-Verify loop, and where AI belongs in offense and defense: tool for scale and proof, not a black box. This presentation is brought to you by Horizon3.ai, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Go headless: managed harness to custom DevOps orchestration
sessions.a: Your AI agents need production-grade orchestration, but should you own the loop or let AWS handle it? We build one on-call responder three ways: an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness for a managed loop with built-in memory and tool routing, AgentCore Runtime for full control, and AWS DevOps Agent as a batteries-included DevOps harness. Then we build the shape most teams land in: your own orchestrator, DevOps Agent composed in headless over remote MCP and A2A. Bring your challenges and leave with patterns for building composable, robust pipelines that automate complex DevOps workflows end-to-end.

sessions.t: Golden Opportunities: Unlocking Business Value with Agentic AI (sponsored by Atos)
sessions.a: Companies have shifted from talking about agents to putting them to work, but moving from an AWS Bedrock AgentCore demo to a governed, production multi-agent system inside a regulated enterprise isn't a straight line. Atos will show what that path looks like, where it breaks, and how to fix it. What you'll learn ⮚Enterprise patterns that separate successful AWS agentic AI deployments from stalled pilots ⮚Building a governance layer on Amazon Bedrock that regulated industries will approve ⮚How GSI partners turn ideas into completed, production-ready deployments ⮚Where AWS tooling is mature, where it's still evolving, and how to architect around the gaps This presentation is brought to you by Atos, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Go-Live to ROI: How Partners Turn Customer Outcomes into Revenue
sessions.a: The partners thriving in the AI era aren't the ones who just deploy, they're the ones who prove impact. The Business Value Realization (BVR) motion is how consulting and managed services partners are building their next growth engine: documenting outcomes, unlocking milestone-based funding, and turning deployments into expansion revenue. Explore how BVR helps partners quantify ROI, earn a new Competency, build customer success practices that drive revenue beyond go-live, and where the motion is heading next. As AI moves from pilot to production, the partners who own the value conversation won't just retain customers, they'll shape what is built next.

sessions.t: Good Fences Make Good Neighbours: A Network perimeter approach to data perimeters
sessions.a: How do you secure that which has no network? AWS services such as S3, SQS, and DynamoDB help teams build and scale faster but come with a different set of security implications than services that live in your VPC. In this session, you'll learn about best practices and architural patterns for building secure networks on AWS using network features like DNS firewall, and Network firewall and layering them with AWS IAM policies like VPC endpoint policy, and Resource Control Policy to help ensure that your resources that live outside of your network behave like they are in your network.

sessions.t: Govern, Bill, and Attribute: The Unit Economics of Production Agents
sessions.a: Your agent demo costs $0.02 a call; in production it's $4. Can you still price it profitably, and can you capture the full AWS consumption it drives downstream? This chalk talk walks the complete unit economics of a production agent: right-sizing cost with prompt caching, model routing, and tool-call minimization; pricing through consumption versus outcome-based billing; and attributing the full impact through AWS Marketplace metering and PRM, so it converts into AWS investment back to you. Real examples like bid optimization, content moderation, and shopping advisors ground each step.

sessions.t: Governed AI agents for regulated financial services at FINRA
sessions.a: FINRA protects investors and enforces regulation for 3,400+ broker-dealer firms and 1.2 million financial professionals, so regulation must evolve as fast as the markets it oversees. FINRA is exploring the role agentic AI services like Amazon Quick can play on FINRA’s Gateway, its primary external platform serving firms. This session covers the how: the design patterns and guardrails for responsible AI in a regulated environment, including draft-and-attest human accountability, data grounding with hallucination detection, tenant isolation, and a pragmatic governance model. Behind that experience, FINRA keeps models and frameworks interchangeable, so capabilities evolve without rebuilding. Leave with a practical framework for governing agentic AI at scale.

sessions.t: Governed ModelOps: From customization to deployment with SageMaker AI
sessions.a: Join us in working through the ModelOps lifecycle, starting with experiment, train, register, approve, to deploy, anchored by the Amazon SageMaker catalog system of record. Using SageMaker managed MLflow and the catalog within SageMaker AI Studio, you'll build governance in as you go with no end-of-cycle compliance scramble. Training runs auto-catalog with model cards, lineage, and audit trails; you'll discover assets with semantic search, trace lineage with OpenLineage, configure access control, gate promotion on quality and compliance, and publish models across accounts. You'll leave able to trace any endpoint to its dataset, experiment, and approval in seconds.

sessions.t: Governing AI agents: Controls for agentic AI at scale
sessions.a: Your teams are building more agents at a scale that can't be governed manually, and this creates not just a visibility problem but an operational and security risk. In this workshop, you build a layered controls stack for an agent fleet: enforce content and business-logic boundaries with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, apply an evaluator pattern for policy validation, and track compliance posture with AWS Config conformance packs. You wire these into an operating model that approves the routine automatically and routes only the ambiguous to a human. You leave with a clear framework and hands-on practices to deploy more agents, confidently, than your team could review individually.

sessions.t: Governing AI assets at scale with MCP Gateway and Registry
sessions.a: As enterprises onboard AI assets (MCP servers, Agents, Skills) they face a governance problem: no unified way to discover, authenticate, or observe them. MCP Gateway and Registry is an open source control plane with centralized registration, OAuth2 auth, semantic tool discovery, and end-to-end telemetry. Walk through the project's architecture, pluggable auth and storage backends, and deployment patterns on Amazon EKS. An AI/ML platform VP shares their production rollout, governance patterns that scaled across business units, and lessons learned contributing back upstream.

sessions.t: Governing autonomous AI agents across cloud boundaries
sessions.a: When autonomous agents coordinate across cloud boundaries, who enforces the rules — and how do you revoke access instantly when one goes rogue? In this chalk talk, we whiteboard governed multi-agent coordination: Cedar as a portable policy engine across AWS, Azure, and GCP, A2A protocol for cross-cloud agent communication, and a kill switch for instant revocation. The audience picks the scenario — flight delays, trade failures, or healthcare cancellations — and we draw how policy, identity, and coordination work at each boundary crossing.

sessions.t: Governing Hundreds of Accounts in Seconds: Agentic AI Meets Landing Zone Operations
sessions.a: When you manage hundreds of AWS accounts, governance can fall behind. Drift accumulates, controls take days to propagate, and problems go undetected until something breaks. We demonstrate Landing Zone Accelerator 2.0 with built-in AI allowing operators to use natural language to apply organizational changes in seconds. We deploy org-wide security controls, provision accounts, and enforce encryption via a Bedrock-powered interface supporting CloudFormation and Terraform. Attendees learn how we built our governance agents with MCP, and how to design pre-deployment previews for multi-account ops.

sessions.t: Govern models and agents on any cloud with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
sessions.a: Your models and agents run across Bedrock, Azure, GCP, and self-hosted infrastructure, and each one needs safety controls and an audit trail. Rebuilding safety controls per cloud does not scale, and it fragments your audit trail. This chalk talk shows how Bedrock Guardrails gives you one control plane for content filtering, PII redaction, prompt attack detection, and automated reasoning checks, wherever inference runs. Apply a pre-configured guardrail with ApplyGuardrail, or run resource-less checks inline with InvokeGuardrailChecks. Both are decoupled from model invocation and support per-step scoring for agentic workflows.

sessions.t: Govern your context layer for AI agents with AWS Context
sessions.a: Learn how to carry your existing data permissions into a governed context layer your AI agents need to work accurately across structured and unstructured data. AWS Context assembles semantic data from your catalogs, glossaries, query logs, and access patterns into one governed context layer, honoring the governance contract placed on your data assets. Each user's identity flows through the agent so every answer is scoped to what they are authorized to see. We will whiteboard and interact on how identity propagates, how retrieval is filtered, and where permissions break.

sessions.t: GPU cluster failure patterns on AWS: observe, diagnose, recover
sessions.a: At scale, GPU clusters fail in ways single-node debugging never taught you: NCCL timeouts that are actually storage problems, DataLoader forks that silently hang collectives, and GPUs that pass every health check yet corrupt your results. In this hands-on builders session, you diagnose these failures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic Fabric Adapter. Read NCCL debug logs, interpret all-reduce bus bandwidth against per-instance baselines, and run open-source health checks that catch faults before your jobs do. You leave with a failure-signature runbook and a triage method distilled from operating large GPU fleets on AWS.

sessions.t: GPU orchestration at scale using NVIDIA Run:ai across the edge
sessions.a: AWS and NVIDIA have collaborated for over a decade to deliver GPU-accelerated solutions from the cloud to the edge, yet Kubernetes still treats GPUs as opaque, unsharable integers. In this L400 code talk, learn how to deploy NVIDIA Run:ai on Amazon EKS and execute a complete model lifecycle on shared GPU infrastructure. Using Terraform, provision an EKS cluster with NVIDIA L4 nodes, install the Run:ai control plane and cluster agents, and configure project-scoped GPU quotas with priority-based sharing. Then see how Run:ai orchestrates a QLoRA fine-tuning job on Qwen3-14B and serves the resulting adapter with vLLM so you can compare base model responses against your fine-tuned model in real time. Leave with a reproducible pattern for maximizing GPU utilization across competing workloads without over-provisioning.

sessions.t: Graviton5: Migrate your workloads, cut costs, get better performance
sessions.a: AWS Graviton5 delivers up to 25% better compute performance than the previous generation, features caches up to five times larger, and offers some of the fastest memory performance available in the cloud. But what do those improvements actually mean for your workloads? In this session, we go beyond the spec sheet into real-world benchmarks across databases, web applications, and ML inference. Hear from a customer who migrated production workloads across multiple Graviton generations and the compounding performance and cost gains they achieved. Walk away with concrete performance data and a practical framework to evaluate Graviton5 for your own migration.

sessions.t: Graviton. Serverless. Apache Iceberg. Your guide to a modern data warehouse strategy
sessions.a: You need your data warehouse to be fast, open, and accessible to everyone on your team. This session shows you how to get there with Amazon Redshift. Take advantage of Graviton-powered RG instances for faster analytics at lower cost. Eliminate the complexity of managing infrastructure with Redshift Serverless. Query open data formats directly in your data lake with native Apache Iceberg support. And put insights in the hands of every team with natural language access. You'll also learn how multi-warehouse architectures let teams scale independently without duplicating data. Leave with a clear architecture strategy you can apply to your environment.

sessions.t: Grounding LLMs in Truth: Build a Live Fact-Checking Pipeline
sessions.a: Walk through the reference architecture of a real-time fact-checking pipeline built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. See how a live audio stream is turned into fact-by-fact verdicts — true, misleading, or false — each cited to its source at broadcast-compatible latency. We'll unpack the moving parts: a chain of specialized agents on AgentCore, hybrid search on Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and custom tool-use hooks. Bring your own use case and leave with a mapped path from it to the reference architecture, plus answers to the concrete design questions blocking you: agent sharding, tabular corpus indexing, guardrails, and streaming reasoning to the UI.

sessions.t: Ground your agents with AWS Context and Amazon SageMaker
sessions.a: Agents are only as good as the context they're given. In this session, see how AWS Context makes the agentic experience in Amazon SageMaker more accurate and useful by grounding agents in business metadata. We'll show how context-aware agents like SageMaker Data Agent break complex requests into structured, multi-step plans, generate validated SQL, Python, and PySpark against your real data, and keep humans in the loop with built-in checkpoints. You'll learn practical techniques to feed the right context to your agents, connect additional sources, and turn a capable assistant into one that truly understands your environment.

sessions.t: Grow Adoption Where Customers Work with AWS Bedrock and Quick
sessions.a: Your customers increasingly live inside an AI work surface, and your product needs to be there too. In this hands-on session, you'll take a SaaS product—its API and a simple agentic capability—and bring it into Amazon Quick using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll adapt it for AgentCore, wire up secure identity, then build Chat Agents, Research, Flows, and Apps that put your product's intelligence in front of users. Customers get your whole product in Quick, as-is. Walk out with a working reference pattern and the ability to spin up POCs for product leadership.

sessions.t: Growing role of CPUs in AI: Inference and agents AI on EC2
sessions.a: CPUs play a critical and growing role in production AI systems. This session explores two CPU-intensive AI patterns on EC2. First, AI inference: serving language model predictions at scale using Graviton and x86 instances, with real-world cost and latency tradeoffs. Second, agentic AI: running sandboxed environments where autonomous agents compile code, execute tools, and interact with external systems, requiring fast, isolated, ephemeral compute. We share production architectures, performance benchmarks across instance families, and practical guidance on matching your AI workload to the right EC2 CPU. Walk away with a decision framework for running AI beyond GPUs.

sessions.t: Growing role of CPUs in AI: Inference and agents AI on EC2

First, AI inference: serving language model predictions at scale using Graviton and x86 instances, with real-world cost and latency tradeoffs. Second, agentic AI: running sandboxed environments where autonomous agents compile code, execute tools, and interact with external systems, requiring fast, isolated, ephemeral compute. We share production architectures, performance benchmarks across instance families, and practical guidance on matching your AI workload to the right EC2 CPU. Walk away with a decision framework for running AI beyond GPUs.

sessions.t: Guardrails for AI-henerated Serverless infrastructure
sessions.a: Coding agents generate full serverless architectures in seconds, but without guardrails they produce over-permissioned IAM policies, skip encryption at rest, and deploy resources that violate your organization's tagging and cost policies. In this chalk talk, discuss operational controls for AI-generated infrastructure: automated security reviews that catch policy violations before deployment, cost estimation gates that flag unexpected spend, compliance checks against organizational standards, and MCP server configurations that enforce service boundaries and naming conventions. We whiteboard which guardrails to automate versus which require human review, and where teams are getting the balance wrong.

sessions.t: Guide to deploying landing zones & modernized networks in hours
sessions.a: Reimagine what migration looks like when landing zone setup and network translation go from weeks to hours. In this chalk talk, we show how AWS Transform's agentic AI compresses that timeline, from migration inventory to fully deployed, validated landing zones and modernized networks. See how production-ready account structures deploy through Control Tower with guardrails in place, and how firewall configurations become optimized VPCs, subnets, and security groups. Bring your questions and hear from the experts building these capabilities.

sessions.t: Guide to deploying landing zones & modernized networks in hours

Bring your questions and hear from the experts building these capabilities.

sessions.t: HA and DR design patterns for Amazon RDS for SQL Server and Oracle
sessions.a: Explore high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) design patterns for SQL Server and Oracle databases on Amazon RDS. In this session, learn about the features offered by Amazon RDS for business continuity, including Multi-AZ deployments, read replicas, and cross-region replication. Discover the customizations that Amazon RDS enables for HA and DR while also allowing you to bring your own license (BYOL) for SQL Server. Also learn how globally resilient solutions architected with Amazon RDS minimize downtime and meet stringent business continuity requirements for mission-critical workloads.

sessions.t: Hands-on distributed training with AWS Trainium and PyTorch
sessions.a: Get hands-on with AWS Trainium and PyTorch's TorchTitan to train models using a fully native PyTorch workflow. This workshop walks you through distributed training on Trainium—covering cluster setup, parallelism strategies, and performance optimization—all through familiar PyTorch APIs. Whether you're training LLMs or fine-tuning domain models, you'll learn how Trainium and TorchTitan simplify scaling without sacrificing native PyTorch flexibility. Leave with the skills to scale model training on Trainium without changing your PyTorch workflow.

sessions.t: Hands-on distributed training with AWS Trainium and PyTorch
sessions.a: Get hands-on with AWS Trainium and PyTorch's TorchTitan to train models using a fully native PyTorch workflow. This workshop walks you through distributed training on Trainium—covering cluster setup, parallelism strategies, and performance optimization—all through familiar PyTorch APIs. Whether you're training LLMs or fine-tuning domain models, you'll learn how Trainium and TorchTitan simplify scaling without sacrificing native PyTorch flexibility. Leave with the skills to scale model training on Trainium without changing your PyTorch workflow.

sessions.t: Hands-on: Harden your AI agents with Nitro Confidential Computing
sessions.a: Agentic AI systems autonomously orchestrate tools, integrate third-party components, and make decisions, introducing risks from compromised dependencies and agents deviating from intended behavior. Protecting prompts, agent memory, retrieval context, and model weights requires strong isolation and verifiable trust. In this workshop, you will build agentic AI apps, identify threats from untrusted supply chains and uncontrolled autonomy, and mitigate them using AWS Confidential Computing on EC2 with cryptographic attestation, isolated execution, open weight models, and Amazon Bedrock.

sessions.t: Hands-on training world models and deploying agents for Physical AI
sessions.a: Physical AI is transforming robotics and autonomous systems with world models that enable agents to understand and interact with their environments. Training and deploying these large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) models requires complex distributed infrastructure. AWS Trainium and the AWS Neuron simplify this with PyTorch integration — apply standard distributed training techniques using familiar APIs while the software stack handles multi-device coordination, compilation, and optimization. In this hands-on session, fine-tune a transformer-based world model, implement parameter-efficient training strategies, and deploy trained agents for real-time inference. Leave with practical skills to adapt Physical AI models and deploy robotic agents at scale.

sessions.t: Hands-on training world models and deploying agents for Physical AI
sessions.a: Physical AI is transforming robotics and autonomous systems with world models that enable agents to understand and interact with their environments. Training and deploying these large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) models requires complex distributed infrastructure. AWS Trainium and the AWS Neuron simplify this with PyTorch integration — apply standard distributed training techniques using familiar APIs while the software stack handles multi-device coordination, compilation, and optimization. Leave with practical skills to adapt Physical AI models and deploy robotic agents at scale.

sessions.t: Hands-on with AWS DevOps agent
sessions.a: AWS DevOps Agent is your always-available operations teammate that investigates, resolves, and proactively prevents incidents. In this hands-on workshop, take the on-call seat: inject real faults into a live microservices store on Amazon EKS, partner with the agent to root-cause them in minutes, and judge its mitigation plans. Then extend it — encode your team's expertise as skills, connect custom MCP tools, automate investigations from alarms, and approve agent-executed fixes. Leave with production-ready patterns that keep your infrastructure running.

sessions.t: Hands-on with AWS DevOps agent
sessions.a: AWS DevOps Agent is your always-available operations teammate that investigates, resolves, and proactively prevents incidents. In this hands-on workshop, take the on-call seat: inject real faults into a live microservices store on Amazon EKS, partner with the agent to root-cause them in minutes, and judge its mitigation plans. Leave with production-ready patterns that keep your infrastructure running.

sessions.t: Hands-on with the AWS Network Firewall proxy for secure egress
sessions.a: AWS Network Firewall now gives you the flexibility to act as an explicit forward proxy for outbound traffic on the firewall you already run. Clients connect to it directly by its proxy FQDN, so no route-table changes are required. The proxy attaches to a NAT gateway and terminates each client connection, letting one firewall consolidate egress for multiple VPCs regardless of overlapping CIDRs. In this builders session you'll get hands-on deploying the proxy and building layered egress controls, up to and including outbound TLS inspection. You'll leave knowing when and how to use the firewall proxy to centralize and enforce egress controls for private workloads.

sessions.t: Hands-On Workshop: Build & Deploy AI Agents with Cloudera Agent Studio (sponsored by Cloudera)
sessions.a: Join this exclusive hands-on workshop to master building and deploying high-impact AI agents with Cloudera Agent Studio. Move from experimentation to production using trusted data, scalable workflows, and governed infrastructure. Led by Cloudera solution architects, you will build multi-agent workflows without code, develop agentic chatbots for data access, learn Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration with AWS tools including Amazon Bedrock and PuppyGraph, and explore the latest Cloudera AI and Workbench enhancements. Designed for data scientists, developers, engineers, and analysts ready to enable secure, scalable, open AI across hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Healthcare & Life Sciences AI Agents: From Spec to Demo in 120 Min
sessions.a: Healthcare and life sciences teams face pressure to apply generative AI but struggle moving from proof-of-concept to prototype. In this hands-on workshop, you use Kiro IDE and spec-driven development to build a functional AI agent—progressing through requirements, design, implementation, and live demo. Choose from four use cases: extract data from handwritten GMP batch records, orchestrate single-cell RNA-seq pipelines on AWS HealthOmics, identify clinical trial candidates using biomarker analysis, or build a patient access agent on Amazon Connect Health. You'll leave with a deployable agent, reusable specs, and a repeatable methodology for rapid AI development in regulated environments.

sessions.t: Healthcare & Life Sciences AI Agents: From Spec to Demo in 120 Min
sessions.a: Healthcare and life sciences teams face pressure to apply generative AI but struggle moving from proof-of-concept to prototype. In this hands-on workshop, you use Kiro IDE and spec-driven development to build a functional AI agent—progressing through requirements, design, implementation, and live demo. Choose from four use cases: extract data from handwritten GMP batch records, orchestrate single-cell RNA-seq pipelines on AWS HealthOmics, identify clinical trial candidates using biomarker analysis, or build a patient access agent on Amazon Connect Health. You'll leave with a deployable agent, reusable specs, and a repeatable methodology for rapid AI development in regulated environments.

sessions.t: Hidden trade-offs in distributed architectures
sessions.a: Asynchronous event-driven architectures enable loosely coupled, scalable, and resilient systems. But the devil is in the details, and hidden complexity emerges when components interact under real-world pressure. Consistency, latency, failure handling, and cost aren't determined by architecture diagrams but by the trade-offs behind the integration patterns and services you choose. Through a real-world case study using AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB, DynamoDB Streams, and AWS Step Functions, you'll investigate unexpected system behavior and uncover the trade-offs behind it. You'll leave with a sharper intuition to see beyond cloud abstractions and make more intentional architectural decisions for resilient systems.

sessions.t: High Growth. Bold Innovation. The Kiwibank Story. (sponsored by Accenture)
sessions.a: How does a nationally owned bank out-innovate much larger competitors? Kiwibank, New Zealand's only 100% NZ-owned bank, must compete against four far larger Australian-owned banks — with a fraction of the resources. Working with Accenture and AWS, Kiwibank is building a governed enterprise AI layer that every future application can draw from. The result: a compounding AI advantage that grows with each new use case, letting the bank launch products faster, serve customers more intelligently, and scale without proportional cost growth. Hear how Kiwibank is using Accenture and AWS to build the AI foundation for its next decade of growth. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How 2 Billion Records Became One Data Product at Verisk (sponsored by Senzing)
sessions.a: Every insurance data product, underwriting or claims, hinges on one question: is this the same person or organization across systems? Verisk answers it once, at scale, treating the answer as a data product. This session unpacks how Verisk used AI-powered entity resolution on AWS to turn fragmented, siloed, acquisition-inherited data into one reusable identity asset, a proprietary entity ID appended across policies, claims, and enrichment data, not another MDM project. A five-person team built this across 2 billion records and 400 million identities with sub-second response. That data commands premium value, and identity became infrastructure, not a cleanup project. This presentation is brought to you by Senzing, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How a brand modernized CX Globally Across Three Regions
sessions.a: You expanded globally. Your customer experience didn't. What started as regional growth became a patchwork of inconsistent tools, siloed operations, and fragile workarounds that couldn't keep pace with your brand. Learn how a comany stopped managing around the complexity and rebuilt from the foundation - modernizing its global CX infrastructure on Amazon Connect Customer across North America, APAC, and EMEA without disrupting a single customer interaction. If your service operations were built for one market and stretched across many, this is what it looks like to standardize at scale and unlock the agility to move toward AI-driven experiences on your terms.

sessions.t: How a Brand Turned AI Governance Into a Strategic Advantage with Amazon Quick
sessions.a: In automotive, data isolation is not optional. You serve thousands of dealer clients who compete with each other, handle consumer financial data under FTC Safeguards rules, and operate across state privacy boundaries. Most AI tools cannot enforce tenant-level separation between competing dealers, restrict access by franchise agreement, or prove compliance across jurisdictions. Hear from a customer who turned that constraint into an advantage: they built a governance model with Amazon Quick that enforces fine-grained data permissions across their dealer network, role-based access controls by business function, and audit frameworks that satisfy regulators and competitive separation requirements. Learn how they validated it against compliance requirements, and how governance became the reason they deployed faster than competitors still waiting on security approval.

sessions.t: How A Customer Met Surge Hiring in Hours, Not Weeks
sessions.a: You expanded fast, but your hiring didn't keep up. What started as seasonal growth has become a scramble of manual screening, scheduling delays, and fragile workarounds that can't keep pace with your brand — forcing the impossible choice between speed and quality. Hear how Universal Studios replaced weeks-long hiring with Amazon Connect Talent, putting AI teammates to work running science-backed candidate assessments and AI-led interviews that take candidates from application to same-day offer — evaluated on the substance of their answers. Built on AWS with Amazon's proven hiring science, Amazon Connect Talent ensures recruiters stay in control of every decision.

sessions.t: How Adobe unified multicloud observability with open source
sessions.a: Adobe operates production services across AWS and Azure, but 20+ monitoring tools and per-cloud dashboards turned every cross-cloud incident into a translation problem before debugging could begin. In this session, hear how Adobe standardized on OpenTelemetry and consolidated to four open-source technologies (Cortex, Grafana Tempo, FluentBit, and Grafana) with AWS as the operational hub processing 1M+ trace samples per second. The result was a single pane of glass for every engineer regardless of where workloads run, and multi-million dollar savings through telemetry compression. Walk away with a proven, vendor-independent playbook for multicloud observability built on open source and open standards.

sessions.t: How A+E Global Media Manages Storage Sprawl and Optimizes Cost (sponsored by Datadog)
sessions.a: As data-intensive and AI workloads drive continued growth in cloud infrastructure and storage, the complexity of understanding usage, ownership, and cost is increasing. In this session, we'll walk through how A+E Global Media gained visibility into the drivers behind rising S3 spend, connected costs to application owners, and established stronger FinOps governance. Attendees will walk away with best practices for architecting cost-efficient systems with Datadog by identifying inefficiencies and connecting cost, storage, and operational context to drive continuous optimization. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How AI Is Transforming Enterprise Application Support (sponsored by HCLTech)
sessions.a: Application support is evolving from reactive issue handling to proactive, AI-native operations. This session presents a proven customer blueprint for governed AI agents that monitor applications, detect anomalies early, analyze root causes, and automate approved remediation while preserving security, compliance, and human oversight. Based on HCLTech's financial services experience, it shares practical lessons for adopting AI-driven operations that reduce support costs, improve application availability, accelerate incident resolution, and free support teams to focus on higher-value business outcomes. Attendees will learn how organizations can operationalize agentic capabilities responsibly, integrate them into existing support models, and create measurable value across modern application management. This presentation is brought to you by HCLTech, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How AI-native startups run untrusted agent code on Lambda MicroVMs
sessions.a: AI agents increasingly generate and execute untrusted code that needs a safe, isolated place to run. A growing set of AI-native startups and ISVs are converging on one pattern: one MicroVM per agent session, spun up on demand, torn down when the work is done. In this session, see how [Customer] built production agent sandboxes on Lambda MicroVMs, walking through the full lifecycle that delivers hardware-level isolation per session. See how they scale to thousands of concurrent sandboxes and the operational tradeoffs they navigated to get there.

sessions.t: How AI-Powered DevSecOps Fueled Intuitive Machines' Race to the Moon (sponsored by GitLab)
sessions.a: In 2019, Intuitive Machines won a NASA contract to land a spacecraft near the Moon's south pole — with five years to build every system from scratch and a team of just 50 developers. Join James Blakeslee, Vice President of Engineering at Intuitive Machines, as he shares how the team used AI-powered DevSecOps to ship mission-critical software fast enough to become the first U.S. venture in 50 years — and the first commercial company ever — to land intact on the Moon. You'll learn how they're now using GitLab Duo Agent Platform and Amazon Bedrock to accelerate development toward their next lunar lander. This presentation is brought to you by GitLab, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How Amazon Ads Built a Service Mesh Without a Control Plane Service
sessions.a: Most service meshes require dedicated infrastructure just to manage the mesh itself. Amazon Ads took a different approach: a fully serverless xDS control plane built with AWS Lambda and S3 that manages hundreds of Envoy proxies serving 100K+ requests per second at 2ms p99 overhead — with no long-running control plane servers. In this session, we walk through the architecture end to end: Envoy sidecars on Amazon ECS for service-to-service communication, an edge proxy for external ingress, and the serverless control plane that ties it together. You'll leave with patterns you can adopt immediately.

sessions.t: How Amazon Ads Built a Service Mesh Without a Control Plane Service
sessions.a: Most service meshes require dedicated infrastructure just to manage the mesh itself. sessions.t: How An AI-First Approach Helped Add 500,000 New Members
sessions.a: 10 million members. Limited visibility into support interactions. High costs. Flybuys needed a new path. In 7 months, they migrated to Amazon Connect Customer, bringing operations in-house, and deploying AI agents that now handle 20% of member voice interactions. The result of the migration has been a 24% cost optimization while adding an additional 500,000 members. Join this session to hear how Flybuys took control of their member experience, unlocked deep visibility across every interaction, and are now moving quickly to scale agentic AI across voice and digital channels.

sessions.t: How Badger Meter unified customer identity for critical infrastructure
sessions.a: Badger Meter delivers smart water solutions supporting critical infrastructure for utilities. Their applications relied on fragmented authentication such as password hashes, siloed SAML integrations, and custom JWT schemes. As their portfolio of customer services grew, managing identity across isolated platforms became unsustainable. Learn how Badger Meter migrated to Amazon Cognito to centralize authentication and reduce friction. This session covers multi-tenant architecture, Lambda triggers for token enrichment, SAML/OIDC federation, and Managed Login—a blueprint for consolidating identity at scale.

sessions.t: How Bayer designed 50K proteins on Amazon Bio Discovery
sessions.a: This chalk talk explores how to architect agentic AI workflows for generative protein design at enterprise scale. Using Bayer's oncology nanobody campaign as the reference implementation, we walk through the technical and scientific decisions behind a pipeline that generated 50,000 candidates and 3,000 prioritized candidates in weeks using Amazon Bio Discovery. Topics include: model orchestration patterns for generative and predictive models, designing scoring functions that encode biological mechanism (not just binding affinity), iterative feedback loops between computation and wet-lab validation, and scaling considerations for enterprise drug discovery programs. Attendees will leave with a reusable architectural blueprint for building agentic biomolecule design workflows on AWS.

sessions.t: How Bayer modernized R&D analytics into an agentic decision engine
sessions.a: Bayer's R&D analytics relied on manual pipelines, fragmented tooling, and engineering-heavy workflows that bottlenecked scientists. In this session, hear how Bayer modernized that stack into an agentic decision engine on AWS, cutting token costs by roughly 600% and saving scientists 70% of their engineering time. We'll trace the modernization journey from legacy analytics architecture through the migration to cloud-native services and show how that foundation enabled autonomous multi-agent workflows that now orchestrate R&D decisions at enterprise scale. Leave with a framework for modernizing analytics into agentic AI capabilities.

sessions.t: How Bayer simplified their genomics pipeline with Amazon S3 Files
sessions.a: Bayer's genomics and research teams relied on a patchwork of workarounds to support specialized software, user scripts, and ad-hoc analysis on cloud-stored data. AWS DataSync and Storage Gateway handle high-throughput data uploads to S3, but downstream access meant managing multiple data copies, manual downloads, and unstable FUSE mounts, adding cost and operational overhead. Bayer shares how adding S3 Files to their architecture eliminated these access workarounds by providing a simple, mountable file interface directly on their S3 data. Learn how their team reduced data duplication and gave researchers access to petabyte-scale genomics datasets without changing their existing tools or workflows.

sessions.t: How Blue Origin built a centralized enterprise knowledge graph on AWS
sessions.a: Building enterprise AI applications shouldn't require every team to reinvent the wheel — standing up data pipelines, managing security, and keeping knowledge bases current. Blue Origin faced this at scale: dozens of teams, hundreds of data sources, and growing demand for AI apps that could reason across all of it. The answer was RAGNet — a centralized enterprise knowledge graph platform built on Amazon Neptune and Amazon Bedrock that aggregates structured and unstructured data into a secure, always-current graph any developer or AI agent can query in plain natural language.

sessions.t: How BMW Group Built an Automotive Industry Model on SageMaker AI
sessions.a: Large Industry Models (LIMs) go beyond general-purpose LLMs, embedding deep expertise in an industry's processes, data, and terminology. BMW Group and the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center share how they are building an automotive LIM on BMW's Problem Management Process spanning the R&D-to-delivery lifecycle. Learn how teacher distillation, QLoRA fine-tuning on Amazon SageMaker, and LLM-as-judge evaluation can help set the foundations toward a Large Industry Model. We then explore how Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on domain knowledge can serve as a cost-effective proxy for Continued Pre-Training (CPT), and how adapter merging composes capabilities without retraining.

sessions.t: How Bridgewater Associates uses agentic SDLC to accelerate change
sessions.a: Learn how Bridgewater Associates, a leading macroeconomic investment manager, built an agentic SDLC platform that transformed the way technology and investment teams work by leveraging AI agents to automate the software development lifecycle. Built as an AI teammate in Slack and powered by an orchestration service running these agents in secure sandboxes, the platform automates every stage of the SDLC—from idea inception through merge requests in GitLab to deploying code that generates investment signals. Amazon Bedrock powers their coding agents, orchestration stages, and custom agents built using agent SDKs. This session will also discuss integration with AWS frontier agents like AWS DevOps Agent.

sessions.t: How Chamberlain and Daikin power smart product innovation with AWS
sessions.a: Manufacturers are transforming products into connected, intelligent offerings that deliver proactive, personalized customer experiences. Discover how AWS helps you build, connect, and monetize smart products at global scale. Hear how Chamberlain Group migrated its myQ smart home product platform, with 15M+ devices and 12M+ users, to AWS—eliminating multi-cloud complexity and furthering their AI and video intelligence offerings. Also learn how Daikin is using AWS to deliver 24/7 remote monitoring and predictive control across an extensive network of HVAC systems. Walk away with proven patterns for scaling connected products and unlocking AI-driven service revenue.

sessions.t: How Citizens Bank reimagined CX with Amazon Connect and generative AI
sessions.a: Citizens Financial Group is transforming its customer service ecosystem using Amazon Connect, Amazon Lex, and generative AI. In this session, learn how Citizens migrated legacy IVR and contact center infrastructure to Amazon Connect, deployed conversational AI across voice and digital channels, and integrated generative AI-powered agent assist and real-time conversation intelligence. We cover the solution architecture spanning Amazon Connect, Amazon Lex, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Lambda, and Amazon EventBridge, along with measurable outcomes in containment rates, handle time, and routing accuracy. Attendees will gain a practical blueprint for enterprise-scale customer experience transformation in financial services.

sessions.t: How Context Graphs Cut AI Token Usage by Up to 70% (sponsored by Sphinx AI)
sessions.a: Context graphs can reduce token usage by up to 70% while maintaining accuracy. This session explores how context graphs help AI agents understand relationships, definitions, and business meaning across enterprise data. We will look at how context graphs capture knowledge that traditional data models miss, and how organizations are applying them. You will see real examples of the architecture and results involved in giving AI the context it needs to reason effectively. This presentation is brought to you by Sphinx AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How Cox Achieved 7x ROI with Agentic AI on AWS (sponsored by Accenture)
sessions.a: Cox Communications partnered with Accenture and Anthropic's Claude on AWS to transform B2B marketing and sales, generating a 7x return on its first-year AI investment. By deploying AI-powered marketing and sales agents across 120 micro-industries and eight customer segments, Cox replaced one-size-fits-all campaigns with personalized engagement at scale. The initiative delivered 55% faster speed to market, a 2-point increase in B2B conversion, 40% higher campaign efficiency, and an 86% reduction in lead management costs while improving data accuracy from 18% to 97%. Today, Cox is operating an end-to-end agentic go-to-market system with human oversight. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How Delta Air Lines achieved always-on code modernization
sessions.a: Every enterprise carries the same growing list: outdated dependencies, end-of-life runtimes, and security vulnerabilities that nobody has time to fix. In this session, learn how AWS Transform uses agentic AI to find these issues across your entire portfolio and fix them without waiting for a human to intervene. We'll cover how to maintain a living inventory of what needs upgrading, prioritize by risk, and automate remediation at scale. Hear how Delta Air Lines drove autonomous remediation across 100+ development teams, turning tech debt from a never-ending backlog into an always-on process.

sessions.t: How Deutsche Bahn made 10 years of cloud modernization pay off in AI
sessions.a: You've invested in cloud. Maybe migrated. Maybe modernized. Your board wants AI yesterday, but 88% of companies use AI and only 1% believe they're at maturity. The gap isn't infrastructure. It's whether your organization can move fast enough. In this fireside chat, an AWS executive-in-residence sits down with Deutsche Bahn leadership to unpack how they built that speed: 550+ autonomous teams, AWS migration completed 18 months early, and enterprise-scale agentic AI now in production. You'll leave with: (1) what "AI-ready" requires beyond cloud, (2) a governance model for agents at scale, and (3) a framework for pilot to all-in.

sessions.t: How Elevance Health Delivers an AI-Native Member Experience on Real-Time Context
sessions.a: Members shouldn't have to navigate fragmented systems to understand their benefits and find the right care. Rather than solving one interaction at a time, Elevance Health designed for the holistic member experience. Serving 46 million members, they are building a real-time context layer that unifies clinical, claims, and behavioral data to power AI agents that deliver personalized guidance across the entire care journey. Amazon Connect Customer consumes this context at the point of interaction, enabling associates and AI agents to anticipate needs, surface relevant information, and trigger next-best-actions. Attendees will learn how semantic data layers and agentic workflows come together under a governed deployment model for regulated healthcare.

sessions.t: How Emirates built multicloud AI agents with open-source LLM orchestration
sessions.a: Enterprises running AI agents across multiple clouds face fragmented model access, inconsistent pricing, and vendor lock-in. Open-source frameworks like LiteLLM provide a unified interface to orchestrate LLMs across Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Google Vertex AI based on use-case requirements and token economics. This session demonstrates how Emirates built a multi-cloud agent architecture using LiteLLM as the routing layer, with Bedrock as the primary backbone. Learn patterns for cost-based routing, fallback strategies, model selection by capability, and unified observability across providers.

sessions.t: How Enterprises Are Eliminating Phone Menu Trees with Agentic AI
sessions.a: Large enterprises run very complex corporate hotlines. Thousands of daily calls in multiple languages spanning diverse business units and product lines. To ensure calls are properly routed to the correct team, forward-thinking companies are replacing their legacy interactive voice response (IVR) systems with multilingual AI agents from Amazon Connect Customer, achieving high autonomous call handling rates. No more menu trees. No more language barriers. Join this session to learn a practical approach to scaling agentic AI enterprise-wide, including lessons learned and future expansion.

sessions.t: How event driven architectures go wrong and how to fix them
sessions.a: Event-driven architectures promise decoupling and scalability, but production systems reveal hard-won lessons. In this chalk talk, we dissect the most expensive anti-patterns teams encounter such as unbounded fan-out, missing dead-letter queues, chatty event schemas that drive up costs, and orchestration gaps that silently drop work. We whiteboard fixes using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Step Functions, and proven enterprise integration patterns, then walk through designs that keep event-driven systems reliable, cost-effective, and observable at scale.
