sessions.t: How Fidelity built a cloud-agnostic AI Gateway
sessions.a: Fidelity Asset Management runs 40+ LLM models across AWS, Azure, and GCP, serving 100K+ daily requests to 20 business units. Rather than building separate integrations per provider, they built a cloud-agnostic AI gateway that provides a single abstraction layer for model access, governance, and observability. Learn how Fidelity Asset Management implemented three-tier rate limiting, centralized audit logging, fine-grained access controls, and real-time cost tracking across all providers without sacrificing developer velocity. Attendees will leave with a reusable pattern for building governed, multi-cloud AI platforms in regulated industries.

sessions.t: How FINRA automated dependency lifecycle management with AI agents
sessions.a: With 2,300 components and over 700,000 dependencies, FINRA uses Kiro and AWS Transform custom to deploy GenAI upgrade agents across Python, Java, and Angular. Learn how governed automation and monthly "Transform-a-thons" reclaimed 1,800 engineering hours across 25 teams in three months, and how to shift from reactive patching to predictable dependency lifecycle management. Discover how FINRA's move to continuous modernization reduces the effort of maintaining technical debt.

sessions.t: How FSI brands are navigating conversational AI for customer engagement
sessions.a: Financial services customers expect fast, personalized service but compliance, security, and regulatory requirements make automation a high-stakes challenge. Discover how Amazon Connect Customer enables financial institutions to deploy agentic AI self-service that blends autonomous reasoning with deterministic guardrails for identity verification, fraud checks, and regulatory disclosures. Learn how to automate complex interactions like account servicing, disputes, and payments while maintaining full compliance and governance. See how leading institutions are going live in weeks, reducing call volumes, improving containment, and elevating CSAT without compromising trust.

sessions.t: How GE Vernova scaled self-service AI Agents to 75,000+ workers on AWS
sessions.a: GE Vernova set out to put AI directly into the hands of every employee; from the C-suite to field engineers through its Amp 2.0 platform. In this session, learn how GE Vernova integrated Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and AgentCore to deliver self-service agentic capabilities enabling employees across all roles to interact with enterprise data, automate workflows, and surface insights via natural language. Learn and discover how the team designed agents serving diverse personas, the governance and guardrails for enterprise-wide deployment, and how AgentCore's managed infrastructure enabled rapid scaling without custom orchestration. Walk away with a blueprint for democratizing AI across a global industrial workforce.

sessions.t: How HealthEdge is consolidating 8,700 servers from multicloud to AWS
sessions.a: Running workloads across multiple clouds and on-premises data centers creates compounding complexity: inconsistent tooling, duplicated licensing costs, and operational overhead that slows everything down. HealthEdge faced exactly this across Azure, GCP, and three data centers while serving 115 health plans that depend on their systems daily. In this session, hear how they're consolidating 8,700 servers, 1,600 databases, and thousands of cloud services onto AWS on a 2-year roadmap. Learn how they evaluated providers, built a strategy around rightsizing and licensing optimization, and are executing without disrupting the health plans that depend on them.

sessions.t: How Hertz Made Karpenter Smarter with autonomous AI-Driven Optimization (sponsored by Cast AI)
sessions.a: Hertz used Cast AI agents to make Karpenter much smarter: the agents autonomously analyze every workload, rightsize it, then continuously instruct Karpenter how to rearrange nodes to cut waste. Hertz's platform engineering team deployed this across their multi-cluster EKS fleet entirely through Terraform. Sonal will show the real numbers: where the extra savings hid, how infrastructure-as-code took onboarding from pre-dev to production, and what it takes to automate cost optimization at fleet scale without babysitting it. This presentation is brought to you by Cast AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How Iberdrola Increased Marketing Capacity 4x with Agentic AI (sponsored by Accenture)
sessions.a: Iberdrola, a Spanish multinational electric utility company, is transforming marketing with CreatIA, an agentic AI platform co-developed with Accenture and AWS. Facing rising demand for content, faster decisions and accelerated campaign delivery, Iberdrola adopted a new operating model powered by specialized AI agents across the marketing lifecycle. CreatIA unifies market intelligence, insights generation, content creation, validation and campaign activation in a single enterprise platform. The solution has reduced time spent analyzing and processing information by 80%, accelerated strategic decision making by 40%, increased creative production capacity by up to four times, and reduced content production costs by 60%. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How Infor Uses AWS Agentic AI to Transform Cloud Operations at Scale
sessions.a: Infor (a Koch Industries company) runs one of the largest enterprise footprints on AWS. As that footprint grew, manual release gates, incident investigations, and periodic security assessments couldn't keep pace. Hear how Infor is adopting AWS agentic AI to reshape operations: DevOps Agent for incident triage and release readiness, Continuum for continuous security validation, and the Well-Architected Agentic AI Lens for production guardrails. Leave with a blueprint for agentic AI at scale.

sessions.t: How ISVs ship agent products to customers faster with AgentCore
sessions.a: Every customer now expects AI agents in your software product. But shipping agents to thousands of customers means solving multi-tenancy, per-customer isolation, identity delegation, and cost attribution before you write a single line of agent logic. That is months of plumbing, not product. In this session, hear how Twilio and Typeform built agent products on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore - serving millions of end users without building custom infrastructure. Learn how they eliminated months of infrastructure work, stayed framework-neutral, and focused engineering on what their customers actually pay for — the agent experience, not the plumbing underneath.

sessions.t: How Itaú built cell-based resilience for critical workloads across clouds
sessions.a: Mission-critical workloads require extreme resilience without the latency penalty of multi-region architectures, especially when strong consistency and real-time external integrations are required. In this session, discover how cell-based and shard-based architectures reduce blast radius and contain failures across cloud providers while keeping latency within strict thresholds. Explore traffic management patterns between cloud providers, data replication strategies including synchronous and asynchronous approaches, and consistency models. Learn how architectural adapters enable workload portability and provider independence. Gain practical patterns for cross-cell replication and automated failover, with examples from Itaú Unibanco's production environment.

sessions.t: How IT leaders actually pulled off their cloud migrations
sessions.a: How did other organizations get their on-premises environments to AWS? In this panel, migration leaders from global organizations share exactly how they did it, including those moving off VMware and other aging infrastructure. You'll hear the real planning decisions, execution strategies, and lessons learned that made their transitions successful. They'll also share where they're headed next with modernization and innovation. Whether you're just getting started or pushing past roadblocks, you'll leave with proven strategies and practical insights to accelerate your own cloud migration.

sessions.t: How Jack in the Box delivers personalized store reporting at scale
sessions.a: Franchise operators run restaurants, not BI tools. In this session, learn how Jack in the Box delivered store-specific performance reports and actionable insights straight to every operator's inbox across 2,100+ locations. We'll cover throttle-aware parallel orchestration, failure isolation patterns, and how this approach turns business intelligence into a scalable, zero-friction communication channel that drives operator engagement and revenue. Walk away with a reusable blueprint for high-volume, per-location reporting in any multi-unit retail or restaurant business

sessions.t: How Kiro learns: an AI coding agent that improves with every session
sessions.a: Learn how Kiro turns working sessions into durable knowledge and how to design, debug, and evaluate an agent’s memory lifecycle. See how Kiro extracts learnings from explicit instructions and task outcomes, such as successful build commands or rejected pull requests. Explore how it consolidates new knowledge with existing memories, resolves contradictions and expiring facts, and retrieves only relevant context for tasks. You’ll also learn how provenance keeps memories auditable and correctable, how memory stays consistent across IDE, CLI, and web, how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory scopes knowledge globally or by repository, and how retrieval quality is measured by task outcomes.

sessions.t: How LG U+ cut migration time 50% with AI-powered app refactoring
sessions.a: Moving servers to the cloud without modernizing the applications on them just moves your technical debt to a new address. LG U+ needed to modernize applications before they could migrate them, and doing both sequentially would have taken too long. In this session, LG U+ shares how they ran AI-powered modernization and migration in parallel across 87 systems spanning 1,579 virtual servers and 107 physical servers. The result: roughly 20% migration velocity improvement and a 50% reduction in Java migration time through AI-assisted refactoring. You'll learn how to modernize at scale without slowing down the move.

sessions.t: How LSEG Built a Multicloud Internal Developer Platform with Kubernetes and AI
sessions.a: At London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), deploying enterprise workloads traditionally took weeks or months of onboarding, governance, networking, and operational setup. In this session, we’ll share how a small AI-augmented engineering team built RouteOne: LSEG’s fully managed multicloud application platform, enabling developers to deploy compliant workloads across multiple cloud providers in minutes by committing their code and a single YAML definition. We’ll explore the Kubernetes-based control plane, enterprise guardrails, and AI-native developer experience powered by APIs, MCP and agent skills. We’ll also share lessons learned from using AI-assisted engineering practices to rapidly deliver a lean, enterprise-grade platform in a regulated environment.

sessions.t: How Max Mara built multicloud FinOps with open source
sessions.a: Max Mara runs hundreds of applications across AWS, GCP, Alicloud, and on-prem serving 20+ million monthly visits, but had no unified view of cost or correlation to business outcomes. In this session, hear how they implemented open-source Cloud Intelligence Dashboards with FOCUS (FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification) to consolidate all sources into a single framework. Learn how unit economics — "Cost per Order" across 11 brands — drove 21% monthly cost optimization with minimal engineering effort. Walk away with an open-source based playbook for multicloud FinOps that delivers measurable results at enterprise scale.

sessions.t: How Mercedes-Benz accelerates engineering and production with AI
sessions.a: Mercedes-Benz is using agentic AI on AWS to transform how vehicles are brought to life, from engineering to production. Hear how Mercedes-Benz is using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to accelerate engineering for 14,000 engineers—building specialized AI agents that reason over millions of interconnected artifacts, compressing specification generation by 90%, from 35 weeks to 3.5. On the factory floor, discover how Mercedes used AWS to build a fully cloud-native manufacturing execution system orchestrating 1M+ vehicles annually, with AI-powered quality intelligence providing rapid root-cause analysis and digital twins helping optimize throughput. Walk away with real-world lessons for deploying industrial AI at scale.

sessions.t: How Moeve turned natural language into enforced governance controls at scale
sessions.a: Organizations struggle to translate compliance requirements like GDPR or NIS2 into enforceable controls without manual policy authoring. This session features Moeve and their Governance Control AI Assistant powered by Amazon Bedrock. You see how engineers ask natural language questions and the system translates intent into SCPs, hooks, and AWS Config rules assigned at OU and account scope, validated through CI/CD and GitOps. You leave with architecture patterns, production lessons, and a practical model for AI-assisted governance at scale.

sessions.t: How Netflix auto-selects the right storage for every ML training workload
sessions.a: ML training workloads demand fast data access, but choosing between FSx Lustre, NVMe caching, and S3 direct reads is complex. At Netflix, we solved this by building an intent-driven storage layer that takes workload shape, dataset size, node count, access pattern, and automatically selects, provisions, and mounts the optimal storage engine. Our users write code once; the backend adapts transparently. In this session, we share the architecture behind our selection framework, how we built a high-throughput S3-to-NVMe hydration cache, and how you can apply the same pattern using generally available AWS storage services to reduce cost and eliminate storage guesswork.

sessions.t: How neurosymbolic AI formalizes natural language into verifiable logic
sessions.a: Organizations want to automate enforcement of critical rules—financial, legal, regulatory—yet those rules live in ambiguous natural-language documents. Bridging this gap is error-prone and expensive. In this session, we show how neurosymbolic AI enables subject-matter experts to formalize natural-language rules into mathematical logic—capturing the original intent in an unambiguous, executable, and verifiable form. We cover the mathematical foundations and demonstrate through practical examples how formalized rules can serve as agent guardrails, compliance checks, and trusted knowledge sources. Attendees will leave with a deep understanding of how neurosymbolic techniques can help them formalize and operationalize their own domain rules.

sessions.t: How Nordstrom, Coca-Cola Andina & Mondelez use agentic supply chains
sessions.a: Supply chain leaders are moving from dashboards that report problems to agents that resolve them, sensing disruption, optimizing routing, and acting in real time. Hear how three retail and CPG leaders deployed agentic AI on AWS at scale. Nordstrom built a multi-agent framework on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, starting with an agent that cut audit investigations from five weeks to thirty seconds. Coca-Cola Andina developed Miruta, a multi-agent routing solution optimizing supply chain operations across its bottling network. And Mondelez is modernizing production and distribution across 150+ countries. Each shares their architecture, what changed for their teams, and measurable results.

sessions.t: How Novartis is Using AI to Reimagine Clinical Development on AWS
sessions.a: Developing a new medicine takes 10–15 years and $2.6 billion — and the timeline is getting longer, not shorter. At Novartis, the Global Drug Development organization recognized that incremental optimization of siloed, sequential clinical processes wouldn't be enough. In this session, learn how Novartis is transforming clinical development with AWS by replacing fragmented legacy systems with a unified NextGen Data Platform. You'll also learn how Novartis stood up an Intelligent Decision System that simulates entire trial operations as a computational twin, and pioneering a collaborative Trial Design Studio where biostatisticians, clinical operations, regulatory, and medical teams co-create protocols in real time.

sessions.t: How Observability Evolved From Dashboards to Agents Writing Code (sponsored by Honeycomb)
sessions.a: Observability's real job has always been closing the feedback loop between what you ship and what happens next. We'll trace how that loop evolved at Honeycomb: from dashboards you stared at, to SLOs that quantified what mattered, to Canvas, agents that investigate with you, and now MCP tools feeding production reality straight back into software written by agents This presentation is brought to you by Honeycomb, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How Paytm powers millions of customer journeys with AI agents on AWS
sessions.a: Every Paytm customer and merchant leaves a trail—payments, transfers, loans, logins, chats, and voice conversations. Together, these events form a story. Pi Agents, Paytm's multimodal agentic platform on AWS, turns that story into action across acquisition, retention, monetization, and support for 50M+ merchants and 80M+ monthly users. A Paytm-built foundation model learns from 100B+ activity sequences, while specialized SLMs and voice models enable sub-second interactions across 10+ languages. Beyond the customer lifecycle, Pi Agents powers sales, marketing, support, and operations. This session explores how Paytm combines these models with agents to understand, decide, and act.

sessions.t: How Prime Video Built an AI-assisted Creative Suite on AWS
sessions.a: Premium animated series traditionally take 3.5 years to produce. Prime Video AI Studios built the AI-Assisted Creative Suite on AWS to compress production to under 12 months—and extend support to live-action shorts, second-unit VFX, and feature films. The suite is powered by AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and AWS Strands that select models, build creative workflows, construct prompts, and evaluate outputs. Learn how Prime Video trains and serves their first-party diffusion-model fleet on Amazon SageMaker and EKS, running on Amazon EC2 P6 GPU clusters for production-grade throughput and latency.

sessions.t: How Rail Operators Are Using Agentic AI to Improve Service Reliability (sponsored by PwC)
sessions.a: Many organizations successfully pilot generative AI but struggle to scale adoption. Rail operators worldwide are now exploring how agentic AI can transform mission-critical operations and improve service reliability. Deutsche Bahn (DB) and Norfolk Southern are among the organizations leading this journey. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, they are transforming rail operations through AI agents embedded into the systems that support daily operations across their transportation networks. The solution combines AI agents and human oversight to automate incident resolution, support operations teams, and improve service reliability. This session explores the journey from proof of concept to production, the governance and safety guardrails required for adoption, and how lighthouse programs are becoming blueprints for enterprise-wide agentic process transformation. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How Ramp tracks and governs AI spend down to the team, model, and API key
sessions.a: When AI token spend spans multiple providers and dozens of teams, knowing who spent what, on which model, and whether it's COGS or OpEx requires its own pipeline. We'll cover ingesting usage data from third-party AI APIs, processing with Temporal workers, persisting on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, running on Amazon ECS Fargate, and surfacing anomalies before they hit your invoice. See how Ramp attributes spend by provider, model, team, and API key, and attributes cost down to the request-level when teams connect their router, gateway, or internal data. Learn how Ramp separates COGS from OpEx for accurate unit economics, then closes the loop with governance.

sessions.t: How Santander governs hundreds of AI agents in production on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Financial institutions need a consistent way for independent teams to build, deploy, and govern AI agents without creating silos or losing visibility. In this session, learn how Banco Santander built Santander Cortex—a self-service platform where business teams configure, deploy, and monitor their own AI agents with tools, knowledge bases, memory, guardrails, and authorization using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We'll cover identity integration, agent-to-agent (A2A) interoperability across independently owned teams, and the governance model that made self-service possible without losing control. The platform runs hundreds of agents, including customer-facing chatbots serving millions of users across more than 10 countries.

sessions.t: How SCHUFA strengthened security operations with AWS Security Hub
sessions.a: Across complex cloud environments, security teams must sift through a growing volume of signals to prioritize the risks that matter most. AWS Security Hub correlates these signals across AWS and multicloud environments to surface critical attack paths and help you respond at scale. Hear firsthand from SCHUFA, Germany's main credit scoring agency, on how they adopted Security Hub to streamline security operations under strict regulatory requirements. We'll also dive into the latest capabilities, including multicloud visibility, enhanced risk correlation, AI-powered detections, and visibility into AI workloads.

sessions.t: How Securian Uses Agentic AI to Prioritize CIO Investments (sponsored by PwC)
sessions.a: CIOs face a question: where should they invest next to strengthen technology capabilities? Securian Financial Group and PwC built an agentic AI Capability Maturity Measurement Instrument (CMMI) engine using Amazon Quick that turns evidence into a repeatable view of capability gaps, investment priorities, and recommendations across 20 IT domains and 2,000+ capability criteria. The solution ingests documents and surveys, applies consistent scoring, and translates results into prioritized actions spanning skills, resources, processes, and tools. Learn how Securian moved from periodic, manual assessments to an on-demand decision engine that helps technology leaders' direct investment where it matters most. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How SoCalGas De-Risked a SAP Migration with Agentic AI on AWS (sponsored by Accenture)
sessions.a: SoCalGas is migrating its decades-old Customer Information System to SAP IS-U, where hypercare is the highest-risk phase for customer and regulatory impacts. Traditional command centers require teams to manually correlate signals across ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, dashboards, logs, and staffing systems, slowing response times. To improve visibility and decision making, Accenture built a multi-agent AI command center on Amazon Bedrock. A Commander agent orchestrates Platform Health, Business KPI, Knowledge, and Situational Awareness agents, while every recommendation is citation-grounded and human-supervised. Learn how agentic AI is helping SoCalGas unify operational intelligence in a mission-critical utility environment. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How startups ship faster with Kiro
sessions.a: Startups live and die by velocity. Small teams, big ambitions, and no time to waste. In this session, hear how fast-moving startups are using Kiro to punch above their weight: turning ideas into working software with spec-driven and agentic development, keeping a lean team focused on product instead of boilerplate, and shipping features that would normally demand far more engineers. We'll describe real patterns startups use to move from concept to production quickly, and share practical takeaways any team can apply. Whether you're a founder, an early engineer, or scaling quickly, learn how agentic development helps small teams build big.

sessions.t: How Stripe built an enterprise agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.a: Operating global payments infrastructure requires AI that is secure, reliable, and scalable across internal and customer-facing experiences. Learn how Stripe built a shared agent platform for Kai, its company-wide AI coworker, and hundreds of other AI workflows. Stripe will share how it integrated Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter with its existing infrastructure, data-access controls, and security model. Discover the architectural decisions that helped Stripe move rapidly from prototype to company-wide adoption, supporting more than 10,000 employees and nearly 500,000 Kai sessions each week.

sessions.t: How T&C Empowers Partners to Build AI-Ready Teams and Drive Customer Impact?
sessions.a: Join this session to discover how AWS Training and Certification empowers partners to transform their workforce through strategic AI skills development. A partner shares their firsthand journey of designing AI learning pathways, implementing gamification that drove engagement at scale, and building sustainable certification programs tied to measurable business outcomes. You'll see how T&C enables this transformation, from foundational cloud fluency through advanced GenAI and Agentic AI readiness and leave with a concrete action plan to accelerate AI readiness across your teams.

sessions.t: How TeleTracking runs AWS at a 30:1 ratio with Grafana Cloud AI (sponsored by Grafana Labs)
sessions.a: TeleTracking's platform is air traffic control for hospitals: 200K+ beds and 100+ command centers depend on it. Re-platforming onto an AI-native foundation has taken its service-to-engineer ratio from 6:1 to 30:1. The lever isn't headcount: It’s relying on one agent to pair gcx and the Grafana Cloud MCP server with AWS MCP tooling. Oren Lion replays an MSK incident where Grafana Assistant identified a cluster-wide broker disruption in minutes, pairing Frontend Observability with Amazon CloudFront to line up what hurt with what changed. He closes with Assistant Investigations, read-only guardrails, and a recipe you can run yourself.. This presentation is brought to you by Grafana Labs, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How the Air Force defends DoD workloads with Amazon Bedrock Agents
sessions.a: AWS built STORMS with the Air Force SOC to defend DoD workloads across AWS accounts in multiple Organizations - pairing centralized security telemetry and one-click containment with a multi-agent Amazon Bedrock system that analyzes logs, answers analyst questions, and executes containment actions.

sessions.t: How the most advanced teams manage the full SDLC on an agentic stack (sponsored by Cursor)
sessions.a: This 201 technical deep dive covers the AI Software Development Lifecycle featuring the Grok product family. SpaceXAI experts and customers in production will demo proven patterns, covering which parts of the SDLC to delegate to agents first, how to structure review and testing when agents write most of the code, and where the Grok API and Grok Voice fit a production workflow. This presentation is brought to you by Cursor, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How to assess your environment to migrate & modernize with confidence
sessions.a: Without a clear picture of what's running in your environment, teams carry forward outdated assumptions, inherit unplanned tech debt, and miss the fastest path to value. Assessment is the foundational step that sets everything else up for success. Learn how to go hands-on with AWS Transform, an agentic assessment experience that delivers results fast, or work with AWS specialists and partners who leverage this technology alongside decades of migration experience. Use assessment data to make informed decisions, optimize environments, and eliminate redundant licensing.

sessions.t: How to build an autonomous compliance environment auditors trust
sessions.a: Auditors want evidence, not promises. Learn how to always keep your AWS environment audit-ready; continuously producing the proof auditors need, without manual intervention. Across services such as AWS Config, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Security Hub and more, we walk through an architecture that automatically collects evidence, maps it to your control frameworks, checks whether the collected evidence meets control requirements, identifies gaps and delivers prescriptive remediation guidance on how to close. We close by exploring how AI is reshaping continuous compliance and audit readiness.

sessions.t: How to Build Autonomous Enterprise Agents with SOPs using Kiro and Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.a: Enterprise operations hit a limitation when humans can't keep up with the volume of exceptions in ERP systems like SAP which is solved by autonomous AI agents. In this session, learn how to build production agents by writing SOPs in natural language. We'll cover how to write SOPs that let agents exercise judgment while embedding guardrails. A single SOP becomes a deployable agent, and this pattern scales across different business processes. Using Kiro's spec-driven development and Strands agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, partners own the full agent lifecycle and differentiate by layering domain expertise and industry-specific IP into SOPs. Walk away with hands-on experience building the agentic architecture that enables autonomous enterprise operations for your customers.

sessions.t: How to Build Omni-Channel AI Agents with Twilio + AWS (sponsored by Twilio)
sessions.a: Orchestrating AI conversations across channels requires more than just connecting APIs. Learn how to build agents that understand context, respond instantly, and adapt to channel constraints. Explore Twilio Agent Connect and Amazon Bedrock integration patterns, plus the operational playbook for deploying engagement AI at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Twilio, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How to decompose Oracle and SQL Server into purpose-built databases
sessions.a: A monolithic traditional RDBMS databases serves transactions, reporting, and search, but serves none of them well. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard how to decompose a proprietary database into purpose-built layers on AWS, including Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for transactional workloads, Aurora pgvector for semantic search and GenAI (RAG), and Amazon Redshift via zero-ETL for real-time analytics, for a smarter modernization approach. We'll walk through how this pattern eliminates licensing costs, removes ETL pipelines, and turns your operational data into an AI-ready platform. Come ready to whiteboard your decomposition use case.

sessions.t: How to Deploy Purpose-Built Clinical AI Agents to Production with Speed and Scale
sessions.a: Providers lose hours daily to documentation, manual coding, and admin work. Leading health IT builders are solving this with purpose-built AI on AWS. In this chalk talk, Innovaccer joins AWS to share how they trained task-specific clinical small language models that deliver consistent outputs where general-purpose LLMs produce unacceptable variance. We use their architecture as a jumping-off point to discuss the full spectrum of paths to production: custom model training on accelerated compute, multi-step agentic workflow orchestration, and embedding fully managed clinical AI capabilities into existing applications.

sessions.t: How to improve your security and governance maturity and prove it to your auditor
sessions.a: With so many security best practices available, knowing what to do first is a challenge. In this session, you learn how to use the AWS Security Maturity Model to systematically identify and prioritize security improvements for your AWS workloads through a phased approach. You discover how to extend your governance capabilities to manage security consistently across multi-cloud environments. Finally, you see how automatic evidence collection helps you continuously demonstrate compliance to auditors, turning security posture into provable assurance.

sessions.t: How to plan a post-quantum migration strategy
sessions.a: Post-quantum migrations can succeed when both the technical and organizational paths are clear. This session delivers a governance-first framework for CISOs and senior technology leaders to drive an organization-wide post-quantum migration. You'll learn how to build executive alignment, establish migration governance, set priorities across business units, and create accountability structures that scale. Learn how AWS is deploying PQ algorithms across our services and how the shared responsibility model applies to this transition. Walk away with a leadership playbook to position your organization ahead of NIST and CNSA 2.0 regulatory timelines.

sessions.t: How to run parallel coding agents without sitting in the loop (sponsored by Cursor)
sessions.a: Running multiple coding agents in parallel can increase throughput, but only if technical leads and engineers avoid being pulled into every agent’s execution loop. Join this session to learn how Grok Bot is an orchestration layer for technical knowledge work, coordinating workflows while saving time and mitigating costs. Through live demos, see Grok Bot operate from its own VM and browser, maintain authenticated tool access, monitor usage, and provision cloud agents on demand. We’ll be joined by a customer in production as well as SpaceXAI engineers as they share the workflows they run today. This presentation is brought to you by Cursor, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How to solve for multicloud identity lifecycle management
sessions.a: Organizations operating in multiple clouds face a compounding multi-cloud identity lifecycle governance challenge. How do you provision, manage, audit, and decommission identities when each cloud provider enforces different authorization models, attribute schemas, and lifecycle hooks? In this session National Institute Health (NIH), a federal research organization, describe how they leverage a centralized identity governance platform to provision identities and entitlements across AWS and Microsoft Azure. You will learn how to avoid governance divergence, and design identity lifecycles where access reviews, birthright provisioning, and decommissioning work consistently - regardless of which cloud the identity lands in.

sessions.t: How to think about NUMA: Optimizing AI inference on EC2
sessions.a: Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) topology shapes how every byte of model weight reaches a compute core, and misalignment silently costs throughput. This session explains why NUMA matters for memory locality when running models on EC2, and what changes across Graviton-, Intel-, and AMD-based instances. CPU inference requires deliberate alignment of threads to data, especially as SIMD and AMX instructions amplify memory bandwidth demands per core. Even on GPU instances, host-side NUMA affects preprocessing and KV cache offload. Understand your hardware topology and leverage it to get the most from your inference workloads.

sessions.t: How to use AI to develop and deploy controls from your internal policies
sessions.a: You maintain internal security policies but turning them into implemented, risk-prioritized controls could be manual and slow. This lightning talk demonstrates how to use Kiro to develop and deploy controls at scale across three layers. Preventive controls that block non-compliant actions, detective controls that identify violations and trigger remediation, and proactive controls that validate configurations before deployment. You leave with a practical approach to using AI to accelerate the entire control lifecycle from policy to enforcement.

sessions.t: How Vanguard Scales AI Oversight Without Scaling Human Review (sponsored by Capgemini)
sessions.a: Human review can't scale linearly with generative-AI volume. Vanguard's AI Center of Excellence built a closed-loop oversight system where every AI response is scored by an LLM-as-judge, confirmed or overturned by a subject-matter expert, and routed through a confusion matrix: confirmed catches sharpen the agent, disagreements calibrate the judge. Each SME label grows a benchmark that resets how much oversight the next cycle needs, proving mathematically that coverage can fall while risk holds flat. Built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Lambda-hosted detector SLMs, SQS, DynamoDB, and SageMaker, the loop moves toward real-time interruption of harmful responses before customers see them. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: How WBD Became the First Media Company to Go Agentic Across AdTech
sessions.a: Buying and selling media has long been manual, constrained by legacy systems and fragmented tools. Warner Bros. Discovery is changing that. As the first media company to integrate agentic AI workflows into every system across the media lifecycle, WBD is leapfrogging the competition by embedding autonomous agents at every step: planning, forecasting, optimization, and measurement. Built on AWS, this converged platform makes linear TV as addressable and measurable as digital. Learn how WBD and AWS are replacing decades of manual process with self improving agents that drive precision, yield, and entirely new monetization models at scale.

sessions.t: How Workday built multicloud data interoperability foundation for Agentic AI
sessions.a: As enterprises scale agentic AI, the hardest problem is often giving agents secure, governed access to data spread across multiple clouds. Physically copying the data between clouds introduces cost, latency, and governance risk. In this session, you will learn how Workday leverages Apache Iceberg catalog federation to build bidirectional, zero-copy integration that enables cross-cloud data access without duplicating or moving data. You will see how this open standard based approach lets AI agents reason over trusted enterprise data in place, with governance and business context preserved.

sessions.t: Hugging Face on AWS: AI Model Deployment at Scale
sessions.a: AWS and Hugging Face collaborate on open source Deep Learning Containers, optimized inference frameworks, and Neuron integrations that make deploying community models production-ready. This session covers the open source stack - from Transformers library optimizations for Graviton and Trainium to TGI container contributions - that enables customers to serve Hugging Face models at 50% lower cost. Learn deployment patterns used by enterprises running open weight LLMs at millions of requests per day.

sessions.t: Human+AI Collaboration: How Amazon Deploys Autonomous Operations on AWS
sessions.a: Amazon deploys humanoids, autonomous mobile robots, and humans as a unified workforce operating side-by-side on the fulfillment floor. Learn how Amazon evolved an AI-powered verification pipeline, built with Amazon Nova on Bedrock to validate 200K+ items, into a fleet orchestration platform dispatching foundation-model inference across humanoids, quadrupeds, AMRs, and drones. We deep-dive into the architectural patterns enabling humans to work alongside robots at scale: a serverless Lambda backend that abstracts the robot form factor, multi-vendor humanoid integration, and edge deployment strategies. You'll leave with a framework for physical AI orchestration of heterogeneous fleets while optimizing throughput and cost.

sessions.t: Human search to agent retrieval: Rearchitecting with OpenSearch Service
sessions.a: Agents don't search like humans. They fire hundreds of sub-queries per task, maintain stateful memory across sessions, and demand, verified answers before taking action. Traditional search architectures weren't built for this, and at agent scale, latency budgets compress, relevance requirements compound, and retrieval failures cascade into hallucinated outputs. In this session, we walk you through how the shift from human search to agent retrieval is reshaping infrastructure requirements and how the latest capabilities in Amazon OpenSearch Service help you address these unique challenges. You'll leave with a clear understanding of what's changing, why it matters, and how to get started.

sessions.t: Hybrid Kubernetes made simple: EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway for on-prem and edge AI
sessions.a: Enterprises are migrating from legacy hypervisors to Kubernetes-native stacks but need hybrid connectivity without complex network changes. In this builder session, attendees set up the newly launched Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway to seamlessly connect on-premises worker nodes to a cloud EKS control plane without modifying existing network infrastructure. They deploy an AI inference workload spanning cloud and edge, configure pod-to-pod communication across environments, implement data residency controls, and validate failover scenarios.

sessions.t: I didn't know AWS WAF did this
sessions.a: Think AWS WAF is just for blocking SQL injection and XSS? Think again. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll dive into creative, real-world use cases - from deploying honeypots and shedding traffic, to stopping account fraud and mitigating DDoS at scale. We'll explore advanced configurations, walk through customer-tested patterns, and whiteboard strategies that make WAF a powerful tool in your security arsenal. Bring your questions and experiences - we're here to break the "WAF does that?" moments together.

sessions.t: I didn't know AWS WAF did this
sessions.a: Think AWS WAF is just for blocking SQL injection and XSS? Think again. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll dive into creative, real-world use cases - from deploying honeypots and shedding traffic, to stopping account fraud and mitigating DDoS at scale. We'll explore advanced configurations, walk through customer-tested patterns, and whiteboard strategies that make WAF a powerful tool in your security arsenal. Bring your questions and experiences - we're here to break the "WAF does that?" moments together.

sessions.t: I didn't know my AI agent was doing that!
sessions.a: AI agents are non-deterministic - they can burn tokens, stall, or drift into wrong behaviour with no warning, and teams often have no visibility until something breaks. In this hands-on builders session, you will use Amazon CloudWatch to observe live agents from both the console and your IDE: trace what an agent actually did, spot failures, and surface anomalous behaviour. Working with real agents - a production agent and a custom chatbot - you build the detection and alerting yourself and leave able to apply it to the agents you run in production.

sessions.t: I didn't know my AI agent was doing that!

Working with real agents - a production agent and a custom chatbot - you build the detection and alerting yourself and leave able to apply it to the agents you run in production.

sessions.t: Implement AI agent safety controls with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.a: Scaling AI agents into production without safety controls creates compliance, cost, and operational risk for financial services organizations. In this workshop, build an agent safety control system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Starting with a deployed agent, configure three signal pipelines: observability via Amazon AgentCore Observability and Amazon CloudWatch; cost monitoring with AWS Budgets; and Amazon AgentCore Runtime Evaluation for behavioral deviation detection. Then build an admin control panel that aggregates alerts and enables human-in-the-loop interventions including session termination and fine-grained authorization via Cedar policies. Leave with a proven approach you can replicate to deliver responsible, governed AI agents at scale.

sessions.t: Implement AI agent safety controls with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.a: Scaling AI agents into production without safety controls creates compliance, cost, and operational risk for financial services organizations. In this workshop, build an agent safety control system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Starting with a deployed agent, configure three signal pipelines: observability via Amazon AgentCore Observability and Amazon CloudWatch; cost monitoring with AWS Budgets; and Amazon AgentCore Runtime Evaluation for behavioral deviation detection. Then build an admin control panel that aggregates alerts and enables human-in-the-loop interventions including session termination and fine-grained authorization via Cedar policies. Leave with a proven approach you can replicate to deliver responsible, governed AI agents at scale.

sessions.t: Implement governance guardrails for autonomous AI agents at scale
sessions.a: Your AI agents need permissions to be useful, but unconstrained permissions can lead to unintended consequences. In this workshop, you will build a defense-in-depth governance framework for agentic workloads. You will create scoped IAM execution roles with permissions boundaries, enforce mandatory Bedrock Guardrails via IAM policy-based enforcement, validate agent policies with IAM Access Analyzer, and implement Cedar-based deterministic enforcement in AgentCore. You will leave with a deployable pattern that constrains agent behavior without blocking legitimate actions.

sessions.t: Implementing agentic AI solutions on-premises and at the edge
sessions.a: Learn how to extend Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to hybrid and edge services like AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones to build distributed agentic apps using Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication with on-prem data. Get hands-on with hybrid agentic AI using Amazon Bedrock and Strands Agents while exploring AWS hybrid and edge solutions for data residency compliance.

sessions.t: Implementing agentic AI solutions on-premises and at the edge
sessions.a: Learn how to extend Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to hybrid and edge services like AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones to build distributed agentic apps using Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication with on-prem data. Get hands-on with hybrid agentic AI using Amazon Bedrock and Strands Agents while exploring AWS hybrid and edge solutions for data residency compliance.

sessions.t: Implement semantic caching for AI agents using ElastiCache for Valkey
sessions.a: Semantic caching uses vector similarity search to retrieve cached LLM responses for semantically equivalent queries, reducing inference latency and cost in agentic AI architectures. In this session, dive deep into implementing semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, covering embedding generation, similarity scoring, and relevance threshold tuning. Explore advanced production patterns including per-user cache namespacing for personalized responses, tenant isolation strategies to prevent cross-tenant data leakage, and techniques for validating that cached responses remain contextually appropriate for incoming queries at scale. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Improving operations with agentic AI
sessions.a: Your operational telemetry is growing faster than your team. Learn how agentic AI can work across your observability stack, correlating metrics, logs, and traces to detect issues, identify root cause, and initiate remediation without waiting for a human to connect the dots. Explore patterns for agents that triage alerts, reduce noise, surface actionable insights, and execute operational runbooks. See how to integrate agents into your monitoring and incident response workflows, from signal detection through resolution. Leave with practical approaches to reduce mean time to recovery, eliminate repetitive toil, and give your team time to focus on reliability improvements that matter.

sessions.t: Improving your database agility with Amazon FSx
sessions.a: Customers self-manage databases on AWS to maintain full control over architecture, functionality, availability, and performance. Amazon FSx provides the high-performance, highly available storage they need to do this at scale. This workshop will whiteboard production architectures for self-managed databases on Linux and Windows using Amazon FSx for OpenZFS, NetApp ONTAP, and Windows File Server. Learn how to architect for high performance and high availability, implement zero-copy snapshots and clones for rapid database refresh, and accelerate backup and recovery. Whether you run Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, or PostgreSQL, bring your architecture questions.

sessions.t: Incident Response Tabletop: Supply Chain
sessions.a: Join the "Supply Chain Incident Response" tabletop exercise, where executive leaders tackle supply chain disruptions in a realistic, interactive simulation. Collaborate to develop and execute strategies for managing crises, explore decision-making and risk assessment, and enhance communication skills. This exercise strengthens your organization's preparedness and resilience, helping you safeguard operations and improve response capabilities. Build robust strategies to handle and recover from supply chain disruptions effectively.

sessions.t: In-Country HPC: How TGS Processes Seismic Data on AWS Brazil
sessions.a: TGS -- one of the world's largest multi-client geoscience data providers -- faced a significant cost challenge running its business-critical Rackmon EFWI GPU workload at scale. By strategically deploying this workload on AWS infrastructure in Brazil, TGS leveraged Brazil's ReData Special Tax Regime to dramatically reduce the tax burden on GPU-intensive seismic processing. The result: material cost savings on one of the most computationally demanding workloads in the energy industry -- and a reusable in-country processing architecture that can serve future customers with data residency requirements in other geographies.

sessions.t: In-Country HPC: How TGS Processes Seismic Data on AWS Brazil
sessions.a: TGS -- one of the world's largest multi-client geoscience data providers -- faced a significant cost challenge running its business-critical Rackmon EFWI GPU workload at scale. sessions.t: Innovate faster, stay compliant: Innovation Sandbox for financial services
sessions.a: Financial services organizations need to experiment fast while meeting regulatory and governance requirements. In this chalk talk, explore how organizations deploy Innovation Sandbox on AWS to give teams safe, ephemeral environments without compromising security posture. We’ll discuss real-world patterns for network isolation, automated guardrails via SCPs, and time-bound account lifecycles that satisfy risk committees and regulators. We’ll walk through how organizations balance developer autonomy with controls mapped to frameworks like SR 26-2 and OCC heightened standards, and you’ll leave with practical approaches for rolling out Innovation Sandbox on AWS while keeping compliance teams confident.

sessions.t: Innovating with agentic AI inside Amazon, powered by AgentCore
sessions.a: Amazon runs thousands of AI agents internally, built on the same AgentCore platform available to every AWS customer. Teams across the company have replaced manual workflows with agents that act autonomously, cutting process times from weeks to hours and eliminating thousands of lines of custom orchestration code. This session brings together the Amazon builders behind these transformations to share the AgentCore capabilities that made it possible, the failure modes they hit at scale, and the design patterns that separate agents that demo well from agents that survive production. Every pattern discussed is one you can adopt today.

sessions.t: Innovation in Identity Security: How We Protect the Cloud & Help You Do It Too
sessions.a: Learn how AWS approaches identity as the foundation of cloud security - both protecting AWS infrastructure and enabling customers to operate securely at scale. Explore how AWS innovates in access management and develops prescriptive, service-specific guidance helping organizations adopt services confidently, drives secure-by-default authorization across 300+ services, and ensures IAM policies work predictably. Millennium Partners will share how they use AWS guidance and threat modeling to evaluate new services, strengthen their security posture, and give developers freedom to innovate faster.

sessions.t: Inside Amazon EKS: the resilient foundation for critical workloads
sessions.a: Real-time financial systems, large-scale AI, and mission-critical platforms run on Kubernetes, and they demand a robust engineering foundation. This session goes under the hood of what makes Amazon EKS the backbone for the most demanding workloads. See how cellular isolation contains blast radius and EKS Provisioned Control Planes eliminate downtime during peak operational periods, backed by an industry-leading SLA as clusters scale into large fleets. Learn how EKS Auto Mode integrates with Application Recovery Controller zonal shift to protect the control plane and running pods during an impaired Availability Zone, keeping critical applications available with no extra configuration.

sessions.t: Inside Amazon S3: How a one-page design reached planetary scale
sessions.a: When Amazon S3 launched in 2006, its design requirements fit one page: scalable, reliable, fast, inexpensive, simple, with no single points of failure. The system was built to treat component failure as normal and use scale as an advantage. Today those founding principles describe an architecture serving hundreds of millions of requests per second across tens of millions of drives, maintaining eleven nines of durability while shipping features without downtime. Hear S3 principal engineers trace the decisions from single host to strong consistency at global scale, how formal methods verify correctness, and how the team balances innovation with operational safety.

sessions.t: Inside Amazon S3 Vectors: architecture and cost optimization for vector search
sessions.a: Vector embeddings power everything from semantic search to RAG, but running them at scale often means high infrastructure costs and operational overhead. In this session, go inside the architecture of Amazon S3 Vectors to see how it delivers vector search at up to 90% lower cost than specialized alternatives, with support for up to 2 billion vectors per index. We'll whiteboard the indexing approach that makes this possible, then explore recent enhancements, including a 100x increase in the per-query search result limit and reduced query pricing, and what they mean for your application's performance and cost.

sessions.t: Inside Amazon S3 Vectors: architecture and cost optimization for vector search
sessions.a: Vector embeddings power everything from semantic search to RAG, but running them at scale often means high infrastructure costs and operational overhead. In this session, go inside the architecture of Amazon S3 Vectors to see how it delivers vector search at up to 90% lower cost than specialized alternatives, with support for up to 2 billion vectors per index. We'll whiteboard the indexing approach that makes this possible, then explore recent enhancements, including a 100x increase in the per-query search result limit and reduced query pricing, and what they mean for your application's performance and cost.

sessions.t: Inside AWS Trainium3: Hardware innovations for better AI economics
sessions.a: What does it take to build a chip purpose-made for AI? In this deep dive, we explore Trainium3 architecture innovations: NeuronCore innovations that delivers higher TFLOPs, hardware-accelerated quantization, softmax acceleration, near-memory compute and Mixture-of-Experts optimizations. We'll share micro-benchmark data showing how these choices translate to real performance for Mixture-of-Experts and other demanding workloads. At the system level, we examine the Trn3 UltraServer family, scaling from 32 to 144 chips via NeuronLink fabric to enables up to 4.4x more performance. Leave with a deep understanding of how to evaluate and leverage purpose-built AI Chips for your AI workloads.

sessions.t: Inside Bayer’s AI agent: Interpretability as governance (sponsored by Thoughtworks)
sessions.a: Enterprise AI governance has focused on controls around agents—identity, permissions, sandboxing, and audit trails. But what happens inside the model? This session explores a live production system: Bayer’s PRINCE research assistant, built with Thoughtworks on AWS to give researchers access to 18,000+ preclinical study reports. We’ll share how Thoughtworks’ AI Research Labs applies mechanistic interpretability research, published at ICML, NeurIPS, and AAAI, to understand why the assistant answers, cites, or refuses queries. See how sparse autoencoders identify internal circuits behind refusal, how targeted steering changes behavior without retraining, and why this matters in regulated environments. Leave with a practical framework for making interpretability a core component of AI governance. This presentation is brought to you by Thoughtworks, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Inside NKI: How AWS designed a kernel language for peak AI performance
sessions.a: What does a kernel language need to unlock peak performance on Trainium, AWS purpose built AI chips to deliver better price performance? The AWS Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) is a Python-embedded DSL that goes beyond framework-level abstractions, giving developers direct access to Trainium's three-level memory hierarchy and four compute engines. Explore the design choices that enable hardware-level optimization, dissect production kernels powering FlashAttention variants, MoE routing, and on-device collectives, and debate where tile-based languages converge or diverge across accelerator architectures. Discover how NKI extends to support MXFP8 and disaggregated inference, and leave equipped to write custom, hardware-optimized kernels.

sessions.t: Inside Real AI Software Factories: Lessons From the Teams Building Them (sponsored by LaunchDarkly)
sessions.a: Everyone's talking about AI software factories. Far fewer have actually built one. In this panel, engineering leaders, partners, and teams putting agents into production go past the hype to the real work: where agents accelerate delivery, where they break, and what it takes to keep humans in control as autonomy scales. Expect specifics, not theory—what worked, what didn't, and what they'd do differently. Whether you're experimenting with coding agents or scaling toward autonomous delivery, you'll leave with practical patterns for building a factory that's genuinely fast and safe. Join us for an honest conversation about engineering at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by LaunchDarkly, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Inside the Agentic Engineering Org of the Future (sponsored by Harness)
sessions.a: What does it actually take to become an AI-native engineering organization? A senior technology executive from a Fortune 500 enterprise sits down with Harness Field CTO Nick Durkin to talk through what it's really taken to go all in on agentic software delivery, orchestrating agents across the entire SDLC instead of one-off automations. They'll get into what that transformation actually looks like end to end, how they decide when an agent runs on its own versus when a human stays in the loop, how agentic engineering has affected cloud migration and consumption, and what it takes to do this at the scale of a Fortune 500 engineering org. This presentation is brought to you by Harness, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Inside the Architecture: Building Secure AI Applications on AWS (sponsored by TrendAI™)
sessions.a: AI is rapidly moving from experimentation to production, creating new challenges for developers, architects, and security teams. In this technical session, explore the real-world architectures enterprises use to build and secure AI applications on AWS. Learn how organizations leverage Amazon Bedrock, EKS, ECS, Security Lake, CloudTrail, and cloud-native automation to protect AI workloads, monitor risk across multi-account environments, and streamline security operations. Through practical deployment patterns and lessons learned from large-scale AWS environments, discover how to build AI applications that are secure, scalable, and production-ready. The session draws on deployment patterns described for TrendAI Vision One on AWS, including AI workload protection, cloud telemetry integration, and AWS-native architecture approaches. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Inside the Governed Agentic Software Factory at Enterprise Scale (sponsored by CloudBees)
sessions.a: Code is now abundant. AI agents now write, test and deploy code autonomously; the bottleneck has shifted from generating code to governing what reaches production. Loreli Cadapan, VP of Product at CloudBees, takes you inside the governed agentic software factories that the world’s most regulated engineering organizations are building, where every change, human or agent, is visible, auditable and accountable. The work starts after the code changes: encode existing rules as enforceable policy across your toolchain, keep humans in the loop where it matters, and ship software you can stand behind. Because you write code for a reason, and we make sure that reason becomes true.

sessions.t: Inside UK AISI: stress-testing frontier AI safety on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: The UK AI Security Institute leads global research into harmful AI capabilities, assessing frontier models for risks like offensive cybersecurity, bioweapon design, and psychological manipulation. In this talk, UK AISI representatives walk through how they built their evaluation infrastructure on Amazon Bedrock, from model access and prompt orchestration to result analysis. Hear highlights from recent research projects and the engineering decisions that make safety evaluation repeatable at scale. Leave with a clearer picture of how rigorous AI safety research runs in production on AWS.

sessions.t: Inside Zeta Global's open lakehouse architecture on AWS
sessions.a: Are you building a data lakehouse and wondering how others have approached the same challenges? Go behind the scenes of a real AWS customer data architecture. Zeta Global's AI Marketing Platform serves thousands of clients using 245 million consumer profiles, but mutli-hour data lag times and rising per-tenant costs were limiting growth. Learn how Zeta built an open streaming lakehouse with Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon EMR, and Amazon MSK that processes 10 TB daily across 10,000+ Apache Iceberg tables, cutting time-to-insight from hours to minutes while maximizing multi-tenant infrastructure efficiency at scale.

sessions.t: Instant Play Demos on Twitch – Increasing Player Engagement
sessions.a: From game build to live campaign - we'll dive deep into the best practices and constraints around launching Instant Play Demos on Twitch, powered by Amazon GameLift Streams. This innovative approach to game marketing gives you the ability to reach potential players and let them try your game before they buy it. No downloads or installs required - just a web browser and internet connection. We'll discuss what kind of content makes for a good demo and engine-specific best practices for generating compatible builds. We'll show you the benefits of launching a campaign and how they perform compared to traditional marketing channels.

sessions.t: Instrument a service with OpenTelemetry
sessions.a: In this live demo, we take an uninstrumented service from zero observability to correlated metrics, logs, and traces in minutes using Open Telemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Walk through the shortest path to production-grade instrumentation: SDK configuration, collector setup, signal routing, and surfacing the first actionable insight.

sessions.t: Integrate Agents with MCP Servers and Tools using AgentCore Gateway
sessions.a: Your agent may handle basic conversations well, but to take real-world actions it needs access to external tools and APIs. In this hands-on lab, use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to expose Lambda functions as MCP-compatible tools with JWT authorization. Register tool targets, connect to a pre-deployed nutrition coach agent, and validate how it dynamically discovers and invokes new capabilities at runtime without redeployment.

sessions.t: Integrating AI agents with event-driven architectures
sessions.a: Most multi-agent systems start with direct API calls between agents—then debugging becomes impossible, one slow agent blocks the chain, and replaying a failed workflow means re-running everything. In this chalk talk, discuss why event-driven patterns solve these coordination problems and how to design multi-agent systems using EventBridge for routing, human-in-the-loop controls that pause and resume agent actions via events, and compute selection—such as Lambda, Fargate, or AgentCore—based on your agent's execution profile. Bring architecture questions; we'll whiteboard patterns for decoupling agents across domains without sacrificing observability.

sessions.t: Integrating AI agents with event-driven architectures
sessions.a: Most multi-agent systems start with direct API calls between agents—then debugging becomes impossible, one slow agent blocks the chain, and replaying a failed workflow means re-running everything. In this chalk talk, discuss why event-driven patterns solve these coordination problems and how to design multi-agent systems using EventBridge for routing, human-in-the-loop controls that pause and resume agent actions via events, and compute selection—such as Lambda, Fargate, or AgentCore—based on your agent's execution profile. Bring architecture questions; we'll whiteboard patterns for decoupling agents across domains without sacrificing observability.

sessions.t: Intelligent Co-Sell in Action
sessions.a: A new generation of agentic capabilities now works alongside AWS Partners at every stage of the deal—anticipating the next move, cutting the busywork, and surfacing opportunity right where sellers already work. This high-energy demo session follows a deal from first opportunity to proven outcome.

sessions.t: Intelligent Co-Sell: Removing Friction and Empowering Customer Conversations
sessions.a: AWS Partners are moving faster than ever—into new regions, new AI-native solution categories, and more complex deal structures—while manual selling processes haven't kept pace. This session reveals how a new generation of AI agents handles the work that used to slow deals down: surfacing co-sell intelligence and funding eligibility in the tools Partners already use. See how intelligent co-sell gives Partners more time selling, bigger and more repeatable deals, and proof of impact that compounds.

sessions.t: Intent-Based Access Control for AI Agents that Actually Do Things (sponsored by WorkOS)
sessions.a: Agent permissions offer two bad options: approve every action manually, or skip permissions and trust the prompt. Auto-approve protects your laptop; it won't stop an agent from deleting a thousand CRM records. Roles and scopes suit static users, not agents whose next action depends on the last prompt. This session introduces Intent-Based Access Control (IBAC), where the agent's intent, not a pre-assigned role, is the unit of permission. WorkOS built Airlock on it: mission-bound tokens, every call evaluated against intent, decisions resolving to allow, deny, or escalate. Live demo across Gmail and Linear, including a blocked exfiltration and real-time human approval. This presentation is brought to you by WorkOS, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Introducing AWS Context: Build governed intelligence for agents at scale
sessions.a: AI agents need to understand what your data means, how it connects, and which definitions and rules apply to each use case. AWS Context automatically builds a governed knowledge graph by unifying structured and unstructured data, managed knowledge bases, and technical and business metadata from AWS and third-party sources. This shared foundation grounds agents in your organization’s data, business rules, relationships, and domain knowledge. In this session, dive into the reference architecture and learn best practices for integrating agents with AWS Context, including considerations for identity management, workload sizing, and production deployments.

sessions.t: Inverting the medallion: Serving reads without hitting Gold
sessions.a: Most teams default to Gold as the serving layer. For regulated systems-of-record like health data stores, ledgers, compliance archives, that's rarely the right choice. They're built for durability and interoperability, not production read traffic. The inverted pattern writes promote up the medallion, reads come from purpose-built Silver projections and Gold holds contractual semantics and never serves directly. In this chalk talk, work through change-data-capture synthesis without source support, write/read path splitting, and a routing gateway developers can't bypass. Bring your most painful regulated read path. Leave knowing when to invert, how to scope projections, and what your gateway must enforce.

sessions.t: Investigating AI Threats: Extending IR to the Generative AI Layer
sessions.a: As organizations adopt generative AI on AWS, security teams need to extend their investigation capabilities into the AI layer. In this hands-on workshop, participants work through a realistic multi-phase incident — tracing a compromised credential from initial exposure through privilege escalation into Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases and AI agents. Using GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, and Athena, you'll reconstruct the full attack chain and walk away with the skills to detect, investigate, and respond when threat actors pivot from traditional cloud resources into generative AI workloads.

sessions.t: It's live. Now what? Operating AI on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Your AI workload is live, and now you own it: latency creeping up, costs outgrowing usage, and no line from spend to teams. Start with the metrics that matter on Amazon Bedrock: time to first token, latency, throttles, and cache tokens. Then learn why latency alone cannot tell you what broke, and how output tokens per second separates a slower model from a longer answer. Also learn why throttling starts before you reach your quota. Finally, attribute token spend to teams using request metadata and caller identity. Leave with an instrumentation checklist and the alarms worth paging on.

sessions.t: Java to Graviton: three migration tools, one decision tree
sessions.a: There are now three ways to migrate Java from x86 to Graviton. AWS Transform Custom runs at scale across hundreds of repos with managed CI/CD and validation. The open-source Java skill runs locally in any agentic IDE, no AWS credentials needed. The Arm MCP server (in Kiro) goes broader, covering non-Java languages and general x86-to-Arm patterns. Each fits a different team size, repo count, and migration timeline. We demo all three on the same codebase, show where each succeeds and where it hands off, and give you a decision framework so you pick the right tool before you start.

sessions.t: Journey to Post Quantum (PQ) Authentication in AWS
sessions.a: You use certificates for identity, keys for token signing, and long-lived roots of trust. Now you need to migrate to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) for authentication. In this session, learn how AWS helps you start and stay PQ-ready while preserving backwards compatibility, performance, and AI-friendly security by default. We will demystify the present state and future trajectory of PQ authentication. We discuss the updated CNSA 2.0 dates when RSA and EC will no longer satisfy authentication requirements and the uncertainty around PQ public certificate formats and Merkle Trees in non-browser scenarios.

sessions.t: Keeping Your Lakehouse Fast: Optimization Methods for Performance & Cost (sponsored by Cloudera)
sessions.a: A common challenge with large-scale Apache Iceberg tables is keeping performance and costs under control as use and volumes grow. Optimizing tables is the solution, but it’s a tough problem to solve. As data volumes grow, querying effectively requires deliberate tuning and optimization strategies. Streaming ingestion, small files, delete files, aging metadata can gradually increase query latency and costs. In this session, you’ll learn the core optimization techniques that every Iceberg developer should understand, including partitioning, compaction, clustering, cleaning, and data skipping. You'll also learn how these techniques improve query planning and when to apply them. At the end of the session, you’ll see how these best practices can be automated using Cloudera Lakehouse Optimizer to improve performance and reduce costs. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Keep sleeping at 3am: Elastic watches your Prometheus metrics so you don't have to
sessions.a: When your kubernetes cluster fires at 3am, who's investigating? In this session we'll show Elastic Nightshift — our autonomous AI SRE — detecting a real Kubernetes incident and working it end to end: from alert to root cause to remediation, with its reasoning made transparent at every step. Nightshift draws on native Prometheus and PromQL metrics in Elastic. Kubernetes logs, out-of-the-box EKS dashboards and workflows, and ES|QL subqueries that correlate metrics with logs and traces in a single investigation. We'll also show how the 30x faster columnar metrics engine and full telemetry retention give Nightshift the complete context it needs to work like your best engineer

sessions.t: Keep your open source observability, move to managed scale
sessions.a: Teams standardized on Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch should not have to abandon their tools to get scale and lower operational overhead. In this hands-on builders session, you will learn about instrumentation and collection powered by OpenTelemetry, and explore that telemetry into managed open source services: ship metrics to PromQL in Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces in Amazon OpenSearch Service, and correlate all signals in Amazon Managed Grafana. Own your telemetry pipelines end-to-end with open standards and AWS managed services.

sessions.t: Kiro Crew: Architecture of an open source AI coding agent built on Kiro
sessions.a: Kiro Crew is an open source AI coding workspace built on Kiro CLI that grew from a side project to 39,000 users and nearly 500 contributors inside Amazon. Unlike single-session assistants, Kiro Crew combines multi-step task orchestration, tool-use planning, and a shared context layer for real engineering workflows. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through how Kiro Crew decomposes complex tasks, selects and chains tools, manages execution state, and integrates with existing developer environments. We'll discuss the design trade-offs that enabled rapid adoption and our journey to open source.

sessions.t: Kiro Writes the PR. Nobody Validates the App. (sponsored by TestMu)
sessions.a: Kiro can now build a whole feature on its own: write the spec, implement it, and open the PR without anyone sitting in the loop. That’s real progress. But nothing in that pipeline actually runs the app and checks it against what the spec promised. The checks that gate the PR look at the code, not the behavior. So the PR arrives looking done, and “done” is still just a guess someone has to trust. The good news is Kiro already produces the one thing a testing agent needs to close that gap: a clear, structured spec of what the feature is supposed to do. We’ll show Kane-CLI plugged in as a Kiro Power, reading that spec, actually running the app the way a user would, and reporting back proof, not just a checkmark, before the PR merges. This presentation is brought to you by TestMu, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: KNFSD File Cache: Extending Your NFS Storage into the Cloud
sessions.a: Need to cache and serve NFS data from on-premises filers, across Availability Zones and Regions, or from other cloud providers with full read and write-back support? In this chalk talk, dive into KNFSD File Cache, an open-source, kernel-based NFS caching proxy on Amazon EC2 that transparently extends existing NFS storage into AWS. A single Terraform module stands up a production-ready, autoscaling cluster with high throughput and at low cost. We discuss hybrid and burst-compute patterns across M&E, HPC, Financial Services, and Life Sciences—eliminating latency without migration, client changes, or vendor lock-in.
