sessions.t: Knowledge Representations for Autonomous Software Lifecycle Management
sessions.a: What formal properties must a software representation satisfy for agents to manage entire application lifecycles autonomously — reasoning at the specification level, not the code level? This session examines the open scientific questions behind agentic code understanding: encoding both structural topology and business semantics into a unified knowledge graph, extracting and grounding business rules when institutional context has been lost, enabling agent reasoning over large heterogeneous graphs without coherence degradation, and establishing deterministic validation signals that replace human judgment with formal guarantees. Drawing from graph theory, knowledge representation, specification mining, and formal verification research, we explore what makes these problems hard, where current approaches break at scale, and what architectural principles make full-lifecycle autonomy tractable. Attendees will leave with a rigorous understanding of the representation and reasoning foundations required for agents that don’t just generate code but understand, validate, evolve, and replace software as knowledge.

sessions.t: Know your data: discovery, context, and AI agents in Amazon S3
sessions.a: Organizations store billions of objects in Amazon S3 but struggle to answer basic questions: What do I have? Where did it come from? Is it still relevant? Learn how S3 Metadata and annotations turn your storage into a searchable, context-rich data estate. See how to attach business meaning directly to objects, query metadata at petabyte scale through managed Apache Iceberg tables, and drive governance workflows from metadata signals. Then discover how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit give AI agents governed access to your data, and how AWS Context lets them reason over relationships across your S3 data.

sessions.t: Kubernetes-native agentic AI on Amazon EKS with open source primitives
sessions.a: Production agentic AI needs a scalable runtime, governed LLM access, persistent memory, observability, tool discovery, and secure code isolation. In this workshop you'll build all six on Amazon EKS using native Kubernetes primitives and open source projects. Tackle all six end-to-end or take individual modules home. Deploy LiteLLM as a multi-model gateway, Mem0 for user-scoped memory, Langfuse for observability into reasoning and tool calls, an MCP registry for tool discovery, and sandboxes for hardware-level code isolation. Leave with a scalable, GitOps-ready, portable reference architecture.

sessions.t: Kubernetes-native agentic AI on Amazon EKS with open source primitives
sessions.a: Production agentic AI needs a scalable runtime, governed LLM access, persistent memory, observability, tool discovery, and secure code isolation. In this workshop you'll build all six on Amazon EKS using native Kubernetes primitives and open source projects. Tackle all six end-to-end or take individual modules home. Deploy LiteLLM as a multi-model gateway, Mem0 for user-scoped memory, Langfuse for observability into reasoning and tool calls, an MCP registry for tool discovery, and sandboxes for hardware-level code isolation. Leave with a scalable, GitOps-ready, portable reference architecture.

sessions.t: KYC in 90 Seconds: Real-Time Onboarding with AgentCore
sessions.a: Opening a bank account used to take days A neobank does it in 90 seconds. The secret: five specialized agents — Identity, Document Analysis, Fraud, Compliance Risk, and Customer Experience orchestrated by a supervisor on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness. This Talk builds that KYC pipeline live: three API calls, no orchestration boilerplate, agents running across jurisdictions with built-in compliance and audit trails You'll see real event-driven architecture with Amazon MSK, real Bedrock Guardrails, and exactly what breaks when you scale it. Production KYC, live code — and the cost and abandonment numbers that make it matter.

sessions.t: Lab Maker: From Prompt to Personalized Lab in Minutes
sessions.a: Lab Maker on AWS Skill Builder generates personalized hands-on labs from natural language prompts, allowing you to learn and experiment in the Console without incurring costs or risking production environments. During this session, we will generate a custom lab in real time before saving and sharing it with a team, demonstrating the full creation-to-collaboration workflow. We will then push Lab Maker further by generating a lab for a recently launched AWS service and uploading real organizational constraints to show how the tool adapts to your specific environment. You will leave this session with the knowledge and confidence to create your own labs.

sessions.t: Lambda for every scale and workload shape
sessions.a: Honeycomb spends millions of dollars a year on Lambda. Every cold query runs through a map-reduce backend that used to mean one tier, Lambda Functions, regardless of shape. We outgrew Lambda Functions, not Lambda: Managed Instances now absorbs steady-state baseline traffic at roughly 7.5x lower cost than Functions, MicroVMs takes spikes of load tolerating 1.5 seconds of added latency, and Functions still catches bursty spillover. We'll walk through the observability and benchmarks that drove each cutover, and the routing logic deciding which tier a query lands on before it executes. You'll learn how to scale your serverless workloads multiple orders of magnitude without linear cost.

sessions.t: Lambda Managed Instances: Always-on Serverless Compute
sessions.a: Some Lambda workloads run constantly. For steady-state, high-throughput functions, per-invocation pricing becomes more expensive than running the same code on EC2, but you don't want to manage instances. Lambda Managed Instances give you EC2 economics with multi-concurrency while Lambda handles instance lifecycle, patching, and scaling. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the decision: when Managed Instances beat standard Lambda pricing, what workloads migrate cleanly versus what needs adaptation, and how to model your break-even point. Bring your Lambda bill. We'll help you find where Managed Instances save money and where they don't.

sessions.t: Lambda MicroVMs: Secure stateful sandboxes for code execution
sessions.a: AI agents generate code, customers upload plugins, and third-party extensions need execution environments. All of it requires strong isolation. In this chalk talk, we discuss Lambda MicroVMs: VM-level, isolated sandboxes with filesystem state that persists across invocations. We cover the security model (how isolation boundaries prevent lateral movement), stateful session management for multi-turn agent interactions, lifecycle controls that limit resource consumption, and integration patterns with Step Functions and EventBridge for orchestrating sandboxed workloads. Bring your multi-tenant architecture questions. We'll whiteboard where MicroVMs fit versus standard Lambda.

sessions.t: Lambda MicroVMs: The Missing Serverless Primitive for Multi-Tenant Agents
sessions.a: Lambda Functions are stateless and time out after 15 minutes. Fargate tasks are expensive to keep warm. When building multi-tenant agent platforms, I needed per-tenant isolation without per-tenant cost. Lambda MicroVMs solve this: Firecracker VM-level isolation, 8-hour stateful execution, auto-suspend when idle, instant resume on next request. This session walks through the architecture I built, replacing always-on containers with MicroVMs as per-tenant agent sandboxes. I'll share the tradeoffs, what surprised me, and a deployable pattern you can take home and ship.

sessions.t: Lambda performance tuning and cost optimization
sessions.a: Most Lambda functions run at default memory settings, which means you're paying more for slower execution. Right-sizing memory often reduces cost and latency at the same time. In this chalk talk, we go beyond memory tuning: cold start elimination with SnapStart and provisioned concurrency, architecture-level savings like batching and right-sizing event source mappings, and when Lambda Managed Instances deliver better economics than per-invocation pricing. We whiteboard the decision points using real cost data and discuss which CloudWatch and Cost Explorer metrics actually drive optimization decisions.

sessions.t: Large-scale VMware exit: engineering a 10,000+ server migration wave engine
sessions.a: Organizations facing VMware licensing pressure need more than a migration plan. They need a structured exit strategy spanning assessment, mobilization, migration, and modernization. In this session, we discuss how AWS Transform drives business outcomes at each phase: portfolio assessment that quantifies TCO reduction, wave planning that protects application uptime, automated cutover orchestration that eliminates risk, and post-migration modernization that captures cloud-native savings. Drawing from real-world examples, we explore how teams compressed 18-month timelines into ten or lower using AWS Transform and agentic capabilities for migrating compute, database and storage resources, then open the discussion to address your specific use cases.

sessions.t: Latest trends: Network/EBS intensive workloads on Amazon EC2 instances
sessions.a: EC2 network 'n' and EBS-optimized 'b' instances deliver the highest, most consistent network and EBS performance in the cloud. Join us for a tour of the latest Graviton and Intel instance types in these families, plus the networking and EBS technologies that unlock peak performance for your workloads. Learn how customers leverage these instances for new workloads associated with AI/ML training and inference, and traditional network-intensive workloads such as security & network virtual appliances, and EBS-intensive workloads such as SQL, NoSQL, and in-memory databases.

sessions.t: Launch a production container app in under 5 minutes
sessions.a: Amazon ECS Express Mode reduces container deployment to three required inputs and a single CLI command. In this builders session, deploy a web application with built-in load balancing, autoscaling, TLS, and canary deployments configured automatically. Explore the full service lifecycle from creation through updates to deletion and see how shared ALBs keep costs low across multiple services. Ideal for developers new to Amazon ECS or looking to simplify their deployment workflow. Bring a laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.t: Layered security for Amazon EKS: Patterns that scale
sessions.a: Kubernetes gives you powerful primitives for running workloads at scale, but its default configuration prioritizes flexibility over security. In this chalk talk, we work through a layered defense strategy for Amazon EKS: hardening the control plane, implementing least-privilege RBAC and pod security standards, securing the software supply chain, enforcing network segmentation, and building runtime threat detection. We'll discuss real-world patterns customers use to move from reactive security posture to proactive guardrails — covering both EKS Auto Mode and self-managed configurations. You'll leave with actionable strategies you can apply immediately.

sessions.t: Learn faster: Experimentation in an AI world
sessions.a: AI makes it possible to generate and test far more product variations than a team could create by hand. But running more experiments only helps if you can release each variation safely, measure the right signals, and separate meaningful results from noise. In this code-focused session, you’ll learn how to use AI and feature flags to control experiment variants, target audiences, adjust exposure, and shut down underperforming tests without redeploying. We’ll also examine how Amazon has recently used AI in experiments on Amazon.com to create variations and extract better signals from the results.

sessions.t: Learnings from resilience testing in AWS
sessions.a: In this talk, we'll describe some of the resilience testing we've been doing in AWS. We'll talk a bit about the Game Day Region, why it exists, and how we use it. We'll talk about the types of test we run, the philosophy behind them, and some takeaways that you, our customers, can also apply.

sessions.t: Learn new AI development skills with Kiro
sessions.a: Discover Kiro, the IDE for structured agentic development. In this builder’s session, explore how to use Kiro as your intelligent partner - helping to understand complex codebases, crystalize detailed requirements, and deliver quality solutions at unprecedented speed. You will iterate with Kiro to finalize your detailed design, before using Kiro to orchestrate AI agents and implement a fully working solution – all while maintaining complete control throughout the development process. You must bring a laptop to participate in this session.

sessions.t: Lessons from Netflix's distributed PostgreSQL migration to Aurora
sessions.a: In this session, explore the migration playbook and lessons learned from moving some of Netflix's largest workloads from a self-managed, distributed PostgreSQL-compatible database on Amazon EC2 to Aurora. Discover how PostgreSQL compatibility minimized code changes while the shared storage architecture of Aurora eliminated cross-node coordination overhead, delivering up to 75% lower, more predictable latency and up to 28% cost savings. Learn about workload selection and sequencing, near-zero downtime cutovers with data consistency validation and rollback planning, and post-migration operational lessons including vacuum debt, connection management, and query plan stability. Walk away with a reusable framework for your own migrations.

sessions.t: Lessons in Scale and Innovation from Amazon's AI-Native Development
sessions.a: AI agents running on AWS are transforming how Amazon teams build, ship, and operate at unprecedented velocity and scale. Discover how autonomous agents write, test, and deploy code around the clock through spec-driven development, while always-on agents process millions of transactions, unify fragmented data, and deliver measurable cost savings without human intervention. Leaders from multiple Amazon business units share the architectures, patterns, and governance models powering this shift, from AI-native development that eliminates idle time to agentic systems that compound value in production on AWS. Leave with a playbook for sustained transformation through autonomous AI.

sessions.t: Let AI agents see and operate your desktop apps on WorkSpaces
sessions.a: Enterprises run critical processes on desktop applications that are too costly to modernize and too important to abandon. Amazon WorkSpaces now lets AI agents operate those same applications the way humans do, seeing the screen and executing workflows without requiring custom integrations or application changes. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into how agents inherit the same identity controls, network isolation, and compliance boundaries as human users. We'll walk through MCP tool forwarding, real-time session control, and domain-joined fleet support. Bring your architecture questions.

sessions.t: Let AI Teammates Build Trusted Supply Chain Forecasts on Day One
sessions.a: Most forecasting stalls when history is thin or inputs disagree. See how Amazon Connect Decisions produces accurate forecasts from your first day, even with limited data. AI teammates orchestrate more than 18 forecasting tools and models trained on Amazon data, then harmonize statistical forecasts, customer commitments, and cross functional inputs into one consensus plan. You will leave knowing how to reach a forecast your whole team trusts, how the system keeps accuracy honest over time, and how to stop reconciling numbers in spreadsheets before every planning cycle.

sessions.t: Level up your bot defense for mobile apps and web with AWS WAF SDK
sessions.a: In this session, we'll dive into advanced bot mitigation using the AWS WAF SDK and label evaluations. Learn how to go beyond basic rule-based blocking to implement dynamic, data-driven defenses that adapt to evolving threats. We'll explore programmatically managing WAF rules, leveraging labels for granular request inspection, and integrating SDK workflows to automate threat response - across mobile app, JavaScript, and API traffic integrations. Through real-world scenarios, you'll see how to distinguish legitimate traffic from sophisticated bots, reduce false positives, and maintain application performance across surfaces. Bring your questions and learn how to implement scalable, intelligent bot protection at the edge.

sessions.t: Leverage the power of MCP servers for resource inventory and compliance across clouds
sessions.a: AI agents can now interact with AWS services through the Model Context Protocol. In this code talk, we live-build a governance agent that uses MCP to query AWS Config for resource configurations. You'll see how to construct compliance checks, detect configuration drift, and trigger automated remediation using natural language all powered by Config's recording and advanced query capabilities. We explain the architecture decisions and trade-offs so you can adapt this pattern to your own governance workflows.

sessions.t: Lifecycle of a pod: trust boundaries in VM-isolated containers
sessions.a: Trace a pod from kubelet's RunPodSandbox call to process execution inside a VM isolated sandbox, then dissect the hard problems at each boundary crossing: how do you enforce policy on what runtime actions are allowed? How do you transport container images into an isolated environment the parent cannot read? Where does attestation fit, and how can you truly trust what is running inside? We examine how the trust model shifts between untrusted host and untrusted guest, explore the tradeoffs between CRI compatibility and security invariants, and discuss how EKS is approaching VM-level workload isolation

sessions.t: Lights, Camera, Fargate—A Reality-TV Startup Hardened for Scale on AWS
sessions.a: In six weeks on reality TV coding show The Full Stack, we built DataSwarm — a data-observability solution shipped as an open-source CLI with cloud-hosted data analysis and remediation. Great demo, wrong architecture. When real users arrived, the demo cracked. So we pivoted. Long-running agents moved off Lambda onto ephemeral ECS Fargate tasks. API keys swapped for firewalled Amazon Bedrock, feature-branched CI/CD with dev-to-prod promotion, and Next.js behind CloudFront, S3, and Lambda@Edge. We break down each tradeoff from first idea to first customer. Leave knowing how to tell demo-grade architectures from customer-grade ones — and when to make the jump.

sessions.t: Live AI and the Infrastructure Behind It (sponsored by Decart)
sessions.a: AI is entering a new era: from static generation to live experiences. From shopping to entertainment, digital experiences are becoming live, visual, and personalized. In this session, Decart will explore the infrastructure powering this shift, what it takes to deliver AI-generated video in real time, and how to bring these experiences to scale. Join us for a look at the technology behind Live AI, and where it’s going next. This presentation is brought to you by Decart, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Live-code inference patterns for agentic workloads on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Agentic workloads are multi-step, tool-calling, and retrieval-augmented, which means they stress the inference layer differently than a single prompt. In this code talk, we build three patterns live: function calling, multi-step reasoning chains, and retrieval-augmented generation with Knowledge Bases. For each, you see how it behaves at the inference level, including token consumption, latency, and retry logic, and how to tune it for cost and speed. You leave with working code for all three patterns that you can adapt to your own agents.

sessions.t: Load-bearing coupling: Finding the coupling you can't cut
sessions.a: Teams break up monoliths to move faster, then find the pieces still fail together. Some coupling is doing real structural work: invariants spanning writes, ordering guarantees, timing assumptions baked into callers. Cut it and you get a distributed monolith, the same dependency with new failure modes. In this session, we whiteboard real systems, insert seams, and price what each dependency costs to cross a boundary: consistency, backpressure, retry semantics. Apply a simple test: if a circuit breaker can't open here without breaking correctness, that coupling is load-bearing. Bring your hardest dependency; leave knowing which coupling to cut, which to keep, and why.

sessions.t: LOTA: Detecting and preventing advanced lateral movement
sessions.a: "Living off the land" (LOTL) attacks use native OS tools to evade detection. In 2026, techniques evolved to "Living off the Agent" (LOTA), compromising enterprise AI agents through subtle prompt injections to exfiltrate data, escalate privileges, and move laterally. Red team studies identified vulnerabilities in production AI agents with distinct LOTA patterns. This chalk talk explores the LOTA taxonomy, detection strategies, and architectural containment patterns. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we'll whiteboard defenses together.

sessions.t: LSEG: Scaling multi-agent AI with assurance on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) manages one of the world's largest risk intelligence datasets, processing millions of records that demand continuous curation and validation. In this session, learn how LSEG built a durable agentic AI framework on Amazon Bedrock—orchestrating multi-agent workflows that combines deterministic rules, AI enrichment, and human review to reduce false positives in financial crime screening. LSEG will share their approach to continuous AI assurance with golden dataset evaluations and staged rollout gates with real-time observability and automated rollback to safely scale automation while maintaining the accuracy global financial institutions require.

sessions.t: Machines on Call for Humans: Agents to run and fix your prod (sponsored by Resolve AI)
sessions.a: We're entering a new era of software operations where the question is no longer whether intelligent agents have a role in production, but whether humans should still be the first responder. As production environments continue to grow more complex, agents are becoming part of the operations team, handling the repetitive work of operating production while engineers focus on the decisions that require judgment, creativity, and experience. This session explores how leading enterprises are rethinking on-call, improving reliability, and reshaping the way production is operated by putting machines on call for humans. This presentation is brought to you by Resolve AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Make AMD Your Default on AWS: Efficient EC2 for the Agentic AI Era with EPYC (sponsored by AMD)
sessions.a: What if you could run agentic AI for over 30% less on Amazon EC2—within the contracts you already have? As autonomous agents call inference models and tools, compute demand explodes and the CPU-to-GPU ratio inverts from 1:8 to 8:1, making processor choice the defining ROI decision. This session proves how 5th-Gen AMD EPYC "Turin" on EC2 runs general-purpose workloads faster and smaller, delivering >30% OpEx savings you can redirect from IT overhead into AI budgets. Partners see how MAP-aligned migration funding, POC support, and co-sell turn efficient, variety-ready AMD infrastructure on AWS into bigger, faster customer wins. This presentation is brought to you by AMD, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Make every GPU count: Maximizing GPU efficiency for inference at scale
sessions.a: When an inference fleet spans thousands of interconnected NVIDIA GPUs in NVL72 racks, scheduling decisions cascade. Place a job wrong, and it fragments a capacity block, starves NVLink bandwidth, or strands GPUs behind a topology boundary. In this session, AWS and OpenAI will share scheduling and bin-packing strategies developed for production inference on Amazon EC2 UltraServers. Explore rack-aware placement that respects 72-GPU NVLink domains, approaches for mixed workload profiles (prefill vs. decode vs. batch), capacity block utilization maximization, and Kubernetes scheduling primitives that enforce topology constraints. Leave with actionable blueprints to efficiently schedule GPU inference at scale.

sessions.t: Make streaming data AI-ready before it goes stale (sponsored by Confluent)
sessions.a: Real-time data loses value when it gets stuck in pipelines. In this session, learn how Confluent, IBM and AWS are helping make streaming data immediately usable for analytics and AI. See how Confluent Tableflow turns Kafka topics into Apache Iceberg tables and registers them in the AWS Glue Data Catalog—eliminating the need for custom streaming pipelines. Discover how this integration enables data engineers to reduce ingestion complexity, strengthen governance and put real-time data to work for analytics and AI with Amazon Athena. This presentation is brought to you by Confluent, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Make the agent code while you sleep
sessions.a: Anyone can prompt an agent. The hard part is getting it to work the way you want—for hours, unattended, without going off the rails. This advanced workshop digs into orchestration. You'll build a custom agent, then set a goal so strong the agent can't redefine it or declare victory early. You'll decompose work across subagents, use directives like /goal to keep execution on track, and design guardrails that let an agent run long and autonomously while landing where you intended. We'll use Kiro, but these patterns transfer to any agentic system. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Make your Connect data talk: 10x faster answers with Quick
sessions.a: Your Amazon Connect contact center knows why handle time spiked yesterday. The hard part is making it confess. The old way: ask another team, wait for the next report, lose hours. We made it self-serve with Amazon Quick Suite. First we tried the obvious path, exporting Connect's raw records to S3, and spent days fighting data that still came out wrong. Then we pivoted to the Connect analytics data lake: contact records, Contact Lens, and sentiment, accurate, zero ETL. The one catch was cross-account Connect Lake Formation. Now anyone asks Quick in plain language and reshapes queries on the fly. 10x faster to answer.

sessions.t: Make your multi-agent orchestration more deterministic
sessions.a: As agents work on longer, more complex tasks, the context window fills up and the agent can lose track of its plan and execution steps. The manual setup required to get multi-agent orchestration to reliably complete these kinds of tasks can be complex and brittle. In this session, you'll learn best practices, tools, and patterns that power users have perfected to set up and scale your multi-agent workloads and take on hours-long tasks with confidence.

sessions.t: Make your vector search faster, more relevant, and cost-efficient
sessions.a: You have a vector workload running and questions piling up: How do I raise relevance? How do I control cost as I scale? Which ranking technique fits my data? We give you a quick tour of vector capabilities in Amazon OpenSearch Service, then spend the rest of the session working through your problems. Topics on the table include hybrid search combining lexical and vector results, ranking with reciprocal rank fusion, maximal marginal relevance, and filtering strategies, when to reach for Automatic Semantic Enrichment or neural sparse vectors instead of building your own embedding pipeline, and cost optimization techniques including quantization, tiered storage, GPU-accelerated indexing, and auto-optimization. Come with a workload in mind and leave with tuning direction for your specific situation.

sessions.t: Making Enterprise Data AI-Ready Without the Data Engineering Overhead (sponsored by Eon)
sessions.a: Enterprise data is spread across databases, object stores, and compute, but making it usable by AI often requires months of data engineering and a growing web of pipelines to build and maintain. In this session, we’ll show how Eon continuously discovers, connects to, classifies, and transforms data across Amazon RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, EC2, S3, and more into a unified, AI-ready data layer. We’ll walk through the architecture and semantic layer on AWS, then share how agents can use Amazon Bedrock to query that governed context in natural language through MCP, with Claude, Amazon Quick, and other AI clients. This presentation is brought to you by Eon, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Making Kiro Crew work for your team
sessions.a: Kiro Crew is the persistent, open source development workspace that remembers your context, learns how you work, and coordinates across your unique tools and workflows, so you come back to progress instead of another workflow to restart. In this session, you'll learn how to make Kiro Crew work for your team: wire in the tools your team already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape shared memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold and maintain team standards and best practices.

sessions.t: Making sense of messy enterprise data with AI on AWS
sessions.a: Organizations struggle to make sense of their data when it's scattered across inconsistent formats, ad-hoc naming conventions, and incomplete records. In this workshop, you will build a scalable pipeline that uses generative AI to transform product descriptions into structured data ready for downstream analysis. Inspired by how AWS tackles life cycle assessment across its data center fleet in the AWS Sustainability Console, you will use Amazon Bedrock and other AWS services to ingest, classify, and contextualize data to deliver sustainability intelligence. You'll then deploy AI agents to orchestrate queries and execute analysis tasks, providing you patterns for any domain.

sessions.t: Making your Amazon Aurora cluster more resilient
sessions.a: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale. Hundreds of thousands of organizations trust Aurora for their workloads today. In this session, learn about features such as Aurora Global Database and Amazon RDS Proxy, and discover best practices to achieve high availability for Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL database clusters. The session includes a whiteboarding discussion on high availability and disaster recovery solutions to help maximize application resilience.

sessions.t: Making your Amazon Aurora cluster more resilient
sessions.a: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale. Hundreds of thousands of organizations trust Aurora for their workloads today. In this session, learn about features such as Aurora Global Database and Amazon RDS Proxy, and discover best practices to achieve high availability for Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL database clusters. The session includes a whiteboarding discussion on high availability and disaster recovery solutions to help maximize application resilience.

sessions.t: Malware Protection: hands-on detection and response for malicious files
sessions.a: In this one-hour builder session, get hands-on with the core capabilities of Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection. Configure on-demand S3 scanning using the SendObjectMalwareScan API, set up automated EBS volume scanning for EC2 instances, and build event-driven response pipelines that quarantine infected objects before they spread. Walk through real malware samples triggering findings, interpret scan results, and integrate with Security Hub for centralized visibility. Leave with a working malware detection and response workflow deployed in your own account.

sessions.t: Manage cloud costs and AI spend with AWS Cost Management
sessions.a: Join this breakout to learn how AI is helping teams manage cloud costs more effectively, and why managing the cost of AI itself is becoming just as important. We cover AWS FinOps enhancements across both dimensions. On the "AI for FinOps" side, learn how your team can operate more efficiently through automation and agentic workflows. On the "FinOps for AI" side, see how you can access and manage your AI spend with granular cost data and governance. Walk away with a repeatable governance model as you scale AI with confidence.

sessions.t: Managing and Monitoring AWS Direct Connect at Scale: Customer Lessons
sessions.a: AWS shares customer best practices for managing and monitoring AWS Direct Connect at hyperscale. Network teams discusses how they operate one of the world's largest Direct Connect footprints — spanning multiple regions and supporting AI training workloads that serve billions of users. We deep-dive into new monitoring capabilities: Amazon CloudWatch metrics for BGP session health and prefix counts, VIF rate limiters that prevent bandwidth contention across shared connections, and Network Synthetic Monitor for proactive path-level health diagnostics. Leave with actionable strategies for alerting, capacity planning, and building unified dashboards for cross-Region network visibility.

sessions.t: Managing software vulnerabilities in the agentic world
sessions.a: Vulnerability management is evolving beyond detection. As AI agents generate and deploy code at machine speed, security teams need a fundamentally different approach to identifying, prioritizing, and resolving software vulnerabilities. In this session, explore how AWS thinks about the future of vulnerability management — from contributing to open source vulnerability databases and detecting malicious packages before they reach your pipeline, to enforcing remediation at scale without slowing development velocity. Learn how to shift from reactive CVE chasing to a proactive posture that accounts for AI-generated code, autonomous deployments, and the expanding software supply chain.

sessions.t: Map once and prove everywhere across multiple compliance frameworks
sessions.a: Regulatory frameworks like SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and the EU AI Act each demand separate assessments, yet a significant portion of their requirements overlap. You spend time collecting duplicate evidence for controls you already have. This chalk talk introduces the control inheritance approach and shows how a single AWS Config rule or organizational policy can satisfy requirements across multiple frameworks. You walk through real examples of framework overlap, automation patterns that eliminate duplicate evidence collection, and a governance approach you can implement immediately.

sessions.t: Mapping and Securing the Enterprise AI Attack Surface (sponsored by Zscaler)
sessions.a: AI is racing across the enterprise—showing up in endpoints, apps, workflows, agents, and data paths faster than most security teams can track. But securing AI takes more than knowing where it exists; it requires understanding how data flows, where it comes from, where it goes, and which users, devices, apps, and AI endpoints interact with it along the way. In this session, we’ll explore how to map the AI attack surface and its data lineage while securing the AI endpoints where innovation actually happens. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Master Agent Skills: From Desktop Builds to Production Deployment
sessions.a: Build, govern, and scale production-ready agent skills across your enterprise on Amazon Quick. Author custom skills on Quick, then shift to the admin perspective: register skills in Quick Catalog for org-wide discovery, configure access policies, and schedule autonomous execution at scale. Through two business-driven use cases — churn prevention from contact center data and intelligent claims processing that eliminates manual back-office work — you'll deploy measurable automation. Leave with working skills, a governance framework for hundreds of agents across teams, and a playbook for communicating ROI to leadership.

sessions.t: Master Apache Iceberg migration on AWS [REPEAT]
sessions.a: Many organizations want to adopt Apache Iceberg but face a practical challenge: how do you migrate existing data lake tables — Hive-style, Apache Hudi, or Delta Lake — without disrupting production workloads? In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn and implement the full spectrum of migration techniques on AWS, from zero-copy in-place approaches to full data rewrites targeting both self-managed Iceberg tables in S3 and Amazon S3 Tables. Beyond the mechanics, you'll implement real-world migration strategies and learn how to choose among them based on downtime tolerance, writer constraints, and data volume. You'll leave with a repeatable playbook for migrating your data lake to Iceberg with minimal risk and zero data loss.

sessions.t: Mastercard: Training a large transaction model on billions of transactions
sessions.a: Large language models transformed text. Large transaction models (LTMs) aim to do the same for payment and commerce data. Instead of brittle, hand-crafted feature pipelines feeding hundreds of specialized models, LTMs are transformer-based foundation models pre-trained directly on billions of anonymized transactions, learning rich representations of transactions, merchant behavior, consumer activity, and financial risk. This session introduces Mastercard's LTM program, the architectural choices behind it, and the unique challenges of tokenizing and training on tabular and sequential financial data at massive scale. We show how foundation models power diverse production use cases, from fraud detection to personalization to reaching underserved cardholders.

sessions.t: Mastering agentic development: skills, custom agents, and steering
sessions.a: The best results from agentic AI don't come from clever one-off prompts, but from shaping how agents work. In this session, go beyond prompting to learn techniques that apply to any agentic coding tool. Craft reusable skills that encode your team's know-how, build custom agents tuned to specific jobs, and use steering files to carry your conventions and architecture across sessions. We'll cover how to set goals the agent will actually follow, when to let it run autonomously, and how to tell a skill that's useful versus noise. We'll demo live in Kiro, but the principles transfer wherever you work.

sessions.t: Mastering agentic development: skills, custom agents, and steering
sessions.a: The best results from agentic AI don't come from clever one-off prompts, but from shaping how agents work. sessions.t: Mastering LLM tokenomics: From token costs to business outcomes
sessions.a: Financial institutions are scaling generative AI and agentic workloads to production and need strategies to keep costs aligned with business value. With enterprise workloads requiring retrieval, orchestration, validation, and governance layers, understanding token economics becomes critical to sustainable growth. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through design patterns for controlling token consumption while maintaining quality, including prompt compression, semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache, tiered model routing with Amazon Bedrock, and cost attribution using Amazon CloudWatch. We'll whiteboard the hidden cost drivers in agentic AI systems and share design patterns that financial institutions use to control token consumption while maintaining quality.

sessions.t: Mastering LLM tokenomics: From token costs to business outcomes
sessions.a: Financial institutions are scaling generative AI and agentic workloads to production and need strategies to keep costs aligned with business value. With enterprise workloads requiring retrieval, orchestration, validation, and governance layers, understanding token economics becomes critical to sustainable growth. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through design patterns for controlling token consumption while maintaining quality, including prompt compression, semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache, tiered model routing with Amazon Bedrock, and cost attribution using Amazon CloudWatch. We'll whiteboard the hidden cost drivers in agentic AI systems and share design patterns that financial institutions use to control token consumption while maintaining quality.

sessions.t: Maximize EKS efficiency: Auto Mode, Graviton, and Spot best practices
sessions.a: Achieving optimal compute efficiency on Amazon EKS demands more than choosing the right instance -- it requires an intelligent infrastructure layer that continuously optimizes on your behalf. In this chalk talk, learn how teams use EKS Auto Mode to eliminate infrastructure toil with up to 40% faster node boot times, over 40% faster scale-out, and up to 70% faster consolidation. Discover how pairing Auto Mode with AWS Graviton5 (M9g, C9g) and EC2 Spot can reduce total cluster spend by up to 40%. You'll leave with actionable strategies for multi-architecture scheduling, right-sizing, and EFA placement for ML workloads.

sessions.t: Maximize EKS efficiency: Auto Mode, Graviton, and Spot best practices
sessions.a: Achieving optimal compute efficiency on Amazon EKS demands more than choosing the right instance -- it requires an intelligent infrastructure layer that continuously optimizes on your behalf. You'll leave with actionable strategies for multi-architecture scheduling, right-sizing, and EFA placement for ML workloads.

sessions.t: Maximize GPU utilization across training and inference on HyperPod
sessions.a: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore how SageMaker HyperPod serves as a unified GPU pool for data processing, training, post-training, and inference without re-platforming. Through live whiteboarding, demos, and production architectures; we'll cover how customers are maximizing GPU utilization across workloads, regions, and multiple teams with shared architectures and GPUs. Then learn how SageMaker Studio gives give data scientists, AI researchers, and machine learning engineers an easy way to to iterate on jobs all on the shared pool of resources. We'll also see how Humain has optimized utilization of compute resources across two large HyperPod clusters, onboarding multiple teams of researchers with team isolation and advanced task submission strategies. Participants will walk away with practical patterns for running the full model lifecycle on resilient, shared infrastructure

sessions.t: Maximizing block storage performance for high-intensity workloads
sessions.a: Amazon EBS handles over 222 trillion I/O operations daily. Performance matters, a lot, but it’s not just about average performance, it’s about stable low latency that minimizes outliers or tail latency. io2 Block Express volumes are designed for that purpose with consistent sub-millisecond latency and 99.999% durability for critical applications such as SAP HANA, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and more. Learn about how its performance characteristics optimize compute utilization, leading to cost efficiency and the success of many performance-demanding use cases.

sessions.t: Maximizing EC2 NVMe local storage
sessions.a: Discover how to leverage the latest high-performance Nitro SSDs in EC2 storage-optimized instances for data-intensive workloads. This technical session explores new capabilities for monitoring and managing NVMe instance storage, including enhanced performance metrics—latency, IOPS, and throughput—to optimize and troubleshoot your workloads. We also demonstrate the new AWS Local Instance Storage (LIS) CSI driver for simplified NVMe volume management in Amazon EKS. Learn best practices for storage performance monitoring and integrating the LIS CSI driver in containerized applications.

sessions.t: MCP and A2A for SaaS: making your product agent-ready
sessions.a: Agentic AI is reshaping how SaaS products reach end customers. Alongside browser and API interactions, exposing capabilities through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and distributing agents via the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol is fast becoming the norm. In this session, build the two pieces every multi-tenant, agent-ready SaaS needs: an MCP server exposing your tools and resources, and an A2A endpoint with agent cards for inter-agent calls. Discover reference architectures for MCP in front of existing APIs, A2A agent cards, and authentication and authorization on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Leave with a blueprint for being a citizen in the agentic ecosystem.

sessions.t: MCP is Just An MVP. Knowledge Lakes Are The Sequel. (sponsored by Atolio)
sessions.a: MCP lets agents connect to systems. It's a minimum viable product, not a complete way to run that connection at scale. Raw database access hit the same wall decades ago, before warehouses and data lakes brought structure and governance at scale. Point-to-point agent connections hit it again: costs climb with every added tool call, latency stacks with every cross-system hop, and permissions rarely travel with retrieved data, making synthesized knowledge a sharper security risk than raw SQL ever posed. This session traces that history, breaks down each failure mode, and maps what a knowledge lake built for agents solves. This presentation is brought to you by Atolio, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: MCP Meets GraphQL: A Typed Foundation for Enterprise AI Agents (sponsored by Apollo GraphQL)
sessions.a: Enterprises connecting AI agents to systems of record face three unsolved problems: can an agent discover what data exists and what it means, get that context without runaway token cost, and touch only what it's authorized to touch. GraphQL, the proven Linux Foundation-backed standard beneath many of the world's largest customer experiences at brands like Netflix, AirBnB, Shopify, Walmart, and countless others, already solves all three through self-describing schemas and field-level queries. This talk lays out the architecture for combining GraphQL with MCP, including Apollo's approach to graph-based orchestration for cost and reliability. This presentation is brought to you by Apollo GraphQL, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Measuring emergent risks in frontier models
sessions.a: As frontier models scale in capability, so does their potential for deceptive and manipulative behavior—risks that static, single-turn evaluations fail to capture. We present our multi-layered approach to measuring emergent deception under Amazon's Frontier Model Safety Framework (FMSF), combining automated benchmarks, expert red-teaming, and uplift studies. We will dive deep into two innovations: D-REX, a benchmark detecting discrepancies between benign outputs and malicious internal chain-of-thought reasoning; and LH-Deception, a multi-agent simulation revealing emergent "chains of deception" across extended task sequences. Together, these tools address critical gaps in frontier safety evaluation and inform deployment governance.

sessions.t: Migrate and modernize infrastructure from your IDE with agentic AI
sessions.a: Migration and modernization involve dozens of manual steps across landing zones, networking, and containerization. What if you could drive the entire workflow from your IDE? In this code talk, you'll see how Kiro and AWS Transform work together as an agentic toolkit. First, generate a multi-account landing zone as infrastructure as code. Next, feed a VMware configuration export to the network agent and get Terraform modules or CDK constructs for VPCs, security groups, and production-ready network topology. Then point the containerization agent at a repo to produce ECR images and deploy to Amazon EKS.

sessions.t: Migrate on-premises storage to AWS with agentic AI
sessions.a: Migrating on-premises storage to AWS typically means weeks of manual assessment, business case building, and wave planning before a single byte moves. AWS Transform's agentic AI capabilities handle the full lifecycle, from automated assessment and business case generation to wave planning and execution, reducing that timeline to hours. In this lightning talk, see how to migrate storage from VMware estates, enterprise databases, and associated data with AI handling the complexity. Leave knowing how to start your first Transform project and accelerate time to results.

sessions.t: Migrate SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL with AI-powered conversion
sessions.a: Migrating SQL Server databases with stored procedures, triggers, and complex T-SQL constructs to Aurora PostgreSQL typically takes weeks of manual schema conversion and dependency resolution. In this workshop, you'll walk through the end-to-end workflow using AWS Transform's agentic AI: assess your SQL Server database, automate schema conversion, resolve dependencies, then hand off to your local IDE where you review, refine, and deploy converted database objects directly. You'll leave knowing how to reduce weeks of manual effort to hours while improving conversion accuracy and confidence.

sessions.t: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB with AI-powered schema design
sessions.a: Amazon DynamoDB schema design is the number one barrier to adoption, requiring upfront knowledge of access patterns and partition strategies, which most teams learn through trial and error. New AI-powered schema design tools for DynamoDB change that. In this live coding session, follow along as a banking payment-processing application is migrated from a relational database to DynamoDB. The session covers workload analysis, optimized table design generation, cost and throughput tradeoff comparisons, and iterative refinement toward production-quality schemas, including reviewing AI-generated code, refining the implementation, migrating data, and demonstrating the complete end-to-end solution.

sessions.t: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB with AI-powered schema design
sessions.a: Amazon DynamoDB schema design is the number one barrier to adoption, requiring upfront knowledge of access patterns and partition strategies, which most teams learn through trial and error. sessions.t: Migrate workloads to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
sessions.a: Running self-managed document databases at scale introduces significant operational burden, version lock-in, and rising infrastructure costs. Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) addresses these challenges with a fully managed, highly available service. In this session, examine compatibility features that simplify migration from existing document database environments, and work through architecture decisions affecting performance, cost, and reliability. Discover how enhancements in version 8.0 deliver up to 5x compression and 7x query performance improvement. Discuss common migration blockers, schema transformation approaches, and newest compatibility additions that reduce friction during cutover. Leave with a framework for planning and executing document database migrations on AWS.

sessions.t: Migrate your NAS to the cloud: Building AI-ready file storage
sessions.a: Enterprises store vast amounts of business-critical data on NAS systems, but aging hardware and rising costs are only part of the story. Legacy file storage also locks data away from modern AI workloads. Learn proven strategies for migrating NAS environments to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, then connecting that data to AWS analytics and AI services, including options like S3 Access Points, Amazon Bedrock, and SageMaker. We cover assessing your NAS estate, executing migrations with minimal disruption, and choosing the right path to unlock your data for modern workloads. You leave with a practical framework for modernizing file storage.

sessions.t: Migrating a Managed Assistant API to Strands Agents SDK
sessions.a: As organizations scale AI agent deployments, the gap between managed APIs and production-grade frameworks becomes a migration challenge. This talk describes a large-scale migration from a managed assistant API serving hundreds of agent projects to Strands Agents, selected for its deterministic orchestration, multi-provider portability, and open-source extensibility. The migration replaced three subsystems (orchestration, conversation persistence, and observability) while preserving all existing tool implementations. This session details the architectural decisions, backward-compatible tool migration, security constraints for production deployment, and evaluation methodology that validated quality parity. These patterns generalize to any organization migrating from managed AI APIs to open-source agent frameworks.

sessions.t: Migrating legacy ETL to serverless with AWS Glue [REPEAT]
sessions.a: Enterprises using traditional ETL tools on-premises infrastructure face mounting pressure from licensing costs, scaling limits, and operational overhead. Migrating these entrenched pipelines to a serverless model is achievable with the right patterns, but the path is rarely a straight lift-and-shift. In this chalk talk, we'll work through proven migration patterns for moving legacy ETL workloads to AWS Glue. We will tackle topics such as converting complex transformation logic, handling incremental and change-data-capture loads, preserving data quality and lineage, and phasing cutover to minimize risk. Bring your toughest migration questions and leave with a practical framework f of how serverless ETL changes the economics and operations of data integration.

sessions.t: Migrating petabytes at scale: Real-world strategies with AWS DataSync
sessions.a: Learn how to plan, build, and implement the migration of 10 petabytes of on-premises data with AWS DataSync. Through interactive discussion and whiteboarding, explore effective approaches for data categorization and creating transfer job manifests that map directly to cost-optimized S3 storage classes. Discover how this data migration architecture accelerates the migration of client data to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP. This chalk talk provides practical insights and best practices for executing large-scale data migrations to AWS.

sessions.t: Mitigating prompt injection with structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Prompt injection works because LLM outputs are unconstrained. Structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock compiles a JSON Schema into a grammar and enforces it during decoding so every token the model emits is a valid position in the schema. In this code talk, we live-code defense schemas for sentiment analysis, intent classification, and SQL validation, then attack them with real injection payloads. We cover provider differences between Claude and open-weight models, strict tool use for agentic workflows, and how to combine grammar enforcement with input validation for defense in depth.

sessions.t: ML, automotive, and robotics simulations at scale on AWS Batch
sessions.a: Simulation and ML workloads share a hard problem: they must burst to enormous scale, run to completion reliably, and do it without a standing fleet draining budget between runs. This session shows how AWS Batch orchestrates large-scale simulation and training pipelines end to end. See how AWS Batch schedules and scales compute on demand, so jobs run when needed and nothing sits idle otherwise. Learn how simulation outputs flow through a shared data lake into GPU-accelerated training, closing the loop between data and models. Discover the orchestration and scheduling patterns that keep a real customer's high-throughput pipeline efficient.

sessions.t: Modeling Human Preference: Pairwise Battles to Agentic Systems
sessions.a: Every time we rank an LLM, we're building a model of human preference — yet for most queries there's no ground truth, only a person's sense of which answer is better, shifting with expertise, culture, and expectations. This session examines how we model preference across two regimes: pairwise battles, arena-style voting ranked through Bradley-Terry, and agentic systems, where preference spans long-horizon, multi-step, tool-using tasks. Reward models and LLM-as-judge are themselves learned preference models; from our experience at Amazon, we examine when to trust them and how to separate progress from preference-overfitting. Attendees will learn what modeling preference at scale demands.

sessions.t: Modernize a Legacy Telecom Billing App with AWS Transform Custom
sessions.a: Got an old telecom application buried under decades of technical debt? In this hands-on session, you'll take a legacy BSS billing system and modernize it using AWS Transform Custom. Start by analyzing the codebase to understand business logic, dependencies, and technical debt. Then apply a built-in catalog transformation to upgrade the language and framework instantly. Next, define your own custom transformation in natural language to convert legacy interfaces to modern APIs. Validate, test for functional equivalence, and deploy to AWS. Walk away with a running modernized app and reusable transformation recipes, plus hands-on experience modernizing real-world telecom applications.

sessions.t: Modernize and containerize legacy apps to Amazon ECS with AWS Transform
sessions.a: Your application runs on an old Java runtime with outdated dependencies. You know it belongs in containers but the upgrade path feels daunting. In this builders session, take a legacy monolithic application and use AWS Transform to identify blockers, upgrade dependencies, generate multi-stage Dockerfiles, build and scan container images for vulnerabilities, and deploy to Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. See how the agent handles multi-repo applications and validates containers before production. Walk through the full lifecycle without writing a single Dockerfile by hand. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.t: Modernize and migrate edge applications with AWS Outposts
sessions.a: Organizations running workloads on legacy virtualization platforms at the edge are looking to modernize these applications to be more resilient, portable, and operationally consistent with their cloud workloads. Simultaneously, AWS Outposts has released new second-generation single- and multi-rack offerings that deliver new instance types and Amazon EBS storage, up to 40% better price-performance, and enhanced networking features for monitoring and security. In this session, we'll cover modernization and migration strategies for organizations looking to move to a cloud operating model at the edge, as well as strategies for existing Outposts users to upgrade to the latest generation.

sessions.t: Modernize confidently with production intelligence
sessions.a: Static code analysis tells you what to modernize. It doesn't tell you what breaks when you do. Runtime dependencies, real traffic patterns, and operational risk stay invisible until cutover, when surprises are most expensive. AWS DevOps Agent adds the missing ingredient: production intelligence fed directly into your AWS Transform modernization plan. The result is assessments grounded in reality and migrations that stay safe through execution. In this chalk talk, we discuss how to incorporate production intelligence from DevOps Agent into an automated migration pipeline by Transform Custom. Bring your modernization challenges to discuss.

sessions.t: Modernize legacy applications into serverless event-driven systems
sessions.a: Join us to learn how to plan and automate your modernization. We show how to reverse-engineer architecture and dependencies from existing code, then generate a serverless, event-driven target. See how teams move from monoliths to event-driven microservices in weeks, and make their applications agent-ready in the process.

sessions.t: Modernize legacy batch into event-driven with AWS Transform & Kiro
sessions.a: Batch processing has powered critical enterprise workloads for decades, from mainframes running COBOL and PL/I to distributed systems on legacy Java. The trade-off? Overnight batch cycles that business processes can no longer afford. In this session, reimagine batch as event-driven microservices using Domain-Driven Design. AWS Transform reverse-engineers business rules from legacy code across platforms with full traceability, and Kiro translates that understanding into microservices specifications, generates production code, and creates Infrastructure as Code for AWS deployment. Leave with a repeatable pattern for reimagining batch workloads as real-time, event-driven microservices built on business rules that took decades to refine. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Modernize .NET Applications with AWS Transform and Kiro
sessions.a: Legacy .NET Framework applications tied to Windows limit your deployment options and increase operational costs. In this lab, you use AWS Transform for .NET in Interactive Mode to automatically port a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to .NET 10 Blazor application. You review the AWS Transform generated assessment report and migration plan, accept the automated transformation, then use Kiro to identify and fix the residual runtime issue that remains after the port.

sessions.t: Modernize SAP business processes with agentic AI on AWS
sessions.a: Enterprise processes span SAP for ERP, Salesforce for CRM, and ServiceNow for ITSM, connected by aging, brittle integrations that are slow to change. Agentic AI offers a better path: replacing point-to-point integrations with agents that reason across applications. In this workshop, you modernize an SAP-centric business process by orchestrating Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents over Model Context Protocol, including the AWS for SAP MCP Server. You implement cross-application use cases spanning finance, supply chain, and operations then leave with a deployable reference architecture for moving from custom integrations to agent-orchestrated workflows.

sessions.t: Modernize Windows to Linux and SQL to PostgreSQL with agentic AI
sessions.a: Moving workloads from Windows to Linux and SQL Server to PostgreSQL has always been a complex, multi-step project. Agentic AI changes the game by orchestrating the entire journey for you. In this expert-level workshop, you'll start with on-premises Windows Server workloads in a simulated data center and migrate to Amazon EC2 covering agent installation, continuous replication, and cutover. Then you'll modernize by upgrading SQL Server to PostgreSQL and migrating PHP to Amazon EKS, applying replatforming patterns in practice. You'll leave with end-to-end experience executing OS and database modernization, accelerated by agentic AI. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Modernize your CI/CD pipeline with AWS
sessions.a: In this workshop, build modern CI/CD pipelines using AWS CodePipeline through the AWS Management Console. Learn how to work with monorepos and branching strategies. Explore safe-deployment features including canary and linear traffic shifting, CloudWatch alarm gates for automatic rollback, stage-level conditions that run integration tests before promotion, and concurrent execution modes to improve pipeline performance. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Modernize your CI/CD pipeline with AWS
sessions.a: In this workshop, build modern CI/CD pipelines using AWS CodePipeline through the AWS Management Console. Learn how to work with monorepos and branching strategies. Explore safe-deployment features including canary and linear traffic shifting, CloudWatch alarm gates for automatic rollback, stage-level conditions that run integration tests before promotion, and concurrent execution modes to improve pipeline performance. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Modernize your full .NET and SQL Server stack with AWS Transform
sessions.a: Modernizing Microsoft workloads means tackling .NET and SQL Server together, not as separate projects. In this workshop, you'll use AWS Transform to compress what typically takes months into a single sprint while targeting 30% cost reduction. Through hands-on modules, you'll containerize .NET applications, use AI-powered agents to reduce technical debt, adopt DevOps practices for .NET workloads, and execute end-to-end SQL Server migrations. You'll leave with a proven approach to transform your full .NET and SQL Server stack into a scalable, cloud-native architecture. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Modernizing Care for the Underserved: Montefiore's Cloud Journey
sessions.a: Montefiore Einstein is one of New York's leading academic health systems, serving 1.3 million Bronx residents across 11 hospitals and 300+ ambulatory locations, where most patients rely on Medicaid and Medicare. To modernize its enterprise technology, Montefiore selected AWS as its strategic cloud provider—including migrating Epic, its EHR platform—building a secure, scalable, and resilient foundation that strengthens security and optimizes costs. This session explores how the transformation enables AI-powered clinical decision support, improves the reliability of critical medical records, and expands patient access through Amazon One Medical. Learn the strategies, lessons, and cloud-first approach driving better outcomes for the communities Montefiore serves.

sessions.t: Modernizing HPC on AWS: Migration at scale with PCS
sessions.a: AWS Parallel Computing Service (PCS) is helping teams modernize their HPC infrastructure by making it easier to migrate off legacy schedulers without disrupting engineering velocity. In this session, hear how organizations have moved to PCS at scale, including how Amazon Leo migrated 400 engineers and achieved 20% cost savings and 50% faster jobs. Walk away with practical migration patterns, performance tuning strategies, and architecture decisions that apply whether you're running simulations, modeling, or other compute-intensive workloads.

sessions.t: Modernizing Legacy Telecommunications OSS/BSS Systems
sessions.a: Legacy modernization is one of the most complex challenges facing Telecommunications companies today. In this Chalk Talk, we will explore strategies to accelerate VMware and mainframe migrations using Agentic AI. Using a real-world scenario, we will walk through how AWS Transform and Amazon Bedrock are used to meet the technical and business requirements of these projects and explore trade-offs in migration design and infrastructure choices. Come ready to discuss your own migration challenges!

sessions.t: Modernizing Legacy Telecommunications OSS/BSS Systems
sessions.a: Legacy modernization is one of the most complex challenges facing Telecommunications companies today. In this Chalk Talk, we will explore strategies to accelerate VMware and mainframe migrations using Agentic AI. Using a real-world scenario, we will walk through how AWS Transform and Amazon Bedrock are used to meet the technical and business requirements of these projects and explore trade-offs in migration design and infrastructure choices. Come ready to discuss your own migration challenges!

sessions.t: Modernizing multi-tenant workloads with AWS Lambda MicroVMs
sessions.a: Many organizations run untrusted or tenant-specific code on shared container clusters with complex isolation logic they built themselves. Namespace hacks, sidecar proxies, and custom scheduling rules all add operational weight without delivering hardware-level guarantees. Lambda MicroVMs offer a modernization path: replace self-managed isolation infrastructure with VM-level sandboxes that persist filesystem state across invocations and scale to zero between tasks. In this session, we cover migration patterns from container-based multi-tenant architectures to MicroVMs, the security model that replaces your custom isolation layer, stateful session management, and integration with orchestration services. We discuss what migrates cleanly and what needs redesign.

sessions.t: Modernizing .NET to Serverless: Native AOT and SnapStart, live
sessions.a: .NET workloads on Lambda have historically meant slower cold starts and JIT warmup time that doesn't match Serverless execution patterns. Native AOT and SnapStart on .NET 10 close that gap, bringing cold starts under 200ms, but modernization isn't flip-a-switch. In this code talk, modernize a .NET function to AOT live, watch it fail, then fix it on stage: serialization with source generators, reflection-based DI replaced, trimming warnings resolved. See real measurements across AOT, SnapStart, and the managed runtime. Walk away with a library compatibility matrix and modernization patterns for your own .NET Serverless journey.

sessions.t: Modernizing VMware workloads with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
sessions.a: Migrating VMware workloads to AWS often means rethinking storage, but it doesn't have to. In this chalk talk, we explore how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides a storage foundation built for VMware migrations. Learn how FSx for ONTAP delivers multi-protocol support, enterprise data management, and ONTAP compatibility that VMware administrators already know. We'll discuss real world migration patterns, cost optimization through deduplication and compression, and high availability with Multi-AZ and zero RPO. Bring your questions and join us to design a migration strategy that minimizes disruption and maximizes your existing ONTAP investments.

sessions.t: Modernizing your compute stack with Lambda's new execution models
sessions.a: You're running workloads across Lambda, EC2, and containers because no single service handled orchestration, always-on compute, and isolated execution. Lambda's new execution models change that: durable functions add checkpointed orchestration, Managed Instances provide always-on compute at EC2 economics, and MicroVMs offer hardware-level sandboxes with persistent state. In this breakout, we discuss the operational decision tree: which execution model to standardize on for each workload class, how to manage mixed-model deployments, monitoring differences across models, and when to migrate workloads between them. Bring your workload portfolio. We'll help you build an operational playbook for multi-model Lambda.

sessions.t: Molecule to Market: Bayer & Capgemini Accelerate Drug Discovery with NVIDIA BioNeMo (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.a: Join us to learn how Bayer Crop Science needed to accelerate target identification and lead optimization within its drug/crop-science discovery pipeline, and was able to accelerate their process with NVIDIA GPUs and BioNeMo. Building on AWS, they created a drug discovery workflow accelerating target identification and lead optimization through GPU-accelerated inference, molecular generation, and protein modeling, running on NVIDIA hardware. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Monetize AI Bot Traffic: Agent-Ready Media with AWS WAF & AI Analysis
sessions.a: AI bots now drive more than half of web traffic, consuming content built for human eyes while sending little value back to publishers. This hands-on workshop tackles both sides of the agent-first internet. First, you'll build a pipeline that transforms any media — images, video, audio — into concise, agent-friendly Markdown summaries using media contextual analysis, interpreting objects, scenes, speech, and meaning while preserving the original for humans. Then you'll monetize that traffic with AWS WAF's new AI traffic monetization capability, setting per-request pricing by bot verification tier and collecting payment via the x402 protocol. Leave with a reusable dual-audience, dual-revenue architecture.

sessions.t: Monitor Agent Performance and Telemetry using AgentCore Observability
sessions.a: A personal finance assistant agent deployed on AgentCore Runtime starts showing intermittent failures and slow responses. In this lab, you will use AgentCore Observability with CloudWatch GenAI dashboards and Transaction Search to diagnose production issues. Trace errors through spans, correlate telemetry with application logs, and identify root causes including a tool timeout and conversation history bloat. Apply fixes, redeploy to AgentCore Runtime, and set up CloudWatch Alarms to catch issues before users do.

sessions.t: Monitor and optimize costs for Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how that spend maps to business outcomes. In this lightning talk, see how to tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

sessions.t: Monitoring and optimizing Amazon S3 with observability tools
sessions.a: As your S3 data estate grows across buckets, tables, and directory storage, operational visibility becomes critical for cost control, performance tuning, and security investigations. In this chalk talk, learn how to build a comprehensive observability strategy for Amazon S3. We will introduce S3 Storage Lens for organization-wide metrics and recommendations, server access logs for request-level diagnostics, CloudWatch metrics for real-time alerting, and S3 Metadata for storage analytics. We will walk through use cases for each tool, including when to reach for one over another, and deep dive into Storage Lens for optimizing at scale. Bring your monitoring questions as we work through real scenarios for identifying cost anomalies, diagnosing latency issues, and auditing access patterns across multi-account environments.

sessions.t: Monitoring and optimizing Amazon S3 with observability tools

We will introduce S3 Storage Lens for organization-wide metrics and recommendations, server access logs for request-level diagnostics, CloudWatch metrics for real-time alerting, and S3 Metadata for storage analytics. Bring your monitoring questions as we work through real scenarios for identifying cost anomalies, diagnosing latency issues, and auditing access patterns across multi-account environments.

sessions.t: More than a heartbeat: Designing health checks that matter
sessions.a: Great health checks tell you exactly how your application is really performing - not just that a port is open. In this chalk talk we whiteboard meaningful health check patterns across ELB, Amazon Global Accelerator, and Amazon Route 53 - covering how to validate database readiness, confirm replica currency, and verify end-to-end request success. We'll explore thresholds, timing configurations, and graceful failover strategies. Bring your architectures - diagrams, napkin sketches, or draw live on the whiteboard - and we'll design your health strategy together. Leave with actionable patterns that reflect true application liveness.

sessions.t: Move AI agents from prototype to production with 1Password (sponsored by 1Password)
sessions.a: An AI agent can be easy to prototype but hard to take to production once it needs access to real systems. For developers, platform engineers, and security teams building with AWS AgentCore, this session shows how 1Password uses the same governed credential workflow from a local sandbox to the cloud without code changes. Attendees will see how this approach helps engineering teams move faster, limits the blast radius of a compromised agent, and gives security teams a clear audit trail. The session covers short-lived credential delivery through the AgentCore gateway and policies that apply consistently from development through production. This presentation is brought to you by 1Password, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Move code modernization at scale from one-time to continuous
sessions.a: Technical debt doesn't stop accumulating when a modernization project ends. Across thousands of repos, outdated dependencies, framework drift, and security gaps compound daily. So why treat code modernization at scale as a one-time campaign? In this chalk talk, we'll explore how AWS Transform is evolving into always-on, autonomous remediation at portfolio scale. We'll dig into what continuous mode looks like in practice, what early enterprise customers are seeing, and how this changes the way your teams think about maintaining code health over time. Bring your questions.

sessions.t: Move code modernization at scale from one-time to continuous
sessions.a: Technical debt doesn't stop accumulating when a modernization project ends. Across thousands of repos, outdated dependencies, framework drift, and security gaps compound daily. So why treat code modernization at scale as a one-time campaign? In this chalk talk, we'll explore how AWS Transform is evolving into always-on, autonomous remediation at portfolio scale.
