Bring your questions.

sessions.t: Move Fast With AI Agents Without Betting the Business (sponsored by MontyCloud)
sessions.a: You are under pressure to put AI agents to work fast, without betting the business. Everyone is racing to build agents, but no one is governing them. MontyCloud is an AI-native, autonomous CloudOps platform built on one conviction. As agents become easy to create, value moves to trusted execution. Walk away with a blueprint for turning insights into governed workflows, and governed workflows into trusted outcomes. See a live demo where any agent, model, or tool acts only with the right context, identity, policy, approvals, and cost controls. Learn why the unit of value is the governed workflow. This presentation is brought to you by MontyCloud, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Move your app to AWS Elastic Beanstalk and forget the ops
sessions.a: Running a production application should not mean owning the infrastructure under it. This lightning talk shows how AWS Elastic Beanstalk assumes ongoing operational responsibility for your applications — deployment, scaling, patching, monitoring, and upgrades — whether you bring source code, a container image, or an existing workload. In a few minutes, you will see how to identify which workloads are ready to move and what the path looks like, so your teams ship applications while AWS runs the operations underneath. You own the application. AWS owns the operational responsibility.

sessions.t: Move your multi-tenant agents to serverless AgentCore
sessions.a: Running multi-tenant agents on Kubernetes gives you flexibility, but it introduces certain operational overhead like cluster management, scaling decisions, and identity plumbing. In this workshop, you'll migrate agents to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's serverless infrastructure without giving up isolation or control. Starting from a working agentic SaaS application on Amazon EKS, you'll progressively refactor each component onto AgentCore: implement tenant isolation, configure shared MCP tools with per-tenant scoping, and instrument tenant-aware memory and observability. You'll validate tenant separation at every step and leave with hands-on experience moving multi-tenant agent infrastructure to a managed architecture. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Move your multi-tenant agents to serverless AgentCore
sessions.a: Running multi-tenant agents on Kubernetes gives you flexibility, but it introduces certain operational overhead like cluster management, scaling decisions, and identity plumbing. In this workshop, you'll migrate agents to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's serverless infrastructure without giving up isolation or control. Starting from a working agentic SaaS application on Amazon EKS, you'll progressively refactor each component onto AgentCore: implement tenant isolation, configure shared MCP tools with per-tenant scoping, and instrument tenant-aware memory and observability. You'll validate tenant separation at every step and leave with hands-on experience moving multi-tenant agent infrastructure to a managed architecture. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Multi-agent AI: Orchestration and choreography, compared
sessions.a: Every multi-agent AI system needs a coordination layer. The hard question is who decides what happens next: a central orchestrator or the agents themselves. In this session, you deploy the same five-agent travel booking pipeline through both orchestration (Step Functions) and choreography (EventBridge). Run identical load tests, inject the same failures, and add a sixth agent to each. Measure blast radius, extensibility cost, and debugging speed to see where the two approaches diverge. Leave knowing when to orchestrate, when to choreograph, and how to combine both in one architecture. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Multi-Agent Operations for Broadcast & Streaming
sessions.a: When live or streaming video breaks, every second costs revenue and audience trust. This session shows how to build coordinated AI agents using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands SDK that ingest observability data from AWS Media Services and partners, reason across signal domains, and accelerate root cause identification. Walk away with an architecture for agentic operations that turns reactive troubleshooting into proactive resolution.

sessions.t: Multicloud in the Real World: Financial Services, Healthcare, and Manufacturing (sponsored by Oracle)
sessions.a: Oracle AI Database@AWS gives organizations a new way to bring mission-critical Oracle data closer to their applications, analytics, and AI services in AWS. This session shares a clear overview of the multicloud value proposition, including application proximity, operational simplicity, enterprise performance, security, and access to AWS services. Three Oracle industry leaders will explore what that value looks like in practice. Hear how financial institutions can strengthen fraud detection, risk management, and customer experiences; how healthcare organizations can generate trusted clinical and operational insights; and how manufacturers can improve forecasting, supply chain decisions, asset performance, and operational efficiency. Leave with a practical understanding of Oracle AI Database@AWS and concrete examples of how multicloud can support industry-specific AI and business outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Oracle, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Multicloud Operating Models for ISVs
sessions.a: ISVs adopting multiple clouds face the same trade-offs. This breakout distills cloud-agnostic operating-model patterns from production multi-cloud estates -- workload placement, abstraction layers, resiliency, and FinOps (optimization, tokenization), and unified observability -- illustrated by SAP running at 25,000+ accounts across AWS, Azure, and GCP. SAP's team walks through what stayed cloud-specific, what they unified, and what they had to invent. Leave with operating-model patterns you can apply across clouds.

sessions.t: Multi-cloud security with AWS security services
sessions.a: Many organizations do not operate in a single cloud provider, creating the need for security solutions that cover multiple providers. In this lightning talk, see how AWS security services deliver unified multicloud security across AWS, Azure, and GCP environments. From posture management and vulnerability detection to risk correlation and asset visibility, learn how security teams can gain a consolidated view and respond to risks across their entire cloud estate.

sessions.t: Multi-Region hedging: Where it works and where it breaks
sessions.a: Failover recovers after impairment; hedging survives it. This chalk talk examines where multi-Region hedging holds and where it breaks. We trace hedging across the stack: racing requests through Route 53 ARC and Elastic Load Balancing, containing blast radius with cell-based routing, and confronting the write path, where Aurora Global Database's asynchronous replication surfaces a consistency-versus-continuity trade-off that routing alone cannot resolve. Bring your availability-critical workload; we'll map its hedgeable read and routing paths against those that force an explicit consistency decision.

sessions.t: Multi-tenant agentic AI with Aurora and DynamoDB
sessions.a: AI agents are autonomous, stateful, and capable of invoking external tools. In a multi-tenant SaaS system, every one of those capabilities is a potential data isolation failure. In this workshop, build a complete multi-tenant agentic AI solution enforcing tenant isolation across Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with row-level security, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon S3 Vectors. Implement tenant-scoped vector stores for RAG, agent memory backed by multiple database engines, MCP-based tool authorization gated by subscription tier, and usage metering. Leave with a working reference architecture that prevents cross-tenant data leakage. Bring a laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Multi-Tenant Agentic Platforms: A Scalable Reference Architecture
sessions.a: SaaS is going AI-native. ISVs must orchestrate third-party agents at scale. This session presents a multi-tenant architecture covering MCP, A2A, and AgentCore for orchestration, entitlement-based monetization, secure token exchange, agent lifecycle via Agent Registry, and cross-tenant observability.

sessions.t: Multi-tenant compute modernization with Amazon EMR on EKS
sessions.a: What does it take to run millions of diverse jobs a day across many tenants without costs spiraling or one bad workload taking down the fleet? In this chalk talk, we explore how organizations modernize a multi-tenant compute layer on EMR on EKS to serve batch analytics, streaming, ML, and agentic AI from one platform. We whiteboard the choices that make it possible: custom bin packing to mix heterogeneous tenant workloads efficiently, EKS provisioned control planes to sustain high job throughput per cluster, and Graviton to drive down cost per job. Bring your scaling challenges and we'll design solutions together.

sessions.t: Multi-tenant isolation with IAM: ABAC, session tags, and token vending machines
sessions.a: Multi-tenant SaaS has two isolation options: application-layer filtering or IAM enforcement. Filtering requires every query and API call to add tenant scoping — one missed filter leaks data. IAM enforcement holds even when code has a bug, and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes it work without per-tenant policy explosion. We cover the stack: ABAC session tags, a Token Vending Machine minting tenant-scoped STS credentials, IAM condition keys for DynamoDB/S3 partition boundaries, and a credential-caching model that keeps latency acceptable at millions of requests per second across thousands of tenants. Leave with a deployable reference architecture and policy template.

sessions.a: Multi-tenant SaaS has two isolation options: application-layer filtering or IAM enforcement. Filtering requires every query and API call to add tenant scoping — one missed filter leaks data. IAM enforcement holds even when code has a bug, and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes it work without per-tenant policy explosion. sessions.t: Multi-tenant SaaS and agentic apps on Amazon EKS
sessions.a: Amazon EKS has become the runtime of choice for ISVs building agentic SaaS, offering the control, workload isolation, and networking flexibility that managed runtimes cannot. The challenge is multi-tenancy: how do you run agent workloads for hundreds of tenants on shared infrastructure without blast radius, cost leakage, or isolation drift? In this workshop, build a multi-tenant agent deployment on EKS with tenant isolation across namespaces and network policies, IRSA-backed credentials per agent workload, and per-tenant observability via OpenTelemetry. Each lab ends with an isolation proof. Leave with a reference architecture you can apply directly to your cluster.

sessions.t: Navigating mergers and divestitures across multiple AWS organizations
sessions.a: Enterprises go through mergers, face divestitures, and inherit multiple AWS Organizations, each with its own structure and identity provider. Consolidating or separating these environments is complex. This interactive session covers patterns for merging AWS organizations, managing multiple organizations in parallel, and splitting organizations cleanly. You dive into the identity challenge of migrating between Microsoft Entra ID, Google, and Okta when each entity brings its own IdP to AWS. You leave with practical patterns and lessons learned engagements with customers like you.

sessions.t: Navigating the Inter-workings of an Agentic SOC & Threat Hunting Analyst
sessions.a: Security analysts face an expanding attack surface with finite time and attention. In this session, we show how analysts can leverage AI-powered agents to accelerate their core workflows — from automated triage and log correlation to proactive threat hunting across CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and threat intelligence feeds. Walk through real investigation scenarios where AI handles the repetitive evidence gathering while analysts focus on judgment calls: scoping impact, deciding containment actions, and validating findings. You will see how to configure trust boundaries so agents act within your approved scope, how source attribution ensures every AI-surfaced claim traces back to a specific log, and how to evaluate whether the AI is actually making your team faster.

sessions.t: Need for Speed: The journey to high EBS performance on EC2 instances
sessions.a: Achieving consistent, low-latency block storage at cloud scale requires rethinking every layer of the IO stack. In this session, we walk you through the architectural evolution of Amazon EBS, and show how a series of innovations reduced hypervisor overhead, slashed network latency, and enabled higher block storage IOPS and throughput on your EC2 instances. We will also discuss how Nitro enabled specific EBS features such as Instance bandwidth Configuration, Torn Write Protection, and detailed performance statistics via NVMe logs. Bring your questions and leave with an understanding of how EBS delivers high performing block storage for your mission-critical applications.

sessions.t: Network Firewall deployment models: pros, cons, best practices
sessions.a: One firewall, many ways to deploy it, and each mode unlocks a different architectural superpower. This session maps your options: distributed, centralized, multi-endpoint, explicit proxy, and the newest firewall modes. Through real architectures, you'll see where each one shines, how they scale, and the patterns that make your network security clean, flexible, and future-ready. Whether you're protecting a single VPC or a global multi-account estate, you'll leave knowing exactly which mode fits your environment and why. If you route traffic through AWS, this is the map that gets you there faster.

sessions.t: Network firewall deployment without the guesswork: codify, deploy, done
sessions.a: Level up your firewall policy operations at scale in this hands-on workshop. Learn to integrate AWS Network Firewall into an existing AWS environment using Terraform. Starting with a realistic multi-VPC setup with AWS Transit Gateway, you will deploy Network Firewall and configure routing, inspection, and logging in minutes using reusable modules. You will then implement the latest Network Firewall features such as web category filtering, JA4 fingerprinting, and EventBridge automation. By the end of this session you will have both practical experience adding Network Firewall to existing environments and reusable patterns ready for your own infrastructure.

sessions.t: Network firewall deployment without the guesswork: codify, deploy, done
sessions.a: Level up your firewall policy operations at scale in this hands-on workshop. Learn to integrate AWS Network Firewall into an existing AWS environment using Terraform. Starting with a realistic multi-VPC setup with AWS Transit Gateway, you will deploy Network Firewall and configure routing, inspection, and logging in minutes using reusable modules. You will then implement the latest Network Firewall features such as web category filtering, JA4 fingerprinting, and EventBridge automation. By the end of this session you will have both practical experience adding Network Firewall to existing environments and reusable patterns ready for your own infrastructure.

sessions.t: Network observability on Amazon EKS: from blind spots to insights
sessions.a: As container workloads grow more distributed and interconnected, the network between them becomes the hardest thing to see. Traffic sprawls across pods, nodes, and AZs, quietly driving up cost through inter-AZ transfer and NAT processing, and when latency spikes, it is hard to tell which flows are responsible. This chalk talk explores how to close that gap with Container Network Observability, Network Flow Monitor, and OpenTelemetry-based Container Insights on Amazon EKS. See how to trace traffic across pods, nodes, and AZs. Learn how to attribute network cost and latency to the workloads driving them, and turn those signals into action.

sessions.t: Network observability on Amazon EKS: from blind spots to insights

sessions.t: Network policy at scale: orchestrate security across organization
sessions.a: As AI workloads multiply and organizations scale to hundreds of accounts, managing network security policies manually becomes a liability. AWS Firewall Manager deploys WAF, Shield, and Network Firewall across your entire multi-account environment from a single policy definition. This session covers best practices for defense-in-depth using Firewall Manager, whether you are rolling out AWS WAF, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, or AWS Network Firewall at scale. Leave with an actionable deployment blueprint for centralized network security orchestration.

sessions.t: Network security architecture: Deployment patterns for firewalls
sessions.a: As organizations scale across multiple accounts with hybrid connectivity, designing effective network inspection becomes critical. Join this chalk talk to discuss deployment patterns for AWS Network Firewall and Gateway Load Balancer with third-party firewalls for ingress and egress inspection.

sessions.t: Network security architecture: Deployment patterns for firewalls
sessions.a: As organizations scale across multiple accounts with hybrid connectivity, designing effective network inspection becomes critical. Join this chalk talk to discuss deployment patterns for AWS Network Firewall and Gateway Load Balancer with third-party firewalls for ingress and egress inspection.

sessions.t: Network Security for AI Agents on AgentCore
sessions.a: AI agents decide at runtime which endpoints to call, and that decision can bypass your security review. In this SimuLearn session, you deploy an agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in VPC mode and route its outbound traffic through AWS Network Firewall. You configure a default-deny policy with an approved-domain allow list, then prove it works: an approved call succeeds while an unapproved call gets dropped. The firewall log becomes your audit evidence.

sessions.t: Network Security Innovations for Agentic Workloads
sessions.a: AI agents plan and execute actions autonomously, at machine speed, with real-world consequences. Unlike traditional automation that follows pre-defined network paths, agent traffic is non-deterministic, calling different APIs and chaining different services each time it runs. In this session, we cover the network security capabilities AWS has built for this shift. You'll see how to inspect and control autonomous traffic at every layer, from DNS resolution to application-layer filtering, enforce least-privilege connectivity for agents, and detect anomalous behavior in machine-to-machine communication.

sessions.t: Never Start Over: Chat to Co-Browse, Voice and Video on Amazon Connect Customer
sessions.a: Your customer is halfway through an application in your app, and stuck. Today they abandon it, call you, and start explaining from scratch. In this hands-on workshop you build a single unbroken conversation that escalates in richness without losing context. A customer opens chat inside your application. When they stall on a form, the agent co-browses the page and sees the blocking field, then uses agent assist to answer a policy question with cited sources. The conversation carries into an in-app call, context intact, no phone number and no repeated details. Documents are reviewed over screen share, identity is confirmed over video, and because it's a joint application the co-applicant and a product specialist join the same call. Walk away with an escalation pattern combining persistent context, WebRTC channels and AI-assisted agents, for any high-consideration interaction.

sessions.t: Next-gen threat detection: GuardDuty advanced security capabilities
sessions.a: Amazon GuardDuty protects millions of accounts using AI and ML models purpose-built for cloud security, and the detection engine keeps getting smarter without requiring action from you. In this session, the lead scientist behind GuardDuty's detection engine takes you inside the research. Learn how the team designs models for security inference at scale, uses distillation and reinforcement learning to keep detection cost-efficient without sacrificing accuracy, and distinguishes normal from anomalous behavior without using customer data for training. See how these advances translate into expanded coverage, faster detection of sophisticated threats, and deeper investigation workflows. You leave with an understanding of the engineering tradeoffs behind AI-native threat detection at AWS scale and how to operationalize the latest capabilities.

sessions.t: Nine Seconds to Zero: Protecting AWS from AI Agent Disasters
sessions.a: In April 2026, an AI coding agent deleted a company's entire production database in nine seconds, without being asked. The agent was confidently wrong and had the permissions to act on it. In this session, we recreate that incident live using Amazon Bedrock, walk through every failure in the chain, then rebuild the architecture with six hardening layers: Bedrock Guardrails, human approval gates, least-privilege IAM, deletion protection, isolated backups, and real-time monitoring. Walk away with a concrete checklist for designing AI-assisted systems that plan for when the AI is wrong, not just when it performs perfectly.

sessions.t: Nitro Isolation Engine: Formally verifying confidentiality
sessions.a: What does it mean, *precisely*, for the data of a virtual machine to be confidential? Answering this question will take us on a journey into low-level systems and high-level mathematics as we unpack this question in the context of the AWS Nitro System, the underlying virtualization platform that powers Amazon EC2. You will discover the low-level hardware and software that isolate virtual machines, our precise mathematical definition of confidentiality, and the methods we use to establish this crucial property for the AWS Nitro Isolation Engine. No background in virtualization systems or formal verification is expected.

sessions.t: No Data Left Behind: The AI-Ready Path Through AWS (sponsored by Qlik)
sessions.a: Your enterprise data is scattered across SAP, mainframes, databases, and cloud platforms that were never designed to talk to each other — and every AI initiative depends on enabling that communication. This session shows how Qlik and AWS modernize that data without downtime, rewrites, or re-platforming risk: zero-footprint CDC, Qlik Open Lakehouse with Apache Iceberg and Amazon Athena, Spark Structured Streaming on Amazon EMR, and governed data products built for AI. You'll also get a bonus preview of Qlik's Studio AI Assistant on Amazon Bedrock and what's next for agentic workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Qlik, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: No room for error: deploying trusted AI when the stakes are high (sponsored by Monte Carlo)
sessions.a: Deploying agents at scale is a major endeavor for any organization; in healthcare, the stakes are especially high. Unpredictable behaviors & unreliable outputs pose a risk to patients, invite scrutiny from regulators, & erode hard-won institutional trust. Regulated industries must balance accuracy alongside their drive to innovate. Barr Moses, co-founder & CEO of Monte Carlo, will delve into this challenging topic with leaders from GE Healthcare. They’ll dissect some of the most difficult failure modes for agents & discuss how reliability practices have to evolve as teams scale agentic workflows in high-stakes environments. Discussed: how AI itself can be turned back on the problem of observing, resolving, and optimizing agents as well as building the guardrails, ownership models, & trust infrastructure that let a highly regulated organization move quickly without compromising on trust. This presentation is brought to you by Monte Carlo, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Northwestern Mutual: Reinventing policy servicing with agentic AI
sessions.a: Financial representatives at Northwestern Mutual traditionally logged service requests and waited for back-office resolution. In this session, we'll walk through the production architecture behind this transformation: Amazon Bedrock Agents connected to core insurance systems through the Model Context Protocol, with orchestration and governance controls designed for a regulated environment. We'll cover authorization patterns, auditability, human oversight, and lessons learned moving from proof of concept to production. Representatives now resolve significantly more requests directly—reducing resolution times, improving good-order processing, and driving higher satisfaction, with participants reporting better outcomes for their clients.

sessions.t: Not all bots are bad: Building a secure perimeter with AWS WAF
sessions.a: Today's edge traffic is a mix of customers, AI agents, scrapers, and bad actors — and treating them all the same costs you either security or revenue. This session shows how to turn AWS WAF into a decision layer that classifies traffic in real time and routes it intelligently: legitimate users get a fast lane, suspicious traffic gets diverted into deception environments that waste attackers' time and reveal their intent, and AI agents get differentiated treatment that opens the door to new monetization models — all without touching your origin logic. You'll leave with a practical blueprint for classification-driven traffic control, deception-based threat response, and monitoring patterns you can put into production right away.

sessions.t: Now serverless has servers. What now?
sessions.a: I spent years advocating for serverless, but as a CTO, I could not always see a viable path to bring it into certain business scenarios. In this talk, I share what has changed with the new AWS capabilities, why this can change the game for larger companies, and, along the way, I explore the concepts and how these services work in more depth to help us think about architecture with more clarity.

sessions.t: NVIDIA Nemotron on AWS for Enterprise Agent Orchestration (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.a: Vanguard is evaluating NVIDIA Nemotron models as a fast and accurate routing layer for its enterprise multi-agent platform. Vanguard will share its experience deploying and benchmarking Nemotron 3 Nano and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning with NVIDIA NIM on AWS, including its approach to measuring routing accuracy, end-to-end completion time, and application-level quality. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: OAuth delegation patterns design for AI agents with Amazon BedRock AgentCore Identity
sessions.a: AI agents act on behalf of users and systems, but how do you delegate the right access without over-permissioning? In this chalk talk, we explore authorization delegation patterns using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity with code examples. We cover every relevant OAuth grant flow: authorization code for user-delegated access, client credentials for machine-to-machine, token exchange for on-behalf-of propagation, and Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) for fine-grained permission scoping. Explore how each pattern maps to real agent scenarios and leave with a decision framework for your architecture.

sessions.t: Observability and operations in the AI era
sessions.a: Generative AI broke the assumptions traditional monitoring was built on, and teams struggle to keep non-deterministic systems predictable, explainable, and affordable. This session opens on that challenge, then shows how the newest observability capabilities give you visibility into model quality, cost, and agent behavior across your AI stack, using traces, spans, and confidence scoring, illustrated with real customer patterns.

sessions.t: Observability-driven scaling: Teaching EKS clusters to right-size themselves
sessions.a: Scaling container workloads reactively by waiting for CPU to spike or pods to crash leaves money on the table and risks user-facing latency. This chalk talk explores observability-driven scaling: using CloudWatch Container Insights, KEDA, and custom metrics pipelines to make Amazon EKS clusters anticipate demand before it arrives. We walk through real architectures where teams replaced reactive HPA with predictive scaling informed by business metrics, reduced over-provisioning by 40%, and cut P99 latency during traffic ramps. Bring your scaling headaches and we'll whiteboard solutions together.

sessions.t: Observability for AI agents: Strands, OpenTelemetry, and Langfuse
sessions.a: You're running AI agents in cloud ops, but can you see inside them? In this hands-on workshop, deploy a Strands Agents SDK agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, then wire up full observability using Strands' built-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation and Langfuse (open-source) as the backend. Trace every LLM call, tool invocation, and reasoning step. Debug failures, analyze token costs, version prompts, and score output quality — all with open source and open standards.

sessions.t: Observability for AI agents: Strands, OpenTelemetry, and Langfuse
sessions.a: You're running AI agents in cloud ops, but can you see inside them? sessions.t: Observability patterns for agentic AI in production
sessions.a: AI agents are non-deterministic, multi-step, and make autonomous decisions and traditional APM isn't enough. Explore observability patterns for agentic workloads: reasoning chain tracing, token cost attribution, guardrail monitoring, and multi-agent coordination. We'll whiteboard architectures in real time. Bring your toughest production agent monitoring questions and leave with actionable patterns.

sessions.t: Observability patterns for Microsoft workloads migrating to AWS
sessions.a: Migrating Microsoft workloads to AWS requires rethinking your monitoring strategy. Existing observability approaches may not translate seamlessly to the cloud, creating blind spots that lead to costly downtime and degraded end-user experiences. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how to strengthen your observability posture as you migrate .NET applications, SQL Server databases, and Windows services to AWS. We'll cover how to use AWS-native and open-source tooling to monitor workloads across VMs, containers, and serverless, giving you confidence to migrate faster while maintaining operational excellence. Bring your questions.

sessions.t: Observable Agents with Lambda Durable Functions and OpenTelemetry
sessions.a: When AI agents run as long-lived, multi-invocation workflows on Lambda Durable Functions, standard observability breaks down. A single durable execution spanning five specialists producing independent telemetry, replays pollute logs with duplicates, and no tool can tell you which agents are failing across thousands of concurrent runs. We'll build a multi-agent purchasing coordinator with Lambda durable functions, instrument it with the OpenTelemetry plugin for one coherent trace across all invocations, and CloudWatch insights to answer fleet-wide queries with business context. Attendees leave with fully observable architecture and the investigation pattern from CloudWatch alarm to end-to-end traces and correlated log entries.

sessions.t: Observe AI agents beyond your perimeter
sessions.a: Your developers are burning tokens on AI coding agents with zero visibility. Claude Code and OpenAI Codex run on laptops, outside your perimeter, with no telemetry reaching your observability backend. In this session, we fix that. Using native OpenTelemetry export and Amazon CloudWatch's OTLP endpoint with a single bearer token, with no collectors, no sidecars, no credential wiring, we ship metrics (token usage, cost, productivity), logs (tool decisions, errors), and traces (agent reasoning chains) directly from developer machines. Then we build a live dashboard with per-team cost attribution and anomaly alerting, all queryable with PromQL. Walk out ready to deploy in minutes.

sessions.t: Observe, investigate, act: smarter ops with Amazon OpenSearch Service
sessions.a: AI agents are becoming your best investigators, triaging alerts, correlating telemetry, and performing root-cause analysis across metrics, logs, and traces in seconds. And agents are a critical workload to observe: you need LLM trace monitoring, per-call cost attribution, and multi-agent workflow debugging to keep token spend and accuracy under control. Whether you're scaling an existing observability platform or modernizing your stack, Amazon OpenSearch Service addresses both sides. In this session, we present capabilities including native OpenTelemetry ingestion, MCP-based agent skills for natural-language issue investigation, and an optimized log-analytics engine delivering 4× price-performance at petabyte scale. Learn how to put AI agents to work on your observability data and how to keep them accountable in production.

sessions.t: Observe me that: Easy OpenTelemetry monitoring for your systems (sponsored by Dash0)
sessions.a: OpenTelemetry is the de-facto open-source standard for vendor-neutral traces, metrics, and logs. But, if you are not an OpenTelemetry expert, the learning curve to add it to your systems can be intimidating. This session covers how to bring OpenTelemetry with zero-code/no-touch instrumentation in applications running on AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2, ECS and EKS, as well as how to bring into your OpenTelemetry pipelines telemetry from various AWS managed services and how to use agentic skills to level up the quality of your instrumentations and get better value out of your telemetry backends, coding agents, and AI tools. You will leave this session with a concrete map to get your OpenTelemetry journey started with tangible results in minutes. This presentation is brought to you by Dash0, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: One agent, any robot: building physical AI with Strands Robots
sessions.a: Physical AI puts agents in the real world. This chalk talk builds a robotics agent with the Strands Robots SDK: one Robot() call gives an agent hands — a MuJoCo simulation by default, real hardware with one code parameter change. We'll whiteboard the loop around the embodied agent: perception, a vision-language-action policy (GR00T, Cosmos 3, LeRobot), and low-level control. We'll cover the the edge-to-cloud intelligence split, the peer-to-peer mesh and AWS IoT bridge coordinating a fleet, and sim-to-real transfer.

sessions.t: One agent to thousands: Building for scale with Newforma
sessions.a: When every team builds agents independently, you get the same ungovernable sprawl that drove the shift from artisanal EC2 to container platforms. Agents are non-deterministic workloads that require deterministic governance, and this tension drives every platform decision, from dual orchestration for known vs. emergent topologies, to policy-based boundaries around soft reasoning, to defense layers that compose without coupling. We walk through how Newforma operationalized this architecture on AWS, and attendees leave understanding how to layer orchestration, policy, and defense into an enterprise agent platform that scales safely.

sessions.t: One AI Assistant, Every Data Source: Unifying Access with Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Your data lives in one platform. Your reports live in another. Your documents live somewhere else. Every time someone needs an answer, they spend time figuring out where to look before they can act. Decisions slow down. Teams duplicate work because they cannot find what already exists. New employees take months to become productive because institutional knowledge is trapped in systems they do not know how to navigate. Hear from a customer who solved this by giving their team a single AI assistant that connects across all their enterprise systems. Instead of training people on where to find information, they ask Amazon Quick and get answers grounded in their real business data, regardless of where it lives. Learn how they configured the integration, how their teams adopted it, and what changed about the speed and quality of decision-making across the organization.

sessions.t: One Control Plane for Every Agent: Architecture Patterns for Cost, Risk, and ROI (sponsored by Boomi)
sessions.a: Every agent call carries cost, permission, and blast radius, and as agents multiply across tools, frameworks, and SaaS, the gaps compound: uncapped spend, unapproved permissions, no shared record. This session breaks down an AI infrastructure layer, running on AWS, that governs every model, agent, and system. A design-time layer publishes an approved catalog of agents, tools, and MCP servers; a runtime layer routes, meters, and enforces policy on every call before it executes. See how spend caps, in-tenant SLMs, and governed APIs turn cost into a controlled input, while one trace gives finance, security, and engineering a shared, audit-ready record. This presentation is brought to you by Boomi, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: One Control to Rule Them All: Guardrail Automation for Every Identity (sponsored by Sonrai Security)
sessions.a: Separate guardrails for humans, machine identities, and AI agents get messy, and rewriting every IAM policy takes forever. SCPs deployed at scope are easy to write. What follows is not. Nobody can say what a policy will break, so it never deploys. Someone gets blocked and the fix becomes a two hour hunt. The tenth control behaves nothing like the first. New accounts inherit none of it. This lightning talk answers all four using only AWS Organizations, SCPs, and RCPs. See how usage data makes a default deny safe, how access returns in seconds, and how least privilege holds. This presentation is brought to you by Sonrai Security, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: One Data Foundation for Agentic AI and Real-Time Analytics on AWS (sponsored by Databricks)
sessions.a: Your team is under pressure to deliver real-time applications, AI agents, operational experiences, and analytics faster—but separate databases, serving layers, and pipelines create stale data, duplicated copies, governance gaps, and scaling challenges. In this session, we’ll explore how Databricks on AWS brings these workloads together with Lakehouse//RT, Lakebase, and the Lakehouse Transactional Application Platform (LTAP). See how teams serve low-latency, high-concurrency analytics, power operational applications and AI agents with live transactional data, and analyze data where it is created—all from one platform and one governed copy of data. You’ll leave with practical architecture guidance for building reliable real-time and AI applications on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Databricks, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: One query across every signal: centralized security investigations at scale
sessions.a: When an alert fires, your first question is "what else happened?" Answering it means correlating API calls, network flows, DNS queries, and application logs, often across dozens of accounts and regions. In this session, we show how security practitioners centralize every signal into a single queryable layer using Amazon CloudWatch unified data store, then investigate incidents with faceted queries that span all telemetry types at once. We walk through building always-on visibility dashboards, running cross-account investigations without switching tools, and using AI-assisted analytics to surface context before you need to go looking for it. You leave with a reference architecture for turning centralized logs into faster investigations and clearer security posture.

sessions.t: One-Way Doors: Launching a Regulated Financial Exchange on AWS in 2026
sessions.a: "AWS turns 20 this year. Starting fresh in 2026 means navigating hundreds of services with no clear map for which decisions are one-way doors. I'll share how we built a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse from the AWS Organizations up. The full security stack (Access Analyzer, Config, GuardDuty, Macie, Security Hub, and WAF) built in the right order from day one. We almost walked through the wrong door. A pre-launch architecture review with our engineers and AWS solution architects caught it in time. Here's how to have that conversation before it's too late."

sessions.t: On-Policy Distillation on HyperPod EKS: Train Smarter Small Models
sessions.a: Frontier models are powerful but costly to deploy. On-policy distillation, adopted by Qwen3, MiMo, and GLM-5, lets you compress a large teacher into a lean, domain-specialized student by training on the student's own rollouts with dense token-level feedback. Unlike Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, it's cheaper, more stable, and doesn't require a verifier. In this code talk, walk through a working implementation on HyperPod EKS: orchestrate teacher inference and student training across GPU pools, manage the rollout buffer, and evaluate convergence.

sessions.t: On-premises to AWS readiness: foundational decisions before your migration
sessions.a: Successful migrations are shaped by decisions made well before the first workload moves. This session explores how choices in licensing, operating models, technology architecture, and organizational readiness influence migration outcomes, whether moving off VMware, aging infrastructure, or other on-premises environments. Learn how to assess dependencies and business constraints, align stakeholders, and build a plan that avoids common pitfalls and adapts as your environment evolves.

sessions.t: Ontology-Powered AI Agents: Verifiable Decisions Across Manufacturing
sessions.a: Manufacturing stakeholders make dozens of high-velocity decisions daily. Each must be traceable, defensible, and grounded in enterprise knowledge and lifecycle data. Yet the systems informing these decisions remain siloed, and AI agents reasoning over this fragmented data cannot produce verifiable results. Ontologies solve this by structuring manufacturing knowledge so agents can trace decisions back to their source data. In this chalk talk, we show how ontology-grounded agents, powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK, make verifiable decisions across the lifecycle with a live demo. Attendees leave with a reference architecture, best practices, and a clear path to building verifiable AI agents for manufacturing.

sessions.t: Open for Business: OpenAI on AWS
sessions.a: There is more than one way to put OpenAI to work on AWS, from coding agents that ship production code to knowledge workflows and custom agents. This session tours OpenAI on AWS, starting with the latest OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock. Put them to work through two agentic surfaces: Codex for coding and ChatGPT Work for knowledge work. Then explore Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents powered by OpenAI, for deploying OpenAI-powered agents in your AWS environment. Leave with a map of OpenAI on AWS and when to choose each path.

sessions.t: Open source agent observability and evals with AgentCore and Langfuse (sponsored by ClickHouse)
sessions.a: Production agents need more than infrastructure. They need an open source foundation for understanding behavior, evaluating quality, and improving continuously without sacrificing control of their data. In this session, learn how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Langfuse combine secure agent infrastructure with open source observability and evaluation, powered by ClickHouse. See how teams capture OpenTelemetry traces, debug trajectories and tool calls, evaluate production quality, turn failures into datasets, and prevent regressions before deployment. We will share a practical architecture for unifying policy and telemetry across AgentCore, EKS, and other runtimes so teams can ship trustworthy agents faster. This presentation is brought to you by ClickHouse, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Open-weights at work: Scaling AI without scaling the bill
sessions.a: Agentic and coding workloads are multiplying token consumption, and paying frontier prices on every call adds up fast. This chalk talk shows how open weight models on Amazon Bedrock let you scale that growth affordably without giving up quality or security. We walk through multi-model strategies for agentic and code generation workloads, the unit economics of open weight versus frontier, and how Bedrock's inference engine design keeps security strong regardless of where a model came from. You leave with a practical path to cost-efficient inference at scale.

sessions.t: Operating Lambda at scale: Choosing the right execution model
sessions.a: You're running workloads across Lambda, EC2, and containers because no single service handled orchestration, always-on compute, and isolated execution. Lambda's new execution models change that: durable functions add checkpointed orchestration, Managed Instances provide always-on compute at EC2 economics, and MicroVMs offer hardware-level sandboxes with persistent state. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the operational decision tree: which execution model to standardize on for each workload class, how to manage mixed-model deployments, monitoring differences across models, and when to migrate workloads between them. Bring your workload portfolio. We'll help you build an operational playbook for multi-model Lambda.

sessions.t: Operating Serverless at scale: What changes at 1000+ functions
sessions.a: What works at 10 Lambda functions may not work at 1,000. Deployments that took seconds now take hours. A single misconfigured function triggers account-level throttling. Observability drowns in noise. In this chalk talk, we discuss what changes at scale: deployment strategies that roll out code safely across hundreds of functions, account structure and concurrency management to prevent blast radius problems, observability approaches that surface signal without drowning in cardinality, and platform engineering patterns that let application teams ship independently. We share what large-scale Serverless operators do differently and where the common pitfalls are.

sessions.t: Operationalize enterprise event routing with Amazon EventBridge
sessions.a: Scaling event-driven architectures across multiple AWS accounts has long meant managing fragmented buses, cross-account routing complexity, and developer friction. Explore how Amazon EventBridge delivers the scale, reliability, and developer experience that modern event-driven applications demand. It simplifies event routing across accounts and teams. Whether you're consolidating existing event infrastructure or designing a new event-driven platform, you'll leave with a clearer picture of how to reduce operational complexity and ship faster.

sessions.t: Operational resilience in regulated environments with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.a: As software delivery accelerates, financial services organizations struggle to manage incidents across fragmented toolchains. In this chalk talk, learn how AWS DevOps Agent acts as an always-on operations teammate for regulated environments—resolving incidents autonomously, strengthening systems proactively, and validating releases before they reach production. We'll whiteboard four patterns: how the agent investigates and resolves incidents in minutes; how the agent learns from past incidents to recommend improvements; how on-demand SRE tasks give your team instant operational intelligence; and how release readiness reviews catch compliance and dependency risks before code ships. Bring your operational challenges and leave with best practices.

sessions.t: Optimize AI apps on Amazon Bedrock for cost, latency, and control
sessions.a: As AI workloads scale, engineers face complex trade-offs between cost, latency, and response quality. This code talk explores advanced optimisation techniques for production AI applications on Amazon Bedrock: prompt engineering, model selection, caching, and context window management. Through live coding, attendees examine the reasoning behind each design decision, observe cost impact via AWS Billing and Cost Management, and learn to instrument apps to detect performance regressions. Understanding the tokenomics of your AI stack is essential to operating efficiently at scale.

sessions.t: Optimize AI costs with practical deployment blueprints for analytics on AWS
sessions.a: Delivering AI at enterprise scale demands more than great models — it requires a data and analytics foundation engineered for cost efficiency from day one. This session examines proven deployment blueprints that pair AWS analytics services with AI/ML workloads to maximize price-performance. We explore patterns including right-sizing your analytics infrastructure for training data preparation, on-demand feature extraction, auto-scaling continuous ETL pipelines and selecting optimal storage formats to minimize costs. Through detailed architectural walkthroughs, you'll learn how to instrument cost observability across your analytics stack, apply tagging strategies for AI workload attribution, and implement governance guardrails that prevent runaway spend — turning your data platform into a competitive advantage for AI delivery.

sessions.t: Optimize AI inference costs: Compare token economics on AWS silicon
sessions.a: Most enterprises run their entire AI pipeline on GPU and can overpay. AWS's silicon portfolio (Trainium & Graviton) along with NVIDIA GPU, Intel, and AMD all offer radically different cost-per-token economics for different workloads. This session delivers a decision framework for matching silicon to workload: training and inference on Trainium, RAG pipelines on Graviton, real-time agents on GPU, batch on Intel/AMD. Includes Bedrock vs. self-host crossover analysis, volume thresholds, and the architecture patterns to put the savings into practice.

sessions.t: Optimize AI workloads with Amazon ElastiCache Serverless
sessions.a: Building highly scalable, high-performance AI and data-driven applications requires intelligent caching strategies. In this session, learn how to build with Amazon ElastiCache to scale workloads across caching patterns such as session caching, KV-caching, and more. Dive deep into microsecond latency networking optimizations that enable sub-millisecond response times, and explore common performance pitfalls with practical solutions to keep applications running smoothly.

sessions.t: Optimize analytics workloads on Amazon EKS for performance and cost
sessions.a: The analytics landscape is undergoing a shift as global data volumes grow at unprecedented rates. This rapid growth, combined with rising demand for real-time analytics, is driving organizations to modernize and optimize their data processing pipelines and analytics workloads. EKS’s cost-performance and scalability make it the best place to run these workloads. In this workshop, you will learn hands-on how to optimize EKS for Spark & Kafka workloads using different Karpenter configurations, Spot and Graviton instances, and NVMe volumes. You will also explore observability best practices and granular cost visualization per job. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Optimize a .NET application for Graviton 5 using AWS Transform
sessions.a: Take a Windows .NET application, run AWS Transform end-to-end (assess, modernize, deploy), and benchmark on Graviton. Compare against the original x86 baseline, inspect what Q got wrong, and tune the result. Covers .NET Framework to modern .NET migration, Lambda packaging on Graviton, and CI integration patterns from production migrations.

sessions.t: Optimize container observability to reduce cost
sessions.a: At scale, container environments generate metrics and logs that increase both cost and noise for engineering teams. This session explores architectural strategies for managing observability data across containerized workloads using OpenTelemetry. Learn how to control metric cardinality, design sampling policies that preserve critical signals, and evaluate managed backend tradeoffs. You'll leave with a framework for building cost-aware container observability.

sessions.t: Optimize cost & performance in Amazon RDS for SQL Server
sessions.a: Cost and performance are top of mind for customers, and these topics go hand in hand. In this chalk talk, learn how to deploy a performant and cost-effective Amazon RDS for SQL Server solution that fits your needs. Explore RDS monitoring tools and native SQL Server features that can be leveraged to pinpoint query inefficiencies, optimize workloads, and right-size your database instances for both cost and peak performance.

sessions.t: Optimize HPC with storage for throughput and IOPS
sessions.a: High-performance computing workloads demand storage that keeps pace with thousands of compute nodes processing data in parallel. Amazon FSx for Lustre delivers sub-millisecond latencies and high throughput without the operational burden of managing a parallel file system. Amazon FSx for OpenZFS adds high IOPS with consistent low-latency response for latency-sensitive workloads. Explore how to select the right deployment type based on your workload profile, leverage native S3 integration for data pipelines, and right-size performance independently from capacity. Bring your questions about CFD (computational fluid dynamics), genomics, semiconductor design, weather modeling, and other compute-intensive workloads.

sessions.t: Optimize performance and cost for archival data with Amazon S3
sessions.a: Not all data needs frequent access, but it still needs the right retrieval strategy when called upon. In this chalk talk, learn how to design a cost-effective archival storage strategy using Amazon S3 Glacier storage classes. We cover how to analyze access patterns to identify archival candidates, automate data movement with S3 Lifecycle policies and S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and design restore workflows using S3 Batch Operations and S3 Event Notifications. Whether you're retaining compliance data for years or staging cold datasets for periodic analytics, leave with a practical framework for balancing retrieval performance against long-term storage costs.

sessions.t: Optimize performance and cost of Amazon EBS at massive scale
sessions.a: Managing production workloads across multiple regions while weighing cost and risk requires optimal strategy. With block storage, operating at scale can mean different things, including delivering high IOPS or I/O bandwidth to applications, managing and monitoring millions of volumes, or protecting petabytes of data with stringent RPO and RTO requirements. In this talk, learn best practices for scaling and managing your Amazon EBS environment, including automation, monitoring at scale, and cost-optimization techniques using cloud-native tools to meet your business needs.

sessions.t: Optimize smarter: EKS performance with APerf and AI-powered analysis
sessions.a: Your EKS workload is running, but is it actually efficient? Profile a live application with APerf to see what's consuming CPU cycles: syscall overhead, worker imbalances, inefficient library calls. Issues invisible in dashboards but obvious in a flame graph. APerf Analyzer MCP generates prescriptive guidance, configuration adjustments, and instance recommendations grounded in actual workload behavior. Implement fixes, redeploy, validate. Tasks escalate: fix a worker imbalance, eliminate a blocking call, resolve a writeback burst. Choose Python, Java, or Node.js. A live leaderboard tracks progress—who will finish first?

sessions.t: Optimize your Amazon Aurora resources to reduce costs
sessions.a: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native managed relational database that lets you create, manage, and scale your database resources with ease. In this session, dive deep into Aurora cost components and see how you can use cost-focused features and tooling to optimize costs for your workload without sacrificing performance or scale. Learn how the Aurora I/O-Optimized configuration can help you achieve cost savings for I/O-intensive workloads, and discover how Database Savings Plans can provide additional cost reductions through flexible commitment-based pricing.

sessions.a: Which EC2 instance performs best? It depends on the workload. In this hands-on workshop, learn a repeatable methodology: observe with APerf, find breaking points, diagnose pipeline bottlenecks, and decide by price-performance across AWS Graviton-, Intel-, and AMD-based instances. Then fix code guided by profiling data.

sessions.t: Optimizing agentic AI: Vanguard's production deployment journey
sessions.a: Deploying AI agents in production is just the beginning. Optimizing them at scale is the real challenge. In this session, Vanguard shares how they transformed their investor-facing AI agent from functional to fast, safe, and personal. Learn the techniques—from prompt caching to adaptive thinking to guardrail tuning—that delivered 70%+ latency reduction without sacrificing safety, and how long-term memory now powers personalized conversations across sessions. Walk away with battle-tested patterns for balancing response quality, cost, and speed in agentic AI at enterprise scale.

sessions.t: Optimizing containerized applications with shared file storage
sessions.a: Containerized workloads can face unpredictable latency spikes, throughput bottlenecks, and runaway costs as they scale. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through techniques for identifying these issues and solving them in production environments. Bring your use cases, performance questions, and architecture challenges as we tune Amazon EFS, Amazon S3 Files, and Amazon FSx for real-world EKS and ECS deployments. We'll cover IO profiling, throughput vs. latency tradeoffs, cost-optimization strategies, multi-attach EFS configurations, FSx volume sizing, and POSIX-compatible pipeline design on S3 Files. You'll leave with practical insights you can apply to your environment immediately.

sessions.t: Optimizing Kubernetes in the Age of AI (sponsored by Zesty)
sessions.a: Agentic development dramatically reduces the cost of writing code, but it hasn’t removed the cost of operating it. Infrastructure teams are now responsible for the cost, performance, and reliability of workloads they didn’t build. In this session, we'll explore how these shifts are changing Kubernetes optimization. We'll discuss why CPU, Memory, and GPU resources are often miscalibrated, why native tools like HPA and Karpenter don't solve resource inefficiencies, and how platform teams can maintain cost accountability without slowing developer velocity. You'll leave with practical strategies to continuously optimize resources, improve utilization, and keep Kubernetes infrastructure cost-efficient as AI adoption scales. This presentation is brought to you by Zesty, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Optimizing model performance with agentic loops on AWS Trainium
sessions.a: Extracting peak performance from AI accelerators requires optimization at multiple levels — from framework configuration to individual kernels — and the complexity grows with every new workload. Agentic loops replace this manual work with autonomous profiling, diagnosis, and code generation, iterating toward performance targets without human intervention. In this session, we demonstrate this workflow on AWS Trainium, purpose-built to deliver better price-performance for AI workloads. Explore how these loops identify bottlenecks, how persistent memory prevents repeated failures, and how long-running campaigns uncover optimizations for different inference shapes. Walk away with practical patterns for agentic optimization on purpose-built silicon.

sessions.t: Optimizing prediction market and trading infrastructure
sessions.a: Centralized exchanges, decentralized exchanges, and prediction markets share a critical challenge: managing the tension between resiliency and latency. AWS customers have solved this at scale on low-latency platforms trading digital assets 24/7. In this session, AWS specialists dive deep into architecture patterns and real-world examples addressing each challenge. Leave with best practices for designing resilient, low-latency trading infrastructure using the latest AWS capabilities built for these markets.

sessions.t: Optimizing SAP RISE for Cost and Scale with Intel (sponsored by Intel)
sessions.a: Discover how Intel's custom SAP-certified Intel® Xeon® 6 processor, exclusively available on AWS, transforms and accelerates your SAP RISE journey. Engineered to deliver the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel cloud processors, this powerful solution unlocks up to 50% higher SAPS performance. Whether migrating, consolidating, or scaling SAP workloads, Intel Xeon 6 on AWS empowers organizations to optimize costs, enhance efficiency, and maximize their SAP RISE investment — driving faster, smarter, and more cost-effective outcomes for modern enterprise demands. This presentation is brought to you by Intel, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Orchestrate AI Agents with AgentCore Runtime
sessions.a: You need more than one agent to reason across inventory, shipments, forecasts, and suppliers at the same time. In this lab, you deploy a multi-agent supply chain system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. You load data into DynamoDB, build container images with CodeBuild, and deploy specialist agents plus a supervisor orchestrator powered by Amazon Nova models. The orchestrator classifies questions, routes them to the right specialists in parallel, and synthesizes their responses into one coherent answer.

sessions.t: Orchestrate failover and failback for effective Disaster Recovery
sessions.a: Failing over one app is easy — orchestrating failover and fail back across interdependent apps is where DR plans break. Real recovery requires dependency-aware orchestration across your entire stack. In this code talk, we live-code full-stack Region failover using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) Region switch: building sequenced workflows so databases switch before app tiers, validating steps with health checks, rehearsing with practice runs, and safely reversing the sequence for fail back. Leave ready to replace your paper DR plan with coded, repeatable recovery and measured RTO to prove it.

sessions.t: Orchestrate GuardDuty and Network Firewall to prevent exfiltration
sessions.a: Compromised workloads and AI agents share a common path: outbound channels that most teams barely monitor. From CVE-driven RCE on EC2 to prompt injection on agentic systems, both threats end with unauthorized data leaving your environment. In this session, dive deep into a layered egress architecture combining AWS Network Firewall, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, VPC endpoint policies, SCPs, RCPs, GuardDuty, and IAM Access Analyzer. We'll trace concrete attack scenarios through each control and show how to orchestrate them to prevent data exfiltration.

sessions.t: Orchestrate multi-layer disaster recovery for critical workloads
sessions.a: Your AZ recovery plan and your Region failover plan were probably built by different teams, tested at different times, and have never run together. The result: untested failover paths that turn outages into incidents. Explore how to build a unified recovery framework with Amazon Application Recovery Controller. From zonal autoshift for rapid single-AZ mitigation, to Region switch for cross-Region failover, learn how ARC unifies both layers into a single orchestrated approach. Then discover how to run automated resilience tests that continuously validate your recovery posture before a real event forces the question.

sessions.t: Orchestrating agentic applications with Lambda durable functions
sessions.a: AI agents are powerful, but production workloads need more than an LLM and a prompt. They require deterministic routing, audit trails, compensation logic, and human oversight. In this workshop, build agentic orchestration using AWS Lambda durable functions and MCP tools. Learn to design workflows that checkpoint progress, recover from failures automatically, and pause for human-in-the-loop approval—all without managing additional infrastructure. You'll implement tool-calling patterns, handle multi-step reasoning with retries, and deploy agents that are observable, testable, and production-ready. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Orchestrating agentic workflows: Step Functions & durable functions
sessions.a: AI agents need orchestration that handles long-running tasks, human approvals, and recovery from partial failures. In this chalk talk, compare AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions for agentic workloads, and learn when to choose code-first, replay-based recovery versus visual state-machine semantics. We’ll whiteboard how durable functions checkpoint progress and resume after failures, how Step Functions handle branching and parallel tool calls, and where Lambda MicroVMs fit for sandboxing agent-generated code execution. Bring your architecture questions—we’ll design hybrid patterns that combine both orchestrators based on your workload shape.

sessions.t: Orchestrating AI Agents for Continuous Code Security Hardening
sessions.a: Agentic AI is increasing the rate at which organizations discover and fix security vulnerabilities — and the rate at which findings arrive faster than anyone can act on them. In this workshop, you'll build an agentic security hardening pipeline using Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore: deterministic scanners fan out across code, dependencies, secrets, and infrastructure; reviewer and triage agents correlate and rank what comes back; and policy-as-code gates decide on demonstrated evidence rather than on agents agreeing. You'll learn how to decompose a security audit into parallelizable agent tasks, and how to keep a human holding every consequential decision before changes reach production.

sessions.t: Orchestrating AI agents with AWS serverless services
sessions.a: Production AI agents need orchestration that handles non-deterministic behavior, multi-hour workflows, human approvals, and multi-agent coordination. Learn how AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda durable functions provide the reliability layer that agents demand. We cover patterns for durable execution, human-in-the-loop controls, event-driven agent communication, and the scale-to-zero economics that make serverless the natural home for agentic workloads.

sessions.t: Orchestrating Physical AI workloads on AWS: Compute and pipeline patterns
sessions.a: Physical AI projects — robotics, autonomous systems, digital twins — require complex multi-stage pipelines spanning simulation, training, evaluation, and edge deployment. Each stage demands different compute and orchestration. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architecture patterns combining AWS Batch for parallel simulation, Amazon EKS with Karpenter for heterogeneous GPU/Trainium training, and SageMaker Hyperpod showcasing managed resiliency. We'll compare when to use EKS vs. Batch vs. ParallelCluster, discuss cost optimization with Capacity Blocks and Spot, and solve attendee architectures live on the whiteboard.

sessions.t: Organize Enterprise Knowledge and Secure Data with Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Amazon Quick transforms how teams access insights and automate decisions. In this SimuLearn session, you design Spaces in Quick to organize enterprise knowledge, configure custom Chat Agents with specialized instructions and curated knowledge bases, and integrate Quick with enterprise systems using Actions and connectors backed by Amazon S3 or Amazon DynamoDB. You then apply row-level and column-level security controls to protect sensitive data and explore Quick Research for comprehensive multi-source analysis and reporting.

sessions.t: Origin management for multi-region applications with Amazon CloudFront
sessions.a: In this session, you'll learn comprehensive origin management with Amazon CloudFront to build secure, resilient content delivery systems. We'll cover automatic failover mechanisms with CloudFront and Route 53, configure granular origin routing with CloudFront Functions, and secure origins using S3 with Origin Access Control (OAC) and VPC private origins for enhanced security. We'll explore integrating on-premises infrastructure through AWS Direct Connect for hybrid architectures, and deploy Origin Shield to further optimize cache performance and reduce origin load.

sessions.t: Outrun technical debt in the age of autonomous development
sessions.a: The legacy estate has not gone away. Aging applications with undocumented business logic, outdated frameworks, and platforms nobody wants to touch remain a priority. Agentic tools have increased development velocity, but speed does not eliminate technical debt — it changes its shape. This compounding debt erodes productivity, weakens security posture, and inflates operational cost. Learn how AWS Transform custom and continuous modernization help organizations assess and remediate technical debt at scale — from framework migrations like Angular to React to language translations like C to Rust.

sessions.t: Owning atoms to bits: How AWS accelerates network innovation at scale
sessions.a: At AWS, we design everything within our infrastructure networks—from buildings to fiber, routers to protocols. This atoms-to-bits ownership lets us move at breakneck speed: the moment we spot an opportunity to improve customer performance or resilience, we drive it into production. In this talk, Senior Principal Engineers cover how they applied this pattern to develop the random graph fabrics reshaping data center topologies and highly available systems for machine learning at planet scale. Learn what it takes to continually refresh, upgrade, and re-architect live infrastructure without ever interrupting a single customer workload.

sessions.t: Own Your Harness: Control Cost & Risk in Enterprise-Wide AI Adoption (sponsored by Presidio)
sessions.a: The fastest way to lose control of AI is to let agents multiply without a harness. This talk walks through Presidio's journey from scattered pilots to enterprise-wide adoption, built on a custom orchestration layer that treats cost, identity, and policy as first-class concerns. Attendees will get an inside look at the architectural decisions, guardrails, and economic models that let us scale AI use predictably across the business. If you're weighing governance (cost and risk) against velocity, this is the playbook you want from day one. This presentation is brought to you by Presidio, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Patterns for embedding FinOps into cloud architectural decisions
sessions.a: Every architectural decision carries a cost implication, yet cost is typically discovered in monthly bills rather than design reviews. In this code talk, we demonstrate how to shift FinOps left, optimising before you deploy rather than reacting after. Through two personas, a FinOps engineer and a builder, you will see live how to embed cost governance into infrastructure-as-code, tackle real architectural trade-offs then show how AI coding assistants accelerate this at scale. You will leave with deployable CloudFormation examples and a decision framework for choosing the right cost governance level for your organisation.

sessions.t: Patterns for mitigating AI-powered security threats in financial services
sessions.a: AI-driven vulnerability identification creates elevated risks for financial services organizations as attackers find and exploit software and configuration flaws at machine speed. Patching alone is no longer sufficient. In this chalk talk, we explore mitigation patterns that help financial institutions reduce exposure and strengthen their defensive posture. Walk through how Amazon Inspector, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, AWS Continuum, Kiro, and network isolation work together to detect, contain, and respond to AI-accelerated threats. Attendees will gain mitigation strategies and actionable next steps they can take back to their security teams.

sessions.t: Performance tuning for streaming ingestion with Apache Iceberg
sessions.a: Unlock real-time streaming into Apache Iceberg with advanced performance tuning. Learn how to optimize ingestion pipelines using Apache Kafka and Apache Flink for fraud detection, IoT monitoring, and real-time analytics. This session covers throughput optimization through partitioning, parallelism, write distribution, batching, and checkpoint tuning. Discover techniques to reduce small file issues with compaction, minimize write amplification with deduplication, and maintain low-latency ingestion at scale, turning raw streaming data into actionable insights with efficiency and reliability.

sessions.t: Persistent memory, shared context, instant discovery. Solving storage for AI agents
sessions.a: Production AI agents need to remember what happened yesterday, share work with other agents today, and find the right data in milliseconds. Most storage wasn't built for this. This session introduces the S3 stack purpose-built for agentic workloads. S3 Files provides a shared file system for multi-agent artifact handoff. S3 Vectors stores embeddings as long-term semantic memory that persists across sessions and restarts. S3 Metadata makes every object discoverable by tag, time, or custom attribute without scanning. Learn reference architectures for coordination, checkpointing, least-privilege access patterns, and framework integration.

sessions.t: Philips' Agentic AI Leap: 45 Days to Minutes on Sales Quotes (sponsored by EPAM)
sessions.a: Philips faced a 45-day sales quoting bottleneck in digital pathology, chasing systems and spreadsheets on every deal. With EPAM and AWS, Philips built Sensei, a conversational AI sales agent, using an AI-native SDLC powered by AWS Kiro and running on Amazon Bedrock with Strands Agents. In under six months, specialized agents for pricing, quoting and CRM cut quote turnaround by 90 percent, generating customer briefings in under two minutes, with governance and compliance built in for a regulated industry. This session shares a practical blueprint for applying agentic AI to complex enterprise workflows at speed, without sacrificing enterprise-grade trust. This presentation is brought to you by EPAM, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Physical AI for MedTech: From Intelligent Devices to Business Impact
sessions.a: Physical AI — AI that senses, reasons, and acts in the physical world — is reshaping medical devices. From surgical robots to connected infusion pumps, imaging to wearables, every next-gen device needs training, simulation, edge deployment, and fleet management at scale. In this chalk talk, we’ll architect the full Physical AI stack on AWS for medical devices — SageMaker for model training, IoT Greengrass for edge inference, regulated OTA at fleet scale, and NVIDIA solutions integrated into the AWS backbone. We’ll whiteboard the hard tradeoffs — edge vs. cloud, regulatory constraints, and scaling from prototype to 100K devices. Leave with a reference architecture and a clear path to pilot

sessions.t: Physical AI in Telecom: A Framework for Workload Placement
sessions.a: Some physical AI workloads need sub-millisecond performance at edge cell sites, others are better suited to a full AWS Region, and many fall in between on AWS Local Zones or AWS Outposts. In this chalk talk, we provide a framework for matching each workload to the right option. We trace the physical AI development lifecycle, examining how data sovereignty, latency, data gravity, and token economics interact to shape placement decisions at each phase. Based on real-world use cases, we discuss the options so you leave with a placement framework you can apply immediately.

sessions.t: Pinpoint latency in microservices with distributed tracing
sessions.a: Diagnosing latency across a high-scale Amazon EKS environment is complex when pods scale dynamically and trace context fails to propagate across service boundaries. In this code talk, we instrument containerized microservices with OpenTelemetry, propagate context across service hops, and correlate spans, metrics, and logs in Amazon CloudWatch. Live coding shows how a single slow request reveals the exact container and code path responsible for degradation, using targeted span attributes and exemplars to make Kubernetes-scale traces navigable. You'll also see the trade-offs behind sampling strategies and collector deployment topologies that affect overhead, fidelity, and cost at production scale.

sessions.t: Pit Crew AI: Building Multi-Agent Cloud Operations on AWS
sessions.a: AI can generate code at racing speed, but production workloads still require continuous attention to security, reliability, cost, and operational risks. In this Code Talk, we build a multi-agent architecture on AWS inspired by a Formula 1 pit crew. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, MCP, GitHub, Jira, and Infrastructure as Code, we evolve from a single agent to a team of specialized agents for security, cost optimization, reliability, and observability. Through a live demonstration, you’ll see how agents turn cloud findings into engineering tasks. Attendees will leave with reusable architectures, orchestration patterns, and examples for cloud operations on AWS.
