sessions.t: Pitfalls of SaaS: Return of the agent
sessions.a: Every SaaS architect has hit the classics: noisy neighbors saturating infrastructure, compounding costs eating margins, deployment models chosen too early. Agents amplify all of them — and add surprises. One agent generates more API calls in a minute than a human makes in a week. Shared memory leaks context across tenants in ways no IAM policy catches. Autonomous tool calls cascade across services with no human in the loop. Revisit classic SaaS pitfalls through an agentic lens: familiar problems in new costumes, genuinely new failure modes, and what to change before you find out the hard way.

sessions.t: Planning for migrations, and operating databases on AWS with Redgate (sponsored by Red Gate)
sessions.a: Moving a database from on-premises to the cloud is easy to get wrong: undersized instances, surprise costs, unplanned downtime. Join Kellyn and John as we look at Redgate Monitor's new database migration planning feature, designed to help you size, plan, and cost a move with real data instead of guesswork. We will also explore how Redgate Monitor is evolving to support the next generation of database operations, supporting teams who are using AI assistants and Agents who need access to observability data quickly, giving operational staff faster answers and smarter recommendations when managing complex database systems. This presentation is brought to you by Red Gate, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Policy to Proof: govern deployments at machine speed
sessions.a: When agents and automated pipelines deploy at machine speed, manual sign-off can't keep up, so the proof has to be built into the pipeline itself. Developers want to ship fast, governance teams want controls enforced, and compliance teams want evidence. In this builder session, you'll build a CI/CD pipeline that satisfies all three: cfn-guard validation against policy rules, CloudFormation deployment, Config evaluation after deployment, and a compliance report generated as a pipeline artifact. The full policy-to-proof loop in one pipeline. You leave with a working pipeline where every deployment validates governance rules and produces audit evidence on its own.

sessions.t: Post-Quantum Cryptography Tabletop Experience
sessions.a: Quantum computing is advancing—is your cryptographic infrastructure ready? In this immersive tabletop, executives will confront the urgent reality that current public-key cryptographic standards face obsolescence. Make high-stakes decisions on migration timelines, technology selection, and stakeholder coordination as quantum threats loom over customer data, transaction systems, and competitive intelligence. Balance budget constraints against discovery, risk prioritization, and implementation speed while navigating regulatory requirements and operational continuity. Compete to build quantum-resistant infrastructure before adversaries exploit today's vulnerabilities. Leave with actionable strategies for leading a post-quantum cryptography migration that protects trust and secures competitive advantage.

sessions.t: Powering America's AI and HPC leadership for mission-critical outcomes
sessions.a: AI and HPC deliver real mission breakthroughs across defense, national security, and science. In this session, hear how AWS's $50B infrastructure investment and leadership-class hyperscale elasticity compress timelines from years to months. Ideal for mission owners, architects, and tech leaders.

sessions.t: Powering Interactive Agents with Live Context (sponsored by Materialize)
sessions.a: How do you keep an agent's understanding of the world fresh enough for it to act on? Interactive agents need current context about the customers, orders, inventory, accounts, and other entities they reason about. But assembling that context from constantly changing operational systems is complex, forcing teams to choose between stale data, expensive recomputation, or complex pipelines. This talk will show how to build continuously updated context in SQL that is trustworthy enough for agents to rely upon. You'll learn how to transform operational data into agent-ready representations, keep attributes and relationships up to date as the underlying data changes, and propagate those changes to search indexes and embeddings when needed. Attend if you're deploying AI agents to production and want to give them fresher, more complete context and tighten their read-act-react loop.

sessions.t: Powering your agentic AI experience with AWS streaming and messaging
sessions.a: Organizations are accelerating innovation with generative and agentic AI—and getting there depends on a handful of real-time data primitives: durable, high-throughput ingestion; stream processing and enrichment; low-latency, event-driven delivery; and a scalable place to land and serve data. In this session, learn how these primitives come together to power the real-time patterns behind agentic AI—and where each one fits: streaming into a real-time semantic layer for fresh retrieval context, event-driven agent invocation so agents act the instant something happens, and continuously sourcing agentic data stores with live data. We'll show how to satisfy each primitive—spanning multi-Region resilience, seamless migration off self-managed infrastructure, direct landing into open table formats and object storage, and simplified networking

sessions.t: Powering Your Forward Deployed Engineers with Kiro and AIDLC
sessions.a: Learn how to power your Forward Deployed Engineers with AI-driven delivery in this hands-on workshop. Work through a full agentic-driven development lifecycle using Kiro: elaborate requirements, generate domain models and code, produce tests and IaC, and deploy, all while staying in control of architecture decisions. Along the way, see how partners scaled persona-based agents across the SDLC, with gains of 2-10X velocity, 3-5X productivity, and 50-70% reduction in design cycle time. Leave with a repeatable approach your teams can apply on the next engagement, and the next, sharpening your AI-driven delivery.

sessions.t: Power streaming analytics on AWS with AI-driven insights
sessions.a: Learn how to build a modern, streaming analytics solution for real-time data processing and power it with agentic AI capabilities to analyze events and extract patterns for actionable responses. This session will provide a hands-on experience on building a streaming solution using Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka for real-time data ingestion, using Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink for complex event processing, and Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock Agent Core to take immediate action. Further evolve this solution to demonstrate the integration with Amazon S3 Tables for deeper analysis.

sessions.t: Power streaming analytics on AWS with AI-driven insights [REPEAT]

Further evolve this solution to demonstrate the integration with Amazon S3 Tables for deeper analysis.

sessions.t: Powertools for agent DevOps: Debug reasoning, not just exceptions
sessions.a: Your agent returned the wrong answer — no exception, no alarm, it just reasoned poorly. Traditional monitoring catches crashes, not bad decisions. In this builder session, you'll use Powertools for AWS Lambda to build agent observability: Logger with log buffering to capture decision context only on failure, Tracer with annotations for confidence scores and tool selections, and Metrics tracking token cost and reasoning steps. Wire OTEL with Strands SDK for end-to-end traces across the agent loop. You leave with dashboards that answer "why did the agent decide this?" - not "did it crash?"

sessions.t: Practical applications of edge compute in Amazon CloudFront
sessions.a: Edge compute is a practical way to build faster, smarter applications. In this interactive chalk talk, we’ll dive into how Amazon CloudFront empowers developers to run custom logic at the edge using CloudFront Functions, Lambda@Edge, and the Key Value Store. We’ll explore real-world use cases, architectural patterns, and recent feature launches that unlock powerful personalization, performance optimization, and cost efficiency. Come ready to whiteboard, ask questions, and discover how to push intelligence closer to your users.

sessions.t: Practical PKI for On-Prem Devices with IAM Roles Anywhere
sessions.a: Secure authentication of your humans and machines is a challenge every organization faces, especially if your proof of identity is not already in AWS. In this session, we'll talk you through multiple ways to set up or use PKI - such as Belgium's eID or a hardware key - to securely access AWS with phishing resistant authentication built using IAM Roles Anywhere. This will include live demos and code samples. By the end of the session we will stop worrying about plain text credential storage because we can use trusted hardware instead.

sessions.t: Prefill, decode, schedule: LLM inference without bubbles
sessions.a: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto distinct GPU pools, but creates new problems. Head-of-line blocking on prefill, stragglers on decode, and pipeline bubbles when phases switch. This session goes deep on how to solve them. We cover temporally-disaggregated pipeline parallelism to eliminate phase-switching bubbles, adaptive scheduling across heterogeneous instances, tensor vs. pipeline parallelism tradeoffs for latency and throughput, constrained decoding with context-sensitive grammars for structured output without sacrificing token throughput, and KV-cache parallelism for multi-million context serving.

sessions.t: Preventing unintended access: a practical guide to data perimeter controls
sessions.a: Are you looking to prevent unintended access to your data and mitigate data exposure risks? This hands-on session demonstrates how data perimeter controls implemented through service control policies (SCPs), resource control policies (RCPs), and VPC endpoint policies help keep corporate data within organizational boundaries. You'll build data perimeter policies for real-life security scenarios and validate their effectiveness using an assessment tool. By the end, you'll have practical knowledge on how to help ensure only trusted identities access trusted resources from expected networks.

sessions.t: Prevent supply chain disruptions with AI-driven insights and action
sessions.a: Only 25% of organizations feel ready to prevent disruptions, and 85% take two or more weeks to resolve the urgent ones. Join a supply chain leader and Amazon to see how agentic AI catches emerging risks early, so teams act before problems turn costly. You will hear the honest before and after, including the hurdles, not just the wins, and leave knowing how to move your team from reacting under pressure to planning ahead with a clear view of risk.

sessions.t: Private AI agent egress: VPC Lattice meets AgentCore Gateway
sessions.a: Your AI agents need to call private MCP servers, internal REST APIs, and OAuth providers — but those backends must never touch the public internet. In this lightning talk, we demo how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway uses managed Amazon VPC Lattice endpoints to route agent traffic privately into your VPC. We'll configure a private MCP server target, show traffic staying on the AWS backbone, and cover key patterns including intermediate domain routing, private certificate workarounds with ALB, and cross-account connectivity. Walk away with a repeatable pattern for secure, zero-public-internet agentic workloads.

sessions.t: Processing PII without exposing it: KYC with Nitro Enclaves
sessions.a: Know Your Customer (KYC) pipelines must screen personally identifiable informaiton (PII) against sanctions lists and politically exposed person (PEP) databases while proving to regulators that data was never exposed to unauthorized systems. Traditional Spark pipelines may give executors access to decrypted PII, creating compliance risk. In this workshop, learn how to combine AWS Nitro Enclaves with Amazon EMR on EKS to process PII at scale without exposing plaintext to the compute layer. You'll configure KMS key policies with PCR0 attestation, deploy enclave sidecars as Kubernetes DaemonSets, and run Spark jobs where only screening decisions leave the enclave boundary.

sessions.t: Production Agentic Trading: Build the pipeline Moeve runs on AgentCore
sessions.a: This session details the implementation of an agentic workforce managing the trade lifecycle in production energy trading operations. In this workshop, you'll build the pipeline Moeve runs in production: a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that extracts deal data from unstructured emails, resolves ambiguity deterministically against master data, and carries evidence per field. You'll harden it with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails on input and output, then score it for accuracy and run-to-run consistency, including the fields that measured badly, and why. You'll leave with a reusable pattern for production deployment of mission-critical trading workflows with strict latency and reliability requirements.

sessions.t: Productionize, secure, and scale agentic applications on Amazon ECS
sessions.a: AI agents are easy to prototype but hard to run in production. They have unique compute requirements, isolation between tenants, networking that connects to tools and APIs, and infrastructure that scales with unpredictable workloads. In this builders session, deploy an agentic AI application on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate and take advantage of what containers give you, including task isolation, unlimited runtime for long-running agent conversations, VPC networking for secure tool access, and Service Connect for multi-agent communication. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

In this builder's session, deploy an agentic AI application on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate and take advantage of what containers give you, including hardware-level task isolation, unlimited runtime for long-running agent conversations, VPC networking for secure tool access, and Service Connect for multi-agent communication. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.t: Production-ready Lambda: Security and performance patterns
sessions.a: A Lambda function that handles traffic well in prototype isn't necessarily production-ready—there's a gap between "works" and "hardened." In this builders' session, take a working Lambda function and add the security and performance layers that production demands. You'll implement least-privilege IAM policies, add request validation and secrets management, reduce cold start duration with SnapStart and right-sized memory, and configure reserved concurrency for predictable performance under load. Each change includes the trade-off: what you gain, what it costs, and when to skip it. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Proof of What You Know: Building Trust in an AI Skills Economy (sponsored by Pearson)
sessions.a: As AI reshapes hiring and learning, proving what you know is becoming just as important as proving who you are. Pearson's digital wallet vision connects verified credentials, skills, and identity into a trusted, portable record that learners can use across certification, education, and employment journeys, helping employers and institutions move beyond self-reported claims to verified evidence of capability. This presentation is brought to you by Pearson, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Protect, recover, validate: Data resiliency for AWS storage
sessions.a: Data protection strategies today must span workloads and prove recovery works before an incident demands it. In this workshop, you'll implement recovery and data protection strategies for Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, and Amazon EBS with AWS Backup. Using a financial services application architecture, you'll configure protection mechanisms for ransomware and insider threats and execute step-by-step recovery procedures against simulated cyber threats. Recover across multiple services, validate restored data integrity, and walk away with patterns to strengthen your own recovery capabilities. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

sessions.t: Protect your analytics workloads with cross-region resilience [REPEAT]
sessions.a: Explore best practices for designing active-active and active-passive architectures for AWS analytics services including AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, Amazon Redshift and AWS Lake Formation based on your RTO and RPO requirements. Learn how to build cross-region resilience when Apache Iceberg tables become an integral part of your architecture, including catalog replication and metadata synchronization. Explore real-world architectural patterns and trade-offs for choosing the right resilience strategy.

sessions.t: Proving your defenses work: validating GuardDuty runtime detection
sessions.a: Your board wants to know your detections work and auditors want evidence. The only way you find out today is when something real hits. In this code talk, you;ll see us build a detection validation program that answers the question before it gets asked. We'll live-code realistic attack scenarios mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, generate the correlated signals that trigger GuardDuty runtime findings, scope detection rules to specific accounts, and interpret findings as they fire. You'll walk out with a repeatable framework your team can run after every GuardDuty update to prove coverage, not assume it.

sessions.t: Pushing AI Boundaries: Transform Marketing with Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker and AWS (sponsored by Adobe)
sessions.a: As generative AI matures into autonomous ecosystems, enterprise marketing demands a new era of collaboration. In this session, discover how Adobe and Amazon co-innovate to deliver next-generation AI capabilities for marketers, business practitioners, and developers. At the center of this revolution is Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker, an advanced AI teammate powered by Adobe Harness. We will showcase how Coworker and its flexible, headless capabilities seamlessly unite Adobe’s deep customer experience expertise with the power of AWS. Attendees will discover how this combined innovation enables teams to transition from manual execution to goal-based, automated workflows with built-in governance. Join us to learn how this partnership helps enterprise organizations take a massive leap forward in operational effectiveness and unlock entirely new business outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Adobe, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Put your data to work: build a knowledge assistant on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Your data lives in documents, images, databases, warehouses, and relationships between entities. In this builders session, build a knowledge assistant that works across all of it on Amazon Bedrock. Use Managed Knowledge Bases with multimodal ingestion to handle PDFs and images, add natural-language querying over structured data, and wire in GraphRAG for questions that span connected entities. Then make it enterprise-ready: secure tenant isolation, concurrency-aware ingestion, and the Agentic Retrieval API for multi-hop, cited answers. Leave with a deployed stack and retrieval patterns you can reuse across your organization.

sessions.t: PyTorch optimizations: Faster AI and lower costs with AWS Graviton
sessions.a: Explore the latest PyTorch optimizations for Arm-based hardware, from improved kernel performance on AWS Graviton to faster training and inference at lower compute cost. We cover real benchmark results, the open-source contributions driving these improvements, and what it looks like to run modern AI workloads on Arm today. Whether you are tuning a model, contributing upstream, or just curious about what the community has been shipping, come get a grounded view of where things stand and where they are heading.

sessions.t: Quantum Error Correction - Progress, Hardware, and What's Next
sessions.a: Quantum computers have the potential to solve some of today's most challenging computational problems — but they suffer from significantly higher error rates than their classical counterparts. In this talk, we introduce quantum error correction (QEC) and compare the hardware requirements of leading QEC methods against the commercial roadmaps of quantum hardware companies. To ground the discussion, we begin with a brief revisit of classical error correction before walking through recent breakthroughs in quantum error correction. Attendees will leave with an informed perspective on where QEC stands today and the challenges that will define the field's progress in the coming years.

sessions.t: Quantum-Proof Your IoT Fleet: Migrate Devices to Post-Quantum Cryptography OTA
sessions.a: NIST has announced post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards and CNSA 2.0 requires quantum-resistant algorithms by 2027. IoT devices deployed today operate for 10–20 years, so they need to be quantum-resistant from day one. In this workshop, migrate a real ESP32-S3 SoC from classical TLS to post-quantum cryptography over the air with zero physical access required. Connect to AWS IoT Core, trigger an OTA delivering ML-KEM and ML-DSA with quantum-safe certificates from AWS Private CA, and watch your device reboot into PQC-secured MQTT. No embedded experience needed. You leave with the ESP32-S3 and open-source code to quantum-proof your fleet at scale.

sessions.t: Queue-based decoupling trade-offs for event-driven workloads
sessions.a: Every decoupling pattern makes trade-offs, and the right one depends on your workload's constraints. In this session, you work through scenarios with competing demands: exactly-once processing, tenant isolation, back pressure, and ordering. Using SQS and Lambda, you configure queue types and concurrency controls, tune batching behavior, and observe how your consumer scales under each configuration. Each scenario forces a trade-off between throughput, ordering, isolation, and cost. You leave knowing which trade-offs to accept for your workload and why. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Ransomware resilience with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
sessions.a: Ransomware does not wait for a scheduled backup window, and neither should your defenses. In this chalk talk, learn how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP's built in Autonomous Ransomware Protection uses machine learning to catch abnormal file activity and automatically create protective snapshots before damage spreads. We cover configuring detection policies, integrating alerts with AWS security services, locking down recovery points with SnapLock, and building automated response workflows. Bring your questions as we design a defense in depth strategy together, one that gets your file data back fast when an attack happens, not just one that flags it.

sessions.t: Ready before the surge - smart ELB capacity reservations
sessions.a: Your Load Balancer scales automatically for most traffic - and now you can prepare it for predictable spikes before they arrive. Product launches, flash sales, live events, and Monday-morning market opens deserve a load balancer that's ready instantly. Load Balancer Capacity Unit (LCU) Reservation pre-provisions a capacity floor so your infrastructure is never caught cold. In this session we introduce new capacity management capabilities across ALB, NLB, and GLB that turn reservation planning into a data-driven workflow. Learn how to analyze historical patterns, set the right capacity floor, and release reservations with confidence.

sessions.t: Real-time agentic architecture on AWS: from batch to real-time AI
sessions.a: Batch jobs and cron schedules fail silently and delay agentic AI outcomes: a missed run, a stuck lock, or a partial write goes unnoticed, adding lag between the moment an event occurs and the moment an agent responds. This advanced deep dive rethinks the architecture—loosely coupled services that deploy and fail independently, wired through events. We show how shifting transactional and analytical workloads to real-time, event-driven patterns fuels responsive agentic AI on AWS.

sessions.t: Real-time AI video enrichment with AWS Elemental Inference
sessions.a: Retrofitting videos to add subtitles, vertical formats, social cuts, and searchable metadata often means new encoders, manual editors, and multiple integrations. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS Elemental Inference can help extend reach, enhance engagement, and improve monetization by layering subtitling, vertical framing, key-moment clipping, and contextual metadata onto live and on-demand video without rebuilding your stack. Learn about the benefits of a single managed service that will improve latency, quality, and lower costs for video workflows.

sessions.t: Real-world AI: How a state agency transformed its contact center
sessions.a: When the Georgia Department of Community Supervision needed to modernize their contact center, they turned to Amazon Connect and AI. In this session, hear firsthand how AI-powered call analysis, real-time transcription, automated case notes, and intelligent agent assistance are transforming how state agencies serve constituents. We share lessons learned from discovery through implementation, including how to prioritize high-impact AI use cases, build stakeholder alignment, and deliver measurable outcomes. Leave with actionable strategies to bring AI-driven contact center innovation to your organization.

sessions.t: Real-world migrations: Lessons learned migrating to AWS Outposts
sessions.a: Organizations with data residency and digital sovereignty requirements face a critical question: how do you move workloads from on-premises infrastructure to AWS Outposts without disrupting compliance posture or operations? This Level 300 session distills lessons from migrating customers to Outposts across industries, organization sizes, and migration strategies. We walk through the processes that delivered results, the quantifiable outcomes we measured, and the critical mistakes we learned to avoid. You leave with a practical playbook for selecting the right migration approach, navigating common blockers, and accelerating Outposts adoption. We also cover transitioning from first-generation to second-generation Outposts hardware.

sessions.t: re:Architecture Rodeo: Architecting AI Governance & Security at Scale
sessions.a: Everyone wants AI. Nobody wants to be the team that shipped it without guardrails. In this Rodeo, your team faces three demanding stakeholders - a security hawk, a data visibility champion, and a platform lead racing to get Agentic AI live. Your mission: build a governance architecture that keeps all of them happy. You'll whiteboard, debate, and build against the clock, then walk judges through your thinking. They love good questions (and they'll have plenty). Come for the competition, stay for the patterns you'll take home. Best architecture rides away with the win.

sessions.t: re:Architecture Rodeo: Building an AI-Ready Data Foundation
sessions.a: Your data estate wasn't designed for AI agents. Nobody's was. But somewhere between your RDBMS, NoSQL clusters, and that untouchable data lake, an agentic-ready architecture waits to be built. In this Rodeo session, your team draws a challenge: a legacy warehouse needing a semantic layer, a sprawling lake needing an ontology, or a metadata mess that lets agents in without letting governance out. Your job: build a data layer that makes agents productive, keeps compliance calm, and gives analysts self-service. You'll whiteboard ontologies, debate metadata, and wire up multi-agent access against the clock. Best architecture rides away with the win.

sessions.t: re:Architecture Rodeo: Designing Agentic AI Applications
sessions.a: Manual handoffs. Approval chains. That one person who "just knows how it works." Every enterprise has processes begging to be automated - and agentic AI is how you finally do it. In this Rodeo session, teams compete to architect end-to-end agentic solutions: multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop decision points, and MCP integration, all under a ticking clock. Present your design to SME judges with hard questions, borrow ideas from your competitors, and walk away with reusable patterns for turning manual chaos into autonomous workflows. Best architecture rides away with the win.

sessions.t: re:Architecture Rodeo: Transforming Customer Experience with AI
sessions.a: Contact centers are being rebuilt as AI-powered CX platforms, and the architecture decisions define who wins. In this competitive session, teams design an end-to-end transformation ranging from voice LLMs and intent-aware routing to seamless bot-to-human handoffs with full context passing. Architect for both greenfield and migration scenarios, then put your design on the line present to SME judges for scoring on scalability, cost, and customer experience.

sessions.t: Rebuild a legacy ETL pipeline as serverless with AWS Transform
sessions.a: Enterprise data teams maintain ETL pipelines built on legacy tools like stored procedures, custom bash scripts, IBM DataStage and others, that resist migration due to undocumented dependencies. In this builders' session, use AWS Transform Custom to discover and map an existing ETL pipeline, generate a modernization blueprint, and rebuild it as a serverless workflow using AWS Glue and Step Functions. Each attendee picks one legacy source module (stored procedures, bash/SQL scripts, or DataStage jobs etc) and works hands-on through discovery, transformation logic analysis, and deploying a modernized pipeline.

sessions.t: Rebuild a legacy ETL pipeline as serverless with AWS Transform

In this builders' session, use AWS Transform Custom to discover and map an existing ETL pipeline, generate a modernization blueprint, and rebuild it as a serverless workflow using AWS Glue and Step Functions. Each attendee picks one legacy source module (stored procedures, bash/SQL scripts, or DataStage jobs etc) and works hands-on through discovery, transformation logic analysis, and deploying a modernized pipeline.

sessions.t: Rebuild CI for AI coding agents with content based caching (sponsored by RWX)
sessions.a: Continuous integration was designed around human pace. A developer pushes a branch, a webhook fires, and a ten minute wait feels acceptable. AI coding agents break that assumption, and validation becomes the longest part of the cycle. Explore how RWX rebuilt the layer underneath continuous integration for agent driven work, including content based caching that skips work already proven unchanged, graph based task execution, a container runtime built for reuse, and a command line interface agents call directly rather than waiting on Git. Learn which parts of a pipeline are structurally slow and which are simply misconfigured. This presentation is brought to you by RWX, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Recover and prove your full stack without disrupting production
sessions.a: Meeting your recovery time and point objectives is non-negotiable. For your critical workloads, that means orchestrated, tier-aware recovery within minutes, with a plan you've actually tested. Most teams haven't, because testing often means disrupting production. So, the plan stays on the shelf and RTOs stay theoretical. In this session, see AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery replicate servers into low-cost staging and recover the full stack in the right order, in minutes, then rehearse the same failover without production noticing. Learn how to run non-disruptive recovery drills against your own environment and prove your RTOs before an incident does it for you.

sessions.t: Red, green, re-architect: Test-driven infrastructure
sessions.a: AI can write your infrastructure in seconds — but did it build what you asked for? In this workshop, you'll apply test-driven development to AI-generated infrastructure. Describe your architecture in plain English, then use Kiro's spec-driven development to decompose it into discrete, testable behaviors. Kiro iterates through each one: writing a failing CDK assertion that encodes it (red), generating minimal infrastructure to pass it (green), then advancing to the next. Once green, refactor toward production readiness using cdk-nag rule packs to enforce Well-Architected practices. Leave with meaningful test coverage and a repeatable pattern for raising your organization's infrastructure coding standards. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Red, green, re-architect: Test-driven infrastructure [REPEAT]

sessions.t: Red Team CTF: When Auth and Guardrails Aren't Enough
sessions.a: The best way to secure an AI agent is to think like the attacker. In this CTF-style session, you start with a production-realistic agent - AgentCore runtime, Bedrock Guardrails, Cognito authentication, and three MCP tools - and you systematically exploit it. Across 6 challenges, you poison trusted data sources, bypass prompt-level access control, jailbreak an authenticated session, compromise a third-party MCP server, exfiltrate data through authorized channels, and burn the inference budget. After each breach, you enable the real fix and verify the attack fails. You will compete on a live leaderboard and leave with a fully hardened agent and a defense-in-depth playbook.

sessions.t: Red teaming Aurora and gen AI: offense, defense, response
sessions.a: Databases and generative AI workloads are high-value targets that demand continuous adversarial testing. In this session, learn how AWS red team engineers use AI to discover innovative ways to strengthen Amazon Aurora and other cloud-native database services against modern threats. Explore how red team findings shape architectural decisions that contain blast radius by design, and how AI-augmented detection and response mechanisms close the loop at machine speed. Walk away with a practical framework for red teaming cloud environments and AI systems, designing for assumed breach, and building response capabilities that match the velocity of modern threats.

sessions.t: Reduce EKS cluster compute costs with EC2 Flex instances
sessions.a: Container orchestration promises to improve resource utilization, but often we find ourselves with nodes that over-provision CPU, and therefore overspend. This might happen when our workloads have a high memory footprint, or when the number of replicas is driven by resilience targets and not actual load. In this session, we'll learn how easy it is to save cost in these situations without losing performance by taking advantage of EC2 Flex instances (e.g., C8i-flex, M8i-flex, R8i-flex). You'll migrate existing EKS cluster nodes, monitor relevant metrics, and measure the actual cost improvement.

sessions.t: Reduce EKS cluster compute costs with EC2 Flex instances

sessions.t: Reduce incident response time on Amazon ECS with AI observability
sessions.a: You get paged. Your ECS service is returning errors. You open six tabs, task logs, ALB metrics, deployment history, CloudWatch alarms, container health and start piecing together a timeline by hand. In this chalk talk, explore how AI-powered observability changes that workflow. See how CloudWatch Investigations ingests your existing telemetry, correlates signals across services and infrastructure, and produces root cause analysis in minutes instead of hours. Discuss how to structure logs and metrics so automated investigation actually works, and how Managed Daemons keep your collectors consistent without redeploying applications. Bring your incident response questions for an open discussion.

sessions.t: Reduce LLM inference costs up to 80% through caching with Valkey
sessions.a: LLM inference depends on limited GPU memory, and a KV cache lets agentic AI applications reuse computed intermediate states across prompts to reduce latency and costs. In this talk, we explain how KV caching works and walk through a production architecture using Valkey as a high-performance datastore, LMCache for KV reuse at inference, and llm-d for cache-aware routing. You will leave with practical implementation guidance and a framework for evaluating when a KV caching tier is the right choice to reduce costs for your AI applications.

sessions.t: Reduce LLM inference costs up to 80% through caching with Valkey
sessions.a: LLM inference depends on limited GPU memory, and a KV cache lets agentic AI applications reuse computed intermediate states across prompts to reduce latency and costs. In this talk, we explain how KV caching works and walk through a production architecture using Valkey as a high-performance datastore, LMCache for KV reuse at inference, and llm-d for cache-aware routing. You will leave with practical implementation guidance and a framework for evaluating when a KV caching tier is the right choice to reduce costs for your AI applications.

sessions.t: Reduce spend and data movement with Amazon Redshift Data Sharing and Graviton
sessions.a: Organizations sharing data across business units often rely on slow, error-prone ETL jobs that create costly duplication. Amazon Redshift Data Sharing enables secure, live access across provisioned and serverless warehouses — within or across accounts and regions — eliminating data movement entirely. Additionally, Redshift Graviton instances deliver up to 35% better price-performance, accelerating workloads on Apache Iceberg tables through optimized columnar processing and parallel I/O. In this session, learn how to break down data silos with cross-warehouse data sharing and boost open data lakehouse performance with Redshift on Graviton.

sessions.t: Reduce token costs by caching inference results on ElastiCache
sessions.a: Multi-agent AI systems now orchestrate complex workflows requiring frequent foundation model calls. In this session, learn how you can reduce latencies to single-digit milliseconds from single-digit seconds with for Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey in agentic AI applications using semantic and KV caching, while also reducing the cost incurred from your foundation models for production workloads. By implementing these caching strategies in agentic architectures like RAG-powered assistants and autonomous agents, customers can create performant and cost-effective production-scale agentic AI systems.

sessions.t: Reducing Lambda cost with Graviton and managed instances
sessions.a: Lambda's default x86 pricing works fine until your steady-state workloads make the per-invocation model expensive at scale. In this builders' session, start with a baseline workload and apply two cost levers: migrate to ARM64 (Graviton) for better price-performance, then deploy on Lambda Managed Instances for EC2 economics with multi-concurrency on steady-state traffic. You'll measure before-and-after cost and performance data at each step, evaluate when each approach makes sense versus default Lambda pricing, and leave with a repeatable migration playbook. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Re-Engineer Enterprise Processes for Agentic AI on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (sponsored by Camunda)
sessions.a: Enterprise AI is moving from experimentation to production, but legacy workflows designed without AI in mind keep agents disconnected from the processes, systems, and controls that determine successful business outcomes. Understand why reengineering now matters: organizations that preserve legacy workflows risk slowing AI adoption while others redesign operations for an AI first world. Discover how Camunda ProcessOS works with Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to discover, re-engineer, and improve end-to-end processes. See how Camunda’s agentic orchestration combines deterministic controls with dynamic AI agents, human approval, observability, and auditability. Learn why you need to re-engineer now, and stop adding agents to yesterday’s workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Camunda, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Refactor your monolith for multi-tenancy and agentic AI in one pass
sessions.a: Most ISV monoliths get modernized in three sequential passes: refactor, then multi-tenant, then agentic. Three trips through the same code, each longer than the last. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into the unified refactor pattern that makes tenancy and agentic bets in the same window. We'll explore how data partitioning decisions shift when agents are also a target, when Amazon EKS becomes the substrate for both migrations, and which patterns create more debt than they solve when combined wrong. Leave with a framework for the one refactor window you can afford. Bring your questions.

sessions.t: Refactor your monolith for multi-tenancy and agentic AI in one pass
sessions.a: Most ISV monoliths get modernized in three sequential passes: refactor, then multi-tenant, then agentic. Three trips through the same code, each longer than the last. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into the unified refactor pattern that makes tenancy and agentic bets in the same window. sessions.t: Regulation to Innovation: A Global Enterprise Guide to Digital Sovereignty (sponsored by Accenture)
sessions.a: Digital sovereignty is a growing priority for global enterprises operating across Europe as they navigate regulatory requirements, geopolitical uncertainty, and increasing demand for cloud and AI innovation. Organizations must balance data residency, compliance, resilience, and business agility without slowing transformation. Learn how leading enterprises are using AWS European Sovereign Cloud as part of a broader cloud strategy to meet sovereignty requirements while continuing to adopt modern cloud services and AI. Accenture will share practical approaches to assessing sovereignty needs, designing compliant architectures, and integrating sovereign cloud capabilities into enterprise environments. Attendees will leave with actionable guidance for balancing trust, resilience, compliance, and innovation at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Reimagine legacy apps to be agentic AI ready with AWS Transform & Kiro
sessions.a: Enterprise core applications were built for stability, not agentic AI. Tightly coupled dependencies across mainframe and interconnected systems make it nearly impossible to add intelligent capabilities without rearchitecting. In this workshop, take a legacy application through the full modernization journey: scope it, reverse-engineer existing behavior with AWS Transform, classify logic into deterministic microservices and AI agents, design target layers with Kiro, build the agentic layer on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, then deploy and validate. Leave with hands-on experience rebuilding a legacy application into an architecture ready for agentic AI. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Reimagine legacy apps to be agentic AI ready with AWS Transform & Kiro
sessions.a: Enterprise core applications were built for stability, not agentic AI. In this workshop, take a legacy application through the full modernization journey: scope it, reverse-engineer existing behavior with AWS Transform, classify logic into deterministic microservices and AI agents, design target layers with Kiro, build the agentic layer on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, then deploy and validate. Leave with hands-on experience rebuilding a legacy application into an architecture ready for agentic AI. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Reimagining the Operating Room: Gen AI's Impact on Surgery (sponsored by Deloitte)
sessions.a: Explore how Generative AI, powered by Proximie and AWS, is fundamentally reshaping the operating room. This session will detail how computer vision and LLMs are creating the OR of the future, supported by Deloitte, to improve productivity and treat more patients in UK NHS Trusts. Attendees will gain insights into the practical application of this powerful alliance and why this innovative approach is vital for the future of healthcare. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Reinvent cloud security with runtime and AI (sponsored by Upwind)
sessions.a: This session explores the evolution of cloud security and why traditional approaches fall short in the era of ephemeral compute and agentic AI. While legacy CloudSec relied on static scanning for visibility, today’s environments are dynamic, real-time, and increasingly autonomous, resulting in blind spots, excessive noise, and incomplete protection. We’ll examine how AI-driven and hybrid cloud architectures introduce new challenges across visibility, protection, and validation, from cross-provider gaps to real-time attack vectors and model vulnerabilities. To address this, Cloud and AI security must move beyond static analysis to a unified, runtime-driven approach. By continuously monitoring activity across the environment and embedding security throughout the SDLC, including production, organizations gain real-time context, better prioritization, and proactive threat mitigation. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Reliable data processing with AWS serverless services
sessions.a: In this chalk talk, learn how to optimize your serverless data processing workflows at scale. We cover AWS Step Functions Distributed Map for massive parallel batch processing and AWS Lambda durable functions for durable execution workflows. See how to combine these with Lambda event source mappings for stream and queue processing. We discuss cost optimization strategies and when to choose each approach for your data workload.

sessions.t: Renaissance Dad: building an agentic learning app for my 9-year-old with Kiro
sessions.a: Werner Vogels told us to become Renaissance Developers — curious polymaths who blend disciplines and own what they build. I took it literally: as a dad, I used Kiro and agentic AI to build a learning app that helps my 9-year-old practice math and school lessons. In this session, I'll share the full architecture: an OCR agent that imports exercises from photos of school notebooks, an adaptive agent that personalizes difficulty, and a coaching agent that guides instead of correcting. We'll deep-dive into multi-agent orchestration patterns, vision model integration, spec-driven development with Kiro, and the guardrails required when your end user is a child. Attendees will leave with reusable agentic patterns applicable far beyond education.

sessions.t: Replacing eligibility rules engines with Neurosymbolic AI in HHS
sessions.a: State HHS agencies spend hundreds of millions maintaining eligibility rules engines built on Drools or proprietary tooling. These systems are brittle, expensive, and impossible to audit. We built a different path: Ingesting policy, using Large Language Models, and building a formal logic representation, followed by using neurosymbolic techniques to produce a verified rule set, enabling deterministic eligibility decisions with full audit trails. No hallucinations. Provable correctness. We walk through the architecture, show a working prototype processing SNAP and Medicaid policy, discuss pricing at scale, and share early results from state engagements.

sessions.t: Reshaping Agentic AI and Business Analytics with Databricks on Intel (sponsored by Intel)
sessions.a: Intel and Databricks are collaborating to optimize price-performance for workloads running on AWS. This session covers optimizations for ISVs running Photon/Spark on Databricks leveraging custom Amazon EC2 instances powered by Intel Xeon processors, delivering advanced AI capabilities and high core density. This presentation is brought to you by Intel, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Resilience for Data Foundations: The Lessons Iceberg Forced Us to Learn (sponsored by Commvault)
sessions.a: When customers needed to recover Iceberg environments in production, we discovered that restoring data was often the easy part. Preserving metadata, table state, consistency, and downstream dependencies proved far more challenging than we expected. In this session, Clumio's product and engineering leaders share the assumptions that didn't survive production, the recovery scenarios that surprised us most, and the architectural lessons that emerged along the way. Leave with practical guidance for designing more resilient data foundations on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Commvault, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Resilience patterns for the disconnected edge with Amazon Leo
sessions.a: Every resilient system eventually has to answer one question: what happens when the network you depend on isn’t there? In this session we discuss Amazon Leo, a low earth orbit satellite connectivity service, as a forcing function to explore patterns for architecting across unreliable, high-latency, and intermittently connected links. We’ll walk through the trade-offs behind routing, data-in-transit security, and where to place compute when bandwidth is scarce and connectivity is a variable. We’ll ground the discussion in hybrid resiliency and edge data collection for AI/ML, but the takeaway is portable to any architecture spanning boundaries you don’t fully control.

sessions.t: Resilience starts where your assumptions end, feat. Autodesk
sessions.a: The challenge most companies face is knowing where they stand with resilience, being willing to validate their assumptions safely, and disciplined enough to continuously improve without slowing delivery. In this session, we walk through Autodesk's journey with resilience testing and automated recovery failover as proof that investing in validation pays off, and you leave with a repeatable lifecycle for turning your own assumptions into proven capabilities. Discover how the next-generation AWS Resilience Hub handles the tedious work like mapping dependencies, assessing posture, and preconfiguring resilience tests, leaving your teams to focus on closing the gap between the system you think you operate and the one you actually do.

sessions.t: Resilient by design: Simplifying last-mile connectivity with AWS
sessions.a: Establishing resilient private connectivity from data centers and branch offices to AWS has traditionally required weeks of partner coordination, physical cross-connects, and manual resilience configurations—yet true resilience demands more than provisioning a second connection. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how AWS Direct Connect and AWS Interconnect each address location diversity, device diversity, BGP routing policy, and failover validation. Compare dedicated links with full routing control to fully managed connections with built-in redundancy, explore integration with AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN, and evaluate maximum versus high resiliency models. Bring your hybrid connectivity challenges.

sessions.t: Resilient by design: Simplifying last-mile connectivity with AWS
sessions.a: Establishing resilient private connectivity from data centers and branch offices to AWS has traditionally required weeks of partner coordination, physical cross-connects, and manual resilience configurations—yet true resilience demands more than provisioning a second connection. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how AWS Direct Connect and AWS Interconnect each address location diversity, device diversity, BGP routing policy, and failover validation. Compare dedicated links with full routing control to fully managed connections with built-in redundancy, explore integration with AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN, and evaluate maximum versus high resiliency models. Bring your hybrid connectivity challenges.

sessions.t: Resilient Cloud Ops: From IaC to Fault Injection
sessions.a: Production infrastructure needs two guarantees: repeatable deployment and proven resilience. In this bootcamp, use AWS CDK and CloudFormation to define and provision cloud resources as code, eliminating manual configuration drift. Then validate your architecture under stress. Troubleshoot VPC connectivity using flow logs, inject controlled faults with AWS Fault Injection Service, and confirm your infrastructure recovers gracefully. Deploy it right, then prove it holds.

sessions.t: Resilient VLM Training at Scale on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.a: Training vision-language models at scale fails in predictable ways — node crashes mid-epoch, checkpoints corrupt, and GPU clusters sit idle during recovery. In this hands-on workshop, build resilient VLM training pipelines on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod that survive real-world failures. Configure automatic health monitoring and node replacement, implement fault-tolerant checkpointing strategies, and design distributed training topologies that resume without losing progress. Using open-source frameworks on multi-node GPU clusters, you'll train a VLM end-to-end while simulating and recovering from infrastructure failures. Leave with battle-tested patterns for keeping large-scale training runs alive.

sessions.t: Resolve Amazon ECS incidents faster with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.a: Incident investigation on Amazon ECS means correlating signals across task logs, service events, deployment history, and CloudWatch metrics - scattered data that takes hours to piece together. In this builders session, deploy AWS DevOps Agent against an ECS workload and experience autonomous incident response. The agent discovers your service topology, receives CloudWatch alarms, investigates autonomously by testing hypotheses against telemetry data, and delivers root cause analysis with specific remediation steps. Practice the full workflow from alarm to resolution without manually searching a single dashboard. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.t: Resolve and Prevent Production Incidents with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.a: AWS DevOps Agent investigates production incidents end-to-end: tracing failures to the responsible change, guiding the fix, and verifying recovery. Once the service is stable, the agent converts root cause findings into automated prevention rules that enforce mandatory review gates on the same class of risk in future deployments. In this SimuLearn session, experience the full investigate, resolve, and prevent lifecycle as one continuous workflow in a single session.

sessions.t: Resolve it all: Build hybrid DNS architectures on AWS
sessions.a: Your enterprise runs workloads across multiple Amazon VPCs while maintaining connectivity to on-premises data centers—and DNS is the glue holding it all together. In this workshop, build a realistic hybrid DNS architecture using the latest Amazon Route 53 capabilities. Participants will learn how to centralize DNS configurations with Route 53 Profiles, replace conditional forwarding rules with native delegation using Resolver Delegation Endpoints, detect and block DNS-based threats with DNS Firewall, and enable secure authenticated resolution for distributed clients with Route 53 Global Resolver. Bring your laptop and resolve hybrid DNS once and for all.

sessions.t: Resolve it all: Build hybrid DNS architectures on AWS
sessions.a: Your enterprise runs workloads across multiple Amazon VPCs while maintaining connectivity to on-premises data centers—and DNS is the glue holding it all together. Participants will learn how to centralize DNS configurations with Route 53 Profiles, replace conditional forwarding rules with native delegation using Resolver Delegation Endpoints, detect and block DNS-based threats with DNS Firewall, and enable secure authenticated resolution for distributed clients with Route 53 Global Resolver. sessions.t: Responsible AI Enablement: Balancing Innovation, Governance and Control (sponsored by Island)
sessions.a: Most organizations are currently stuck between two worlds: the urgent need to adopt AI to remain competitive, & the critical mandate to protect corporate data & reputation. AI is evolving faster than any tool in IT history, and faster than any organization can keep up with. The temptation to simply block access to AI is strong, but just saying "No" means ceding the advantage to those able to say "Yes!". The 3 Pillars of a "Secure Yes": Visibility: Knowing what AI is being used across the org. Accountability: Defining who owns the data & the output. Resilience: Building frameworks that adapt as regulations change. In this session, we will outline the framework for secure AI adoption. We will move past the hype to discuss how leaders can build visibility, maintain accountability, and foster a culture of responsible innovation. This presentation is brought to you by Island, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Rethinking Agentic Security: How Cyera Scaled AI Securely in Days (sponsored by Cyera)
sessions.a: As AI shifts from assistive systems to autonomous agents, data becomes the control surface. Agents need a goldilocks balance of data, identity, and process access: enough to be effective, too much and you end up on Twitter. Cyera solved this internally, reaching 88% weekly AI usage across engineering and non-engineering teams in 17 days. Adoption was not the hard part. The wiring was. How do you govern access and give builders a permit path so they ship instead of wait? Join us for what we learned, and what it means on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Rethinking the boundary between messaging and streaming
sessions.a: Modern event-driven architectures still separate cleanly into "queues" and "streams," but real workloads no longer do. Replay, request-response, ordering, and high throughput increasingly appear across both patterns, making the wrong service choice costly to unwind. This session explores the architectural spectrum across messaging and streaming systems, drawing on services such as Amazon SQS, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon MSK. Through a real CQRS architecture, we build a practical decision framework for when to choose messaging, streaming, or a hybrid approach, and which trade-offs matter most.

sessions.t: Rethink release management for the agentic coding era
sessions.a: GitOps was designed for human-speed change. Agentic coding tools now generate pull requests faster than any team can review and safely release. Your release process is the new bottleneck. In this code talk, we'll live-code a GitOps release workflow where AWS DevOps Agent acts as an intelligent release manager, validating the results through a release pipeline at every promotion gate. Instead of manual approvals, DevOps Agent uses production intelligence (runtime dependencies, service health, deployment risk) to make real-time go/no-go decisions. Learn how to wire DevOps Agent into your GitOps reconciliation loop so releases match the velocity of agentic code generation without sacrificing safety.

sessions.t: Rethink release management for the agentic coding era
sessions.a: GitOps was designed for human-speed change. Agentic coding tools now generate pull requests faster than any team can review and safely release. Your release process is the new bottleneck. In this code talk, we'll live-code a GitOps release workflow where AWS DevOps Agent acts as an intelligent release manager, validating the results through a release pipeline at every promotion gate. Instead of manual approvals, DevOps Agent uses production intelligence (runtime dependencies, service health, deployment risk) to make real-time go/no-go decisions. Learn how to wire DevOps Agent into your GitOps reconciliation loop so releases match the velocity of agentic code generation without sacrificing safety.

sessions.t: Rewriting the AWS SDK for Python: Async from the ground up
sessions.a: If you've ever wrapped boto3 in asyncio hacks, juggled thread pools for concurrent AWS calls, or wished for proper streaming support, this talk is for you. We're rewriting the AWS SDK for Python with async built in from day one. We'll share the engineering challenges - why async-native is harder than "just add await" - and then show you the result: clean concurrent calls, bidirectional streaming with Bedrock and Transcribe, and a migration path that doesn't require rewriting your application overnight.

sessions.t: Right Compute, right time, right price: A decision framework for HPC and AI at scale
sessions.a: Large-scale HPC and AI workloads share the same hard problem: getting the right compute, at the right time, at the right price. In this chalk talk, we cover the architecture and provisioning decisions that matter when you move beyond a single instance. Architecture side: cluster design for distributed AI training and tightly coupled HPC simulation, networking trade-offs and where CPUs (x86, Graviton) fit alongside GPUs in production pipelines. Provisioning side: Capacity Blocks for predictable GPU bursts, On-Demand Capacity Reservations for sustained workloads, Spot for fault-tolerant jobs, and Savings Plans for steady-state fleets. We share real customer examples leveraging Amazon EC2 across HPC and AI/ML. Bring your hardest capacity and cost questions.

sessions.t: Right-size and scale Amazon ECS with effective autoscaling patterns
sessions.a: Autoscaling containerized workloads means scaling both tasks and the infrastructure underneath them. This chalk talk explores Amazon ECS autoscaling patterns including target tracking, step scaling, and scheduled scaling across AWS Fargate and Amazon ECS Managed Instances. Understand how these patterns interact with capacity providers so you can balance performance against cost. Discuss right-sizing tasks, handling traffic spikes, and avoiding over-provisioning. Bring your scaling challenges for an interactive technical discussion.

Bring your scaling challenges for an interactive technical discussion.

sessions.t: Right-size your observability: maximize signal, minimize spend
sessions.a: Your telemetry is scattered across tools. Your storage costs keep climbing. Your AI agents are a black box. In this chalk talk, we'll tackle your problems head-on with Amazon OpenSearch Service. Bring your toughest scenarios. Ask how our purpose-built log analytics engine reduces cost while boosting query performance. Ask how to unify logs, traces, and metrics into a single OpenTelemetry-native pane of glass with cost efficiency. If you're building AI agents, ask how to trace LLM calls, track per-invocation cost, and debug multi-agent workflows. And for any workload, ask how to stack cost levers like right-sizing, tiered storage, and writeable warm to maximize savings.

sessions.t: Right tool, right layer: Combining ML models and autonomous agents
sessions.a: Financial institutions deploy dozens of models and manual workflows that struggle to work together at scale. Machine learning excels at fast, explainable decisions while agentic AI orchestrates multi-step workflows with reasoning and adaptability. Real value is knowing when to use each and combining them into one system. In this chalk talk, we present a decision framework and demonstrate an architecture where machine learning models score and detect while agents reason, act, and close the loop while delivering the auditability regulators require. We walk through a Know Your Customer (KYC) example, then open the floor. Bring your use case.

sessions.t: Ring's Security Evolution: From Doorbell to Enterprise Platform (sponsored by Ring LLC)
sessions.a: Ring started with a simple mission: make neighborhoods safer with a video doorbell. That mission has scaled — from 100M+ residential cameras to SMB storefronts and jobsites with mobile security towers, to an AI-powered Appstore unlocking entirely new use cases across elder care, workforce analytics, and beyond. Now, Ring is making its boldest leap yet: a cloud-native enterprise platform built on AWS, combining video management, intelligent alerting, third-party camera ingestion, and access control. Join this lightning round to trace Ring's evolution and see what's next for enterprise security. This presentation is brought to you by Ring LLC, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Rivian's journey to Multi-Availability Zone factory resilience on AWS Outposts
sessions.a: Discover why Rivian chose AWS Outposts to support mission-critical manufacturing applications that produce vehicles at their Normal, IL plant. Explore how Rivian architected highly redundant infrastructure across multiple Outpost racks, leveraging fast EC2 provisioning and scaling to meet production line demands. We cover Multi-AZ deployment for high availability, RDS read replicas across racks for database resilience, and AWS Unified Operations for proactive observability across their hybrid environment. Learn how Rivian plans to scale this model into their 9 million square-foot mega factory in Georgia.

sessions.t: Route, cache and batch: a multi-model decision framework on Bedrock
sessions.a: Treating every request the same is what makes inference expensive at scale, and most of that cost is repeat work you already paid for. This chalk talk whiteboards how prompt caching on Amazon Bedrock eliminates redundant computation across system prompts, shared context, and multi-turn conversations, then shows where Intelligent Prompt Routing and batch inference extend the savings further. We walk through cache-hit economics, how to structure prompts for maximum reuse, and when routing or batching is the better lever. Bring your traffic patterns and questions, and leave with a caching-first cost strategy tuned to your workloads.

sessions.t: Route or escalate: Confidence boundaries in multi-domain AI agents
sessions.a: Building a GenAI system that answers questions across technology domains is straightforward — until the model doesn't know the answer and doesn't say so. For builders designing multi-agent or RAG-based systems, this session presents the confidence-gated routing architecture behind AWS Specialist Agent: classifying every query into high-confidence retrieval, low-confidence escalation to a human specialist, or cross-domain composition. We cover why flat vector retrieval fails multi-domain queries, the trade-offs of graph-based knowledge ontology, and the evaluations framework measuring confidence calibration. Walk away with a routing pattern you can apply any time your AI system must self-report uncertainty rather than hallucinate with authority.

sessions.t: Routing events at scale with Amazon EventBridge
sessions.a: Amazon EventBridge simplifies event routing for distributed applications. In this chalk talk, explore how to centralize multi-account event routing without custom infrastructure. We discuss routing policies, event discovery with schema registry, and access controls that let platform teams govern while app teams move independently. We also explore rate limiting and backpressure so your applications gracefully handle traffic spikes and protect downstream systems without losing events.

sessions.t: Rubrik Agentic Cyber Resilience: Secure and Recover at Machine Speed (sponsored by Rubrik)
sessions.a: AI-powered attacks and agentic overreach now move at machine speed — a rogue AI agent with privileged access can do as much damage as a ransomware crew. This session introduces Rubrik's Agentic Cyber Resilience platform, unifying data, identity, and AI agents end to end. The Preemptive Recovery Engine identifies clean points in peacetime so recovery starts in minutes, not weeks. It governs every agent action and rewinds mistakes before they spread across your environment. One platform, one clean point, one recovery. This presentation is brought to you by Rubrik, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Rubrik Powers Autonomous Business Recovery for AWS (sponsored by Rubrik)
sessions.a: When a ransomware attack strikes, native snapshots and manual scripting are fundamentally broken. IT teams are left piecing together obsolete dependency maps and restoring untested backups that risk re-infecting the environment. Rubrik turns this into a fully automated, orchestrated sequence, powered by anchor-tag discovery, unified air-gapped backups, and our Preemptive Recovery Engine. This session breaks down Rubrik Autonomous Business Recovery for Cloud Applications: a single tag builds a living dependency map, one policy closes protection gaps across the stack, and recovery rebuilds network, compute, then data from a validated clean point without manual scripting. This presentation is brought to you by Rubrik, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Running AI agents you can trust on Amazon EKS
sessions.a: AI agents are rapidly moving from prototype to production, and running them at scale presents new challenges. Untrusted, AI-generated code executes in your environment. Many agents share the same infrastructure. Workloads spin up, act, and tear down constantly. Join this session to learn how to run agents securely on Amazon EKS with VM-level isolation, wire up the primitives agents need for tools, memory, and orchestration, and manage fleets of short-lived, bursty workloads. You'll also see how the same EKS platform you run your critical workloads on extends into the agentic era and where we're headed next.

sessions.t: Running compute-efficient workloads on Amazon EKS Auto Mode
sessions.a: Amazon EKS Auto Mode, powered by open source Karpenter, simplifies infrastructure management while optimizing compute resources. Karpenter provisions Amazon EC2 Instances based on the requirements of your workload. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll gain practical experience in advanced workload scheduling, continually compute optimization with Karpenter consolidation, explore AWS Graviton and AWS spare capacity through Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Whether you’re new to EKS Auto Mode, or an experienced operator you’ll learn best practices for running efficient workloads on Amazon EKS while simplifying Kubernetes cluster management.

sessions.t: Running untrusted code in sandboxes with AWS Lambda MicroVMs
sessions.a: AI coding assistants generate code. Customers upload plugins. Third parties submit extensions. All of it needs to run somewhere and that somewhere can't be your production environment. In this builders' session, use AWS Lambda MicroVMs to build secure sandboxes that execute untrusted code at scale with hardware-level tenant isolation. You'll configure sandbox lifecycle management, implement resource limits and permissions boundaries, set up observability for sandboxed executions, and test failure modes when code misbehaves. Walk away with a working isolation architecture you can adapt for your own multi-tenant workloads. Bring your laptop.

sessions.t: Running Vercel in Your Own AWS Account (sponsored by Vercel)
sessions.a: This session explores how Vercel Enterprise customers can run workloads in their own AWS account while continuing to use the Vercel developer experience. You’ll learn about the separation between the Vercel control plane and customer runtime, and why this model can help organizations meet data privacy, security, and compliance requirements. You’ll see how the setup works through a live walkthrough and demo, and how this architecture can support broader access to tools like v0, Amazon Q, and other coding agents. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Run your largest SAP HANA on AWS: EC2 High Memory deep dive
sessions.a: Running SAP HANA at scale requires infrastructure that matches the size and criticality of your Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) workloads. EC2 High Memory instances deliver capacity from 256 GB to 32 TB, backed by the AWS Nitro architecture for consistent performance and hardware-level isolation. In this session, we deep dive into the Nitro design powering these instances and hear how customers are scaling production ERP to 32 TB on AWS. Walk away with architectural guidance and real-world deployment patterns for running your largest HANA workloads in a scale-up configuration.

sessions.t: SaaS Agents Anywhere
sessions.a: Customers make deliberate choices about where their workloads run. For SaaS vendors delivering agentic products, that means the runtime has to meet the workload where it is, not the other way around. This chalk talk teaches the everywhere agent pattern for SaaS: keep the control plane on AWS, run the agent runtime and data-plane execution wherever the customer's data lives. Learn three decisions: which destinations to support and when (multi-cloud, on-prem, or both), how to run agent runtimes outside AWS without rewriting your control plane (packaging, model backend selection, dependency portability), and how to manage identity, observability, and lifecycle across environments you don't own. Leave with the decision framework for shipping SaaS agents anywhere the customer's data lives.

sessions.t: SaaS Agents Anywhere: building distributed agentic deployments
sessions.a: SaaS vendors deploy agents across a spectrum: fully provider-hosted, fully tenant-controlled, and hybrid models in between. Once customers have data residency or cost-visibility requirements, deployment topology determines the operational pattern. In this workshop, build a distributed agentic deployment on AWS spanning your accounts and a tenant's, then exercise the three concerns that surface everywhere on the spectrum: lifecycle management of agents you can't directly see, observability across account boundaries, and reliability when the agent runs somewhere you don't operate. Leave with a working reference deployment you can adapt to your own tenancy model.

sessions.t: Safer, simpler, faster upgrades with managed blue/green deployments
sessions.a: Blue/green deployments for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS simplify the process of upgrading and performing maintenance on your databases. In this chalk talk, you will architect a blue/green database upgrade solution to support major or minor engine version upgrades and perform schema changes with minimal and predictable downtime. Active participation is encouraged as you architect a solution to meet your requirements. In open discussion, learn the trade-offs involved in database management when using blue/green deployments and how to design the most effective upgrade solution to meet your needs.
