sessions.t: Same code, any compute: Portable architecture on AWS
sessions.a: Your business logic shouldn't be coupled to a compute service. In this session, apply Hexagonal Architecture and 12-factor patterns to design workloads where compute is a deployment decision, not an architectural one. Through live code, see the same logic packaged as a Lambda function, a Fargate task, and an EKS pod using AWS Lambda Web Adapter and runtime-neutral handler patterns. You'll learn where portability pays off, where it adds unnecessary abstraction, and how to evaluate the trade-offs between pay-per-request, always-on containers, and orchestrated clusters for your workloads.

sessions.t: Sandboxing AI Agents on EKS: Isolation That Scales
sessions.a: AI agents execute untrusted code — one prompt injection away from data exfiltration. This session covers building graduated isolation for autonomous agents on EKS using the agent-sandbox controller. You'll learn why runtime tiers (runc → gVisor → Firecracker) map to different threat models, how SandboxClaim resources manage ephemeral agent lifecycle, and Cilium FQDN egress filtering that prevents exfiltration without blocking legitimate tool use. We'll whiteboard Karpenter NodePool design for gVisor-capable nodes, discuss cost tradeoffs between isolation levels, and share what breaks when you over-isolate. Leave with a production-ready isolation framework.

sessions.t: SAST Is Dead: Program Analysis for AI Agents (sponsored by Semgrep)
sessions.a: LLMs didn't kill security testing, they exposed tools that guess at context they don't have. This talk explains what we learned by reinventing program analysis for new end users: builders and agents. We had to develop benchmarks and add determinism with program slicing to better control costs and deliver the optimal price per true vulnerability detected. This presentation is brought to you by Semgrep, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Scalable LLM inference, easy on the ops: CrowdStrike on SageMaker AI
sessions.a: When adversaries move in seconds, security has to move faster. CrowdStrike shares how they built scalable, real-time LLM inference on Amazon SageMaker to power threat detection at massive scale, where sub-second latency is a hard requirement. Learn how dedicated, configurable endpoints gave them full control over performance, while SageMaker AI's managed infrastructure removed the operational overhead. Walk away with a blueprint for running latency-critical workloads on SageMaker Managed Inference, without running the stack yourself.

sessions.t: Scale AI-powered software development securely with Bedrock
sessions.a: Your dev teams are adopting AI coding agents fast: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, open-source agents, and more. Without a shared platform, every team rolls its own auth, its own cost tracking, its own rules. In this builders session, build one platform on Amazon Bedrock that manages all of them. Package your security policies, coding standards, and delivery practices as reusable plugins, agent skills, and MCP servers, then apply consistent identity, sandboxing, observability, and cost controls across every agent. See a team onboard and take an issue from plan to tested change. Leave with a working reference architecture.

sessions.t: Scale data for RAG and AI agents cost-effectively with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.a: Discover how S3 Vectors transforms retrieval workloads for AI agents and RAG pipelines with native vector storage and query capabilities. This session explores recent enhancements that deliver deeper, more comprehensive search results per query while dramatically reducing costs at scale, reducing the need for multiple round trips while running large-scale RAG, semantic search, and AI workloads. Learn architecture best practices, performance optimization techniques, and diverse vector use cases, from semantic search to large-scale RAG implementations.

sessions.t: Scale financial risk simulations with AWS Batch and Amazon ECS
sessions.a: Financial institutions run millions of simulations overnight to price options, stress-test portfolios, and satisfy regulators. Scaling those workloads means balancing queue depth against compute cost. AWS Batch on Amazon ECS eliminates that tradeoff — containers scale elastically, Spot instances cut compute cost, and job orchestration handles retries and memory tuning without custom scripts. In this chalk talk, walk through a production architecture where a quantitative hedge fund runs its entire research compute on AWS Batch. Then open the whiteboard and discuss how to apply these patterns to your own pricing engines, VaR calculations, or scenario analysis workloads.

sessions.t: Scale, optimize and deploy inference with Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode
sessions.a: Accelerated workloads make node provisioning challenging. Picking the wrong instance, scheduling constraint, or disruption policy impacts GPU utilization and drives up costs. This deep dive covers how Amazon EKS provisions and scales accelerated compute for real inference workloads, whether you run managed Auto Mode or self-managed Karpenter. See how both select across GPU and accelerator families and honor topology-aware scheduling. Learn the NodePool and disruption settings that keep utilization high without hurting latency-sensitive serving. Discover how Dynamic Resource Allocation and GPU sharing squeeze more inference out of every device, plus accelerator-aware node repair that keeps long-running jobs healthy.

sessions.t: Scale production agents reliably with AgentCore
sessions.a: What changes when you go from ten agent sessions to ten thousand? In this chalk talk, whiteboard the architectural and operational patterns that determine whether your agents perform reliably at scale. Discuss microVM isolation for secure multi-tenancy, elastic scaling that handles traffic spikes without capacity planning, and long-running task handling with human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Cover resiliency patterns: what happens when a tool call fails, how to handle model timeouts, and designing for graceful degradation. Walk through the infrastructure decisions you make once and benefit from forever. Bring your scaling scenarios and we architect solutions together.

sessions.t: Scale reinforcement learning globally with sparse weight updates (sponsored by Modal)
sessions.a: Reinforcement learning post training usually keeps trainers and rollout workers in one tightly coupled GPU cluster. This talk shows how to keep backpropagation on fast local fabric while moving independent rollout workers to elastic GPU capacity across regions and clouds. The key is to diff weights in the precision actually served, then publish lossless sparse version transitions instead of full checkpoints. Attendees will learn why Adam/Muon updates often disappear under BF16 rounding, how version aware sidecars commit exact weight versions, and how this architecture turns globally available inference capacity into practical reinforcement learning capacity. This presentation is brought to you by Modal, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Scale Through Partners: The Partner-Led SMB Growth Engine
sessions.a: SMB is a $1T opportunity—98% of global businesses are small/mid-size, 81% are increasing AI spend, yet fewer than 300 AWS partners hold the SMB Competency. This session unpacks AWS's Indirect Selling engine: new incentives aligned to growth, AI-powered lead generation, SMB solution selling, and a Partnership Maturity Framework turning opportunistic engagement into repeatable business practice. You'll leave with unit economics proving indirect selling reaches SMBs globally, a clear activation timeline from Opportunity through full Business Practice, and specific first moves to build a scalable, profitable SMB practice on AWS—your 20-minute roadmap to outsized growth.

sessions.t: Scale your coding agents beyond the laptop with AgentCore
sessions.a: Developers want Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro with laptop-like feel but without laptop limits: no parallelism, no persistence, no isolation. In this hands-on workshop, you will deploy a coding agent to AgentCore's runtime in three commands, then build real workflows: a code review agent, PR automation, and a repo consolidation job. You will run agents in parallel across isolated microVMs, persist and share state with BYO S3 and EFS, connect models through Bedrock, and wire an agent to wake on GitHub events and work in the background. Leave with working code you can drop straight into your own repos.

sessions.t: Scaling agent memory with Amazon S3 Vectors and S3 Files
sessions.a: Persistent, scalable memory is foundational to production AI agents. In this session, learn how the combination of S3 Vectors and S3 Files provides a unified memory layer for agents by using S3 Vectors for embedding-based semantic recall and S3 Files for low-latency, mutable working memory and shared state across agent sessions. We’ll cover architecture patterns for short-term and long-term memory, multi-agent memory sharing, and managing memory lifecycle and cost as usage grows, including how recent S3 Vectors enhancements improve retrieval economics at scale. Leave with patterns for memory architectures that scale to millions of agent interactions.

sessions.t: Scaling AI Defenses with AWS and CrowdStrike (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
sessions.a: AI is accelerating innovation — and accelerating attackers. From prompt injection and data exfiltration to cloud privilege escalation, adversaries are increasingly exploiting AI-powered architectures to move faster than traditional defenses. In this session, AWS and CrowdStrike experts will demonstrate how organizations can securely build and defend modern AI workloads running on AWS. Attendees will explore real-world architectures using Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore and see how attackers move across identity, cloud, and AI services to exploit security gaps. Through live demonstrations and architectural guidance, the session will show how AWS and CrowdStrike help organizations surface shadow AI; visualize attack paths across code and AI services; stop AI-specific attacks; automate protection workflows; and deliver real-time cloud detection and response (CDR) across modern AI environments. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Scaling and securing MCP Servers with AWS Load Balancing and WAF
sessions.a: MCP servers are becoming essential infrastructure in enterprise AI environments, and running them in production demands both scalability and security. Join this chalk talk to explore patterns for scaling and securing your MCP servers using AWS native services. We'll cover how to configure Application Load Balancer for MCP traffic characteristics, implement health checks and routing policies, scale horizontally across availability zones, and enforce security controls with AWS WAF - including request filtering, rate limiting, and tool-level access policies. Whether you're running a handful of MCP servers or deploying at enterprise scale, you'll leave with actionable architectures for production-ready deployments.

sessions.t: Scaling EC2 Spot with a focus on capacity, GPUs, and allocation
sessions.a: Today, organizations run ML training, inference, and large-scale simulations on Spot across CPU and GPU instance families. But scaling Spot successfully requires understanding how capacity actually behaves. In this session, the EC2 Spot product leader shares what the data reveals: which diversification strategies consistently deliver high fill rates, how allocation strategies differ for CPU vs. GPU workloads, and when tools like Spot Placement Score and EC2 Capacity Manager make the difference. You'll leave with a modern playbook covering instance diversification, multi-Region/AZ deployment, checkpointing for long-running jobs, and capacity rebalancing patterns the largest Spot customers use today.

sessions.t: Scaling ElastiCache globally: 400+ clusters & 1.3 trillion ops/day
sessions.a: Managing ride-hailing demand across 1,100+ cities and 8+ million daily transactions in real time requires scalable, resilient, sub-millisecond in-memory data operations. In this session, learn how inDrive evolved from a monolithic on-premises Redis OSS cluster to over 400 distributed Amazon ElastiCache clusters spanning 8 AWS Regions, executing 1.3 trillion operations daily. Discover how inDrive eliminated bottlenecks in single-CPU utilization, network saturation, and hotspot shards, and how a zero-downtime migration to the Valkey engine on ElastiCache improved performance and reduced costs. Attendees leave with a production-tested blueprint for scaling data-intensive systems across multiple AWS Regions.

sessions.t: Scaling Frontier AI model inference on AWS Trainium
sessions.a: Every team moving AI to production hits the same wall: scaling frontier model inference against growing token demand, tighter latency budgets, and spiraling compute costs. This workshop tackles that problem head-on. Experience how purpose-built chips changes the inference economics equation as you deploy Frontier AI models on AWS Trainium, apply optimization techniques, and learn how the Neuron software stack integrates with familiar open-source frameworks - no rewrites required - to achieve superior tokenomics. Leave with actionable skills to run performant, cost-effective model inference at production scale on AWS Trainium.

sessions.t: Scaling inference compute across clusters (sponsored by Baseten)
sessions.a: Your traffic outgrows a single cluster long before you expect it to. Colin McGrath explains how Baseten runs inference across more than 80 GPU clusters and roughly 15 cloud providers as one system: how capacity gets found and claimed, how requests get routed to the right region under real load, how large models get delivered to new clusters quickly, and how autoscaling behaves when traffic is bursty and cold starts are expensive. He covers what happens when a whole region goes down, and the patterns that matter most for teams scaling past one cluster. This presentation is brought to you by Baseten, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Scaling interactive GenerativeAI at Netflix with AWS Local Zones
sessions.a: Generative AI VFX and Animation teams at Netflix require the latest GPU hardware for creative workflows including real-time rendering, VFX editorial, and color correction. These workloads demand low-latency access to high-performance compute close to creative teams. AWS Local Zones make this possible by placing G7e instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs in the Los Angeles metro. Netflix's Studio GenAI Infrastructure, including GenAI Sessions and Universal Compute Service, uses Local Zones to serve just-in-time combinations of software and hardware in secure, isolated sandbox environments. Tools like ComfyUI and AIToolkit with complex dependencies run on task-oriented, elastic GPU assignments, so Netflix scales creative AI workloads efficiently without managing physical infrastructure.

sessions.t: Scaling ISV Revenue: Accelerating Co-Sell with AWS Marketplace
sessions.a: AWS Marketplace has become the fastest path for ISVs to scale co-sell, but unlocking its full potential means going beyond procurement and using it as the backbone of how you sell. This session unpacks how high-performing ISVs combine ISV Accelerate with AWS Marketplace to accelerate co-sell. Three points separate top performers: (1) structuring AWS seller alignment to generate Marketplace-routed pipeline, (2) using private offers and channel-partner workflows to compress enterprise deal cycles by 30-40%, and (3) mining Marketplace buyer signals to drive expansion and proactive renewal. Walk away with a focused playbook for turning Marketplace into a scalable revenue motion.

sessions.t: Scaling Multi-Account IAM at Netflix: Access, Visibility and Credentials
sessions.a: Managing IAM across a large, fast-growing AWS footprint quickly outgrows manual review — every permission change creates friction for engineers and queue time for operators. We'll cover a control-plane approach that ties together high-level IAM abstractions, automated workflows, and business context to drive the majority of AWS access needs. Developers describe intent against concrete resources instead of hand-writing JSON; Access Analyzer–backed probes auto-approve routine changes; administrators get a single pane of glass over SCPs, identity and resource policies, CloudTrail/S3 errors, and AWS Config history. Credential delivery flows through the same plane, enabling context-aware scoping for human and agentic callers alike.

sessions.t: Scaling Multi-Cluster EKS Without Burning Your Infrastructure Budget
sessions.a: Managing hundreds of Amazon EKS clusters breaks standard multi-tenant architectures under the weight of shared control planes, noisy neighbors, and runaway cross-AZ data transfer costs. This interactive chalk talk skips the slides to whiteboard the painful realities of multi-cluster fleet topology at scale. We will dissect the architectural trade-offs between monolithic clusters and localized micro-clusters, mapping out exact blast-radius constraints. Bring your worst infrastructure bottlenecks; we will openly debate cluster life-cycle automation, shared VPC patterns, and cost-allocation frameworks, leaving you with a battle-tested blueprint to optimize fleet operations on Monday morning.

sessions.t: Scaling operations with MCP, ACP, and A2A
sessions.a: Operational complexity doesn't scale linearly but your approach to managing it can. In this chalk talk, we'll use AWS DevOps Agent to explore three protocols shaping how operations teams work at scale: MCP (connecting to operational data and actions), ACP (delegating tasks to purpose-built agents), and A2A (coordinating across autonomous agents). We'll discuss how protocol choice affects decision-making, when to extend capabilities vs. delegate, and how to design architectures that grow with your operational footprint. Leave with a clear mental model for when to reach for each protocol and how they fit together.

Leave with a clear mental model for when to reach for each protocol and how they fit together.

sessions.t: Scaling Pharma Transformation Through Data-Driven Agentic AI (sponsored by Tech Mahindra)
sessions.a: Hear from a leading U.S. pharmaceutical company on its journey to transforming enterprise AI from isolated experiments into a scalable business capability. Discover how Tech Mahindra helped establish trusted data foundations, harness Agentic AI to enrich product and customer master data, unlock semantic intelligence, and create governed data products that power enterprise-wide insights, including drug demand forecasting. This session will explore the architectural principles, governance strategies, and leadership decisions required to scale compliant, trusted, and value-driven AI. Join Tech Mahindra and a pharma industry leader to learn how data-driven Agentic AI is reshaping the future of the intelligent pharma enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by Tech Mahindra, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Scaling website delivery with Amazon CloudFront: one configuration, many sites
sessions.a: Most enterprises don't run just one website — they run many: corporate sites, regional or sub-brand sites, internal portals, plus full environment tiers (Dev, QA, Staging, Prod) for each. Managing TLS certificates, WAF rules, and cache behavior separately creates configuration drift, inconsistent security posture, and operational overhead that scales with your site count. In this workshop, you'll use Amazon CloudFront to define a single reusable baseline configuration and apply it consistently across many website profiles — whether they represent different brands, business units, or environment tiers — while still allowing targeted overrides where a site genuinely needs to differ. You'll leave with a working reference architecture and a decision framework for what belongs in the baseline vs. the override.

sessions.t: Secrets rotation patterns for agentic pipelines at scale
sessions.a: Autonomous agents provision, consume, and rotate credentials without a human in the loop. In this chalk-talk, work through how to build a secrets lifecycle for multi-step agentic workflows: issue dynamic secrets using AWS temporary credentials and leverage AWS Secrets Manager for secrets rotation, Scope each agent with resource policies and VPC endpoint conditions to enforce a data perimeter, and apply AWS KMS envelope encryption so ephemeral secrets never persist in plaintext. Leave with deployable templates for zero-standing-privilege secret delivery across chained agent invocations.

sessions.t: Secure agents at scale on Amazon ECS with VM-level isolation
sessions.a: If you run agents, multi-tenant services, or regulated workloads on shared infrastructure, the isolation boundary is an important security consideration. This session shows how to design that boundary using VM-level isolation on Amazon ECS. You will leave knowing how to isolate tenants and untrusted agent workloads from one another, apply least-privilege execution toward compliance obligations, and run it all efficiently at scale. Whether you build agentic AI platforms or sensitive multi-tenant applications, you will walk away with a practical blueprint for strong isolation on ECS.

sessions.t: Secure AI Agent Access with AgentCore Identity
sessions.a: Not every caller should have access to your AI agents, and you should verify who is calling them before responding. In this hands-on lab, you deploy an IT help desk agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and configure AgentCore Identity to enforce inbound authentication. You set up an Amazon Cognito user pool as the identity provider, obtain and decode a JSON Web Token (JWT), and test that the agent rejects unauthenticated callers while allowing verified employees through.

sessions.t: Secure AI the same way you secure everything else on AWS
sessions.a: You already run security and governance on AWS with IAM, CloudTrail, KMS, and VPC boundaries, and AI workloads on Bedrock inherit all of it. This chalk talk shows how: IAM scoping for model access, data perimeter policies, full prompt and response logging in CloudTrail, and KMS encryption at rest and in transit. There is no separate governance stack to learn and no new tools to onboard. You leave knowing how to extend the security patterns your organization already trusts to cover AI workloads on Bedrock.

sessions.t: Secure and modernize code simultaneously with agentic AI
sessions.a: Most modernization teams bolt security on as an afterthought, creating costly late-stage vulnerabilities. In this code talk, you'll follow along as we build a custom agent using Strands Agents SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that takes a security-first approach. We wire up AWS Transform agents for tech debt analysis via MCP integrations, connect AWS Continuum for deep code-level vulnerability scanning, and orchestrate everything through Kiro. The result: an agent that synthesizes a security-hardened modernization plan and autonomously executes it. See AI agents collaborate in real time to transform and secure code simultaneously, eliminating handoffs between teams.

sessions.t: Secure and Scalable Multi-Tenant Deployment Patterns for Amazon Quick
sessions.a: As organizations scale their adoption of Amazon Quick across business units, subsidiaries, and partner ecosystems, deploying a secure multi-tenant architecture becomes critical. This chalk talk explores proven deployment patterns that balance tenant isolation, governance, and operational efficiency when rolling out Amazon Quick at enterprise scale. We will walk through two primary isolation strategies: multi-account separation using AWS Organizations for environment-level boundaries (dev/staging/prod), and namespace-based logical isolation within a single account for user-cohort segmentation.

sessions.t: Secure by Design: The AWS foundation for your AI applications
sessions.a: As organizations deploy AI and agents in production, leaders need confidence that their cloud provider is secure by design. This session explores why AWS is designed to be the most secure foundation for AI. We detail how AWS foundational security extends into AI services, examine the AI security differentiators that build on this foundation, and walk through the security capabilities customers can use to protect their most critical AI workloads. You will leave with a clear picture of why organizations trust AWS for AI.

sessions.t: Secure Coding Agents for Regulated Environments with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (sponsored by Act Security)
sessions.a: Learn how HUB International, a top-five global insurance broker, partnered with AWS and Act Security to securely bring autonomous coding agents into a regulated enterprise environment, without giving the agents standing credentials or expanding the attack surface. The team transformed the local Claude Code experience into a secure, per-user cloud sandbox on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, preserving the familiar IDE and terminal workflow while moving execution to the cloud. See how OIDC authentication through the corporate IdP, per-call token minting through AgentCore Identity, and Cedar-based authorization for tools exposed through AgentCore Gateway enforce per-user, per-action access. Finally, discover how Act Security sustains least privilege over time and enforces narrower policies - whether you are deploying AgentCore for the first time or hardening an existing environment. This presentation is brought to you by Act Security, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Secure data transfers at scale with AWS DataSync and Transfer Family
sessions.a: Organizations moving data to AWS need transfers that are fast, secure, and manageable at petabyte scale. In this session, learn how AWS DataSync and AWS Transfer Family help you accelerate migrations, automate ongoing data movement, and enable secure file exchanges with external partners. We'll cover best practices for maximizing throughput, designing transfer architectures for performance and cost efficiency, and integrating secure workflows across hybrid and multi-cloud environments. Hear directly from a customer about how they used these services to solve large-scale data movement challenges in production.

sessions.t: Secure your CI to operate at machine speed (sponsored by Chainguard)
sessions.a: AI agents are changing how software is built, introducing new security challenges across the software supply chain. CI environments are particularly vulnerable, with access to sensitive credentials and elevated permissions. We’ll explore how Chainguard's trusted artifacts, isolated build environments, and integrations with AWS can reduce risk from development through deployment and what securing software delivery looks like when AI agents are doing more of the work. This presentation is brought to you by Chainguard, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Securing AI agents: Governance patterns for regulated workloads
sessions.a: Financial institutions building agentic AI platforms face a fundamental problem: security and governance controls were designed for humans and applications, not autonomous agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard the architecture decisions that matter most—covering identity, authorization, secrets, tenancy, and governance—and classify each as a one-way or two-way door. We'll walk through concrete patterns including agent authentication, agent-to-tool authorization, application-layer data segregation, and a multi-source governance model using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon CloudWatch, and AWS CloudTrail. Leave with decisions you can apply to your own agentic platform.

sessions.t: Securing AI agents: Governance patterns for regulated workloads
sessions.a: Financial institutions building agentic AI platforms face a fundamental problem: security and governance controls were designed for humans and applications, not autonomous agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard the architecture decisions that matter most—covering identity, authorization, secrets, tenancy, and governance—and classify each as a one-way or two-way door. We'll walk through concrete patterns including agent authentication, agent-to-tool authorization, application-layer data segregation, and a multi-source governance model using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon CloudWatch, and AWS CloudTrail. Leave with decisions you can apply to your own agentic platform.

sessions.t: Securing AI and Autonomous Agents: Protecting the Lifecycle Across Any Platform (sponsored by Fortinet)
sessions.a: AI agents are actively running code, accessing databases, and making critical business decisions across every industry. But as these systems gain independence, they also introduce complex security risks throughout their lifecycle. Are you ready to protect a system that learns and acts on its own as your organization embarks on the AI journey? Join our panel of top AI and cybersecurity experts as they break down the end-to-end security of AI systems and agentic applications. We will explore real-world customer challenges and share practical strategies to safeguard autonomous agents across cloud and on-premises environments. This presentation is brought to you by Fortinet, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Securing AI Coding Agents: Defence in Depth Across the Development Lifecycle
sessions.a: AI coding agents optimise for task completion, not security, generating code faster than humans can review. This chalk talk presents a defence-in-depth framework spanning five phases - pre-generation, authoring, PR, pipeline, and deployment - with three lines of defence at each: deterministic controls, AI screening, and human judgment. We cover author-time techniques (steering, specs, scoped MCP, hooks) and build-time gates (SAST, SCA, IaC scanning, AI-assisted review, approval) using Kiro, AWS Security Agent, and CodePipeline. Leave with a layered model you can apply on Monday.

sessions.t: Securing AI Coding Agents: Defence in Depth Across the Development Lifecycle

sessions.t: Securing Amazon Bedrock agents with AWS WAF and a self-healing security agent
sessions.a: As enterprises move generative AI agents from prototype to production, securing the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes a first-class requirement — not an afterthought. In this hands-on workshop, you'll attach AWS WAF natively to a Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with no ALB, no VPC interface endpoint, and no Lambda proxy required, enabling managed rule groups, rate-based rules, and IP-based access controls that protect every tool behind the gateway with a single configuration. We will launch simulated attacks and watch AWS WAF block them in real time. Finally, you'll build an agent that pulls signals from AWS WAF and autonomously remediates threats, generating a plain-English incident summary.

sessions.t: Securing Amazon Bedrock agents with AWS WAF and a self-healing security agent

sessions.t: Securing and observing Amazon EKS clusters
sessions.a: In this hands-on session, explore how to automate the identification, analysis, and mitigation of risks in Amazon EKS clusters. Learn how to implement robust security controls—including role-based access control (RBAC), EKS Pod Identity, and service accounts—to apply least-privilege access and secure workload isolation. Discover how to use AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch to gain deep visibility into EKS cluster activities, enabling real-time monitoring and automated risk detection. You will learn the skills to automate risk management processes, helping your Kubernetes workloads remain resilient against evolving threats.

sessions.t: Securing and optimizing your software supply chain with Amazon ECR
sessions.a: Raise the bar on your software supply chain security with AWS. In this chalk talk, we will discuss DevOps security best-practices, threat detection and incident response for containers, and how to leverage AWS security services including Amazon ECR, Amazon GuardDuty, and Amazon Inspector to protect your Amazon EKS workloads. Discover how you can ensure CVE patching while optimizing storage to accelerate image delivery through seamless integration with open-source tools for publishing and deploying containerized workloads at scale. Learn how to efficently streamline your software supply chain while mitigating risks.

sessions.t: Securing and optimizing your software supply chain with Amazon ECR
sessions.a: Raise the bar on your software supply chain security with AWS. Discover how you can ensure CVE patching while optimizing storage to accelerate image delivery through seamless integration with open-source tools for publishing and deploying containerized workloads at scale. Learn how to efficently streamline your software supply chain while mitigating risks.

sessions.t: Securing applications at machine speed in the frontier model era
sessions.a: Frontier AI models discover code vulnerabilities in minutes. Security teams still take days or weeks to validate, prioritize, and fix them. AWS Continuum closes that gap with one continuous workflow: discover risks in your code, prioritize by real exploitability, validate in a sandbox with reproduction steps, and remediate at machine speed within guardrails you define. In this session, we walk through how Continuum operates end-to-end: building a security context graph from your infrastructure, identity, and code to determine what is reachable, confirming exploitability through sandboxed proof-of-concept, and generating validated fixes. You see graduated trust in action, starting with human approval and promoting to autonomous remediation as confidence builds. You leave understanding how to move from manual triage to continuous discovery, validation, and remediation.

sessions.t: Securing Multi-Agent Systems
sessions.a: Multi-agent systems create a larger attack surface than single-agent deployments: prompt injections that propagate across agent boundaries, identity spoofing, tool-chain escalation, and data exfiltration through natural-language covert channels. In this chalk talk, we threat-model this risk using the OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, then whiteboard defense-in-depth patterns for validating inter-agent messages, enforcing least-privilege orchestration, and detecting anomalous behavior before it cascades. Leave with a set of recommendations and architectures that demonstrate how to layer security controls in a multi-agent system.

sessions.t: Securing OpenClaw deployments on AWS
sessions.a: In this session, we introduce the OpenClaw architecture, compare the major variants and their security posture differences, and then map the threat landscape for AWS-hosted deployments. Drawing on years of experience helping customers deploy, we cover the infrastructure and runtime threat landscape. You will leave with a reference architecture that applies defense-in-depth principles to such OpenClaw deployments on AWS, minimizing risk without sacrificing capability.

sessions.t: Securing Software & AI Supply Chains with Network Firewall at Coupang
sessions.a: Coupang, South Korea's largest e-commerce platform, runs millions of daily transactions on AWS. At that scale, every open-source library, container base image, and AI model weight pulled from the internet is a supply chain risk. Dive deep into AWS Network Firewall's architecture and latest capabilities, including centralized management and container-aware egress inspection. See how Coupang built cloud-native egress control that scales automatically across a container-first fleet, automates allowlist management, and mitigates rogue AI dependencies and dynamic payloads. Walk away with battle-tested patterns to lock down your software and AI supply chains without sacrificing developer velocity.

sessions.t: Securing the AI-Native Cloud (sponsored by Upwind)
sessions.a: In this session, we will demonstrate how AI is redefining cloud security by moving beyond static posture management to real-time, context-aware protection. The session will showcase how organizations can gain continuous visibility across their environments and respond to threats as they emerge. Attendees will see how AI-driven analysis of runtime behavior enables faster detection of anomalies, prioritization of real risks, and automated response across dynamic, multi-cloud infrastructures. The session will highlight how security teams can reduce noise, strengthen security processes, and proactively respond to threats before they escalate. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Securing the Bedrock: A Strong API Foundation for AI Innovation (sponsored by Kong)
sessions.a: AI moves fast until it hits production. Then agents that looked solid in a POC start making calls they shouldn't, hammering the vector database, or failing quietly under load, because the API layer underneath wasn't built for it. This session covers what a strong API foundation does for AI at scale: fine-grained authorization keeps context retrieval inside its data privacy boundaries, touching only what it's permitted to touch; rate limiting protects vector databases from resource exhaustion; edge caching cuts query latency without extra engineering; and circuit breaking plus canary deployments let teams ship changes without compromising security or compliance. You'll leave with architectural blueprints and real enterprise examples showing how the right API foundation turns governance from a blocker into what lets AI teams move faster. Presented by Kong an AWS Partner, alongside FanDuel. This presentation is brought to you by Kong, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Securing the Enterprise in the Age of AI Agents: From Zero Trust to Agentic Security (sponsored by Zscaler)
sessions.a: AI isn’t just another workload—it’s introducing agents that act, connect, and make decisions at machine speed. This session reframes Zero Trust for an agent-driven world: how to govern agent-to-agent communication, constrain access to sensitive data, and reduce risk without slowing the business. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Securing Your AI-Accelerated Software Supply Chain with AWS Well-Architected
sessions.a: Modern software depends on open-source packages from npm, PyPI, and Maven. AI assistants pull them into your codebase faster than ever, sometimes suggesting packages that don’t exist or shouldn’t be trusted. Attackers exploit this through “slopsquatting.” Supply chain incidents show registries targeted via credential compromise, typosquatting, and token farming at scale. This workshop builds a layered defense aligned to the AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar. You replace long-lived credentials with OIDC, sign artifacts with AWS Signer, and govern dependencies with CodeArtifact package groups. You scan AI-generated and human-written code with Amazon Inspector, then detect threats with GuardDuty and Security Hub. You leave with a defense-in-depth blueprint that scales with AI-accelerated development across your environment.

sessions.t: Security compliance and hardening with EC2 Image Builder
sessions.a: Discover how to leverage EC2 Image Builder to create secure, compliant, and hardened AMIs. Learn to automate security baseline implementation, including CIS benchmarks. We'll demonstrate building compliance checks into Image Builder pipelines, integrating vulnerability scanning, and implementing automated testing for regulatory standards.

sessions.t: Security compliance and hardening with EC2 Image Builder
sessions.a: Discover how to leverage EC2 Image Builder to create secure, compliant, and hardened AMIs. Learn to automate security baseline implementation, including CIS benchmarks. We'll demonstrate building compliance checks into Image Builder pipelines, integrating vulnerability scanning, and implementing automated testing for regulatory standards.

sessions.t: Security Jam - brought to you by Fortinet
sessions.a: Come with your team of four, or join a team and meet new friends in the session. Compete head-to-head, race to the top of the leaderboard, and win prizes based on speed and accuracy. Are you ready to defend cloud environments with agentic AI-powered security on AWS? We provide incident response scenarios where you can sharpen your skills by working through simulated breaches. Can you identify the attack vector that caused the compromise? How would you deploy AI agents to autonomously detect and contain the threat? How can you architect self-healing defenses that prevent incidents from recurring? Whether you are new to AWS, new to security, or experienced in both, this session is for you. Our guided exercises and AWS experts will support learners of all levels. All you need is a computer, a desire to learn, and a competitive spirit to take on the challenge.

Our guided exercises and AWS experts will support learners of all levels. All you need is a computer, a desire to learn, and a competitive spirit to take on the challenge.

sessions.t: Security Leverage at AI Velocity: The Operating Model Shift
sessions.a: AI investment is no longer just an engineering decision. It's a security decision. AI velocity and security velocity compound together to produce enterprise value. The same velocity AI gives your developers is now available to your adversaries. The asymmetry that protected enterprises for decades is shifting. This session covers the operating model shift that compounds enterprise value rather than erodes it. We show how engineers paired with frontier agents, carrying application context across design, code, and pen testing, produce security leverage for your organization.

sessions.t: Security → Zero-Trust Identity & Data Protection in the Agentic Era
sessions.a: Security reviews stall AI rollouts more than any capability gap, and agentic AI raises the bar. This chalk talk goes past "is it secure?" to the architecture that gets a CISO to yes. We'll whiteboard the full identity path: SSO through providers like Okta and Ping, with end-user identity propagated to the data so authorization is enforced per user, in real time, across 1P AWS and 3P sources. Then we extend that trust to agents: agent identity, deterministic policy checks on every tool call, and data protection—Purview DLP, default guardrails, deny-by-default, full SIEM auditability.

sessions.t: See the routes change: Live BGP with AWS Direct Connect
sessions.a: AWS Direct Connect can feel like a mystery beneath the surface — many customers never get hands-on access. In this show and tell, we change that. Starting from a live connection and an on-premises router, provision a virtual interface via the CLI and watch BGP establish in real time — then break things on purpose. See how route advertisements propagate, what ECMP and AS path prepending look like from both sides, and how BGP Route Visibility metrics in Amazon CloudWatch diagnose issues as they happen. Whether you run 1G or hundreds of 100G ports, walk away thinking differently about operating Direct Connect.

sessions.t: See where every AI dollar goes on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: AI spend scales fast, and you can't optimize what you can't attribute. In this code talk, build Bedrock cost visibility live: combine CloudWatch metrics and supported invocation logs for timely usage signals with Cost Explorer and CUR 2.0 for billing reporting. Add attribution by IAM principal and cost-allocation tags, then assemble a dashboard that maps spend to teams, workloads, and models while accounting for each source's freshness and granularity. Turn that visibility into action: match steady workloads to Reserved Tier, choose models for price-performance, and set budgets and alerts. Leave with working code and a repeatable, finance-ready cost view.

sessions.t: Select and launch the right EC2 instance for your workload and budget
sessions.a: With hundreds of EC2 instance types spanning compute, memory, storage, and accelerator families, choosing the right one can be overwhelming. In this session, learn a practical framework for matching your workload characteristics—CPU, memory, network, and storage requirements—to the optimal instance type and size. We cover cost-performance tradeoffs across On-Demand, Spot, and Savings Plans, share real-world selection patterns for common workloads, and demo tools that simplify decision-making. Leave with a repeatable process to right-size from day one.

sessions.t: Self-healing data pipelines with agentic AI and Apache Iceberg [REPEAT]
sessions.a: Join this session to experience the magic of agentic AI and Apache Iceberg coming together on AWS to build a self-correcting data pipeline. We will dive into an agentic architecture for an Iceberg-based data pipeline where critical telemetry signals such as data loss, schema drift, cost spikes, are not only detected and diagnosed but also remediated and verified - all in real time. Attendees will walk away with a blueprint on how to unify DataOps, MLOps, and FinOps for their data pipelines.

sessions.t: Self-Healing Enterprise-Wipro & AWS Moving from System of Record to System of Action (sponsored by Wipro)
sessions.a: For decades, enterprises have invested in technologies that digitize, automate and optimize work. Yet when disruptions occur, decisions still depend on emails, escalations, meetings and manual coordination across teams. The next phase of enterprise transformation is about creating enterprises that can sense change, assess impact, coordinate responses and drive outcomes at speed. Wipro and AWS demonstrate how intelligent agents, enterprise systems and human expertise come together to create a Self-Healing Enterprise, one that can proactively identify issues, orchestrate actions across functions and continuously adapt while keeping humans accountable for critical business decisions. Through a realistic business disruption scenario, see how organizations can evolve beyond visibility and automation towards systems of action that improve resilience, responsiveness and operational efficiency. This presentation is brought to you by Wipro, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge with AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
sessions.a: As organizations use agentic AI to automate complex infrastructure operations, many face constraints around data residency, low latency, and security that prevent reliance on cloud-hosted AI services alone. This session explores how customers deploy self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge to meet these requirements while unlocking autonomous operations. Learn how to provision, configure, and optimize AI agents across customer environments spanning AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones. Attendees learn how to architect and operate AI agents that run locally, satisfying data sovereignty, latency, and security mandates while delivering intelligent, autonomous infrastructure management across hybrid environments.

sessions.t: Self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge with AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
sessions.a: As organizations use agentic AI to automate complex infrastructure operations, many face constraints around data residency, low latency, and security that prevent reliance on cloud-hosted AI services alone. This session explores how customers deploy self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge to meet these requirements while unlocking autonomous operations. Learn how to provision, configure, and optimize AI agents across customer environments spanning AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones. Attendees learn how to architect and operate AI agents that run locally, satisfying data sovereignty, latency, and security mandates while delivering intelligent, autonomous infrastructure management across hybrid environments.

sessions.t: Self-verifiable watermarks: defending AI provenance against forgery
sessions.a: As organizations deploy generative AI at scale, watermarking has become the critical trust layer for establishing content provenance, meeting emerging regulatory requirements, and protecting brand integrity. But what if an adversary could stamp a fake watermark onto any image and frame your service? We show a diffusion-based forgery attack bypasses current defenses with just 1,000 samples. To close this gap, we introduce a self-verifiable message mechanism—SeedBind and ContentBind—that transforms verification into a structural consistency check, reducing forged bit accuracy to near-random without modifying the underlying watermarking pipeline. Discover how to harden AI provenance at scale.

sessions.t: Sell to the AI Buyer, Scale Revenue, and Build Long-Term Value
sessions.a: The buying journey is shifting to AI agents and assistants that evaluate and procure software autonomously. If your solution isn't readable and transactable by a machine, you're invisible to a growing share of the market. This session shows AWS Partners how to show up for the AI buyer, from listing optimization to working alongside other agents, and how a growth toolkit (trials, bundling, demand generation) turns visibility into compounding revenue. Walk away with an implementation path that covers day-one discoverability through long-term governance.

sessions.t: Serverless at 1M RPS: Lambda, DynamoDB & SQS Scaling Lessons
sessions.a: We push Lambda, DynamoDB, and SQS to one million requests per second and share what breaks. Learn partition-aware DynamoDB design for extreme write throughput, Lambda concurrency shaping to prevent downstream crush, SQS as a backpressure buffer with adaptive batching, and retry amplification math that turns a blip into a cascade. We present real numbers: cold start budgets at scale, the exact crossover point where serverless cost exceeds containers, and the operational trade-offs at each threshold.

sessions.t: Serverless at 1M RPS: Lambda, DynamoDB & SQS Scaling Lessons [REPEAT]

sessions.t: Serverless compute built for the web
sessions.a: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this session, see how to build full-stack web applications entirely on AWS serverless services, from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. We cover architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical blueprints for production-ready serverless web development.

sessions.t: Serverless developers in the agentic era: What changes, what doesn't
sessions.a: Serverless architectures that worked well for API backends and event processing now have a new type of consumer: AI agents that call your functions as tools, generate events, and write code that deploys alongside yours. In this session, we cover what actually changes: function design patterns for agent consumption, orchestration choices for non-deterministic workflows, cost governance when an agent loop calls 200 functions in a single reasoning chain, and observability that tracks token spend alongside invocation metrics. We also cover what doesn't change, and where existing Serverless patterns hold up without modification.

sessions.t: Serverless Java in 2026
sessions.a: Java on Lambda used to mean cold start anxiety and compromised JIT performance. Not anymore. SnapStart and GraalVM native AOT deliver sub-second startup, and Lambda Managed Instances give steady-state JVM workloads full JIT optimization at EC2 economics. In this chalk talk, we go beyond cold starts: discuss refactoring patterns for moving Java monoliths to serverless, framework choices that work well on Lambda (and ones that don't), and how AI-assisted tools identify decomposition boundaries and generate Lambda handlers from existing service classes. Bring your Java architecture.

sessions.t: Serverless observability: OpenTelemetry and vended logs
sessions.a: Debugging distributed serverless applications used to mean stitching together X-Ray traces, CloudWatch logs, and custom metrics from multiple extensions. In this chalk talk, we cover setup and configuration, end-to-end tracing with API Gateway vended logs, and distributed tracing across Step Functions, EventBridge, and SQS. We also discuss observability for agentic workloads: tracking token consumption, tool call success rates, and workflow checkpoint state. Bring your observability questions, especially around cost at scale: sampling, filtering, and cardinality management.

sessions.t: Serverlesspresso: Build an event-driven app from the ground up
sessions.a: Build a fully event-driven, serverless coffee-ordering web application using AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, and Lambda durable functions. Design scalable, fault-tolerant architectures as you simulate customers placing orders and baristas managing them in real time. Discover how durable functions simplify complex workflow orchestration by checkpointing progress, automatically recovering from failures, and pausing execution while waiting on long-running tasks—all without managing additional infrastructure or writing custom state management code. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Serverless streaming data processing with AWS Lambda and Apache Kafka
sessions.a: Build a serverless streaming data pipeline in 60 minutes. In this builders' session, you design and deploy a real-time location tracking app that ingests events from Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK), processes them with AWS Lambda, and pushes live updates to a dashboard through AWS AppSync—no consumer fleet to manage, no scaling logic to write. Experiment with Lambda event source mapping for Kafka, applying recent improvements in filtering, batching, and error handling. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: ServiceNow: The AI Control Tower for Business Reinvention (sponsored by ServiceNow)
sessions.a: AI without workflows is just expensive advice. The next generation of AI leaders are moving beyond disconnected copilots and isolated use cases to reinvent how work gets done. Join ServiceNow to learn how the AI Control Tower for Business Reinvention helps organizations govern AI, connect enterprise data, and orchestrate work across every agent, model, and workflow. Discover how AI that thinks and workflows that act enable enterprises to deploy AI quickly while maintaining trust, security, and control. This presentation is brought to you by ServiceNow, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Serving World Model at scale with AWS Trainium and Native PyTorch
sessions.a: The next major leap in AI is predicting and interacting with the physical world. World models bridge digital reasoning with real-world execution, introducing new infrastructure demands for video generation, robotics, and gaming workloads at scale. We'll explore the emerging architecture of world models and why AWS Trainium, purpose-built for better price-performance, is well suited to serve them. Learn how native PyTorch support with torch.compile fuses operations into optimized device graphs, and how NKI custom kernels accelerate critical operators like attention. You'll leave equipped to take world model inference from eager prototyping to compiled deployment using familiar PyTorch workflows.

sessions.t: Setting up the Right AI Architecture: Bringing Together Agents, Teams, and Context (sponsored by Notion)
sessions.a: Every organization is building their AI architecture in real-time: deciding which agents to use, which data sources to connect them to, and figuring how to get teams to collaborate across it all. These different layers have been arranged over many years of procuring tools, but can sometimes feel like a jumbled mess in the AI era. This session offers a practical way to reexamine your tech architecture. We'll cover four patterns that recur across organizations as they try to structure their business for the AI era, plus pitfalls to avoid to ensure your tech stack is optimized for AI. This presentation is brought to you by Notion, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Shared file storage for containers, serverless, and Lambda
sessions.a: Containers spin up and disappear. Your application state needs to outlive them. Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx, and Amazon S3 Files give your containerized and serverless workloads durable, shared file storage. We'll break down when to choose each service based on access patterns, performance, and cost. You'll see how real teams run stateful microservices using EFS on ECS/EKS, leverage FSx for high-performance file system workloads on Fargate, and unlock POSIX capabilities to S3 object data for analytics and AI workloads with S3 Files.

sessions.t: Shared Judgment: Security Culture for the Agentic Era
sessions.a: Your agents are reviewing PRs, shipping code, and answering messages. They communicate on your behalf, surfacing every weak relationship in your org. Soft skills have never mattered more. Shift Left and Shift Down brought security in as automation to build trust in systems. Agents have moved the question to trust between humans. Security teams have historically operated at a remove: by org chart, tooling, and reputation. That distance becomes a liability when agents reduce the time between decision and consequence. This session is about building a security function whose core output is shared judgment with the engineers it serves.

sessions.t: Ship agents, not chaos: a 90-day pattern for production on AWS. (sponsored by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
sessions.a: AI agents are moving from pilots into production faster than most organizations can govern them, and independent teams building in parallel are creating what practitioners now call agent sprawl. This session presents a repeatable 90-day pattern that converts sprawl into governed agents ready for production, using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Guardrails, and Kiro alongside NIST AI RMF and the Well-Architected Generative AI Lens. Architects, platform owners, and public-sector leaders see how a governed runtime, evidence-based mission KPIs, and cost discipline turn compliance into an accelerator. Audit-ready patterns from CDW customer engagements across regulated commercial and public-sector missions are included This presentation is brought to you by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Ship Agents You Can Trust: An Agent Evaluation Framework for Partners
sessions.a: Partners shipping production agents at scale need to answer: is this good enough for customers? Agentic transformation doesn't end at build; quality evaluation is the missing layer. In this chalk talk, we walk through an open-source evaluation framework: define test criteria for your agent, run it in a sandbox on Bedrock, calibrate an automated judge against human labels, and track failure rates in CI. For multi-agent systems, attribute failures to the agent that caused them, not where the harm showed up.

sessions.t: Ship AI Agents Faster with AgentCore Harness
sessions.a: Building a production-ready AI agent meant writing orchestration code, packaging containers, and managing deployment pipelines. AgentCore Harness eliminates all of that. In this hands-on lab, you declare what your agent does through configuration and let AgentCore handle the execution loop. You create a harness agent, iteratively add tools, attach AWS Skills, swap models mid-session to suit your output requirements, and publish versioned endpoints for safe rollout to your customers.

sessions.t: Ship faster with AWS CloudFormation
sessions.a: AWS CloudFormation lets you manage infrastructure as code with increasing confidence and speed, whether you're deploying directly or through AI agents. In this chalk talk, we dive into the capabilities that shorten your dev-test cycle and keep deployments safe: deploy in seconds with Express mode, catch errors before deployment with pre-deployment validation, author templates faster using the CloudFormation Language Server in your IDE, connect AI agents to CloudFormation with the Agent Skill and MCP Server, reorganize stacks without disruption using Stack Refactoring, and prevent accidental overwrites with drift-aware change sets. Bring your templates and your toughest questions, we'll workshop solutions live.

In this session, we build the pipeline stages: validate policies at pull request time with Access Analyzer, simulate critical access paths before deployment, preview Service Control Policies (SCP) impact against real CloudTrail data, and automatically triage Access Denied errors in production using IAM's new debugging API and autofix recommendations. We'll write commit gates that block overly permissive policies, integration tests that ensure operational permissions, and auto-triage that turns production denials into automated remediation commits.

sessions.t: Shipping AI Code with Confidence Using Bluebox by Dynatrace and AWS Kiro (sponsored by Dynatrace)
sessions.a: See how Western Governors University uses Bluebox by Dynatrace and AWS Kiro to deliver AI-generated code with greater confidence. By combining live production intelligence with AI-assisted development, teams can provide agents with real runtime context, detect issues quickly, and create evidence-backed GitHub Issues for rapid remediation. Learn how Bluebox supports the software lifecycle before, during, and after deployment, helping teams validate fixes, reduce risk, and accelerate software delivery. This presentation is brought to you by Dynatrace, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Ship Reliable AI Agents with Strands Evaluation and AgentCore Evaluations
sessions.a: Your AI agent works in demos, but can you trust it enough for production? How do you test behavior that can vary on every run, and catch regressions when prompts, models, tools, or workflows change? In this 300-level Code Talk, we'll turn real-world agent failure modes into representative test cases, evaluate both answers and actions, and add risk-based quality gates into CI/CD. Using Strands Evaluation and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, you'll leave this session able to design and implement an evaluation pipeline tailored to your own agents, backed by a public reference implementation you can adapt.

sessions.a: Rolling update, blue/green, canary, or linear? Amazon ECS gives you deployment strategies with built-in safety controls, no extra tooling required. This chalk talk explores how native Amazon ECS deployment options work and when to use each one. Discuss traffic shifting percentages, validation hooks for pre-traffic testing, and alarm integration for automated rollbacks. Learn how to tune bake time and coordinate multi-service deployments so you can ship changes confidently at any scale. Bring your release pipeline challenges for an open discussion.

sessions.a: Staying ahead of threats in the cloud means seeing them before they spread. In this session, we'll demonstrate how Illumio brings together AWS firewall data and live traffic flows to surface risk in real time, how segmentation shuts down exposure across your environment, and how quarantine actions stop compromised workloads in their tracks. See the full journey live, from blind spots to contained blast radius. This presentation is brought to you by Illumio, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Simple Governance: How Kiro Makes Enterprise Policies Human-Friendly
sessions.a: Kiro agents execute code, invoke models, and interact with external services on behalf of developers. Enterprise administrators desire to constrain what agents can do without slowing developers down. We built a centralized governance system backed by Dogwood/Cedar that compiles admin-authored policies into governance documents enforced across every client (IDE, CLI, Web,Mobile) and server-side services. The system separates governance from configuration, uses deny-wins semantics with fail-closed enforcement, and scopes rules by hierarchies. Learn how we use Kiro itself to author and analyze governance policies to make enterprise controls human-friendly and manageable.

sessions.t: Simplify Data Analytics operations with AI-powered Apache Spark agents on AWS
sessions.a: Running analytics workloads at scale carries a hidden operational tax: teams commonly lose significant engineering time to debugging failures, leave performance and cost improvements on the table, and spend months on each version upgrade. In this talk, we walk through a family of AI-powered agents for AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, and Amazon Athena. The Spark Troubleshooting Agent finds the root cause of a failure and recommends the code or config fix - cutting debugging time from hours to minutes. The Spark Upgrade Agent plans an upgrade, transforms the code, and validates both runtime and data quality - turning months into hours. We share what worked in production for both agents - the design choices, failure modes, and validation strategies that made them reliable - and distill lessons that generalize to any team applying LLMs to complex infrastructure.

sessions.t: Simplify identity and security management in an open data architecture on AWS
sessions.a: As organizations unify data across Amazon S3 data lakes, S3 Tables, and Amazon Redshift using the open data lakehouse architecture, securing access at scale becomes critical. In this chalk talk, we dive deep into simplifying trusted identity propagation so end-user identities — not shared service roles — reach the data plane, designing multi-dimensional tag-based access control taxonomies that scale automatically through inheritance, enforcing column-level and cell-level security across federated catalogs, and auditing every access event to individual users.

sessions.t: Simplify multicloud: manage and monitor VMs in one place
sessions.a: As your compute spreads across multiple clouds and on-premises, every environment ends up with its own agents, tooling, and consoles. Patching, access, and monitoring happen a different way in each one, and no single view shows what is running or how it behaves. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to bring every instance under one operational model with AWS Systems Manager, no matter where it runs, and then get metrics and logs from all of them into Amazon CloudWatch. We work through the tradeoffs and patterns that hold at scale. Leave able to run and observe your whole fleet as one.

sessions.t: Simplify secure file sharing with Transfer Family no-code web apps
sessions.a: Traditional file transfer solutions often require complex client software, custom scripts, or technical expertise, creating barriers for business users who need to share data. Learn how AWS Transfer Family web apps enable secure, browser-based file transfers that automatically trigger data processing workflows. We'll show you how to build automated pipelines that process files upon upload while maintaining enterprise-grade security through AWS IAM Identity Center for your workforce or Amazon Cognito for external users. Discover how to streamline file ingestion, kick off validations, and orchestrate downstream processing, starting with a simple drag-and-drop interface for your end users.

sessions.a: You're running AWS CloudHSM, but do you still need to? AWS Key Management Service (KMS) capabilities now cover many workloads that once required dedicated HSMs, at lower cost and operational overhead. In this chalk talk, bring your architecture and we'll work through the decision together. Using a framework from real customer migrations, we'll whiteboard your use case, identify what's keeping you on CloudHSM, and map a migration path to KMS where it fits. Leave with concrete next steps to simplify your cryptographic infrastructure.

sessions.t: Single Agent to Global Scale: One Postgres, Any Workload, Run by Agents (sponsored by YugabyteDB)
sessions.a: An agent needs a Postgres database for perhaps twenty minutes. A payments platform needs one that never goes down across three regions. Most teams cover that range with different products, several vendors, and scores of on-call operators. Yugabyte delivers it as a single stack on AWS. YugabyteDB is distributed PostgreSQL built for global scale and resilience that also scales down to fractional instances. YugabyteDB AMP puts agents in charge of the fleet, handling provisioning, migration, and on-demand tuning. Meko gives agent teams the shared context they run on. See what it takes to run every Postgres workload on one foundation. This presentation is brought to you by YugabyteDB, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Six Ways AI Fails Who Your Nonprofit Serves — And How to Stop Each One
sessions.a: Every AI application touching real people can fail in ways that cause harm. In this chalk talk, we walk one application through six failure modes — PII exposure, phantom citations, out-of-scope advice, unreviewed judgments, hidden bias, and unaccountable decisions — and whiteboard a defense-in-depth architecture using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, AgentCore, Automated Reasoning, and human-in-the-loop patterns. Leave with a responsible AI stack applicable to any form factor — chatbot, agent, RAG pipeline, or model call — whether you serve donors, patients, customers, or citizens.

sessions.t: Skip Refactoring and Simplify Operations with Nutanix on AWS (sponsored by Nutanix)
sessions.a: Cloud migrations often stall when rewriting applications takes too long. As projects drag on, organizations are left managing a fragmented, expensive mix of on-premises and cloud silos. Nutanix Cloud Clusters on AWS addresses this friction by establishing a single control plane and a consistent operating model across environments. In this session, learn how to move workloads to AWS bare metal quickly without refactoring. Discover how to eliminate management silos, accelerate migration timelines, and simplify hybrid cloud operations. This presentation is brought to you by Nutanix, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Small Language Models, Total Control: Sovereign AI Agents, Lower Cost (sponsored by Boomi)
sessions.a: Enterprises are waking up to a hard truth: the AI their business now depends on runs on infrastructure, models, and pricing they don't control. In this session, Boomi's engineering and AI leadership show a different path — AI agents that run anywhere you choose (your Amazon VPC, your data center, behind your firewall) powered by small language models fine-tuned to each agent's job and served entirely on infrastructure you govern. You'll see the full architecture on AWS — Amazon EKS, EC2 GPU instances, Amazon S3, Aurora, MSK, and Amazon Bedrock as a governed escalation path — plus the fine-tuning pipeline (LoRA SFT + DPO), the evaluation gate that decides when a small model is ready, and a live demo of an agent reasoning locally at a fraction of the latency and cost of a frontier LLM. This presentation is brought to you by Boomi, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Smoking on Airplanes: Rethinking How Enterprises Trust Software (sponsored by Glow)
sessions.a: Every day, employees install browser extensions, IDE plugins, and open-source packages with powerful access to corporate devices, code, credentials, and data. AI coding agents are accelerating this practice by recommending and installing software to complete tasks. Yet much of it enters the enterprise without comprehensive security review. We've normalized a practice that may someday seem as unthinkable as smoking on airplanes. In this session, we'll expose hidden risks in plugin and package ecosystems, show why traditional application controls miss this rapidly changing software layer, and explore what security teams must rethink as AI makes software adoption faster and increasingly autonomous. This presentation is brought to you by Glow, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Snowflake: Build a Multi-Engine Architecture on A single AI Ready Governed Data Copy (sponsored by Snowflake)
sessions.a: Delivering enterprise analytics and AI requires an architecture designed for operational flexibility not forcing complex data movement. Snowflake's interoperable lakehouse gives teams total agency to query and write to data where it lives using the right engine for every job. This session explores how organizations establish universal open metadata governance powered by Apache Polaris while preserving rich semantic business context across tools. Learn how the Snowflake AI Data Cloud simplifies data management, lowers total cost of ownership, and accelerates time to insight for every team, and agent, across your AWS cloud environment. This presentation is brought to you by Snowflake, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Solving Problems Faster with AI SRE​ (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
sessions.a: The complexity of problems continues to grow, and smart organizations know that leveraging AI is the quickest way to get this complexity under control and keep customers happy.​ In this session, you’ll see a demo of and learn how to use AI SRE in Splunk Observability Cloud to troubleshoot and remediate problems faster no matter how complex or distributed your operating environment is, all powered by OpenTelemetry. ​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Spec-Driven AI Development with Kiro
sessions.a: The AI Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) brings structure, traceability, and human oversight to every phase of high-velocity, Agentic-AI powered software delivery. In this bootcamp, apply AI-DLC in Kiro to build a production application through Feature Specs, control agent behavior with steering files and execution modes, extend capabilities with MCP servers and Kiro Powers, and automate workflows with hooks. Leave with a governed, repeatable process for shipping quality software with AI assistance.

sessions.t: Specs, not vibes: Strangling the monolith in the IDE
sessions.a: Your architecture is full of pets: brittle EC2 instances run by manual runbooks, with no contract between decisions and infrastructure. In this code talk, we abandon slides and prove the Strangler pattern live in the IDE with Kiro and spec-driven development. We decompose a monolith into bounded contexts, generate CDK from the spec, and shift traffic from pets to serverless cattle, confronting the hard parts: where to cut the seam, running old and new together, keeping data consistent. Every architectural decision becomes a machine-verifiable contract you can apply to your own monolith.
