You design flexible schemas, create agent tools for client management and natural language analytics, deploy the agent on ECS Fargate, configure Bedrock Guardrails for health safety, and implement anomaly detection using database change streams.

sessions.t: Spec-to-App Development with Kiro
sessions.a: Kiro, the Agentic IDE, transforms a single natural language prompt into structured requirements, a technical design, and an executable implementation plan. In this SimuLearn session, you build a city event management application by guiding Kiro through its spec-driven workflow: generating EARS-format user stories, reviewing architecture decisions, and executing a sequenced task list that produces a working MVP. You also configure a Kiro Hook that automatically validates data files on save.

sessions.t: Speed Wins: Compress Migration Timelines from Pipeline to Production
sessions.a: Enterprises face a wall of technical debt standing between them and the AI opportunity. In this session, learn how AWS Transform helps compressing the entire partner lifecycle — from intelligent prospecting and AI-powered co-sell through to automated delivery and simplified funding — and why first-movers will own disproportionate share of the opportunity.

sessions.t: SQL Server to Amazon RDS: lessons from Xero's 900 database migration
sessions.a: What does it take to migrate the databases behind 5 million small businesses without anyone noticing? Xero, the global cloud accounting platform, moved 900 SQL Server databases to Amazon RDS for SQL Server with near-zero downtime. In this session, Xero shares how the team orchestrated cutovers, approached schema migration, and used managed patching, automated backups, and capacity planning in Amazon RDS to return engineering time to product development. The session covers the migration planning and decision points most relevant to engineering teams running large SQL Server fleets on aging self-managed infrastructure.

sessions.t: State of the art Fairness and Admission Control
sessions.a: Preventing long outages, meta-stable events, thundering herds, Denial of Service Attacks, resource or concurrency starvation, or noisy neighbor issues all depend on fairness and admission control. We’ll do a deep, interactive dive into practical techniques that prevent or mitigate real-world issues. We’ll get into details of back-pressure, PID control loops, shuffle sharding, floodgates, and other novel techniques that we’ve developed at AWS, and we’ll cover common mistakes that we see in the industry.

sessions.t: State Street: AI agents that write, deploy, and govern at scale
sessions.a: Landing zones, drift detection, and migration backlogs pile up faster than platform teams can manage. In this lightning talk, State Street will share how they built AI agents that embed directly in application teams, taking infrastructure requirements as input, generating compliant Terraform, and handling provisioning without a ticket queue. Every resource stays within policy guardrails before it reaches production. Learn how integrating AI agents into the DevOps lifecycle accelerates delivery while maintaining governance and security across the enterprise.

sessions.t: Stop building agents that stop short of action (sponsored by IBM)
sessions.a: AI value does not come from more agents—it comes from agents that can complete real work across enterprise systems without creating new risk. In this session, learn how IBM is helping teams build agentic workflows that connect software delivery, automation and governance across AWS environments. Learn how a connected approach to software development, orchestration and governance helps agents modernize applications, coordinate work and act across the enterprise with the visibility and control needed to scale. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Stop Building Agents Without Unified Enterprise Context (sponsored by Glean)
sessions.a: Many AI programs start with a model, a prompt, and a narrow workflow. They stall when agents need to understand permissions, people, policies, past decisions, and data spread across AWS and SaaS systems. This session shows a different path: establish a governed enterprise context layer and scale the enterprise workflows that prove value. Attendees will learn the elements that make up a robust context platform, what to keep open and flexible, and how to measure whether agents improve real work. This presentation is brought to you by Glean, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Stop fighting fires: operations that prevent incidents
sessions.a: The best incident is the one that never happens, yet most teams stay stuck firefighting. Learn to collect the right operational signals beyond just observability and use AI to spot problems before they page anyone. We'll cover auto-healing and remediation with traditional techniques and AI agents that catch misconfiguration before production. You'll discover how early-warning systems spot issues before customers do, and how agentic investigation turns past incidents into ranked recommendations that prevent future ones. Walk away with actionable steps to start building proactive operations.

sessions.t: Stop fixing, start preventing with Well-Architected Agent
sessions.a: Reactive incident response grows more expensive as environments scale. AWS Well-Architected Agent shifts resilience and security from periodic review to continuous, automated assessment. Its agentic reasoning identifies single points of failure, recovery gaps, and vulnerabilities across 100+ services, ranking findings by workload criticality and business goals. Crucially, each recommendation includes cross-pillar trade-off analysis - showing cost and performance implications — so you improve resilience and security without unintended consequences elsewhere. Walk away able to catch risks before they become incidents.

sessions.t: Stop Moving AWS Data. Turn It into Action with Splunk​ (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
sessions.a: Machine data across AWS environments is growing faster than teams can move, normalize, and analyze it. What if you could stop moving all that data and start putting it to work? In this session, learn how Cisco Data Fabric, powered by Splunk, federates data across AWS and enterprise sources, correlates it at scale, and prepares it for AI and agentic workflows. Through practical architecture patterns and a live demonstration, you’ll see how to reduce data movement and operational cost while turning distributed telemetry into trusted context, faster decisions, and action.​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Stop paying for idle GPUs on Amazon EKS (sponsored by Apptio)
sessions.a: AI workloads can consume millions of dollars in infrastructure before anyone notices whether they're being used efficiently. GPUs sit idle, clusters become overprovisioned, and engineering teams struggle to balance performance with rapidly growing costs. In this session, learn how engineering teams running Amazon EKS can identify wasted GPU capacity, understand the true cost of AI workloads, and automate optimization without sacrificing application performance. We'll share practical techniques to improve utilization, reduce waste, and optimize AI infrastructure at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Apptio, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Stop Rolling Back AI Agents: Production Patterns That Work
sessions.a: The demo shipped. The agent went live. Then someone pulled it back. 74% of enterprises have rolled back a deployed AI agent, and the organizations that invested in governance roll back more often, not less. 88% of pilots never reach production. The infrastructure that gets an agent from demo to production is where the gap lives. We'll walk through the failure patterns that cause rollbacks: agents that fail silently, prompts treated as safety boundaries, and monitoring blind to non-deterministic failures. You'll leave with the patterns that prevent them: infrastructure-level guardrails, blast radius containment, and observability built for probabilistic systems.

sessions.t: Stop the bleed: control and optimize agent costs on AgentCore
sessions.a: Your agent cost $0.02 per session in testing. In production it's $0.14 and climbing. Token consumption grows unpredictably as agents retry, loop, and fan out across tools, and most teams have no visibility into where the money goes. This chalk talk breaks down where agent costs actually hide and how to control them on AgentCore: per-session budgets that kill runaway loops, model routing that drops to cheaper models for simple subtasks, cost attribution at the team and workload level, prompt caching strategies, and how to measure the tradeoff between cost and quality with evaluations.

sessions.t: Stop threats at DNS: what's new in Route 53 DNS Firewall
sessions.a: DNS is where threats are first visible and Amazon Route 53 DNS Firewall is turning that visibility into defense. This session explores how Route 53 DNS Firewall's evolving security capabilities help you resolve, inspect, and protect egress DNS query traffic to the internet across global, multi-account environments. See how deeper integration with other AWS security services, expanded DNS threat detection, wider visibility, and a growing partner ecosystem come together to strengthen your first line of defense. Whether you run a single VPC or a global network across AWS and hybrid networks, you'll leave with a clear picture of how DNS security for egress traffic is advancing and how to put it to work.

sessions.t: Stop troubleshooting your AWS network from memory and stale diagrams
sessions.a: Your network grew faster than your documentation. Routes were added in a sprint, VPC attachments stacked during migrations, and somewhere along the way, your team lost the full picture. When something breaks, you're troubleshooting from memory and stale diagrams. In this session, learn how to turn that around in hours instead of months. See how to point AI-assisted tooling at your live environment to map every resource, trace every traffic path, and surface misconfigurations before they become incidents. Then take it further: modernize what you find with current AWS network security capabilities. Walk out with a repeatable workflow you can run against your own network this week.

sessions.t: Storage decisions when you're building a multi-tenant business
sessions.a: When your business delivers cloud services to your customers, how you map tenants to storage is one of the earliest architectural choices, and it shapes everything that follows: onboarding automation, billing boundaries, isolation guarantees, and how accounts, users, and data relate to each tenant. Your workload mix adds another dimension, because data types using object, file, or block storage drive the handling of tenancy differently. In this chalk talk, we walk through silo, bridge, and pool deployment models, examining how workload profile, tenant count, and business requirements drive the choice. Bring your architecture and we'll work through it.

sessions.t: Storage performance in EC2 instances: What matters to your workload
sessions.a: Peak SSD IOPS and throughput dominate benchmarks, but production workloads tell a different story. In this chalk talk, we explore why latency-consistent mixed read/write performance drives real application outcomes across database, analytics, and distributed file system workloads. We'll walk through how workload profiles map to different performance dimensions (throughput vs. IOPS vs. latency consistency), how real-world write mixes reveal true storage performance, and how emerging AI workloads are creating demand for an entirely new storage performance profile.

sessions.t: Storage performance in EC2 instances: What matters to your workload
sessions.a: Peak SSD IOPS and throughput dominate benchmarks, but production workloads tell a different story. sessions.t: Strategies for agentic-ready architectures on Amazon EKS
sessions.a: As AI agents become first-class workloads, the platforms that host them must evolve. This session explores how Amazon EKS enables agentic-ready architectures — combining multi-tenancy isolation, dynamic scaling, and fine-grained security boundaries to safely run autonomous agent workflows at scale. We'll examine how platform engineering patterns born from SaaS modernization (control plane/application plane separation, tenant-aware networking, and cost allocation) translate directly to orchestrating multi-agent systems. Attendees will learn practical patterns to provision, isolate, and observe agentic workloads on Kubernetes while maintaining operational control and cost efficiency.

sessions.t: Strategies for optimizing enterprise licenses on AWS
sessions.a: Enterprise organizations running commercial software on AWS face licensing decisions that directly impact cost and compliance. This session explores strategies for optimizing Microsoft and other enterprise software licenses across AWS services including Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS. An AWS licensing expert walks through assessment approaches and optimization levers. Then hear from a customer who ran an AWS Optimization and Licensing Assessment across three workstreams: rightsizing, Availability Zone consolidation, and database modernization, and turned a one-time assessment into an ongoing optimization practice. You'll leave with strategies you can apply to your own licensing environment.

sessions.t: Streamline Claims Processing with Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Claims adjusters spend hours retrieving policy data, applying business rules, and drafting decision letters manually. In this SimuLearn session, you use Amazon Quick Automate to orchestrate the entire claims process. You configure REST API and MCP connectors, build a multi-step workflow with Custom Agent steps, and chain together policy retrieval, rules validation, and AI-powered letter generation. The workflow handles missing data gracefully and stores audit-ready decision letters in S3.

sessions.t: Surviving the drop: Build a flash-sale control plane with CloudFront
sessions.a: Product drops, ticket on-sales, and viral promotions can spike traffic 50x in seconds - and origin infrastructure is the wrong place to absorb it. In this workshop, build a complete launch-day control plane using Amazon CloudFront Functions and CloudFront KeyValueStore. Implement a launch gate with VIP early access, a percentage-based throttle that dials traffic to your purchase origin in real time, sticky A/B testing for product pages, and a global kill switch - all controlled by KeyValueStore updates that propagate worldwide in seconds, with zero deployments and zero origin changes. Along the way, use edge location metadata for geo-staggered launches and trace every gate decision with CloudFront Functions access logging. Leave with patterns you can apply to any high-demand launch event. Attendees must bring a laptop.

sessions.t: Switch models without disrupting customers on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Your application is working in production, and then a newer model arrives with better benchmarks or lower cost. You need to decide whether moving is worth the risk. A switch can change outputs, break prompts, raise costs, and create weeks of retesting. This session shows how to reduce that disruption on Amazon Bedrock. Test candidate models against your own use cases, compare quality, latency, and cost, and update prompts without rewriting them by hand. See how Bedrock Evaluations and Advanced Prompt Optimization help you measure the impact before rollout. Leave with a practical plan for switching models without disrupting customers.

sessions.t: Tag once, find anything: scale resource tracking across accounts
sessions.a: Inconsistent tags make it hard to see what runs where. In this code talk, we build automation that keeps tagging clean at scale: a tagging schema that defines the keys and values that matter, an AWS Config rule that flags non-compliant resources, and an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that remediates them automatically or with approval. We also query untagged resources across thousands of resources and multi accounts. Leave with working code you can adapt for cost allocation, access scoping, and AI-assisted root-cause analysis.

sessions.t: Take Voice and Image AI into Production with OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by OpenAI)
sessions.a: Build production AI workflows that turn language, vision, voice, and structured data into useful action. This session explores how developers can combine varied enterprise inputs with tool use on Amazon Bedrock. Learn approaches for model routing and evaluation, and explore the security and governance considerations involved in making voice and image workflows dependable in production.

sessions.t: Talk to your market data: Agentic AI meets exchange feeds
sessions.a: In this builders’ session, connect an Amazon Bedrock agent layer to a high-performance data pipeline that turns 560M IEX exchange messages into an interactive playground. Analysts describe trading ideas in natural language (no SQL or Python required) while the agent queries Parquet data, generates strategy logic, runs backtests, and returns results. Dig into the C++ parsing, serverless orchestration with AWS Batch and AWS Fargate, Amazon S3, and guardrail patterns that make it production ready. Leave with architecture patterns, a cost model, and a blueprint for adding an agentic layer that takes anyone from market intuition to tested strategy in minutes.

sessions.t: Taming AI Token Costs and Security Risks with Cribl and AWS (sponsored by Cribl)
sessions.a: Govern enterprise AI: Optimize costs, control prompt risks, and gain visibility with Cribl and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cribl, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Tapestry, Grupo Boticario & Nestle Purina on agentic commerce
sessions.a: AI agents are changing how consumers discover and buy, splitting into two investments: retailers building conversational shopping on their own properties, and consumer goods companies optimizing how their products surface when agents shop on a consumer's behalf. In this session, hear how Tapestry built the Kate Spade AI Gift Concierge that turns luxury gifting into a guided conversation; Grupo Boticario launched an agentic Virtual Assistant orchestrating product discovery and checkout for millions of users; and Nestle Purina implemented an Answer Engine Optimization strategy, using their native chatbot Allie to pressure-test how external AI engines surface proprietary brand data before releasing it into circulation.

sessions.t: Teaching agents to pay with Stripe (sponsored by Stripe)
sessions.a: AI agents can already search, reason, and call tools. What changes when they can spend money, too? This talk explores the shift from human checkout to machine-native commerce, where payments become part of an agent's reasoning loop. We will look at how agents can discover and purchase products today, then explore Stripe’s Machine Payments Protocol and a future where agents autonomously pay for APIs, compute, data, and other capabilities needed to complete a task. When software becomes the buyer, developers may need to rethink not only checkout, but also how software itself is discovered, priced, and consumed. This presentation is brought to you by Stripe, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Teaching Quick to Remember and Connect with Memory and Knowledge Graphs
sessions.a: Every conversation with an AI assistant starts from scratch. Your agent doesn't remember what worked yesterday, can't tell you who owns a project without searching again, and repeats the same mistakes because failures are never captured. In this chalk talk, we show how Amazon Quick breaks out of statelessness with two primitives: a continuous-learning memory layer where a background agent extracts reusable knowledge after each session and scores it with a probabilistic confidence model, and a personal knowledge graph that connects people, projects, decisions, and evidence across your tools so the agent has a map of your world before it reads a single document. We'll whiteboard the architecture and the tradeoffs that shaped it, then open it up — bring your hardest questions about memory staleness, confidence calibration, graph noise, or making agents that actually get better over time.

sessions.t: Teaching Telemetry to Think: From Raw Signals to Root Cause
sessions.a: An AI agent investigating an incident starts cold: no sense of normal, no topology, no causal history. It rebuilds context from raw documents every time. What if the telemetry understood itself first? We'll examine an intelligence layer for agentic observability, where streaming detectors and a live service graph distill billions of signals into incident observations, then fine-tuned reasoning models, built on open-weight LLMs, correlate them into ranked root causes. Whiteboard with us on the hard parts: what to teach a model versus retrieve at inference, how domain fine-tuning beats frontier scale, and where reasoning models still fail.

sessions.t: Tech debt anonymous: bring your worst code to this chalk talk
sessions.a: We all have it: the monolith nobody wants to touch, and the pile of small apps and Lambda functions racking up end-of-life notices. This chalk talk is your support group. Bring your real modernization headaches and we'll discuss how AWS Transform tackles the whole spectrum. On one side, Transform custom handles the big, complex jobs: decomposing Java and .NET monoliths, translating languages, upgrading frameworks at scale. On the other, continuous modernization autonomously scans thousands of repositories, prioritizes what's drifting, and opens remediation pull requests on a schedule. Bring questions about your own portfolio and leave with a plan of attack.

sessions.t: Techniques for Cost-Optimized Video Understanding on AWS
sessions.a: Video understanding unlocks powerful insights from media assets, but cost concerns often slow adoption. In this hands-on session, we walk through practical techniques for building cost-optimized video understanding pipelines on AWS. You'll learn how to reduce inference costs, right-size your architecture, and accelerate time to value without sacrificing accuracy. Whether you're processing thousands of hours of content for metadata enrichment, content moderation, or search, these patterns help you scale AI-driven video analysis while keeping your bill predictable. Leave with actionable blueprints you can implement immediately.

sessions.t: Tekion: Reinventing automotive retail with agentic AI on AWS
sessions.a: Automotive retail runs on complex, menu-driven workflows — scheduling service, ordering parts, structuring deals, closing books. Tekion, whose cloud-native platform powers thousands of dealerships, reimagined it as conversational AI, the industry's first AI-native automotive DMS. Built on Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, Tekion's production agents — spanning sales, service, parts, F&I, and accounting — execute actions rather than suggesting them, serving every role from service advisor to dealer principal. Learn how Tekion architected a reusable agent platform, applied guardrails for safe autonomy, and turned industry operations AI-native.

sessions.t: Telecom Contact Centers: Design Patterns for integrated AI Agents
sessions.a: Telecom customers demand fast, accurate service, yet IVR systems frustrate them, and when calls reach a human agent, context from the automated interaction is lost. Based on real-world implementations, this chalk talk explores alternatives to IVR using AI powered agents. We will walk through architectural options for customer facing agents built on Amazon Connect, how to pass conversation context to human agents when they step in, and options for integrating with OSS/BSS services using MCP and prebuilt integrations in Amazon Connect. We will examine the trade-offs that come with each design choice, so bring your questions!

sessions.t: Telecom NOC operations: Automating incident response with AI agents
sessions.a: Modern telecom networks span thousands of distributed components, forcing network operations teams to interpret high volumes of alarms, separate root causes from downstream symptoms, and coordinate remediation across systems under time pressure. In this workshop, you will build AI agents that read, reason about, and execute Standard Operating Procedures for network deployment and remediation. First, deploy a 5G standalone core on Amazon EKS using an agent built with the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock. Next, operate a closed-loop remediation agent, inject real failures, and observe how it detects, correlates, and resolves problems.

sessions.t: Tenant-isolated agent memory: one IAM policy for AgentCore Memory
sessions.a: Managing memory for hundreds of tenants in SaaS shouldn't require hundreds of IAM policies — yet most products scaling multi-tenant agents on AWS end up there: a namespace per tenant-agent pair, a policy per tenant, deployment times that climb with every customer. In this chalk talk, learn how to isolate both layers of agent memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — short-term session events and long-term extracted records — with one Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policy backed by AWS Security Token Service (STS) session tags. We cover the actorId and namespace conventions, the Token Vending Machine that mints per-tenant credentials, and the anti-patterns that break isolation as you scale. Leave with the reference architecture and the IAM policy template you can use on Monday.

sessions.t: Tenant isolation at scale: Network patterns for ISVs on AWS
sessions.a: As ISVs scale their SaaS platforms, network architecture becomes a critical decision: balancing tenant isolation, compliance, and operational efficiency. In this chalk talk, examine proven connectivity patterns using AWS PrivateLink, AWS Transit Gateway, and Amazon VPC Lattice for multi-tenant environments. Explore how to enforce strong tenant boundaries at the network layer, handle cross-account connectivity at scale, and reduce operational complexity as your business grows. Whether building a new multi-tenant platform or evolving an existing one, leave with actionable architecture blueprints ready for production.

sessions.t: Testing serverless and event-driven applications
sessions.a: You're shipping faster with serverless, but your testing strategy hasn't kept up. Local mocks drift from cloud behavior. Integration tests require full deployments. Contract changes between services break downstream consumers silently. In this chalk talk, whiteboard testing approaches that match how serverless developers actually work: unit testing business logic in isolation, integration testing service interactions without deploying everything, and contract testing event schemas between producers and consumers. We cover local versus cloud testing tradeoffs, when each makes sense, and chaos engineering techniques like injecting message delays, duplicates, and out-of-order delivery to catch failures before your users do.

sessions.t: The 3-step blueprint for scaling AI with a modern enterprise core (sponsored by IBM)
sessions.a: AI is a catalyst for growth and innovation, yet only 17% of AI initiatives reach full-scale production. Join IBM and AI trailblazers to explore the three-step blueprint for scaling AI on AWS: modernizing the enterprise core across applications, data and infrastructure; fostering a culture that moves innovation forward; and putting digital labor to work in real workflows. Discover how IBM Consulting helps organizations move beyond isolated use cases, accelerate ideas into production and make AI work inside the enterprise, not around it. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: The AgentCore Governance Loop: Policy, Guardrails, Observability
sessions.a: Building an agent takes an afternoon. Operating it safely across a team takes architecture. In this session learn how to build a multi-agent reference platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and walk the full governance loop including cataloging agents for discovery, enforcing what they can do with Cedar policy at the gateway, filtering what they can say with Guardrails, and tracing behavior through observability. You will learn where the pieces integrate cleanly and where the seams break. You leave with a governance reference architecture you can adapt to any agentic workload, plus the lessons the documentation leaves out.

sessions.t: The agent fabric: shipping your software into the agentic economy
sessions.a: Your customers' AI agents won't stop at your product boundary. They expect your data, workflows, and agents to be reachable. If you're not, someone else will be. This workshop teaches the agent fabric pattern for making software products interoperable in the agentic economy: cross-organization agent discovery, cross-account identity, and the A2A protocol. Register specialist agents in AWS Agent Registry so a customer's coordinator can discover your capabilities, build that coordinator with the Strands Agents SDK, and wire cross-account trust and observability with AgentCore Identity and Observability. Leave with the pattern for shipping your product into the agentic economy.

sessions.t: The Agent Harness: Unifying Fragmented Tools for Mission AI Advisors
sessions.a: Advisors across mission-driven organizations—financial advisors, benefits navigators, program coordinators—juggle fragmented tools, manual research, and delayed plan delivery while clients go underserved. AI agents change this equation. See how to collapse this fragmentation into configuration using the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness. Learn to securely plug domain-specific skills and disparate Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers directly into the harness to generate tailored action plans in real time. Then, deploy the agent to isolated microVM sessions utilizing native memory strategies and Bedrock Guardrails. Leave with sample configurations, deployment patterns, and blueprints for building production advisors that scale.

sessions.t: The Agent Harness You Own on AWS for Regulated Industries
sessions.a: In regulated industries the model is easy; the governable, auditable, defensible agent is hard. AgentCore ships primitives, but the governance harness you own on top is the real work. We build the rails it does not give you: a fail-closed, blocklist-first permission gate where deny beats a broad allow; a hash-chained audit verifiable off-cloud; and a RACI gate binding every action to a named human. Each maps onto a managed AWS primitive — Identity, Guardrails, Evaluations, Lambda MicroVMs for isolation — naming where the primitive ends and your code begins. You leave with the rails.

Each maps onto a managed AWS primitive — Identity, Guardrails, Evaluations, Lambda MicroVMs for isolation — naming where the primitive ends and your code begins. You leave with the rails.

sessions.t: The Agentic MSP: AI Agents & Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in Action
sessions.a: MSPs managing hundreds of customer environments can no longer rely on manual, reactive workflows. In this hands-on workshop, MSP teams will deploy a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — using natural language to monitor, diagnose, and remediate issues across accounts in real time. Participants will trigger live incidents, orchestrate autonomous fixes with DevOps, FinOps, and Security agents, and explore how Kiro and AWS Transform accelerate development and modernization. The session covers agent-to-agent coordination, cross-account operations, and MCP-based tool access. MSPs will leave with a production-ready blueprint to transform operations from reactive to agentic. Laptops required — everyone builds live.

sessions.t: The Agentic MSP: AI Agents & Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in Action

In this hands-on workshop, MSP teams will deploy a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — using natural language to monitor, diagnose, and remediate issues across accounts in real time. Participants will trigger live incidents, orchestrate autonomous fixes with DevOps, FinOps, and Security agents, and explore how Kiro and AWS Transform accelerate development and modernization. The session covers agent-to-agent coordination, cross-account operations, and MCP-based tool access. MSPs will leave with a production-ready blueprint to transform operations from reactive to agentic. Laptops required — everyone builds live.

sessions.t: The Agentic MSP: How AI Compounds Customer Outcomes at Every Layer
sessions.a: The most profitable Managed Services Providers aren't just using AI internally. They're creating a compounding cycle: automate your own operations with Agentic AI, deliver measurably better outcomes to customers, then help those customers adopt AI themselves so the results multiply. This session shows how the AWS Managed Services Provider Program rewards that progression, from foundational automation through outcome-based delivery powered by AI agents. Leave with your own assessment and a concrete plan to reach the next level.

sessions.t: The agentic restaurant: AI agents that run your kitchen
sessions.a: The restaurant industry is transforming as AI agents move from pilots to production. Leading QSR and casual dining brands are deploying a "virtual general manager," multiple specialized agents orchestrated together to optimize drive-thru ordering, kitchen workflows, labor scheduling, and guest experience in real time. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a multi-agent architecture using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK, with Amazon Nova Sonic powering voice ordering at sub-2-second latency. We design a supervisor agent coordinating specialists across drive-thru, kitchen prep, inventory, and labor scheduling. Explore how agents share context, resolve conflicts, validate decisions against synthetic personas before deployment, and maintain human-in-the-loop oversight. Bring your architecture challenges.

sessions.t: The agentic restaurant: AI agents that run your kitchen

Explore how agents share context, resolve conflicts, validate decisions against synthetic personas before deployment, and maintain human-in-the-loop oversight. Bring your architecture challenges.

sessions.t: The Agentic SDLC (sponsored by Postman)
sessions.a: Autonomous agents are no longer assisting the software development lifecycle. They are rewriting it. When agents write, review, test, and ship code at machine speed, the SDLC stops being a sequence of human handoffs and becomes a control problem. This session covers the failure modes that only appear at scale: review queues that no human can absorb, test suites that validate the wrong invariants, provenance gaps that make incidents unexplainable, and CI/CD pipelines built for tens of commits a day now absorbing thousands. It closes with the specific architectural decisions engineering leaders should be making now, drawn from our own experience running agents in production. This presentation is brought to you by Postman, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: The agent orchestration spectrum: Agents, Step Functions, or Lambda?
sessions.a: "Orchestration mode matters more for end user experience than just model choice. In this live-coding session, I build the same GenAI workload three ways: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Step Functions, and AWS Lambda durable functions - and show what each costs in latency, dollars, and debuggability on a production content platform. Leave with a reusable decision framework to match orchestration to your workload."

sessions.t: The agent orchestration spectrum: Agents, Step Functions, or Lambda?
sessions.a: "Orchestration mode matters more for end user experience than just model choice. In this live-coding session, I build the same GenAI workload three ways: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Step Functions, and AWS Lambda durable functions - and show what each costs in latency, dollars, and debuggability on a production content platform. Leave with a reusable decision framework to match orchestration to your workload."

sessions.t: The age of vertical models: training to deployment on SageMaker AI
sessions.a: Purpose-built domain models are delivering breakthrough results. Intercom's Fin AI agent resolves over 2 million customer issues per week, powered by vertical foundation models that achieve superior accuracy at a fraction of the cost and latency of general-purpose alternatives. Learn how Intercom's ML team trained, evaluated, and deployed domain-specific models on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, and how vertical models are unlocking new levels of performance on real production workloads. Walk away with a blueprint for building and serving your own vertical FM at scale.

sessions.t: The AI-Native Advantage: Deploying Agentic CX in Weeks, Not Months
sessions.a: Enterprises have long accepted months of integration work and vendor complexity as the cost of delivering connected customer experiences. This session challenges that assumption. Hear how one enterprise replaced fragile, multi-vendor architectures with an AI-native solution and deployed agentic customer experiences in weeks - not months - with no compromises on speed, scale, or results. If your CX roadmap is still dictated by what your stack can stitch together, this is what becomes possible when you build on a foundation designed for the future.

sessions.t: The Amplification Effect: How AI Sharpens the Builder
sessions.a: Replacement anxiety dominates the AI conversation, but builders who use AI as a daily collaborator are discovering the opposite: AI amplifies human capability. This breakout session presents a practical framework for using AI tooling as a skills accelerator. We'll show how builders who integrate AI into daily workflows develop stronger critical thinking, faster adaptability, and deeper domain reasoning. Drawing from real-world examples, you'll learn how the act of collaborating with AI and refining its direction builds the exact human capabilities organizations need most. Walk away with a progression model from proficiency to mastery and techniques to start sharpening your skills immediately.

sessions.t: The Art of the Impossible: How Amazon Shapes What's Possible with AWS
sessions.a: Across Amazon, teams are solving challenges once considered impossible: from deploying AI agents that autonomously resolve millions of customer interactions, to creating viewing experiences that transcend the limitations of the physical world, to delivering real-time insights in milliseconds. In this session, hear from a variety of Amazon businesses as they share how AWS services like Amazon Bedrock, Amazon AgentCore, and Amazon SageMaker transform ambitious ideas into production-ready solutions at unprecedented scale. Learn the architectural patterns and AI-native practices that enable Amazon builders to achieve what was previously unimaginable, and how you can too.

sessions.t: The AWS CLI in an Agentic World: Less Tokens, More Done
sessions.a: AI coding agents are increasingly orchestrating cloud infrastructure, but they can be expensive and slow when every action requires chaining low-level API calls. The AWS CLI offers a different path: composable, structured commands that collapse multi-step workflows into single invocations. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Agent Toolkit gives AI agents first-class access to AWS through the CLI, why purpose-built commands are inherently cheaper for agents to execute, and what "developer experience for machines" means for CLI design going forward.

sessions.t: The AWS CLI in an Agentic World: Less Tokens, More Done
sessions.a: AI coding agents are increasingly orchestrating cloud infrastructure, but they can be expensive and slow when every action requires chaining low-level API calls. The AWS CLI offers a different path: composable, structured commands that collapse multi-step workflows into single invocations. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Agent Toolkit gives AI agents first-class access to AWS through the CLI, why purpose-built commands are inherently cheaper for agents to execute, and what "developer experience for machines" means for CLI design going forward.

sessions.t: The AWS Console in the age of agentic compute
sessions.a: From model testing to capacity planning, compute can be complex and costly to get wrong. As development moves into an agentic era, see how AWS Console innovations provide a trusted tool to support your workflow, verify instances, save costs, govern with confidence. Move faster. Stay in control.

sessions.t: The AWS network I would build today: Identity over topology (sponsored by Tailscale)
sessions.a: Modern AWS environments can grow from a handful of VPCs into complex regional and global routing topologies. This session explores a different model: keeping VPC networking local and predictable while using identity-aware connectivity between users, workloads, and networks. See how Tailscale connects AWS environments and resources, including those that cannot run an agent, and explore an experimental integration with AWS Gateway Load Balancer and GENEVE. Attendees will learn the tradeoffs, where native AWS networking remains the right choice, and how identity-aware networking can reduce connectivity complexity without sacrificing control. This presentation is brought to you by Tailscale, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: The Capability Overhang: Ask More of the Frontier (sponsored by Anthropic)
sessions.a: Frontier models can do more than anyone asks of them. At Anthropic, the hardest part of testing a new model is finding work hard enough to make it fail. Outside, most teams hand Claude the tasks they gave last year's model. This session closes that gap: what the newest Claude models do on AWS when you delegate the job, not the task. Multi-day autonomous work, large migrations end to end, agents that verify their results and keep going. Evals, live demos, and how our researchers keep raising the bar. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: The cloud holodeck: Stream NVIDIA Omniverse, scale headless sim on AWS
sessions.a: Interactive simulation needs RTX-class GPUs engineers lack; rendering millions of frames needs a fleet nobody wants to babysit. Amazon DCV streams a full NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim workstation from EC2 G instances to any browser, while AWS Batch runs the same scenes headless across GPU fleets for scale. The AWS Visual Asset Management System is the control plane: launching jobs, tracking runs, and versioning outputs. Watch an engineer open a cloud viewport and fan out a thousand-frame jobs live.

sessions.t: The co-build playbook: Turn AWS partner programs into deployable industrial solutions (sponsored by Belden)
sessions.a: Manufacturers know their machines generate valuable data — yet most digital initiatives stall before they scale, trapped between legacy OT protocols and cloud analytics that were never designed for the plant floor. This session shows how a connected partner ecosystem closes that gap. Learn how Belden acquires, conditions, and secures data at the physical layer, and how Edge2Web Factory Insights turns that data into high-powered analytics and AI-enriched insights based on AWS IoT SiteWise. Discover the reference architecture behind a joint deployment, from edge protocol connectivity to AI-driven insight. See how co-development with AWS compressed the path from whiteboard to production. And explore how to apply this pattern to your own operations. This presentation is brought to you by Belden, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: The Control Plane for Your Agent Workforce: Governance, Cost and ROI at Scale (sponsored by Cognition)
sessions.a: Cognition has rolled out Devin, the autonomous software engineer, at the world's largest Fortune 500 companies. Along the way, we learned that scaling an agent workforce hinges on three questions every enterprise asks: How do we onboard agents? How do we know they're delivering value? How do we ensure they only do what they're supposed to? Drawing from real deployments, this session introduces the practical patterns we developed to answer them — governance, cost controls, ROI measurement, and federated configurations. You'll leave with a playbook for turning agents from a promising pilot into a trusted, scaled workforce. This presentation is brought to you by Cognition, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: The coordination decision: when to orchestrate and when to let go
sessions.a: Distributed workflows need coordination, and most teams pick one approach everywhere: a central orchestrator, or independent services reacting to events. Both fail at scale: orchestration bottlenecks every team's releases, and choreography lets flows stall silently because no component owns the outcome. This session teaches a per-flow method: does any component need to own the flow end-to-end, including completion, failure compensation, and ordering? Using a logistics platform running both patterns on AWS Step Functions and Amazon EventBridge, see the real costs of each, and where orchestration and events hand off.

sessions.t: The cost of over-engineering: When your architecture fights you
sessions.a: Not every workload needs microservices, event-driven patterns, or serverless. Over-decomposed architectures create distributed monoliths, event spaghetti, and operational nightmares that cost more and move slower than the monolith they replaced. In this chalk talk, examine real-world anti-patterns: services split too small, queues added without purpose, and abstractions that add latency without value. We’ll whiteboard decision frameworks for right-sizing architecture, including the signals that tell you when decomposition earns its complexity and when it doesn’t. Bring your diagrams and discuss where simplification improves speed, reduces cost, and strengthens reliability. Leave able to right-size your own architecture with confidence.

sessions.t: The EBA cloud party: compete to build agentic migration solutions
sessions.a: The cloud journey isn't just about migration anymore. It's about building intelligent frameworks that transform how organizations operate. In this gamified Experience-Based Acceleration (EBA) workshop, cross-functional teams compete in real time to architect migration and modernization solutions, build agentic AI workflows that automate at scale, and deploy AI-powered applications on AWS. Push boundaries, solve real challenges together, and have fun doing it. Walk away with battle-tested architectures, agentic automation patterns, and a cloud-fluent mindset your team can adopt immediately. Ready to play?

sessions.t: The Economics of an AWS Partner: Revenue, Incentives & Marketplace
sessions.a: A forward-looking session reframing Partner economics for the year ahead. Revenue measurement is no longer just tracking—it's the backbone connecting all Partner programs. Walk away with a clear action plan to position for next-year advantages.

sessions.t: The Evaluator Is the Algorithm: Evolving SOTA for $15
sessions.a: We discovered a phase transition in LLM-guided code evolution: when the evaluation function provides smooth gradient signal, SOTA emerges automatically regardless of model choice; when it doesn't, no compute compensates. This "evaluator-dominance principle" emerged from stress-testing evolutionary search across 403 problems in 27 domains on Amazon Bedrock — 20× the scale of Google's original AlphaEvolve — achieving 96% SOTA-matching at $15/problem median cost. We'll present the Bedrock-native architecture (MAP-Elites, staged evaluation cascade, Opus/Haiku phase routing), a production vehicle routing deployment saving 1.28% on 100,000-customer routes at $530 total spend, and the evaluator design methodology that determines success or failure.

sessions.t: The Frontier Doesn't Hold Still: Running Claude Agents at Scale on AWS (sponsored by Anthropic)
sessions.a: Enterprises are moving faster with AI than ever. And they're falling further behind. Once the first agents land and the numbers look good, most teams turn to cost control while the frontier keeps moving. This session covers how to do both with Claude on AWS: the security and compliance controls enterprises require, execution inside your own boundary, observability and cost governance, and the safeguards that let you trust agents with more. Then how to keep expanding what agents do as new models arrive, so efficiency doesn't become the ceiling. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: The future of Kubernetes on AWS
sessions.a: Kubernetes has become a standard for organizations looking to modernize their application portfolios. AWS developed Amazon EKS to make Kubernetes more accessible to organizations of all sizes, helping them focus on what matters most for their businesses. In this session, join Amazon EKS product leadership to learn about the latest innovations and strategies for building Kubernetes platforms and applications faster, including building and orchestrating agents. Discover how various organizations use Amazon EKS to run their most demanding applications in the cloud, on premises, and at the edge.

sessions.t: The golden path for agentic workloads: safe by default on Amazon EKS
sessions.a: Every team is shipping agentic apps, and they are landing on your platform faster than you can review them. As the platform team, you own the blast radius: untrusted code, over-broad permissions, and unbounded egress you never signed off on. This code talk walks through the controls that let you say yes safely. See how to enforce VM-level isolation for workloads running untrusted or AI-generated code. Learn how to scope identity and network egress so an agent reaches only what it should. Discover how to codify these as policy so every new agent inherits the guardrails by default.

sessions.t: The Governance Gap Keeping AI Agents Out of Production (sponsored by WSO2)
sessions.a: Every leader is under pressure to show AI value now. Some move fast, and agents sprawl across teams with no shared controls. Others lock everything down, and pilots never reach production. Both point to the same gap: governance maturity hasn't kept pace with agent speed. This talk covers how governance becomes an accelerator, not a blocker, to production AI. You’ll learn how to design identity, policy, and guardrails from day one, so agents ship with the same controls whether they run on AWS Bedrock, hybrid, or otherwise. Get the principles right early, and agents move from pilot to production without every team reinventing governance on their own. Takeaways: Why AI programs sprawl or stall, and what governance maturity looks like in between. How trusted AI governance turns into speed instead of slowing teams down. What governance principles to design in from day one, on AWS & beyond. This presentation is brought to you by WSO2, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: The Infrastructure Behind AI: Scaling Access to Web Data (sponsored by Oxylabs)
sessions.a: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence directly mirrors the continuous evolution of web intelligence infrastructure. As machine learning models demand exponentially richer datasets, web data extraction has transformed from simple parsing into a sophisticated, mission-critical engineering discipline. In this session, explore how modern web scraping infrastructure actively evolves alongside artificial intelligence to solve live data bottlenecks and complex anti-automation challenges. Discover high-throughput extraction architectures, real-world pipeline designs, and strategic business use cases that turn dynamic web data into production-ready intelligence. Learn how advanced web data infrastructure fuels current artificial intelligence capabilities and shapes the future of automated enterprise decision-making. This presentation is brought to you by Oxylabs, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: The judgment gap: when Terraform scans clean but fails the audit
sessions.a: Checkov, trivy, and Prowler check rules someone already wrote. SOC 2 CC6.1 is a sentence open to interpretation. Between them sits the judgment gap, where AI-generated Terraform for S3, CloudFront, API Gateway, and Lambda often lands. We map the gap on the whiteboard together: take real controls from SOC 2 and PCI DSS, set them against what scanner rules verify, and mark what is left over. Then we discuss what closes the remainder: better authoring-side skills, human review, multi-model review, or accepting the risk. Bring a control your team owns; we trace where its enforcement lives, or does not.

sessions.t: The Mathematics of Backlogs: Why Your Queue Will Never Drain
sessions.a: Your consumers are healthy, your pods are green - yet your backlog isn't shrinking. Why? Because systems provisioned for steady-state have zero recovery capacity. In this chalk talk, we'll derive the formulas that govern backlog formation and drain, explore the non-linear utilization cliff where small traffic spikes become catastrophic, and work through the real-world complications: retry amplification, stale-message degradation, and multi-stage cascades. Bring your architectures - we'll whiteboard whether they can actually recover from failure, or just survive it.

sessions.t: The memory of an agent: running RAG on EKS at scale
sessions.a: An agent is only as good as what it can recall, and the retrieval layer is where that breaks. I run a vector store on Amazon EKS behind a service mesh, and this session is about operating it. What changes as the corpus grows, the latency and cost tradeoffs between vector stores, why the service mesh both helps and complicates, and the retrieval failures that look like the model being wrong but are not. I will show the architecture and the decisions behind it. You will leave with a pattern for running a production retrieval layer agents can depend on.

sessions.t: The Neuron Stack: Enabling open source ML solutions on AWS Trainium
sessions.a: The Neuron software stack has evolved into an open source-first architecture. Developers can read, modify, and contribute to the components that compile, optimize, and execute ML workloads on Trainium. This session covers how Neuron enables open source ML solutions on Trainium. We show what's open source, how it integrates with upstream projects like PyTorch and distributed training frameworks, and how developers use these tools without modifications. Attendees leave understanding the Neuron stack, which parts are open source, and how to use and contribute to them.

sessions.t: The Next Phase of AI for SRE: Distributed Reasoning for Enterprise Operations (sponsored by Ciroos)
sessions.a: AI for SRE isn’t just a speed or accuracy problem; it’s a problem of deeper understanding. This session explores how team members across different domains in an enterprise can use a shared AI reasoning layer to operate production systems and collaborate effectively to increase reliability. We’ll show how this AI reasoning layer handles the extremes of alert storms and alert silence, catching deployment-triggered anomalies before they cause production impact. Learn how teams are moving beyond reactive dashboards, using state-of-the-art techniques to instantly correlate cross-domain telemetry, execute complex investigations, and achieve proactive reliability in dynamic cloud and hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by Ciroos, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: The Physical AI Blueprint: A Full-Stack Solution with AWS and NVIDIA (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.a: Get hands-on building a complete Physical AI pipeline using the AWS and NVIDIA toolchain. This workshop walks you through each stage—synthetic data generation with Isaac Sim, foundation model training with GR00T and Cosmos, digital twin simulation in Omniverse, edge deployment via IoT Greengrass, multi-robot orchestration with AgentCore, and continuous learning with SageMaker using NVIDIA OSMO. Walk away with a working blueprint you can apply to manufacturing, logistics, or autonomous systems. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: The Road to 10x velocity
sessions.a: This is a real-world case study documenting the journey toward 10x engineering velocity using Kiro. Prime Video Financial Systems started at 3x with AI-assisted sprints, then evolved to autonomous agent-driven delivery: agents pick up tasks, implement, raise CRs, and address review feedback 24/7, with engineers retaining control of final approval and merge. Each step compounds: parallel execution, zero idle time, and engineers freed to focus on design and review. It's an honest, in-progress story showing builders the concrete methodology, leveraging Kiro to build an end-to-end software development lifecycle orchestration framework, and the architectural decisions required to move from acceleration toward order-of-magnitude transformation.

sessions.t: The security you inherit: how the AWS platform protects your workloads by default
sessions.a: Every organization has finite security resources. The more the platform handles, the more your team can focus on securing what is unique to your application — your data, your logic, your users. In this session, we explore the security capabilities built into the AWS platform that work before you write a single IAM policy. From threat intelligence that blocks malicious actors at the network edge, to Nitro's zero operator access architecture that eliminates an entire class of insider risk, to automated reasoning that mathematically proves your policies behave as intended — these are protections you inherit just by running on AWS. We also cover PrivateLink for eliminating public internet exposure, default encryption, and S3 Block Public Access. Understand what the platform already handles so you can direct your security investment where it matters most: the application layer.

sessions.t: The Trade Desk's Cloud Journey: AI-Assisted Optimization to AI Agents
sessions.a: The Trade Desk operates a real-time advertising platform on AWS, where infrastructure must handle massive scale while making bidding decisions in milliseconds. At that scale, cloud cost optimization isn't a one-time exercise, it's a continuous discipline with one constraint: improve efficiency without compromising business-critical performance. In this breakout, The Trade Desk shares how it evolved from traditional cost audits to an AI-assisted, agentic approach. Learn how the team built an internal MCP server that enables AI agents to investigate cost and usage data, uncover savings across services like S3, NAT Gateway, EBS, and Graviton, and build a repeatable framework for continuously optimizing cloud workloads.

sessions.t: Think Beyond DevOps: SRE, SOC, and Compliance in One AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.a: As AI speeds up releases, continuous security control assurance and detecting threats in millions of telemetry signals get harder. We transformed AWS DevOps Agent into one agent for SRE, SOC and compliance, effectively addressing AI-era cloud security challenges in production. With AWS Config Conformance Packs for compliance-as-code and security MCP for finding triage, it produces point-in-time compliance and well-architected assessments, and drives alarm-triggered agentic SOC investigations within a controlled agent space, automating responses and keeping human-in-the-loop on high-risk mitigations only. You'll learn the methodology to design an agentic compliance and SOC solution that ports seamlessly into your own environment.

sessions.t: Thinking agentic: What developers using Serverless need to know
sessions.a: You've been building event-driven, async systems for years. Agents are a new type of consumer in your existing architecture. In this chalk talk, we discuss what actually changes: reframing functions as tools with schema-first interfaces, managing agent state with storage and checkpoints, and handling non-deterministic failures from LLM calls. We walk through a practical path from "I have a serverless app" to "my app has agent capabilities," adding capabilities incrementally without rewriting what already works. Bring your architecture. We'll whiteboard where agents fit in what you've already built.

sessions.t: Threat Detection and IR in AgentCore Workloads
sessions.a: Step into an AWS environment where command-and-control callbacks from agent tools, exfiltrated credentials, and disabled safety guardrails occurred across AgentCore workloads. Your mission: detect, investigate, and respond. Using Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub alongside CloudWatch and AgentCore Observability, you'll triage findings, correlate security events with application traces, map entity relationships, isolate compromised resources, and build automated remediations. You'll leave with practical skills to secure AgentCore systems you can trust.

sessions.t: Threat Modeling the Agentic SDLC: From User Story to Deployment
sessions.a: Agentic development is accelerating, but how do you threat model a workflow where AI makes decisions autonomously? In this Code Talk, walk through an end-to-end process: from threat modeling a user story with AWS Continuum for threat modeling (capabilities are delivered through AWS Security Agent), through the developer workflow, to deployment. See how ThreatForest - an agentic tool built on the Strands framework - autonomously generates attack trees and MITRE ATT&CK mappings, and how to build a reusable mitigations catalogue that scales across your organization. Leave with working patterns and hard-won lessons from real-world implementations, including where traditional threat modeling assumptions break down for agentic systems.

sessions.t: Threat Technique Catalog for AWS: Practical Controls for Real TTPs
sessions.a: Threat actors are evolving faster than ever, leveraging AI-generated exploits and automated attack tooling to move at machine speed. AWS CIRT sees these techniques firsthand across customer incidents of all sizes. The Threat Technique Catalog for AWS (TTC), extending the MITRE ATT&CK framework, documents these recurring TTPs with detection and mitigation guidance specific to AWS. This session covers how to turn observed attacker patterns into an advantage: build actionable detections and mitigations into your security operations before the next incident hits.

sessions.t: Token Counts to Business Impact: Measurable AI Architectures at Scale
sessions.a: As AI workloads scale, the question shifts from "what does this cost?" to "is this delivering real value?" The answer depends on your workload, architecture, and adoption maturity. We present progressive architecture patterns using agentic software development — from vibe-coding to cloud agents to self-hosted inference to custom models — with a live demo across the AWS AI Stack, including Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker HyperPod, and Trainium, showing how the right metrics evolve with your architecture. You'll leave with cost-per-outcome comparisons, spend controls that work at scale, and an ROI measurement framework with architecture patterns to implement across any AI workload.

sessions.t: Token-efficient retrieval for production AI agents (sponsored by Exa)
sessions.a: Most agent bills aren't driven by the model, they're driven by the context it's given. Raw web pages, HTML boilerplate, and 10 blue links padded with irrelevant text quietly multiply token spend and degrade answer quality. This lightning talk walks through how Exa engineered retrieval to hand LLMs exactly the text they need: neural search that returns precise passages instead of whole pages, highlight extraction tuned to the query, and context-budgeting techniques that cut input tokens dramatically without hurting accuracy. Using real production traces, we'll show how token-efficient retrieval changes the economics of agents at scale on AWS, and give you a practical checklist you can apply to any RAG or agent pipeline this week. This presentation is brought to you by Exa, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Tokenomics for AI on AWS: Local inference plus Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by Spectro Cloud)
sessions.a: Power users in AI teams building on AWS face the challenge of frontier models delivering the best answers and token costs scaling with adoption. Not every prompt requires frontier models. The ones that do, belong on the best endpoint. This talk covers a working pattern for enterprise inference on AWS: PaletteAI Inference Launchpad running local open-weight models for routine requests, Amazon Bedrock as the burst target to extend capacity, and frontier models as needed for complex work. We will show how routing, quotas, and per-team attribution keep tokenomics predictable, so platform teams can enable AI adoption without inheriting the bill. This presentation is brought to you by Spectro Cloud, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Tokenomics: Understanding What Your AI Actually Costs (sponsored by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
sessions.a: Your AI pilot ran smoothly and stayed on budget. Then you launched, and the invoice was much higher than the estimate. This session breaks down why that happens and what to do about it. We'll walk through where AI spend actually goes once a system leaves the demo stage, why agentic AI costs differently than a simple chatbot, and how choosing the right model for each task, not just the flagship model for everything, can cut spend dramatically without hurting quality. You'll leave with a practical framework for tracking cost, avoiding common budgeting traps, and having a more confident conversation with finance the next time AI spend comes up. This presentation is brought to you by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Too many tools: Building software in the age of agents
sessions.a: AI now touches every stage of software delivery: coding assistants, autonomous agents, modernization tools, security scanners, operations, and the list grows every week. Which do you actually use, and when? This open discussion helps you make sense of the SDLC tooling landscape. Bring your scenario and we'll talk through it together: when to hand work to an autonomous agent versus a deterministic tool, how to chain AI across design, code, review, and operations without creating new bottlenecks, and how to avoid adopting every shiny agent at once. Leave with a plan for building software with AI, not just a tool list.

sessions.t: Too many tools: Building software in the age of agents
sessions.a: AI now touches every stage of software delivery: coding assistants, autonomous agents, modernization tools, security scanners, operations, and the list grows every week. Leave with a plan for building software with AI, not just a tool list.

sessions.t: Track Cross-Domain Attack Vectors with AWS Security Hub Extended
sessions.a: In this 20-minute lightning talk, see how AWS Security Hub Extended correlates signals across endpoint, identity, email, data, browser, and AI domains into a single attack narrative. We show how cross-domain correlation surfaces attack vectors invisible to any single tool, and how customers deploy preconfigured detection patterns for immediate value.

sessions.t: Train and deploy large-scale models with governance at every step
sessions.a: Training a large-scale model is the easy part. Getting it into production with the right data flowing in, governance enforced, and multiple deployment paths ready is where most teams stall. This chalk talk works through how to build one training pipeline on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, bring in enterprise data that amplifies model value while respecting data protection policies, and deploy the same model into Amazon Bedrock for inference or Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for agent orchestration. Governance follows the model at every step. No bolted-on compliance. You leave with an architecture you can build against immediately.

sessions.t: Transform Episodic Content into High-Converting Microdramas
sessions.a: Turn your episodic content into binge-worthy microdramas. In this session, you'll learn how to build both single- and multi-episode formats, multiply one source into a library of platform-ready content assets, and monetize a story in multiple ways — across ad-supported, subscription, and social distribution. We'll walk through scroll-stopping production techniques optimized for vertical, mobile-first viewing, and the pacing and cliffhanger patterns that drive completion and re-watch rates. Leave with a repeatable workflow for producing microdrama series at scale and a clear playbook for turning your existing catalog into high-converting, agent- and platform-ready short-form video.

sessions.t: Transforming business and SAP with Amazon Innovations
sessions.a: The SAP landscape is changing, with customers not just asking “How can you help us migrate and run our SAP applications in the cloud?”, but instead: “How can you help us transform our business, simplify our business processes, and leverage AI to serve our customers and employees?”. Join this session to learn how our marquee customers are combining SAP modernization with Amazon's extensive portfolio to revolutionize customer experiences. You'll hear how customers are redefining customer experience and transforming business processes including finance procurement, manufacturing, operation etc by leveraging Pan-Amazon services, and AWS AI services alongside SAP.

sessions.t: Transforming Customer Experiences Through Tapestry’s Order Management (sponsored by Digitate)
sessions.a: Customers expect fast, personalized, and seamless experiences across every interaction with a brand. For Tapestry, connecting consumer feedback, sentiment, and operational signals is key to identifying issues that can impact customer experience and brand reputation. In this session, Sonal Sharan will share how Tapestry is leveraging ignio's AI Agents to continuously analyze these signals, surface emerging concerns, and provide real-time visibility into business-impacting issues. Intelligent workflows help prioritize and route issues for faster resolution, while actionable insights support more proactive customer engagement, resulting in a more connected, responsive, and customer-centric organization delivering exceptional experiences across Tapestry’s leading brands. This presentation is brought to you by Digitate, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Transforming from a Connectivity  Provider to an AI Delivery Channel
sessions.a: Explore how a leading carrier built an AI delivery channel embedding intelligence directly into voice networks for real-time, contextual services. Discover their ultra-low-jitter wireless network enabling Physical AI workloads at scale using Bedrock and SageMaker across AWS Regions, Local Zones, and Outposts.

sessions.t: Transforming legacy core to agentic AI with Nissan & Bread Financial
sessions.a: Legacy mainframe applications were built for stability, scale, and batch-oriented processing, but they were never designed to power real-time, intelligent, agentic experiences. Modernization changes that. Discover how Nissan reimagined core operations into a cloud-native platform designed for responsiveness, adaptability, and AI-ready workflows. Hear how Bread Financial is evolving beyond credit-processing architectures to accelerate innovation by decomposing monolithic capabilities into bounded context services, creating a modern foundation for autonomous workflows. See how both used AWS Transform to extract business rules from decades-old applications and Kiro to forward-engineer production-ready code. Learn how modernized applications unlock the architecture that makes agentic AI possible.

sessions.t: Transforming Patient Engagement with AI and Cloud (sponsored by Incedo Inc.)
sessions.a: Life sciences organizations are reimagining patient engagement through cloud data and artificial intelligence. This session explores how generative AI and intelligent automation can help create more connected personalized and responsive patient experiences across the patient journey. Drawing on real world transformation experiences the discussion will highlight practical opportunities to improve patient engagement reduce friction and enable more proactive interactions while addressing the data governance and adoption considerations required to scale AI responsibly. Attendees will gain practical perspectives on how life sciences organizations can move from AI experimentation to scalable solutions that deliver meaningful patient and business outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Incedo Inc., an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Transform your SaaS for the agentic AI era on Amazon ECS
sessions.a: Your multi-tenant SaaS application runs on Amazon ECS. Now your customers expect AI-powered features but adding agents to an existing platform introduces new challenges. Including tenant isolation for model access, per-tenant memory and conversation state, cost attribution across shared infrastructure, and agent orchestration at scale. In this workshop, you start with a working SaaS application on Amazon ECS and progressively add agentic capabilities using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Implement tenant-aware agent routing, configure isolated tool execution with ECS task-level security boundaries, add persistent memory per tenant, and instrument with end-to-end observability. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Troubleshooting and recovering failed Amazon ECS deployments
sessions.a: Your Amazon ECS deployment just failed: new tasks will not launch, traffic is not shifting, and your team needs to ship an update now. In this code talk, we live-troubleshoot real failures step by step, showing how to diagnose the root cause, recover the service, and build guardrails that prevent repeat failures. We then go further, using the AWS DevOps Agent and ECS remote MCP tools to diagnose issues faster by correlating signals and surfacing likely causes. You will leave with a repeatable troubleshooting playbook for ECS deployments, both manual and AI-assisted.

sessions.t: Troubleshooting and recovering failed Amazon ECS deployments
sessions.a: Your Amazon ECS deployment just failed: new tasks will not launch, traffic is not shifting, and your team needs to ship an update now. In this code talk, we live-troubleshoot real failures step by step, showing how to diagnose the root cause, recover the service, and build guardrails that prevent repeat failures. You will leave with a repeatable troubleshooting playbook for ECS deployments, both manual and AI-assisted.

sessions.t: Trust at Scale: Unlocking Enterprise Agentic AI (sponsored by Qlik)
sessions.a: Agentic AI dies at scale. It is easy to get one agent working on one dataset for one team. The challenge is trusting its answers across hundreds of thousands of users, regions, languages, regulators, and constantly changing data. AWS provides global infrastructure, security, data residency, and compliance controls to scale AI. Qlik provides trusted governed data, business context, and intelligence that agents can rely on. See how Amazon Bedrock and the Qlik MCP Server bring trusted Qlik intelligence to production agents and any LLM including Amazon Quick. Learn how enterprises can scale agentic AI without sacrificing trust governance or choice. This presentation is brought to you by Qlik, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Trust but verify: Building the audit loop for AI-driven operations
sessions.a: AI agents act fast. Auditors ask questions slowly. Bridge that gap with an observability layer that satisfies both. This session walks through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore traces across multi-agent workflows, Amazon CloudWatch for decision-level visibility and drift detection, escalation thresholds that keep humans in the loop, and patterns for reconstructing agent reasoning after the fact. Walk away with a practical audit loop you can implement for agents running in production.

sessions.t: Trust but verify: Building the audit loop for AI-driven operations
sessions.a: AI agents act fast. Auditors ask questions slowly. Bridge that gap with an observability layer that satisfies both. This session walks through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore traces across multi-agent workflows, Amazon CloudWatch for decision-level visibility and drift detection, escalation thresholds that keep humans in the loop, and patterns for reconstructing agent reasoning after the fact.
