sessions.t: Trusted intent: How Kiro proves your specs before writing any code
sessions.a: Your AI agent writes code fast, but is it building what you actually meant? Kiro's requirements analysis goes far beyond asking an LLM to generate a spec. It combines auto-formalization, SMT solvers, and neuro-symbolic techniques to mathematically detect ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. In this session, learn how we turned decades of formal methods into a developer experience that feels like answering simple yes/no questions while catching the bugs that cost the most to fix.

sessions.t: Trusting agents in production: end-to-end security with AgentCore
sessions.a: AI agents call APIs, access databases, and act on behalf of users, making security non-negotiable before you go to production. But they introduce new attack surfaces: persistent sessions, autonomous tool execution, and permissions that compound across steps. This session shows how to secure agents end to end with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: microVM isolation so sessions can't leak into each other, identity propagation so every action traces back to a user, Gateway policies that control which tools agents can reach, and Cedar authorization for least-privilege at every call. Leave with a blueprint for production.

sessions.t: Trusting an Autonomous Agent With Your Production Environment (sponsored by NeuBird AI)
sessions.a: The biggest barrier to autonomous operations isn't capability, it's trust.Handing an incident to an autonomous agent raises a fair question. How do you know it is not guessing from raw log lines. This session shows how NeuBird AI reasons over your live environment and shows the causal chain behind every root cause, not a coincidence in the metrics. We’ll examine the guardrails that make production deployment safe: VPC-native execution, zero external data retention, complete auditable reasoning paths, and human-gated action approvals. Learn how to safely transition from human-driven triage to trusted, autonomous production operations on your own terms. This presentation is brought to you by NeuBird AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Trust the Agent, Keep the Keys: The Journey to Autonomous Operations (sponsored by PagerDuty)
sessions.a: AI is shipping more code to production than ever before, but incidents are taking longer to resolve. Hear from peers at different stages of operational maturity, all testing out ways to put AI and automation to work so their teams get more time back for innovation. Panelists will share how they decide what's safe to automate outright, where to keep a human in or on the loop, and where full human judgment still matters. You'll hear what convinced them to hand over more control, what happened when it didn't go as planned, and how they cut toil without losing their grip on the systems they're accountable for. This presentation is brought to you by PagerDuty, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Turbocharge your Agentic Consulting Practice with Agentic Consultants
sessions.a: Partners are building agentic consulting practices with human consultants, but what if they could deliver 10x more engagements by augmenting their teams with consulting agents? In this hands-on builders' session, work alongside a team of consulting agents that guide a human consultant through structured discovery — asking the right questions and validating assumptions — then build out business requirements, generate agent designs and AWS architectures, calculate ROI-backed financial models, and export ready-to-use Statement of Work — all in a single, AI-accelerated workflow you can take straight back to your practice.

sessions.t: Turbocharge your Agentic Consulting Practice with Agentic Consultants

sessions.t: Turn a Bee wearable into your re:Invent notetaking companion
sessions.a: re:Invent keynotes don't slow down for note-taking. Last year's CEO keynote announced roughly 28 launches in two hours. Careful notes still leave you with names, not links. So build an agent that does the finding. Every attendee gets a Bee Pioneer wearable: it transcribes while you listen, and a double-press bookmarks anything worth a deep dive. Your agent (Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock) reads the transcript and researches each announcement through the AWS MCP Server, producing one markdown file linking every launch to its docs. Then make it yours: benchmark cheaper models, post to Slack, or run it in the cloud.

sessions.t: Turn autonomous agents into accountable ones
sessions.a: Your AI agents pass the demo but struggle in production because of limited accountability and controls. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard a governance framework that closes the loop. You get governed agent accounts with AWS Control Tower, hard API boundaries with AWS Organizations policies, and runtime tool-access controls and behavior scoring in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. AWS Config detects drift from policy and triggers automated rollback. You leave with a repeatable, observe-score-remediate pattern for keeping AI agents operating within your policies."

sessions.t: Turn AWS Marketplace listings into self-service buyer journeys
sessions.a: Make it easier for customers to find, subscribe and deploy your software in by providing a self-service path from evaluation to purchase. In this session, explore how to transform your AWS Marketplace listing using demos, free trials, AI-guided evaluation and usage-based pricing. Learn the repeatable patterns for reducing procurement delays, measuring buyer progression, activating listings, and directing qualified buyers.

sessions.t: Turning Data into Decisions: Pacific Life's Modern Insurance Operations with AWS AI (sponsored by PwC)
sessions.a: Abstract: PwC-built Generative AI data processing solution for Pacific Life Re, hosted on AWS. The solution automates the ingestion, transformation, validation, schema mapping, and PII redaction of client actuarial datasets that arrive in different formats, languages, and quality levels. In short, it helps PLRe move from manual, time-consuming data preparation to a secure, auditable, AI-enabled workflow that can reduce processing times from weeks to days, improve data quality, and provide clean, validated outputs for actuarial, pricing, and R&D teams. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Turning migration security from afterthought into advantage
sessions.a: You migrate workloads to AWS but governance controls typically follow after landing, creating rework. This chalk talk explores how to embed guardrails directly into your AWS Transform migration workflow using AWS Organizations, IAM Identity Center, AWS Config, and AWS Security Hub so workloads arrive with controls already in place. Bring your migration challenges and leave with a practical design for secure-by-default landing that integrates governance into agentic AI-driven migration from discovery through execution.

sessions.t: Turning Pharma Field Insights into Enterprise Intelligence (sponsored by ZS)
sessions.a: Learn how ZS and AWS help pharma teams turn field insights into AI-powered intelligence. This presentation is brought to you by ZS, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Turn log storage into log intelligence
sessions.a: Give your operations teams the full picture without jumping between tools. Learn how to bring logs, metrics, and traces into a unified data store for analytics and improved troubleshooting. Instead of just storing logs and treating logs as text to grep during an outage, use centralization rules that bring telemetry together across accounts and regions, telemetry pipelines that enrich and route data in flight, intelligence tiering that matches storage cost to query value, and AI-assisted log analytics that surface answers instead of waiting for you to ask the right question. This is about making logs work for you — not the other way around. You'll leave with a clear architecture for unified log analytics you can take back to your org and put into production.

sessions.t: Turn PQC readiness into the trust story your board needs
sessions.a: Organizations planning post-quantum cryptography (PQC) migrations face the same three questions: where do I start my migration plan, which workloads do I prioritize, and how do I get buy-in from leadership? With NIST PQC standards finalized, the algorithm question is settled, the open question is how to plan and fund the transition. In this chalk talk we whiteboard the PQC Readiness Maturity Model: five levels from discovery to quantum-ready, each with measurable milestones. You leave with a practical framework to scope your inventory, prioritize transitions, modernize how you protect data, and build the board narrative that funds your migration program.

sessions.t: Turn raw telemetry into answers with OpenTelemetry
sessions.a: Raw telemetry arrives noisy, unlabeled, and hard to query, so teams waste time cleaning data before they can act. In this hands-on builders session, you set up OpenTelemetry for metrics, logs, and traces from a live sample application, then use Amazon CloudWatch pipeline processors to enrich and normalize the data in flight. You build the enrichment rules, explore results with natural language query, and leave with a reusable pattern for turning raw signals into analysis-ready telemetry.

sessions.t: Turn raw telemetry into answers with OpenTelemetry
sessions.a: Raw telemetry arrives noisy, unlabeled, and hard to query, so teams waste time cleaning data before they can act. In this hands-on builders session, you set up OpenTelemetry for metrics, logs, and traces from a live sample application, then use Amazon CloudWatch pipeline processors to enrich and normalize the data in flight. You build the enrichment rules, explore results with natural language query, and leave with a reusable pattern for turning raw signals into analysis-ready telemetry.

sessions.t: Turn security logs into actionable intelligence
sessions.a: Security teams drown in logs but struggle to investigate fast. In this hands-on session, turn raw security telemetry from CloudTrail, S3 access logs, and VPC flow logs into actionable intelligence with Amazon CloudWatch. We'll centralize logs in the CloudWatch Unified Data Store, then query across sources to investigate real scenarios: after-hours data access, credential misuse, and exfiltration patterns. You'll build a security dashboard that surfaces who did what, from where, and when. Walk away with reusable queries and dashboards you can deploy in your own accounts, moving from reactive log search to proactive security visibility.

sessions.t: Turn your cloud migration into a security transformation
sessions.a: Forward-looking organizations aren't just migrating to AWS — they're using migration to transform their entire security posture. In this workshop, your workloads have just landed on AWS and you'll immediately secure them using sandbox accounts. You'll use Amazon GuardDuty to detect runtime-level threats and malware, Amazon Inspector to prioritize software vulnerabilities, and AWS Security Hub to correlate findings into actionable exposures. You'll finish by building an automated remediation pipeline that isolates compromised resources without human intervention. Leave with a repeatable Day 1 security playbook for any migrated workload. Laptop required.

sessions.t: Turn your coding agent into an always-on dev team with AgentCore
sessions.a: Claude Code, Kiro, and Codex are impressive individually, but in an enterprise they run stateless, isolated from team context, and invisible to governance. AgentCore turns any coding agent into a production system: shared memory so the agent understands your architecture across sessions, microVM isolation so jobs run in parallel without interference, identity propagation so agents access only what they should, and full trace observability so you know what every agent did and why. This session shows what changes when you pair popular coding agents with a production platform, and how our customer deployed this across hundreds of developers.

sessions.t: Twenty years of cloud architecture
sessions.a: Instant, vast scale and elasticity. Infrastructure as Code. Eventual consistency. Immutable infrastructure. Serverless. Event-driven computing. Internet of Things. Chaos engineering. Zero trust. Pervasive observability. Twenty years of cloud have produced an extraordinary density of patterns — each arriving with conviction and shaping what came next. Some became invisible foundations we build on without thinking. Others evolved in ways nobody predicted. And the evolution continues — now with agentic architectures. What has stood the test of time? What's still evolving? And what can we learn to be ready for the next twenty years?

sessions.t: Uncovering Value with Velocity in Clinical Data Management with Autonomous AI Agents (sponsored by Cognizant)
sessions.a: Today's Clinical Data Management processes are burdened by high-intensity manual tasks , ranging from protocol reviews, EDC configuration, and data validation to final database lock and reporting. These activities are time-consuming, error-prone, and delay study timelines. AI-driven multi-agent systems can intelligently automate protocol reviews, edit check programming, data validation, and query management accelerating study timelines, improving data accuracy, and enabling teams to focus on strategic, high-value activities. Know how integrating advanced AI-driven automation with human expertise enhances data accuracy, streamlines workflows, and accelerates decision-making processes, empowering clinical teams to achieve superior research outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Cognizant, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Uncover the Opportunity. Build the AI Agent. Scale It Live. (sponsored by NiCE)
sessions.a: Your CX data already knows where automation will pay off. See Agentic Analytics pinpoint the opportunity, then watch that recommendation become a working AI agent — built, tested, and scaled live. ​ This presentation is brought to you by NiCE, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Understand your network: practical network observability on AWS
sessions.a: You're collecting Amazon VPC Flow Logs and Amazon CloudWatch metrics—but still can't answer "why can't this instance reach the internet?" In this chalk talk, explore practical approaches to network observability on AWS, no deep expertise required. Cover the key logs and metrics that actually matter, how to read them, and how to set up simple dashboards and alerts that tell you something is wrong before your users do. Bring your monitoring questions—we'll discuss real scenarios and help you build observability that works for your team.

sessions.t: Under the hood of Kiro Crew: orchestration, memory, and safe autonomy
sessions.a: Handing real work to a crew of agents raises real questions: How does it coordinate parallel subagents without losing the thread? How does memory save across sessions so agents don't start cold? How do you give agents access to your code and CI while staying safe? In this chalk talk, we'll dig into how Kiro Crew works: observable multi-agent orchestration over Agent Client Protocol, self-evolving memory and skills you can inspect and edit, scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs, and defense-in-depth security with sandboxing, denied-by-default commands, and signed audit logs. Bring your architecture and security questions and we'll whiteboard through them.

Bring your architecture and security questions and we'll whiteboard through them.

sessions.t: Under the hood with Amazon EBS: Achieving sub-millisecond latency
sessions.a: Amazon EBS powers mission-critical applications with consistent sub-millisecond latency across millions of volumes. This session offers a behind-the-scenes look at the architectural innovations and engineering practices that make this possible. Learn how EBS leverages the AWS Nitro System, purpose-built hardware, and advanced I/O path optimizations to deliver reliable low-latency performance at hyperscale. Gain insights into how these capabilities translate into performance benefits for databases, analytics platforms, and latency-sensitive workloads.

sessions.t: Unexpected resilience: Lessons from a thousand incidents
sessions.a: After years of investigating incidents - both within AWS and across customer industries - some resilience lessons stand out. Not the obvious ones, but surprises no runbook could anticipate. We share the strangest, most counterintuitive findings from years of troubleshooting under pressure: failure modes nobody planned for, fixes that made things worse, and patterns that only emerge after enough failures. This isn't a best-practices talk - it's a field guide to building resilience from the unexpected. You'll leave with a sharper eye for hidden risks in your infrastructure - and fresh leads on things you didn't know were there.

sessions.t: Unified Commerce Intelligence for Amazon Sellers on Amazon Quick
sessions.a: Brands selling on Amazon generate rich signals across commerce and advertising — order trends, catalog performance, competitive pricing, campaign metrics, and customer engagement. The opportunity lies in connecting these signals into a unified view that drives faster, smarter decisions. In this chalk talk, we design an architecture that composes two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers — the SP-API MCP Server for Selling Partner operations and the Amazon Ads MCP Server for campaigns and reporting — behind Amazon Qucik as a conversational layer. We'll whiteboard how brands can build cross-domain queries, like correlating ad spend with order velocity or surfacing catalog insights that inform campaign strategy. Leave with production-grade patterns for building agentic commerce workflows tailored to your brand's data

sessions.t: Unified observability with Amazon OpenSearch Service
sessions.a: Most teams run observability across fragmented tools: one for metrics, another for logs and traces, each with its own cost model and blind spots. In this session, you work hands-on to consolidate your observability stack on Amazon OpenSearch Service. You integrate Amazon Managed Prometheus for metrics, configure native OpenTelemetry ingestion for traces and logs, and see how a single pane of glass eliminates the context-switching that slows down investigations. Then you optimize for cost and scale: warm tiering, direct query for infrequently accessed data, and O-series instances for log-heavy workloads. Finally, you use AI-powered investigation to perform natural-language root-cause analysis across your unified telemetry and monitor your agents' behavior in production. You leave with a working observability setup that scales, costs less, and investigates faster.

sessions.t: Unifying fragmented data: A lakehouse for the agentic AI era
sessions.a: Financial services organizations face growing data volumes, strict regulations, and architectures where siloed warehouses and separate data lakes fragment data, drive up costs, and slow insights. In this chalk talk, we walk through a modern Lakehouse architecture on AWS that combines the cost benefits of data lakes with the governance and performance of data warehouses. We explain how Amazon S3 Tables with managed Apache Iceberg and AWS Glue Catalog semantic search deliver a single governed data foundation supporting agentic AI, traditional AI/ML, and analytics workloads. Learn practical patterns for a scalable Lakehouse you can apply immediately.

sessions.t: Unit 42: Defending Against Real World Frontier AI Threats (sponsored by Palo Alto Networks)
sessions.a: Frontier AI is transforming cyber threats, acting as a force multiplier across the kill chain. Adversaries leverage AI to scale social engineering, accelerate vulnerability discovery, and iterate malicious code. In this 20-minute lightning session, Unit 42 shares practical insights into the evolving AI threat landscape. We will highlight Palo Alto Networks’ approach to securing the frontier by combining AI-powered Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW) to stop advanced attacks with identity-centric controls for prevention. Attendees will learn how threat intelligence and proactive defense work together to outpace machine scale adversaries. This presentation is brought to you by Palo Alto Networks, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Unlock cost efficiency with Graviton savings tools
sessions.a: While AWS Graviton delivers up to 40% better price-performance, uncovering those savings across your fleet shouldn't take weeks of manual analysis. Building a concrete migration plan for a specific environment is where teams get stuck. The Graviton Savings Dashboard is an Amazon Quick visualization of your Graviton usage, realized savings, and migration opportunities over time. The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill that any AI coding agent can run against your accounts to produce a prioritized migration roadmap on demand. This lightning talk demonstrates both tools against a real-world scenario, showing how to analyze compute usage, visualize potential savings, and turn efficiency insights into actionable migration plans you can use to accelerate your Graviton adoption.

sessions.t: Unlocking SAP Data with AI: From Zero-ETL to Agentic Automation
sessions.a: Critical business data remains locked inside SAP ERP and BW systems, limiting real-time insights and AI-driven automation. In this hands-on workshop, learn how to break down data silos using a modern, cost-effective architecture without expensive ETL pipelines. Explore a unified analytics strategy spanning Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS-native services that enables end-to-end SAP data modernization. Then, build with the AWS for SAP MCP Server, enabling agentic AI to orchestrate across SAP, Salesforce, and AWS without writing code.

sessions.t: Unlock intelligent AI with MCP-powered agentic Neptune graph reasoning
sessions.a: Graph-based agentic reasoning empowers AI systems to dynamically interact with the rich context and relationships in an Amazon Neptune graph, enabling intelligent, flexible, and scalable AI solutions that extract valuable insights from complex, interconnected data. In this session, build a generative AI application for investment analysis spanning the full lifecycle, from raw unstructured data to autonomous AI agents, by combining Neptune, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Construct autonomous AI workflows that extract entities and relationships from raw EDGAR data, build a domain knowledge graph, surface actionable insights from graph relationships, and build an agent to find investment analysis trends. Bring your laptop to participate.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Unlock Secure Vibe Coding on AWS Today (sponsored by Superblocks)
sessions.a: Your business teams already build apps with AI, often on real company data. Most of those apps never make it to production. The rest run without guardrails, and IT can't see who built what or what data it touches. Blocking the tools doesn't stop the building. This session lays out a third option: a reference blueprint for governed vibe coding in your own AWS account. Learn how to set guardrails once for every AI-built app, catch vulnerable code before it ships, keep a full audit trail, and make sure every app still has an owner when its builder leaves. This presentation is brought to you by Superblocks, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Unlock your Graviton savings potential using AI and analytics tools
sessions.a: How much can you save by migrating to Graviton? In this builder session, explore a real-world scenario and uncover two ways to answer that question. The Graviton Savings Dashboard is an Amazon Quick visualization of your Graviton usage, realized savings, and migration opportunities. The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill any AI coding agent can run to produce a prioritized migration roadmap on demand. Deploy both hands-on, identify migration candidates, and see how quickly cost data becomes a migration strategy. Walk away with actionable insights and a deployment kit.

The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill any AI coding agent can run to produce a prioritized migration roadmap on demand. sessions.t: Unlock your S3 data for AI agents
sessions.a: You’ve built a rich data lake in Amazon S3. Now how do your AI agents actually find and use that data? In this chalk talk, explore patterns for connecting AI agents to S3 resources, including S3 Tables, S3 Metadata, and annotations, with real-time, governed access. Learn how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit for AWS help agents discover and operate on your data, how the AWS Context knowledge graph surfaces relationships agents can reason over, and how curated skills handle common data lake and analytics workflows. Bring your questions as we discuss permission boundaries and practical integration patterns.

sessions.t: Unlock your S3 data for AI agents
sessions.a: You’ve built a rich data lake in Amazon S3. Now how do your AI agents actually find and use that data? In this chalk talk, explore patterns for connecting AI agents to S3 resources, including S3 Tables, S3 Metadata, and annotations, with real-time, governed access. Learn how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit for AWS help agents discover and operate on your data, how the AWS Context knowledge graph surfaces relationships agents can reason over, and how curated skills handle common data lake and analytics workflows. Bring your questions as we discuss permission boundaries and practical integration patterns.

sessions.t: Use AWS Continuum to move from annual pentesting to continuous security
sessions.a: AI coding tools can make developers 10–20x more productive and yet many organizations may only be able to pentest critical apps once a year. The rest need to go untested entirely. In this builders' session, use AWS Security Agent (now part of Continuum) to run an on-demand penetration test against a live application. You'll triage findings by exploitability, validate real-world impact, and apply automated code remediations. Leave with prescriptive next steps to scan your own applications using a frontier AI agent that secures workloads from design through deployment. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Using AI for Impact: Achieving Sustainability and ROI on AWS
sessions.a: AI is accelerating sustainability at unprecedented speed, but only if the infrastructure behind it keeps pace. Learn how customers leverage AI for autonomous building control, emission factor mapping, supply chain carbon accounting, disclosure drafting, and transforming procurement data into sustainability intelligence using natural language. Then explore how AWS makes AI infrastructure more sustainable through hardware design decisions that minimize embodied carbon, custom silicon optimized for energy efficiency, and ML-driven data center optimization. Leave with a clear understanding of the AWS services powering these solutions, how AWS is building a more sustainable infrastructure, and how to get started.

sessions.t: Using AI to scale legacy app modernization with Experian & Itaú
sessions.a: A successful modernization approach only matters if it scales beyond the first pilot. Experian and Itaú share how they grew their approach with AWS Transform and Kiro from a single engagement into an enterprise-wide operating model. Experian compresses mainframe analysis from months to days, then standardizes modernization across 550+ workloads and multiple regions with a fully agentic reverse-engineering pipeline. Itaú expanded to 43 business domains, processing nearly 140 million lines of code in a single month. Leave with the operating models that scale modernization from one application to the entire portfolio, unlocking AI-driven capabilities along the way.

sessions.t: Validate your hands-on AWS skills & earn a Microcredential
sessions.a: In this session, you will be given time to attempt a microcredential exam of your choice on AWS Skill Builder. These timed, hands-on exams test your skills in a live, provisioned AWS environment and test on popular topics. The product and developer team will be onsite to walk you through the UI and introduce the exam. Please note - this is an individual exam, and you will not be provided any hints or guidance outside of what is provided in the typical test environment. This exam is free to take on AWS Skill Builder. Attendees are required to bring their own device to complete the exam. Those who pass will be issued a microcredential badge on Credly.

sessions.t: Vector search, agents, and image matching with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.a: Amazon DynamoDB supports native vector search, enabling semantic queries, agentic recommendations, and image-based matching without additional infrastructure. In this session, explore how to design a single-table data model for a recipe database, bulk-load thousands of items with embeddings, and build three vector-powered features: semantic search, a smart recommendation agent, and image-based meal matching. Learn how to configure vector indexes, composite keys, and global secondary indexes on a fully serverless stack, and leave with reusable patterns to add vector search to your own DynamoDB workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Verifying Post-Quantum Cryptography at Speed
sessions.a: Traditionally, cryptographic engineering involves a performance/assurance trade-off: clean code is easy to audit and maintain, yet slow; handwritten assembly is fast, yet hard to validate. Discover how automated reasoning helps to overcome this tension, following the example of mlkem-native and mldsa-native, two open-source post-quantum cryptography libraries co-maintained by AWS and deployed in AWS-LC, Amazon's cryptography library. In these libraries, constraint solving enables automated superoptimization at the assembly level, while formal verification vets the result. Contrary to the popular belief that assurance costs speed, it is automated reasoning that enables deep optimization, verification and rapid deployment of cryptographic code at cloud scale.

sessions.t: Vertiv’s Amazon Quick Journey: Scaling Agentic AI Globally with Deloitte & AWS (sponsored by Deloitte)
sessions.a: Vertiv, a global digital infrastructure company, faced fragmented AI experimentation, limited accessibility, and complex enterprise integrational barriers preventing consistent scaling. Vertiv's AI journey began with VeGA, a GenAI platform turned agentic with their recent release of VeGA 3.0. Powered by Amazon Quick, it enables employees to generate content, automate workflows, and create custom applications. In one year, nearly one-third of the workforce was registered in VeGA, spanning functions across all functions and regions. Attendees will learn the architectural blueprint for evolving from basic AI assistants to intelligent agentic systems, including connectors used, data streamlining strategies, and practical implementation steps. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Virtualization Architecture Behind AgentCore's Runtime Security Model
sessions.a: Journey into the sophisticated virtualization architecture that powers AgentCore's runtime security model. This session examines the intricate mechanics of session isolation at the virtualization layer, exploring advanced techniques in compute and memory virtualization, virtual machine snapshot optimization, and virtual memory deduplication. Drawing from operating systems research and systems security principles, we'll demonstrate how these components work together to create robust security boundaries for agent workloads. Attendees will gain deep technical insights into the mathematical and systems-level concepts that position AWS at the forefront of secure agent runtime architectures, showcasing our industry-leading approach to securing code execution in agent environments.

sessions.t: Visualize and interpret domain knowledge graphs using AI
sessions.a: Complex systems like supply chains, energy grids, and decarbonization efforts are difficult to model because relationships between actors are hidden across siloed data. A knowledge graph can surface these connections, helping organizations simulate what-if scenarios and act on high impact opportunities. In this builder session, use Amazon Neptune to construct an ontology-typed knowledge graph that maps stakeholder dependencies and sustainability regulatory impacts. Then simulate competing interventions and use an Amazon Bedrock agent to interpret which action drives the broadest impact. Leave with a reusable pattern for modeling complex systems and identifying high-leverage intervention points.

sessions.t: Visualizing agent identity privileges to monitor multi-agent behavior
sessions.a: If one of your AI agents quietly gained admin-level access right now, would you know? In multi-agent systems, each handoff between agents can widen permissions, and traditional monitoring won't catch it. In this code talk, we build a real-time graph answering three questions: who are my agents, what can each one do, and what can they reach through each other? We connect IAM roles, Cedar policies, and CloudWatch data into one visual map, then add alerts that fire the instant any permission chain exceeds what you defined. You leave with the tool that catches it first.

sessions.t: Visualizing multi-tenant isolation: Catch your noisy neighbors
sessions.a: Managing multi-tenant platforms forces trade-offs between cost, complexity, and performance. This session tackles two common challenges: tenant data isolation and the noisy-neighbor problem. Starting from a single-tenant architecture, you consolidate into a shared Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster, building isolation through Cognito-issued JWTs, Lambda-based dynamic policy generation, IAM authentication, and RDS Proxy connection pooling. Then you implement queuing tiers with Amazon SQS to manage load. Visualize real-time request flows, data isolation, and noisy-neighbor effects on your own dynamic architecture simulation and a central 16,000-LED display. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts with AWS Transform
sessions.a: Many organizations struggle to migrate VMware workloads due to complex dependencies, network translation challenges, and the need to support both cloud and on-premises targets. In this workshop, attendees use AWS Transform MGN, an agentic AI service, to execute an end-to-end VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts. Participants work through AI-driven discovery, dependency mapping, intelligent wave planning, automated network conversion, and orchestrated execution. Attendees also experience how Trianz's Concierto platform integrates with AWS Transform to streamline migration to AWS Outposts with automated orchestration and operational governance. Leave with hands-on skills to accelerate your VMware migration projects.

sessions.t: Warehouse Alchemy: How Eni's AI agents cut days of sourcing to minutes
sessions.a: Eni operates one of the world's most complex upstream supply chains, managing exploration and production materials across warehouses on multiple continents. Tubular items alone represent €1.5 billion out of a €2.5 billion inventory — scattered across dozens of facilities with fragmented visibility. Engineers searching for available spare parts faced a manual, days-long process of cross-referencing spreadsheets, navigating import restrictions, certifications, third-party stock, and delivery schedules — often resulting in unnecessary new purchases while surplus materials sat idle in distant warehouses. With Eni's expansion into fast-track development, biofuel production, and CCUS, the traditional material management approach couldn't keep pace with the speed and complexity of global operations.

sessions.t: Watch AWS Transform convert SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL live
sessions.a: Modernizing SQL Server and its dependent .NET applications to Aurora PostgreSQL typically requires months of manual effort across schema conversion, stored procedure rewriting, and application code changes. In this code talk, see how AWS Transform uses agentic AI to automate this journey end-to-end. Through a live walkthrough, we'll showcase complex schema transformations, T-SQL to PL/pgSQL stored procedure conversions, Entity Framework provider updates, and wave-based orchestration of multi-database estates with human-in-the-loop validation checkpoints. Ask questions throughout. Leave with patterns for modernizing SQL Server at scale.

sessions.t: Web grounding on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: Learn about the ways in which customers can ground their AI applications in current web information with Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

sessions.t: Well-Architected in your AI coding agent: Find gaps before you commit
sessions.a: Architecture reviews happen at milestones: a design review here, an operational readiness check there. But AI coding agents make architectural decisions dozens of times a day, and governance that runs at milestone pace can't keep up. In this session, you will configure open-source Well-Architected skills in your coding agent, run a full Well-Architected review and catch resilience, security, and operational gaps in minutes. Then author a custom skill that encodes your team's standards and trade-offs. You leave with a review loop that runs every commit. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: What Breaks First: Detection Engineering Lessons at AWS Scale (sponsored by Datadog)
sessions.a: Tighten the detection rule and you miss the variant. Loosen them and you drown the on-call. Deviate too far either way and you risk missing attackers and getting compromised. FanDuel handled adjustments by hand for years, until attackers started moving faster than the tuning backlog. Join FanDuel and Datadog to see detection rebuilt around automation: SIEM logic as code, orchestrated enrichment and triage, vulnerability workflows in the same pipeline. Attendees will leave with practical patterns for scaling detection engineering, reducing analyst toil, and knowing where AI helps and where it creates new work. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: What Building an SRE Agent Taught Us About Agents at Scale
sessions.a: Anyone can wire up an agent, but operating one safely and cheaply across thousands of sessions is where developer craft begins. Grounded in a production SRE agent we built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK, this session dissects engineering around agentic models: session isolation, context management, and least privilege identity. What broke, and how we fixed it: an agent with too much access, context bloat that wrecked cost, a crash during a tool call that forced durable recovery. You will see where architectures leak, how to evaluate on production traces, and tradeoffs behind resilient agent infrastructure.

sessions.t: What Can Neurosymbolic AI Prove About Agent Behavior?
sessions.a: AI agents that write and execute code autonomously create a fundamental trust problem: how do you guarantee behavioral boundaries without constraining the flexibility that makes agents useful? This chalk talk examines how neurosymbolic AI is making provable guarantees practical at scale: autoformalization translating natural-language constraints into temporal logic, satisfiability solvers whose exponential improvement keeps pace with exponentially harder verification problems, and LLMs guiding proof search in theorem provers like Lean, creating a virtuous cycle where better proofs yield stronger provers. We'll stratify what can be proved today, what requires LLM-discovered inductive invariants, and where undecidability still draws a hard line.

sessions.t: What happens in Bedrock stays in Bedrock
sessions.a: You want to ship AI, but your compliance team won't sign off until the solution meets their regulatory requirements. This session shows how Bedrock protects data from the hardware up, with zero operator access enforced at the chip so no one, not even AWS operators, can access your prompts and completions. See how data residency controls and strict workload separation extend that protection, and how those guarantees map to the compliance frameworks your teams already use. You leave ready to have the conversation that gets your AI workload approved.

sessions.t: What Observability at the Speed of AI Looks Like (sponsored by groundcover)
sessions.a: For a company like Polymarket, moving fast isn’t a nice-to-have. It’s a requirement. Failing to scale quickly enough can stall unprecedented momentum, while compromising its PII and security posture can carry even greater risk. Built on AWS, this session explores how Polymarket uses groundcover to shift infrastructure responsibilities to AI agents, build agentic development loops, maintain full data residency, and gain instant visibility into every change, no matter how quickly production evolves. We’ll also share the immediate impact: at least 50% lower MTTR for infrastructure escalations and an approximately 7% reduction in Polymarket’s AWS bill. This presentation is brought to you by groundcover, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: What's new and what's next for Amazon ECS
sessions.a: Amazon ECS keeps getting simpler to run and more capable at scale, and this session provides a product and engineering leadership view of where it is headed next. See how recent investments make ECS faster to deploy applications on, more cost-efficient, and ready for a new class of AI and agentic workloads. We'll discuss the range of compute options, from Fargate to Amazon ECS Managed Instances and how they provide customers choice and flexibility. You will leave this session knowing how to apply the newest ECS capabilities to your workloads today, and what to plan for as the roadmap unfolds.

sessions.t: What's new in Amazon Bedrock
sessions.a: AI moves fast: new models, new economics, and new governance capabilities. Attend this breakout to learn about the latest innovations across Amazon Bedrock. We cover recent model additions from OpenAI, Anthropic, and more, along with advances in inference and updates across security, governance, and cost management. Whether you are new to Bedrock or want to keep up with the latest releases, this session offers something for everyone. Leave knowing what is available today and where to focus next.

sessions.t: What's new in Amazon Redshift
sessions.a: Cut costs, query faster, and unify your warehouse and data lake without trade-offs. In this session, learn how new Graviton-powered RG instances deliver better price-performance, a built-in data lake engine lets you read and write Apache Iceberg tables in place, multi-warehouse architecture gives teams independent scale with shared data, and Redshift Serverless improvements let you get insights on your data without managing infrastructure. Whether you're consolidating on open table formats or building the analytics backbone for AI agents, walk away knowing exactly how to put these capabilities to work.

sessions.t: What's new in Amazon Route 53: DNS innovations for 2026
sessions.a: Explore the latest innovations in Amazon Route 53, AWS's fully managed DNS service. This session covers 2026 launches including Route 53 Global Resolver for secure anycast DNS resolution from anywhere without VPNs, DNS Views sharing across accounts, and expanded DNS Firewall threat protection through partnerships. In this session, we also cover Profiles enhancements for simplified multi-VPC DNS management with granular IAM controls, and expanded domain registration support. Learn how these capabilities help you secure DNS resolution, simplify hybrid and multi-account architectures, and strengthen your DNS security posture at scale.

sessions.t: What's new in Amazon SageMaker platform
sessions.a: Amazon SageMaker platform is where data engineering, analytics, and AI come together. In this session, see what's new across the platform including innovations in lakehouse architecture that eliminates silos between data teams and AI teams, catalog capabilities for data discovery and governance, and streamlined development experiences that get you from raw data to production models faster. Whether you are building pipelines, running SQL analytics, or training models, learn how SageMaker platform delivers enterprise-grade governance with the flexibility to work the way your team needs.

sessions.t: What's new in Application Security: Securing applications at machine speed
sessions.a: AI is accelerating your release cadence. AWS application security capabilities help engineering teams ship secure applications faster, including AI-powered workloads. In this session, learn how AI-driven services enforce organizational guardrails before code is written, perform threat modeling, review code for vulnerabilities, generate fixes automatically, and enable on-demand penetration testing. See how to codify these into paved pathways that give developers room to build with AI while maintaining consistent security standards. Leave with a clear plan for embedding AWS application security into your platform, from design through continuous validation.

sessions.t: What's new in AWS Data Processing
sessions.a: Explore the latest advancements in AWS Analytics designed to transform your data processing landscape. This session unveils powerful new capabilities across key services, including Amazon EMR for scalable big data processing, AWS Glue for seamless data integration, Amazon Athena for optimized querying, and Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA) for complex workflow orchestration. Discover how these innovations can supercharge performance, optimize costs, and streamline your entire data ecosystem. Whether you're looking to enhance scalability, improve data integration, accelerate queries, or refine workflow management, join us to gain actionable insights that will position your organization at the forefront of data processing innovation.

sessions.t: What's new in AWS Serverless
sessions.a: The serverless landscape moves fast, and the months leading up to re:Invent bring a wave of new capabilities for building event-driven applications. This hands-on workshop is your chance to explore the latest releases the moment they land. Build with the newest serverless features, work through the technical trade-offs that matter in real systems, and leave with production-ready patterns you can apply the moment you're back at your desk. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: What's new in AWS Serverless
sessions.a: The serverless landscape moves fast, and the months leading up to re:Invent bring a wave of new capabilities for building event-driven applications. This hands-on workshop is your chance to explore the latest releases the moment they land. Build with the newest serverless features, work through the technical trade-offs that matter in real systems, and leave with production-ready patterns you can apply the moment you're back at your desk. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: What's new in full-stack AWS app development
sessions.a: Web developers are under pressure to deliver differentiating experiences to more users, faster than ever. Building secure, reliable, scalable applications at 10x speed takes solutions that let developers start easily, ship quickly, and iterate without friction. In this breakout, we'll share how AWS is evolving to meet the needs of modern full-stack developers from defining backends in code and connecting real-time data, to deploying and scaling globally with minimal overhead. Join us to see what's new and where full-stack development on AWS is headed.

sessions.t: What's new with Amazon API Gateway
sessions.a: Your next API consumer might not be a person. AI agents, MCP servers, and coding assistants are calling APIs programmatically, and they need machine-readable schemas, predictable error contracts, and discoverable endpoints. In this session, we cover what's new with Amazon API Gateway: recent launches, direct service integrations that eliminate Lambda glue code, declarative event wiring, and patterns from real customer deployments. We also discuss how to design APIs that serve both human developers and autonomous agents without maintaining separate interfaces.

sessions.t: What's new with OpenSearch: AI-native search, agents & observability
sessions.a: "The OpenSearch project has shipped its most transformative year ever. From agentic search with autonomous relevance tuning and persistent memory, to GPU-accelerated vector search with 58% throughput gains, to a reimagined observability stack with Prometheus and Apache Iceberg support, the 3.x release train delivers capabilities builders can use today. OpenSearch Ambassador Dotan Horovits and TSC Chair Andrew Ross walk you through what's new, what it means for your architecture, and how to put it to work, whether you're building RAG pipelines, deploying monitoring, or creating AI agents."

sessions.t: What's new with the AWS Sustainability service
sessions.a: If you've ever wanted to know more about the environmental impact of your cloud usage, this session is for you. In this lightning talk, learn about the latest features of the AWS Sustainability service, including expanded impact areas beyond carbon, increased data granularity, and programmatic access via APIs. We walk through how to use the service to track progress against your sustainability goals and integrate environmental data into your existing workflows and reporting processes. Whether you're just getting started or already reporting on cloud emissions, this session has you covered.

sessions.t: What SOA taught us about building agents in production
sessions.a: You’ve taken AI agents from prototype to production, and now you own the hard parts: orchestration sprawl, brittle integrations, and behavior hard to test or observe. The patterns that hold up in production look a lot like ones SOA builders already know. This session explores what emerged: multi-agent orchestration mirroring service meshes, tool-use protocols (MCP) formalizing what APIs did for services, evaluation frameworks echoing contract testing, and hard-won lessons about agent observability and trust boundaries. You leave with concrete patterns from the SOA playbook, updated for the agentic era.

sessions.t: What to do next after your cloud migration
sessions.a: Rehosting gets workloads to AWS, but that's just the beginning. This session covers the first 90 days after cutover: stabilizing the environment, building observability so decisions are based on real utilization data instead of pre-migration assumptions, applying auto-scaling and right-sizing adjustments that accelerate ROI, and knowing when a workload is ready to modernize versus when to leave it alone. AWS specialists share the decisions and strategy to turn your freshly migrated environment into one worth the investment.

sessions.t: When agentic AI meets critical infrastructure (sponsored by IBM)
sessions.a: Agentic AI can transform how utilities serve customers, manage infrastructure and respond to operational events. Join IBM Consulting and industry leaders to see how organizations are putting agentic AI to work on AWS across complex operational workflows. Through real client stories, explore how modern platforms, trusted data and secure software foundations help teams improve service, strengthen resilience and move AI into production with confidence. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: When agents disagree: Resolving competing goals in cloud operations
sessions.a: When two agents manage the same workload, each optimizing a different objective, conflicting actions are the default, not the exception. A consensus layer changes the pattern: pillar-aligned agents carry workload goals and live signals as context, reason toward agreement, and produce a single decision playbook before any action executes. In this session, you build one pillar agent from scratch, configure its context layer, connect it to the consensus flow, and watch shared context resolve a live disagreement without rules or priority overrides. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: When agents run code: sandboxes for reliable DevOps
sessions.a: LLMs hallucinate. Code doesn't. When your AI agent investigates a production incident, some answers demand computation, not just reasoning. In this code talk, we crack open the sandbox in AWS DevOps Agent: an ephemeral, investigation-scoped Linux environment where the agent writes and runs code inside a Lambda MicroVM with read-only AWS access and zero lateral blast radius. We'll discuss how networking allowlists, pre-installed packages, and executable skills give you deterministic, auditable results for log parsing, metric correlation, and multi-source analysis. Bring your problems and we'll whiteboard the isolation boundaries live.

sessions.t: When AI agents make high-stakes decisions: Build governance on AWS
sessions.a: When AI agents approve aid applications, triage patients, or allocate resources, failure isn't a bug — it's a harm. In this workshop, build a production governance layer for high-stakes agentic workflows using AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock, and AgentCore. Implement human approval gates that don't kill velocity, audit trails that satisfy regulators, cost budgets with automatic circuit-breakers, and guardrails for consistent enforcement of policies. Test your governance stack against adversarial scenarios. Leave with a deployable framework applicable anywhere AI decisions affect people — social services, healthcare, finance, or government.

sessions.t: When AI agents make high-stakes decisions: Build governance on AWS
sessions.a: When AI agents approve aid applications, triage patients, or allocate resources, failure isn't a bug — it's a harm. In this workshop, build a production governance layer for high-stakes agentic workflows using AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock, and AgentCore. Implement human approval gates that don't kill velocity, audit trails that satisfy regulators, cost budgets with automatic circuit-breakers, and guardrails for consistent enforcement of policies. Test your governance stack against adversarial scenarios. Leave with a deployable framework applicable anywhere AI decisions affect people — social services, healthcare, finance, or government.

sessions.t: When AI Moves Money: Secure the Agentic Future of Financial Services (sponsored by TrendAI™)
sessions.a: Organizations are racing to adopt AI, but many struggle to balance innovation, governance, and security. In this session, learn how Discover how technology leaders are enabling AI innovation while reducing operational risk and complexity. enterprises are using TrendAI Vision One on AWS to accelerate AI initiatives, gain visibility across complex cloud environments, and reduce operational risk without slowing the business. Discover real-world deployment patterns, lessons learned, and the architectural principles that help security teams move from reactive defense to proactive risk management while enabling AI at scale. Built on AWS-native services and integrated across the cloud ecosystem, this approach helps organizations simplify operations, improve threat detection, and confidently embrace the next wave of transformation. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: When Guardrails Break: Defense in Depth for Non-Deterministic AI (sponsored by Darktrace)
sessions.a: Organizations are deploying copilots, AI agents, and LLM-driven workflows faster than governance and security can adapt. Non-deterministic AI creates a new attack surface across prompts, agents, data, and runtime behavior, and acts as both defensive force multiplier and adversarial accelerant. Static guardrails are necessary but insufficient: they miss novel behavior, unsafe tool use, and risk that only surfaces when AI interacts with identities and downstream systems. This session presents a defense-in-depth model for securing AI at runtime, using NIST's Secure/Defend/Thwart framing: an identity control plane for agents, least-privilege and JIT access, runtime observability, behavior detection, and autonomous investigation and containment. We'll share a blueprint for a minimum viable AI security baseline, and why behavioral oversight is the decisive layer for securing AI at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Darktrace, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: When one tenant spikes 100x, your architecture decides who pays
sessions.a: One tenant spikes 100x. The architecture either isolates the blast radius or turns it into every tenant's outage. Multi-tenant platforms face four decisions at this boundary. Where to place isolation so one workload cannot starve another. How fan-out creates backpressure that propagates upstream. When fair queuing replaces custom throttling code. What qualifies as real-time versus safely queueable. In this chalk talk you decide where your isolation boundaries belong and what trade-offs each placement creates. Bring your own scaling problem. We draw the architecture together.

sessions.t: When security, speed, and trust all matter: Lessons from Project Glasswing
sessions.a: In 2026, a frontier AI model demonstrated it could discover and chain software exploits at machine speed. This new reality forced the industry to confront an entirely new class of offensive capability. In this session, learn how AWS Security's Office of the CISO engaged executive customers and partners to build playbooks to help assess AI-era vulnerability management and remediation. We share the lessons implemented with customers, the internal changes AWS made to operate as a more secure AI-first organization, and practical steps every security team can take now.

sessions.t: When Software Builds and Improves Itself (sponsored by Factory)
sessions.a: Software is becoming more than something companies build. It is becoming the system through which they improve. The next generation of software factories will turn business signals into production software, measure the outcomes, and use those outcomes to improve each cycle of development. Engineers set the goals, architecture, policies, and approval gates, while the system handles execution and continuously improves itself. Factory cofounder Eno Reyes will share what this future looks like, what has to be true to build it, and why self-improving software will fundamentally change how every company operates. This presentation is brought to you by Factory, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: When tags run out: cost allocation for AI and multi-tenant workloads (sponsored by DoiT)
sessions.a: Tag-based allocation works until the resource stops belonging to anyone. A multi-tenant EKS cluster, a shared inference endpoint, a queue five services write to: each lands on the bill once, charged to whoever provisioned it. No amount of tagging discipline fixes that, because there is nothing to tag. This session covers where tag coverage structurally breaks down, and the alternative: measuring the running system to attribute shared spend to the team, feature, and customer that caused it, then reconciling back to the bill so the allocation still foots. Includes what this looks like in production on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by DoiT, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Where do agents fit? A capability-first approach to agentic AI
sessions.a: Not every workflow needs an agent, and applying agentic AI where it doesn’t fit adds nondeterminism, cost, and failure modes a deterministic design would have avoided. This chalk talk introduces a capability-first methodology for architects and engineering leaders evaluating agentic paths in their workflows, manual or software-driven. We’ll ideate on a scoring framework that assesses the inherent nature of the work to reveal where agentic approaches thrive. You’ll apply the PERCEIVE-REASON-ACT pattern for isolating AI reasoning from orchestration, and walk away with a repeatable rubric your teams can adopt immediately.

sessions.t: Where embeddings live: Designing production retrieval on AWS
sessions.a: Where should vector embeddings live? In your operational database, a dedicated vector store, or across several? In this session you evaluate the trade-offs across latency, data freshness, cost, and retrieval quality. You implement the same retrieval pattern across three engines: Amazon OpenSearch Service for combined lexical and vector search, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector for SQL-native filtered retrieval, and Amazon S3 Vectors for cost-optimized scale. You then combine them into a hybrid architecture that orchestrates a single query and merges the results with reciprocal rank fusion. You leave able to answer where your embeddings should live, backed by patterns you built yourself. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.t: Where's the slowdown? Build observability from frontend to databases
sessions.a: When an application slows down, the cause can hide anywhere from the frontend to the database, and siloed tools make teams guess. In this workshop, you will build full-stack observability across application, infrastructure, and database layers, bringing RDS and Aurora signals and database logs into one store and correlating them with audit activity. You decide what to trace and build the dashboards that connect a symptom to its root cause. Leave with skills to trace any slowdown across layers in a single pane.

sessions.t: Where's the slowdown? Build observability from frontend to databases

sessions.t: Which customization path? A decision framework for fine-tuning on AWS
sessions.a: Off the shelf models work for prototyping, but production forces a choice, which technique, which service, which tradeoffs. In this chalk talk, we work through the decision framework live. When Supervised Fine Tuning is enough, when DPO or RLAIF earns its added cost, and when RLVR or multi-turn RL is the right call, and what data each demands. We will learn how to choose across SageMaker Serverless Customization, Training Jobs, HyperPod, and Bedrock Custom Model Import based on traffic, budget, and control needs. Bring a real use case and we'll place it on the map.

sessions.t: Who’s Pulling the Strings? Securing GitHub from Rogue AI Agents (sponsored by Zscaler)
sessions.a: With the rise of autonomous AI agents like Devin, Cursor, and Amazon Q, the security boundary has shifted from the network perimeter directly to the developer's workspace. These AI tools and automated integration pipelines establish dynamic, encrypted connections straight to GitHub, third-party repositories, and cloud workloads—creating blind spots that legacy firewalls cannot see. Join us as we map out this highly interconnected AI developer ecosystem and showcase why traditional security fails. We will share a unified, proxy-based Zero Trust architecture that inspects encrypted developer traffic, secures access to critical repositories, and isolates untrusted AI actions. You’ll leave with an actionable blueprint to protect your code, APIs, and AI integrations while maintaining peak developer velocity. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Who's Your Security MVP? Here's How AI Ranks Them (sponsored by Trellix)
sessions.a: Yeah, yeah, AI SOC, we get it. But what really goes into getting wins out of AI in security vs saving a couple of clicks? This talk will show the importance of small (dumb) LLM's and how they create opportunities for secops by allowing you to use more tokens, anywhere you want. It will demo how you can go beyond enriching a few alerts to stack rank your most valuable security tools in an ROI thunderdome. You'll learn the AI confidence guardrail framework you need so you to actually start taking actions on your behalf without accidentally deleting all your VM's when you asked it to "eliminate all vulnerabilities." Seeing is believing, so there will be real-world demos of where AI works, where it doesn't, and why--bring your 3D glasses. This presentation is brought to you by Trellix, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Why Enterprise RAG Fails: Document AI and  Ontology Patterns on AWS
sessions.a: Most teams blame embeddings, vector databases, or foundation models when RAG systems underperform. In practice, failures often originate earlier in the pipeline where business meaning is lost during document ingestion. This session explores production Document AI patterns on AWS, including layout-aware extraction, ontology-driven classification, semantic chunking, metadata enrichment, and retrieval optimization. Using financial services examples, we demonstrate how domain ontologies improve extraction accuracy, retrieval relevance, and explainability. Attendees will learn practical architecture patterns, implementation tradeoffs, and a framework for building scalable, trustworthy RAG systems for enterprise workloads.

sessions.t: Why Multi-Agent Systems Fail in Production (And How to Fix It) (sponsored by MongoDB)
sessions.a: Most AI agents don't fall apart in production because the model isn't smart enough. They fail because state is fragmented: one agent can't see what another already learned, and nobody can reconstruct what was retrieved, decided, or handed off. In a multi-tenant setting, that's a governance problem, not just a debugging one. This session shows an architecture that fixes it by giving every layer a clear job: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore manages session context and end-to-end tracing, MongoDB Atlas handles durable memory, tenant-aware vector search, and audit history, and the MongoDB MCP Server connects the two so access stays governed. You'll watch agents share state, retrieve tenant-scoped data, and leave a replayable decision trail. Leave with a reference architecture for multi-agent state sharing and a model for what audit-ready really looks like. A MongoDB & AWS technical session. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Winning the DDoS Game: defend your app under real-time attack
sessions.a: Compete in a team-based environment where you face real-time threats aimed at your web application. Use the latest capabilities in AWS WAF and AWS Shield to mitigate HTTP floods, web exploits, and malicious bots that disrupt your customers. This risk-free event puts teamwork to the test as you work under pressure. Watch a real-time scoreboard as your team works through each level. Whether it's volumetric attacks or the new wave of AI-driven traffic hitting your APIs, you'll leave prepared to defend against what's coming next. The most effective team earns a prize!

sessions.t: Winning the War on Fraud with Network-Powered Intelligence (sponsored by Vonage, Part of Ericsson)
sessions.a: Fraud is winning. SIM swaps have surged over 1,000%; synthetic identity cases are up 60% year-over-year, legacy OTP defenses are structurally broken — and fraudsters know it. Every industry feels it. Banks, healthcare providers, retailers, rideshare and delivery platforms, all fighting the same battle, all demanding the same answer: security that doesn't sacrifice the customer experience. As the first and only communications and Network API provider to achieve the AWS Financial Services Industry Competency, Vonage is changing the equation. Discover how enterprises are moving to a model where identity is verified silently at the network layer, before fraud happens. Built on AWS, powered by direct carrier intelligence. This presentation is brought to you by Vonage, Part of Ericsson, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Woodside's SOC Journey: From Eyes on Glass to Threat Hunting with AWS SIR
sessions.a: Security teams are stretched thin by routine monitoring and alert triage while threats move faster than ever. In this session, hear how a global energy company partnered with AWS Security Incident Response to fundamentally rethink how their SOC delivers value. Learn how they offloaded eyes-on-glass monitoring and incident response operations to AWS, freeing security professionals to focus on proactive threat hunting and higher-value security work. See how integration with existing ITSM workflows enabled seamless adoption, and how the partnership proved its value during a real supply chain attack where the combined approach accelerated detection, containment, and resolution. Whether you lead a SOC or are evaluating how to scale your security operations without scaling headcount, this session provides a blueprint for transforming from reactive monitoring to proactive defense.

sessions.t: Workload Identity Federation in multicloud environments
sessions.a: Eliminating long-lived credentials across clouds is essential for secure multicloud operations. This session presents three proven identity federation patterns: using SPIFFE/SPIRE for cryptographic workload identity across Kubernetes clusters, leveraging native OIDC providers from GKE and Azure to assume AWS IAM roles with short-lived tokens, and federating Kubernetes service accounts across cloud boundaries. We walk through architecture decisions, trust policy design, and security best practices for each approach - covering GCP Workload Identity, Microsoft Entra ID federation, and cross-cluster OIDC. Attendees leave with actionable blueprints for credential-free multicloud access.

sessions.t: World models for indoor robots: what breaks and why
sessions.a: World models promise to give robots predictive understanding of their environment, yet applying them to indoor robotics exposes fundamental gaps in how transformers reason about geometry. In this session, we present findings from building a trajectory-conditioned lidar world model for Diligent Robotics' hospital fleet on AWS. We examine why standard loss metrics fail for generative spatial predictions, why rotation breaks factored attention even with explicit conditioning, and the minimal set of inductive biases needed to restore geometric coherence. Attendees leave with a diagnostic framework for spatial reasoning failures in transformer-based world models.

sessions.t: World Models & Physical AI: The Next Frontier in Intelligent Systems
sessions.a: World models—AI systems that simulate and predict complex environments—are emerging with new modalities including Video, Vision, Language, Action to power physical AI, autonomous systems, and real-time video generation. From humanoid robotics to immersive entertainment, these models are transforming how machines perceive, think, and interact with the physical world. In this panel, hear from researchers and customers on how they're building and deploying world models in production, the business opportunities they unlock, and the unique technical challenges they present. Learn how AWS AI infrastructure powers these use cases at scale with speed, efficiency, and automatic fault recovery.

sessions.t: You cannot write the eval for a failure you have not seen yet (sponsored by Arize AI)
sessions.a: LLM-as-a-judge works beautifully when you already know what you're looking for. You write the rubric, validate it against human labels, and it catches the failure you designed it to catch. But agents in production don't fail the way you anticipated. They fail as they meet new tools, new users, and environments that shifted underneath them, and every new failure arrives after the rubric was written. This talk argues the evaluation layer itself must become agentic. Instead of specifying a metric, you describe the behavior you want, and a judge with tool access inspects the trace, finds the spans that matter, classifies what went wrong, and generates labels you can monitor against. We'll cover why this became viable only recently, where it fails, and how to keep an agentic judge honest against human labels, so you know when to reach for one and how to validate it. This presentation is brought to you by Arize AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Your Agent Has an Upstream Dependency You Can't See (sponsored by Brave)
sessions.a: Verify, don't trust: a reproducible needle test that surfaces undeclared upstream calls in any stack. This presentation is brought to you by Brave, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Your Agent Is in Production. Can You Explain What It Did? (sponsored by Datadog)
sessions.a: Your team shipped an agent to production last quarter. It works, mostly. When it doesn't, nobody can explain why. This session covers what changes when non-deterministic systems enter your stack: which signals actually matter for agentic workloads, how to trace a multi-step agent across tools and models, and where AI agents can safely take action in your own operations. Live examples from Datadog LLM Observability, the Agent Console, AI Guard, and Bits AI. You'll leave with an instrumentation checklist. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Your AI agent gets a budget when Agentic AIOps meets FinOps (sponsored by ManageEngine)
sessions.a: AI agents can now detect, diagnose, and act in seconds. Observability tells them what is happening. The harder question is how they decide. What is an action worth, and what should an agent optimize for? The intersection of Agentic AIOps and FinOps answers both. The result is a blueprint for business-aware autonomous operations, and three practical steps to apply it in your own environment. This presentation is brought to you by ManageEngine, an AWS Partner.

sessions.t: Your data is your AI advantage: From foundation to business value
sessions.a: Your AI is only as good as the data underneath it. Most teams treat data preparation and model serving as separate problems, then wonder why costs spike and quality drops at scale. This chalk talk connects the two. We whiteboard how to design governed data products that feed customization, inference on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and agent workloads on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Then apply cost levers like prompt caching, distillation, and batch inference that compound when built on clean, governed data. You leave with the design decisions that let you scale AI with confidence and control.

sessions.t: Your data, your engine: How open source and open standards power analytics on AWS
sessions.a: Open table formats and open-source engines like DuckDB give organizations the freedom to choose the right tool for each workload, from interactive dashboards and exploratory analytics to large-scale data processing, with no lock-in. In this session, learn how to capitalize these open tools to build on AWS and turn it into a competitive advantage for your business. We deep dive into the application of each engine, how they complement one another across the analytics lifecycle, and how data governance capabilities like catalog access, fine-grained governance, and consistent table management on AWS further simplify multi-engine architectures in production.

sessions.t: Your IPs, your rules: Dynamic edge routing without NAT for AWS BYOIP
sessions.a: Some workloads need the public IP the world sees to live directly on the Amazon EC2 instances—no translation in the path. Email gateways rotating sender IPs, VPN concentrators assigning a dedicated address per client, or security appliances terminating traffic on the exact advertised address need the instance to own those public IPs. In this live-coding talk, we build that model end-to-end on AWS: writing CloudFormation for BYOIP pools and Bring Your Own ASN, coding NAT-free ingress routing so traffic arrives untranslated, and configuring BGP peering with Amazon VPC Route Server for high availability. Walk away with a reusable stack.

sessions.t: Your network, your rules: Global routing policies with AWS Cloud WAN
sessions.a: As global networks scale, they demand deterministic traffic paths—not best-effort routing. In this workshop, gain granular control over traffic flows between Regions, VPCs, and on-premises locations using AWS Cloud WAN routing policies across a multi-Region network. Through hands-on labs, configure route filtering to control reachability, summarize prefixes to reduce routing table complexity, and influence preferred paths with BGP attributes. Leave with practical skills to design scalable, policy-driven connectivity architectures. Bring your laptop.
