sessions.t: Your next Quantum developer might be an AI agent
sessions.a: AI is changing who can build quantum applications. See how AI assistants including Kiro, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Jupyter AI, and Classiq help developers move from natural-language prompts to optimized quantum workloads on Amazon Braket. Learn how AI generates code, synthesizes hardware-aware circuits, benchmarks on simulators and QPUs, and integrates with HPC resources. Through real examples, you'll see how AI-native workflows reduce complexity, accelerate experimentation, and make quantum development accessible to more builders.

sessions.t: Your playbook for modernizing 988K lines of .NET in 2 days
sessions.a: Transaction Network Services (TNS) needed to modernize their Altitude payments platform that included 274 projects, 988K lines of code, and 20 years of legacy .NET Framework to .NET 10. Their estimate: six months. The result: two days, 26 modules migrated, and 34 security vulnerabilities resolved. In this session, you'll learn what made it possible - from upgrading shared libraries first, running deterministic tools before AI, using human-verified tests, to keeping engineers on the keyboard after the tools stop running. Walk away with a practical, repeatable playbook for accelerating large-scale .NET modernization.

sessions.t: Your playbook: turn your scattered databases into AI-ready infrastructure
sessions.a: Business-critical data scattered across Oracle, SQL Server, and VMware or Nutanix-hosted databases is the number one blocker to deploying agentic AI at scale. In this lightning talk, you'll get a practical playbook for database migration to AWS: real licensing challenges, cost optimization strategies, and modernization pathways that accelerate the path to cloud-native databases using AWS Transform and agentic AI. You'll leave with a clear migration framework that turns fragmented data estates into AI-ready infrastructure, no matter where your databases live today.

sessions.t: Your regulator set your RTO. Not your architecture.
sessions.a: Organizations with pre-approved failover regions recover in hours. Those without recover in weeks. Same impairment. Same services. One governance decision separates them, and it’s made years before the event. This session presents architectural patterns for multi-Region recovery under sovereignty constraints, drawn from real operational experience with regulated workloads under regional pressure. Three categories: decisions that set your resilience ceiling before any event, dependencies that create circular failure during recovery, and assets nobody backs up until they become the critical path. You leave with the decisions to evaluate before your next DR test.

sessions.t: Your system made a decision. you cannot explain it.
sessions.a: Your system makes a decision. A human makes a decision. Both write to the same log in the same format. Three months later you need to know which was which. You cannot tell. This is not a logging problem. It is a runtime architecture problem. If decision origin is not captured at the boundary when the decision happens, no system can recover it after. Whether you need this for compliance, debugging, or customer trust, the architectural fix is identical. In this chalk talk you will decide: what to capture at the decision boundary, how much context to store, and when reproducibility justifies the cost.

sessions.t: Your Users Aren't Waiting to Build AI Agents. Are You Ready?
sessions.a: The spreadsheet wizards and automation tinkerers in your organization are already reaching for low-code and visual builder tools to assemble AI agents on their own. Call it citizen agent building: either governance sprawl, or your fastest path to scale. This interactive chalk talk gives platform, security, and data leaders a reference pattern that puts low-code builders on top and Amazon Bedrock beneath, so the security, data residency, and governance enterprises need come from the foundation rather than from each agent. Amazon Bedrock makes governance possible; your architecture makes it the default.

sessions.t: Your WAN, reimagined: SD-WAN on the AWS global backbone
sessions.a: Your enterprise WAN was built for a world where applications lived in data centers. That world is gone—but you're still paying for MPLS circuits and waiting weeks for new sites. What if you could replace that backbone entirely? AWS offers the largest global infrastructure footprint of any provider: resilient, agile, low-latency, and encrypted. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how to connect your SD-WAN to AWS Cloud WAN, maintain segmentation from branch to VPC, and pay only for what you use—no long-term contracts. Bring your WAN architecture and we'll show you what it looks like without the middlemen.

sessions.t: Zero-Shot Demand Forecasting with Chronos 2, SMUS, and Quick Suite
sessions.a: Stockouts and overstocks quietly erode margin for retail and CPG brands, driving lost sales, markdowns, and working capital tied up in the wrong inventory. Traditional forecasting models take months to train and tune, and struggle with the cold-start problem for new products and locations. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to architect zero-shot demand forecasting pipelines using Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio with the Chronos 2 time-series foundation model, developed by the Amazon Science team and proven on Amazon's own retail and CPG demand at scale, requiring no historical model training. We walk through the end-to-end design: SMUS notebooks for rapid experimentation, Chronos 2 for multi-variate time series prediction, and Amazon Quick Suite for conversational analytics that let planners explore forecasts in natural language..

sessions.t: Zero to multimodal in 60 mins: Building Live Sync on Connect Customer
sessions.a: What does it take to synchronize a live voice conversation with a real-time visual interface — and make it feel like magic? In this chalk talk, we'll answer that question by building one from scratch. No slides, no hand-waving — just building, live, from zero to a working multimodal agent in 60 minutes. At the end, we'll deploy what we built and every phone in the room becomes a live demo.

sessions.t: Zero-Trust by Design: How Bee Protects Personal Data Even from Itself on AWS
sessions.a: Personal agentic AI represents a new frontier — devices that understand you deeply enough to act on your behalf. Bee is Amazon's AI wearable that helps users capture and act on insights from their daily lives. But deep personalization demands deep trust and privacy. In this session, learn how the Bee team architected a zero-trust pipeline using AWS Nitro Enclaves and confidential computing to keep sensitive data cryptographically isolated at every stage. We'll share the attestation models, data minimization tradeoffs, and design principles you can apply to build AI-powered experiences your users trust from day one.

sessions.t: Zero trust for non-human identities: IAM for autonomous agents
sessions.a: Agents access tools, call APIs, and delegate to other agents. They need layered identity controls at every stage. In this builders' session, apply zero trust principles to a multi-agent environment using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll configure agent identities with OAuth providers, enforce least privilege via OBO token exchange, differentiate agents from humans with IAM MCP condition keys, and set Gateway rules blocking unauthorized access. Then, you stress test your setup using cross-chain access, privilege escalation, identity spoofing to see each blocked by a different layer you built.
